Founder Lab is a weekly build day for early-stage founders. Bring what you're stuck on — check in on what you're testing and what you learned, then get to work: office hours with investors and operators, and open build time with founders at your stage. Same day, every week.

​Who is this for?

​Founders building venture-scale startups, pre-seed to Series A — AI, deep tech, frontier, or any technical or science vertical. Connected through a common thread of relentless honesty and proof arc: something built to scale, tested and iterated on weekly.

​The System

​Every check-in runs through FounderOS, the proof engine that turns weekly work into a track record with venture visibility.

​Review Reps: How are you stuck, what did you learn, and what needs to change.

​Pressure-Test Logic: Use adversarial feedback to identify flaws in current hypotheses.

​Anchor the Roadmap: Align on near-term technical unlocks and business milestones.

​Design the Next Interval: Lock the specific success gates for the upcoming build cycle.

​Direct Feedback: Receive "brutal honesty" testing from founders, operators, and venture advisors.

events.name: La Residencia NYC: Opening Night for Latin Women Building with AI
events.description:
An intimate evening for women building with AI.

Human in the Loop is the first Sobremesa of La Residencia, our opening event in New York: an evening for Latina women who are using AI, building with it, or just getting started, and want to stay the ones making the decisions.

Who you'll meet
Founders, creatives, consultants, and ambitious women building their careers and something of their own. Some are building with AI every day; some are just starting. All of them are making something. Come ready to tell us what you're working on, and to see what the latinas next to you are building. The best part of rooms like this is who you walk out knowing.
Wait, what's a salon?
Not a panel. Not a class. Not networking with name tags. A salon is the oldest format for thinking together: one host, one question, and a room of people who came to actually talk. Salons started in Paris, hosted by women who chose who came and guided the conversation. We call ours Sobremesa, for the conversation that keeps going after the meal is over. No stage, no slides, no laptops. Everyone speaks, everyone listens, and nobody leaves the same.

You'll leave with
* Real connections with Latina women who are building something, and a look at what they're making with AI
* A card to keep: four questions to ask yourself every time you open AI

Your host
Clau Romero is a Peruvian brand and business strategist in New York. She builds with AI and keeps the decisions human: AI in service of your judgment, not the other way around. She is the founder of La Residencia.

About La Residencia
La Residencia is a community of Latina women where AI is learned and judgment is cultivated. Technology is within everyone's reach. Knowing what to do with it is what sets us apart.

events.name: Reciprocal Founders Roundtable (40 and Over)
events.description:
A small, facilitated roundtable for founders who aren't hustle-culture kids.
Bring one conversation you've been avoiding. Leave with real perspective on it, and a handful of founders who know what you're actually dealing with.
No stage. No audience. No pitching. 
Facilitated by executive leadership coach Daniel Stillman, author of Good Talk: How to Design Conversations that Matter. 
Who is this for?
Being a founder takes commitment, sacrifice, and sometimes hustle. But the hustle-culture narrative doesn't match the life you want as you get older. You're not 25 with nothing to lose. You have a mortgage. You want a proper vacation. Maybe you have aging parents to care for. And a mission you still want to bring into the world. 

Why a Roundtable?
You don’t need another big networking event, or a poorly moderated panel you could have watched on YouTube at 2x.

You need an intimate, high-trust, off-the-record room where you can get real with other founders, builders and entrepreneurs. 

A roundtable is one where everyone shares, everyone is heard, and everyone gets more than they imagined.

The Conversation
Conversations are the atomic unit of change. Our lives are built by the conversations we have, and defined by the ones we avoid. The cofounder conflict you brush off but never resolve. The hire you won't admit isn't working. The pivot you keep putting off.
The ones we avoid most are with ourselves. The bargains we never renegotiated. The anxiety we can't politely ask to leave. The question we keep not answering.
The un-had conversation doesn't disappear. It goes underground and gets more expensive. This roundtable is designed to create the space for the most important questions and conversations you’re facing right now.

Application and Curation
Admission is by invitation only - please complete all application questions so we can curate the group, optimizing for:

People actively building
Openness, Curiosity and Generosity
Commitment - people who don’t show up won’t be invited to come again
The Prework: 
This is a small room, on purpose, so we’re only selecting a handful of folks who are willing to do some thinking before they get in the room. Apply with your thoughtful answers to the registration questions.
The Format: 
Five rounds of conversation: 
Connection and Learning - so we know who we are and why we’re building what we are each building
Exploration: Sharing your avoided conversation with the group
Stories Vs Advice: Sharing stories to help each other through shared empathy, not problem solving
Asks and Offers: What’s something you need from the group? What’s something you can offer in generosity?
Closing Round - What you’re taking away from the conversation - what you’re committed to
The Follow Up:
Join a continuing conversation with the attendees, where you can share the resource you mentioned, ask that follow-up question, and get the support you need from a generous, growing community.
Your Co-Hosts
Daniel Stillman designs conversations for a living, and insists that you do too. He's an executive coach and facilitator who works with founders and founding teams on how they lead, communicate, and navigate the conversations that matter. He hosts The Conversation Factory podcast (a top 100 Management podcast) and wrote Good Talk: How to Design Conversations that Matter, a handbook for changemakers and innovators.
Anson Wu is the founder of Ugly Talk, the no-BS event series where battle-tested founders share the setbacks, pivots, and lessons behind the wins. Since 2019 it's grown across New York, Chicago, San Francisco, and Miami. Anson also runs Grey Journal, the digital media company behind it, and came up as a designer and agency founder. By his own description, a recovering underthinker still mining the lessons from two failed startups.
About Ugly Talk
Started in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough “aha!” moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons and insights.
With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, and Miami, we’ve built a vibrant community of thousands of founders and industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape.
Official Website: UglyTalk.com

Why You Think the Way You Do About Money: A live panel on the psychology behind every financial decision you've ever made

​Here's a question nobody asks at a normal finance event:

​Why does your best friend save obsessively while you can't walk past a sale, even though you make the same salary?

​Why do you know exactly what you "should" do with your money and still not do it?

​Why did you inherit your dad's spending anxiety instead of his frugality?

​That's the whole point of this panel. Rebecca Pino (financial advisor) and Suzanne Kirkendall (behavioral scientist) are turning the mic on each other — and on you.

​No slide decks, no "5 tips to save more" energy. Just two people who study money and behavior for a living, asking each other the questions they actually want answered, then opening the floor so the audience can grill them both together.

LinkedIn, Minus the Ick
Build visibility without losing yourself in the process. 

LinkedIn can be cringe: the forced positivity, the AI content, and the pressure to post like everyone else in your feed. This Mastermind is a discussion, not a lecture, on how to show up on the feed while building your own voice.

Juliette and Sondra have grown their audiences past 5K and pivoted industries, landed projects, and received job offers because of posting consistently on LinkedIn.

  • A clearer sense of how to create human content instead of AI-sounding content

  • An accountability buddy for your LinkedIn goals

Perfect for:

Sales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). events.name: The Future of Social Health: Building Technology That Brings Us Together
events.description:
The Future of Social Health: Building Technology That Brings Us Together

An SCC x Fabrik gathering, sponsored by Entrelacs

Friday, November 13, 2026, 4:00–6:00 pm

Can technology help people feel closer to each other? Most public debate assumes it can't.

Philosopher Andy Clark offers a more useful starting point. In a 2025 essay in Nature Communications, he argues that people have always thought with tools, from pen and paper to maps to AI, and that what matters is how each partnership between person and tool is designed. If tools can help us think, they can also help us see our relationships more clearly.

Disconnection doesn't look the same for everyone. Someone who moved cities for a job may have no one nearby to call when something goes wrong, while a patient with family close by can still feel that nobody understands what they're going through. A program built for one of them rarely helps the other. This evening looks at technology that can tell situations like these apart, and at what it takes to build it well.


The Social Connection Collective and Fabrik are bringing together the researchers and founders building these tools with HR and corporate wellness leaders, clinicians, investors, and technologists.


What happens during the afternoon 

  • Interview and demo. Dr. Hans Rocha IJzerman, social psychologist and founder and CEO of Entrelacs, talks with [interviewer] about his research on loneliness and social connection, including a LONELY-EU review of 2,720 questionnaires showing how differently the field measures it. A demo of Entrelacs follows.

  • Founder pitches. founders building technology for connection (3-5 mins each) Hands-on time. Try the tools with the people who built them.

  • Happy hour. Keep the conversation going with light snacks and drinks.

When you arrive, we'll ask you one question: What's one tool, app, or habit that keeps you close to someone? Your answers will open the conversation.

Event Timeline:

3:00 - Arrival and setup

4:00 - Arrival of attendees with Prompt Question

4:30 - Interview / Panel , Demo specifically for Hans

5:00 - Rapid Fire Round, Startups Elevator Pitch (3-5 mins each) 

5:15 - 6:00pm Meet and Mingle with Founders and time for connecting

From our sponsor:

Everyone who RSVPs is welcome to take the Entrelacs assessment before the event and bring their own private Keystone report. https://forms.gle/xdiR2YZtpJVuJ6zC9

The Social Connection Collective is a grassroots global community working to strengthen belonging and reduce loneliness — connecting people, ideas, and organizations dedicated to building a more connected world.

events.name: Wine Wisdom: What's Really in Your Glass?
events.description:
🍷 Wine tasting included with ticket!
Are you a wine enthusiast, sommelier wannabee, or maybe just looking to expand your palate? Then this night is perfect for you! Join us as Certified Sommelier & Wine Educator, Anna Arfaras shares her Wine Wisdom...
What are we actually tasting when we drink wine? Through an interactive palate-training experiment, we’ll isolate the four primary structural components of wine: tannin, acidity, sweetness, and alcohol. By tasting each element independently, participants will learn how these components affect the taste and feel of a wine, how to recognize them in the glass, and ultimately better understand what they like and why they like it.
What are we actually tasting when we drink wine? What do terms like acidity, tannin, body, alcohol, and residual sugar really mean, and how do they affect what we experience in the glass? Most importantly, how can understanding these basic elements help us better identify and communicate what we actually like to drink?
Anna Arfaras is a Certified Sommelier with nearly two decades of experience in the wine and hospitality industry. Her career has taken her through acclaimed restaurants and luxury hospitality operations in New York City, Las Vegas, Orlando, and the Bahamas, with roles ranging from floor sommelier to multi-unit beverage director.

Her experience spans nearly every side of the wine business, including building and managing wine programs, restaurant operations, hospitality consulting, distribution, and supplier sales, with particular expertise in Italian wine. Through her consulting work, Anna has advised restaurants and hospitality groups on wine programs, beverage strategy, operations, and staff education.

Combining a sommelier’s knowledge with years of practical experience buying, selling, serving, and teaching wine, Anna approaches wine education with a focus on making an often-intimidating subject engaging, approachable, and genuinely fun.

Men’s work can help to expand emotional range and resilience, and your ability to express feelings - here in the group through creating a safe space, and out in the world, at your job and in your relationships.

This circle is for both men who have experienced men's work and for men who are curious about men's work.

I work as executive leadership coach and keynote speaker, for organizations of all shapes, sizes and industries. I have learned that at the heart of real change is a conversation - one with yourself, as well as conversations with others. I create space for leaders and their teams to have the conversations that matter.

I’ve been co-leading a men’s group since 2018, and have taught and facilitated men's work in person, online, and at multi-day retreats. Men’s work has been an important part of my ongoing personal development and has allowed me to expand my emotional range and resilience. It’s also expanded my range and the depth in my one-on-one coaching and team transformation work.

I also host The Conversation Factory podcast (a top 100 Management Podcast) and am the author of “Good Talk: How to Design Conversations that Matter” a handbook for changemakers and innovators.

When's the last time you left a happy hour actually...happy? 🍸

​We’ve both spent years inside institutions and companies as operators, coaches, and facilitators, and we kept seeing the same thing:

​People are disconnected, disengaged, and depleted.

events.name: The NYC Subway System: Underappreciated Art Museum
events.description:
🍻 Craft Beer and Snacks Included with Ticket Purchase!
If you're living in NYC, chances are that you ride the subway! But did you know all the incredible art that you might be missing without even realizing it? Join us as Museum Educator and Guide Kristin McCollum opens our eyes to the most underappreciated art museum in the world!
Millions of people ride the subway every day without realizing they're walking through a museum full of art and history, containing countless stories of New York City. This talk digs deep on the history of the NYC subway and why we have such an extensive and diverse amount of art in our stations. 
Kristin McCollum is a museum educator, guide, actor, and improviser. She creates and leads tours at the New York Transit Museum, Morgan Library & Museum, and the Museum of the City of New York. When she's not in a gallery or subway station, she's teaching and performing improv with Improvolution in the West Village or making NYC history and art videos as NerdingOutOnNYC. She and her trash dog Rory are proud residents of Hell's Kitchen.
"...my main goal is to make people more aware of the art as they're commuting and how deep the stories go. The history of the NYC subway system is also so unique and fascinating - and will hopefully make the hodgepodge nature of it more endearing to people. Introducing the less well-known artists that are featured has been very rewarding, and highlighting New York stories that may have been lost through time but are represented in the art is really cool."

events.name: Startup Pitch Mixer
events.description: Join our event in New York! We design Pitch & Networking nights to help founders sharpen their thinking through direct, candid feedback & to give strong investors access to serious teams. Our pitch night is complemented by a structured networking session before & after the pitch session.  What to expect: Startups pitch live & receive focused feedback from angels & VC partners Structured networking session before & after the pitches Entrepreneurs, startup founders, & operators are joining to network, exchange ideas, & build strong connections Active investors & venture scouts joining to discover the best startups early  Who you will meet at the event: Founders Investors, VC partners, Venture Scouts Marketers, Salespeople, Business Advisors Industry Disruptors AI Experts Entrepreneurs from Europe, Asia, & the United Kingdom  We Welcome New Investors: We invite investors to our event to expand their network, get acquainted with new startups, evaluate them, share feedback, & participate in discussions with early-stage & serial founders. We offer complimentary tickets to institutional investors, angels, & venture scouts with a proven track record. If you'd like to access our database of promising startups or provide mentorship support to our best startups, please fill out this short Investor Application Form, & our team will contact you.  Want to Pitch? A limited number of founders will have the opportunity to pitch their startup or business to a panel of investors & experts. 4-6 selected founders will pitch their startup, followed by a short Q&A where participants can ask questions & share feedback. Apply by filling out the Pitch Application Form & sending us your pitch deck. Spots are limited, & we select founders in advance. To maintain high-quality pitches, you are required to present with a pitch deck. We will share our pitching guide and, if you'd like, coach you so you're fully prepared for pitch night.  The best startups will be featured across our social media & included in our investor newsletter. Requirements for attendees: Dress code: smart casual. Bring good energy.  Join our event & secure your ticket today! About us: Startup Valley is a global event organizer hosting pitch nights in 25 cities since 2023. Since then, we have hosted 850 events for 40,000 attendees. Over these years, we connected countless outstanding early-stage startups to serious investors, & we are not planning to stop. We maintain strategic partnerships with VC funds in the US, Europe, & Asia to support our community. Do you have a question, a partnership proposal, or want to clarify something? Reach us at hello@startupvalley.club Agenda 18:00-18:30 - Registration: Guests register, receive badges, & event programs. This is an opportunity for casual networking, making first connections, & preparing for the event. 18:30-19:00 - Event Kickoff & Interactive Networking: Official welcome from the organizers with a brief overview of the event goals & schedule. Interactive networking session to connect with key contacts. 19:00-19:50 - Startup Pitch Session: Startups present their projects to investors & experts. Each team has 5 minutes to pitch, covering the project's core idea, business model, & target market. 19:50-21:00 - Chill & Networking: Participants enjoy casual conversations with investors, discuss collaboration opportunities, & exchange ideas over refreshments. FAQ Can I pitch? Yes! To pitch, please purchase a Pitch Ticket & fill out the Pitch Application Form. We will contact you to discuss & approve your pitch. The pitch duration is 5 minutes. You will also have some time to answer questions from the audience. How does the pitch go? Selected founders present on stage to the audience & the investors in the room. You get 5 minutes to pitch your idea, business model, target market, & investment ask, followed by a short Q&A. The best startups are featured across our social media channels & in the investor newsletter. Who will I meet? Founders, angel investors, VC partners, venture scouts, AI experts, engineers, operators, marketing & sales experts, & international entrepreneurs from across Europe, Asia, & the US. Do investors get free tickets? Yes! Please apply above or email hello@startupvalley.club, & we will issue a complimentary ticket for you & your team. Can I request a refund? Yes. Refunds are available if requested at least 1 day before the event start time. Please submit the refund request on the platform where you purchased your ticket, or email us at hello@startupvalley.club

events.name: Trajectories - Facts, Fictions & Futures Of Spacefaring Societies
events.description: Science fiction has long imagined humanity's path beyond Earth, from post-scarcity utopias to contested frontiers to desperate exoduses. Which way are we headed? This week's interactive community conversation tests those visions against the technological, economic, societal, & cultural forces shaping our spacefaring future right now. Because the future isn't something we predict but something we choose, the question isn't just where we're headed, but where we dare to go. OUR FACILITATORVince Lucich, an engineer & startup founder whose work involves building spacecraft for the emerging orbital economy, will lead us on this idea exploration of the future. WHO'S IT FOR?Idea people. Founders. Builders. Creatives. Researchers. The Curious. And their Supporters --------------FORMATOur format explores ideas together through our diverse backgrounds, while building relationships & community through the process. We want you to talk to each other, instead of just being talked at. 6:00PM - Settle in, grab a drink & some food at the bar, & meet some new people before we start our event. 6:30PM - Our conversation begins with our facilitator presenting the knowledge & context for the conversation along the way. The conversation between attendees will explore from surface level understandings, to deep implications & future iterations. 7:45PM - Meet & connect with new people, catch up with people you haven't seen in a while, discover all the different ways you overlap. And then just hang out, grab a drink, play some pool or ping pong! Or stay for the band afterwards! Our desire is to be the antithesis of NYC's corporate panel & transactional networking culture. We aim to create a vibrant idea & build space in NYC that focuses on the passion & values beyond the money & the hustle.

events.name: Borderless Office - Identity & Access In World Of Remote-First Growth
events.description: Join Antoine Jebara (Co-founder, JumpCloud) & Noah Landow (Founder & CEO, Macktez) for an informal conversation between an expert on scaling global technology companies & the evolution of identity & access management & the founder of a technology consulting firm. In an era defined by remote work & the rapid rise of agentic AI, the concepts of identity & security are shifting beneath our feet. As AI agents begin to act on our behalf, how do we maintain control, responsibility, & security? If an AI agent executes a transaction or accesses a database, who is truly holding the keys? Antoine brings a unique perspective from the front lines of this transition, from pioneering decentralized 2FA & password management at MYKI to driving global strategy & partner ecosystems at JumpCloud. Join us at the Macktez office, after work, over light snacks & sips, for an exploratory conversation on the challenges of scaling fast-growing global companies & how different security architectures impact our long-term safety in a cloud-first world. We will dive into the shifting landscape of encryption, the unique hurdles of managing remote-first organizations, & what it truly means to "identity" ourselves in the age of AI. Photography, audio, & video recording may occur at this event & by attending you consent to such recording media & its release, publication, exhibition, or reproduction. Event StructureWe ask that guests arrive between 7-7:30 pm to minimize disruption during the talk. 7 pm - Doors open, opportunity to mingle over snacks & sips with other attendees7:30 pm - Guests take their seats for the talk8:15 pm - Informal mixer resumes On AttendanceWe have a limited capacity. If your plans change, please update your registration so someone else can join. A bit about Macktez, & why we host this seriesMacktez is a technology consultancy collaborating with organizations going through dynamic change. Our goal is to form a lasting partnership between our team & our clients, so we can anticipate their technology challenges & help them navigate growth, disruption, & other evolving conditions. Each event in our Tte--Tech series is an opportunity to explore a specific cultural, scientific, historical, & personal issue. We fire at the synapses that connect each topic to other fields of interest & to our individual lives. And we do so in a comfortable environment to facilitate conversation that can be casual, surprising, & illuminating. To learn more, visit us at macktez.com.

events.name: An Unmuted Debate: Primary Party Crashers
events.description: Should primaries be open to every voter? More Americans now identify as independent than as Democrat or Republican. Yet in New York & many other states, those voters are shut out of the primaries that often decide who actually wins. So are closed primaries locking out the voters our politics needs most? And would opening them make anything better? Open primaries let any registered voter participate, regardless of party. Supporters say they force candidates to campaign to the whole electorate, reward problem-solvers over partisans, & give millions of independents a real voice. Critics say parties have the right to choose their own nominees, that open systems invite strategic crossover voting & voter confusion, & that the evidence they reduce polarization is thin. So who's right? Are open primaries the fix for a system that rewards the extremes? Or are they a reform that promises more than it delivers? John Opdycke is the founder & president of Open Primaries, a national organization working to enact & protect open & nonpartisan primaries. He has spent three decades in independent & reform politics, helped found the New York State Independence Party, & writes the monthly column Brash Tacks for The Fulcrum. Lindsey Cormack is an associate professor of political science & director of the Diplomacy Lab at Stevens Institute of Technology. She is the author of How to Raise a Citizen (And Why It's Up to You to Do It) & Congress & U.S. Veterans, created the DCInbox database of congressional newsletters, & serves as Secretary of Manhattan Community Board 8. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

events.name: Drinks & Hacking: IT Happy Hour with The Objective-See Foundation
events.description: Join Rippling IT & The Objective-See Foundation for a happy hour at the Rippling NYC office. Over drinks & light bites, enjoy networking with your fellow IT pros & enjoy a presentation from Patrick Wardle, Co-Founder of the Objective-See Foundation, titled: Your Agent, My Orders: Hacking ChatGPT. A bit more about Patrick's presentation: AI agents need broad access to our files, accounts, & devices, making them prime targets for hackers. We took a closer look at ChatGPT's macOS desktop app & uncovered vulnerabilities that allow attackers to turn your trusted AI assistant against you. The impact? Attackers could hijack your Dot, take over your OpenAI account, access protected files, & more. Worse, these attacks present new challenges for traditional security tools: when an AI agent is compromised, malicious activity can look just like the agent doing its job. We'll demo what happens when ChatGPT gets hacked, discuss why AI agents pose new security challenges, & explore what all this means for Mac admins & the future of endpoint security. You can read more about this in NYT & Wired - & we hope to see you in-person for the full presentation. See you soon! A bit about us: Rippling IT amplifies your abilities & supercharges your skills. Control the entire user lifecycle in one system with fully built Identity, Device, & Inventory management tools, & 500+ integrations-including custom SCIM & SAML. Simplify, secure, & scale all from one single platform. Objective-See is a non-profit foundation focused on macOS security, driven by the mission to create free tools, grow & support a global community of students, researchers, & defenders, & advance Apple security through education, research, collaboration, & opportunity, around the world.

events.name: Powering The Transition - Closing Skills Gap In New Energy Infrastructure
events.description: In partnership with Schneider Electric, Google, Barclays, LACI & IYF The energy transition is underway - but the workforce needed to deliver it is not keeping pace. Across the full arc of how energy is generated, moved, stored, serviced, & used - spanning utilities, power generation, advanced manufacturing, fleet electrification, data centers, & industrial infrastructure - a persistent & structural challenge has emerged: the skilled trades & technician roles most critical to new energy infrastructure face serious & growing skills gaps, & too often the employers, training providers, & talent leaders working to close them are doing so in isolation. NationSwell, in partnership with Barclays, LACI, IYF, Schneider Electric, & Google is convening a working session at Brooklyn Army Terminal - home to BATWorks, NYC's emerging climate innovation hub - to change that. Bringing together talent leaders, hiring managers, & workforce training providers, this in-person convening will use IYF's proven industry competency framework to surface & validate the most critical skills gaps across the skilled trades workforce driving new energy infrastructure.  The day will move from insight to action. The goal is a shared vocabulary & shared priorities that attendees can take back to their organizations, & use to advocate for the training investments, certifications, & systems changes the new energy infrastructure demands. BATWorks offers a uniquely fitting backdrop: a place where growth-stage climate companies, workforce development, & hands-on innovation converge. Where employers are growing & talent supply can grow with them. Attendees will leave knowing they are not alone in this challenge - & with concrete, validated priorities to guide the next steps.

events.name: The Outliers Summit
events.description: The Outliers Summit 2026We're excited to announce the Outliers Summit. November 5 & 6 in New York City. A two-day gathering for founders, creators, operators, builders, & thinkers bringing unreasonably ambitious ideas to life, hosted by Ankur Nagpal & Andrew Yeung, in partnership with AngelList.  Previously, we called this event the OOO Summit. But this year, we've evolved the brand & doubled the event to reflect what we believe the future will look like. Over the last two years, thousands of ambitious people attended our summit - multi-hyphenates, hybrid creator-entrepreneurs, solo builders, AI-native founders, & even people running companies of one with agents doing the rest. The word to describe this kind of person is Outlier. The type of person who chooses to take the unconventional path & pave their own way. This year, the Outliers Summit will be two full days:  DAY 1: NOVEMBER 5 // HOW OUTLIERS BUILD Tactical sessions where you leave having built the thing yourself - an app, an agent, an audience, a brand.  DAY 2: NOVEMBER 6 // HOW OUTLIERS THINK Off-the-record conversations about the bets & mindsets that separate outliers from everyone else.  SpeakersSam Parr, Founder of My First Million, Hampton, The Hustle (acq for >$25M) Ryan Hoover, Founder of Product Hunt & Weekend Fund Sahil Lavingia, Founder & CEO of Gumroad ($1B paid out to creators) Zach Sims, Co-founder & CEO of Codecademy (acq for >$500M) Andy Dunn, Founder of Bonobos & Pie (acq for >$300M) Nadya Okamoto, Founder of August & Co-Founder of Pie Nat Eliason, Author & Head of Founders School Nik Sharma, Founder of Sharma Brands Carina Hong, Founder of Axiom (raised $200M at a $1.6B val) & many MORE to be announced. & many more ... to be announced.  Who You'll Be In the Room WithAcross 13 events in 2024 & 2025, 4,298 people from 3,083 companies have come through our events. 54% are founders, C-suite, VP+ or investors 39% are founders & CEOs specifically 48% of founders have raised $1M or more 22% come back for two or more of our events They also come from Google, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, Stripe, Ramp, Notion, Palantir, Goldman Sachs, & a16z, & from the several thousand startups that make up the rest of the room. Every guest is reviewed before approval. If you are unreasonably ambitious, we'd love to meet you.  Past speakersSahil Bloom is a New York Times Bestselling Author & one of the pioneers of 'threads' onTwitter Andrew Yang founded the Forward political party in 2021, Venture for America in 2011, & the ex-CEO of Manhattan Prep. Sam Parr is the Founder of The Hustle, Hampton, My First Million. Alex Lieberman is the Co-founder of Morning Brew. Kyla Scanlon is the Founder of Bread. Guillermo Rauch is the CEO of Vercel. Brianne Kimmel is the Founder at Worklife Ventures. Justin Welsh has built his 1-person business to >$2m in revenue per year with 95% profit margins, events.name: AI & Future Of Life Sciences
events.description: Join UJA Healthcare for our kickoff event:a timely talk featuring Mikael Dolsten, M.D., Ph.D., former chief scientific officer at Pfizer, on how artificial intelligence is advancing medicine & reshaping the life sciences industry. After a reception with light bites & mingling,you'll hear from Dr. Dolsten in conversation with Avi Kometz, M.D., a partner at Deerfield Management, about how AI is accelerating drug discovery, advancing cancer treatment & gene therapies, impacting clinical trials, & opening new possibilities for public health. You'll also hear about UJA's powerful work improving the lives of people in need here in New York, in Israel, & around the world. Dr. Mikael DolstenMikael Dolsten, M.D., Ph.D., is a physician-scientist & investment advisor who serves on several public & private boards as a director or chairman & as strategic advisor to leading business groups in biomedicine & AI TechBio. Dr. Dolsten is the former chief scientific officer & president of Research & Development at Pfizer During his 16-year tenure at Pfizer, he led the approval of more than 36 medicines & vaccines. Dr. Dolsten holds an M.D. & a Ph.D. in tumor immunology from Lund University, where he is a visiting adjunct professor, & has published more than 160 scientific papers. Avi Kometz, M.D., is a partner on Deerfield Management's Medical Technologies team. He was a partner at Ascent Biomedical Ventures, leading investments in biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, & health IT. He also led corporate development at a pediatric pharmaceutical company & advised healthcare clients at McKinsey. He began as a clinician in South Africa & went on to found & build a group of clinics.

events.name: 1st Annual Antitrust Summit
events.description: A global focus on competition law, policy & enforcement comes to New YorkAfter two years of leading the competition debate in London, the Antitrust Summit is crossing the Atlantic. Our London forum brought together more than 385 leading enforcers, economists & corporate executives to discuss the plot twists of modern antitrust law, policy & enforcement. Now, we bring that same rigorous discussion to the US at a particularly consequential moment. The administration in Washington, DC quickly signalled a departure from the neo-Brandeisian period. Dealmaking activity continues to surge. Yet for all the enthusiasm around M&A, the antitrust environment remains unpredictable. Heightened scrutiny of sectors central to the cost of living, increased state intervention in transactions & firms, & a growing role for state attorneys-general in enforcement are contributing to uncertainty. At the same time, AI is reshaping competition & investment dynamics as long-running antitrust cases against technology companies move forward. Against this backdrop, ahead of the November midterm elections, the Antitrust Summit will provide the insights & clarity needed to navigate a changing landscape. Join us in New York on October 28th for the latest edition of our Antitrust Summit series.

events.name: Can Your Agents Actually Ship?
events.description: Can your agents actually ship?Compose your AI-native SDLCYour AI agents can't be trusted with data they can't find, can't understand, & aren't sure they're allowed to touch. And even when they get it right, the code they write still stalls in a delivery pipeline built for human speed. On Nov2 we will tackle both: first the data foundations agents need to trust, then the SDLC they need to ship through. Opening talk: From a Data Swamp to a Data Agent You Can Trust The evening opens with Grzegorz Krl on the data foundations AI agents need to find, understand & safely access your data. We've run this talk at Boston & San Francisco Tech Week, & both times it ran long because nobody wanted to stop asking questions. Full session details: https://luma.com/il0xoz9a Main session: Can your agents actually ship? AI can write code. Getting that code to production is another matter. Most engineering organizations hit the same wall: the bottleneck isn't the agent, it's everything downstream of it. Pipelines, CI, reviews, security gates, release processes: all of it was built for human speed, not AI. Visdom, built by VirtusLab, is the missing layer between AI coding & production. It lets you compose an AI-native SDLC, piece by piece: the context, validation, governance & orchestration agents need to ship safely & at scale. events.name: Daytona AI Builders
events.description: An event dedicated to exploring all things AI Engineering! Event partners: AWS & Antimetal Agenda 5:30 pm - 6:00 pmWelcome Gathering & Opening Remarks Marijan Cipcic, Principal Events Manager at Daytona  6:00 pm - 6:15 pmTalk "Forkable Sandboxes for Long-Running Agents" Muhammad Annas Hashmi, DevRel at Daytona Outline:Agents are starting to do real software work: installing dependencies, editing files, running tests, starting servers, & debugging over long sessions. But most AI systems still treat each run like a disposable prompt-response loop. That breaks down once the useful state lives not just in tokens, but in the actual machine. This talk is about the runtime layer agents need to become reliable builders. I'll show how forkable Daytona sandboxes let you pause at important moments in an agent run, branch the environment, & sample multiple continuations from the same machine state. For builders, this turns long-running agent workflows into something you can inspect, compare, recover, & eventually optimize.  6:15 pm - 6:30 pmTalk "Multi-Agent Investment AI Assistant built on Amazon Bedrock Agentcore" Sam Farber, Sr. Solutions Architect at AWS Outline:Investment research teams spend days manually gathering data across markets, risk metrics, sentiment indicators, financial statements, & alternative data sources before synthesizing findings into actionable reports. This talk will show how a multi-agent AI system can automate that workflow. A supervisor agent breaks down a research question, delegates to 10 domain-specific specialists running in parallel, & compiles their findings into a comprehensive investment report. The system maintains conversation memory across each agent, allowing researchers to have targeted conversations & follow-ups with each specialized agent.  6:30 pm - 6:45 pmTalk "Building a World Model for Production Agents" Shreyas Iyer, Co-founder & CTO of Antimetal Outline:Production systems are increasingly complex, with critical knowledge scattered across code, infrastructure, telemetry, & people's heads. In this talk, we'll explore how to build a persistent world model that gives AI agents a shared understanding of production. We'll break down four foundational layers: physical topology, temporal changes, causal relationships, & organizational context to show how they enable agents to investigate incidents, assess changes, & proactively manage production, building on what they've learned across tasks.  6:45 pm - 6:55 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker TBA Outline:TBA  6:55 pm - 7:05 pmTalk "Letting AI agents use credentials they never see" Chase Erickson, Solutions Engineer at Infisical Outline:Infisical manages the secrets your Daytona agents depend on. The Daytona secret sync pushes them from Infisical to your Daytona organization & keeps them current, rotations included. Infisical's Agent Vault, a proxy, adds the credential to requests bound for the services you configure, so the agent never sees it. In this talk, we'll show how an agent in a Daytona sandbox calls an API without ever holding the secret.  7:05 pm - 8:30 pmNetworkingWith pizzas & beverages About event This is dynamic gathering for AI enthusiasts, innovators, & professionals to collaborate, share ideas, & explore the latest advancements in artificial intelligence. Whether you're building AI products, researching cutting-edge algorithms, or simply passionate about the field, join us to connect, learn, & drive the future of AI forward.

events.name: Tech Table Talk: Career, Family & Life On Your Terms
events.description: Tech Table Talk: Career, Family & Life on Your Terms is an intimate dinner bringing together women in tech for an honest conversation about career, fertility, family planning, & building a life on their own terms. Hosted by Baddies in Tech in partnership with Spring Fertility, the evening will create space for women to have the kinds of conversations we don't often have: How do you think about growing your career while also considering a future family? What options are available if your personal & professional timelines do not align perfectly? And how can having more information today create more choices tomorrow? We're setting the Tech Table to create space for a conversation you may have been thinking about but have not had anyone to talk to about. You'll walk away not just with a great meal & new professional connections, but also more information, more context, & more confidence to make decisions that feel right for the life you're building! What to ExpectWelcome & Opening ToastBaddies in Tech & Spring Fertility will welcome the group & set the tone for an open, judgment-free conversation about career, fertility, family planning, & the life you're building. Dinner & Tech Table TalkOver dinner, guests will have the opportunity to connect more deeply with one another through thoughtful conversation & curated table prompts, exploring the realities of building a career while also thinking about relationships, motherhood, fertility, timing, & what it means to make decisions on your own terms. Fertility Planning Q&A with Dr. Shante Sullivan-PikeThroughout the evening, Dr. Shante Sullivan-Pike of Spring Fertility will help answer questions & demystify fertility, fertility preservation, & family-planning options. Dr. Chantae Sullivan-Pyke is a double board certified Fertility Specialist & Site Director of Spring Fertility Long Island. She completed her medical training at Yale University, Columbia University, & the University of Pennsylvania. Dr. Sullivan-Pyke brings a thoughtful & compassionate approach to fertility care, rooted in deep clinical experience & a genuine connection with her patients. She combines her expertise with a strong commitment to the patient experience, creating a supportive & empowering atmosphere throughout the process. Her areas of clinical focus include IVF, fertility preservation, & oncofertility, & she is particularly passionate about helping her patients navigate complex fertility decisions with clarity & confidence. What You'll Leave WithFresh perspective on navigating career goals alongside personal & family plans New relationships with women thinking through many of the same questions A better understanding of your fertility & family-planning options More clarity around fertility preservation & when it may be worth exploring Greater confidence asking questions about your reproductive health A stronger connection to the Baddies in Tech & Spring Fertility communitie Attendance is complimentary & curated. Because this dinner is intentionally intimate & limited to approximately 20-25 guests, registrations will be reviewed to create a group that aligns with the purpose of the evening. Submitting the registration form expresses your interest in attending & does not guarantee an invitation. Confirmed guests will be notified approximately one week before the event.

events.name: Ugly Talks - Failure Is Key To Success
events.description: Failure gets talked about like it is part of the journey. That is the lie. The real thing is messier. Missed bets. Wrong hires. Near-breakdowns. The week you stop sleeping & start doing math at 3:00 AM. Founders are expected to eat it quietly & keep moving. No language for what happened. No playbook for what to do next. Ugly Talk is a founder room for the part nobody posts. No fluff. No consultants. Just builders with scars, talking about the call that cost them.  Why you should be in this room.Hear what failure cost them. Then hear what they did next. Learn how experienced founders separate self-worth from outcomes when things go sideways. Spot the patterns behind repeat mistakes. And the early signals you should not ignore. Leave with a few concrete moves for the next hard week. Not inspiration. Meet other founders in the thick of it. The ones who are still building.  What's on the table.Dare to suck: how permission to fail unlocks real progress The moment things broke: missed opportunities, wrong turns, near-breakdowns, & what changed afterward Failure vs identity: separating self-worth from outcomes Treating setbacks as data: what to measure, what to ignore, & how to decide fast Rejection as redirection: how founders find the signal in the no Habits for staying focused & resilient when everything feels uncertain  Run of show6:00 - 6:30 PM: Reception (check-in & light drinks) 6:30 - 6:40 PM: Welcome remarks 6:40 - 6:50 PM: Keynote Speech by Ben McKean 6:50 - 7:30 PM: Panel Discussion 7:30 - 7:45 PM: Audience Q&A 7:45 - 8:00 PM: Mixer + snacks & drinks  Featured speakers.Ben McKean - Founder & Chief Executive Officer, Hungryroot Ben McKean is the Founder & CEO of Hungryroot, a personalized healthy eating assistant that uses AI to make meal planning, food shopping, & nutrition effortless & enjoyable. Prior to Hungryroot, Ben was a Vice President & General Manager at Groupon, overseeing their food & beverage business. Ben came to Groupon through the acquisition of Savored, which he founded in 2009. Savored was the nation's leading provider of yield management technology to the restaurant industry, used by over two thousand restaurants nationwide & nearly one million diners. Prior to Savored, Ben worked in Merrill Lynch's technology investment banking group. Ben is a graduate of Georgetown University & currently lives in North Carolina with his wife & kids. Stephen McKinney - Founder & CEO, Bizbe Stephen McKinney is a serial entrepreneur with over a decade of experience across tech, marketing, & logistics. He's the founder & CEO of Bizbe.com, an AI-native business brokerage & lower middle market M&A firm based in New York & Miami. A former contestant on ABC's Shark Tank, Steve previously founded & led Retty Logistics, a seven-figure last-mile delivery company acquired by DXP Logistics & Webster Logistics. Dmitry Koltunov - Founder & CEO, Arbor Dmitry Koltunov is a serial entrepreneur, technologist, educator, & storyteller. He is the founder & CEO of Arbor, an AI-powered content engine that helps enterprises scale their communications with video & beyond. Previously, he co-founded & served as CTO of ALICE, a hospitality technology company that grew into a global industry leader before being acquired by Expedia Group. Dmitry also leads the New York City chapter of the Startup Leadership Program, New York's oldest startup fellowship, whose 500+ alumni have collectively raised more than $1 billion in funding across every industry imaginable. He is passionate about helping founders navigate the challenges of building & scaling companies. Outside of technology, Dmitry is an award-winning songwriter & theater producer currently developing a new musical for Broadway. He holds degrees in Computer Science & Economics from the University of Pennsylvania & is a CFA charterholder. Gwendolyn von Rahn - Co-Founder & CEO, Sweetling Health Gwendolyn von Rahn is the Co-Founder & CEO of Sweetling Health, an postpartum intelligence platform built for at-risk & hard-to-reach populations. She's a second-time exited founder, an award-winning marketer with over a decade of experience building consumer brands for women, Gwen led creative & brand teams at Vogue, InStyle, & POPSUGAR before founding & scaling a mission-driven consumer brand into Nordstrom distribution that raised over $1M for melanoma research through the Melanoma Research Foundation. She holds a Cornell Johnson MBA & founded Sweetling from her own lived experience with the postpartum care gap.  Who's hosting it.Victoria Yampolsky - President, The Startup Station Victoria Yampolsky is the Founder & President of The Startup Station, a strategic CFO advisory firm & financial education platform for startups. She partners with founders on financial strategy, modeling, & fundraising, having supported over 150 companies across 15 industries in raising more than $50M in venture capital. Victoria is also an advocate for female founders & access to capital, & has taught finance to more than 20,000 entrepreneurs through programs including the Bank of America Institute for Women's Entrepreneurship at Cornell. She began her career at Deutsche Bank & Capgemini, & holds a BS in Computer Science from Cornell University & an MBA from Columbia Business School.  Who's getting in.Early-stage tech founders & operators navigating uncertainty, setbacks, or the emotional weight of building a company. Expected roles may include: Founders & co-founders (pre-seed to Series A) Operators (COO, Head of Ops, Chief of Staff) Product & Engineering leads building through ambiguity Growth & GTM leads working through missed targets & pivots Finance & strategy leaders supporting founder decision-making  Who's backing this.The Startup Station The Startup Station - is a CFO advisory & financial education platform for early-stage startups. We help early-stage founders build investor-ready financials & tell their funding story with confidence. In the past decade, we've helped 150+ founders raise over $50M & educated 20,000+ entrepreneurs worldwide. The Startup Station also runs Speed Pitch, an exclusive investor-founder matchmaking event series for early-stage startups where founders are matched with 3 investors by sector, stage, & check size. Mind Your Business Every attendee will receive a free copy of keynote speaker Ben McKean's Mind Your Business. Mind Your Business is a practical parable for people rethinking work as AI advances. Set over a four-day retreat, it follows six participants competing for funding to bring one vision to life. As they evaluate six competing proposals, they begin to confront deeper questions about what gives them energy, who they serve, & what they uniquely contribute. Those patterns form what the book calls their Soulcode-the way purpose, belonging, imagination, & courage shape how they work. Told with humor & warmth, the story turns familiar workplace tensions into practical lessons for contributing more deeply, seeing new possibilities, & acting with greater conviction. At its core, the book argues that the opportunity of the AI era isn't doing more work-it's knowing what work is worth doing. GREY Journal GREY Journal - Media partner spotlighting modern entrepreneurs (featured on Apple News + Google News).  About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough "aha!" moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons & insights. With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami, we've built a vibrant community of thousands of founders & industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape. Official Website: UglyTalk.com Important Notice for Ugly Talk AttendeesAdmission & Confirmation Attendance is by approval only. Approved guests will receive a confirmation email along with a calendar invite. Invitations are non-transferable. Additional event details will be shared as the event approaches. Code of Conduct By attending, you agree to: Maintain respect & professionalism, adhering to all venue rules, policies, & applicable laws. Refrain from harassment, discrimination, unwelcome sexual advances (verbal or physical), intimidation, or inappropriate photography/recording. Report any violations to the event hosts immediately. Violations may result in immediate removal from the event & exclusion from future invitations. Liability & Risk Participation is voluntary & at your own risk. The event organizers, hosts, sponsors, & venue are not liable for personal injury, lost or stolen belongings, or any other damages incurred during the event. Media Consent By attending, you grant the event organizers & affiliated entities the right to capture, use, & distribute photos, videos, & audio recordings of you for promotional, marketing, & other lawful purposes, including digital & print media, advertising, & social media. You waive any right to inspect or approve the final materials & release all claims related to their use. Communications By registering, you agree to receive marketing & promotional communications from Ugly Talk & its co-hosts, partners, & sponsors. You may unsubscribe at any time. Agreement If you do not agree to this Code of Conduct, please refrain from attending the event.  Join us to stay updated on upcoming Ugly Talk events! Join the newsletter  Follow us on IG  Official website

The ones who are still building.  What's on the table.Dare to suck: how permission to fail unlocks real progress The moment things broke: missed opportunities, wrong turns, near-breakdowns, & what changed afterward Failure vs identity: separating self-worth from outcomes Treating setbacks as data: what to measure, what to ignore, & how to decide fast Rejection as redirection: how founders find the signal in the no Habits for staying focused & resilient when everything feels uncertain  Run of show6:00 - 6:30 PM: Reception (check-in & light drinks) 6:30 - 6:40 PM: Welcome remarks 6:40 - 6:50 PM: Keynote Speech by Ben McKean 6:50 - 7:30 PM: Panel Discussion 7:30 - 7:45 PM: Audience Q&A 7:45 - 8:00 PM: Mixer + snacks & drinks  Featured speakers.Ben McKean - Founder & Chief Executive Officer, Hungryroot Ben McKean is the Founder & CEO of Hungryroot, a personalized healthy eating assistant that uses AI to make meal planning, food shopping, & nutrition effortless & enjoyable. Prior to Hungryroot, Ben was a Vice President & General Manager at Groupon, overseeing their food & beverage business. Ben came to Groupon through the acquisition of Savored, which he founded in 2009. Savored was the nation's leading provider of yield management technology to the restaurant industry, used by over two thousand restaurants nationwide & nearly one million diners. Prior to Savored, Ben worked in Merrill Lynch's technology investment banking group. Ben is a graduate of Georgetown University & currently lives in North Carolina with his wife & kids. Stephen McKinney - Founder & CEO, Bizbe Stephen McKinney is a serial entrepreneur with over a decade of experience across tech, marketing, & logistics. He's the founder & CEO of Bizbe.com, an AI-native business brokerage & lower middle market M&A firm based in New York & Miami. A former contestant on ABC's Shark Tank, Steve previously founded & led Retty Logistics, a seven-figure last-mile delivery company acquired by DXP Logistics & Webster Logistics. Dmitry Koltunov - Founder & CEO, Arbor Dmitry Koltunov is a serial entrepreneur, technologist, educator, & storyteller. He is the founder & CEO of Arbor, an AI-powered content engine that helps enterprises scale their communications with video & beyond. Previously, he co-founded & served as CTO of ALICE, a hospitality technology company that grew into a global industry leader before being acquired by Expedia Group. Dmitry also leads the New York City chapter of the Startup Leadership Program, New York's oldest startup fellowship, whose 500+ alumni have collectively raised more than $1 billion in funding across every industry imaginable. He is passionate about helping founders navigate the challenges of building & scaling companies. Outside of technology, Dmitry is an award-winning songwriter & theater producer currently developing a new musical for Broadway. He holds degrees in Computer Science & Economics from the University of Pennsylvania & is a CFA charterholder. Gwendolyn von Rahn - Co-Founder & CEO, Sweetling Health Gwendolyn von Rahn is the Co-Founder & CEO of Sweetling Health, an postpartum intelligence platform built for at-risk & hard-to-reach populations. She's a second-time exited founder, an award-winning marketer with over a decade of experience building consumer brands for women, Gwen led creative & brand teams at Vogue, InStyle, & POPSUGAR before founding & scaling a mission-driven consumer brand into Nordstrom distribution that raised over $1M for melanoma research through the Melanoma Research Foundation. She holds a Cornell Johnson MBA & founded Sweetling from her own lived experience with the postpartum care gap.  Who's hosting it.Victoria Yampolsky - President, The Startup Station Victoria Yampolsky is the Founder & President of The Startup Station, a strategic CFO advisory firm & financial education platform for startups. She partners with founders on financial strategy, modeling, & fundraising, having supported over 150 companies across 15 industries in raising more than $50M in venture capital. Victoria is also an advocate for female founders & access to capital, & has taught finance to more than 20,000 entrepreneurs through programs including the Bank of America Institute for Women's Entrepreneurship at Cornell. She began her career at Deutsche Bank & Capgemini, & holds a BS in Computer Science from Cornell University & an MBA from Columbia Business School.  Who's getting in.Early-stage tech founders & operators navigating uncertainty, setbacks, or the emotional weight of building a company. Expected roles may include: Founders & co-founders (pre-seed to Series A) Operators (COO, Head of Ops, Chief of Staff) Product & Engineering leads building through ambiguity Growth & GTM leads working through missed targets & pivots Finance & strategy leaders supporting founder decision-making  Who's backing this.The Startup Station The Startup Station - is a CFO advisory & financial education platform for early-stage startups. We help early-stage founders build investor-ready financials & tell their funding story with confidence. In the past decade, we've helped 150+ founders raise over $50M & educated 20,000+ entrepreneurs worldwide. The Startup Station also runs Speed Pitch, an exclusive investor-founder matchmaking event series for early-stage startups where founders are matched with 3 investors by sector, stage, & check size. Mind Your Business Every attendee will receive a free copy of keynote speaker Ben McKean's Mind Your Business. Mind Your Business is a practical parable for people rethinking work as AI advances. Set over a four-day retreat, it follows six participants competing for funding to bring one vision to life. As they evaluate six competing proposals, they begin to confront deeper questions about what gives them energy, who they serve, & what they uniquely contribute. Those patterns form what the book calls their Soulcode-the way purpose, belonging, imagination, & courage shape how they work. Told with humor & warmth, the story turns familiar workplace tensions into practical lessons for contributing more deeply, seeing new possibilities, & acting with greater conviction. At its core, the book argues that the opportunity of the AI era isn't doing more work-it's knowing what work is worth doing. GREY Journal GREY Journal - Media partner spotlighting modern entrepreneurs (featured on Apple News + Google News).  About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough "aha!" moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons & insights. With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami, we've built a vibrant community of thousands of founders & industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape. Official Website: UglyTalk.com Important Notice for Ugly Talk AttendeesAdmission & Confirmation Attendance is by approval only. Join us for light bites, drinks, & lively conversations.   ///   BNYDC RULES, PROTOCOLS & ACKNOWLEDGEMENT  Check-In Procedure All visitors must check-in at Building 92. Visitors arriving through other entry points will be redirected to enter through official entry locations.All visitors must register for the event. No one will be admitted without an official RSVP. It is highly recommended that you RSVP in advance although day of registration is permitted.A valid photo ID is required for entry. Visitors under 18 must be accompanied by an adult & do not need a photo ID.Visitors who fail to register or do not present a valid photo ID will be denied entry.Expect an estimated 5-minute check-in & security screening process.  Security Protocols All bags will be checked at the entrance for prohibited items.Prohibited items include but are not limited to alcohol; weapons, noise-making devices; laser pointers; fireworks; professional camera equipment; large political signs, banners, or flags; & other materials that may cause harm, damage, or disruption.Bags must not exceed the size of a standard school backpack (Approximately 18 x 14 x 6)Large bags, including roller bags, will not be permitted.  Campus Rules for Event All visitors must stay in approved areas. Visitors should not enter closed or restricted spaces during the event. This includes active construction areas.If buildings & businesses are open, please be respectful while in their spaces & remain mindful that these are working studios & manufacturing centers.Participating businesses may choose to close their spaces at their discretion, including if they determine that visitors are being disruptive.The Brooklyn Navy Yard is an active manufacturing & industrial campus. Visitors are expected to walk on sidewalks where possible & to be mindful of road traffic.To ensure proper pedestrian movement, do not congregate in ways that block entrances, exits, roadways, or parking lots during your visit.Visitors are prohibited from causing damage to Brooklyn Navy Yard property or causing disruptions to other visitors, business owners or workers, & volunteers & staff working at the event.  Photo Acknowledgement & Permissions By registering for the event, you understand that photography and/or video may be taken at the event for marketing or promotional purposes & you consent to being filmed or photographed for such use. Furthermore, you release the Brooklyn Navy Yard Development Corporation, its officers, employees, & agents, from any liability in connection with such photography or videography & the use thereof, & waive any claims you may have for payment in connection with such materials & the use thereof.   Newsletter Acknowledgement & Permission By signing up for this event, you are agreeing to be added to the free Brooklyn Navy Yard public newsletter list. Newsletters are sent 1 - 2 times each month & list public programs, events, & exhibitions at the Yard. You may unsubscribe at any time.

events.name: Health2Tech - MedTech Edition
events.description: Health2Tech - a series of digital health events.Join us on November 5th for an exclusive gathering that brings together the brightest minds in the digital health space. Hosted by Bailey Morgan, Audrey Guazzone, Maria Putilina & Alex Koshykov, this evening promises to be a confluence of innovation, inspiration, & invaluable networking.  Important!  To keep this session highly focused, priority will be given to MedTech experts, device founders, bioengineers, clinicians, & specialized investors. If you work outside the MedTech space, we appreciate your understanding - we'll review your application & confirm attendance based on remaining capacity.  Want to Showcase Your Medical Device Live?If you are building a medical device or physical HealthTech product, we have live demo spots available to feature your innovation in front of NYC investors, healthcare leaders, & potential partners. How to apply: Fill out the form - Open Google Form Register on this Luma page. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, so please apply early!  Event Schedule: 5:30 PM - 6:00 Doors Open. Begin the evening with a warm welcome & a chance to settle in. 6:00 - 6:45 Panel on: "What Makes a MedTech Company Investable?". 6:45 - 8:30 Networking. Connect, converse, & collaborate with peers driven by a common passion for advancing healthcare through technology.  About our Panelists: Steven Levy Steven is a Partner at Unorthodox Ventures where he focuses on investing in venture stage MedTech companies. Before joining Unorthodox Ventures, Steven worked for the prior 23 years as an investment banker, having held senior roles at Lehman Brothers, Stifel Financial & Cowen & Co. Steven has executed over 100 transactions with aggregate deal value in excess of $30 billion. Steven headed the M&A efforts for the Financial Sponsors practice at Lehman Brothers, covered Financial sponsors & headed the Consumer M&A efforts at Cowen & covered Financial Sponsors, led execution on technology & consumer M&A transactions & headed up the firm's investment banking efforts in Israel at Stifel. Steven received his B.A. from Binghamton University & graduated as a member of Phi Beta Kappa & received his M.B.A. from the Wharton School, at the University of Pennsylvania. Bryan Spielman is a Managing Partner at Northwell Health Equity Partners. He is a seasoned C-suite executive with a track record of driving multi-billion-dollar value creation across the healthcare & technology sectors. Most recently, as Chief Growth Officer at Advarra, he spearheaded the company's $5 billion sale to Blackstone & CPPIB. Prior to that, at Medidata, he helped scale the company from a $400 million to over $2.3 billion market valuation. Bryan spent 12 years in investment banking at Centerview Partners, UBS, & Bear Stearns, advising on over $50 billion in transactions. He holds an MBA from NYU Stern School of Business & a BA from the University of Pennsylvania. Host/Moderator: Maria Putilina, MD, MS, is a medical advisor & innovator, boasting over a decade of driving transformative change within the healthcare industry. Her expertise spans Business Administration, Medicine, & Science, which she honed in healthcare consulting, helping companies build & execute innovation strategies.  Why Attend? Meet like-minded individuals who are actively shaping the health tech landscape. Share experiences, discuss challenges, & explore potential solutions with fellow founders. Learn from the journeys of other entrepreneurs, discover something new, seek advice, & perhaps find the mentor or partner you've been looking for.  Who Should Attend? Digital Health Founders at various stages of their startup journey. Healthcare Professionals who are passionate about health innovation. Investors looking to make impactful contributions to the digital health & medtech spaces.  Why This Event Is A Must? Hear from thought leaders & innovators in the digital health domain (at every event, we'll have a new set of speakers). Connect with peers, potential collaborators, & mentors. Participate in engaging Q&As & discussions that can spark new ideas & opportunities.  Venue Details: Because of limited capacity, we won't be able to accommodate everyone, so please register whenever you are sure you can attend. Partner Brown Rudnick is a leading international law firm that provides exceptional, client-driven service in global litigation, crisis management (restructuring, investigations, & special situations), brand & reputation management, life sciences, & technology.  We advise on high-profile cross-border matters while providing the kind of personal attention to clients that is typically found at boutiques. Our enterprising & tenacious lawyers serve our clients around the globe from offices in key financial centers in the U.S. & the U.K., & have been recognized by, among others, Chambers USA, Legal 500, Benchmark Litigation, & Law360 for excellence in their fields. To learn more about our Emerging Growth Companies & Venture Capital group, please visit us here. About the organisers Audrey Guazzone is an innovation & commercialization strategist who helps medtech & digital health companies navigate international growth. Through LeanLia, she combines market validation, commercialization strategy, & hands-on business development to help companies grow in the U.S. She is passionate about connecting healthcare innovators & ecosystems across America & Europe. Maria Putilina, MD, MS, is a medical advisor & innovator, boasting over a decade of driving transformative change within the healthcare industry. Her expertise spans Business Administration, Medicine, & Science, which she honed in healthcare consulting, helping companies build & execute innovation strategies. Bailey Morgan is a healthtech leader who blends clinical expertise with business strategy to drive healthcare innovation & growth. A former speech-language pathologist, she has helped raise over $10 million in capital, led go-to-market teams across SaaS & CPG companies, & closed more than $2 million in technology sales. As Chief of Staff at Groth Pain & Spine, she leads change management & technology integration across a growing provider network, while also advising healthcare technology companies & serving as Director & Treasurer of a nonprofit supporting individuals living with dementia & their caregivers. Alex Koshykov is a co-founder of BeKey & a digital health expert who constantly shares news, introduces promising technologies, & promotes secure software & hardware for the healthcare industry on his YouTube channel. Additionally to that, he is a co-founder of YODD, a medical device startup. Additional Information By signing up, your email will be automatically added to the Health2Tech newsletter with news & upcoming events - but don't worry, we won't flood your inbox! ;) Also, just a note that this event might be photographed or filmed. If we do capture some moments, Health2Tech may use the photos or videos for marketing & communication purposes. By registering, you're giving us the thumbs up for using your image for these reasons.

events.description: Building Technology for the Moments That Matter Mission By Design is an intentional networking experience bringing together NYC's brightest minds across Product, Design, & Engineering to explore what it means to build technology that directly impacts the communities we live in. Join Axon, in partnership with Baddies in Tech, for an inside look at Axon 911, one of Axon's newest areas of innovation & the leader in public safety & emergency response technology.  Expect a tech-forward conversation exploring how teams are modernizing emergency response technology by solving complex real-world problems & making product & technical decisions where speed, clarity, & trust matter. You'll hear directly from the founders & leaders behind Axon 911, how they're shaping the day-to-day work & what they're building, how mission influences the product, & what it means to create technology for moments when every second counts. This experience is designed for the builders: Product, Design, & Engineering professionals who are curious about how technology can create tangible real-world impact & want to connect with other thoughtful builders across NYC. Come for intentional networking, thought-provoking conversations with the people behind the technology, and, if you're exploring your next move, an opportunity to connect directly with Axon's hiring teams. Step inside the work, meet the people shaping it, & see what it looks like when mission is built by design. What to ExpectArrival & ConnectionEase into the evening with drinks, light bites, & intentional networking with fellow Product, Design, & Engineering professionals from across NYC. Inside Axon 911 PanelA candid conversation with the founders & leaders behind Axon 911 on the technology, product decisions, & real-world challenges shaping the future of emergency response. For those exploring their next move, this is also an opportunity to learn more about the teams being built at Axon & connect directly with the people behind the hiring process. Who Should AttendThis experience is designed for mid to senior-level professionals across: Product Management Product Design / UX Software Engineering Engineering Leadership This is for thoughtful builders who are curious about mission-driven technology, real-world impact, & connecting with other people shaping what comes next. What You'll Leave WithNew relationships with NYC Product, Design, & Engineering events.name: Startup Pitch Mixer
events.description: Join our Pitch & Networking Night in New York! We design Pitch & Networking nights to help founders sharpen their thinking through direct, candid feedback, & to give strong investors access to serious teams. The pitch session comes with structured networking before & after. WHAT TO EXPECT- Startups pitch live & get focused feedback from angels & VC partners- Structured networking before & after the pitches- Founders, entrepreneurs & operators networking, exchanging ideas & building connections- Active investors & venture scouts discovering the best startups early WHO YOU WILL MEET- Founders- Investors, VC partners & venture scouts- Marketers, salespeople & business advisors- Industry disruptors & AI experts- Entrepreneurs from Europe, Asia & the UK AGENDA18:00 - 18:30  Registration & casual networking18:30 - 19:00  Kickoff & interactive networking19:00 - 19:50  Startup pitch session (5 min per pitch + Q&A)19:50 - 21:00  Chill & networking over refreshments FOR INVESTORSComplimentary tickets are available to institutional investors, angels & venture scouts with a proven track record. If you'd like access to our database of promising startups or want to mentor our best teams, fill out the Investor Application Form & our team will contact you. WANT TO PITCH?4-6 selected founders pitch to a panel of investors & experts, each followed by a short Q&A.- Buy a Pitch Ticket & fill out the Pitch Application Form with your deck- Spots are limited, & founders are selected in advance- A pitch deck is required. We share our pitching guide & offer coaching if you'd like it- The best startups are featured on our social media & in our investor newsletter DRESS CODESmart casual. Bring good energy. FAQCan I pitch?Yes. Buy a Pitch Ticket & fill out the Pitch Application Form. We'll contact you to approve your pitch. You get 5 minutes plus audience Q&A. How does the pitch go?You present on stage for 5 minutes, covering your idea, business model, target market & investment ask, followed by a short Q&A. Do investors get free tickets?Yes. Apply via the form or email hello@startupvalley.club & we'll issue a complimentary ticket for you & your team. Can I request a refund?Yes, up to 1 day before the event. Request it on the platform where you bought your ticket, or email hello@startupvalley.club ABOUT STARTUP VALLEYStartup Valley is a global event organizer that has hosted pitch nights in 25 cities since 2023: 850 events & 40,000 attendees so far. We have strategic partnerships with VC funds in the US, Europe & Asia. Questions or partnerships: hello@startupvalley.club
