events.name: PMAI: Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Sales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. - Bring a computer. You're writing three things tonight.- Most founders can get meetings. The deals die after meeting one.- You'll leave with your buyer in one sentence, a cold email written to a real person, & five questions for your next call. About Farzad, the speaker Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding & generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: Startup Pitch Mixer
events.description: Join our event in New York! We design Pitch & Networking nights to help founders sharpen their thinking through direct, candid feedback & to give strong investors access to serious teams. Our pitch night is complemented by a structured networking session before & after the pitch session. What to expect: Startups pitch live & receive focused feedback from angels & VC partners Structured networking session before & after the pitches Entrepreneurs, startup founders, & operators are joining to network, exchange ideas, & build strong connections Active investors & venture scouts joining to discover the best startups early  Who you will meet at the event: Founders Investors, VC partners, Venture Scouts Marketers, Salespeople, Business Advisors Industry Disruptors AI Experts Entrepreneurs from Europe, Asia, & the United Kingdom  We Welcome New Investors: We invite investors to our event to expand their network, get acquainted with new startups, evaluate them, share feedback, & participate in discussions with early-stage & serial founders. We offer complimentary tickets to institutional investors, angels, & venture scouts with a proven track record. If you'd like to access our database of promising startups or provide mentorship support to our best startups, please fill out this short Investor Application Form, & our team will contact you.  Want to Pitch? A limited number of founders will have the opportunity to pitch their startup or business to a panel of investors & experts. 4-6 selected founders will pitch their startup, followed by a short Q&A where participants can ask questions & share feedback. Apply by filling out the Pitch Application Form & sending us your pitch deck. Spots are limited, & we select founders in advance. To maintain high-quality pitches, you are required to present with a pitch deck. We will share our pitching guide and, if you'd like, coach you so you're fully prepared for pitch night.  The best startups will be featured across our social media & included in our investor newsletter. Requirements for attendees: Dress code: smart casual. Bring good energy.  Join our event & secure your ticket today! About us: Startup Valley is a global event organizer hosting pitch nights in 25 cities since 2023. Since then, we have hosted 850 events for 40,000 attendees. Over these years, we connected countless outstanding early-stage startups to serious investors, & we are not planning to stop. We maintain strategic partnerships with VC funds in the US, Europe, & Asia to support our community. Do you have a question, a partnership proposal, or want to clarify something? Reach us at hello@startupvalley.club Agenda 18:00-18:30 - Registration: Guests register, receive badges, & event programs. This is an opportunity for casual networking, making first connections, & preparing for the event. 18:30-19:00 - Event Kickoff & Interactive Networking: Official welcome from the organizers with a brief overview of the event goals & schedule. Interactive networking session to connect with key contacts. 19:00-19:50 - Startup Pitch Session: Startups present their projects to investors & experts. Each team has 5 minutes to pitch, covering the project's core idea, business model, & target market. 19:50-21:00 - Chill & Networking: Participants enjoy casual conversations with investors, discuss collaboration opportunities, & exchange ideas over refreshments. FAQ Can I pitch? Yes! To pitch, please purchase a Pitch Ticket & fill out the Pitch Application Form. We will contact you to discuss & approve your pitch. The pitch duration is 5 minutes. You will also have some time to answer questions from the audience. How does the pitch go? Selected founders present on stage to the audience & the investors in the room. You get 5 minutes to pitch your idea, business model, target market, & investment ask, followed by a short Q&A. The best startups are featured across our social media channels & in the investor newsletter. Who will I meet? Founders, angel investors, VC partners, venture scouts, AI experts, engineers, operators, marketing & sales experts, & international entrepreneurs from across Europe, Asia, & the US. Do investors get free tickets? Yes! Please apply above or email hello@startupvalley.club, & we will issue a complimentary ticket for you & your team. Can I request a refund? Yes. Refunds are available if requested at least 1 day before the event start time. Please submit the refund request on the platform where you purchased your ticket, or email us at hello@startupvalley.club

events.name: Climate Scaling Summit
events.description: The true entry points for startups working with government Join LACI at BATWorks & The Trust for Governors Island for a Climate Scaling Summit focused on one critical inflection point: how climate startups break into government as a customer, regulator, & partner. Securing contracts with the government can feel opaque to founders, but true entry points exist even if they are not always obvious to a first-time founder. This session demystifies how startups can work with government agencies & offers a valuable opportunity for founders to ask agencies & entities for feedback, technical support, & opportunities to scale. The morning opens with a fireside chat/panel, followed by five hands-on workshops covering: LegislationPermitting & CodePilot KPIs for Government AgenciesCapital Projects & Public-Private DevelopmentEducation & Workforce This is the final of four Climate Scaling Summits hosted by LACI at BATWorks in 2026, all under the theme of accelerating commercialization of clean energy innovation in NY by focusing on common problems faced by startups after the pilot stage. About LACI & The Trust for Governors Island LACI has deployed $25M in cleantech pilots over the past four years, from first commercial deployments to the nation's first zero-emissions delivery zone & is now supercharging the Pilots at BAT program & deeper deployment of the LACI Cleantech Debt Fund.  The Trust for Governors Island's Climate Piloting Program offers early-stage companies & innovators the opportunity to test & scale climate products & services in a real-world environment. Since its launch in 2023, the program has advanced projects in living shorelines, clean water, circular economy, buildings, energy, air quality, & urban agriculture-opening doors to new customers, suppliers, talent, investors, & public agency partnerships. The program is a core initiative of the Trust's Center for Climate Solutions, an initiative dedicated to accelerating equitable climate solutions for cities on Governors Island. Visit www.govisland.org/climate to learn more.

events.name: Prototyping In Public - Where Art & Science Get Tested On Gallery Floor
events.description: What if a museum ran like a lab, with the experiment still in progress? Ann Neumann is Director of Galleries & Exhibitions at the MIT Museum. Her question for the evening: can a museum serve as infrastructure for public experimentation, a place where visitors take part in the work rather than just walk through it? If you build products, run pilots, or spend your days deciding what's ready to put in front of real people, this is a look at how one of the best-known science museums handles prototyping in public. In collaboration with the National Arts Club & its Art & Technology Committee, Ann will walk through the interactive projects she's shepherded at the MIT Museum. Each one works as a prototype for engaging the public with technologies like CRISPR, machine learning, & sensory neuroscience. Reserve your spot & arrive early. Space is limited. Founded in 1898, the National Arts Club is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit with a mission to stimulate, foster, & promote public interest in the arts & to educate the American people in the fine arts. Annually, the Club offers more than 150 free programs-both in-person & virtually-to the public, including exhibitions, theatrical & musical performances, lectures, & readings, attracting an audience of over 30,000 in-person visitors & thousands more online.

events.name: AI & Future Of Community
events.description: At a moment when loneliness, social isolation, & declining trust are contributing to a growing crisis of community, artificial intelligence is rapidly changing how we communicate & connect with one another. Can AI help strengthen human connection, or could it deepen the forces pulling us apart? Pioneering AI researcher David Blei, Central Synagogue Senior Rabbi Angela Buchdahl, & technologist Jamie Metzl - author of The AI Ten Commandments - talk to constitutional scholar Noah Feldman in a wide-ranging conversation exploring one of the defining questions of our age. Artificial intelligence is transforming our world at breathtaking speed. It promises extraordinary breakthroughs in medicine, science, education, & human creativity while raising profound questions about truth, justice, freedom, meaning, & the future of our civilization. Can these technologies help us become not only more productive, but wiser, more compassionate, & more ethical? What values should guide the creation of increasingly powerful intelligent systems, & what choices must we make today to shape the future we want? Representing wide-ranging, divergent viewpoints on this transformative technology, Blei, Buchdahl, Metzl, & Feldman gather to explore the legal, ethical, philosophical, scientific, & spiritual dimensions of how AI stands to change our world. Can intelligent machines help us become more ethical? How should democratic societies govern increasingly powerful AI systems? Most importantly, what can we do today to ensure that AI strengthens, rather than diminishes, our communities? Join us for a timely conversation offering fresh insight into the choices that are shaping the future of humanity. Copies of The AI Ten Commandments: A New Moral Code for Humanity by Jamie Metzl, To Be a Jew Today by Noah Feldman, & Heart of a Stranger: An Unlikely Rabbi's Story of Faith, Identity, & Belonging by Rabbi Angela Buchdahl will be available for purchase; the authors will sign books following the program. An initiative of the 92NY Belfer Center for Innovation & Social Impact.

At a moment when loneliness, social isolation, & declining trust are contributing to a growing crisis of community, artificial intelligence is rapidly changing how we communicate & connect with one another. Can AI help strengthen human connection, or could it deepen the forces pulling us apart? Pioneering AI researcher David Blei, Central Synagogue Senior Rabbi Angela Buchdahl, & technologist Jamie Metzl - author of The AI Ten Commandments - talk to constitutional scholar Noah Feldman in a wide-ranging conversation exploring one of the defining questions of our age. Artificial intelligence is transforming our world at breathtaking speed. It promises extraordinary breakthroughs in medicine, science, education, & human creativity while raising profound questions about truth, justice, freedom, meaning, & the future of our civilization. Can these technologies help us become not only more productive, but wiser, more compassionate, & more ethical? What values should guide the creation of increasingly powerful intelligent systems, & what choices must we make today to shape the future we want? Representing wide-ranging, divergent viewpoints on this transformative technology, Blei, Buchdahl, Metzl, & Feldman gather to explore the legal, ethical, philosophical, scientific, & spiritual dimensions of how AI stands to change our world. Can intelligent machines help us become more ethical? How should democratic societies govern increasingly powerful AI systems? Most importantly, what can we do today to ensure that AI strengthens, rather than diminishes, our communities? Join us for a timely conversation offering fresh insight into the choices that are shaping the future of humanity. Copies of The AI Ten Commandments: A New Moral Code for Humanity by Jamie Metzl, To Be a Jew Today by Noah Feldman, & Heart of a Stranger: An Unlikely Rabbi's Story of Faith, Identity, & Belonging by Rabbi Angela Buchdahl will be available for purchase; the authors will sign books following the program. An initiative of the 92NY Belfer Center for Innovation & Social Impact.

events.name: Ugly Talk: CPG Founders What Worked, What Didn't & The 2027 Outlook
events.description: A bigger order can leave you with a smaller margin. That is an ugly way to learn what growth costs. CPG founders will unpack the calls shaping their brands in 2026. The channels that moved product. The partners that mattered. The pivots they had to make. Bring the decisions you are still wrestling with. Hear what these founders are changing as they finish Q4 & plan for 2027.  Why you should be in this room.Hear which channels moved product & which ate margin. Learn what founders wish they had asked before choosing a co-packer or distributor. Explore where food service & alternative distribution could fit your brand. Hear how founders responded when their customers, markets, or plans changed. Pressure-test your 2027 assumptions against what these founders are seeing in 2026.  What's on the table.Production & partners. Refining the recipe, choosing co-manufacturers, & finding partners who deliver what they promise. Distribution & margin. Which channels earned their place, which disappointed, & what founders changed in response. Finding the customer. What urban & suburban markets taught founders about who actually buys their products. Food service & other routes. Where founders are looking beyond familiar shelves to move product. The 2027 calls. Which trends held up, which missed, & what founders are carrying into next year.  Featured speakers.Liv Truesdell - Founder, FROST Buttercream Liv Truesdell started her career in consumer investment banking, working with food & beverage companies, which ultimately led her to launch FROST Buttercream. FROST is an all-natural Italian Meringue Buttercream made with real butter & egg whites, with ~57% less sugar than a leading buttercream & no palm oils, artificial dyes or preservatives. After hundreds of iterations, Liv created a new premium, refrigerated frosting segment in a category unchanged for ~71 years. FROST launched in NY/NJ retail in 2025, has since expanded across the country, & won the Startup CPG Shelfie Award within its first six months. Glenn Johnson - Marketing Consultant/Fractional CMO As a fractional CMO, Glenn Johnson works on a scalable basis with founders who are tired of bad execution, broken strategies, & agencies that just don't get it. Whether launching from scratch or fixing a brand, packaging, & positioning that fails to translate, Glenn steps in to repair what's broken & build what's next. Operating as Chief Storyteller, Creative Director, & Brand Strategist, he bridges high-level strategy with hands-on execution. From naming, logo design, & packaging to pricing architecture & true ICP targeting, Glenn nails how your brand looks, feels, & scales. A former Madison Avenue VP/Creative Director specializing in luxury & bespoke audiences, Glenn is the trusted sounding board founders rely on to turn complex ideas into scalable brand equity. Moderating Ugly Talks for me is about unpacking the messy truths & hard lessons of entrepreneurship-sharing insights in an engaged & entertaining way.  Who's getting in.Food & beverage founders building in crowded categories. Early-stage CPG founders moving from commercial kitchens to co-manufacturing. Operators working through production, distribution, pricing, & margin decisions. Buyers & investors who want to understand what helps a brand move product & stay in business.  About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough "aha!" moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons & insights. With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami, we've built a vibrant community of thousands of founders & industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape. Official Website: UglyTalk.com  Important Notice for Ugly Talk AttendeesAdmission & Confirmation Attendance is by approval only. Approved guests will receive a confirmation email along with a calendar invite. Invitations are non-transferable. Additional event details will be shared as the event approaches. Code of Conduct By attending, you agree to: Maintain respect & professionalism, adhering to all venue rules, policies, & applicable laws. Refrain from harassment, discrimination, unwelcome sexual advances (verbal or physical), intimidation, or inappropriate photography/recording. Report any violations to the event hosts immediately. Violations may result in immediate removal from the event & exclusion from future invitations. Liability & Risk Participation is voluntary & at your own risk. events.name: Silicon Alley Hack | Build Cool Hardware
events.description: Everyone & their grandma is hosting a hackathon. This is the one where you build something physical. Silicon Alley Hack is a one-day, in-person sprint for builders who'd rather solder than ship a vibe-coded app. Microcontrollers. Sensors. Connected devices. Real hardware that runs in the real world & has to work when we plug it in on stage. Application-based. Teams of 4. Every team gets an STM32 development board & peripherals on arrival. Bring your laptop, your wits, & your soldering instincts.  The Problem StatementSoftware ate the world & then got bored. The interesting frontier moved back to atoms - robots that navigate a room, drones that deliver, sensors that make a physical space legible to a machine. All of it runs on constrained silicon, in real time, in places where the cloud is too slow, too far, or not there at all. So that's the terrain: edge intelligence. Machines that sense the world & act on it, on-device.  The Challenge ThemeThe sealed spec will live somewhere in here: Sense  decide  act, running on-device IoT, sensors, & connected devices Physical/digital interaction - things that move, respond, or react Anything that runs on hardware, not just in a browser Constraints you can count on: You'll be working on an STM32 development board & peripherals - get familiar before you show up It has to run live. Slides don't win. Working hardware wins. First team to solve it take the prizes. This is a race, not a showcase.  What to ExpectA live race-to-win challenge dropped at kickoff An STM32 dev kit + peripherals for every team, free 5 hours of focused build time Team formation on-site, or come with your crew Breakfast & lunch provided Exciting prizes for the winning A room full of NYC's hardware people - embedded engineers, drone builders, robotics founders, spatial-data folks  Schedule10:00 - 11:00 AM - Doors open. Breakfast, networking mixer, team formation. 11:00 - 11:30 AM - Partner intros, Root Access demo, challenge drop, rules & judging criteria. 11:30 AM - 4:30 PM - Build sprint. Lunch provided. Clock does not stop. 4:30 - 5:15 PM - Live hardware demos to the judges. 5:15 - 6:00 PM - Photos & Mixer.  PrizesA mix of cash, credits, & perks for the winning team. Sponsors are getting locked in - full breakdown announced before doors.  Who Should AttendEmbedded & firmware engineers Robotics, drone, & hardware builders EE / CE students & anyone who's ever blown up a dev board Founders building physical products Software engineers who want to get their hands on real silicon Anyone curious, ambitious, & hands-on  Sponsors[Sponsor TBD - reach out to somyag00@gmail.com to sponsor]  Hosts & PartnersSomya Gupta - The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Pulse NYC AI - A community, incubator, & venture fund built for founders, researchers, & technologists shaping the future of AI in New York City. ConnNext - A next-gen mobile app & community built for career growth.

events.name: Six Math Essentials w/ Terence Tao
events.description: Book Launch & Conversation with Janna Levin Widely regarded as the world's greatest living mathematician, Fields Medalist Terence Tao approaches mathematics as a sublime art-a quiet, rigorous effort to map the hidden scaffolding of reality. To mark the publication of his first popular book, Six Math Essentials, join us for an evening with Tao in conversation with Pioneer Works Director of Sciences Janna Levin. Tracing the central pillars of his book-from algebra as abstraction & geometry beyond sight, to navigating uncertainty & the mathematics of change-they will reveal math not as obscure magic, but as a deeply creative, interconnected way of thinking. Often referred to as the Mozart of mathematics, Tao will also explore how AI is transforming his own practice, the frontier of research, & our collective future. Together, we will consider what becomes of human intuition & creativity when the tools of thought are no longer uniquely human-and whether the true beauty of math lies not in the answers we find, but in the human mind reaching for them. Tao will sign copies of Six Math Essentials following the conversation, with books available for purchase on site. (Unable to attend? Order a signed copy here.) Please note that seating is limited & will be available on a first-come, first-served basis.   About the speakersTerence Tao is an Australian-American professor of mathematics at UCLA whose work focuses primarily on harmonic analysis, partial differential equations, combinatorics, & analytic number theory. The recipient of a Fields Medal, a MacArthur Genius Grant, & a Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics, among many other accolades, he is one of the most decorated & prolific mathematicians working today. Tao is the author of several academic books including Solving Mathematical Problems: A Personal Perspective & Additive Combinatorics, as well as his first popular math book, Six Math Essentials. He lives in Los Angeles. Janna Levin is the Claire Tow Professor of physics & astronomy at Barnard College of Columbia University. A Guggenheim Fellow, she has contributed to our understanding of black holes, extra dimensions, & cosmology. She is the founding director of sciences at Pioneer Works & the founding editor-in-chief of the magazine Pioneer Works Broadcast. She often contributes to news, documentaries, & radio, including as the presenter of the NOVA feature Black Hole Apocalypse on PBS & as a contributor to CBS, CNN, BBC, & NBC. She has authored books on black holes & the universe-Black Hole Blues, How the Universe Got its Spots, & Black Hole Survival Guide-as well as a PEN award-winning novel, A Madman Dreams of Turing Machines. You can find her current writings in Higher Dimensions. This program is funded by the Simons Foundation International & administered by the Simons Foundation's Science, Society & Culture division.

events.name: The AI Briefing By Startup Grind: Who Owns The Data Layer Behind Enterprise AI
events.description: The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise.  This month's source: The Formula for Agentic AI Value: Applied AI Index 2026 (Boston Consulting Group - Sep 2026) Secondary sources: 5 Emerging Trends in Enterprise Data & AI (The Modern Data Company - Aug 2026) Agentic context layers (VentureBeat Intelligence - Oct 2026) Most of the money behind enterprise AI no longer runs through IT. BCG surveyed 1,330 CxOs & senior executives. AI spending has more than tripled, to 3.3% of revenue, & 2.8 points of it sit outside the enterprise IT budget. Business units generate about two-thirds of the value AI creates. So who owns the data their agents run on? BCG says the gap between leaders & everyone else has moved up the stack, to whether a company's data is current, consistently defined, trustworthy, & managed with clear ownership. It tells companies to keep their definitions, business rules & decision logic in a layer they control & could move to another vendor. VentureBeat's August survey points the other way. 98% of companies running retrieval in production use at least one system someone else built, & 2% name building & owning their context layer as their likely direction. 64% have already caught an AI agent giving a confidently wrong answer because of their own company's data.  The Mission: Deciding who owns the definitions, rules & context your AI runs on This series has spent the year on readiness: how fast enterprises adopted, where leadership's confidence outran results, how governance fell behind agents, & whether the workforce was ready. October's discussion turned to a question none of those sessions answered: who owns the data layer? We'll test BCG's advice against what data teams report from the inside. 61% call a reliable context layer critical for AI agents, & 16% engineer one on purpose.  The Format: The numbers: BCG's spending & ownership data, & where a self-reported executive survey stops being evidence. Cross-pollinated debate: Who owns it in your org? IT, the data team, the business unit paying for the agent, or the model vendor whose stack holds the context. The semantic layer problem: In VentureBeat's survey, companies running or building a semantic layer were about twice as likely to report a confidently wrong agent answer (78% vs. 37%). We'll work through why, & what it means for anyone about to fund one.  Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: See where AI budgets & accountability sit at the 7.5% of companies BCG calls future-built (all of them have clear ownership of the AI agenda), & decide whose name goes on the data layer before a vendor's does. Founders & Builders: Hear what buyers mean when they ask about lock-in. 37% of VentureBeat's respondents plan to keep standalone tools alongside the model, & 22% expect to consolidate onto one model provider's stack. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Compare notes on the work underneath. 46% of respondents say their teams spend more than a quarter of their time maintaining & integrating tools, & 8.4% say the data feeding their AI is trustworthy enough for production.  The Prep: This is a working session, not a lecture. Read the report here. Bring one wrong answer your AI gave & where the bad data came from.

events.name: Alpha Agentic Economy Summit
events.description: The Alpha Agentic Economy Summit is the gathering for leaders building the agentic enterprise & those accountable for its decisions. On November 6, 2026, at Nasdaq MarketSite in New York City, Alpha brings together board directors, management teams, investors, & technology leaders to address a defining challenge: enterprises are delegating authority to AI faster than their governance can adapt. AI agents are already executing transactions, writing & deploying code, & making operational decisions between board meetings. As their authority expands, so does the exposure: financial loss, operational disruption, legal liability, & reputational damage. Boards need to understand where that authority sits, how it is controlled, & what evidence demonstrates that oversight is working. The Summit connects the boardroom with the people shaping this shift. Confirmed speakers include Gary Vaynerchuk, Chairman of VaynerX; Stacy Brown-Philpot, Founder & Managing Partner of Cherryrock Capital; Ann Miura-Ko, Co-Founding Partner of Floodgate; Laura Desmond, CEO of Smartly; Al Zollar, board director at BNY, IBM, & Nasdaq; & Madhu Muthukumar, Chief Product Officer of SoFi. They join leaders including Navrina Singh of Credo AI, Philip Rathle of Neo4j, Wasim Khaled of Blackbird.AI, Ned Koh of Aaru, Dara Ladjevardian of Delphi, Bri Treece of Fathom, & Andrew Yang of Noble Mobile. alpha.ac These leaders bring perspectives across enterprise deployment, venture investment, corporate oversight, AI governance, & the technologies changing how companies operate. Directors with oversight responsibility & executives with execution responsibility will engage directly with the builders & investors advancing the agentic economy. Attendance is curated to keep the room senior, focused, & conducive to substantive conversation. Working conversations take place under the Chatham House Rule, creating space for candid discussion of architectures, incidents, controls, & consequential decisions. Sessions give speakers time to examine the material in depth. Questions continue during deliberate intermissions, where delegates can connect directly with speakers & peers in smaller conversations. The format is built for practical outcomes. There are no vendor pitches. The focus is on real systems, delegated authority, & the decisions leaders must make: what agents may do, who owns their actions, when humans must intervene, & how performance & accountability can be verified. Delegates leave with a clearer view of where agents are entering the enterprise, relationships with the people shaping that transition, & concrete priorities for their next board, committee, or management meeting. In the agentic economy, every decision to delegate authority is a governance decision. Growth depends on getting it right. Governance is Alpha.

events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: Did Maha Maha?
events.description: Has the MAHA movement made Americans healthier than the establishment? Americans spend more on healthcare than anyone else in the world. Yet we have soaring rates of obesity, diabetes, & chronic disease. So is the medical establishment failing us? And is MAHA actually doing any better? RFK's MAHA movement has put ultra-processed foods, environmental toxins, & chronic disease at the center of the national conversation. Supporters say it's finally challenging a healthcare system that profits from treating illness instead of preventing it. Critics say it's undermining trust in vaccines, established science, & the institutions responsible for keeping Americans healthy. So who's right? Is MAHA forcing a long-overdue reckoning with a broken healthcare system? Or is it replacing imperfect science with something far more dangerous? Kerry Semle is a biomedical engineer, former medical technology executive, & women's health advocate with 15 years of experience in medical devices & diagnostics. She's advocated for greater investment in women's health research & improved access to care. Emily Kaplan is the CEO & co-founder of the Broken Science Initiative, an organization challenging the scientific establishment & questioning how medical research is conducted, evaluated, & trusted. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

events.description: A free, two-hour workshop for founders who want to build a stronger investor pitch & deliver it with confidence.You know your business. You know the opportunity. Cut unnecessary information, close narrative gaps, & make the value easier to grasp. 2. Deliver it with confidence & credibilityA strong deck isn't enough. Learn to make a strong first impression, create buy-in, use pace & pauses to make key numbers land, stress the words that carry value, & steady your voice under pressure. Use your voice to communicate with the composure & authority investors expect. 3. Test & refine your pitchPitch in front of others & discover where the room leans in, where you lose them, & what needs to change. Use live feedback to tighten your messaging & delivery. 4. Cut unnecessary information, close narrative gaps, & make the value easier to grasp. 2. Deliver it with confidence & credibilityA strong deck isn't enough. Learn to make a strong first impression, create buy-in, use pace & pauses to make key numbers land, stress the words that carry value, & steady your voice under pressure. Use your voice to communicate with the composure & authority investors expect. 3. Test & refine your pitchPitch in front of others & discover where the room leans in, where you lose them, & what needs to change. Use live feedback to tighten your messaging & delivery. 4. The live-feedback experienceEach hour includes 15 minutes of tips, first from Anthony Rose on creating compelling content, then from David Goldberg on delivering it with conviction, followed by 45 minutes of live, instructive feedback so founders can improve their pitches on the spot. What you'll leave withA sharper, more focused investor pitch A clearer understanding of your strengths & gaps Practical techniques for presenting with confidence Real-world feedback on your messaging & delivery Specific next steps for continuing to improve Greater insight into what can move an investor from listening to wanting to know more Who should attendFounders & startup leaders at different stages of the fundraising journey. Whether you're preparing to pitch for the first time or you've pitched before & know it could be stronger, the goal is the same: leave with a better pitch than the one you walked in with. Your facilitatorsAnthony Rose, CEO, SeedLegalsFounder & CEO of SeedLegals, the legaltech platform that helps startups get investment-ready, run a funding round, & handle their legals, used by over 60,000 startups. Before SeedLegals, his career spanned 3D graphics, peer-to-peer music, internet video, & social TV, including heading up BBC iPlayer. Wired Magazine's 2009 cover story called him "The Man Who Saved the BBC." David Goldberg, CEO, Prosody.center & Edge StudioFounder of Prosody.center & EdgeStudio.com, an international voiceover recording center. He has directed, coached, & trained over 10,000 celebrities, politicians, CEOs, & founders on more than 13,000 spoken-word projects over 38 years. He identifies the blind spots that hold founders back when they pitch (pacing, phrasing, wording, emphasis, tone, body language, composure, nonverbal cues), then shows the precise adjustments that change how investors experience & respond to you. DetailsWhen: Friday, October 30, 1-3pm ET, in person, Times Square, NYCCost: Free to join. Co-founders are welcome too.Capacity: Seating is limited, & registrations are approved individually. Come prepared to work on your business, test your ideas, & practice your pitch, not simply take notes.

events.name: How To Get Your Startups Finances In Order
events.description: Whether you've raised funding, started generating revenue, or are building your business, do you have a system to track where the money goes? When a co-founder pays for something personally, how is that expense recorded, approved & reimbursed? Can you see what has been paid, what is still outstanding, & where the supporting documents are? Getting your finances organised starts with the processes you use every day. In this Lunch & Learn, we'll explore how to build simple financial systems that help you manage your startup's money & understand your business as it grows. What we'll cover  Your DocumentationWhat invoices, receipts, contracts & payment records should you capture-and how can you keep them organised?  Your Financial ProcessesHow can you set up a consistent system for invoicing, payments, expense claims & founder reimbursements, so nothing gets missed or paid twice?  Your BookkeepingHow do your everyday records become reliable accounts, & what should you keep updated each month?  Your NumbersWhat can revenue, margins, profit, cash flow & runway tell you-and which numbers should you regularly review?  Your Business DecisionsHow can your numbers help you plan spending, assess pricing & decide whether you can afford your next hire?  Your Readiness for OpportunitiesHow can organised records & clear financial reports help you prepare information for tax filing, grant applications & funding conversations? This session is perfect for startup founders, entrepreneurs & early-stage teams-including those who have already raised funding-who want to establish practical financial systems & better understand their business performance. Presented by Mathura Kannan, ICAEW Chartered Accountant, Managing Director of Simply Empowering & Co-Founder of Expop, who works with businesses to set up financial processes, manage their accounting & turn their numbers into useful insights.

events.name: An UNMUTED Book Club: The 100 Years War On Palestine
events.description: READING NOT REQUIRED - just be curious! Next up: Rashid Khalidi's The Hundred Years' War on Palestine, the 2020 book that argues the Israeli-Palestinian conflict isn't simply a tragic struggle between two peoples claiming the same land, but a century-long colonial campaign against Palestinians, backed first by Britain & later by the United States. Khalidi, a Palestinian-American historian at Columbia, tells the story through six turning points, beginning with the 1917 Balfour Declaration & moving through the creation of Israel, the wars that followed, & the failures of the peace process. Drawing on historical archives & his own family's experiences, he makes a provocative argument: that Palestinians have never been negotiating on equal terms, & that understanding the conflict as a dispute between two competing national movements obscures the enormous imbalance of power between them. It's a forceful challenge to conventional accounts of Israel's founding, Zionism, & America's role in the region, & one that raises uncomfortable questions about nationalism, colonialism, & self-determination. Show up even if you only got through a chunk. We'll talk about where Khalidi's account is most convincing, where it leaves out important context, whether Zionism is best understood as a colonial movement or a national liberation movement, & what his interpretation of the past means for the possibility of peace today. UNMUTED is a discussion forum for the politically curious. Accessible. Engaging. Social. Open-minded is the name of the game. Join your people.

events.name: Is Everything Predictable - AI, Prediction Markets & Philosophy Of Foresight
events.description: In this six-week course, explore works from philosophy, cultural studies, & journalism to understand how technologies that predict the future also shape the present.The age of AI, prediction markets, & real-time data analysis brings predictive reasoning into all corners of human life. Once considered a niche academic interest area, the philosophy & politics of prediction is now relevant to everybody. Is Everything Predictable?: AI, Prediction Markets, & the Philosophy of Foresight presents scholarly material on forecasting technologies in a rigorous but highly accessible format.Drawing from a range of sources, we center scholarly texts & deeply-researched journalism that uncover the links between digital calculation, philosophical notions of time & free will, & the reality of living in an age where everything seems reducible to calculation.Guest speakers from academia & tech journalism will round out our seminar sessions, & for our final meeting, students have the option of presenting original research or creative work in an event open to the general public.SyllabusIn the early weeks of the course, we read texts from contemporary media studies & political theory that construe prediction & speculation as forms of governance. We also address probabilistic reasoning as a key feature of artificial intelligence & prediction market mechanisms, using frameworks suitable for participants without any background in STEM. As we will see, the similarities & differences between how probability works in AI versus prediction markets have much to tell us about these tools effects on everything from global warfare & the environment to creativity & personal relationships.After establishing a strong practical & theoretical foundation in AI & prediction markets, we turn to philosophical writing on the nature of freedom, self-expression, & power. These texts urge us to ask whether predictive technologies empower us with highly advanced forms of knowledge; if they inhibit us by constraining our imagination of whats possible; or if both of these outcomes might be true at once. We also read articles & listen to podcast interviews with our guest speakers in anticipation of their visits.Throughout our sessions, we examine case studies related to tech companies, specific applications, & major actors in the AI & prediction market space. The courses culminating event  a salon open to the general public  reflects our interest in connecting questions & concerns that seem highly academic to current events & everyday life. Students who choose to give presentations will participate in an additional workshop or one-on-one advising session to help them prepare. By the courses end, we will be able to navigate a world driven by predictive technologies with greater clarity, confidence, & wisdom, & to share our perspectives on them in a way that empowers those around us.Learning OutcomesConnect AI & prediction market functionalities to political & cultural affairsDevelop critical reading skills applicable to philosophy & journalismApply frameworks from the theoretical humanities to real-world developments in politics & technologyMake scholarly ideas accessible to a wide range of audiencesScholarshipsIndex scholarships are designed to benefit underrepresented groups, BIPOC members of our community, & those for whom the class price is not accessible. These need-based scholarships will go to the candidates who best demonstrate why they should be chosen for the free spot to our class. You can apply for a scholarship here.Instructor BioEmma Stamm is a writer & professor with a background in philosophy & the social study of science & technology (STS). She holds a PhD in Interdisciplinary Studies from Virginia Tech & has taught courses on the philosophy & social implications of technology at Villanova University, Virginia Tech, the Acid Horizon Research Commons, New York University, where she currently teaches for the Department of Media, Culture, & Communication. As a public-facing scholar, she has written for Vice Motherboard, Real Life Mag, & Communications of the Association for Computing Machinery, in addition to co-hosting the LEPHT HAND podcast. She is the co-founder & Executive Director of theLenox Institute for Advanced Study, which makes critical science & tech education accessible beyond academia.RefundsWe get that things come up, but we rely on headcounts to make our programs viable. events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Plan Your Best Year With AI
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back  In Person at SalesforceWe're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City and sponsored by Boldforce.This Month We Present...Plan Your Best Year With AIJoin the community for an interactive planning session to reflect on the past year, identify your biggest opportunities, and build an AI-powered roadmap for the year ahead.Before we rush into a new year with another list of goals, lets get clear about what were actually building.What worked this year? What didnt? What deserves more of your energy? And where could AI help you turn those intentions into action?For our final AI & The Culture meetup of the year, were bringing the community together for an interactive planning and reflection session designed to help you look back, think forward, and build a roadmap for what comes next.This isnt about asking AI to magically plan your life. Its about using these tools as thought partnersto help you reflect, uncover patterns, explore possibilities, make decisions, and turn big ambitions into actionable next steps.Together well explore: How to use AI to reflect on your wins, lessons, challenges, and unfinished business from the past year Prompts that help you identify opportunities you might be overlooking How to turn big goals into realistic projects, milestones, and next steps Ways to use AI as a strategic thought partner for your creative work, career, business, or personal projects How to identify where AI and automation can give you back time in the year ahead Building a personalized AI-powered roadmap you can actually use after you leave the roomAnd because this is AI & The Culture, were making space for something AI cant replace: community.Youll have an opportunity to reflect alongside other creatives, founders, educators, artists, technologists, and curious mindsto exchange ideas, share what youre building, and potentially meet the people who can help you move it forward.The goal isnt to leave with 47 resolutions.Its to leave with clarity, priorities, and a plan.Who Should Attend? Creators and content makers Filmmakers, writers, artists, and storytellers Educators and community builders Entrepreneurs, founders, and solopreneurs Marketers, strategists, and creative professionals Technologists and AI enthusiasts Anyone ready to be more intentional about what theyre building nextWhether you already have your next year mapped out or youre still staring at a blank page wondering where to begin, youre welcome here.Come Ready to BuildThis one is especially hands-on, so come prepared to participate. Bring your laptop Bring a notebook or something to write with Bring a few goals, ideas, or questions youve been thinking about for the year ahead Bring your curiosity and a willingness to shareWell be working through reflection exercises, AI prompts, and planning activities togetherso you can leave with the beginnings of a roadmap, not just another page of notes.Come ready to reflect. Come ready to plan. Come ready to build.About AI & The CultureAI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, and culture.Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams and King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, and culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, and community.Were building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI.This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture  grounded in community, focused on real-world use, and centered on learning together in the room.Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Lets build  together. About Your HostsShirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, and co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, and creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, and real-world execution.About King WilloniusKing Willonius is a creative technologist and cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, and creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, and community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable and useful  especially for creatives and innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm. Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio)#AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: Data By Design
events.description: In conversation with Shannon Mattern. P&T Knitwear is pleased to welcome Lauren Klein, Tanvi Sharma, & Silas Munro to celebrate & discuss the release of their book Data by Design, which explores how the history of data visualization holds the key to designing a more just future. They will be in conversation with Shannon Mattern, & will sign books after the talk! Doors open at 6:30pm with the talk starting closer to 7:00pm. Come early & grab a drink from the P&T Cafe! Tickets & books are available both on eventbrite & at the door. Housekeeping notes: This is a ticketed in-store event with limited amphitheater-style seating.Doors open at 6:30pm, with the talk starting around 7:00pm.Cost of a book bundle ticket reflects the total cost of the feature event book (MSRP plus tax). Each book bundle ticket guarantees ticket holders one (1) copy of the feature event book.The talk will be followed by a book signing. Books signed at P&T Knitwear events must be purchased from P&T Knitwear.If you would like a signed copy & cannot attend the event, we're happy to take your pre-order. We ship most places!About the authors:Lauren Klein is Professor of Data & Decision Sciences & English at Emory University, where she also directs the Digital Humanities Lab & the Atlanta Interdisciplinary AI Network. Her research brings together computational & critical methods to explore questions of gender, race, & justice, both in early America & today. Klein is the author (with Catherine D'Ignazio) of the award-winning Data Feminism (MIT Press, 2020), & the editor (with Matthew K. Gold) of Debates in the Digital Humanities (Univ. of Minnesota Press), among other books & papers. Her next book, Data by Design: Visualization & Power from Abolition to the Dawn of Data Science (MIT Press), will be out in October 2026.  Silas Munro is a designer, artist, writer, curator, surfer, & descendant of the Banyole people of Eastern Uganda. He founded the design studio Polymode, whose clients include MoMA, the MET, Nike, & the Hammer. Munro is the curator & author of Strikethrough: Typographic Messages of Protest at Letterform Archive & the co-curator of Reverberations: Lineages in Design History at the Ford Foundation Gallery. He contributed to W. E. B. Du Bois's Data Portraits: Visualizing Black America, & co-authored the first BIPOC-centered design history course, Black Design in America: African Americans & the African Diaspora in Graphic Design 19th-21st Century. His visual art was recently exhibited at Data Consciousness: Reframing Blackness in Contemporary Print at Print Center New York. Tanvi Sharma is a design technologist working at the intersection of data, aesthetics, & the humanities. She is currently an Art Director at Apple & co-author of Data by Design (MIT Press, 2026). She has previously worked at Pentagram, Public Policy Lab, & Spotify. She lives in Harlem, NY, with her two cats, Yuchi & Bubbles. More at tanvi.network.   About the moderator:Shannon Mattern is the Director of Creative Research at the Metropolitan New York Library Council, a state-founded, member-supported non-profit linking hundreds of libraries & archives across the city. Previously, she held tenured full professorships in media studies, anthropology, & art history at The New School & the University of Pennsylvania. She is the author of four books, the (co-)editor of six collections, & the author of over 100 articles & chapters about urban technology, knowledge infrastructures, maps, maintenance, data art, & other heterogenous subjects. She was the 2025 Kluge Chair in Modern Culture at the Library of Congress & the 2025 Design Indexer in residence at the Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum. You can find her at wordsinspace.net.

events.name: Responsible Tech Summit - Embedding Accountability AI Era
events.description: At a time when artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping society, the conversation is shifting from broad principles to real-world accountability. The 2026 summit will explore the theme of Principles to Power: Embedding Accountability in the AI Era. For years, the Responsible Tech field has been guided by ethical frameworks, voluntary commitments, & emerging standards. Today, the challenge is clear: how do we translate those ideas into systems of governance, oversight, & design that ensure innovation does not come at the expense of safety, rights, or trust? The Responsible Tech Summit is designed as a curated convening for 375 leaders that helps align & shape the direction of the movement. Participants will include global governance leaders, AI researchers, industry practitioners, policy experts, civil society advocates, & philanthropic leaders who are building the infrastructure of accountability for the digital age. Through keynotes, panels, & conversations, attendees will explore topics such as accountability by design, platform oversight, youth online safety, the Responsible Tech economy, & the evolving global regulatory landscape. All ticket proceeds fund free resources & services for the Responsible Tech community that our organization provides. Can't make it in person? The event will be livestreamed for free on All Tech Is Human's YouTube page, where recordings will also be available afterward. - Are you a journalist looking to potentially cover the Responsible Tech Summit? Reach out to Hello@AllTechIsHuman.org. Speakers for the Responsible Tech Summit 2026 Camille Francois - President, ROOST Eli Pariser - Co-Director, New_ Public Cathy O'Neil, Founder, Author, Mathematician & Data Scientist, O'Neil Risk Consulting & Algorithmic Auditing Rumman Chowdhury, CEO, Humane Intelligence PBC Alex Bores, Assembly Member, New York City's 73rd District Beth Goldberg, Founding Executive Director of Humanity AI Sinead Bovell, Founder, WAYE Alexis Wales, Chief Information Security Officer, GitHub Alison Lee, Chief R&D Officer, The Rithm Project Amanda Craig, General Manager of Responsible AI Public Policy, Microsoft Anya Schiffrin, Director, Media Program, Columbia University (SIPA) Carrie Varoquiers, Chief Impact Officer, Workday Joshua Elder, Senior Vice President & Head of Grantmaking, Siegel Family Endowment Julie Cordua, CEO, Thorn Fernanda Del Castillo, Director of AI Governance, Mastercard Kathy Pham, Faculty & Senior Fellow, Product & Responsible AI, Harvard University Kristin Hansen, Executive Director, Civic Health Project J. Trevor Hughes, President & CEO of IAPP Shreya Singh Hernndez, Senior Manager, Aspen Digital, The Aspen Institute Melanie Plaza, Chief Technology Officer, AE Studio Courtney Radsch, Director of the Center for Media & Digital Governance, Open Markets Institute; Fellow, Brookings Institution Andrew Rasiej, Founder, Civic Hall Clement Wolf, Director, Responsible AI Strategy, Google Hale Sirin, Program Scientist, Schmidt Sciences AI & Advanced Computing Institute Jeff Collins, Director of Trust & Safety, Amazon Web Services Alisar Mustafa, Head of AI Safety, Duco Experts   Agenda10:00 - 11:00 am ET | Check-in & Networking 11:00 - 11:10 am | Welcome remarks 11:15 - 11:45 am | Panel: Beyond Benchmarks: Turning Evaluations into Enforceable Standards 11:50 - 12:00 pm | Lightning talk 12:05 - 12:35 pm | Panel: Safety by Design: Accountability at the Intersection of AI, Industry, & Advocacy 12:40 - 1:40 pm | Lunch 1:45 - 2:05 pm | Fireside Chat: Open-Source, Open Questions: Transparency in the Age of AI 2:10 - 2:40 pm | Panel: Shared Risk, Shared Responsibility: Rethinking Responsible AI Governance 2:45 - 3:05 pm | Fireside Chat: Alignment in Practice: Building AI That Wants to be Good 3:05 - 3:30 pm | Networking break 3:30 - 4:00 pm | Panel: Trust as Strategy & the Fight Against AI-Enabled Fraud 4:05 - 4:15 pm | Keynote 4:15 - 4:25 pm | Lightning Talk 4:30 - 5:00 pm | Panel: Rebuilding the Commons: Community & Pluralism in the AI Era 5:05 - 5:25 pm | Fireside Chat: Looking Back to Look Ahead: Co-Designing AI After a Decade of Tech Lessons 5:25 - 5:30 pm | Closing remarks *See the full agenda & bios of our speakers here.   Sponsors for the Responsible Tech Summit 2026Special thanks to our strategic partners, Columbia World Projects, Forum One, & Highspring, for helping bring this critical conversation to life. WorkdayWorkday operates at the heart of the enterprise - HR, finance, & IT - where the margin for error is effectively zero. By tightly coupling AI with the context, guardrails, & trusted processes that run the business, Workday goes beyond AI that assists work to agents that do the work & drive measurable outcomes. More than 11,500 organizations worldwide, including more than 65% of the Fortune 500, trust Workday to deliver. MastercardMastercard is a global technology company in the payments industry, connecting consumers, financial institutions, merchants, & governments in more than 200 countries & territories. The company is committed to building a sustainable, inclusive digital economy that benefits everyone, everywhere. PinterestPinterest is a visual search & discovery platform where people find inspiration, curate ideas & shop products - all in a positive place online. Headquartered in San Francisco, Pinterest has over 600 million monthly active users worldwide. MicrosoftMicrosoft is a global technology leader empowering every person & organization on the planet to achieve more through its platforms & productivity tools. The company is committed to advancing responsible AI & ensuring emerging technologies are developed & deployed safely & ethically. Siegel Family EndowmentSiegel Family Endowment takes an inquiry-driven approach to grantmaking, informed by the scientific method. As technology reshapes society, we fund organizations asking critical questions about its impact on learning, work, & infrastructure. Founded in 2011 by David Siegel, co-founder & co-chairman of Two Sigma, we advance technology in the public interest, supporting research & initiatives that imagine a more inclusive, resilient technology-driven society. AE StudioAE Studio is an applied AI & AI alignment company that builds software products for clients while advancing research on making advanced AI systems safe & beneficial. Its recent work with Anthropic, GRAM, trains dangerous knowledge into removable modules so it can be stripped from a model before release. AE Studio reinvests its commercial success into neglected approaches to AI alignment research. Learn more at ae.studio. GoogleGoogle's mission is to organize the world's information & make it universally accessible & useful. As a leader in AI & computing, the company is focused on developing technology responsibly to benefit people & society. Kapor FoundationThe Kapor Foundation works at the intersection of racial equity & technology to expand access to K-12 computer science & postsecondary tech pathways, improve tech accountability & worker protections, & increase investments in infrastructure & innovation. We advocate for policy changes, build the capacity of partners, conduct research, support partners through grantmaking, & invest in entrepreneurship & VC. We believe that when technology includes diverse perspectives & is harnessed to address societal challenges, we can transform the tech ecosystem for Black, Latine, & Native communities, & society as a whole. Kapor Foundation works collectively with the Kapor Center family of organizations, Kapor Capital, & SMASH to reimagine & reconstruct a more inclusive & equitable technology sector. Check out Kapor Foundation's Responsible AI Principles for Advancing a More Equitable Innovation Future. IAPPThe IAPP is a policy-neutral, not-for-profit association founded in 2000 with a mission to define, promote & improve the professions of privacy, AI governance & digital responsibility globally. Civic Health ProjectCivic Health Project is a nonpartisan nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing scalable solutions to the dangerous divisions that threaten American democracy. Since our founding in 2019, we have supported more than 75 academic researchers, grassroots practitioners, creatives, & technologists who are helping reduce polarization, strengthen civic norms, & foster social cohesion. Today, Civic Health Project focuses primarily on exploring the vast potential of promising new technologies to help resolve conflict, improve civil discourse & deliberation, foster social cohesion, & uphold societal norms. Normsy.ai, our flagship in-house project, brings this mission to life. It identifies toxic content in real time & equips users to respond with respectful, trust-building messages grounded in social science & supported by artificial intelligence. We are also part of the initiative The Forum, a new model for civic leadership at a time when trust is low, division is high, & the need for credible, citizen-led solutions has never been greater. GitHubGitHub is the world's leading platform for agentic software development - powered by Copilot to build, scale, & deliver secure software. Over 225 million developers, including more than 90% of the Fortune 100 companies, use GitHub to collaborate, & more than 140,000 organizations have adopted GitHub Copilot. CinderCinder is the industry's first Trust & Safety operations platform to help organizations combat Internetabuse at scale. We provide Trust & Safety teams with a single system to manage complex integrityoperations & investigations to create a safe environment for their users. Interested in sponsoring our summit or forming a strategic partnership? Email us at hello@alltechishuman.org.   About All Tech Is HumanAll Tech Is Human is the coordination layer & connective tissue for the Responsible Tech ecosystem. By uniting key individuals across civil society, government, industry, academia, & philanthropy, we provide a sandbox for solution-building & socialization to influence key levers of change. We specialize in taking a whole-of-ecosystem approach to tackling thorny tech & society issues, shaping the Responsible Tech movement, & ensuring that our tech future is aligned with the public interest. We are the premier gathering for the Responsible Tech community, convening thousands of people globally. We curate the defining resource for the movement, the Responsible Tech Guide, used by academia, industry, civil society, & policy professionals. We have the largest online community for the Responsible Tech movement hosted on Slack with over 15,000 members across 117 countries. We have the go-to job board for the community, our curated Responsible Tech Job Board & related talent pool. Refund Policy & Billing DetailsRefund requests made before October 1 at 5:00 pm ET are subject to a $50 administrative fee. Refund requests made between October 2 & the final refund deadline of October 16 at 5:00 pm ET face a late cancellation fee of $100. No refunds or ticket transfers are permitted after October 16. Please note: credit card statements for this purchase will show a charge from "Social Science Research Council (SSRC)," All Tech Is Human's fiscal sponsor.

Founded in 2011 by David Siegel, co-founder & co-chairman of Two Sigma, we advance technology in the public interest, supporting research & initiatives that imagine a more inclusive, resilient technology-driven society. AE StudioAE Studio is an applied AI & AI alignment company that builds software products for clients while advancing research on making advanced AI systems safe & beneficial. Its recent work with Anthropic, GRAM, trains dangerous knowledge into removable modules so it can be stripped from a model before release. AE Studio reinvests its commercial success into neglected approaches to AI alignment research. Learn more at ae.studio. GoogleGoogle's mission is to organize the world's information & make it universally accessible & useful. As a leader in AI & computing, the company is focused on developing technology responsibly to benefit people & society. Kapor FoundationThe Kapor Foundation works at the intersection of racial equity & technology to expand access to K-12 computer science & postsecondary tech pathways, improve tech accountability & worker protections, & increase investments in infrastructure & innovation. We advocate for policy changes, build the capacity of partners, conduct research, support partners through grantmaking, & invest in entrepreneurship & VC. We believe that when technology includes diverse perspectives & is harnessed to address societal challenges, we can transform the tech ecosystem for Black, Latine, & Native communities, & society as a whole. Kapor Foundation works collectively with the Kapor Center family of organizations, Kapor Capital, & SMASH to reimagine & reconstruct a more inclusive & equitable technology sector. Check out Kapor Foundation's Responsible AI Principles for Advancing a More Equitable Innovation Future. IAPPThe IAPP is a policy-neutral, not-for-profit association founded in 2000 with a mission to define, promote & improve the professions of privacy, AI governance & digital responsibility globally. Civic Health ProjectCivic Health Project is a nonpartisan nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing scalable solutions to the dangerous divisions that threaten American democracy. Since our founding in 2019, we have supported more than 75 academic researchers, grassroots practitioners, creatives, & technologists who are helping reduce polarization, strengthen civic norms, & foster social cohesion. Today, Civic Health Project focuses primarily on exploring the vast potential of promising new technologies to help resolve conflict, improve civil discourse & deliberation, foster social cohesion, & uphold societal norms. Normsy.ai, our flagship in-house project, brings this mission to life. It identifies toxic content in real time & equips users to respond with respectful, trust-building messages grounded in social science & supported by artificial intelligence. We are also part of the initiative The Forum, a new model for civic leadership at a time when trust is low, division is high, & the need for credible, citizen-led solutions has never been greater. GitHubGitHub is the world's leading platform for agentic software development - powered by Copilot to build, scale, & deliver secure software. Over 225 million developers, including more than 90% of the Fortune 100 companies, use GitHub to collaborate, & more than 140,000 organizations have adopted GitHub Copilot. CinderCinder is the industry's first Trust & Safety operations platform to help organizations combat Internetabuse at scale. Email us at hello@alltechishuman.org.   About All Tech Is HumanAll Tech Is Human is the coordination layer & connective tissue for the Responsible Tech ecosystem. By uniting key individuals across civil society, government, industry, academia, & philanthropy, we provide a sandbox for solution-building & socialization to influence key levers of change. We specialize in taking a whole-of-ecosystem approach to tackling thorny tech & society issues, shaping the Responsible Tech movement, & ensuring that our tech future is aligned with the public interest. We are the premier gathering for the Responsible Tech community, convening thousands of people globally. We curate the defining resource for the movement, the Responsible Tech Guide, used by academia, industry, civil society, & policy professionals. We have the largest online community for the Responsible Tech movement hosted on Slack with over 15,000 members across 117 countries. We have the go-to job board for the community, our curated Responsible Tech Job Board & related talent pool. Refund Policy & Billing DetailsRefund requests made before October 1 at 5:00 pm ET are subject to a $50 administrative fee. Refund requests made between October 2 & the final refund deadline of October 16 at 5:00 pm ET face a late cancellation fee of $100. events.name: Innovation in Public Mixer 5.0  Year End Capital
events.description: Edition 5.0. Theme, year end capital. The monthly room where founders, investors & operators actually get matched. Capped & curated. Everyone leaves with at least one named introduction & the framing for the conversation. November is when allocators are deploying what is left of the year & family offices are planning the next one. This edition leans toward the capital side of the network. Who we are. Propel Earth has run 100+ events & built a network of 36,000+ founders, investors, operators, & service providers across six continents. We are not an events company. We are an outcomes company that happens to use rooms. You bring the intent. We deliver the outcome. This is not a business card room. We cap it at 40-50 people & we curate it. Tell us what you are building & who you need when you register, & before you walk in we hand you at least one match: a specific person, plus the framing for the conversation. Everyone leaves having met someone who matters to what they are working on. You do not need to apply to the cohort to attend. This room is open. Tickets Early Access - $20. Limited, nearly gone.General Admission - $40.Free for Propel Private Network members. Dinner is highly encouraged - the kitchen at The Wilson is excellent. Come hungry & stay late. What Propel actually does for you 1  Innovation in Public - our GTM accelerator. For founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go-to-market: content, distribution, & more sales. Four weeks, twice a week, building in public, closing with a public showcase in front of the room. Applications open for the August cohort  Apply here 2  The Propel Private Network. Stop networking. Start getting matched. Every month we personally hand you three introductions chosen for what you need right now - someone who can pay you, hire you, or move your company forward. It works both ways: you go into the pool too. Founding rate $200/mo, first 25 members, locked for life  Claim a founding membership 3  Propel Community Coworking x Wayo Club. Come Wednesday night, then come back Thursday & build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, founded by Jason Malefakis. Wayo is a curated community workspace network where members work from premium venues alongside thoughtfully selected founders, operators, & consultants they can collaborate with, refer, hire, or do business with. Attendees typically report being 1.5 to 2x more productive than working from home or a cafe, & leave with 2 to 3 meaningful connections. Lunch is included. Register with us  Propel Community Coworking 1.0  Get a Wayo Community Workday membership  Join the Wayo Anytime waitlist 4  Featured Founder. Build your founder or service-provider profile on Propel & we will give you one additional intro on us  propel.earth/featured-founders On camera: Nik Michael of the Pivot Point podcast is shooting photography, video, & follow-up interviews with select attendees. Want to be featured, reach out to him directly. Newsletter  propelearth.beehiiv.com  Propel Earth  propel.earth  Questions, text Stephen at 516 307 6380. About The WilsonThe Wilson NYC is a popular American comfort-food restaurant & bar located in NoMad/Chelsea. While the restaurant does not hold traditional culinary stars (like Michelin), it acts as a highly-rated, frequent event space for awards shows & local hospitality honors due to its event duplex & outdoor patio. The Wilson has also been celebrated for supporting its employees through the One Fair Wage What Propel does, & what it has produced Nine ways we connect this network. Every one of these is a room we have already run. Founders & Investors. We put founders in rooms with the people who write checks. Demo Night NYC ran in front of 35+ investors. Founders x Investors Night at PhD Lounge, the Funders x Founders High Line Walk, the Harvard Club Investment Dinner, & the NYTW Pitch Competition with 800+ registrations. Every monthly mixer does the same thing at a smaller scale, which is why we cap the room & match you before you arrive. Founders & Service Providers. You tell us what you need & we match you to someone vetted who does it. Legal, tax, engineering, design, growth, operations. Our Founders Meet Providers rooms exist for exactly this, & the Propel Marketplace runs it year round. Featured provider this month is Moshe Cohen, CPA, offering a 30 minute startup tax & finance session for $120. Book a session or browse the marketplace Hiring & Talent. Our Tech Job Fair & Developer Job Fair each brought over 150 engineers & operators into the room. That now runs continuously on Propel Earth Jobs, where employers, candidates, & referrers all work in one place. Post a role or find one Product Launches. We launch products to the whole network. The ConnNext App Launch Party pulled 475 registrations, the largest event we have ever run. BECOMEFAMOUS.AI pulled 222. If you are launching something & you need a room, reply to this & we will build it. Capital & Family Office. The capital side of the network. Our Private Markets Discussion Panel drew 280 registrations & Family Office Crypto with Forum Pay brought allocators into the room. These are smaller rooms with higher stakes. See the next one Masterclasses & Info Sessions. Free, online, & taught by specialists who actually do the work. Our Social Impact Cohort Info Session drew 297 registrations. TRIIBE TALK on branding drew 157. Tax, legal, fundraising, & go to market, taught by operators. See the calendar The GTM Accelerator. Four weeks for founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go to market help: content, distribution, & more sales. You get a dedicated BDR, a custom digital asset kit, & a public showcase in front of the room. Our last cohort presented at Demo Day to 35+ investors. August applications are open & you can see how we represented the last cohort The Social Rooms. Not everything is a pitch. Foundersgiving Party & Pitch Roast drew 381 people. LABYRINTH at Hotel Chelsea drew 309. Above Fridays Rooftop Networking, Holiday Chemistry Night, & Bowling & Business. These are the rooms where relationships actually form, & they are the reason the other eight verticals work. Community Coworking. Come to the mixer on Wednesday, then come back Thursday & actually build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, coffee & lunch included. Members receive three curated introductions every month plus free entry to every mixer & select special events. $200 per month, & the first 25 founding members lock that rate for life.
