It's a direct line to the most ambitious builders, with a community that actually shows up. Link to apply for membership: Link For more info please message me 917-242-2821, dylan@thebuilderseries.co Find us here: Instagram  LinkedIn  TikTok  Facebook  X : WhatsApp Broad Channel This is the 4rd edition of our luncheon. This time, we're hosting it in an $8.5M townhouse, because we believe in high-class experiences, & incredible people. Every room has been bigger than the last. Our 2nd edition versus the 1st: Founder revenue: $90M+ a year, up from $18M+ in August. Money being raised: $197M+ across 19 founders, up from $95M+ across 14 in August. Capital already raised: $43M+, up from $35M+ in August. The investors at the table: We feature 6 investors from our network, & we always end up with more. 1st edition: We expected 6. We brought 10. 2nd edition: We expected 10. We brought 12. $2B+ combined AUM across both events. $1M average check, $100K minimum. $10M+ in live check capacity. Who this room is for To get into this room, you should to have raised at least $1M or be doing $1M+ in ARR. Our last edition averaged $3.8M+ ARR per founder. Raised your first round, onto your second, or bootstrapped to $1M or 15M ARR? You're in the right place. If you're an exited founder, LP/GP, dealmaker or capital raiser, you belong in this room too. Every investor here is from our network. We're curating this room deliberately, matching founders to the investors most likely to be a fit, & making the introduction ourselves. The goal: getting founders funded by our investor network. The 6 Investors joining us from our network: (More will be joining) Jay Spindel: Jay Spindel (Managing Director) of INTE Securities & (Special Advisor) to SOJA Ventures. With decades of experience in capital formation & investing, he has helped numerous emerging-growth companies secure funding & pursue their strategic objectives. Jay brings a broad, cross-sector perspective, with experience supporting companies in agentic AI, advertising technology, healthcare services, & renewable energy. Through INTE Securities, an SEC-registered & FINRA-member broker-dealer, he advises companies & family offices on capital-raising initiatives. As a Special Advisor to SOJA Ventures, he plays a key role in securing capital for the firm's portfolio companies & supporting their long-term growth., FINRA member broker-dealer connecting issuers with accredited & institutional capital. Moshe Neuman (Founder, MN Ventures): Moshe is an angel investor, advisor & startup guru who has mentored more than 100 founders. He's now building MN Ventures, a new VC fund raising $100M, as he moves from angel investing into running his own fund. He backs companies at the very earliest stages.  Triet Leminh: Principal, LMT Partners: Lawyer, founder, & investor backing pre-seed to Series A founders building in enterprise & regulated industries. Writing $200K-$300K checks.  DJ Patel (Head of Direct Investing, UV: DJ leads direct investments at UV, which manages $75M-$100M. He backs Seed to Series A companies in healthtech, fintech & AI infrastructure, with typical checks of $500K-$600K.  Gonzalo Quincot (Founder, Sinober): Sinober is a financial intelligence platform that combines public & private market intelligence with institutional-grade methodology, corporate finance & proprietary AI tools to sharpen investment & capital decisions for individuals & businesses. Invests in automation, robotics, data centers & applied AI.  Dr. David Cunic (Serial Entrepreneur & Investor, UCS Advisor [confirm]): A 17-time founder who has built companies across 3 countries & 8 states, with 7 exits. He represents a network of more than 1,000 angel investors who are always looking for quality deal flow. He also helps companies at the friends-and-family, pre-seed & seed stages raise capital, writing checks himself.  All 6 senior investors confirmed. Part of building rooms is making sure real capital is present. Six investors actively deploying writing capital will be joining. Our first confirmed: Why we do this: Putting active investors in the same room as exceptional founders, & keeps the room small enough to ensure everyone actually meets. We value intentional networking & community. If you're here to meet the best of the best, this is the room. Why we do this Our intent is simple: bring good, smart humans together, put active investors in the same room as incredible founders. Intentional community has been lost. We're rebuilding it. What to expect A Korean-style small bites lunch, courtesy of our team, with dishes shared family style Conversations with fellow high-performing startup leaders & investors An experience designed for meaningful connections with ambitious peers solving similar problems A beautiful private townhouse, with room to move between the kitchen, the deck & the garden The format is intentionally part standing, part seated, so you can enjoy incredible food without being anchored to a single table or a single conversation.

events.name: Ground Truth: The Live Agents Hackathon
events.description: Every AI model you've ever used is stuck in the past. Ground Truth is a one-day hackathon where you fix that. Join localhost:nyc, The Builder Series & You.com for 10 hours of building AI agents grounded in the live web. Real-time data, deep research, verifiable answers. Come build the kind of agent people would trust with a real decision. Problem StatementEvery LLM is frozen at its training cutoff. It doesn't know what happened this morning, & when it doesn't know, it guesses, confidently. That's the gap between a cool demo & a product people rely on. Your challenge: build an AI agent that knows what's true right now. It searches the live web through the You.com API, reads the sources, reasons over them & shows its receipts. The Challenge TracksLive Wire (real-time agents): agents that wake up when the world changes. Price moves, breaking news, a competitor launch, a policy change, a new job posting. If it happened in the last hour, your agent already knows & already acted. The Analyst (deep research): pick a profession (VCs, lawyers, journalists, recruiters, doctors, policy staffers) & replace its 40-hour research memo with a 4-minute one, every claim cited. Receipts (trust & verification): agents that fact-check claims, catch AI hallucinations, verify sources & show their work. Best Content (open to every team): post about what you built, tag You.com, & win a dedicated prize. What to ExpectA kickoff walkthrough of the You.com API: Search, Contents, Research & the hosted MCP server Free You.com API credits for every builder 6 hours of building Teams of up to 4, or solo if that's your thing Team matching at kickoff if you're coming alone Mentors from You.com on the floor all day Live demos to judges at the end, plus food all day Prizes1st Place Overall: $500 cash Best Content: TBD JudgesTBD Who Should AttendEngineers (full stack, backend, AI/ML) Founders & aspiring founders building with AI Designers & product people who want to ship something real Researchers & analysts who know exactly what a great research agent should do You don't need a finished idea. Just show up ready to build. SponsorsYou.com: AI search infrastructure that gives agents real-time, cited access to the web through its Search, Contents & Research APIs. Hostslocalhost:nyc: Making NYC the biggest startup ecosystem in the world. The Builder Series   The Builder Series: A 60,000+ member community redefining what networking looks like - curating founders, operators, investors & more into intentional rooms built for experiences people remember & relationships that last. It's a direct line to the most ambitious builders, with a community that actually shows up.   Connect with Me: Join 60,000+ people shaping the future  Join the Newsletter  Follow the Builder Series  Find me here

Request it on the platform where you bought your ticket, or email hello@startupvalley.club ABOUT STARTUP VALLEYStartup Valley is a global event organizer that has hosted pitch nights in 25 cities since 2023: 850 events & 40,000 attendees so far. We have strategic partnerships with VC funds in the US, Europe & Asia. Questions or partnerships: hello@startupvalley.club

We brought 12. $2B+ combined AUM across both events. $1M average check, $100K minimum. $10M+ in live check capacity. Who this room is for To get into this room, you should to have raised at least $1M or be doing $1M+ in ARR. Our last edition averaged $3.8M+ ARR per founder. Raised your first round, onto your second, or bootstrapped to $1M or 15M ARR? You're in the right place. If you're an exited founder, LP/GP, dealmaker or capital raiser, you belong in this room too. Every investor here is from our network. With decades of experience in capital formation & investing, he has helped numerous emerging-growth companies secure funding & pursue their strategic objectives. Jay brings a broad, cross-sector perspective, with experience supporting companies in agentic AI, advertising technology, healthcare services, & renewable energy. Through INTE Securities, an SEC-registered & FINRA-member broker-dealer, he advises companies & family offices on capital-raising initiatives. As a Special Advisor to SOJA Ventures, he plays a key role in securing capital for the firm's portfolio companies & supporting their long-term growth., FINRA member broker-dealer connecting issuers with accredited & institutional capital.  Moshe Neuman (Founder, MN Ventures): Moshe is an angel investor, advisor & startup guru who has mentored more than 100 founders. He's now building MN Ventures, a new VC fund raising $100M, as he moves from angel investing into running his own fund. He backs companies at the very earliest stages.  Triet Leminh: Principal, LMT Partners: Lawyer, founder, & investor backing pre-seed to Series A founders building in enterprise & regulated industries. Writing $200K-$300K checks.  DJ Patel (Head of Direct Investing, UV: DJ leads direct investments at UV, which manages $75M-$100M. He backs Seed to Series A companies in healthtech, fintech & AI infrastructure, with typical checks of $500K-$600K.  Gonzalo Quincot (Founder, Sinober): Sinober is a financial intelligence platform that combines public & private market intelligence with institutional-grade methodology, corporate finance & proprietary AI tools to sharpen investment & capital decisions for individuals & businesses. Invests in automation, robotics, data centers & applied AI.  Dr. David Cunic (Serial Entrepreneur & Investor, UCS Advisor [confirm]): A 17-time founder who has built companies across 3 countries & 8 states, with 7 exits. He represents a network of more than 1,000 angel investors who are always looking for quality deal flow. He also helps companies at the friends-and-family, pre-seed & seed stages raise capital, writing checks himself.  All 6 senior investors confirmed. Part of building rooms is making sure real capital is present. Six investors actively deploying writing capital will be joining. Our first confirmed: Why we do this: Putting active investors in the same room as exceptional founders, & keeps the room small enough to ensure everyone actually meets. We value intentional networking & community. If you're here to meet the best of the best, this is the room. Why we do this Our intent is simple: bring good, smart humans together, put active investors in the same room as incredible founders. Intentional community has been lost. We're rebuilding it.  What to expect A Korean-style small bites lunch, courtesy of our team, with dishes shared family style Conversations with fellow high-performing startup leaders & investors An experience designed for meaningful connections with ambitious peers solving similar problems A beautiful private townhouse, with room to move between the kitchen, the deck & the garden The format is intentionally part standing, part seated, so you can enjoy incredible food without being anchored to a single table or a single conversation.

events.name: The Next Wave: AI & The Future Of Ocean Conservation, with Ocean Agentics
events.description: The world has committed to protecting 30% of the ocean by 2030, a target scientists see as the minimum for a healthy ocean. With four years to go, only about 3% is effectively protected. Countries & communities pursuing the 30x30 goal often lack the data, tools & technical teams to propose & implement conservation efforts at the speed & scale needed to get there. AI is starting to help with some of the hardest parts of that work. It can map where whales & other wildlife gather so countries know which waters to protect, & help coast guards catch illegal fishing vessels inside protected areas. However, most of these tools still sit out of reach of the small island nations & coastal communities with the most at stake. Whether AI narrows that gap or widens it depends on whether it's built with & for the people who will use it. Join Anew & Ocean Agentics for an evening of conversation with people leading this work across ocean technology, science, philanthropy & policy. We'll talk about what responsible AI for the ocean could look like, & what it would take for these tools to reach the people who need them. Drinks & mingling to follow. Ocean Agentics is a nonprofit building open tools that put frontier technology & marine data in the hands of people protecting the ocean. Our current focus is on providing engineering support to the countries & stakeholders implementing the High Seas Treaty, which covers two-thirds of the ocean. Anew is a gathering space & discovery center for social transformation located in NYC. We host interactive events & workshops, an accelerator program for nonprofits, & a retail lab featuring ethically-sourced coffee & gifts.

events.name: Growth Council - Off-The-Record Problem Solving For Scaling Founders
events.description: Are you a founder or entrepreneur? If so, you know that scaling your business past Seed & Series A can expose many gaps in your business all at once - talent/employee friction, messy positioning, legal nuances, capital efficiency...and the list goes on. And while most founder events only focus on panels with generic advice, our new event "The Growth Council" aims to do something different. The mission of this event is to give the founder community access to experts who can help you at your specific stage of growth. The Growth Council is a small-group, peer-to-peer advisory session built specifically for Seed to Series B founders who want to explore their challenges with experts from across the industry & outside their network. Founders will have access to experts in various areas, rotating at specific intervals to ensure they meet with as many experts as possible (think speed dating, but less awkward). These conversations are meant to challenge assumptions & empower founders with new perspectives on their most pressing problems. You'll walk away with fresh perspectives, a bigger network, & connections who can help facilitate you on your journey towards success. The Expert Council Bring us your founder questions, your bottlenecks, or gut-check a current decision & get actionable takeaways from those who have been there before. You'll meet with cross-functional leaders such as: TJ Allison (Sales Advisor & Executive Coach, TJAllison.com) - Sales expert who focuses on revenue & the "Inner Game" to grow revenue & sense of self. Simon Gibson (Fractional VP of Marketing, Formerly GIPHY) - Marketing leader who blends creative storytelling & data-driven strategy to build culturally relevant brands & scale businesses. Rebekah Huber (Cofounder, Kindred Works) - Ops specialist who builds the systems that give founders their time back. Anna Kaplan (Founder & CEO, Narrativ By AK) - Narrative & messaging specialist who helps founders craft a story that wins the room. Marc Kaufman (Partner, Potomac Law Group) - Intellectual property attorney specializing in creating IP assets that increase funding. Fractional CFO TBD Agenda 6:00 PM - 6:30 PM | Arrivals & Light BitesCasual networking over food & drinks before we kick off. 6:30 PM - 6:45 PM | Council & Sponsor IntrosQuick, 60-second introductions from each expert on the specific fires they help extinguish. 6:45 PM - 7:45 PM | Growth Council HuddlesRotate at regular intervals. At each table, state your burning question, get sharp direct feedback from the functional expert, & compare notes with peer founders. 7:45 PM - 8:30 PM | Drinks & Direct ConnectionsInformal wrap-up to continue conversations with experts & founders. Who Should Apply This event is strictly curated for Seed, Series A, & Series B founders / co-founders leading venture-backed tech startups. Capacity is strictly capped at 35 founders to maintain small group sizes & high-signal discussions. Requests to join will be reviewed to preserve the peer dynamic. Hosted By: Kindred Works - Fractional operations & employee engagement partners for high-growth startups. Narrativ by AK - Strategic positioning & narrative development for founders. Tavern - A Physical Social Network Want to host your own event? events.name: 122nd NY Hardware Meetup
events.description: The Hardware Meetup community is excited to announce our next event at Parter's NYC office. Hardware Meetups happen across 35+ cities around the world, bringing together hardware professionals to network & learn from each other. You might not realize it, but NYC is a hotbed for this kind of innovation & tonight you'll meet two companies working at the cutting edge of this technology. THANK YOU TO OUR HOST PARTER Parter is the AI-native BOM optimization platform that takes hardware from design to production without supply chain surprises. events.name: Worn: Smart Glasses Hackathon
events.description: Two days, one overnight build, & real smart glasses on your face. Join us at Cornell Tech with MicroLumin, the Shenzhen team behind the CES 2026 award-winning M6 display glasses, & build the first wave of apps for waveguide display glasses. This is a hands-on hardware hackathon for engineers & builders who would rather ship on real devices than talk about the future of spatial computing. Problem StatementSmart glasses are finally light enough to wear all day. What's missing is software that feels natural to use. Your challenge is to build anthropocentric interfaces: apps that start from how people see, move, talk & pay attention, not from how phones work. These should be things you'd actually keep on your face. The Challenge ThemeHeads-up assistants that show the right info at the right moment Live captioning, translation & conversation memory Navigation & wayfinding without looking down at a phone Accessibility for low-vision, hard-of-hearing & neurodivergent users Hands-free workflows for field techs, clinicians, chefs & mechanics New input patterns: voice, ring, head motion & glanceable UI Making the glasses useful with AI on what the camera sees What to ExpectMicroLumin AR glasses handed out to teams for the build SDK access & docs shared before the event so you can start early A workshop from Dr. Zhaoen Dai, MicroLumin's founder & CEO, on AR & where the AI industry is heading An overnight build from Friday evening into Saturday Teams of up to 4, or match with teammates at kickoff Food, caffeine & other builders who care about hardware Live demos on the device, worn by your team, in front of the judges ScheduleFriday, Nov 20 5:30 PM: Doors open, check-in, dinner 6:15 PM: Welcome & kickoff with the organizers, Cornell Tech & MicroLumin 6:35 PM: Challenge brief & a walkthrough of the MicroLumin SDK 7:00 PM: Team formation: 30-second idea pitches, then a mixer to find teammates 7:45 PM: Teams locked, hardware handed out, devices set up 8:00 PM: Hacking begins 9:00 PM: SDK help desk & mentor office hours open 11:30 PM: Late-night snacks Overnight 12:00 AM to 8:00 AM: Overnight build, with a quiet rest area for anyone who needs a nap All night: A MicroLumin engineer is online for live SDK support (it's afternoon in Shenzhen) Saturday, Nov 21 8:00 AM: Breakfast & coffee 9:00 AM: Morning check-in: each team shares where they are & what's blocking them 10:00 AM: Workshop with Dr. Zhaoen Dai, MicroLumin's founder & CEO, on designing for AR & waveguide displays 11:00 AM: Workshop: [Topic & speaker TBD] 12:30 PM: Lunch 2:00 PM: Code freeze, project submissions due 2:15 PM: Demo expo: judges go table to table & teams demo on the device 3:45 PM: Finalists announced 4:00 PM: Finalists demo on stage: 3 minutes, worn by the team, plus 2 minutes of Q&A 4:45 PM: Talk by Dr. Dai on AR & where the AI industry is heading, while judges deliberate 5:30 PM: Awards 6:00 PM: Hardware return & wrap PrizesTBD JudgesTBD Who Should AttendHardware Founders Engineers at companies like Meta, Amazon & Google who want to build on AR hardware iOS & Android developers Hardware tinkerers, embedded & computer vision engineers Product designers interested in spatial & glanceable UI Spots are limited & approval is required. You don't need prior AR experience, just the drive to build something real overnight. SponsorsMicroLumin: Shenzhen-based maker of AR display glasses, including the M6 series & several CES 2026 award winners. MicroLumin is providing the hardware & SDK support for teams. HostsSomya Gupta: The face of the NYC startup ecosystem. Stephen Jin: Johnson MBA '27 at Cornell, board director at Gona Semiconductor, Angel Investing Waftech - Founded in 2007 & based in Penang, Malaysia, Waftech designs & manufactures wafer-handling & automation equipment for semiconductor manufacturing. Waftech delivers end-to-end, from R&D & design through manufacturing & after-sales service, & is ISO 9001:2015 certified. Waftech is a subsidiary of Gona Semiconductor, a Shanghai-headquartered equipment group. Olivia Iarmak: AI Quality Ops Lead at Meta Reality Labs working on Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses, & co-founder of HQ Labs. Vishal Kharker: Lead Product Manager at RTX Fintech & Research, previously at Barclays & RBC Capital Markets. Info site: https://worn-hacks.com

events.name: Hype vs Reality - AI Debunk Night
events.description: October 2026 | In-Person at Pier 57 (Livestream TBA)Hype vs. Reality: An AI Debunk Night Every week there's a new AI headline designed to make your heart race. "700 agents went rogue." "AI just crossed the terrifying line." "Your job is next." This month, we're slowing down & reading the receipts. No outside food allowed. The venue has food for sale.   The format: We take the biggest AI stories of the year & break each one down in three moves:  What the headline said  What the primary sources actually show  What's genuinely still unknown The main event: The July 2026 Hugging Face breach - the "rogue agent swarm" story that's been viewed 15M+ times. We'll walk through OpenAI's own incident report & the independent METR investigation to show what really happened (spoiler: it's less "machine uprising," more "someone didn't patch an internal proxy"). "AI will kill us all" - who's selling the timelines, & what the technical critics actually claim Apply to give a presentation here. --- Speakers:Norman BBernie T(More TBA) Sponsors:Current Sponsor list still being compiled. If you'd like to sponsor the event, please reach out to us at speaking@thoughtful.events

events.name: What Makes A Good Life? A Guided Public Discussion On AI
events.description: The oldest question philosophers have asked is: What makes a good life? This inquiry has been important not only for guiding individual decisions, but also for shaping institutions & public policy. Now, amid the rapid changes AI is bringing to every aspect of our lives, & the growing debate about its risks & benefits, we must ask: What makes a good life, & how does AI enable or hinder it? Together, we will explore this question through prompts & shared reflection. Dr. Ece Tekbulut is a political philosopher & the founder of Thinking Through. She earned her Ph.D. from Columbia University. Through Thinking Through, she brings rigorous philosophical inquiry into everyday life, convening groups to engage with themes central to contemporary society, especially where people feel at an impasse. One such focus is AI's impact on human flourishing. Her work fosters public discourse on AI's implications & the ethical questions that surround it, & she writes on AI & society for Medyascope. Wissam Kahi is the founder of Odyssey Lead, where he helps companies capture the value of AI that usually gets lost between the boardroom & the front line. For seven years he led digital transformation across United Rentals' network of more than 1,500 locations, & he learned there that AI only sticks when the people who do the work help shape it. His essays on Substack & his novella The Panama Dilemma explore the question at the heart of tonight's discussion: what makes a good life when the machine is doing the living? Matt Konwiser is an Ecosystem Leader & Field CTO at IBM. He serves on the AI Advisory Council at the Global Technology Industry Association (GTIA) & writes a regular column on AI for CFO Intelligence Magazine. He also co-hosts AI Diatribe, a podcast built around direct, practical conversations about where AI is headed & what organizations should do about it. Anew is a gathering space & discovery center for social transformation located in NYC. We host interactive events & workshops, an accelerator program for nonprofits, & a retail lab featuring ethically-sourced coffee & gifts.

Her work fosters public discourse on AI's implications & the ethical questions that surround it, & she writes on AI & society for Medyascope. Wissam Kahi is the founder of Odyssey Lead, where he helps companies capture the value of AI that usually gets lost between the boardroom & the front line. For seven years he led digital transformation across United Rentals' network of more than 1,500 locations, & he learned there that AI only sticks when the people who do the work help shape it. His essays on Substack & his novella The Panama Dilemma explore the question at the heart of tonight's discussion: what makes a good life when the machine is doing the living? Matt Konwiser is an Ecosystem Leader & Field CTO at IBM. He serves on the AI Advisory Council at the Global Technology Industry Association (GTIA) & writes a regular column on AI for CFO Intelligence Magazine. He also co-hosts AI Diatribe, a podcast built around direct, practical conversations about where AI is headed & what organizations should do about it. Anew is a gathering space & discovery center for social transformation located in NYC. We host interactive events & workshops, an accelerator program for nonprofits, & a retail lab featuring ethically-sourced coffee & gifts.

events.name: AI Content System
events.description: Time Rich presents a working session, hosted by Ella Molony Cook, with co-hosting partner Wispr Flow & presenting partner Stanley. It opens with a short panel on why trust + distribution is now your moat. Then you build your content system in three parts: capture, context, create. You schedule your posts before you leave, so next week is handled. Every guest gets six months of Wispr Pro & Stanley. WHO IT'S FORFounders, business owners & investors who post in bursts, or know they should post more, & want content that sounds like them without writing every word. THE PANEL: YOUR MOAT IS YOUR DISTRIBUTIONA short conversation with investors, founders & ex-Google/YouTube on why visibility, trust & authority matter more than ever. WHAT GETS BUILTCapture. You'll set up Wispr Flow & brief your agent by voice instead of typing. Your best ideas sit in voice notes that never turn into posts, because nothing keeps running when you're busy. Your calls, voice notes & talks become raw material, & we pull ten stories out of your own words.Context. A tone of voice brief, the words you never use, & a call to action matched to each story.Create. Content agents that draft, repurpose across platforms & schedule. By the end, a week of posts is scheduled & the system is set up to fill the next one. Rather have it built for you? The Stanley team will be in the room. Just ask. WHAT TO BRING Laptop, charger & phone. Setup runs on iMessage or WhatsApp. One recording: a talk, a podcast, a call or a voice note Your three best published posts The one thing you want every post to drive: a booked call, a newsletter sign-up or a product AGENDA6:00-6:30 PM  Doors open, meet other founders6:30-6:35 PM  Welcome from Ella6:35-6:55 PM  Panel: your moat is your distribution6:55-8:20 PM  The build: capture, context, create8:20-9:00 PM  Q&A, drinks & mingling POWERED BY STANLEYStanley is an AI Head of Content. You text it a voice note, it drafts in your voice, & it repurposes whatever already performed. Stanley is our presenting partner for the night, so everyone builds on it live. OUR PARTNERTime Rich runs on voice, powered by Wispr FlowWispr Flow is our co-hosting partner. You'll talk to your agents instead of typing to them, & every guest leaves with six months of Wispr Pro. THE ROOMElla Molony Cook is an Australian 4x founder with 1 exit & an investor in Anthropic. Founder of Time Rich a media & AI education platform. Has a community of over 63K+ subscribers on Substack filled with founders, SMBs, angel investors, leaders & has hosted 250+ founder & investor experiences. Max Rivera is an angel investor & GP at GHOST Angels, a fund of Snapchat alumni backing early-stage consumer AI startups. He led global partnerships at Snap from pre-IPO to a $120B public company. Today he leads partnerships for Microsoft AI. Aishwarya Balaji is a 2x founder, venture fund advisor, investor & global speaker. She has spotted & built for emerging markets again & again, from ed-tech & Web3 to non-alc & the creator economy. Rodolphe Kdderitzsch is on the Stanley team. He's ex-Google/YouTube & Squarespace, & a startup founder. TIME RICH CLUBWhere founders, creators & investors come to invest in themselves, their relationships, & building a system to become Time Rich. Whether you're building a company, backing your next deal, or just getting started, this is where you do it alongside people who are building too. Inside the Club: Private conversations on investing, entrepreneurship, building your brand, time hacks & running your life on AI Fireside chats with family offices, exited founders & thought leaders A network of founders, creators & investors who build companies & allocate capital Seats are limited & we read every application.

events.description: Presented by EvalScience, Agent Evaluation Science NYC 2026 is a one-day symposium bringing together researchers & practitioners working on how AI agents should be evaluated. Featured speakers & contributors include Hanna Wallach (Microsoft Research), Jason Weston (Meta / NYU), Yoav Artzi (Cornell Tech), Nouha Dziri (Cohere Labs), Peter Henderson (Princeton), Olawale Salaudeen (UIUC), Rachneet Kaur (J.P. Morgan), Ida Momennejad (Microsoft Research), & Saurabh Jha (IBM Research). We will discuss what agent evaluations should measure, how reliability & validity should be established, where benchmarks & graders fail, how evaluation infrastructure should be built, & what changes when agents are evaluated in interactive & real-world settings. The program includes invited talks, contributed research presentations, posters, a fireside conversation, & extended discussion & networking. November 20, 2026  New York City Registration is free & approval-based. We welcome researchers, builders, & practitioners working on evaluation methods, benchmarks, agent behavior, evaluation infrastructure, & real-world evaluation problems. We are also accepting contributions including ongoing or published research, evaluation studies, tools, failure analyses, & lessons from evaluating deployed systems. Learn more: https://evalscience.org/2026fall-nyc/

events.name: Founder Lab: NYC
events.description:
Founder Lab is a weekly build day for early-stage founders. Bring what you're stuck on — check in on what you're testing and what you learned, then get to work: office hours with investors and operators, and open build time with founders at your stage. Same day, every week.

​Who is this for?

​Founders building venture-scale startups, pre-seed to Series A — AI, deep tech, frontier, or any technical or science vertical. Connected through a common thread of relentless honesty and proof arc: something built to scale, tested and iterated on weekly.

​The System

​Every check-in runs through FounderOS, the proof engine that turns weekly work into a track record with venture visibility.

​Review Reps: How are you stuck, what did you learn, and what needs to change.

​Pressure-Test Logic: Use adversarial feedback to identify flaws in current hypotheses.

​Anchor the Roadmap: Align on near-term technical unlocks and business milestones.

​Design the Next Interval: Lock the specific success gates for the upcoming build cycle.

​Direct Feedback: Receive "brutal honesty" testing from founders, operators, and venture advisors.

​Founder Lab NY is headed by Keenan Williams, RTC venture advisor, former YC founder ('17).

​*Fabrik Day Pass discount is available via your dashboard.

​Agenda
​9:00 AM — Doors open

​10:30 AM — Group check-in

​12:00 PM — Lunch break

​After Check-Ins — Logic Refinement & Workspace 1:1 office hours / feedback + workspace access will commence. Lunch is occasionally provided.

​New or Visiting Founders
​Founder Lab is the core operating cadence for RTC founders. Activate FounderOS to access the full system.

Seasons are fleeting here in New York. Maybe you’re like me, currently grasping onto Summer and in denial that Fall is here (despite it being amazing) because of the fear of the cold winter that follows.

But what if instead… we embraced the Fall? And the joys of this time?

Building off last month’s session on rest, we are diving into a reflection, discussion and mini art session focused on embracing the seasons.

Come join us to reflect and discuss questions like:

What good can this new season bring you?

How can you try to stay in the present?

Wednesday, October 28th, 5:30 - 7:30 pm @ Fabrik Dumbo

Evening Flow ~

5:30 - 6 pm: Arrive, mingle & snack

6 - 6:30 pm: Written Reflection with provided prompts and Mini Drawing Activity (Solo) - Please arrive before 6!

6:30 - ~7/7:30 pm: Small Group Discussion (sharing optional)

7:30 pm-on: We'll wrap up formal discussion by 7:30 the latest, but you're welcome to stay later for continued mingling & connection.

All are welcome. You can be un-/under-employed, in career transition, employed or none of the above! This is a safe, welcoming space for you to come wherever you're at.

Please bring your journal/notebook if you have one! Paper and pens will be provided.

Light snacks and non-alch drinks will be provided.

⭐ Note: this is also a phone-free event. Please step away from the group if you need to use your phone. Thank you!

About the Host:

MELISSA CENTER is an actress, award-winning filmmaker known for visceral women’s stories, and crowdfunding expert who has helped fellow creatives raise over $2.1M for their independent films, plays & albums.

As an actor, her most notable credits include roles on Chicago Fire (NBC), FBI (CBS), This is Us (NBC), Grey's Anatomy (ABC), and more. Favorite roles onstage include “Maggie” in A Chorus Line (Dir. Mitzi Hamilton), “Olivia” in Sex with Strangers (Hollywood Fringe), and “Jan” in 50 Words (The Lab Creative, LA). She is the writer, director, Executive Producer and star of short film JEWFACE, set to premiere in 2027. She is the Executive Producer of Liner Notes, currently in development. She is the producer, co-writer and star of feature film, All I Want (Prime, AppleTv, Vudu, TubiTV, itunes) and the co-director, writer and star of award-winning viral short film R.V, a narrative that anticipated the overturn of Roe vs Wade. Her short film His Name is Niv, which she wrote and directed, is inspired by her own experience with sexual assault.

Her solo show Marrying Jake Gyllenhaal, that she wrote, starred in and produced, debuted The Pico, LA followed by Edinburgh Fringe Digital and Caveat, NYC, with global coverage in Ms. Magazine & Psychology Today. melissacenter.com

events.description:
A small, facilitated roundtable for founders who aren't hustle-culture kids.
Bring one conversation you've been avoiding. Leave with real perspective on it, and a handful of founders who know what you're actually dealing with.
No stage. No audience. No pitching. 
Facilitated by executive leadership coach Daniel Stillman, author of Good Talk: How to Design Conversations that Matter. 
Who is this for?
Being a founder takes commitment, sacrifice, and sometimes hustle. But the hustle-culture narrative doesn't match the life you want as you get older. You're not 25 with nothing to lose. You have a mortgage. You want a proper vacation. Maybe you have aging parents to care for. And a mission you still want to bring into the world. 

Why a Roundtable?
You don’t need another big networking event, or a poorly moderated panel you could have watched on YouTube at 2x.

You need an intimate, high-trust, off-the-record room where you can get real with other founders, builders and entrepreneurs. 

A roundtable is one where everyone shares, everyone is heard, and everyone gets more than they imagined.

The Conversation
Conversations are the atomic unit of change. Our lives are built by the conversations we have, and defined by the ones we avoid. The cofounder conflict you brush off but never resolve. The hire you won't admit isn't working. The pivot you keep putting off.
The ones we avoid most are with ourselves. The bargains we never renegotiated. The anxiety we can't politely ask to leave. The question we keep not answering.
The un-had conversation doesn't disappear. It goes underground and gets more expensive. This roundtable is designed to create the space for the most important questions and conversations you’re facing right now.

Application and Curation
Admission is by invitation only - please complete all application questions so we can curate the group, optimizing for:

People actively building
Openness, Curiosity and Generosity
Commitment - people who don’t show up won’t be invited to come again
The Prework: 
This is a small room, on purpose, so we’re only selecting a handful of folks who are willing to do some thinking before they get in the room. Apply with your thoughtful answers to the registration questions.
The Format: 
Five rounds of conversation: 
Connection and Learning - so we know who we are and why we’re building what we are each building
Exploration: Sharing your avoided conversation with the group
Stories Vs Advice: Sharing stories to help each other through shared empathy, not problem solving
Asks and Offers: What’s something you need from the group? What’s something you can offer in generosity?
Closing Round - What you’re taking away from the conversation - what you’re committed to
The Follow Up:
Join a continuing conversation with the attendees, where you can share the resource you mentioned, ask that follow-up question, and get the support you need from a generous, growing community.
Your Co-Hosts
Daniel Stillman designs conversations for a living, and insists that you do too. He's an executive coach and facilitator who works with founders and founding teams on how they lead, communicate, and navigate the conversations that matter. He hosts The Conversation Factory podcast (a top 100 Management podcast) and wrote Good Talk: How to Design Conversations that Matter, a handbook for changemakers and innovators.
Anson Wu is the founder of Ugly Talk, the no-BS event series where battle-tested founders share the setbacks, pivots, and lessons behind the wins. Since 2019 it's grown across New York, Chicago, San Francisco, and Miami. Anson also runs Grey Journal, the digital media company behind it, and came up as a designer and agency founder. By his own description, a recovering underthinker still mining the lessons from two failed startups.
About Ugly Talk
Started in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough “aha!” moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons and insights.
With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, and Miami, we’ve built a vibrant community of thousands of founders and industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape.

events.name: Built to Connect: Technology and Social Health
events.description:
Built to Connect: Technology and Social Health

An afternoon with Social Connection Collective, Fabrik, and Dr Hans Rocha IJzerman, 

Can technology help people feel closer to each other? Most public debate assumes it can’t.

Philosopher Andy Clark offers a more useful starting point. In a 2025 essay in Nature Communications, he argues that people have always thought with tools, from pen and paper to maps to AI, and that what matters is how each partnership between person and tool is designed. If tools can help us think, they can also help us see our relationships more clearly.

Today, most organizations see connection through a single score. Take two employees who both score as lonely on a standard survey. One moved cities last year and has no one nearby to call when something goes wrong. The other has plenty of friends but nobody at work who understands what she is dealing with. If the company sees only the score, it will probably offer both of them the same thing, such as a team social or a wellbeing app, and that may help neither. The questionnaires make this worse. A LONELY-EU review of 2,720 of them found that two tools measuring the same thing share, on average, only 15.6% of their content, so a score can depend as much on the questionnaire as on the person.

Used well, AI can tell these two situations apart from what each person says and suggest a next step that fits. For the first employee, that might be building one reliable contact close to home. For the second, it might be an honest conversation with a colleague who has been through the same thing.

Social Connection Collective and Fabrik are bringing together HR leaders, therapists, researchers, and founders to test that idea with real tools in hand.

What happens in our afternoon together

  • Interview and demo. Dr. Hans Rocha IJzerman, social psychologist and CEO of Entrelacs, talks with [interviewer] about his research on loneliness and social connection, followed by a live demo of Entrelacs.

  • Rapid-fire pitches. [N] founders building tools for connection at work, in healthcare, and in communities, 30 seconds each.

  • Hands-on time. Try the tools with the people who built them.

  • Happy hour. Keep the conversation going at [venue].

Arrive with your own results. After you RSVP, you’ll get a link to Entrelacs. It takes 10 to 20 minutes and gives you your own Keystone report: the one area of your social life most worth working on, with evidence-based actions for the coming week. Your report is private. If you’d rather try it on our afternoon together, [alternatively, a station will be set up at the venue].

For HR leaders: Organizations at the event can claim a pilot slot for their team!

Who should come: HR and total rewards leaders deciding which wellbeing programs to fund; therapists and clinicians who see disconnection behind what clients bring in; and researchers and builders working on social health.

When you arrive, we’ll ask you one question: What’s one tool, app, or habit that keeps you close to someone? Your answers will open the conversation.

About our Featured Founder:

Dr Hans Rocha IJzerman directs Annecy Behavioral Science Lab, which has worked with the WHO on global priority setting for social connection and whose research anchors the EU's loneliness monitoring framework, and he is a principal investigator of the Horizon Europe consortium LONELY-EU. He is an Associate Researcher at the University of Oxford and the author of Heartwarming (W.W. Norton, 2021). A longtime advocate for rigor and open science, he co-founded the Psychological Science Accelerator, a network of labs in more than 80 countries, and serves on the advisory board for the Center for Open Science's TOP Guidelines.

As CEO of Entrelacs, he brings this science to employers. Employees talk privately with Lacis, an AI confidant that works out which part of their social life most affects how they're doing and suggests what to try next.

Through an interactive palate-training experiment, we’ll isolate the four primary structural components of wine: tannin, acidity, sweetness, and alcohol. By tasting each element independently, participants will learn how these components affect the taste and feel of a wine, how to recognize them in the glass, and ultimately better understand what they like and why they like it.
What are we actually tasting when we drink wine? What do terms like acidity, tannin, body, alcohol, and residual sugar really mean, and how do they affect what we experience in the glass? Most importantly, how can understanding these basic elements help us better identify and communicate what we actually like to drink?
Anna Arfaras is a Certified Sommelier with nearly two decades of experience in the wine and hospitality industry. Her career has taken her through acclaimed restaurants and luxury hospitality operations in New York City, Las Vegas, Orlando, and the Bahamas, with roles ranging from floor sommelier to multi-unit beverage director.

Her experience spans nearly every side of the wine business, including building and managing wine programs, restaurant operations, hospitality consulting, distribution, and supplier sales, with particular expertise in Italian wine. Through her consulting work, Anna has advised restaurants and hospitality groups on wine programs, beverage strategy, operations, and staff education.

Combining a sommelier’s knowledge with years of practical experience buying, selling, serving, and teaching wine, Anna approaches wine education with a focus on making an often-intimidating subject engaging, approachable, and genuinely fun.

events.name: Drop-In Men's Work Group
events.description:
A meeting where men can do their work.
Men’s work is just this: being mindful and relating intentionally with other people who identify as men, to allow ourselves to just be, together, in a deeper way. We sometimes call this deeper connection "dropping in".

Men’s work can help to expand emotional range and resilience, and your ability to express feelings - here in the group through creating a safe space, and out in the world, at your job and in your relationships.

This circle is for both men who have experienced men's work and for men who are curious about men's work.

Anyone who identifies as male can join.

How it will work

We'll meet from 6:30 PM sharp until 8:30PM. Please come sober, with your phone off, and ready to spend the whole time with the group.

Expect a series of conversations and guided experiences to connect you more deeply to yourself and to others.

Please Note: This is not therapy.
This is a mutual support group, hosted by peers.
About your Host, Daniel Stillman

I work as executive leadership coach and keynote speaker, for organizations of all shapes, sizes and industries. I have learned that at the heart of real change is a conversation - one with yourself, as well as conversations with others. I create space for leaders and their teams to have the conversations that matter.

I’ve been co-leading a men’s group since 2018, and have taught and facilitated men's work in person, online, and at multi-day retreats. Men’s work has been an important part of my ongoing personal development and has allowed me to expand my emotional range and resilience. It’s also expanded my range and the depth in my one-on-one coaching and team transformation work.

I also host The Conversation Factory podcast (a top 100 Management Podcast) and am the author of “Good Talk: How to Design Conversations that Matter” a handbook for changemakers and innovators.

Learn more at www.DanielStillman.com

A portion of the proceeds from ticket sales will go to the Ever Forward Club, which provides support programs and workshops to disadvantaged young men and boys in the Bay Area.

Agreements for the gathering:

I agree to…

Come prepared and ready to both give and receive support for the group members by being well rested and nourished.  I will take care of myself.

I will include all the men in the conversation.  I will not dominate.

I will not be violent.

I agree to keep everything discussed or revealed in the group completely confidential except for what I share or another man’s reaction to what I share.  

I agree to keep the physical space we use and occupy in better shape than I found it.

For the duration of the session I will honor myself and my colleagues by not coming under the influence of any mood altering recreational substance, including drugs and alcohol. 

I agree that our time together is not counseling or therapy.  

If there is any reason to believe that I may be of harm to myself or others, I am required to share this with the group.

If you're living in NYC, chances are that you ride the subway! But did you know all the incredible art that you might be missing without even realizing it? Join us as Museum Educator and Guide Kristin McCollum opens our eyes to the most underappreciated art museum in the world!
Millions of people ride the subway every day without realizing they're walking through a museum full of art and history, containing countless stories of New York City. This talk digs deep on the history of the NYC subway and why we have such an extensive and diverse amount of art in our stations. 
Kristin McCollum is a museum educator, guide, actor, and improviser. She creates and leads tours at the New York Transit Museum, Morgan Library & Museum, and the Museum of the City of New York. When she's not in a gallery or subway station, she's teaching and performing improv with Improvolution in the West Village or making NYC history and art videos as NerdingOutOnNYC. She and her trash dog Rory are proud residents of Hell's Kitchen.
"...my main goal is to make people more aware of the art as they're commuting and how deep the stories go. The history of the NYC subway system is also so unique and fascinating - and will hopefully make the hodgepodge nature of it more endearing to people. Introducing the less well-known artists that are featured has been very rewarding, and highlighting New York stories that may have been lost through time but are represented in the art is really cool."

events.name: Your Investor Pitch - What To Say & How To Say It
events.description: A free, two-hour workshop for founders who want to build a stronger investor pitch & deliver it with confidence.You know your business. You know the opportunity. But can you communicate it in a way that makes investors understand the potential, believe in you, & want to continue the conversation? On October 30, join a group of founders for a focused working session to assess the pitch you have today, identify what's missing, & turn it into a sharper, more compelling investor presentation. Anthony Rose, CEO of SeedLegals.com, tells you exactly what investors need to hear. David Goldberg, CEO of Prosody.center, shows you exactly how they need to hear it. Two hours, both experts, free. What you'll work on1. Build the right investor storyStructure your pitch around what investors need to understand: opportunity, differentiation, competition, financials, traction, scalability, & why now. Cut unnecessary information, close narrative gaps, & make the value easier to grasp. 2. Deliver it with confidence & credibilityA strong deck isn't enough. Learn to make a strong first impression, create buy-in, use pace & pauses to make key numbers land, stress the words that carry value, & steady your voice under pressure. Use your voice to communicate with the composure & authority investors expect. 3. Test & refine your pitchPitch in front of others & discover where the room leans in, where you lose them, & what needs to change. Use live feedback to tighten your messaging & delivery. 4. The live-feedback experienceEach hour includes 15 minutes of tips, first from Anthony Rose on creating compelling content, then from David Goldberg on delivering it with conviction, followed by 45 minutes of live, instructive feedback so founders can improve their pitches on the spot. What you'll leave withA sharper, more focused investor pitch A clearer understanding of your strengths & gaps Practical techniques for presenting with confidence Real-world feedback on your messaging & delivery Specific next steps for continuing to improve Greater insight into what can move an investor from listening to wanting to know more Who should attendFounders & startup leaders at different stages of the fundraising journey. Whether you're preparing to pitch for the first time or you've pitched before & know it could be stronger, the goal is the same: leave with a better pitch than the one you walked in with. Your facilitatorsAnthony Rose, CEO, SeedLegalsFounder & CEO of SeedLegals, the legaltech platform that helps startups get investment-ready, run a funding round, & handle their legals, used by over 60,000 startups. Before SeedLegals, his career spanned 3D graphics, peer-to-peer music, internet video, & social TV, including heading up BBC iPlayer. Wired Magazine's 2009 cover story called him "The Man Who Saved the BBC." David Goldberg, CEO, Prosody.center & Edge StudioFounder of Prosody.center & EdgeStudio.com, an international voiceover recording center. He has directed, coached, & trained over 10,000 celebrities, politicians, CEOs, & founders on more than 13,000 spoken-word projects over 38 years. He identifies the blind spots that hold founders back when they pitch (pacing, phrasing, wording, emphasis, tone, body language, composure, nonverbal cues), then shows the precise adjustments that change how investors experience & respond to you. DetailsWhen: Friday, October 30, 1-3pm ET, in person, Times Square, NYCCost: Free to join. Co-founders are welcome too.Capacity: Seating is limited, & registrations are approved individually. Come prepared to work on your business, test your ideas, & practice your pitch, not simply take notes.

events.name: An Unmuted Debate: Primary Party Crashers
events.description: Should primaries be open to every voter? More Americans now identify as independent than as Democrat or Republican. Yet in New York & many other states, those voters are shut out of the primaries that often decide who actually wins. So are closed primaries locking out the voters our politics needs most? And would opening them make anything better? Open primaries let any registered voter participate, regardless of party. Supporters say they force candidates to campaign to the whole electorate, reward problem-solvers over partisans, & give millions of independents a real voice. Critics say parties have the right to choose their own nominees, that open systems invite strategic crossover voting & voter confusion, & that the evidence they reduce polarization is thin. So who's right? Are open primaries the fix for a system that rewards the extremes? Or are they a reform that promises more than it delivers? John Opdycke is the founder & president of Open Primaries, a national organization working to enact & protect open & nonpartisan primaries. He has spent three decades in independent & reform politics, helped found the New York State Independence Party, & writes the monthly column Brash Tacks for The Fulcrum. Lindsey Cormack is an associate professor of political science & director of the Diplomacy Lab at Stevens Institute of Technology. She is the author of How to Raise a Citizen (And Why It's Up to You to Do It) & Congress & U.S. Veterans, created the DCInbox database of congressional newsletters, & serves as Secretary of Manhattan Community Board 8. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

events.name: Post Human Investment Summit
events.description: In the 1980s, Renaissance Technologies pioneered a new way to beat the markets: computing power, statistics, & signal processing. Today that approach anchors a $1.2 trillion asset class, but one built almost entirely on short-horizon trades. The holy grail has always been the opposite: long-horizon investing, fully automated. An agentic Warren Buffett. With the tools we had, it felt out of reach. Agentic reasoning systems may finally change that. A new wave of frontier researchers, 6 newly launched fully agentic funds, & tiger teams inside established funds are setting out to build it. Join us for a one day summit alongside many of the early leaders in this space, to share ideas, challenge assumptions, & brainstorm the various paths ahead for this burgeoning space. The event will be a tightly curated group of researchers, builders, investment professionals, & LPs. We invest in engineers, researchers, & scientists building solutions to the world's greatest challenges, including Circle, Abridge, Algorand, PillPack, Jellyfish, Neural Magic, Hometap, Asimov, & PathAI, & others.

events.name: Growth Council - Off-The-Record Problem Solving For Scaling Founders
events.description: Are you a founder or entrepreneur? If so, you know that scaling your business past Seed & Series A can expose many gaps in your business all at once - talent/employee friction, messy positioning, legal nuances, capital efficiency...and the list goes on. And while most founder events only focus on panels with generic advice, our new event "The Growth Council" aims to do something different. The mission of this event is to give the founder community access to experts who can help you at your specific stage of growth. The Growth Council is a small-group, peer-to-peer advisory session built specifically for Seed to Series B founders who want to explore their challenges with experts from across the industry & outside their network. Founders will have access to experts in various areas, rotating at specific intervals to ensure they meet with as many experts as possible (think speed dating, but less awkward). These conversations are meant to challenge assumptions & empower founders with new perspectives on their most pressing problems. You'll walk away with fresh perspectives, a bigger network, & connections who can help facilitate you on your journey towards success. The Expert Council Bring us your founder questions, your bottlenecks, or gut-check a current decision & get actionable takeaways from those who have been there before. You'll meet with cross-functional leaders such as: TJ Allison (Sales Advisor & Executive Coach, TJAllison.com) - Sales expert who focuses on revenue & the "Inner Game" to grow revenue & sense of self. Simon Gibson (Fractional VP of Marketing, Formerly GIPHY) - Marketing leader who blends creative storytelling & data-driven strategy to build culturally relevant brands & scale businesses. Rebekah Huber (Cofounder, Kindred Works) - Ops specialist who builds the systems that give founders their time back. Anna Kaplan (Founder & CEO, Narrativ By AK) - Narrative & messaging specialist who helps founders craft a story that wins the room. Marc Kaufman (Partner, Potomac Law Group) - Intellectual property attorney specializing in creating IP assets that increase funding. Fractional CFO TBD Agenda 6:00 PM - 6:30 PM | Arrivals & Light BitesCasual networking over food & drinks before we kick off. 6:30 PM - 6:45 PM | Council & Sponsor IntrosQuick, 60-second introductions from each expert on the specific fires they help extinguish. 6:45 PM - 7:45 PM | Growth Council HuddlesRotate at regular intervals. At each table, state your burning question, get sharp direct feedback from the functional expert, & compare notes with peer founders. 7:45 PM - 8:30 PM | Drinks & Direct ConnectionsInformal wrap-up to continue conversations with experts & founders. Who Should Apply This event is strictly curated for Seed, Series A, & Series B founders / co-founders leading venture-backed tech startups. Capacity is strictly capped at 35 founders to maintain small group sizes & high-signal discussions. Requests to join will be reviewed to preserve the peer dynamic. Hosted By: Kindred Works - Fractional operations & employee engagement partners for high-growth startups. Narrativ by AK - Strategic positioning & narrative development for founders. Tavern - A Physical Social Network Want to host your own event? events.name: Unmuted  Debate - AI & China
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In July, a Chinese lab you'd probably never heard of published Kimi K3: 2.8 trillion parameters, billed as the largest open model on earth, weights posted free on Hugging Face for anyone to download. It's one of four Chinese labs that spent the last year closing the gap with the American frontier, then giving the result away. Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi. Four of the five most-used open models in the world now come out of Beijing, & American developers are running them inside hospitals, law firms, & startups because they're the cheapest, fastest tools available. No API someone in Washington controls. No off switch. Just download & go. One camp says a model is just math. Open weights run on a consumer's machine, the code is right there to inspect, & cutting Americans off from the best tools on the planet is how you lose a technology race. The other camp says the giveaway is the strategy. China seeds the world's infrastructure with their standards, their defaults, their assumptions, & the dependency follows once switching costs become unbeatable. So: should Americans be allowed to build on Chinese open-weight models or is this the new Cold War's Monkey's Paw? Arguing for, Rob Li is Managing Partner of Amont Partners, a New York global equity firm that invests across the US & Asia. He has spent his career putting capital on both sides of the Pacific, from Yum China to Alibaba deals, & he thinks the country that walls itself off from the best tools available loses. Arguing against, Will McKelvey is a Principal at Lerer Hippeau, one of New York's oldest venture firms, where he backs early-stage founders & spends his days watching for the future of AI, especially in consumer. He got his start by way of a congressional office, & he thinks the cheapest model on the market is the one you pay for slowly. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones. In collaboration with COMMITTEE OF 100Committee of 100 (C100) is a nonprofit U.S. leadership organization of distinguished Chinese Americans dedicated to advancing the full participation of Chinese Americans in American society & fostering constructive U.S.-China relations. For more than 35 years, C100 has brought together leaders across business, government, academia, technology, media, the arts, & other fields to advance its dual mission. Learn more at committee100.org.

events.name: Ugly Talk: CPG Founders What Worked, What Didn't & The 2027 Outlook
events.description: A bigger order can leave you with a smaller margin. That is an ugly way to learn what growth costs. CPG founders will unpack the calls shaping their brands in 2026. The channels that moved product. The partners that mattered. The pivots they had to make. Bring the decisions you are still wrestling with. Hear what these founders are changing as they finish Q4 & plan for 2027.  Why you should be in this room.Hear which channels moved product & which ate margin. Learn what founders wish they had asked before choosing a co-packer or distributor. Explore where food service & alternative distribution could fit your brand. Hear how founders responded when their customers, markets, or plans changed. Pressure-test your 2027 assumptions against what these founders are seeing in 2026.  What's on the table.Production & partners. Refining the recipe, choosing co-manufacturers, & finding partners who deliver what they promise. Distribution & margin. Which channels earned their place, which disappointed, & what founders changed in response. Finding the customer. What urban & suburban markets taught founders about who actually buys their products. Food service & other routes. Where founders are looking beyond familiar shelves to move product. The 2027 calls. Which trends held up, which missed, & what founders are carrying into next year.  Featured speakers.Liv Truesdell - Founder, FROST Buttercream Liv Truesdell started her career in consumer investment banking, working with food & beverage companies, which ultimately led her to launch FROST Buttercream. FROST is an all-natural Italian Meringue Buttercream made with real butter & egg whites, with ~57% less sugar than a leading buttercream & no palm oils, artificial dyes or preservatives. After hundreds of iterations, Liv created a new premium, refrigerated frosting segment in a category unchanged for ~71 years. events.description: Everyone & their grandma is hosting a hackathon. This is the one where you build something physical. Silicon Alley Hack is a one-day, in-person sprint for builders who'd rather solder than ship a vibe-coded app. Microcontrollers. Sensors. Connected devices. Real hardware that runs in the real world & has to work when we plug it in on stage. Application-based. Teams of 4. Every team gets an STM32 development board & peripherals on arrival. Bring your laptop, your wits, & your soldering instincts.  The Problem StatementSoftware ate the world & then got bored. The interesting frontier moved back to atoms - robots that navigate a room, drones that deliver, sensors that make a physical space legible to a machine. All of it runs on constrained silicon, in real time, in places where the cloud is too slow, too far, or not there at all. So that's the terrain: edge intelligence. Machines that sense the world & act on it, on-device.  The Challenge ThemeThe sealed spec will live somewhere in here: Sense  decide  act, running on-device IoT, sensors, & connected devices Physical/digital interaction - things that move, respond, or react Anything that runs on hardware, not just in a browser Constraints you can count on: You'll be working on an STM32 development board & peripherals - get familiar before you show up It has to run live. Slides don't win. Working hardware wins. First team to solve it take the prizes. This is a race, not a showcase.  What to ExpectA live race-to-win challenge dropped at kickoff An STM32 dev kit + peripherals for every team, free 5 hours of focused build time Team formation on-site, or come with your crew Breakfast & lunch provided Exciting prizes for the winning A room full of NYC's hardware people - embedded engineers, drone builders, robotics founders, spatial-data folks  Schedule10:00 - 11:00 AM - Doors open. Breakfast, networking mixer, team formation. 11:00 - 11:30 AM - Partner intros, Root Access demo, challenge drop, rules & judging criteria. 11:30 AM - 4:30 PM - Build sprint. Lunch provided. Clock does not stop. 4:30 - 5:15 PM - Live hardware demos to the judges. 5:15 - 6:00 PM - Photos & Mixer.  PrizesA mix of cash, credits, & perks for the winning team. events.name: Borderless Office - Identity & Access In World Of Remote-First Growth
events.description: Join Antoine Jebara (Co-founder, JumpCloud) & Noah Landow (Founder & CEO, Macktez) for an informal conversation between an expert on scaling global technology companies & the evolution of identity & access management & the founder of a technology consulting firm. In an era defined by remote work & the rapid rise of agentic AI, the concepts of identity & security are shifting beneath our feet. As AI agents begin to act on our behalf, how do we maintain control, responsibility, & security? If an AI agent executes a transaction or accesses a database, who is truly holding the keys? Antoine brings a unique perspective from the front lines of this transition, from pioneering decentralized 2FA & password management at MYKI to driving global strategy & partner ecosystems at JumpCloud. Join us at the Macktez office, after work, over light snacks & sips, for an exploratory conversation on the challenges of scaling fast-growing global companies & how different security architectures impact our long-term safety in a cloud-first world. We will dive into the shifting landscape of encryption, the unique hurdles of managing remote-first organizations, & what it truly means to "identity" ourselves in the age of AI. Photography, audio, & video recording may occur at this event & by attending you consent to such recording media & its release, publication, exhibition, or reproduction. Event StructureWe ask that guests arrive between 7-7:30 pm to minimize disruption during the talk. 7 pm - Doors open, opportunity to mingle over snacks & sips with other attendees7:30 pm - Guests take their seats for the talk8:15 pm - Informal mixer resumes On AttendanceWe have a limited capacity. We fire at the synapses that connect each topic to other fields of interest & to our individual lives. events.name: The AI Briefing By Startup Grind: Who Owns The Data Layer Behind Enterprise AI
events.description: The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise.  This month's source: The Formula for Agentic AI Value: Applied AI Index 2026 (Boston Consulting Group - Sep 2026) Secondary sources: 5 Emerging Trends in Enterprise Data & AI (The Modern Data Company - Aug 2026) Agentic context layers (VentureBeat Intelligence - Oct 2026) Most of the money behind enterprise AI no longer runs through IT. BCG surveyed 1,330 CxOs & senior executives. AI spending has more than tripled, to 3.3% of revenue, & 2.8 points of it sit outside the enterprise IT budget. Business units generate about two-thirds of the value AI creates. So who owns the data their agents run on? BCG says the gap between leaders & everyone else has moved up the stack, to whether a company's data is current, consistently defined, trustworthy, & managed with clear ownership. It tells companies to keep their definitions, business rules & decision logic in a layer they control & could move to another vendor. VentureBeat's August survey points the other way. 98% of companies running retrieval in production use at least one system someone else built, & 2% name building & owning their context layer as their likely direction. 64% have already caught an AI agent giving a confidently wrong answer because of their own company's data.  The Mission: Deciding who owns the definitions, rules & context your AI runs on This series has spent the year on readiness: how fast enterprises adopted, where leadership's confidence outran results, how governance fell behind agents, & whether the workforce was ready. October's discussion turned to a question none of those sessions answered: who owns the data layer? We'll test BCG's advice against what data teams report from the inside. 61% call a reliable context layer critical for AI agents, & 16% engineer one on purpose.  The Format: The numbers: BCG's spending & ownership data, & where a self-reported executive survey stops being evidence. Cross-pollinated debate: Who owns it in your org? IT, the data team, the business unit paying for the agent, or the model vendor whose stack holds the context. The semantic layer problem: In VentureBeat's survey, companies running or building a semantic layer were about twice as likely to report a confidently wrong agent answer (78% vs. 37%). events.name: Startup Pitch Mixer
events.description: Join our Pitch & Networking Night in New York! We design Pitch & Networking nights to help founders sharpen their thinking through direct, candid feedback, & to give strong investors access to serious teams. The pitch session comes with structured networking before & after. WHAT TO EXPECT- Startups pitch live & get focused feedback from angels & VC partners- Structured networking before & after the pitches- Founders, entrepreneurs & operators networking, exchanging ideas & building connections- Active investors & venture scouts discovering the best startups early WHO YOU WILL MEET- Founders- Investors, VC partners & venture scouts- Marketers, salespeople & business advisors- Industry disruptors & AI experts- Entrepreneurs from Europe, Asia & the UK AGENDA18:00 - 18:30 Registration & casual networking18:30 - 19:00 Kickoff & interactive networking19:00 - 19:50 Startup pitch session (5 min per pitch + Q&A)19:50 - 21:00 Chill & networking over refreshments FOR INVESTORSComplimentary tickets are available to institutional investors, angels & venture scouts with a proven track record. If you'd like access to our database of promising startups or want to mentor our best teams, fill out the Investor Application Form & our team will contact you. WANT TO PITCH?4-6 selected founders pitch to a panel of investors & experts, each followed by a short Q&A.- Buy a Pitch Ticket & fill out the Pitch Application Form with your deck- Spots are limited, & founders are selected in advance- A pitch deck is required. We share our pitching guide & offer coaching if you'd like it- The best startups are featured on our social media & in our investor newsletter DRESS CODESmart casual. Bring good energy. FAQCan I pitch?Yes. Buy a Pitch Ticket & fill out the Pitch Application Form. We'll contact you to approve your pitch. You get 5 minutes plus audience Q&A. How does the pitch go?You present on stage for 5 minutes, covering your idea, business model, target market & investment ask, followed by a short Q&A. Do investors get free tickets?Yes. Apply via the form or email hello@startupvalley.club & we'll issue a complimentary ticket for you & your team. Can I request a refund?Yes, up to 1 day before the event. Request it on the platform where you bought your ticket, or email hello@startupvalley.club ABOUT STARTUP VALLEYStartup Valley is a global event organizer that has hosted pitch nights in 25 cities since 2023: 850 events & 40,000 attendees so far. We have strategic partnerships with VC funds in the US, Europe & Asia. Questions or partnerships: hello@startupvalley.club

events.name: Founder Pitch Clinic
events.description: Join us at Fabrik NYC in DUMBO, Brooklyn for an in-person, hands-on pitch clinic designed to help founders become more confident on stage & sharpen the way they pitch to investors. Whether you are preparing for a fundraising round, an investor meeting, or your next demo day, you will learn practical tools to communicate your story with greater confidence, clarity, & impact. The clinic features two focused, 30-minute workshops covering how you show up & what you say. Don't Calm Down with Dave Wolovsky In this interactive workshop, Dave will share practical exercises to help you compose yourself when pitching, work with pressure rather than against it, & perform with greater presence in high-stakes moments. Dave is a Cognitive Performance Coach with an MS in Neuroscience & Education from Columbia University. He coaches founders on focus & daily energy management & serves as a StartX accelerator mentor. Learn more at https://effortwise.com/founders. The Art of Pitching to Attract Investors with Anthony Rose Anthony will break down how to communicate your vision & opportunity & present your business in a way that resonates with investors. Anthony is the founder & CEO of SeedLegals, the legaltech platform used by more than 50,000 startups to get investment-ready, run funding rounds, & handle legal needs. Before SeedLegals, his career included leading BBC iPlayer. Wired Magazine's 2009 cover story called him The Man Who Saved the BBC. Come ready to learn, practice, & leave with techniques you can use in your next pitch. The room seats 100. Hosted by SeedLegals, Meera Mawkin, Dave Wolovsky, & Fabrik NYC. Presented with Propel Earth Original event & registration details https://luma.com/dehgirvb The exact address is available after registering on the original Luma page.
