events.name: AI Content System
events.description: Time Rich presents a working session, hosted by Ella Molony Cook, with co-hosting partner Wispr Flow & presenting partner Stanley. It opens with a short panel on why trust + distribution is now your moat. Then you build your content system in three parts: capture, context, create. You schedule your posts before you leave, so next week is handled. Every guest gets six months of Wispr Pro & Stanley. WHO IT'S FORFounders, business owners & investors who post in bursts, or know they should post more, & want content that sounds like them without writing every word. THE PANEL: YOUR MOAT IS YOUR DISTRIBUTIONA short conversation with investors, founders & ex-Google/YouTube on why visibility, trust & authority matter more than ever. WHAT GETS BUILTCapture. You'll set up Wispr Flow & brief your agent by voice instead of typing. Your best ideas sit in voice notes that never turn into posts, because nothing keeps running when you're busy. Your calls, voice notes & talks become raw material, & we pull ten stories out of your own words.Context. A tone of voice brief, the words you never use, & a call to action matched to each story.Create. Content agents that draft, repurpose across platforms & schedule. By the end, a week of posts is scheduled & the system is set up to fill the next one. Rather have it built for you? The Stanley team will be in the room. Just ask. WHAT TO BRING Laptop, charger & phone. Setup runs on iMessage or WhatsApp. One recording: a talk, a podcast, a call or a voice note Your three best published posts The one thing you want every post to drive: a booked call, a newsletter sign-up or a product AGENDA6:00-6:30 PM  Doors open, meet other founders6:30-6:35 PM  Welcome from Ella6:35-6:55 PM  Panel: your moat is your distribution6:55-8:20 PM  The build: capture, context, create8:20-9:00 PM  Q&A, drinks & mingling POWERED BY STANLEYStanley is an AI Head of Content. You text it a voice note, it drafts in your voice, & it repurposes whatever already performed. Stanley is our presenting partner for the night, so everyone builds on it live. OUR PARTNERTime Rich runs on voice, powered by Wispr FlowWispr Flow is our co-hosting partner. You'll talk to your agents instead of typing to them, & every guest leaves with six months of Wispr Pro. THE ROOMElla Molony Cook is an Australian 4x founder with 1 exit & an investor in Anthropic. Founder of Time Rich a media & AI education platform. Has a community of over 63K+ subscribers on Substack filled with founders, SMBs, angel investors, leaders & has hosted 250+ founder & investor experiences. Max Rivera is an angel investor & GP at GHOST Angels, a fund of Snapchat alumni backing early-stage consumer AI startups. He led global partnerships at Snap from pre-IPO to a $120B public company. Today he leads partnerships for Microsoft AI. Aishwarya Balaji is a 2x founder, venture fund advisor, investor & global speaker. She has spotted & built for emerging markets again & again, from ed-tech & Web3 to non-alc & the creator economy. Rodolphe Kdderitzsch is on the Stanley team. He's ex-Google/YouTube & Squarespace, & a startup founder. TIME RICH CLUBWhere founders, creators & investors come to invest in themselves, their relationships, & building a system to become Time Rich. Whether you're building a company, backing your next deal, or just getting started, this is where you do it alongside people who are building too. Inside the Club: Private conversations on investing, entrepreneurship, building your brand, time hacks & running your life on AI Fireside chats with family offices, exited founders & thought leaders A network of founders, creators & investors who build companies & allocate capital Seats are limited & we read every application.

events.description: Join Propel Earth for a private dinner with funded early-stage founders in NYC focused on IP law, patents, AI, ownership, and investor diligence.This is not a webinar.This is an intimate founder dinner for people building real companies who want to better understand how intellectual property affects fundraising, product development, defensibility, and long-term company value.Most founders do not think about IP until it becomes a problem.A competitor files first.An investor flags a gap in diligence.A contractor owns code the company thought it owned.An AI tool creates uncertainty around who actually owns the core product.This dinner is designed to help founders avoid those mistakes early while meeting other high-quality founders in the same stage of building.Over dinner, well discuss the IP decisions that matter in the first few years of a startup, including patents, trademarks, trade secrets, AI-generated work, contractor ownership, fundraising diligence, and what founders should have documented before the stakes get higher.Expect a curated room, real conversation, and a chance to build relationships with other early-stage funded founders in NYC.Dinner is complimentary for approved guests.Who Should AttendFunded foundersTechnical foundersEarly-stage startup operatorsAI, SaaS, software, marketplace, biotech, fintech, and product-led foundersFounders preparing for investor diligenceFounders working with contractors, agencies, developers, or outside contributorsFounders who want to understand what they should protect before it With decades of experience in capital formation and investing, he has helped numerous emerging-growth companies secure funding and pursue their strategic objectives.Jay brings a broad, cross-sector perspective, with experience supporting companies in agentic AI, advertising technology, healthcare services, and renewable energy. Through INTE Securities, an SEC-registered and FINRA-member broker-dealer, he advises companies and family offices on capital-raising initiatives. As a Special Advisor to SOJA Ventures, he plays a key role in securing capital for the firms portfolio companies and supporting their long-term growth., FINRA member broker-dealer connecting issuers with accredited and institutional capital.Moshe Neuman (Founder, MN Ventures): Moshe is an angel investor, advisor and startup guru who has mentored more than 100 founders. Hes now building MN Ventures, a new VC fund raising $100M, as he moves from angel investing into running his own fund. He backs companies at the very earliest stages.Triet Leminh: Principal, LMT Partners: Lawyer, founder, and investor backing pre-seed to Series A founders building in enterprise and regulated industries. Writing $200K$300K checks.DJ Patel (Head of Direct Investing, UV: DJ leads direct investments at UV, which manages $75M$100M. He backs Seed to Series A companies in healthtech, fintech and AI infrastructure, with typical checks of $500K$600K.Gonzalo Quincot (Founder, Sinober): Sinober is a financial intelligence platform that combines public and private market intelligence with institutional-grade methodology, corporate finance and proprietary AI tools to sharpen investment and capital decisions for individuals and businesses. Invests in automation, robotics, data centers and applied AI.Dr. David Cunic (Serial Entrepreneur & Investor, UCS Advisor [confirm]): A 17-time founder who has built companies across 3 countries and 8 states, with 7 exits. He represents a network of more than 1,000 angel investors who are always looking for quality deal flow. He also helps companies at the friends-and-family, pre-seed and seed stages raise capital, writing checks himself.All 6 senior investors confirmed.Part of building rooms is making sure real capital is present. Six investors actively deploying writing capital will be joining. We value intentional networking & community.If you're here to meet the best of the best, this is the room.Why we do thisOur intent is simple: bring good, smart humans together, put active investors in the same room as incredible founders. events.name: Ugly Talks - Failure Is Key To Success
events.description: Failure gets talked about like it is part of the journey. That is the lie. The real thing is messier. Missed bets. Wrong hires. Near-breakdowns. The week you stop sleeping & start doing math at 3:00 AM. Founders are expected to eat it quietly & keep moving. No language for what happened. No playbook for what to do next. Ugly Talk is a founder room for the part nobody posts. No fluff. No consultants. Just builders with scars, talking about the call that cost them.  Why you should be in this room.Hear what failure cost them. Then hear what they did next. Learn how experienced founders separate self-worth from outcomes when things go sideways. Spot the patterns behind repeat mistakes. And the early signals you should not ignore. Leave with a few concrete moves for the next hard week. Not inspiration. Meet other founders in the thick of it. The ones who are still building.  What's on the table.Dare to suck: how permission to fail unlocks real progress The moment things broke: missed opportunities, wrong turns, near-breakdowns, & what changed afterward Failure vs identity: separating self-worth from outcomes Treating setbacks as data: what to measure, what to ignore, & how to decide fast Rejection as redirection: how founders find the signal in the no Habits for staying focused & resilient when everything feels uncertain  Run of show6:00 - 6:30 PM: Reception (check-in & light drinks) 6:30 - 6:40 PM: Welcome remarks 6:40 - 6:50 PM: Keynote Speech by Ben McKean 6:50 - 7:30 PM: Panel Discussion 7:30 - 7:45 PM: Audience Q&A 7:45 - 8:00 PM: Mixer + snacks & drinks  Featured speakers.Ben McKean - Founder & Chief Executive Officer, Hungryroot Ben McKean is the Founder & CEO of Hungryroot, a personalized healthy eating assistant that uses AI to make meal planning, food shopping, & nutrition effortless & enjoyable. Prior to Hungryroot, Ben was a Vice President & General Manager at Groupon, overseeing their food & beverage business. Ben came to Groupon through the acquisition of Savored, which he founded in 2009. Savored was the nation's leading provider of yield management technology to the restaurant industry, used by over two thousand restaurants nationwide & nearly one million diners. Prior to Savored, Ben worked in Merrill Lynch's technology investment banking group. Ben is a graduate of Georgetown University & currently lives in North Carolina with his wife & kids. Stephen McKinney - Founder & CEO, Bizbe Stephen McKinney is a serial entrepreneur with over a decade of experience across tech, marketing, & logistics. He's the founder & CEO of Bizbe.com, an AI-native business brokerage & lower middle market M&A firm based in New York & Miami. A former contestant on ABC's Shark Tank, Steve previously founded & led Retty Logistics, a seven-figure last-mile delivery company acquired by DXP Logistics & Webster Logistics. Dmitry Koltunov - Founder & CEO, Arbor Dmitry Koltunov is a serial entrepreneur, technologist, educator, & storyteller. He is the founder & CEO of Arbor, an AI-powered content engine that helps enterprises scale their communications with video & beyond. Previously, he co-founded & served as CTO of ALICE, a hospitality technology company that grew into a global industry leader before being acquired by Expedia Group. Dmitry also leads the New York City chapter of the Startup Leadership Program, New York's oldest startup fellowship, whose 500+ alumni have collectively raised more than $1 billion in funding across every industry imaginable. He is passionate about helping founders navigate the challenges of building & scaling companies. Outside of technology, Dmitry is an award-winning songwriter & theater producer currently developing a new musical for Broadway. He holds degrees in Computer Science & Economics from the University of Pennsylvania & is a CFA charterholder. Gwendolyn von Rahn - Co-Founder & CEO, Sweetling Health Gwendolyn von Rahn is the Co-Founder & CEO of Sweetling Health, an postpartum intelligence platform built for at-risk & hard-to-reach populations. She's a second-time exited founder, an award-winning marketer with over a decade of experience building consumer brands for women, Gwen led creative & brand teams at Vogue, InStyle, & POPSUGAR before founding & scaling a mission-driven consumer brand into Nordstrom distribution that raised over $1M for melanoma research through the Melanoma Research Foundation. She holds a Cornell Johnson MBA & founded Sweetling from her own lived experience with the postpartum care gap.  Who's hosting it.Victoria Yampolsky - President, The Startup Station Victoria Yampolsky is the Founder & President of The Startup Station, a strategic CFO advisory firm & financial education platform for startups. She partners with founders on financial strategy, modeling, & fundraising, having supported over 150 companies across 15 industries in raising more than $50M in venture capital. Victoria is also an advocate for female founders & access to capital, & has taught finance to more than 20,000 entrepreneurs through programs including the Bank of America Institute for Women's Entrepreneurship at Cornell. She began her career at Deutsche Bank & Capgemini, & holds a BS in Computer Science from Cornell University & an MBA from Columbia Business School.  Who's getting in.Early-stage tech founders & operators navigating uncertainty, setbacks, or the emotional weight of building a company. Expected roles may include: Founders & co-founders (pre-seed to Series A) Operators (COO, Head of Ops, Chief of Staff) Product & Engineering leads building through ambiguity Growth & GTM leads working through missed targets & pivots Finance & strategy leaders supporting founder decision-making  Who's backing this.The Startup Station The Startup Station - is a CFO advisory & financial education platform for early-stage startups. We help early-stage founders build investor-ready financials & tell their funding story with confidence. In the past decade, we've helped 150+ founders raise over $50M & educated 20,000+ entrepreneurs worldwide. The Startup Station also runs Speed Pitch, an exclusive investor-founder matchmaking event series for early-stage startups where founders are matched with 3 investors by sector, stage, & check size. Mind Your Business Every attendee will receive a free copy of keynote speaker Ben McKean's Mind Your Business. Mind Your Business is a practical parable for people rethinking work as AI advances. Set over a four-day retreat, it follows six participants competing for funding to bring one vision to life. As they evaluate six competing proposals, they begin to confront deeper questions about what gives them energy, who they serve, & what they uniquely contribute. With founder/CEOs Ben McKean (Hungryroot)

Nov 02 (Mon)  @ 06:00 PM

Venue, To Be Announced

Failure gets talked about like it is part of the journey. That is the lie. The real thing is messier. Missed bets. Wrong hires. Near-breakdowns. The week you stop sleeping & start doing math at 3:00 AM. Founders are expected to eat it quietly & keep moving. No language for what happened. No playbook for what to do next. Ugly Talk is a founder room for the part nobody posts. No fluff. No consultants. Just builders with scars, talking about the call that cost them.  Why you should be in this room.Hear what failure cost them. Then hear what they did next. Learn how experienced founders separate self-worth from outcomes when things go sideways. Spot the patterns behind repeat mistakes. And the early signals you should not ignore. Leave with a few concrete moves for the next hard week. Not inspiration. Meet other founders in the thick of it. The ones who are still building.  What's on the table.Dare to suck: how permission to fail unlocks real progress The moment things broke: missed opportunities, wrong turns, near-breakdowns, & what changed afterward Failure vs identity: separating self-worth from outcomes Treating setbacks as data: what to measure, what to ignore, & how to decide fast Rejection as redirection: how founders find the signal in the no Habits for staying focused & resilient when everything feels uncertain  Run of show6:00 - 6:30 PM: Reception (check-in & light drinks) 6:30 - 6:40 PM: Welcome remarks 6:40 - 6:50 PM: Keynote Speech by Ben McKean 6:50 - 7:30 PM: Panel Discussion 7:30 - 7:45 PM: Audience Q&A 7:45 - 8:00 PM: Mixer + snacks & drinks  Featured speakers.Ben McKean - Founder & Chief Executive Officer, Hungryroot Ben McKean is the Founder & CEO of Hungryroot, a personalized healthy eating assistant that uses AI to make meal planning, food shopping, & nutrition effortless & enjoyable. Prior to Hungryroot, Ben was a Vice President & General Manager at Groupon, overseeing their food & beverage business. Ben came to Groupon through the acquisition of Savored, which he founded in 2009. Savored was the nation's leading provider of yield management technology to the restaurant industry, used by over two thousand restaurants nationwide & nearly one million diners. Prior to Savored, Ben worked in Merrill Lynch's technology investment banking group. Ben is a graduate of Georgetown University & currently lives in North Carolina with his wife & kids. Stephen McKinney - Founder & CEO, Bizbe Stephen McKinney is a serial entrepreneur with over a decade of experience across tech, marketing, & logistics. He's the founder & CEO of Bizbe.com, an AI-native business brokerage & lower middle market M&A firm based in New York & Miami. A former contestant on ABC's Shark Tank, Steve previously founded & led Retty Logistics, a seven-figure last-mile delivery company acquired by DXP Logistics & Webster Logistics. Dmitry Koltunov - Founder & CEO, Arbor Dmitry Koltunov is a serial entrepreneur, technologist, educator, & storyteller. He is the founder & CEO of Arbor, an AI-powered content engine that helps enterprises scale their communications with video & beyond. The pitch session comes with structured networking before & after. WHAT TO EXPECT- Startups pitch live & get focused feedback from angels & VC partners- Structured networking before & after the pitches- Founders, entrepreneurs & operators networking, exchanging ideas & building connections- Active investors & venture scouts discovering the best startups early WHO YOU WILL MEET- Founders- Investors, VC partners & venture scouts- Marketers, salespeople & business advisors- Industry disruptors & AI experts- Entrepreneurs from Europe, Asia & the UK AGENDA18:00 - 18:30  Registration & casual networking18:30 - 19:00  Kickoff & interactive networking19:00 - 19:50  Startup pitch session (5 min per pitch + Q&A)19:50 - 21:00  Chill & networking over refreshments FOR INVESTORSComplimentary tickets are available to institutional investors, angels & venture scouts with a proven track record. We have strategic partnerships with VC funds in the US, Europe & Asia. Questions or partnerships: hello@startupvalley.club

Connect, converse, & collaborate with peers driven by a common passion for advancing healthcare through technology.  About our Panelists: Steven Levy Steven is a Partner at Unorthodox Ventures where he focuses on investing in venture stage MedTech companies. Steven has executed over 100 transactions with aggregate deal value in excess of $30 billion. Steven headed the M&A efforts for the Financial Sponsors practice at Lehman Brothers, covered Financial sponsors & headed the Consumer M&A efforts at Cowen & covered Financial Sponsors, led execution on technology & consumer M&A transactions & headed up the firm's investment banking efforts in Israel at Stifel. Steven received his B.A. from Binghamton University & graduated as a member of Phi Beta Kappa & received his M.B.A. from the Wharton School, at the University of Pennsylvania. Bryan Spielman is a Managing Partner at Northwell Health Equity Partners. He is a seasoned C-suite executive with a track record of driving multi-billion-dollar value creation across the healthcare & technology sectors. Most recently, as Chief Growth Officer at Advarra, he spearheaded the company's $5 billion sale to Blackstone & CPPIB. Prior to that, at Medidata, he helped scale the company from a $400 million to over $2.3 billion market valuation. Bryan spent 12 years in investment banking at Centerview Partners, UBS, & Bear Stearns, advising on over $50 billion in transactions. He holds an MBA from NYU Stern School of Business & a BA from the University of Pennsylvania. Host/Moderator: Maria Putilina, MD, MS, is a medical advisor & innovator, boasting over a decade of driving transformative change within the healthcare industry. We advise on high-profile cross-border matters while providing the kind of personal attention to clients that is typically found at boutiques. Our enterprising & tenacious lawyers serve our clients around the globe from offices in key financial centers in the U.S. & the U.K., & have been recognized by, among others, Chambers USA, Legal 500, Benchmark Litigation, & Law360 for excellence in their fields. To learn more about our Emerging Growth Companies & Venture Capital group, please visit us here. About the organisers Audrey Guazzone is an innovation & commercialization strategist who helps medtech & digital health companies navigate international growth. Through LeanLia, she combines market validation, commercialization strategy, & hands-on business development to help companies grow in the U.S. She is passionate about connecting healthcare innovators & ecosystems across America & Europe. Maria Putilina, MD, MS, is a medical advisor & innovator, boasting over a decade of driving transformative change within the healthcare industry. Her expertise spans Business Administration, Medicine, & Science, which she honed in healthcare consulting, helping companies build & execute innovation strategies. Bailey Morgan is a healthtech leader who blends clinical expertise with business strategy to drive healthcare innovation & growth. A former speech-language pathologist, she has helped raise over $10 million in capital, led go-to-market teams across SaaS & CPG companies, & closed more than $2 million in technology sales. As Chief of Staff at Groth Pain & Spine, she leads change management & technology integration across a growing provider network, while also advising healthcare technology companies & serving as Director & Treasurer of a nonprofit supporting individuals living with dementia & their caregivers. Alex Koshykov is a co-founder of BeKey & a digital health expert who constantly shares news, introduces promising technologies, & promotes secure software & hardware for the healthcare industry on his YouTube channel. Additionally to that, he is a co-founder of YODD, a medical device startup. Additional Information By signing up, your email will be automatically added to the Health2Tech newsletter with news & upcoming events - but don't worry, we won't flood your inbox! ;) Also, just a note that this event might be photographed or filmed. If we do capture some moments, Health2Tech may use the photos or videos for marketing & communication purposes. By registering, you're giving us the thumbs up for using your image for these reasons.

events.name: Drinks & Hacking: IT Happy Hour with The Objective-See Foundation
events.description: Join Rippling IT & The Objective-See Foundation for a happy hour at the Rippling NYC office. Over drinks & light bites, enjoy networking with your fellow IT pros & enjoy a presentation from Patrick Wardle, Co-Founder of the Objective-See Foundation, titled: Your Agent, My Orders: Hacking ChatGPT. A bit more about Patrick's presentation: AI agents need broad access to our files, accounts, & devices, making them prime targets for hackers. We took a closer look at ChatGPT's macOS desktop app & uncovered vulnerabilities that allow attackers to turn your trusted AI assistant against you. The impact? Attackers could hijack your Dot, take over your OpenAI account, access protected files, & more. Worse, these attacks present new challenges for traditional security tools: when an AI agent is compromised, malicious activity can look just like the agent doing its job. We'll demo what happens when ChatGPT gets hacked, discuss why AI agents pose new security challenges, & explore what all this means for Mac admins & the future of endpoint security. You can read more about this in NYT & Wired - & we hope to see you in-person for the full presentation. See you soon! A bit about us: Rippling IT amplifies your abilities & supercharges your skills. Control the entire user lifecycle in one system with fully built Identity, Device, & Inventory management tools, & 500+ integrations-including custom SCIM & SAML. Simplify, secure, & scale all from one single platform. Objective-See is a non-profit foundation focused on macOS security, driven by the mission to create free tools, grow & support a global community of students, researchers, & defenders, & advance Apple security through education, research, collaboration, & opportunity, around the world.

Bring good energy.  Join our event & secure your ticket today! About us: Startup Valley is a global event organizer hosting pitch nights in 25 cities since 2023. Refunds are available if requested at least 1 day before the event start time. events.name: Climate Scaling Summit
events.description: The true entry points for startups working with government Join LACI at BATWorks & The Trust for Governors Island for a Climate Scaling Summit focused on one critical inflection point: how climate startups break into government as a customer, regulator, & partner. Securing contracts with the government can feel opaque to founders, but true entry points exist even if they are not always obvious to a first-time founder. This session demystifies how startups can work with government agencies & offers a valuable opportunity for founders to ask agencies & entities for feedback, technical support, & opportunities to scale. The morning opens with a fireside chat/panel, followed by five hands-on workshops covering: LegislationPermitting & CodePilot KPIs for Government AgenciesCapital Projects & Public-Private DevelopmentEducation & Workforce This is the final of four Climate Scaling Summits hosted by LACI at BATWorks in 2026, all under the theme of accelerating commercialization of clean energy innovation in NY by focusing on common problems faced by startups after the pilot stage. About LACI & The Trust for Governors Island LACI has deployed $25M in cleantech pilots over the past four years, from first commercial deployments to the nation's first zero-emissions delivery zone & is now supercharging the Pilots at BAT program & deeper deployment of the LACI Cleantech Debt Fund.  The Trust for Governors Island's Climate Piloting Program offers early-stage companies & innovators the opportunity to test & scale climate products & services in a real-world environment. Since its launch in 2023, the program has advanced projects in living shorelines, clean water, circular economy, buildings, energy, air quality, & urban agriculture-opening doors to new customers, suppliers, talent, investors, & public agency partnerships. The program is a core initiative of the Trust's Center for Climate Solutions, an initiative dedicated to accelerating equitable climate solutions for cities on Governors Island. Visit www.govisland.org/climate to learn more.

events.name: Trajectories - Facts, Fictions & Futures Of Spacefaring Societies
events.description: Science fiction has long imagined humanity's path beyond Earth, from post-scarcity utopias to contested frontiers to desperate exoduses. Which way are we headed? This week's interactive community conversation tests those visions against the technological, economic, societal, & cultural forces shaping our spacefaring future right now. Because the future isn't something we predict but something we choose, the question isn't just where we're headed, but where we dare to go. OUR FACILITATORVince Lucich, an engineer & startup founder whose work involves building spacecraft for the emerging orbital economy, will lead us on this idea exploration of the future. WHO'S IT FOR?Idea people. Founders. Builders. Creatives. Researchers. The Curious. And their Supporters --------------FORMATOur format explores ideas together through our diverse backgrounds, while building relationships & community through the process. We want you to talk to each other, instead of just being talked at. 6:00PM - Settle in, grab a drink & some food at the bar, & meet some new people before we start our event. 6:30PM - Our conversation begins with our facilitator presenting the knowledge & context for the conversation along the way. The conversation between attendees will explore from surface level understandings, to deep implications & future iterations. 7:45PM - Meet & connect with new people, catch up with people you haven't seen in a while, discover all the different ways you overlap. And then just hang out, grab a drink, play some pool or ping pong! Or stay for the band afterwards! Our desire is to be the antithesis of NYC's corporate panel & transactional networking culture. We aim to create a vibrant idea & build space in NYC that focuses on the passion & values beyond the money & the hustle.

events.name: Data By Design
events.description: In conversation with Shannon Mattern. P&T Knitwear is pleased to welcome Lauren Klein, Tanvi Sharma, & Silas Munro to celebrate & discuss the release of their book Data by Design, which explores how the history of data visualization holds the key to designing a more just future. They will be in conversation with Shannon Mattern, & will sign books after the talk! Doors open at 6:30pm with the talk starting closer to 7:00pm. Come early & grab a drink from the P&T Cafe! Tickets & books are available both on eventbrite & at the door. Housekeeping notes: This is a ticketed in-store event with limited amphitheater-style seating.Doors open at 6:30pm, with the talk starting around 7:00pm.Cost of a book bundle ticket reflects the total cost of the feature event book (MSRP plus tax). Each book bundle ticket guarantees ticket holders one (1) copy of the feature event book.The talk will be followed by a book signing. Books signed at P&T Knitwear events must be purchased from P&T Knitwear.If you would like a signed copy & cannot attend the event, we're happy to take your pre-order. We ship most places!About the authors:Lauren Klein is Professor of Data & Decision Sciences & English at Emory University, where she also directs the Digital Humanities Lab & the Atlanta Interdisciplinary AI Network. Her research brings together computational & critical methods to explore questions of gender, race, & justice, both in early America & today. Klein is the author (with Catherine D'Ignazio) of the award-winning Data Feminism (MIT Press, 2020), & the editor (with Matthew K. Gold) of Debates in the Digital Humanities (Univ. of Minnesota Press), among other books & papers. Her next book, Data by Design: Visualization & Power from Abolition to the Dawn of Data Science (MIT Press), will be out in October 2026.  Silas Munro is a designer, artist, writer, curator, surfer, & descendant of the Banyole people of Eastern Uganda. He founded the design studio Polymode, whose clients include MoMA, the MET, Nike, & the Hammer. Munro is the curator & author of Strikethrough: Typographic Messages of Protest at Letterform Archive & the co-curator of Reverberations: Lineages in Design History at the Ford Foundation Gallery. He contributed to W. E. B. Du Bois's Data Portraits: Visualizing Black America, & co-authored the first BIPOC-centered design history course, Black Design in America: African Americans & the African Diaspora in Graphic Design 19th-21st Century. His visual art was recently exhibited at Data Consciousness: Reframing Blackness in Contemporary Print at Print Center New York. Tanvi Sharma is a design technologist working at the intersection of data, aesthetics, & the humanities. She is currently an Art Director at Apple & co-author of Data by Design (MIT Press, 2026). She has previously worked at Pentagram, Public Policy Lab, & Spotify. She lives in Harlem, NY, with her two cats, Yuchi & Bubbles. More at tanvi.network.   About the moderator:Shannon Mattern is the Director of Creative Research at the Metropolitan New York Library Council, a state-founded, member-supported non-profit linking hundreds of libraries & archives across the city. Previously, she held tenured full professorships in media studies, anthropology, & art history at The New School & the University of Pennsylvania. She is the author of four books, the (co-)editor of six collections, & the author of over 100 articles & chapters about urban technology, knowledge infrastructures, maps, maintenance, data art, & other heterogenous subjects. She was the 2025 Kluge Chair in Modern Culture at the Library of Congress & the 2025 Design Indexer in residence at the Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum. You can find her at wordsinspace.net.

In conversation with Shannon Mattern. P&T Knitwear is pleased to welcome Lauren Klein, Tanvi Sharma, & Silas Munro to celebrate & discuss the release of their book Data by Design, which explores how the history of data visualization holds the key to designing a more just future. They will be in conversation with Shannon Mattern, & will sign books after the talk! Doors open at 6:30pm with the talk starting closer to 7:00pm. Come early & grab a drink from the P&T Cafe! Tickets & books are available both on eventbrite & at the door. Housekeeping notes: This is a ticketed in-store event with limited amphitheater-style seating.Doors open at 6:30pm, with the talk starting around 7:00pm.Cost of a book bundle ticket reflects the total cost of the feature event book (MSRP plus tax). Each book bundle ticket guarantees ticket holders one (1) copy of the feature event book.The talk will be followed by a book signing. Books signed at P&T Knitwear events must be purchased from P&T Knitwear.If you would like a signed copy & cannot attend the event, we're happy to take your pre-order. We ship most places!About the authors:Lauren Klein is Professor of Data & Decision Sciences & English at Emory University, where she also directs the Digital Humanities Lab & the Atlanta Interdisciplinary AI Network. Her research brings together computational & critical methods to explore questions of gender, race, & justice, both in early America & today. Klein is the author (with Catherine D'Ignazio) of the award-winning Data Feminism (MIT Press, 2020), & the editor (with Matthew K. Gold) of Debates in the Digital Humanities (Univ. of Minnesota Press), among other books & papers. Her next book, Data by Design: Visualization & Power from Abolition to the Dawn of Data Science (MIT Press), will be out in October 2026.  Silas Munro is a designer, artist, writer, curator, surfer, & descendant of the Banyole people of Eastern Uganda. He founded the design studio Polymode, whose clients include MoMA, the MET, Nike, & the Hammer. Munro is the curator & author of Strikethrough: Typographic Messages of Protest at Letterform Archive & the co-curator of Reverberations: Lineages in Design History at the Ford Foundation Gallery. He contributed to W. E. B. Du Bois's Data Portraits: Visualizing Black America, & co-authored the first BIPOC-centered design history course, Black Design in America: African Americans & the African Diaspora in Graphic Design 19th-21st Century. His visual art was recently exhibited at Data Consciousness: Reframing Blackness in Contemporary Print at Print Center New York. Tanvi Sharma is a design technologist working at the intersection of data, aesthetics, & the humanities. She is currently an Art Director at Apple & co-author of Data by Design (MIT Press, 2026). She has previously worked at Pentagram, Public Policy Lab, & Spotify. She lives in Harlem, NY, with her two cats, Yuchi & Bubbles. More at tanvi.network.   About the moderator:Shannon Mattern is the Director of Creative Research at the Metropolitan New York Library Council, a state-founded, member-supported non-profit linking hundreds of libraries & archives across the city. Previously, she held tenured full professorships in media studies, anthropology, & art history at The New School & the University of Pennsylvania. She is the author of four books, the (co-)editor of six collections, & the author of over 100 articles & chapters about urban technology, knowledge infrastructures, maps, maintenance, data art, & other heterogenous subjects. She was the 2025 Kluge Chair in Modern Culture at the Library of Congress & the 2025 Design Indexer in residence at the Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum. You can find her at wordsinspace.net.

events.name: Powering The Transition - Closing Skills Gap In New Energy Infrastructure
events.description: In partnership with Schneider Electric, Google, Barclays, LACI & IYF The energy transition is underway - but the workforce needed to deliver it is not keeping pace. Across the full arc of how energy is generated, moved, stored, serviced, & used - spanning utilities, power generation, advanced manufacturing, fleet electrification, data centers, & industrial infrastructure - a persistent & structural challenge has emerged: the skilled trades & technician roles most critical to new energy infrastructure face serious & growing skills gaps, & too often the employers, training providers, & talent leaders working to close them are doing so in isolation. NationSwell, in partnership with Barclays, LACI, IYF, Schneider Electric, & Google is convening a working session at Brooklyn Army Terminal - home to BATWorks, NYC's emerging climate innovation hub - to change that. Bringing together talent leaders, hiring managers, & workforce training providers, this in-person convening will use IYF's proven industry competency framework to surface & validate the most critical skills gaps across the skilled trades workforce driving new energy infrastructure.  The day will move from insight to action. The goal is a shared vocabulary & shared priorities that attendees can take back to their organizations, & use to advocate for the training investments, certifications, & systems changes the new energy infrastructure demands. BATWorks offers a uniquely fitting backdrop: a place where growth-stage climate companies, workforce development, & hands-on innovation converge. Where employers are growing & talent supply can grow with them. Attendees will leave knowing they are not alone in this challenge - & with concrete, validated priorities to guide the next steps.

events.name: Red Carpet Room Launch Party
events.description: If you show up with a backpack or your laptop you will be banned from the event. Please leave backpacks at home. RED CARPET ROOM Formerly Fun HouseHosted by Anwar EnterprisesSaturday, October 31, 2026 Exact address released to confirmed guests 24 hours before doors. About the Event Red Carpet Room is the next chapter of Fun House, rebuilt around a single idea: the people building brands should be building them together. This is a mixer for founders, creators, & investors from the Anwar Events community, gathered in one room with a shared reason to be there. Everyone in attendance is constructing something with their name attached to it. The night is designed so the person who can unblock you is standing a few feet away. We are doing it on Halloween on purpose. The city will be full of parties where nothing happens beyond the party itself. This one gives you a panel worth sitting through, a room worth working, & footage of yourself that you will actually use. Run of Show [7pm] - Doors, check-in, & open networking to start the night[8pm] - Panel: operators who built audiences, companies, & reputations from nothing   SPECIAL GUESTS BEING REVEALED NEXT WEEK [9pm] - Open mixer, with Red Carpet Show interviews running in the back room Who's Coming The typical guest is a founder raising or building, a creator monetizing an audience, or an investor looking for both. Expect crossover from fashion, music, media, tech, art & consumer brands, since that is who the Anwar Events community actually contains. Whether you are hiring, raising, pitching a collaboration, or looking for people who take their work as seriously as you do, you will be in the right room. The Red Carpet Show Throughout the night, Ilias will pull guests aside for on-camera interviews for The Red Carpet Show. There is one question at the center of every interview: how can he help you. Those conversations get cut into content that reaches an audience of 70,000 plus founders, investors, & creators. Sitting down costs you four minutes & can put your company in front of people you would never cold email. Dress Code Halloween night calls for more than a costume assembled at the last minute. Come dressed as the version of yourself the press would photograph, whether that means black tie, full character, or your own blend of both. Cameras run from the door onward, so arrive accordingly. Capacity & Entry Space is limited & the guest list is curated. A confirmed RSVP secures your place only until capacity fills, so arriving early is strongly recommended. Bring a valid ID for check-in at the door. About the Host Ilias Anwar is an entrepreneur, marketer, & community builder based in New York City. He has produced more than 600 events across NYC, LA, & San Francisco, cultivating a network of over 70,000 founders, investors, & creators. His work includes brand partnerships with Google, Red Bull, Andreessen Horowitz, & Universal Music Group, along with activations at NFL Super Bowl Weekend & New York Fashion Week. Today he runs Anwar Enterprises, a venture studio that launches & scales consumer & tech companies through distribution first. If you need to meet someone in this city, they have probably attended one of his events. Partners & Sponsors Creatorsarethenewstudios.comCanvas helps creators, founders, & brands turn ideas into media IP they own. AI agents handle the story, production plan, budget, & distribution, & your first IP is free. Happyboards.comHappyBoards makes chef-built charcuterie boards & grazing tables from locally sourced ingredients. It delivers same-day across 27+ Northeast cities, & HappyBoards is feeding the room tonight.Stay Connected Future Anwar Events drop to the community first. Get on the list at luma.com/iliasanwar & follow along on Instagram, X, & LinkedIn for everything we run next. Community Standards Red Carpet Room is inclusive of gender, sexuality, race, religion, & ability. Discrimination or harassment of any kind will not be tolerated on site. For urgent security concerns during the event, please contact venue staff directly. Disclaimers By attending this event, you agree to the following terms. Photography, Video, & Recording: This event will be photographed, filmed, live-streamed, & audio recorded. By entering the venue, you consent to being captured on camera & to the use of your name, image, voice, statements, & likeness by Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, The Red Carpet Show, & their affiliated partners & sponsors. Marketing & Promotional Use: Any material captured at this event may appear in promotional content, social media, websites, newsletters, press coverage, paid advertising, sponsor recap materials, & future marketing assets, worldwide & in perpetuity, without compensation. Guests waive any right to inspect or approve the finished material before publication. On-Camera Interviews: Participation in The Red Carpet Show is entirely voluntary. Sitting for an interview grants Anwar Enterprises the full right to edit, distribute, & monetize that footage across any platform, in any format, without further approval. Opting Out: If you do not wish to be photographed or filmed, please notify event staff upon arrival & avoid the designated filming areas. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to accommodate your request, though appearance in wide or crowd shots cannot be fully prevented. Guest Policy: This is a private, invitation-only event. RSVPs are non-transferable & entry is subject to ID verification. Organizers reserve the right to refuse entry at their discretion. Capacity & Access: This event has a strict capacity limit. A confirmed RSVP does not guarantee entry once capacity has been reached, so early arrival is strongly encouraged. Code of Conduct: All attendees are expected to conduct themselves professionally & respectfully. Organizers reserve the right to remove any guest whose behavior is disruptive or inappropriate, without refund or recourse. Liability: Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, & the venue are not responsible for loss, theft, or damage to personal property. Attendance is at your own risk. Data & Registration: Information submitted at registration may be shared with event sponsors & partners in accordance with their respective privacy policies. Guests may opt out of sponsor communications at any time. Changes & Cancellations: Event details including time, venue, panelists, & programming are subject to change. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to notify registered guests of any material changes.

events.name: PMAI: Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Sales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. - Bring a computer. You're writing three things tonight.- Most founders can get meetings. The deals die after meeting one.- You'll leave with your buyer in one sentence, a cold email written to a real person, & five questions for your next call. About Farzad, the speaker Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding & generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: The Outliers Summit
events.description: The Outliers Summit 2026We're excited to announce the Outliers Summit. November 5 & 6 in New York City. A two-day gathering for founders, creators, operators, builders, & thinkers bringing unreasonably ambitious ideas to life, hosted by Ankur Nagpal & Andrew Yeung, in partnership with AngelList.  Previously, we called this event the OOO Summit. But this year, we've evolved the brand & doubled the event to reflect what we believe the future will look like. Over the last two years, thousands of ambitious people attended our summit - multi-hyphenates, hybrid creator-entrepreneurs, solo builders, AI-native founders, & even people running companies of one with agents doing the rest. The word to describe this kind of person is Outlier. The type of person who chooses to take the unconventional path & pave their own way. This year, the Outliers Summit will be two full days:  DAY 1: NOVEMBER 5 // HOW OUTLIERS BUILD Tactical sessions where you leave having built the thing yourself - an app, an agent, an audience, a brand.  DAY 2: NOVEMBER 6 // HOW OUTLIERS THINK Off-the-record conversations about the bets & mindsets that separate outliers from everyone else.  SpeakersSam Parr, Founder of My First Million, Hampton, The Hustle (acq for >$25M) Ryan Hoover, Founder of Product Hunt & Weekend Fund Sahil Lavingia, Founder & CEO of Gumroad ($1B paid out to creators) Zach Sims, Co-founder & CEO of Codecademy (acq for >$500M) Andy Dunn, Founder of Bonobos & Pie (acq for >$300M) Nadya Okamoto, Founder of August & Co-Founder of Pie Nat Eliason, Author & Head of Founders School Nik Sharma, Founder of Sharma Brands Carina Hong, Founder of Axiom (raised $200M at a $1.6B val) & many MORE to be announced. & many more ... to be announced.  Who You'll Be In the Room WithAcross 13 events in 2024 & 2025, 4,298 people from 3,083 companies have come through our events. 54% are founders, C-suite, VP+ or investors 39% are founders & CEOs specifically 48% of founders have raised $1M or more 22% come back for two or more of our events They also come from Google, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, Stripe, Ramp, Notion, Palantir, Goldman Sachs, & a16z, & from the several thousand startups that make up the rest of the room. Every guest is reviewed before approval. If you are unreasonably ambitious, we'd love to meet you.  Past speakersSahil Bloom is a New York Times Bestselling Author & one of the pioneers of 'threads' onTwitter Andrew Yang founded the Forward political party in 2021, Venture for America in 2011, & the ex-CEO of Manhattan Prep. Sam Parr is the Founder of The Hustle, Hampton, My First Million. Alex Lieberman is the Co-founder of Morning Brew. Kyla Scanlon is the Founder of Bread. Guillermo Rauch is the CEO of Vercel. Brianne Kimmel is the Founder at Worklife Ventures. Justin Welsh has built his 1-person business to >$2m in revenue per year with 95% profit margins, without hiring a team or increasing his hours Nathan Barry, Founder, CEO of Kit (Formerly ConvertKit)  Why You Should AttendBuild a powerful network of founders, investors, & industry leaders. Unlock growth tactics & stay ahead of the curve-know where the puck is going. Learn how to scale your business-from six to seven figures, or even seven to ten. Grow a profitable lifestyle business or blitzscale your venture-backed startup. Build a powerful personal brand & grow your audience. Master marketing strategies to go viral. Whether you're just starting out or are already an entrepreneur, gain the insights you need to accelerate your success.  Meet the OrganizersAnkur Nagpal has built & sold two companies for nine figures: Teachable for $250M & Carry to AngelList. He's now building USVC alongside Naval Ravikant, a public venture fund opening access to world-class startup investments. Andrew Yeung is the founder of Fibe & The Shortlist NYC. He is also an angel investor & Partner at Next Wave NYC, a pre-seed venture fund. Andrew has hosted over 300 events for 50,000 founders, operators, investors, & tech professionals that were featured by Bloomberg, Business Insider, Fast Company, Fortune Magazine, Axios, Newsweek, & Forbes. Business Insider dubbed him the "Gatsby of Silicon Alley." Pie is the real-life social networking app that helps people turn online connections into real-world plans. Built around events & shared favorites-from run clubs & watch parties to live music & vintage markets-Pie makes it effortless to discover what's happening, invite friends, & show up. With over 300,000 users, Pie is on a mission to defeat social isolation & rebuild in-person community. Pie was named "Apps We Love" & "App of the Day" by Apple & the most promising startup in Chicago by 1871. Learn more at getpie.app. Together, Ankur Nagpal & Andrew Yeung are creating the premier summit for business owners, operators, & disruptors-a place where entrepreneurs don't just learn, but also build, network, & grow.  Meet Our Partners Stan: build a business around your ideasStan helps creators & entrepreneurs build businesses around their ideas. Stanley is their private beta AI partner that turns conversations, experiences, & expertise into personalized content & opportunities, built in public with founders & creators who believe the future belongs to those who learn, share, & build openly. Learn more at stan.store.  Circle: the modern platform for digital businessesBring your audience, products, & customer relationships into one place. Create websites, newsletters, courses, memberships, events, & communities, then use built-in AI, automation, & customer data to grow & manage your business. Learn more at circle.co.  Whop: the first end-to-end API for running a businessWhop is building the first end-to-end API for running a business, enabling money movement, customer acquisition, & mobilization of an on-demand workforce. Learn more at whop.com.  Rho: the new standard for business bankingRho is the all-in-one banking platform for startups. With banking set up in minutes, 2% cashback cards, & powerful tools for managing spend, paying bills, & closing the books, Rho helps high-growth startups move fast & stay focused-with support that goes to the ends of the earth to help you win.  Agree: the first revenue platform that starts at the contractAgree instantly converts every signed agreement into invoices, payments, & revenue workflows, with zero manual work. Agree helps SMBs & mid-market companies get invoices out faster, collect cash sooner, & eliminate manual work by making the contract the single source of truth for revenue. Learn more at agree.com.  Deel: hire, manage & pay talent anywhereDeel is the global work platform that helps founders hire, manage & pay talent anywhere. With Deel, startups handle payroll, HR, benefits, mobility, performance, & device management across 150+ countries, all on one platform. Learn more at deel.com.  Digital Executive: high-performing LatAm talent for under $2,000 a monthDigital Executive is a staffing company that helps U.S. businesses hire high performing, English fluent talent in Latin America for under $2,000 a month. They recruit across sales, marketing, operations, design, customer support, & more. No long term contracts, low buyout fees, & great talent at a fraction of the cost of hiring in the U.S.  Book an Outliers discovery call.  FAQCan I get a refund or transfer my ticket? We do not offer refunds, but you can transfer your ticket to another attendee if you can no longer attend. Just reach out to our support team to arrange the transfer. If I'm not approved for the event, will I be charged? No, only approved attendees will be charged. If your application is not accepted, you will not be billed. If you have any other questions, send an email to andrew@meetfibe.com   *By registering, I agree to receive emails from the Outliers Summit (unsubscribe anytime) & consent to being photographed or recorded at the event, & to the organizers & their partners using those images & recordings for promotional & marketing purposes.

events.name: Can Your Agents Actually Ship?
events.description: Can your agents actually ship?Compose your AI-native SDLCYour AI agents can't be trusted with data they can't find, can't understand, & aren't sure they're allowed to touch. And even when they get it right, the code they write still stalls in a delivery pipeline built for human speed. On Nov2 we will tackle both: first the data foundations agents need to trust, then the SDLC they need to ship through. Opening talk: From a Data Swamp to a Data Agent You Can Trust The evening opens with Grzegorz Krl on the data foundations AI agents need to find, understand & safely access your data. We've run this talk at Boston & San Francisco Tech Week, & both times it ran long because nobody wanted to stop asking questions. Full session details: https://luma.com/il0xoz9a Main session: Can your agents actually ship? AI can write code. Getting that code to production is another matter. Most engineering organizations hit the same wall: the bottleneck isn't the agent, it's everything downstream of it. Pipelines, CI, reviews, security gates, release processes: all of it was built for human speed, not AI. Visdom, built by VirtusLab, is the missing layer between AI coding & production. It lets you compose an AI-native SDLC, piece by piece: the context, validation, governance & orchestration agents need to ship safely & at scale. Come see what that looks like in practice. We'll cover: Why AI adoption stalls after the first wave of excitement What infrastructure an AI-native SDLC actually requires How Visdom connects agents to your SDLC, component by component Live demos of AI agents shipping production-ready code Q&A with the Visdom team Evaluating AI coding assistants or already rolling them out across teams? This session is about what happens after the code is written.  What you'll see liveA hands-on walkthrough of how Visdom removes friction across context, execution, & validation, turning your SDLC into a system AI agents can reliably operate on: Deep repository scanning that builds the semantic context AI agents actually need: not just open files, but the full dependency & intent graph across your codebase Blast radius scoring on an AI-generated PR before it touches CI, catching what code review misses when your team merges 3x more than last quarter Governed sandbox execution with full audit trails: the missing layer between the AI suggested it & it's running in production A live maturity assessment on a real delivery pipeline: where it stands today, & the smallest concrete step that unlocks the next level Who should join?CTOs, CDOs, VPs of Engineering & Data, Heads of Platform & AI, & senior engineers responsible for developer productivity, data platforms & AI adoption strategy. Especially if your AI tools shine in demos but stall in your CI/CD pipeline, or your agents can't tell which table is the right one. Why it's worth your time Get a practical diagnostic for making your data usable by AI agents See what an AI-native SDLC looks like in practice (live demo) Learn how to assess your AI maturity, step by step Learn how to start small, validate quickly, & evolve without big upfront risk Agenda6:00 PM - Doors open, drinks & networking6:30 PM - Opening talk: From a Data Swamp to a Data Agent You Can Trust (incl. Q&A)7:00 PM - Panel: real stories from AI adoption7:45 PM - Live demo: Visdom8:15 - 9:00 PM - Q&A & networking SpeakersPractitioners working hands-on with AI-driven delivery, data platforms, developer tooling, & real-world implementation: Grzegorz Krl, Tech Lead & Data Architect at VirtusLabGrzegorz believes that solid data systems start with a deep understanding of what the business actually needs. He works closely with organizations to put their business domains at the center of every data initiative, so that architectures, models & pipelines reflect how the business really operates. Artur Skowroski, Head of Application Development at VirtusLabArtur has spent more than ten years in the industry, on everything from greenfield builds to systems older than he is. He has worked as a Software Engineer, Tech Lead, Architect & Technical Product Manager, which gives him a broad view of the problems he tackles. He still likes to stay hands-on & has been writing a weekly roundup of the JVM ecosystem at jvm-weekly.com for over two years. Hosted by VirtusLabWe work with organizations ranging from global brands (including top-tier investment banks, Databricks, Airbnb, & DHL) to fast-growing startups, helping them build data platforms & AI systems that actually scale. At our core, we're engineers working with engineers, & we actively support the community through meetups, events, & shared learning. If you're working on AI in software delivery, this is where it starts to actually work.

events.name: Responsible Tech Summit - Embedding Accountability AI Era
events.description: At a time when artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping society, the conversation is shifting from broad principles to real-world accountability. The 2026 summit will explore the theme of Principles to Power: Embedding Accountability in the AI Era. For years, the Responsible Tech field has been guided by ethical frameworks, voluntary commitments, & emerging standards. Today, the challenge is clear: how do we translate those ideas into systems of governance, oversight, & design that ensure innovation does not come at the expense of safety, rights, or trust? The Responsible Tech Summit is designed as a curated convening for 375 leaders that helps align & shape the direction of the movement. Participants will include global governance leaders, AI researchers, industry practitioners, policy experts, civil society advocates, & philanthropic leaders who are building the infrastructure of accountability for the digital age. Through keynotes, panels, & conversations, attendees will explore topics such as accountability by design, platform oversight, youth online safety, the Responsible Tech economy, & the evolving global regulatory landscape. All ticket proceeds fund free resources & services for the Responsible Tech community that our organization provides. Can't make it in person? The event will be livestreamed for free on All Tech Is Human's YouTube page, where recordings will also be available afterward. - Are you a journalist looking to potentially cover the Responsible Tech Summit? Reach out to Hello@AllTechIsHuman.org. Speakers for the Responsible Tech Summit 2026 Camille Francois - President, ROOST Eli Pariser - Co-Director, New_ Public Cathy O'Neil, Founder, Author, Mathematician & Data Scientist, O'Neil Risk Consulting & Algorithmic Auditing Rumman Chowdhury, CEO, Humane Intelligence PBC Alex Bores, Assembly Member, New York City's 73rd District Beth Goldberg, Founding Executive Director of Humanity AI Sinead Bovell, Founder, WAYE Alexis Wales, Chief Information Security Officer, GitHub Alison Lee, Chief R&D Officer, The Rithm Project Amanda Craig, General Manager of Responsible AI Public Policy, Microsoft Anya Schiffrin, Director, Media Program, Columbia University (SIPA) Carrie Varoquiers, Chief Impact Officer, Workday Joshua Elder, Senior Vice President & Head of Grantmaking, Siegel Family Endowment Julie Cordua, CEO, Thorn Fernanda Del Castillo, Director of AI Governance, Mastercard Kathy Pham, Faculty & Senior Fellow, Product & Responsible AI, Harvard University Kristin Hansen, Executive Director, Civic Health Project J. Trevor Hughes, President & CEO of IAPP Shreya Singh Hernndez, Senior Manager, Aspen Digital, The Aspen Institute Melanie Plaza, Chief Technology Officer, AE Studio Courtney Radsch, Director of the Center for Media & Digital Governance, Open Markets Institute; Fellow, Brookings Institution Andrew Rasiej, Founder, Civic Hall Clement Wolf, Director, Responsible AI Strategy, Google Hale Sirin, Program Scientist, Schmidt Sciences AI & Advanced Computing Institute Jeff Collins, Director of Trust & Safety, Amazon Web Services Alisar Mustafa, Head of AI Safety, Duco Experts   Agenda10:00 - 11:00 am ET | Check-in & Networking 11:00 - 11:10 am | Welcome remarks 11:15 - 11:45 am | Panel: Beyond Benchmarks: Turning Evaluations into Enforceable Standards 11:50 - 12:00 pm | Lightning talk 12:05 - 12:35 pm | Panel: Safety by Design: Accountability at the Intersection of AI, Industry, & Advocacy 12:40 - 1:40 pm | Lunch 1:45 - 2:05 pm | Fireside Chat: Open-Source, Open Questions: Transparency in the Age of AI 2:10 - 2:40 pm | Panel: Shared Risk, Shared Responsibility: Rethinking Responsible AI Governance 2:45 - 3:05 pm | Fireside Chat: Alignment in Practice: Building AI That Wants to be Good 3:05 - 3:30 pm | Networking break 3:30 - 4:00 pm | Panel: Trust as Strategy & the Fight Against AI-Enabled Fraud 4:05 - 4:15 pm | Keynote 4:15 - 4:25 pm | Lightning Talk 4:30 - 5:00 pm | Panel: Rebuilding the Commons: Community & Pluralism in the AI Era 5:05 - 5:25 pm | Fireside Chat: Looking Back to Look Ahead: Co-Designing AI After a Decade of Tech Lessons 5:25 - 5:30 pm | Closing remarks *See the full agenda & bios of our speakers here.   Sponsors for the Responsible Tech Summit 2026Special thanks to our strategic partners, Columbia World Projects, Forum One, & Highspring, for helping bring this critical conversation to life. WorkdayWorkday operates at the heart of the enterprise - HR, finance, & IT - where the margin for error is effectively zero. By tightly coupling AI with the context, guardrails, & trusted processes that run the business, Workday goes beyond AI that assists work to agents that do the work & drive measurable outcomes. More than 11,500 organizations worldwide, including more than 65% of the Fortune 500, trust Workday to deliver. MastercardMastercard is a global technology company in the payments industry, connecting consumers, financial institutions, merchants, & governments in more than 200 countries & territories. The company is committed to building a sustainable, inclusive digital economy that benefits everyone, everywhere. PinterestPinterest is a visual search & discovery platform where people find inspiration, curate ideas & shop products - all in a positive place online. Headquartered in San Francisco, Pinterest has over 600 million monthly active users worldwide. MicrosoftMicrosoft is a global technology leader empowering every person & organization on the planet to achieve more through its platforms & productivity tools. The company is committed to advancing responsible AI & ensuring emerging technologies are developed & deployed safely & ethically. Siegel Family EndowmentSiegel Family Endowment takes an inquiry-driven approach to grantmaking, informed by the scientific method. As technology reshapes society, we fund organizations asking critical questions about its impact on learning, work, & infrastructure. Founded in 2011 by David Siegel, co-founder & co-chairman of Two Sigma, we advance technology in the public interest, supporting research & initiatives that imagine a more inclusive, resilient technology-driven society. AE StudioAE Studio is an applied AI & AI alignment company that builds software products for clients while advancing research on making advanced AI systems safe & beneficial. Its recent work with Anthropic, GRAM, trains dangerous knowledge into removable modules so it can be stripped from a model before release. AE Studio reinvests its commercial success into neglected approaches to AI alignment research. Learn more at ae.studio. GoogleGoogle's mission is to organize the world's information & make it universally accessible & useful. As a leader in AI & computing, the company is focused on developing technology responsibly to benefit people & society. Kapor FoundationThe Kapor Foundation works at the intersection of racial equity & technology to expand access to K-12 computer science & postsecondary tech pathways, improve tech accountability & worker protections, & increase investments in infrastructure & innovation. We advocate for policy changes, build the capacity of partners, conduct research, support partners through grantmaking, & invest in entrepreneurship & VC. We believe that when technology includes diverse perspectives & is harnessed to address societal challenges, we can transform the tech ecosystem for Black, Latine, & Native communities, & society as a whole. Kapor Foundation works collectively with the Kapor Center family of organizations, Kapor Capital, & SMASH to reimagine & reconstruct a more inclusive & equitable technology sector. Check out Kapor Foundation's Responsible AI Principles for Advancing a More Equitable Innovation Future. IAPPThe IAPP is a policy-neutral, not-for-profit association founded in 2000 with a mission to define, promote & improve the professions of privacy, AI governance & digital responsibility globally. Civic Health ProjectCivic Health Project is a nonpartisan nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing scalable solutions to the dangerous divisions that threaten American democracy. Since our founding in 2019, we have supported more than 75 academic researchers, grassroots practitioners, creatives, & technologists who are helping reduce polarization, strengthen civic norms, & foster social cohesion. Today, Civic Health Project focuses primarily on exploring the vast potential of promising new technologies to help resolve conflict, improve civil discourse & deliberation, foster social cohesion, & uphold societal norms. Normsy.ai, our flagship in-house project, brings this mission to life. It identifies toxic content in real time & equips users to respond with respectful, trust-building messages grounded in social science & supported by artificial intelligence. We are also part of the initiative The Forum, a new model for civic leadership at a time when trust is low, division is high, & the need for credible, citizen-led solutions has never been greater. GitHubGitHub is the world's leading platform for agentic software development - powered by Copilot to build, scale, & deliver secure software. Over 225 million developers, including more than 90% of the Fortune 100 companies, use GitHub to collaborate, & more than 140,000 organizations have adopted GitHub Copilot. CinderCinder is the industry's first Trust & Safety operations platform to help organizations combat Internetabuse at scale. We provide Trust & Safety teams with a single system to manage complex integrityoperations & investigations to create a safe environment for their users. Interested in sponsoring our summit or forming a strategic partnership? Email us at hello@alltechishuman.org.   About All Tech Is HumanAll Tech Is Human is the coordination layer & connective tissue for the Responsible Tech ecosystem. By uniting key individuals across civil society, government, industry, academia, & philanthropy, we provide a sandbox for solution-building & socialization to influence key levers of change. We specialize in taking a whole-of-ecosystem approach to tackling thorny tech & society issues, shaping the Responsible Tech movement, & ensuring that our tech future is aligned with the public interest. We are the premier gathering for the Responsible Tech community, convening thousands of people globally. We curate the defining resource for the movement, the Responsible Tech Guide, used by academia, industry, civil society, & policy professionals. We have the largest online community for the Responsible Tech movement hosted on Slack with over 15,000 members across 117 countries. We have the go-to job board for the community, our curated Responsible Tech Job Board & related talent pool. Refund Policy & Billing DetailsRefund requests made before October 1 at 5:00 pm ET are subject to a $50 administrative fee. Refund requests made between October 2 & the final refund deadline of October 16 at 5:00 pm ET face a late cancellation fee of $100. No refunds or ticket transfers are permitted after October 16. Please note: credit card statements for this purchase will show a charge from "Social Science Research Council (SSRC)," All Tech Is Human's fiscal sponsor.

Headquartered in San Francisco, Pinterest has over 600 million monthly active users worldwide. MicrosoftMicrosoft is a global technology leader empowering every person & organization on the planet to achieve more through its platforms & productivity tools. The company is committed to advancing responsible AI & ensuring emerging technologies are developed & deployed safely & ethically. Siegel Family EndowmentSiegel Family Endowment takes an inquiry-driven approach to grantmaking, informed by the scientific method. As technology reshapes society, we fund organizations asking critical questions about its impact on learning, work, & infrastructure. Founded in 2011 by David Siegel, co-founder & co-chairman of Two Sigma, we advance technology in the public interest, supporting research & initiatives that imagine a more inclusive, resilient technology-driven society. AE StudioAE Studio is an applied AI & AI alignment company that builds software products for clients while advancing research on making advanced AI systems safe & beneficial. Its recent work with Anthropic, GRAM, trains dangerous knowledge into removable modules so it can be stripped from a model before release. AE Studio reinvests its commercial success into neglected approaches to AI alignment research. Learn more at ae.studio. GoogleGoogle's mission is to organize the world's information & make it universally accessible & useful. As a leader in AI & computing, the company is focused on developing technology responsibly to benefit people & society. Kapor FoundationThe Kapor Foundation works at the intersection of racial equity & technology to expand access to K-12 computer science & postsecondary tech pathways, improve tech accountability & worker protections, & increase investments in infrastructure & innovation. We advocate for policy changes, build the capacity of partners, conduct research, support partners through grantmaking, & invest in entrepreneurship & VC. Since our founding in 2019, we have supported more than 75 academic researchers, grassroots practitioners, creatives, & technologists who are helping reduce polarization, strengthen civic norms, & foster social cohesion. Today, Civic Health Project focuses primarily on exploring the vast potential of promising new technologies to help resolve conflict, improve civil discourse & deliberation, foster social cohesion, & uphold societal norms. Normsy.ai, our flagship in-house project, brings this mission to life. events.name: SOSV Deep Tech Summit
events.description: SOSV DEEP TECH SUMMIT Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. The producers of the Summit are SOSV's Ned Desmond, Ben Joffe, & Norm Amandi. More DetailsSOSV's mission is to invest in deep tech companies that advance human & planetary health, & embedded in building an 800+ company portfolio with a remarkable array of companies applying AI in the physical world. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

Every session ends with something real in hand, not just notes. Real customers, not guesses. Founders talk to 5 to 10 potential users & put a working product in front of them. Two tracks. No-code founders build with tools like Lovable, Replit, v0 & Bolt. Founders who code use Claude Code or Cursor. Honest checks built in. Founders open & verify every source, set their success target before the results come in, & have a second tool test every build. A live product with a real ask.
