events.description: Cohort Wednesday Coworking is a weekly working session in NYC for everyone making something. Spend the day alongside passionate people in different fields & different stages, but deep in the work that's more than a job. We meet every Wednesday to build a lasting community that helps, supports, & learns new ideas from each other.  9:30 AM - Coffee & introductions  10:00 AM - Heads down. Check out the live board to see who's here & how you can intersect.  1:00 PM - Lunch. The best part of the day. Break bread together & get to know each other.  ~4:00 PM - Demo. Feedback. Share your work. Ask questions & get answers from the community. AFTER: Get together & hang out, talk more, & grab a meal together! Come for an hour or stay all day. We show up every week. Cohort is a community of builders, creatives, & founders in NYC. We show up for each other every week - with true accountability, real support, & honest feedback. Our goal is to create a community with a culture of building ideas in NYC.  Photography Notice We take photos & video at events to share on social & our site. By attending, you're okay with us using them to promote Cohort. Not into it? Tell us when you arrive & we'll keep you out of frame.   More from CohortKeep building, exploring ideas, & meeting the community. events.name: Startup Pitch Mixer
events.description: Join our Pitch & Networking Night in New York! We design Pitch & Networking nights to help founders sharpen their thinking through direct, candid feedback, & to give strong investors access to serious teams. The pitch session comes with structured networking before & after. WHAT TO EXPECT- Startups pitch live & get focused feedback from angels & VC partners- Structured networking before & after the pitches- Founders, entrepreneurs & operators networking, exchanging ideas & building connections- Active investors & venture scouts discovering the best startups early WHO YOU WILL MEET- Founders- Investors, VC partners & venture scouts- Marketers, salespeople & business advisors- Industry disruptors & AI experts- Entrepreneurs from Europe, Asia & the UK AGENDA18:00 - 18:30 Registration & casual networking18:30 - 19:00 Kickoff & interactive networking19:00 - 19:50 Startup pitch session (5 min per pitch + Q&A)19:50 - 21:00 Chill & networking over refreshments FOR INVESTORSComplimentary tickets are available to institutional investors, angels & venture scouts with a proven track record. If you'd like access to our database of promising startups or want to mentor our best teams, fill out the Investor Application Form & our team will contact you. WANT TO PITCH?4-6 selected founders pitch to a panel of investors & experts, each followed by a short Q&A.- Buy a Pitch Ticket & fill out the Pitch Application Form with your deck- Spots are limited, & founders are selected in advance- A pitch deck is required. We share our pitching guide & offer coaching if you'd like it- The best startups are featured on our social media & in our investor newsletter DRESS CODESmart casual. Bring good energy. FAQCan I pitch?Yes. Buy a Pitch Ticket & fill out the Pitch Application Form. We'll contact you to approve your pitch. You get 5 minutes plus audience Q&A. How does the pitch go?You present on stage for 5 minutes, covering your idea, business model, target market & investment ask, followed by a short Q&A. Do investors get free tickets?Yes. Apply via the form or email hello@startupvalley.club & we'll issue a complimentary ticket for you & your team. Can I request a refund?Yes, up to 1 day before the event. Request it on the platform where you bought your ticket, or email hello@startupvalley.club ABOUT STARTUP VALLEYStartup Valley is a global event organizer that has hosted pitch nights in 25 cities since 2023: 850 events & 40,000 attendees so far. We have strategic partnerships with VC funds in the US, Europe & Asia. Questions or partnerships: hello@startupvalley.club

events.name: Health2Tech - MedTech Edition
events.description: Health2Tech - a series of digital health events.Join us on November 5th for an exclusive gathering that brings together the brightest minds in the digital health space. Hosted by Bailey Morgan, Audrey Guazzone, Maria Putilina & Alex Koshykov, this evening promises to be a confluence of innovation, inspiration, & invaluable networking.  Important!  To keep this session highly focused, priority will be given to MedTech experts, device founders, bioengineers, clinicians, & specialized investors. If you work outside the MedTech space, we appreciate your understanding - we'll review your application & confirm attendance based on remaining capacity.  Want to Showcase Your Medical Device Live?If you are building a medical device or physical HealthTech product, we have live demo spots available to feature your innovation in front of NYC investors, healthcare leaders, & potential partners. How to apply: Fill out the form - Open Google Form Register on this Luma page. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, so please apply early!  Event Schedule: 5:30 PM - 6:00 Doors Open. Begin the evening with a warm welcome & a chance to settle in. 6:00 - 6:45 Panel on: "What Makes a MedTech Company Investable?". 6:45 - 8:30 Networking. Connect, converse, & collaborate with peers driven by a common passion for advancing healthcare through technology.  About our Panelists: Steven Levy Steven is a Partner at Unorthodox Ventures where he focuses on investing in venture stage MedTech companies. Before joining Unorthodox Ventures, Steven worked for the prior 23 years as an investment banker, having held senior roles at Lehman Brothers, Stifel Financial & Cowen & Co. Steven has executed over 100 transactions with aggregate deal value in excess of $30 billion. Steven headed the M&A efforts for the Financial Sponsors practice at Lehman Brothers, covered Financial sponsors & headed the Consumer M&A efforts at Cowen & covered Financial Sponsors, led execution on technology & consumer M&A transactions & headed up the firm's investment banking efforts in Israel at Stifel. Steven received his B.A. from Binghamton University & graduated as a member of Phi Beta Kappa & received his M.B.A. from the Wharton School, at the University of Pennsylvania. Bryan Spielman is a Managing Partner at Northwell Health Equity Partners. He is a seasoned C-suite executive with a track record of driving multi-billion-dollar value creation across the healthcare & technology sectors. Most recently, as Chief Growth Officer at Advarra, he spearheaded the company's $5 billion sale to Blackstone & CPPIB. Prior to that, at Medidata, he helped scale the company from a $400 million to over $2.3 billion market valuation. Bryan spent 12 years in investment banking at Centerview Partners, UBS, & Bear Stearns, advising on over $50 billion in transactions. He holds an MBA from NYU Stern School of Business & a BA from the University of Pennsylvania. Host/Moderator: Maria Putilina, MD, MS, is a medical advisor & innovator, boasting over a decade of driving transformative change within the healthcare industry. Her expertise spans Business Administration, Medicine, & Science, which she honed in healthcare consulting, helping companies build & execute innovation strategies.  Why Attend? Meet like-minded individuals who are actively shaping the health tech landscape. Share experiences, discuss challenges, & explore potential solutions with fellow founders. Learn from the journeys of other entrepreneurs, discover something new, seek advice, & perhaps find the mentor or partner you've been looking for.  Who Should Attend? Digital Health Founders at various stages of their startup journey. Healthcare Professionals who are passionate about health innovation. Investors looking to make impactful contributions to the digital health & medtech spaces.  Why This Event Is A Must? Hear from thought leaders & innovators in the digital health domain (at every event, we'll have a new set of speakers). Connect with peers, potential collaborators, & mentors. Participate in engaging Q&As & discussions that can spark new ideas & opportunities.  Venue Details: Because of limited capacity, we won't be able to accommodate everyone, so please register whenever you are sure you can attend. Partner Brown Rudnick is a leading international law firm that provides exceptional, client-driven service in global litigation, crisis management (restructuring, investigations, & special situations), brand & reputation management, life sciences, & technology.  We advise on high-profile cross-border matters while providing the kind of personal attention to clients that is typically found at boutiques. Our enterprising & tenacious lawyers serve our clients around the globe from offices in key financial centers in the U.S. & the U.K., & have been recognized by, among others, Chambers USA, Legal 500, Benchmark Litigation, & Law360 for excellence in their fields. To learn more about our Emerging Growth Companies & Venture Capital group, please visit us here. About the organisers Audrey Guazzone is an innovation & commercialization strategist who helps medtech & digital health companies navigate international growth. Through LeanLia, she combines market validation, commercialization strategy, & hands-on business development to help companies grow in the U.S. She is passionate about connecting healthcare innovators & ecosystems across America & Europe. Maria Putilina, MD, MS, is a medical advisor & innovator, boasting over a decade of driving transformative change within the healthcare industry. Her expertise spans Business Administration, Medicine, & Science, which she honed in healthcare consulting, helping companies build & execute innovation strategies. Bailey Morgan is a healthtech leader who blends clinical expertise with business strategy to drive healthcare innovation & growth. A former speech-language pathologist, she has helped raise over $10 million in capital, led go-to-market teams across SaaS & CPG companies, & closed more than $2 million in technology sales. As Chief of Staff at Groth Pain & Spine, she leads change management & technology integration across a growing provider network, while also advising healthcare technology companies & serving as Director & Treasurer of a nonprofit supporting individuals living with dementia & their caregivers. Alex Koshykov is a co-founder of BeKey & a digital health expert who constantly shares news, introduces promising technologies, & promotes secure software & hardware for the healthcare industry on his YouTube channel. Additionally to that, he is a co-founder of YODD, a medical device startup. Additional Information By signing up, your email will be automatically added to the Health2Tech newsletter with news & upcoming events - but don't worry, we won't flood your inbox! ;) Also, just a note that this event might be photographed or filmed. If we do capture some moments, Health2Tech may use the photos or videos for marketing & communication purposes. By registering, you're giving us the thumbs up for using your image for these reasons.

events.name: 1st Annual Antitrust Summit
events.description: A global focus on competition law, policy & enforcement comes to New YorkAfter two years of leading the competition debate in London, the Antitrust Summit is crossing the Atlantic. Our London forum brought together more than 385 leading enforcers, economists & corporate executives to discuss the plot twists of modern antitrust law, policy & enforcement. Now, we bring that same rigorous discussion to the US at a particularly consequential moment. The administration in Washington, DC quickly signalled a departure from the neo-Brandeisian period. Dealmaking activity continues to surge. Yet for all the enthusiasm around M&A, the antitrust environment remains unpredictable. Heightened scrutiny of sectors central to the cost of living, increased state intervention in transactions & firms, & a growing role for state attorneys-general in enforcement are contributing to uncertainty. At the same time, AI is reshaping competition & investment dynamics as long-running antitrust cases against technology companies move forward. Against this backdrop, ahead of the November midterm elections, the Antitrust Summit will provide the insights & clarity needed to navigate a changing landscape. Join us in New York on October 28th for the latest edition of our Antitrust Summit series.

events.name: Startup Pitch Mixer
events.description: Join our Pitch & Networking Night in New York! We design Pitch & Networking nights to help founders sharpen their thinking through direct, candid feedback, & to give strong investors access to serious teams. The pitch session comes with structured networking before & after. WHAT TO EXPECT- Startups pitch live & get focused feedback from angels & VC partners- Structured networking before & after the pitches- Founders, entrepreneurs & operators networking, exchanging ideas & building connections- Active investors & venture scouts discovering the best startups early WHO YOU WILL MEET- Founders- Investors, VC partners & venture scouts- Marketers, salespeople & business advisors- Industry disruptors & AI experts- Entrepreneurs from Europe, Asia & the UK AGENDA18:00 - 18:30  Registration & casual networking18:30 - 19:00  Kickoff & interactive networking19:00 - 19:50  Startup pitch session (5 min per pitch + Q&A)19:50 - 21:00  Chill & networking over refreshments FOR INVESTORSComplimentary tickets are available to institutional investors, angels & venture scouts with a proven track record. If you'd like access to our database of promising startups or want to mentor our best teams, fill out the Investor Application Form & our team will contact you. WANT TO PITCH?4-6 selected founders pitch to a panel of investors & experts, each followed by a short Q&A.- Buy a Pitch Ticket & fill out the Pitch Application Form with your deck- Spots are limited, & founders are selected in advance- A pitch deck is required. We share our pitching guide & offer coaching if you'd like it- The best startups are featured on our social media & in our investor newsletter DRESS CODESmart casual. Bring good energy. FAQCan I pitch?Yes. Buy a Pitch Ticket & fill out the Pitch Application Form. We'll contact you to approve your pitch. You get 5 minutes plus audience Q&A. How does the pitch go?You present on stage for 5 minutes, covering your idea, business model, target market & investment ask, followed by a short Q&A. Do investors get free tickets?Yes. events.name: Trajectories - Facts, Fictions & Futures Of Spacefaring Societies
events.description: Science fiction has long imagined humanity's path beyond Earth, from post-scarcity utopias to contested frontiers to desperate exoduses. Which way are we headed? This week's interactive community conversation tests those visions against the technological, economic, societal, & cultural forces shaping our spacefaring future right now. Because the future isn't something we predict but something we choose, the question isn't just where we're headed, but where we dare to go. OUR FACILITATORVince Lucich, an engineer & startup founder whose work involves building spacecraft for the emerging orbital economy, will lead us on this idea exploration of the future. WHO'S IT FOR?Idea people. Founders. Builders. Creatives. Researchers. The Curious. And their Supporters --------------FORMATOur format explores ideas together through our diverse backgrounds, while building relationships & community through the process. We want you to talk to each other, instead of just being talked at. 6:00PM - Settle in, grab a drink & some food at the bar, & meet some new people before we start our event. 6:30PM - Our conversation begins with our facilitator presenting the knowledge & context for the conversation along the way. The conversation between attendees will explore from surface level understandings, to deep implications & future iterations. 7:45PM - Meet & connect with new people, catch up with people you haven't seen in a while, discover all the different ways you overlap. And then just hang out, grab a drink, play some pool or ping pong! Or stay for the band afterwards! Our desire is to be the antithesis of NYC's corporate panel & transactional networking culture. We aim to create a vibrant idea & build space in NYC that focuses on the passion & values beyond the money & the hustle.

events.name: Ugly Talk - Building Fandoms In 2027
events.description: A customer buys once. A fan brings people with them. Getting there takes months of showing up. Listening. Keeping promises. Giving people a reason to care when you are no longer in their feed. This Ugly Talk gets into the work behind real fandom. The creator calls that went nowhere. The community plays that looked dead for months. The moment loyal customers pushed back & the brand had to answer. No follower-count victory laps. Just the decisions, mistakes, & proof behind communities that stick.  Why you should be in this room.Hear how consumer brands turn one-time buyers into people who recruit other buyers. Learn which signals reveal loyalty before revenue catches up. See how brands build with creators from the first idea through launch. Learn what to keep doing when the community looks quiet. Hear how leaders respond when their biggest supporters become their loudest critics.  What's on the table.Building superfans at scale: What makes customers care enough to bring other people in. Creators & co-creation: How brands share the build instead of buying a post at the end. Measuring fandom: The numbers that matter after likes & reach stop telling the truth. The slow build: What to do when months of work look like nothing is happening. When fandom turns: What community pushback reveals about the trust you built. Managing a crisis: How to respond fast, own the miss, & keep trust intact.  Who's hosting it. Rob Fajardo - Founder, LeaveNormalBehind Rob Fajardo is an entrepreneur, operator, & cultural architect whose work centers on a simple question: what does winning look like? Early in his career, Rob helped drive the fidget spinner phenomenon by building & activating an influencer network across Instagram & Facebook, reaching over 150 million people. Since then, he has worked with brands including DoorDash, Lowe's, FedEx, Converse, Red Bull, & Wyndham Resort Group, & has been featured in Forbes, Entrepreneur, Thrive Global, & BuzzFeed. Rob is the founder of Leave Normal Behind, a global network of purpose-driven leaders, creators, & investors built around meaningful connection, personal growth, & human flourishing. Over the past decade, he has brought together people across industries & generations through designed gatherings & strategic collaborations. He also serves as Head of Operations for the School of Content at The School of Hard Knocks, one of the world's largest business media platforms with 26M+ followers, where he coaches business owners generating six to nine figures on go-to-market. In addition, he is a Strategic Advisor to The AI Collective, the world's largest AI community, with 70,000+ members across 25+ global chapters.  Who's getting in.CPG & consumer-brand founders building a customer base that sticks. Brand & community leaders responsible for loyalty & retention. Creators building their own audience or working with consumer brands. Marketers who care about advocacy, repeat purchases, & long-term growth.  About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough "aha!" moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons & insights. With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami, we've built a vibrant community of thousands of founders & industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape. Official Website: UglyTalk.com Important Notice for Ugly Talk AttendeesAdmission & Confirmation Attendance is by approval only. Approved guests will receive a confirmation email along with a calendar invite. Invitations are non-transferable. You waive any right to inspect or approve the final materials & release all claims related to their use. Communications By registering, you agree to receive marketing & promotional communications from Ugly Talk & its co-hosts, partners, & sponsors. events.name: Startup Pitch Mixer
events.description: Join our event in New York! We design Pitch & Networking nights to help founders sharpen their thinking through direct, candid feedback & to give strong investors access to serious teams. Our pitch night is complemented by a structured networking session before & after the pitch session. What to expect: Startups pitch live & receive focused feedback from angels & VC partners Structured networking session before & after the pitches Entrepreneurs, startup founders, & operators are joining to network, exchange ideas, & build strong connections Active investors & venture scouts joining to discover the best startups early  Who you will meet at the event: Founders Investors, VC partners, Venture Scouts Marketers, Salespeople, Business Advisors Industry Disruptors AI Experts Entrepreneurs from Europe, Asia, & the United Kingdom  We Welcome New Investors: We invite investors to our event to expand their network, get acquainted with new startups, evaluate them, share feedback, & participate in discussions with early-stage & serial founders. We offer complimentary tickets to institutional investors, angels, & venture scouts with a proven track record. If you'd like to access our database of promising startups or provide mentorship support to our best startups, please fill out this short Investor Application Form, & our team will contact you.  Want to Pitch? A limited number of founders will have the opportunity to pitch their startup or business to a panel of investors & experts. 4-6 selected founders will pitch their startup, followed by a short Q&A where participants can ask questions & share feedback. Apply by filling out the Pitch Application Form & sending us your pitch deck. Spots are limited, & we select founders in advance. To maintain high-quality pitches, you are required to present with a pitch deck. We will share our pitching guide and, if you'd like, coach you so you're fully prepared for pitch night.  The best startups will be featured across our social media & included in our investor newsletter. Requirements for attendees: Dress code: smart casual. Bring good energy.  Join our event & secure your ticket today! About us: Startup Valley is a global event organizer hosting pitch nights in 25 cities since 2023. Since then, we have hosted 850 events for 40,000 attendees. Over these years, we connected countless outstanding early-stage startups to serious investors, & we are not planning to stop. We maintain strategic partnerships with VC funds in the US, Europe, & Asia to support our community. Do you have a question, a partnership proposal, or want to clarify something? Reach us at hello@startupvalley.club Agenda 18:00-18:30 - Registration: Guests register, receive badges, & event programs. This is an opportunity for casual networking, making first connections, & preparing for the event. 18:30-19:00 - Event Kickoff & Interactive Networking: Official welcome from the organizers with a brief overview of the event goals & schedule. Interactive networking session to connect with key contacts. 19:00-19:50 - Startup Pitch Session: Startups present their projects to investors & experts. Each team has 5 minutes to pitch, covering the project's core idea, business model, & target market. 19:50-21:00 - Chill & Networking: Participants enjoy casual conversations with investors, discuss collaboration opportunities, & exchange ideas over refreshments. FAQ Can I pitch? Yes! To pitch, please purchase a Pitch Ticket & fill out the Pitch Application Form. We will contact you to discuss & approve your pitch. The pitch duration is 5 minutes. You will also have some time to answer questions from the audience. How does the pitch go? Selected founders present on stage to the audience & the investors in the room. You get 5 minutes to pitch your idea, business model, target market, & investment ask, followed by a short Q&A. The best startups are featured across our social media channels & in the investor newsletter. Who will I meet? Founders, angel investors, VC partners, venture scouts, AI experts, engineers, operators, marketing & sales experts, & international entrepreneurs from across Europe, Asia, & the US. Do investors get free tickets? Yes! Please apply above or email hello@startupvalley.club, & we will issue a complimentary ticket for you & your team. Can I request a refund? Yes. Refunds are available if requested at least 1 day before the event start time. Please submit the refund request on the platform where you purchased your ticket, or email us at hello@startupvalley.club

Furthermore, you release the Brooklyn Navy Yard Development Corporation, its officers, employees, & agents, from any liability in connection with such photography or videography & the use thereof, & waive any claims you may have for payment in connection with such materials & the use thereof.   Newsletter Acknowledgement & Permission By signing up for this event, you are agreeing to be added to the free Brooklyn Navy Yard public newsletter list. events.name: The Next Wave: AI & The Future Of Ocean Conservation, with Ocean Agentics
events.description: The world has committed to protecting 30% of the ocean by 2030, a target scientists see as the minimum for a healthy ocean. With four years to go, only about 3% is effectively protected. Countries & communities pursuing the 30x30 goal often lack the data, tools & technical teams to propose & implement conservation efforts at the speed & scale needed to get there. AI is starting to help with some of the hardest parts of that work. It can map where whales & other wildlife gather so countries know which waters to protect, & help coast guards catch illegal fishing vessels inside protected areas. However, most of these tools still sit out of reach of the small island nations & coastal communities with the most at stake. Whether AI narrows that gap or widens it depends on whether it's built with & for the people who will use it. Join Anew & Ocean Agentics for an evening of conversation with people leading this work across ocean technology, science, philanthropy & policy. We'll talk about what responsible AI for the ocean could look like, & what it would take for these tools to reach the people who need them. Drinks & mingling to follow. Ocean Agentics is a nonprofit building open tools that put frontier technology & marine data in the hands of people protecting the ocean. Our current focus is on providing engineering support to the countries & stakeholders implementing the High Seas Treaty, which covers two-thirds of the ocean. Anew is a gathering space & discovery center for social transformation located in NYC. We host interactive events & workshops, an accelerator program for nonprofits, & a retail lab featuring ethically-sourced coffee & gifts.

events.name: Worn: Smart Glasses Hackathon
events.description: Two days, one overnight build, & real smart glasses on your face. Join us at Cornell Tech with MicroLumin, the Shenzhen team behind the CES 2026 award-winning M6 display glasses, & build the first wave of apps for waveguide display glasses. This is a hands-on hardware hackathon for engineers & builders who would rather ship on real devices than talk about the future of spatial computing. Problem StatementSmart glasses are finally light enough to wear all day. What's missing is software that feels natural to use. Your challenge is to build anthropocentric interfaces: apps that start from how people see, move, talk & pay attention, not from how phones work. These should be things you'd actually keep on your face. The Challenge ThemeHeads-up assistants that show the right info at the right moment Live captioning, translation & conversation memory Navigation & wayfinding without looking down at a phone Accessibility for low-vision, hard-of-hearing & neurodivergent users Hands-free workflows for field techs, clinicians, chefs & mechanics New input patterns: voice, ring, head motion & glanceable UI Making the glasses useful with AI on what the camera sees What to ExpectMicroLumin AR glasses handed out to teams for the build SDK access & docs shared before the event so you can start early A workshop from Dr. Zhaoen Dai, MicroLumin's founder & CEO, on AR & where the AI industry is heading An overnight build from Friday evening into Saturday Teams of up to 4, or match with teammates at kickoff Food, caffeine & other builders who care about hardware Live demos on the device, worn by your team, in front of the judges ScheduleFriday, Nov 20 5:30 PM: Doors open, check-in, dinner 6:15 PM: Welcome & kickoff with the organizers, Cornell Tech & MicroLumin 6:35 PM: Challenge brief & a walkthrough of the MicroLumin SDK 7:00 PM: Team formation: 30-second idea pitches, then a mixer to find teammates 7:45 PM: Teams locked, hardware handed out, devices set up 8:00 PM: Hacking begins 9:00 PM: SDK help desk & mentor office hours open 11:30 PM: Late-night snacks Overnight 12:00 AM to 8:00 AM: Overnight build, with a quiet rest area for anyone who needs a nap All night: A MicroLumin engineer is online for live SDK support (it's afternoon in Shenzhen) Saturday, Nov 21 8:00 AM: Breakfast & coffee 9:00 AM: Morning check-in: each team shares where they are & what's blocking them 10:00 AM: Workshop with Dr. Zhaoen Dai, MicroLumin's founder & CEO, on designing for AR & waveguide displays 11:00 AM: Workshop: [Topic & speaker TBD] 12:30 PM: Lunch 2:00 PM: Code freeze, project submissions due 2:15 PM: Demo expo: judges go table to table & teams demo on the device 3:45 PM: Finalists announced 4:00 PM: Finalists demo on stage: 3 minutes, worn by the team, plus 2 minutes of Q&A 4:45 PM: Talk by Dr. Dai on AR & where the AI industry is heading, while judges deliberate 5:30 PM: Awards 6:00 PM: Hardware return & wrap PrizesTBD JudgesTBD Who Should AttendHardware Founders Engineers at companies like Meta, Amazon & Google who want to build on AR hardware iOS & Android developers Hardware tinkerers, embedded & computer vision engineers Product designers interested in spatial & glanceable UI Spots are limited & approval is required. You don't need prior AR experience, just the drive to build something real overnight. SponsorsMicroLumin: Shenzhen-based maker of AR display glasses, including the M6 series & several CES 2026 award winners. MicroLumin is providing the hardware & SDK support for teams. HostsSomya Gupta: The face of the NYC startup ecosystem. Stephen Jin: Johnson MBA '27 at Cornell, board director at Gona Semiconductor, Angel Investing Waftech - Founded in 2007 & based in Penang, Malaysia, Waftech designs & manufactures wafer-handling & automation equipment for semiconductor manufacturing. Waftech delivers end-to-end, from R&D & design through manufacturing & after-sales service, & is ISO 9001:2015 certified. Waftech is a subsidiary of Gona Semiconductor, a Shanghai-headquartered equipment group. Olivia Iarmak: AI Quality Ops Lead at Meta Reality Labs working on Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses, & co-founder of HQ Labs. Vishal Kharker: Lead Product Manager at RTX Fintech & Research, previously at Barclays & RBC Capital Markets. Info site: https://worn-hacks.com

events.name: An UNMUTED Book Club: The 100 Years War On Palestine
events.description: READING NOT REQUIRED - just be curious! Next up: Rashid Khalidi's The Hundred Years' War on Palestine, the 2020 book that argues the Israeli-Palestinian conflict isn't simply a tragic struggle between two peoples claiming the same land, but a century-long colonial campaign against Palestinians, backed first by Britain & later by the United States. Khalidi, a Palestinian-American historian at Columbia, tells the story through six turning points, beginning with the 1917 Balfour Declaration & moving through the creation of Israel, the wars that followed, & the failures of the peace process. Drawing on historical archives & his own family's experiences, he makes a provocative argument: that Palestinians have never been negotiating on equal terms, & that understanding the conflict as a dispute between two competing national movements obscures the enormous imbalance of power between them. It's a forceful challenge to conventional accounts of Israel's founding, Zionism, & America's role in the region, & one that raises uncomfortable questions about nationalism, colonialism, & self-determination. Show up even if you only got through a chunk. We'll talk about where Khalidi's account is most convincing, where it leaves out important context, whether Zionism is best understood as a colonial movement or a national liberation movement, & what his interpretation of the past means for the possibility of peace today. UNMUTED is a discussion forum for the politically curious. Accessible. Engaging. Social. Open-minded is the name of the game. Join your people.

events.name: AI Founders Supper Club
events.description: Hi fellow founders  Angela & Hamza here from the AI Furnace. The AI Founders Supper Club is a private founders dinner club hosted by The AI Furnace (the largest community of AI startups in the world). Once a month, we host 15-20 early stage AI founders for a night of delicious food, discussions & connections with curated high quality founders in NYC. This is a referral based network, so feel free to apply here but the other way to get in is by being referred in by an existing founder member. What to expect: A 3-course meal, courtesy of our partners Meet dope founders building out of NYC Real conversations & place to vibe with other founders, solving similar problems ABOUT OUR HOSTS & SPONSORS The AI Furnace is NYC's largest & most active AI community. It was started by AI founders, Angela Mascarenas & Hamza Zaveri, who were based in NYC & London & started the org to support fellow AI founders & operators building in local cities outside of Cerebral Valley (San Francisco). It has since grown to a global community of 20,000 AI founders, operators & researchers & has since organized events in 4 countries & 7 cities including NYC, London, Paris, Dubai, Boston, DC, & Philly. Fidelity Private Shares brings certainty to startup founders with their cap table platform to help automate equity management operations & financings in a single collaborative hub. Leverage the scenario modeling tool & secure data room to prepare for the next round of funding. From inception to IPO, Fidelity has the expertise & robust support to help guide you. Connect with Charlie Stephens for more information. PwC's Emerging Company Solutions (ECS) practice is the leading provider of audit, tax, & IPO readiness services to companies backed by venture capital (VC) & private equity (PE) firms. More specifically, PwC's ECS practice has the greatest market share & is the #1 provider of audits of technology, software, & media company IPOs amongst the Big 4 accounting firms since 2017. Whether it be in connection with a Series A capital raise, a later-stage VC or PE firm investment, leading up to, during & subsequent to an IPO, PwC's ECS practice is uniquely positioned to be with you every step of the way, helping you achieve your business goals while minimizing risk. Niural is an AI-native, end-to-end HR & finance platform transforming global payroll, PEO, & compliance. Powered by EMMA, our intelligent AI coworker, Niural brings payroll, HR, & finance into a single, streamlined ecosystem. From automated payroll & HR workflows to global compliance across multiple jurisdictions-including support for both fiat & crypto payments-Niural helps companies scale with confidence. We make global operations smarter, faster, & more efficient. Ramp is an all-in-one financial operations platform designed to save businesses time & money. Combining corporate cards, expense management, bill payments, accounting automation, procurement, travel, treasury, & more, Ramp empowers finance teams to do their best work. More than 70,000 companies, from family-owned farms to space startups, have saved $10B & 27.5M hours with Ramp since its founding in 2019. Investors include Founders Fund, Thrive Capital, Khosla Ventures, Sequoia, Greylock, Stripe, Goldman Sachs, Coatue, & Redpoint, as well as over 100 angel investors who were founders or executives of leading companies.

events.name: Hype vs Reality - AI Debunk Night
events.description: October 2026 | In-Person at Pier 57 (Livestream TBA)Hype vs. Reality: An AI Debunk Night Every week there's a new AI headline designed to make your heart race. "700 agents went rogue." "AI just crossed the terrifying line." "Your job is next." This month, we're slowing down & reading the receipts. No outside food allowed. The venue has food for sale.   The format: We take the biggest AI stories of the year & break each one down in three moves:  What the headline said  What the primary sources actually show  What's genuinely still unknown The main event: The July 2026 Hugging Face breach - the "rogue agent swarm" story that's been viewed 15M+ times. We'll walk through OpenAI's own incident report & the independent METR investigation to show what really happened (spoiler: it's less "machine uprising," more "someone didn't patch an internal proxy"). "AI will kill us all" - who's selling the timelines, & what the technical critics actually claim Apply to give a presentation here. --- Speakers:Norman BBernie T(More TBA) Sponsors:Current Sponsor list still being compiled. If you'd like to sponsor the event, please reach out to us at speaking@thoughtful.events

events.description: The true entry points for startups working with government Join LACI at BATWorks & The Trust for Governors Island for a Climate Scaling Summit focused on one critical inflection point: how climate startups break into government as a customer, regulator, & partner. Securing contracts with the government can feel opaque to founders, but true entry points exist even if they are not always obvious to a first-time founder. This session demystifies how startups can work with government agencies & offers a valuable opportunity for founders to ask agencies & entities for feedback, technical support, & opportunities to scale. The morning opens with a fireside chat/panel, followed by five hands-on workshops covering: LegislationPermitting & CodePilot KPIs for Government AgenciesCapital Projects & Public-Private DevelopmentEducation & Workforce This is the final of four Climate Scaling Summits hosted by LACI at BATWorks in 2026, all under the theme of accelerating commercialization of clean energy innovation in NY by focusing on common problems faced by startups after the pilot stage. About LACI & The Trust for Governors Island LACI has deployed $25M in cleantech pilots over the past four years, from first commercial deployments to the nation's first zero-emissions delivery zone & is now supercharging the Pilots at BAT program & deeper deployment of the LACI Cleantech Debt Fund.  The Trust for Governors Island's Climate Piloting Program offers early-stage companies & innovators the opportunity to test & scale climate products & services in a real-world environment. Since its launch in 2023, the program has advanced projects in living shorelines, clean water, circular economy, buildings, energy, air quality, & urban agriculture-opening doors to new customers, suppliers, talent, investors, & public agency partnerships. The program is a core initiative of the Trust's Center for Climate Solutions, an initiative dedicated to accelerating equitable climate solutions for cities on Governors Island. events.description: Join Antoine Jebara (Co-founder, JumpCloud) & Noah Landow (Founder & CEO, Macktez) for an informal conversation between an expert on scaling global technology companies & the evolution of identity & access management & the founder of a technology consulting firm. In an era defined by remote work & the rapid rise of agentic AI, the concepts of identity & security are shifting beneath our feet. As AI agents begin to act on our behalf, how do we maintain control, responsibility, & security? If an AI agent executes a transaction or accesses a database, who is truly holding the keys? Antoine brings a unique perspective from the front lines of this transition, from pioneering decentralized 2FA & password management at MYKI to driving global strategy & partner ecosystems at JumpCloud. Join us at the Macktez office, after work, over light snacks & sips, for an exploratory conversation on the challenges of scaling fast-growing global companies & how different security architectures impact our long-term safety in a cloud-first world. We will dive into the shifting landscape of encryption, the unique hurdles of managing remote-first organizations, & what it truly means to "identity" ourselves in the age of AI. Photography, audio, & video recording may occur at this event & by attending you consent to such recording media & its release, publication, exhibition, or reproduction. Event StructureWe ask that guests arrive between 7-7:30 pm to minimize disruption during the talk. 7 pm - Doors open, opportunity to mingle over snacks & sips with other attendees7:30 pm - Guests take their seats for the talk8:15 pm - Informal mixer resumes On AttendanceWe have a limited capacity. events.name: Business Funding - An International Perspective
events.description: Every stage of growing a business is a funding decision, even when it doesn't feel like one. How you pay for the next market, the next hire, the next acquisition quietly shapes what the business is worth years later, & who you can sell it to. events.name: Unmuted  Debate - AI & China
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In July, a Chinese lab you'd probably never heard of published Kimi K3: 2.8 trillion parameters, billed as the largest open model on earth, weights posted free on Hugging Face for anyone to download. It's one of four Chinese labs that spent the last year closing the gap with the American frontier, then giving the result away. Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi. Four of the five most-used open models in the world now come out of Beijing, & American developers are running them inside hospitals, law firms, & startups because they're the cheapest, fastest tools available. No API someone in Washington controls. No off switch. Just download & go. One camp says a model is just math. Open weights run on a consumer's machine, the code is right there to inspect, & cutting Americans off from the best tools on the planet is how you lose a technology race. The other camp says the giveaway is the strategy. China seeds the world's infrastructure with their standards, their defaults, their assumptions, & the dependency follows once switching costs become unbeatable. So: should Americans be allowed to build on Chinese open-weight models or is this the new Cold War's Monkey's Paw? Arguing for, Rob Li is Managing Partner of Amont Partners, a New York global equity firm that invests across the US & Asia. He has spent his career putting capital on both sides of the Pacific, from Yum China to Alibaba deals, & he thinks the country that walls itself off from the best tools available loses. Arguing against, Will McKelvey is a Principal at Lerer Hippeau, one of New York's oldest venture firms, where he backs early-stage founders & spends his days watching for the future of AI, especially in consumer. He got his start by way of a congressional office, & he thinks the cheapest model on the market is the one you pay for slowly. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones. In collaboration with COMMITTEE OF 100Committee of 100 (C100) is a nonprofit U.S. leadership organization of distinguished Chinese Americans dedicated to advancing the full participation of Chinese Americans in American society & fostering constructive U.S.-China relations. For more than 35 years, C100 has brought together leaders across business, government, academia, technology, media, the arts, & other fields to advance its dual mission. Learn more at committee100.org.

events.name: Tech Table Talk: Career, Family & Life On Your Terms
events.description: Tech Table Talk: Career, Family & Life on Your Terms is an intimate dinner bringing together women in tech for an honest conversation about career, fertility, family planning, & building a life on their own terms. Hosted by Baddies in Tech in partnership with Spring Fertility, the evening will create space for women to have the kinds of conversations we don't often have: How do you think about growing your career while also considering a future family? What options are available if your personal & professional timelines do not align perfectly? And how can having more information today create more choices tomorrow? We're setting the Tech Table to create space for a conversation you may have been thinking about but have not had anyone to talk to about. You'll walk away not just with a great meal & new professional connections, but also more information, more context, & more confidence to make decisions that feel right for the life you're building! What to ExpectWelcome & Opening ToastBaddies in Tech & Spring Fertility will welcome the group & set the tone for an open, judgment-free conversation about career, fertility, family planning, & the life you're building. Dinner & Tech Table TalkOver dinner, guests will have the opportunity to connect more deeply with one another through thoughtful conversation & curated table prompts, exploring the realities of building a career while also thinking about relationships, motherhood, fertility, timing, & what it means to make decisions on your own terms. Fertility Planning Q&A with Dr. Shante Sullivan-PikeThroughout the evening, Dr. Shante Sullivan-Pike of Spring Fertility will help answer questions & demystify fertility, fertility preservation, & family-planning options. Dr. Chantae Sullivan-Pyke is a double board certified Fertility Specialist & Site Director of Spring Fertility Long Island. She completed her medical training at Yale University, Columbia University, & the University of Pennsylvania. Dr. Sullivan-Pyke brings a thoughtful & compassionate approach to fertility care, rooted in deep clinical experience & a genuine connection with her patients. She combines her expertise with a strong commitment to the patient experience, creating a supportive & empowering atmosphere throughout the process. Her areas of clinical focus include IVF, fertility preservation, & oncofertility, & she is particularly passionate about helping her patients navigate complex fertility decisions with clarity & confidence. What You'll Leave WithFresh perspective on navigating career goals alongside personal & family plans New relationships with women thinking through many of the same questions A better understanding of your fertility & family-planning options More clarity around fertility preservation & when it may be worth exploring Greater confidence asking questions about your reproductive health A stronger connection to the Baddies in Tech & Spring Fertility communitie Attendance is complimentary & curated. Because this dinner is intentionally intimate & limited to approximately 20-25 guests, registrations will be reviewed to create a group that aligns with the purpose of the evening. Submitting the registration form expresses your interest in attending & does not guarantee an invitation. Confirmed guests will be notified approximately one week before the event.

events.name: What Makes A Good Life? A Guided Public Discussion On AI
events.description: The oldest question philosophers have asked is: What makes a good life? This inquiry has been important not only for guiding individual decisions, but also for shaping institutions & public policy. Now, amid the rapid changes AI is bringing to every aspect of our lives, & the growing debate about its risks & benefits, we must ask: What makes a good life, & how does AI enable or hinder it? Together, we will explore this question through prompts & shared reflection. Dr. Ece Tekbulut is a political philosopher & the founder of Thinking Through. She earned her Ph.D. from Columbia University. Through Thinking Through, she brings rigorous philosophical inquiry into everyday life, convening groups to engage with themes central to contemporary society, especially where people feel at an impasse. One such focus is AI's impact on human flourishing. Her work fosters public discourse on AI's implications & the ethical questions that surround it, & she writes on AI & society for Medyascope. Wissam Kahi is the founder of Odyssey Lead, where he helps companies capture the value of AI that usually gets lost between the boardroom & the front line. For seven years he led digital transformation across United Rentals' network of more than 1,500 locations, & he learned there that AI only sticks when the people who do the work help shape it. His essays on Substack & his novella The Panama Dilemma explore the question at the heart of tonight's discussion: what makes a good life when the machine is doing the living? Matt Konwiser is an Ecosystem Leader & Field CTO at IBM. He serves on the AI Advisory Council at the Global Technology Industry Association (GTIA) & writes a regular column on AI for CFO Intelligence Magazine. events.name: Is Everything Predictable - AI, Prediction Markets & Philosophy Of Foresight
events.description: In this six-week course, explore works from philosophy, cultural studies, & journalism to understand how technologies that predict the future also shape the present.The age of AI, prediction markets, & real-time data analysis brings predictive reasoning into all corners of human life. Once considered a niche academic interest area, the philosophy & politics of prediction is now relevant to everybody. Is Everything Predictable?: AI, Prediction Markets, & the Philosophy of Foresight presents scholarly material on forecasting technologies in a rigorous but highly accessible format.Drawing from a range of sources, we center scholarly texts & deeply-researched journalism that uncover the links between digital calculation, philosophical notions of time & free will, & the reality of living in an age where everything seems reducible to calculation.Guest speakers from academia & tech journalism will round out our seminar sessions, & for our final meeting, students have the option of presenting original research or creative work in an event open to the general public.SyllabusIn the early weeks of the course, we read texts from contemporary media studies & political theory that construe prediction & speculation as forms of governance. We also address probabilistic reasoning as a key feature of artificial intelligence & prediction market mechanisms, using frameworks suitable for participants without any background in STEM. As we will see, the similarities & differences between how probability works in AI versus prediction markets have much to tell us about these tools effects on everything from global warfare & the environment to creativity & personal relationships.After establishing a strong practical & theoretical foundation in AI & prediction markets, we turn to philosophical writing on the nature of freedom, self-expression, & power. These texts urge us to ask whether predictive technologies empower us with highly advanced forms of knowledge; if they inhibit us by constraining our imagination of whats possible; or if both of these outcomes might be true at once. We also read articles & listen to podcast interviews with our guest speakers in anticipation of their visits.Throughout our sessions, we examine case studies related to tech companies, specific applications, & major actors in the AI & prediction market space. The courses culminating event  a salon open to the general public  reflects our interest in connecting questions & concerns that seem highly academic to current events & everyday life. Students who choose to give presentations will participate in an additional workshop or one-on-one advising session to help them prepare. By the courses end, we will be able to navigate a world driven by predictive technologies with greater clarity, confidence, & wisdom, & to share our perspectives on them in a way that empowers those around us.Learning OutcomesConnect AI & prediction market functionalities to political & cultural affairsDevelop critical reading skills applicable to philosophy & journalismApply frameworks from the theoretical humanities to real-world developments in politics & technologyMake scholarly ideas accessible to a wide range of audiencesScholarshipsIndex scholarships are designed to benefit underrepresented groups, BIPOC members of our community, & those for whom the class price is not accessible. These need-based scholarships will go to the candidates who best demonstrate why they should be chosen for the free spot to our class. You can apply for a scholarship here.Instructor BioEmma Stamm is a writer & professor with a background in philosophy & the social study of science & technology (STS). She holds a PhD in Interdisciplinary Studies from Virginia Tech & has taught courses on the philosophy & social implications of technology at Villanova University, Virginia Tech, the Acid Horizon Research Commons, New York University, where she currently teaches for the Department of Media, Culture, & Communication. As a public-facing scholar, she has written for Vice Motherboard, Real Life Mag, & Communications of the Association for Computing Machinery, in addition to co-hosting the LEPHT HAND podcast. She is the co-founder & Executive Director of theLenox Institute for Advanced Study, which makes critical science & tech education accessible beyond academia.RefundsWe get that things come up, but we rely on headcounts to make our programs viable. If you request a refund...More than 4 weeks before the program begins  100% refundMore than 2 weeks before the program begins  50% refundFewer than 2 weeks before the program begins  No refundThanks for understanding & for supporting our ability to provide cool offerings through your purchase.Media Release ClauseBy attending this event, you consent to being photographed, filmed, or recorded, & grant Index Space permission to use this content for promotional or informational purposes.

Is Everything Predictable?: AI, Prediction Markets, & the Philosophy of Foresight presents scholarly material on forecasting technologies in a rigorous but highly accessible format.Drawing from a range of sources, we center scholarly texts & deeply-researched journalism that uncover the links between digital calculation, philosophical notions of time & free will, & the reality of living in an age where everything seems reducible to calculation.Guest speakers from academia & tech journalism will round out our seminar sessions, & for our final meeting, students have the option of presenting original research or creative work in an event open to the general public.SyllabusIn the early weeks of the course, we read texts from contemporary media studies & political theory that construe prediction & speculation as forms of governance. We also address probabilistic reasoning as a key feature of artificial intelligence & prediction market mechanisms, using frameworks suitable for participants without any background in STEM. As we will see, the similarities & differences between how probability works in AI versus prediction markets have much to tell us about these tools effects on everything from global warfare & the environment to creativity & personal relationships.After establishing a strong practical & theoretical foundation in AI & prediction markets, we turn to philosophical writing on the nature of freedom, self-expression, & power. These texts urge us to ask whether predictive technologies empower us with highly advanced forms of knowledge; if they inhibit us by constraining our imagination of whats possible; or if both of these outcomes might be true at once. We also read articles & listen to podcast interviews with our guest speakers in anticipation of their visits.Throughout our sessions, we examine case studies related to tech companies, specific applications, & major actors in the AI & prediction market space. The courses culminating event  a salon open to the general public  reflects our interest in connecting questions & concerns that seem highly academic to current events & everyday life. Students who choose to give presentations will participate in an additional workshop or one-on-one advising session to help them prepare. By the courses end, we will be able to navigate a world driven by predictive technologies with greater clarity, confidence, & wisdom, & to share our perspectives on them in a way that empowers those around us.Learning OutcomesConnect AI & prediction market functionalities to political & cultural affairsDevelop critical reading skills applicable to philosophy & journalismApply frameworks from the theoretical humanities to real-world developments in politics & technologyMake scholarly ideas accessible to a wide range of audiencesScholarshipsIndex scholarships are designed to benefit underrepresented groups, BIPOC members of our community, & those for whom the class price is not accessible. These need-based scholarships will go to the candidates who best demonstrate why they should be chosen for the free spot to our class. You can apply for a scholarship here.Instructor BioEmma Stamm is a writer & professor with a background in philosophy & the social study of science & technology (STS). She holds a PhD in Interdisciplinary Studies from Virginia Tech & has taught courses on the philosophy & social implications of technology at Villanova University, Virginia Tech, the Acid Horizon Research Commons, New York University, where she currently teaches for the Department of Media, Culture, & Communication. As a public-facing scholar, she has written for Vice Motherboard, Real Life Mag, & Communications of the Association for Computing Machinery, in addition to co-hosting the LEPHT HAND podcast. She is the co-founder & Executive Director of theLenox Institute for Advanced Study, which makes critical science & tech education accessible beyond academia.RefundsWe get that things come up, but we rely on headcounts to make our programs viable. events.name: The Outliers Summit
events.description: The Outliers Summit 2026We're excited to announce the Outliers Summit. November 5 & 6 in New York City. A two-day gathering for founders, creators, operators, builders, & thinkers bringing unreasonably ambitious ideas to life, hosted by Ankur Nagpal & Andrew Yeung, in partnership with AngelList.  Previously, we called this event the OOO Summit. But this year, we've evolved the brand & doubled the event to reflect what we believe the future will look like. Over the last two years, thousands of ambitious people attended our summit - multi-hyphenates, hybrid creator-entrepreneurs, solo builders, AI-native founders, & even people running companies of one with agents doing the rest. The word to describe this kind of person is Outlier. The type of person who chooses to take the unconventional path & pave their own way. This year, the Outliers Summit will be two full days:  DAY 1: NOVEMBER 5 // HOW OUTLIERS BUILD Tactical sessions where you leave having built the thing yourself - an app, an agent, an audience, a brand.  DAY 2: NOVEMBER 6 // HOW OUTLIERS THINK Off-the-record conversations about the bets & mindsets that separate outliers from everyone else.  SpeakersSam Parr, Founder of My First Million, Hampton, The Hustle (acq for >$25M) Ryan Hoover, Founder of Product Hunt & Weekend Fund Sahil Lavingia, Founder & CEO of Gumroad ($1B paid out to creators) Zach Sims, Co-founder & CEO of Codecademy (acq for >$500M) Andy Dunn, Founder of Bonobos & Pie (acq for >$300M) Nadya Okamoto, Founder of August & Co-Founder of Pie Nat Eliason, Author & Head of Founders School Nik Sharma, Founder of Sharma Brands Carina Hong, Founder of Axiom (raised $200M at a $1.6B val) & many MORE to be announced. & many more ... to be announced.  Who You'll Be In the Room WithAcross 13 events in 2024 & 2025, 4,298 people from 3,083 companies have come through our events. 54% are founders, C-suite, VP+ or investors 39% are founders & CEOs specifically 48% of founders have raised $1M or more 22% come back for two or more of our events They also come from Google, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, Stripe, Ramp, Notion, Palantir, Goldman Sachs, & a16z, & from the several thousand startups that make up the rest of the room. Every guest is reviewed before approval. If you are unreasonably ambitious, we'd love to meet you.  Past speakersSahil Bloom is a New York Times Bestselling Author & one of the pioneers of 'threads' onTwitter Andrew Yang founded the Forward political party in 2021, Venture for America in 2011, & the ex-CEO of Manhattan Prep. Sam Parr is the Founder of The Hustle, Hampton, My First Million. Alex Lieberman is the Co-founder of Morning Brew. Kyla Scanlon is the Founder of Bread. Guillermo Rauch is the CEO of Vercel. Brianne Kimmel is the Founder at Worklife Ventures. Justin Welsh has built his 1-person business to >$2m in revenue per year with 95% profit margins, without hiring a team or increasing his hours Nathan Barry, Founder, CEO of Kit (Formerly ConvertKit)  Why You Should AttendBuild a powerful network of founders, investors, & industry leaders. Unlock growth tactics & stay ahead of the curve-know where the puck is going. Learn how to scale your business-from six to seven figures, or even seven to ten. Grow a profitable lifestyle business or blitzscale your venture-backed startup. Build a powerful personal brand & grow your audience. Master marketing strategies to go viral. Whether you're just starting out or are already an entrepreneur, gain the insights you need to accelerate your success.  Meet the OrganizersAnkur Nagpal has built & sold two companies for nine figures: Teachable for $250M & Carry to AngelList. He's now building USVC alongside Naval Ravikant, a public venture fund opening access to world-class startup investments. Andrew Yeung is the founder of Fibe & The Shortlist NYC. He is also an angel investor & Partner at Next Wave NYC, a pre-seed venture fund. Andrew has hosted over 300 events for 50,000 founders, operators, investors, & tech professionals that were featured by Bloomberg, Business Insider, Fast Company, Fortune Magazine, Axios, Newsweek, & Forbes. Business Insider dubbed him the "Gatsby of Silicon Alley." Pie is the real-life social networking app that helps people turn online connections into real-world plans. Built around events & shared favorites-from run clubs & watch parties to live music & vintage markets-Pie makes it effortless to discover what's happening, invite friends, & show up. With over 300,000 users, Pie is on a mission to defeat social isolation & rebuild in-person community. Pie was named "Apps We Love" & "App of the Day" by Apple & the most promising startup in Chicago by 1871. Learn more at getpie.app. Together, Ankur Nagpal & Andrew Yeung are creating the premier summit for business owners, operators, & disruptors-a place where entrepreneurs don't just learn, but also build, network, & grow.  Meet Our Partners Stan: build a business around your ideasStan helps creators & entrepreneurs build businesses around their ideas. Stanley is their private beta AI partner that turns conversations, experiences, & expertise into personalized content & opportunities, built in public with founders & creators who believe the future belongs to those who learn, share, & build openly. Learn more at stan.store.  Circle: the modern platform for digital businessesBring your audience, products, & customer relationships into one place. Create websites, newsletters, courses, memberships, events, & communities, then use built-in AI, automation, & customer data to grow & manage your business. events.name: Space Art - Culture Beyond Earth
events.description: Space Art: Culture Beyond Earth As space exploration expands beyond scientific & technological frontiers, art is opening new ways to consider humanity's cultural presence beyond Earth. Prof. Barilaro examines how music & artistic practice can connect scientific research with human experience, from creative interventions in space missions to explorations of the algorithmic sky. Drawing on work at the NYUAD Space Art Laboratory, the presentation considers how art can serve as a tool for research, experimentation, & expression, while raising new questions about creativity, identity, & who gets to shape humanity's voice in space. *Registrants will receive a QR code to access the campus. SpeakerLeonardo Barilaro, Visiting Associate Professor of Space Technology & Sonic Arts; Artist in Residence; Lead, Space Art Laboratory, NYUAD

events.name: Ugly Talks - Failure Is Key To Success
events.description: Failure gets talked about like it is part of the journey. That is the lie. The real thing is messier. Missed bets. Wrong hires. Near-breakdowns. The week you stop sleeping & start doing math at 3:00 AM. Founders are expected to eat it quietly & keep moving. No language for what happened. No playbook for what to do next. Ugly Talk is a founder room for the part nobody posts. No fluff. No consultants. Just builders with scars, talking about the call that cost them.  Why you should be in this room.Hear what failure cost them. Then hear what they did next. Learn how experienced founders separate self-worth from outcomes when things go sideways. Spot the patterns behind repeat mistakes. And the early signals you should not ignore. Leave with a few concrete moves for the next hard week. Not inspiration. Meet other founders in the thick of it. The ones who are still building.  What's on the table.Dare to suck: how permission to fail unlocks real progress The moment things broke: missed opportunities, wrong turns, near-breakdowns, & what changed afterward Failure vs identity: separating self-worth from outcomes Treating setbacks as data: what to measure, what to ignore, & how to decide fast Rejection as redirection: how founders find the signal in the no Habits for staying focused & resilient when everything feels uncertain  Run of show6:00 - 6:30 PM: Reception (check-in & light drinks) 6:30 - 6:40 PM: Welcome remarks 6:40 - 6:50 PM: Keynote Speech by Ben McKean 6:50 - 7:30 PM: Panel Discussion 7:30 - 7:45 PM: Audience Q&A 7:45 - 8:00 PM: Mixer + snacks & drinks  Featured speakers.Ben McKean - Founder & Chief Executive Officer, Hungryroot Ben McKean is the Founder & CEO of Hungryroot, a personalized healthy eating assistant that uses AI to make meal planning, food shopping, & nutrition effortless & enjoyable. Prior to Hungryroot, Ben was a Vice President & General Manager at Groupon, overseeing their food & beverage business. Ben came to Groupon through the acquisition of Savored, which he founded in 2009. Savored was the nation's leading provider of yield management technology to the restaurant industry, used by over two thousand restaurants nationwide & nearly one million diners. Prior to Savored, Ben worked in Merrill Lynch's technology investment banking group. Ben is a graduate of Georgetown University & currently lives in North Carolina with his wife & kids. Stephen McKinney - Founder & CEO, Bizbe Stephen McKinney is a serial entrepreneur with over a decade of experience across tech, marketing, & logistics. He's the founder & CEO of Bizbe.com, an AI-native business brokerage & lower middle market M&A firm based in New York & Miami. A former contestant on ABC's Shark Tank, Steve previously founded & led Retty Logistics, a seven-figure last-mile delivery company acquired by DXP Logistics & Webster Logistics. Dmitry Koltunov - Founder & CEO, Arbor Dmitry Koltunov is a serial entrepreneur, technologist, educator, & storyteller. He is the founder & CEO of Arbor, an AI-powered content engine that helps enterprises scale their communications with video & beyond. Previously, he co-founded & served as CTO of ALICE, a hospitality technology company that grew into a global industry leader before being acquired by Expedia Group. Dmitry also leads the New York City chapter of the Startup Leadership Program, New York's oldest startup fellowship, whose 500+ alumni have collectively raised more than $1 billion in funding across every industry imaginable. He is passionate about helping founders navigate the challenges of building & scaling companies. Outside of technology, Dmitry is an award-winning songwriter & theater producer currently developing a new musical for Broadway. He holds degrees in Computer Science & Economics from the University of Pennsylvania & is a CFA charterholder. Gwendolyn von Rahn - Co-Founder & CEO, Sweetling Health Gwendolyn von Rahn is the Co-Founder & CEO of Sweetling Health, an postpartum intelligence platform built for at-risk & hard-to-reach populations. She's a second-time exited founder, an award-winning marketer with over a decade of experience building consumer brands for women, Gwen led creative & brand teams at Vogue, InStyle, & POPSUGAR before founding & scaling a mission-driven consumer brand into Nordstrom distribution that raised over $1M for melanoma research through the Melanoma Research Foundation. She holds a Cornell Johnson MBA & founded Sweetling from her own lived experience with the postpartum care gap.  Who's hosting it.Victoria Yampolsky - President, The Startup Station Victoria Yampolsky is the Founder & President of The Startup Station, a strategic CFO advisory firm & financial education platform for startups. She partners with founders on financial strategy, modeling, & fundraising, having supported over 150 companies across 15 industries in raising more than $50M in venture capital. Victoria is also an advocate for female founders & access to capital, & has taught finance to more than 20,000 entrepreneurs through programs including the Bank of America Institute for Women's Entrepreneurship at Cornell. She began her career at Deutsche Bank & Capgemini, & holds a BS in Computer Science from Cornell University & an MBA from Columbia Business School.  Who's getting in.Early-stage tech founders & operators navigating uncertainty, setbacks, or the emotional weight of building a company. Expected roles may include: Founders & co-founders (pre-seed to Series A) Operators (COO, Head of Ops, Chief of Staff) Product & Engineering leads building through ambiguity Growth & GTM leads working through missed targets & pivots Finance & strategy leaders supporting founder decision-making  Who's backing this.The Startup Station The Startup Station - is a CFO advisory & financial education platform for early-stage startups. We help early-stage founders build investor-ready financials & tell their funding story with confidence. In the past decade, we've helped 150+ founders raise over $50M & educated 20,000+ entrepreneurs worldwide. The Startup Station also runs Speed Pitch, an exclusive investor-founder matchmaking event series for early-stage startups where founders are matched with 3 investors by sector, stage, & check size. Mind Your Business Every attendee will receive a free copy of keynote speaker Ben McKean's Mind Your Business. Mind Your Business is a practical parable for people rethinking work as AI advances. Set over a four-day retreat, it follows six participants competing for funding to bring one vision to life. As they evaluate six competing proposals, they begin to confront deeper questions about what gives them energy, who they serve, & what they uniquely contribute. Those patterns form what the book calls their Soulcode-the way purpose, belonging, imagination, & courage shape how they work. Told with humor & warmth, the story turns familiar workplace tensions into practical lessons for contributing more deeply, seeing new possibilities, & acting with greater conviction. At its core, the book argues that the opportunity of the AI era isn't doing more work-it's knowing what work is worth doing. GREY Journal GREY Journal - Media partner spotlighting modern entrepreneurs (featured on Apple News + Google News).  About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough "aha!" moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons & insights. With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami, we've built a vibrant community of thousands of founders & industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape. Official Website: UglyTalk.com Important Notice for Ugly Talk AttendeesAdmission & Confirmation Attendance is by approval only. Approved guests will receive a confirmation email along with a calendar invite. Invitations are non-transferable. Additional event details will be shared as the event approaches. Code of Conduct By attending, you agree to: Maintain respect & professionalism, adhering to all venue rules, policies, & applicable laws. Refrain from harassment, discrimination, unwelcome sexual advances (verbal or physical), intimidation, or inappropriate photography/recording. Report any violations to the event hosts immediately. Violations may result in immediate removal from the event & exclusion from future invitations. Liability & Risk Participation is voluntary & at your own risk. The event organizers, hosts, sponsors, & venue are not liable for personal injury, lost or stolen belongings, or any other damages incurred during the event. Media Consent By attending, you grant the event organizers & affiliated entities the right to capture, use, & distribute photos, videos, & audio recordings of you for promotional, marketing, & other lawful purposes, including digital & print media, advertising, & social media. You waive any right to inspect or approve the final materials & release all claims related to their use. Communications By registering, you agree to receive marketing & promotional communications from Ugly Talk & its co-hosts, partners, & sponsors. You may unsubscribe at any time. Agreement If you do not agree to this Code of Conduct, please refrain from attending the event.  Join us to stay updated on upcoming Ugly Talk events! Join the newsletter  Follow us on IG  Official website
