events.name: Can Your Agents Actually Ship?
events.description: Can your agents actually ship?Compose your AI-native SDLCYour AI agents can't be trusted with data they can't find, can't understand, & aren't sure they're allowed to touch. And even when they get it right, the code they write still stalls in a delivery pipeline built for human speed. On Nov2 we will tackle both: first the data foundations agents need to trust, then the SDLC they need to ship through. Opening talk: From a Data Swamp to a Data Agent You Can Trust The evening opens with Grzegorz Krl on the data foundations AI agents need to find, understand & safely access your data. We've run this talk at Boston & San Francisco Tech Week, & both times it ran long because nobody wanted to stop asking questions. Full session details: https://luma.com/il0xoz9a Main session: Can your agents actually ship? AI can write code. Getting that code to production is another matter. Most engineering organizations hit the same wall: the bottleneck isn't the agent, it's everything downstream of it. Pipelines, CI, reviews, security gates, release processes: all of it was built for human speed, not AI. Visdom, built by VirtusLab, is the missing layer between AI coding & production. It lets you compose an AI-native SDLC, piece by piece: the context, validation, governance & orchestration agents need to ship safely & at scale. Come see what that looks like in practice. We'll cover: Why AI adoption stalls after the first wave of excitement What infrastructure an AI-native SDLC actually requires How Visdom connects agents to your SDLC, component by component Live demos of AI agents shipping production-ready code Q&A with the Visdom team Evaluating AI coding assistants or already rolling them out across teams? This session is about what happens after the code is written.  What you'll see liveA hands-on walkthrough of how Visdom removes friction across context, execution, & validation, turning your SDLC into a system AI agents can reliably operate on: Deep repository scanning that builds the semantic context AI agents actually need: not just open files, but the full dependency & intent graph across your codebase Blast radius scoring on an AI-generated PR before it touches CI, catching what code review misses when your team merges 3x more than last quarter Governed sandbox execution with full audit trails: the missing layer between the AI suggested it & it's running in production A live maturity assessment on a real delivery pipeline: where it stands today, & the smallest concrete step that unlocks the next level Who should join?CTOs, CDOs, VPs of Engineering & Data, Heads of Platform & AI, & senior engineers responsible for developer productivity, data platforms & AI adoption strategy. Especially if your AI tools shine in demos but stall in your CI/CD pipeline, or your agents can't tell which table is the right one. Why it's worth your time Get a practical diagnostic for making your data usable by AI agents See what an AI-native SDLC looks like in practice (live demo) Learn how to assess your AI maturity, step by step Learn how to start small, validate quickly, & evolve without big upfront risk Agenda6:00 PM - Doors open, drinks & networking6:30 PM - Opening talk: From a Data Swamp to a Data Agent You Can Trust (incl. Q&A)7:00 PM - Panel: real stories from AI adoption7:45 PM - Live demo: Visdom8:15 - 9:00 PM - Q&A & networking SpeakersPractitioners working hands-on with AI-driven delivery, data platforms, developer tooling, & real-world implementation: Grzegorz Krl, Tech Lead & Data Architect at VirtusLabGrzegorz believes that solid data systems start with a deep understanding of what the business actually needs. He works closely with organizations to put their business domains at the center of every data initiative, so that architectures, models & pipelines reflect how the business really operates. Artur Skowroski, Head of Application Development at VirtusLabArtur has spent more than ten years in the industry, on everything from greenfield builds to systems older than he is. He has worked as a Software Engineer, Tech Lead, Architect & Technical Product Manager, which gives him a broad view of the problems he tackles. He still likes to stay hands-on & has been writing a weekly roundup of the JVM ecosystem at jvm-weekly.com for over two years. Hosted by VirtusLabWe work with organizations ranging from global brands (including top-tier investment banks, Databricks, Airbnb, & DHL) to fast-growing startups, helping them build data platforms & AI systems that actually scale. At our core, we're engineers working with engineers, & we actively support the community through meetups, events, & shared learning. If you're working on AI in software delivery, this is where it starts to actually work.

events.name: Future Of AI Infrastructure
events.description: Let's talk about what's coming in the world of AI infra. Anthony Erondu is a Principal Consultant focused on AI infrastructure, GPU compute & Physical AI. He partners with high growth companies across the space to build product & engineering teams, placing talent from VP level leaders through senior ICs across some of the most critical areas of the AI stack. Akaanksha Sinha is an award-winning trailblazer in AI, cybersecurity & governance architecture. Over a decade in the enterprise stack. She founded AKAVAM, a governance-through-architecture company for enterprise AI. Its platform, AEVO, combines infrastructure as code, policy as code & compliance as code into deterministic execution, turning organizational context into operating capability. Ex-IBM, Deloitte, CUNY Srinivas Venkatanarayanan is a Senior Systems Research Engineer in Nvidia, Working in Cosmos Search. He specializes in multimodal reasoning, search & Curation for Post-training Vision Language Action Models. He works in Autonomous Vehicle & Robotics domain. Joshua Ness is a Senior AI Advisor & Consultant based in New York City. He spent 6 years at Verizon 5G Labs where he advised on enterprise adoption of 5G & edge computing technologies for clients, including the NFL, Disney, & MasterCard. He currently advises PE-backed global technology firms on AI implemention & organizational structure, including tech infrastructure modernization & regulatory compliance. Joshua holds a Fulbright Specialist appointment through which he works with the government of the Philippines on national AI readiness programs. He holds certifications from AWS, IBM, & IEEE in applied AI & cloud infrastructure.

events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: Did Maha Maha?
events.description: Has the MAHA movement made Americans healthier than the establishment? Americans spend more on healthcare than anyone else in the world. Yet we have soaring rates of obesity, diabetes, & chronic disease. So is the medical establishment failing us? And is MAHA actually doing any better? RFK's MAHA movement has put ultra-processed foods, environmental toxins, & chronic disease at the center of the national conversation. Supporters say it's finally challenging a healthcare system that profits from treating illness instead of preventing it. Critics say it's undermining trust in vaccines, established science, & the institutions responsible for keeping Americans healthy. So who's right? Is MAHA forcing a long-overdue reckoning with a broken healthcare system? Or is it replacing imperfect science with something far more dangerous? Kerry Semle is a biomedical engineer, former medical technology executive, & women's health advocate with 15 years of experience in medical devices & diagnostics. She's advocated for greater investment in women's health research & improved access to care. Emily Kaplan is the CEO & co-founder of the Broken Science Initiative, an organization challenging the scientific establishment & questioning how medical research is conducted, evaluated, & trusted. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

events.name: OverdriveAI Summit
events.description: Overdrive AIHosted by TechUnited:NJ, creators of Propelify, heralded by Forbes as the "SXSW of the Northeast," OverdriveAI is back, & this year it's a debate. The hottest topics in AI, argued live, both sides on stage. Jobs, energy, education, & more. Sharp thinkers go head to head, you hear the case for & against, & you decide where you land. Taking place this year at the Newark Museum of Art, where tech & culture share a roof, OverdriveAI brings together founders, operators, investors, & researchers from across the Northeast for a day built around one idea: the biggest questions in AI don't have easy answers, so let's actually argue about them. TICKETS ARE NOW LIVE!EXPLORE THE FULL OVERDRIVEAI EXPERIENCE Community AI TrainingHands-on morning AI training at EqualSpace designed for all experience levels. No prior AI experience required. Reserve Your Spot Executive AI TrainingA focused, practical AI training designed for executives & business leaders ready to better understand & apply AI within their organizations. Reserve Your Spot Pitch Roast LiveStartups pitch. Comedians roast. Everyone wins. Close out OverdriveAI with an evening of bold ideas, founder pitches, comedy, & connection. Reserve Your Spot   What to Expect Community AI Training A hands-on morning (10a-12p ET) AI training at EqualSpace designed for all experience levels. Come ready to learn, explore, & put AI into practice. No prior experience required. Executive AI Training Turn AI into practical business advantage. Start your morning with a focused AI training session designed for executives, business leaders, & decision-makers navigating the rapidly evolving AI landscape. This interactive session will explore practical ways leaders can better understand, evaluate, & apply AI within their organizations helping you move from conversation to action. The AI Debates The main event at the Newark Museum of Art. Will AI take your job or grow the economy? Who pays for AI's energy appetite? Does AI belong in the classroom? Can you still trust what you see? Startup demos will be featured between rounds & the afternoon will roll into TechUnited:NJ Birthday Party! Final topics & speakers are still being locked in, ticket holders hear every name first. Here's what's on the table so far: AI takes jobs vs. AI grows the economy - does automation erase more work than it creates? Is AI raising your energy bill? - the data center buildout is reshaping the grid, & New Jersey's in the middle of it. Does AI belong in the classroom? - a tutor for every student, or the end of learning how to think? Is it time for universal basic income? - if productivity keeps compounding, someone decides where the gains go. Can we handle deepfakes? - synthetic media's getting cheap & convincing, what's the real defense? Got a debate we missed? Suggest it, & if it makes the stage, you'll know it was yours. Live debates. Experts, opposing sides of one question, no hedging.Hot takes. Short, sharp presentations from speakers with a strong point of view.Networking. 300+ founders, researchers, & investors in one room, this year in a new venue built for it. Pitch Roast Live Closing the night at Newark Culture Club Close with startup pitches & a high-energy evening experience. Four founders pitch, three comedians & two investors roast. One walks out a winner! Last Year, at Nokia Bell Labs Speakers joined us from OpenAI, IBM, CoreWeave, Verizon, Perplexity, Nokia Bell Labs, BetterFutureLabs, NJEDA, & the NJ AI Hub. 16 speakers, 300+ attendees, a packed house. This year's lineup is coming together now, & it's bigger. OverdriveAI is one of many events TechUnited:NJ runs for its 13,000+ member community, from AI Demo Night to Propelify. Inquire about membership to hear about what's next. TechUnited:NJ members receive complimentary admission to OverdriveAI as part of their membership. Not a member yet? Join TechUnited:NJ to unlock complimentary access to OverdriveAI, along with year-round member benefits & opportunities to connect with New Jersey's innovation community.

events.name: Red Carpet Room Launch Party
events.description: If you show up with a backpack or your laptop you will be banned from the event. Please leave backpacks at home. RED CARPET ROOM Formerly Fun HouseHosted by Anwar EnterprisesSaturday, October 31, 2026 Exact address released to confirmed guests 24 hours before doors. About the Event Red Carpet Room is the next chapter of Fun House, rebuilt around a single idea: the people building brands should be building them together. This is a mixer for founders, creators, & investors from the Anwar Events community, gathered in one room with a shared reason to be there. Everyone in attendance is constructing something with their name attached to it. The night is designed so the person who can unblock you is standing a few feet away. We are doing it on Halloween on purpose. The city will be full of parties where nothing happens beyond the party itself. This one gives you a panel worth sitting through, a room worth working, & footage of yourself that you will actually use. Run of Show [7pm] - Doors, check-in, & open networking to start the night[8pm] - Panel: operators who built audiences, companies, & reputations from nothing   SPECIAL GUESTS BEING REVEALED NEXT WEEK [9pm] - Open mixer, with Red Carpet Show interviews running in the back room Who's Coming The typical guest is a founder raising or building, a creator monetizing an audience, or an investor looking for both. Expect crossover from fashion, music, media, tech, art & consumer brands, since that is who the Anwar Events community actually contains. Whether you are hiring, raising, pitching a collaboration, or looking for people who take their work as seriously as you do, you will be in the right room. The Red Carpet Show Throughout the night, Ilias will pull guests aside for on-camera interviews for The Red Carpet Show. There is one question at the center of every interview: how can he help you. Those conversations get cut into content that reaches an audience of 70,000 plus founders, investors, & creators. Sitting down costs you four minutes & can put your company in front of people you would never cold email. Dress Code Halloween night calls for more than a costume assembled at the last minute. Come dressed as the version of yourself the press would photograph, whether that means black tie, full character, or your own blend of both. Cameras run from the door onward, so arrive accordingly. Capacity & Entry Space is limited & the guest list is curated. A confirmed RSVP secures your place only until capacity fills, so arriving early is strongly recommended. Bring a valid ID for check-in at the door. About the Host Ilias Anwar is an entrepreneur, marketer, & community builder based in New York City. He has produced more than 600 events across NYC, LA, & San Francisco, cultivating a network of over 70,000 founders, investors, & creators. His work includes brand partnerships with Google, Red Bull, Andreessen Horowitz, & Universal Music Group, along with activations at NFL Super Bowl Weekend & New York Fashion Week. Today he runs Anwar Enterprises, a venture studio that launches & scales consumer & tech companies through distribution first. If you need to meet someone in this city, they have probably attended one of his events. Partners & Sponsors Creatorsarethenewstudios.comCanvas helps creators, founders, & brands turn ideas into media IP they own. AI agents handle the story, production plan, budget, & distribution, & your first IP is free. Happyboards.comHappyBoards makes chef-built charcuterie boards & grazing tables from locally sourced ingredients. It delivers same-day across 27+ Northeast cities, & HappyBoards is feeding the room tonight.Stay Connected Future Anwar Events drop to the community first. Get on the list at luma.com/iliasanwar & follow along on Instagram, X, & LinkedIn for everything we run next. Community Standards Red Carpet Room is inclusive of gender, sexuality, race, religion, & ability. Discrimination or harassment of any kind will not be tolerated on site. For urgent security concerns during the event, please contact venue staff directly. Disclaimers By attending this event, you agree to the following terms. Photography, Video, & Recording: This event will be photographed, filmed, live-streamed, & audio recorded. By entering the venue, you consent to being captured on camera & to the use of your name, image, voice, statements, & likeness by Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, The Red Carpet Show, & their affiliated partners & sponsors. Marketing & Promotional Use: Any material captured at this event may appear in promotional content, social media, websites, newsletters, press coverage, paid advertising, sponsor recap materials, & future marketing assets, worldwide & in perpetuity, without compensation. Guests waive any right to inspect or approve the finished material before publication. On-Camera Interviews: Participation in The Red Carpet Show is entirely voluntary. Sitting for an interview grants Anwar Enterprises the full right to edit, distribute, & monetize that footage across any platform, in any format, without further approval. Opting Out: If you do not wish to be photographed or filmed, please notify event staff upon arrival & avoid the designated filming areas. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to accommodate your request, though appearance in wide or crowd shots cannot be fully prevented. Guest Policy: This is a private, invitation-only event. RSVPs are non-transferable & entry is subject to ID verification. Organizers reserve the right to refuse entry at their discretion. Capacity & Access: This event has a strict capacity limit. A confirmed RSVP does not guarantee entry once capacity has been reached, so early arrival is strongly encouraged. Code of Conduct: All attendees are expected to conduct themselves professionally & respectfully. Organizers reserve the right to remove any guest whose behavior is disruptive or inappropriate, without refund or recourse. Liability: Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, & the venue are not responsible for loss, theft, or damage to personal property. Attendance is at your own risk. Data & Registration: Information submitted at registration may be shared with event sponsors & partners in accordance with their respective privacy policies. Guests may opt out of sponsor communications at any time. Changes & Cancellations: Event details including time, venue, panelists, & programming are subject to change. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to notify registered guests of any material changes.

events.name: Alpha Agentic Economy Summit
events.description: The Alpha Agentic Economy Summit is the gathering for leaders building the agentic enterprise & those accountable for its decisions. On November 6, 2026, at Nasdaq MarketSite in New York City, Alpha brings together board directors, management teams, investors, & technology leaders to address a defining challenge: enterprises are delegating authority to AI faster than their governance can adapt. AI agents are already executing transactions, writing & deploying code, & making operational decisions between board meetings. As their authority expands, so does the exposure: financial loss, operational disruption, legal liability, & reputational damage. Boards need to understand where that authority sits, how it is controlled, & what evidence demonstrates that oversight is working. The Summit connects the boardroom with the people shaping this shift. Confirmed speakers include Gary Vaynerchuk, Chairman of VaynerX; Stacy Brown-Philpot, Founder & Managing Partner of Cherryrock Capital; Ann Miura-Ko, Co-Founding Partner of Floodgate; Laura Desmond, CEO of Smartly; Al Zollar, board director at BNY, IBM, & Nasdaq; & Madhu Muthukumar, Chief Product Officer of SoFi. They join leaders including Navrina Singh of Credo AI, Philip Rathle of Neo4j, Wasim Khaled of Blackbird.AI, Ned Koh of Aaru, Dara Ladjevardian of Delphi, Bri Treece of Fathom, & Andrew Yang of Noble Mobile. alpha.ac These leaders bring perspectives across enterprise deployment, venture investment, corporate oversight, AI governance, & the technologies changing how companies operate. Directors with oversight responsibility & executives with execution responsibility will engage directly with the builders & investors advancing the agentic economy. Attendance is curated to keep the room senior, focused, & conducive to substantive conversation. Working conversations take place under the Chatham House Rule, creating space for candid discussion of architectures, incidents, controls, & consequential decisions. Sessions give speakers time to examine the material in depth. Questions continue during deliberate intermissions, where delegates can connect directly with speakers & peers in smaller conversations. The format is built for practical outcomes. There are no vendor pitches. The focus is on real systems, delegated authority, & the decisions leaders must make: what agents may do, who owns their actions, when humans must intervene, & how performance & accountability can be verified. Delegates leave with a clearer view of where agents are entering the enterprise, relationships with the people shaping that transition, & concrete priorities for their next board, committee, or management meeting. In the agentic economy, every decision to delegate authority is a governance decision. Growth depends on getting it right. Governance is Alpha.

events.name: AI Content System
events.description: Time Rich presents a working session, hosted by Ella Molony Cook, with co-hosting partner Wispr Flow & presenting partner Stanley. It opens with a short panel on why trust + distribution is now your moat. Then you build your content system in three parts: capture, context, create. You schedule your posts before you leave, so next week is handled. Every guest gets six months of Wispr Pro & Stanley. WHO IT'S FORFounders, business owners & investors who post in bursts, or know they should post more, & want content that sounds like them without writing every word. THE PANEL: YOUR MOAT IS YOUR DISTRIBUTIONA short conversation with investors, founders & ex-Google/YouTube on why visibility, trust & authority matter more than ever. WHAT GETS BUILTCapture. You'll set up Wispr Flow & brief your agent by voice instead of typing. Your best ideas sit in voice notes that never turn into posts, because nothing keeps running when you're busy. Your calls, voice notes & talks become raw material, & we pull ten stories out of your own words.Context. A tone of voice brief, the words you never use, & a call to action matched to each story.Create. Content agents that draft, repurpose across platforms & schedule. By the end, a week of posts is scheduled & the system is set up to fill the next one. Rather have it built for you? The Stanley team will be in the room. Just ask. WHAT TO BRING Laptop, charger & phone. Setup runs on iMessage or WhatsApp. One recording: a talk, a podcast, a call or a voice note Your three best published posts The one thing you want every post to drive: a booked call, a newsletter sign-up or a product AGENDA6:00-6:30 PM  Doors open, meet other founders6:30-6:35 PM  Welcome from Ella6:35-6:55 PM  Panel: your moat is your distribution6:55-8:20 PM  The build: capture, context, create8:20-9:00 PM  Q&A, drinks & mingling POWERED BY STANLEYStanley is an AI Head of Content. You text it a voice note, it drafts in your voice, & it repurposes whatever already performed. Stanley is our presenting partner for the night, so everyone builds on it live. OUR PARTNERTime Rich runs on voice, powered by Wispr FlowWispr Flow is our co-hosting partner. You'll talk to your agents instead of typing to them, & every guest leaves with six months of Wispr Pro. THE ROOMElla Molony Cook is an Australian 4x founder with 1 exit & an investor in Anthropic. Founder of Time Rich a media & AI education platform. Has a community of over 63K+ subscribers on Substack filled with founders, SMBs, angel investors, leaders & has hosted 250+ founder & investor experiences. Max Rivera is an angel investor & GP at GHOST Angels, a fund of Snapchat alumni backing early-stage consumer AI startups. Today he leads partnerships for Microsoft AI. Aishwarya Balaji is a 2x founder, venture fund advisor, investor & global speaker. He's ex-Google/YouTube & Squarespace, & a startup founder. TIME RICH CLUBWhere founders, creators & investors come to invest in themselves, their relationships, & building a system to become Time Rich. events.name: Responsible Tech Summit - Embedding Accountability AI Era
events.description: At a time when artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping society, the conversation is shifting from broad principles to real-world accountability. The 2026 summit will explore the theme of Principles to Power: Embedding Accountability in the AI Era. For years, the Responsible Tech field has been guided by ethical frameworks, voluntary commitments, & emerging standards. Today, the challenge is clear: how do we translate those ideas into systems of governance, oversight, & design that ensure innovation does not come at the expense of safety, rights, or trust? The Responsible Tech Summit is designed as a curated convening for 375 leaders that helps align & shape the direction of the movement. Participants will include global governance leaders, AI researchers, industry practitioners, policy experts, civil society advocates, & philanthropic leaders who are building the infrastructure of accountability for the digital age. Through keynotes, panels, & conversations, attendees will explore topics such as accountability by design, platform oversight, youth online safety, the Responsible Tech economy, & the evolving global regulatory landscape. All ticket proceeds fund free resources & services for the Responsible Tech community that our organization provides. Can't make it in person? The event will be livestreamed for free on All Tech Is Human's YouTube page, where recordings will also be available afterward. - Are you a journalist looking to potentially cover the Responsible Tech Summit? Reach out to Hello@AllTechIsHuman.org. Speakers for the Responsible Tech Summit 2026 Camille Francois - President, ROOST Eli Pariser - Co-Director, New_ Public Cathy O'Neil, Founder, Author, Mathematician & Data Scientist, O'Neil Risk Consulting & Algorithmic Auditing Rumman Chowdhury, CEO, Humane Intelligence PBC Alex Bores, Assembly Member, New York City's 73rd District Beth Goldberg, Founding Executive Director of Humanity AI Sinead Bovell, Founder, WAYE Alexis Wales, Chief Information Security Officer, GitHub Alison Lee, Chief R&D Officer, The Rithm Project Amanda Craig, General Manager of Responsible AI Public Policy, Microsoft Anya Schiffrin, Director, Media Program, Columbia University (SIPA) Carrie Varoquiers, Chief Impact Officer, Workday Joshua Elder, Senior Vice President & Head of Grantmaking, Siegel Family Endowment Julie Cordua, CEO, Thorn Fernanda Del Castillo, Director of AI Governance, Mastercard Kathy Pham, Faculty & Senior Fellow, Product & Responsible AI, Harvard University Kristin Hansen, Executive Director, Civic Health Project J. Trevor Hughes, President & CEO of IAPP Shreya Singh Hernndez, Senior Manager, Aspen Digital, The Aspen Institute Melanie Plaza, Chief Technology Officer, AE Studio Courtney Radsch, Director of the Center for Media & Digital Governance, Open Markets Institute; Fellow, Brookings Institution Andrew Rasiej, Founder, Civic Hall Clement Wolf, Director, Responsible AI Strategy, Google Hale Sirin, Program Scientist, Schmidt Sciences AI & Advanced Computing Institute Jeff Collins, Director of Trust & Safety, Amazon Web Services Alisar Mustafa, Head of AI Safety, Duco Experts   Agenda10:00 - 11:00 am ET | Check-in & Networking 11:00 - 11:10 am | Welcome remarks 11:15 - 11:45 am | Panel: Beyond Benchmarks: Turning Evaluations into Enforceable Standards 11:50 - 12:00 pm | Lightning talk 12:05 - 12:35 pm | Panel: Safety by Design: Accountability at the Intersection of AI, Industry, & Advocacy 12:40 - 1:40 pm | Lunch 1:45 - 2:05 pm | Fireside Chat: Open-Source, Open Questions: Transparency in the Age of AI 2:10 - 2:40 pm | Panel: Shared Risk, Shared Responsibility: Rethinking Responsible AI Governance 2:45 - 3:05 pm | Fireside Chat: Alignment in Practice: Building AI That Wants to be Good 3:05 - 3:30 pm | Networking break 3:30 - 4:00 pm | Panel: Trust as Strategy & the Fight Against AI-Enabled Fraud 4:05 - 4:15 pm | Keynote 4:15 - 4:25 pm | Lightning Talk 4:30 - 5:00 pm | Panel: Rebuilding the Commons: Community & Pluralism in the AI Era 5:05 - 5:25 pm | Fireside Chat: Looking Back to Look Ahead: Co-Designing AI After a Decade of Tech Lessons 5:25 - 5:30 pm | Closing remarks *See the full agenda & bios of our speakers here.   Sponsors for the Responsible Tech Summit 2026Special thanks to our strategic partners, Columbia World Projects, Forum One, & Highspring, for helping bring this critical conversation to life. WorkdayWorkday operates at the heart of the enterprise - HR, finance, & IT - where the margin for error is effectively zero. By tightly coupling AI with the context, guardrails, & trusted processes that run the business, Workday goes beyond AI that assists work to agents that do the work & drive measurable outcomes. More than 11,500 organizations worldwide, including more than 65% of the Fortune 500, trust Workday to deliver. MastercardMastercard is a global technology company in the payments industry, connecting consumers, financial institutions, merchants, & governments in more than 200 countries & territories. The company is committed to building a sustainable, inclusive digital economy that benefits everyone, everywhere. PinterestPinterest is a visual search & discovery platform where people find inspiration, curate ideas & shop products - all in a positive place online. Headquartered in San Francisco, Pinterest has over 600 million monthly active users worldwide. MicrosoftMicrosoft is a global technology leader empowering every person & organization on the planet to achieve more through its platforms & productivity tools. The company is committed to advancing responsible AI & ensuring emerging technologies are developed & deployed safely & ethically. Siegel Family EndowmentSiegel Family Endowment takes an inquiry-driven approach to grantmaking, informed by the scientific method. As technology reshapes society, we fund organizations asking critical questions about its impact on learning, work, & infrastructure. Founded in 2011 by David Siegel, co-founder & co-chairman of Two Sigma, we advance technology in the public interest, supporting research & initiatives that imagine a more inclusive, resilient technology-driven society. AE StudioAE Studio is an applied AI & AI alignment company that builds software products for clients while advancing research on making advanced AI systems safe & beneficial. Its recent work with Anthropic, GRAM, trains dangerous knowledge into removable modules so it can be stripped from a model before release. AE Studio reinvests its commercial success into neglected approaches to AI alignment research. Learn more at ae.studio. GoogleGoogle's mission is to organize the world's information & make it universally accessible & useful. As a leader in AI & computing, the company is focused on developing technology responsibly to benefit people & society. Kapor FoundationThe Kapor Foundation works at the intersection of racial equity & technology to expand access to K-12 computer science & postsecondary tech pathways, improve tech accountability & worker protections, & increase investments in infrastructure & innovation. events.name: Spatial Analytics w/ Python
events.description: Join PyData NYC on October 27th at 6:30 PM for an evening exploring geospatial data science with Python, featuring Brendan Collins, Founder & CTO at Makepath & creator of Xarray-Spatial! Discover how Python can transform spatial data into powerful insights, from terrain analysis & hydrology to scalable CPU- & GPU-accelerated computing. Please bring your  to follow along & sign up using your official government-issued name.  Pizza & drinks will be provided - Thank you, Makepath! Agenda xarray-spatial: In & Out of the Raster-verseSpeaker: Brendan Collins (Founder & CTO at Makepath)Spatial data comes in many shapes & sizes, but some of the most powerful spatial analysis techniques begin by viewing the world as a grid.Led by the library's creator & maintainer, this talk introduces Xarray-Spatial, an open-source Python library for scalable raster analysis with CPU & GPU acceleration.We'll learn how to enter the Raster-verse by bringing spatial data into Xarray, explore the Raster-verse using algorithms for terrain analysis, hydrology, proximity, & more, & escape the Raster-verse through techniques like zonal statistics & polygonization.Finally, we'll discuss contributing to the Raster-verse, sharing lessons from maintaining Xarray-Spatial & how AI-augmented development is transforming open-source contributions, code quality, & scientific software engineering.Whether you're a GIS practitioner, data scientist, or Python developer, you'll leave with practical ideas for working with spatial data & contributing to open source.  About the SpeakerBrendan Collins is the Founder & CTO of Makepath, where he helps early-stage startups & Fortune 500 engineering teams realize their product ambitions.A former employee of Anaconda, Brendan has spent the past decade applying PyData technologies, including NumPy, Xarray, & Numba, to engineering challenges across the public, private, & nonprofit sectors.When not writing in the third person, Brendan enjoys swimming, playing the banjo, & gardening.  NetworkingConnect with fellow data enthusiasts, Python developers, researchers, & community leaders. Build meaningful connections, exchange ideas, & explore opportunities for collaboration.

events.name: Your Investor Pitch - What To Say & How To Say It
events.description: A free, two-hour workshop for founders who want to build a stronger investor pitch & deliver it with confidence.You know your business. You know the opportunity. But can you communicate it in a way that makes investors understand the potential, believe in you, & want to continue the conversation? On October 30, join a group of founders for a focused working session to assess the pitch you have today, identify what's missing, & turn it into a sharper, more compelling investor presentation. Anthony Rose, CEO of SeedLegals.com, tells you exactly what investors need to hear. David Goldberg, CEO of Prosody.center, shows you exactly how they need to hear it. Two hours, both experts, free. What you'll work on1. Build the right investor storyStructure your pitch around what investors need to understand: opportunity, differentiation, competition, financials, traction, scalability, & why now. Cut unnecessary information, close narrative gaps, & make the value easier to grasp. 2. Deliver it with confidence & credibilityA strong deck isn't enough. Learn to make a strong first impression, create buy-in, use pace & pauses to make key numbers land, stress the words that carry value, & steady your voice under pressure. Use your voice to communicate with the composure & authority investors expect. 3. Test & refine your pitchPitch in front of others & discover where the room leans in, where you lose them, & what needs to change. Use live feedback to tighten your messaging & delivery. 4. The live-feedback experienceEach hour includes 15 minutes of tips, first from Anthony Rose on creating compelling content, then from David Goldberg on delivering it with conviction, followed by 45 minutes of live, instructive feedback so founders can improve their pitches on the spot. What you'll leave withA sharper, more focused investor pitch A clearer understanding of your strengths & gaps Practical techniques for presenting with confidence Real-world feedback on your messaging & delivery Specific next steps for continuing to improve Greater insight into what can move an investor from listening to wanting to know more Who should attendFounders & startup leaders at different stages of the fundraising journey. Whether you're preparing to pitch for the first time or you've pitched before & know it could be stronger, the goal is the same: leave with a better pitch than the one you walked in with. Your facilitatorsAnthony Rose, CEO, SeedLegalsFounder & CEO of SeedLegals, the legaltech platform that helps startups get investment-ready, run a funding round, & handle their legals, used by over 60,000 startups. Before SeedLegals, his career spanned 3D graphics, peer-to-peer music, internet video, & social TV, including heading up BBC iPlayer. Wired Magazine's 2009 cover story called him "The Man Who Saved the BBC." David Goldberg, CEO, Prosody.center & Edge StudioFounder of Prosody.center & EdgeStudio.com, an international voiceover recording center. He has directed, coached, & trained over 10,000 celebrities, politicians, CEOs, & founders on more than 13,000 spoken-word projects over 38 years. He identifies the blind spots that hold founders back when they pitch (pacing, phrasing, wording, emphasis, tone, body language, composure, nonverbal cues), then shows the precise adjustments that change how investors experience & respond to you. DetailsWhen: Friday, October 30, 1-3pm ET, in person, Times Square, NYCCost: Free to join. Co-founders are welcome too.Capacity: Seating is limited, & registrations are approved individually. Come prepared to work on your business, test your ideas, & practice your pitch, not simply take notes.

events.description: Join UJA Healthcare for our kickoff event:a timely talk featuring Mikael Dolsten, M.D., Ph.D., former chief scientific officer at Pfizer, on how artificial intelligence is advancing medicine & reshaping the life sciences industry. After a reception with light bites & mingling,you'll hear from Dr. Dolsten in conversation with Avi Kometz, M.D., a partner at Deerfield Management, about how AI is accelerating drug discovery, advancing cancer treatment & gene therapies, impacting clinical trials, & opening new possibilities for public health. You'll also hear about UJA's powerful work improving the lives of people in need here in New York, in Israel, & around the world. Dr. Mikael DolstenMikael Dolsten, M.D., Ph.D., is a physician-scientist & investment advisor who serves on several public & private boards as a director or chairman & as strategic advisor to leading business groups in biomedicine & AI TechBio. Dr. Dolsten is the former chief scientific officer & president of Research & Development at Pfizer During his 16-year tenure at Pfizer, he led the approval of more than 36 medicines & vaccines. Dr. Dolsten holds an M.D. & a Ph.D. in tumor immunology from Lund University, where he is a visiting adjunct professor, & has published more than 160 scientific papers. Avi Kometz, M.D., is a partner on Deerfield Management's Medical Technologies team. He was a partner at Ascent Biomedical Ventures, leading investments in biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, & health IT. He also led corporate development at a pediatric pharmaceutical company & advised healthcare clients at McKinsey. He began as a clinician in South Africa & went on to found & build a group of clinics.

events.name: PMAI - Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Learn How to SellSales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. - Bring a computer. You're writing three things tonight.- Most founders can get meetings. The deals die after meeting one.- You'll leave with your buyer in one sentence, a cold email written to a real person, & five questions for your next call. About Farzad, the speaker Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding & generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.description: Join us at Fabrik NYC in DUMBO, Brooklyn for an in-person, hands-on pitch clinic designed to help founders become more confident on stage & sharpen the way they pitch to investors. Whether you are preparing for a fundraising round, an investor meeting, or your next demo day, you will learn practical tools to communicate your story with greater confidence, clarity, & impact. The clinic features two focused, 30-minute workshops covering how you show up & what you say. Don't Calm Down with Dave Wolovsky In this interactive workshop, Dave will share practical exercises to help you compose yourself when pitching, work with pressure rather than against it, & perform with greater presence in high-stakes moments. Dave is a Cognitive Performance Coach with an MS in Neuroscience & Education from Columbia University. He coaches founders on focus & daily energy management & serves as a StartX accelerator mentor. events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Plan Your Best Year With AI
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back  In Person at SalesforceWe're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City and sponsored by Boldforce.This Month We Present...Plan Your Best Year With AIJoin the community for an interactive planning session to reflect on the past year, identify your biggest opportunities, and build an AI-powered roadmap for the year ahead.Before we rush into a new year with another list of goals, lets get clear about what were actually building.What worked this year? What didnt? What deserves more of your energy? And where could AI help you turn those intentions into action?For our final AI & The Culture meetup of the year, were bringing the community together for an interactive planning and reflection session designed to help you look back, think forward, and build a roadmap for what comes next.This isnt about asking AI to magically plan your life. Its about using these tools as thought partnersto help you reflect, uncover patterns, explore possibilities, make decisions, and turn big ambitions into actionable next steps.Together well explore: How to use AI to reflect on your wins, lessons, challenges, and unfinished business from the past year Prompts that help you identify opportunities you might be overlooking How to turn big goals into realistic projects, milestones, and next steps Ways to use AI as a strategic thought partner for your creative work, career, business, or personal projects How to identify where AI and automation can give you back time in the year ahead Building a personalized AI-powered roadmap you can actually use after you leave the roomAnd because this is AI & The Culture, were making space for something AI cant replace: community.Youll have an opportunity to reflect alongside other creatives, founders, educators, artists, technologists, and curious mindsto exchange ideas, share what youre building, and potentially meet the people who can help you move it forward.The goal isnt to leave with 47 resolutions.Its to leave with clarity, priorities, and a plan.Who Should Attend? Creators and content makers Filmmakers, writers, artists, and storytellers Educators and community builders Entrepreneurs, founders, and solopreneurs Marketers, strategists, and creative professionals Technologists and AI enthusiasts Anyone ready to be more intentional about what theyre building nextWhether you already have your next year mapped out or youre still staring at a blank page wondering where to begin, youre welcome here.Come Ready to BuildThis one is especially hands-on, so come prepared to participate. Bring your laptop Bring a notebook or something to write with Bring a few goals, ideas, or questions youve been thinking about for the year ahead Bring your curiosity and a willingness to shareWell be working through reflection exercises, AI prompts, and planning activities togetherso you can leave with the beginnings of a roadmap, not just another page of notes.Come ready to reflect. Come ready to plan. Come ready to build.About AI & The CultureAI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, and culture.Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams and King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, and culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, and community.Were building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI.This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture  grounded in community, focused on real-world use, and centered on learning together in the room.Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Lets build  together. About Your HostsShirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, and co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, and creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, and real-world execution.About King WilloniusKing Willonius is a creative technologist and cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, and creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, and community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable and useful  especially for creatives and innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm. Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio)#AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: Ugly Talk: CPG Founders What Worked, What Didn't & The 2027 Outlook
events.description: A bigger order can leave you with a smaller margin. That is an ugly way to learn what growth costs. CPG founders will unpack the calls shaping their brands in 2026. The channels that moved product. The partners that mattered. The pivots they had to make. Bring the decisions you are still wrestling with. Hear what these founders are changing as they finish Q4 & plan for 2027.  Why you should be in this room.Hear which channels moved product & which ate margin. Learn what founders wish they had asked before choosing a co-packer or distributor. Explore where food service & alternative distribution could fit your brand. Hear how founders responded when their customers, markets, or plans changed. Pressure-test your 2027 assumptions against what these founders are seeing in 2026.  What's on the table.Production & partners. Refining the recipe, choosing co-manufacturers, & finding partners who deliver what they promise. Distribution & margin. Which channels earned their place, which disappointed, & what founders changed in response. Finding the customer. What urban & suburban markets taught founders about who actually buys their products. Food service & other routes. Where founders are looking beyond familiar shelves to move product. The 2027 calls. Which trends held up, which missed, & what founders are carrying into next year.  Featured speakers.Liv Truesdell - Founder, FROST Buttercream Liv Truesdell started her career in consumer investment banking, working with food & beverage companies, which ultimately led her to launch FROST Buttercream. FROST is an all-natural Italian Meringue Buttercream made with real butter & egg whites, with ~57% less sugar than a leading buttercream & no palm oils, artificial dyes or preservatives. After hundreds of iterations, Liv created a new premium, refrigerated frosting segment in a category unchanged for ~71 years. FROST launched in NY/NJ retail in 2025, has since expanded across the country, & won the Startup CPG Shelfie Award within its first six months. Glenn Johnson - Marketing Consultant/Fractional CMO As a fractional CMO, Glenn Johnson works on a scalable basis with founders who are tired of bad execution, broken strategies, & agencies that just don't get it. Whether launching from scratch or fixing a brand, packaging, & positioning that fails to translate, Glenn steps in to repair what's broken & build what's next. Operating as Chief Storyteller, Creative Director, & Brand Strategist, he bridges high-level strategy with hands-on execution. From naming, logo design, & packaging to pricing architecture & true ICP targeting, Glenn nails how your brand looks, feels, & scales. A former Madison Avenue VP/Creative Director specializing in luxury & bespoke audiences, Glenn is the trusted sounding board founders rely on to turn complex ideas into scalable brand equity. Moderating Ugly Talks for me is about unpacking the messy truths & hard lessons of entrepreneurship-sharing insights in an engaged & entertaining way.  Who's getting in.Food & beverage founders building in crowded categories. Early-stage CPG founders moving from commercial kitchens to co-manufacturing. Operators working through production, distribution, pricing, & margin decisions. Buyers & investors who want to understand what helps a brand move product & stay in business.  About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough "aha!" moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons & insights. With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami, we've built a vibrant community of thousands of founders & industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape. Official Website: UglyTalk.com  Important Notice for Ugly Talk AttendeesAdmission & Confirmation Attendance is by approval only. Approved guests will receive a confirmation email along with a calendar invite. Invitations are non-transferable. Additional event details will be shared as the event approaches. Code of Conduct By attending, you agree to: Maintain respect & professionalism, adhering to all venue rules, policies, & applicable laws. Refrain from harassment, discrimination, unwelcome sexual advances (verbal or physical), intimidation, or inappropriate photography/recording. Report any violations to the event hosts immediately. Violations may result in immediate removal from the event & exclusion from future invitations. Liability & Risk Participation is voluntary & at your own risk. events.name: Monday Founders Coworking Pod
events.description: If you're an early stage founder, building alone is hard. You lose momentum, get stuck with no one to ask, & there's no one checking if you actually did what you said you'd do this week. We're a small group of founders working together for the month - think study group, but for building. We help each other, check in, & keep each other on track. Now we're opening it up to more people, in pods of 3-5. Here's how it works: you tell your pod what you're trying to get done, & they hold you to it. Stuck on something? Someone in the pod probably knows the answer. Starting to slip? Someone notices. Same faces every week, so you're never starting over with strangers. This is an outgrowth of our Wednesday coworking events - just smaller. We're here to build the idea & building culture NYC deserves. We focus on that foundational layer of relationships & community that allows for ideas to spread & building to happen. events.name: PMAI: Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Sales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. - Bring a computer. You're writing three things tonight.- Most founders can get meetings. The deals die after meeting one.- You'll leave with your buyer in one sentence, a cold email written to a real person, & five questions for your next call. About Farzad, the speaker Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding & generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: An Unmuted Debate: Primary Party Crashers
events.description: Should primaries be open to every voter? More Americans now identify as independent than as Democrat or Republican. Yet in New York & many other states, those voters are shut out of the primaries that often decide who actually wins. So are closed primaries locking out the voters our politics needs most? And would opening them make anything better? Open primaries let any registered voter participate, regardless of party. Supporters say they force candidates to campaign to the whole electorate, reward problem-solvers over partisans, & give millions of independents a real voice. Critics say parties have the right to choose their own nominees, that open systems invite strategic crossover voting & voter confusion, & that the evidence they reduce polarization is thin. So who's right? Are open primaries the fix for a system that rewards the extremes? Or are they a reform that promises more than it delivers? John Opdycke is the founder & president of Open Primaries, a national organization working to enact & protect open & nonpartisan primaries. He has spent three decades in independent & reform politics, helped found the New York State Independence Party, & writes the monthly column Brash Tacks for The Fulcrum. Lindsey Cormack is an associate professor of political science & director of the Diplomacy Lab at Stevens Institute of Technology. She is the author of How to Raise a Citizen (And Why It's Up to You to Do It) & Congress & U.S. Veterans, created the DCInbox database of congressional newsletters, & serves as Secretary of Manhattan Community Board 8. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

events.name: Vibecoding 101
events.description: A 4-week scaffolded, hands-on introduction to vibecoding for beginners.Vibecoding, or AI-assisted software development, is the practice of guiding coding agents to translate your ideas into working software - without writing code yourself. We see vibecoding as 4 different product skills in a trench coat. While they may not write code, effective vibecoders mobilize concepts & workflows across software engineering, design, quality assurance, & product management. This course is a scaffolded, hands-on introduction to the fundamental skills & concepts required for a sustainable vibecoding practice. Students will learn through a combination of short lectures, applied exercises, personalized feedback, & demos to peers. We begin by working with coding agents in a multiplayer environment designed for beginners. We will create interactive frontends, learn the basics of the terminal, build integrations with APIs, & create stateful, full-stack applications with a database & user authentication. By the end of the course, students will transition to state-of-the-art coding agents installed on their personal machines, which they will use to build & deploy a working prototype to the web. SyllabusSession 1: Coding agents & frontends We introduce the course & core concepts of vibecoding. We introduce a basic taxonomy of web architecture. Students practice creating basic interactive frontends. Session 2: CLIs, APIs, & the terminal We cover core backend & data concepts. We gently introduce the terminal. Students practice writing simple CLI programs, & integrating with an API. Session 3: Stateful full-stack applications We cover databases & user authentication; students build a full stack app. Session 4: Deployment & demos The final session covers deployment. Students demo their prototypes for the class. Learning OutcomesAcquire core vocabulary & mental models for software development. Prompt coding agents to create frontends, API integrations, & stateful applications. Be able to translate your ideas into working prototypes using AI. Practice presenting your product ideas to peers & colleagues. ResourcesThis new world of ours rewards being a dilettante with a vague mental map of vast territories.- Ted Underwood There is a new kind of coding I call vibecoding,' where you fully give in to the vibes, embrace exponentials, & forget that the code even exists. It's possible because the LLMs (e.g. Cursor Composer w Sonnet) are getting too good it's not really coding - I just see stuff, say stuff, run stuff, & copy paste stuff, & it mostly works.- Andrej Karpathy Slow is smooth, & smooth is fast.- Anonymous ScholarshipIndex scholarships are designed to benefit members of our community who do not have expendable cash to pay for the course, & those for whom the class price is not accessible. These need-based scholarships will go to the candidates who best demonstrate why they should be chosen for the free spot to our class based on the following criteria: Belong to groups that are traditionally underrepresented in the graphic design & creative industries Do not have jobs that would pay for these courses as professional development Cannot independently afford the class at list price Share our value of intentional community The number of selected applicants chosen is subject to the discretion of Index & the instructor, but every course will select at least one. Apply for a scholarship here. Applications close October 20th. Instructor Bio Bill Roberts is an independent technologist based in Brooklyn. Drawn to socially beneficial uses of technology, he has 10 years of software engineering experience on teams spanning healthcare, climate, politics, & education. He runs Legible Labs, a product studio that helps clients design & build AI applications. As a research engineer, he has coauthored papers in peer-reviewed journals & conferences that empirically evaluate the capabilities of AI in educational settings. Bill holds a BA in Computer Science & Sociology from Columbia University.   Refunds We get that things come up, but we rely on headcounts to make our programs viable. If you request a refund... More than 4 weeks before the program begins  100% refundMore than 2 weeks before the program begins  50% refundFewer than 2 weeks before the program begins  No refund Thanks for understanding & for supporting our ability to provide cool offerings through your purchase. Media Release Clause By attending this event, you consent to being photographed, filmed, or recorded, & grant Index Space permission to use this content for promotional or informational purposes.

events.name: Data By Design
events.description: In conversation with Shannon Mattern. P&T Knitwear is pleased to welcome Lauren Klein, Tanvi Sharma, & Silas Munro to celebrate & discuss the release of their book Data by Design, which explores how the history of data visualization holds the key to designing a more just future. They will be in conversation with Shannon Mattern, & will sign books after the talk! Doors open at 6:30pm with the talk starting closer to 7:00pm. Come early & grab a drink from the P&T Cafe! Tickets & books are available both on eventbrite & at the door. Housekeeping notes: This is a ticketed in-store event with limited amphitheater-style seating.Doors open at 6:30pm, with the talk starting around 7:00pm.Cost of a book bundle ticket reflects the total cost of the feature event book (MSRP plus tax). Each book bundle ticket guarantees ticket holders one (1) copy of the feature event book.The talk will be followed by a book signing. Books signed at P&T Knitwear events must be purchased from P&T Knitwear.If you would like a signed copy & cannot attend the event, we're happy to take your pre-order. We ship most places!About the authors:Lauren Klein is Professor of Data & Decision Sciences & English at Emory University, where she also directs the Digital Humanities Lab & the Atlanta Interdisciplinary AI Network. Her research brings together computational & critical methods to explore questions of gender, race, & justice, both in early America & today. Klein is the author (with Catherine D'Ignazio) of the award-winning Data Feminism (MIT Press, 2020), & the editor (with Matthew K. Gold) of Debates in the Digital Humanities (Univ. of Minnesota Press), among other books & papers. Her next book, Data by Design: Visualization & Power from Abolition to the Dawn of Data Science (MIT Press), will be out in October 2026.  Silas Munro is a designer, artist, writer, curator, surfer, & descendant of the Banyole people of Eastern Uganda. He founded the design studio Polymode, whose clients include MoMA, the MET, Nike, & the Hammer. Munro is the curator & author of Strikethrough: Typographic Messages of Protest at Letterform Archive & the co-curator of Reverberations: Lineages in Design History at the Ford Foundation Gallery. He contributed to W. E. B. Du Bois's Data Portraits: Visualizing Black America, & co-authored the first BIPOC-centered design history course, Black Design in America: African Americans & the African Diaspora in Graphic Design 19th-21st Century. His visual art was recently exhibited at Data Consciousness: Reframing Blackness in Contemporary Print at Print Center New York. Tanvi Sharma is a design technologist working at the intersection of data, aesthetics, & the humanities. She is currently an Art Director at Apple & co-author of Data by Design (MIT Press, 2026). She has previously worked at Pentagram, Public Policy Lab, & Spotify. She lives in Harlem, NY, with her two cats, Yuchi & Bubbles. More at tanvi.network.   About the moderator:Shannon Mattern is the Director of Creative Research at the Metropolitan New York Library Council, a state-founded, member-supported non-profit linking hundreds of libraries & archives across the city. Previously, she held tenured full professorships in media studies, anthropology, & art history at The New School & the University of Pennsylvania. She is the author of four books, the (co-)editor of six collections, & the author of over 100 articles & chapters about urban technology, knowledge infrastructures, maps, maintenance, data art, & other heterogenous subjects. She was the 2025 Kluge Chair in Modern Culture at the Library of Congress & the 2025 Design Indexer in residence at the Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum. You can find her at wordsinspace.net.

events.name: Daytona AI Builders
events.description: An event dedicated to exploring all things AI Engineering! Event partners: AWS & Antimetal Agenda 5:30 pm - 6:00 pmWelcome Gathering & Opening Remarks Marijan Cipcic, Principal Events Manager at Daytona  6:00 pm - 6:15 pmTalk "Forkable Sandboxes for Long-Running Agents" Muhammad Annas Hashmi, DevRel at Daytona Outline:Agents are starting to do real software work: installing dependencies, editing files, running tests, starting servers, & debugging over long sessions. But most AI systems still treat each run like a disposable prompt-response loop. That breaks down once the useful state lives not just in tokens, but in the actual machine. This talk is about the runtime layer agents need to become reliable builders. I'll show how forkable Daytona sandboxes let you pause at important moments in an agent run, branch the environment, & sample multiple continuations from the same machine state. For builders, this turns long-running agent workflows into something you can inspect, compare, recover, & eventually optimize.  6:15 pm - 6:30 pmTalk "Multi-Agent Investment AI Assistant built on Amazon Bedrock Agentcore" Sam Farber, Sr. Solutions Architect at AWS Outline:Investment research teams spend days manually gathering data across markets, risk metrics, sentiment indicators, financial statements, & alternative data sources before synthesizing findings into actionable reports. This talk will show how a multi-agent AI system can automate that workflow. A supervisor agent breaks down a research question, delegates to 10 domain-specific specialists running in parallel, & compiles their findings into a comprehensive investment report. The system maintains conversation memory across each agent, allowing researchers to have targeted conversations & follow-ups with each specialized agent.  6:30 pm - 6:45 pmTalk "Building a World Model for Production Agents" Shreyas Iyer, Co-founder & CTO of Antimetal Outline:Production systems are increasingly complex, with critical knowledge scattered across code, infrastructure, telemetry, & people's heads. In this talk, we'll explore how to build a persistent world model that gives AI agents a shared understanding of production. We'll break down four foundational layers: physical topology, temporal changes, causal relationships, & organizational context to show how they enable agents to investigate incidents, assess changes, & proactively manage production, building on what they've learned across tasks.  6:45 pm - 6:55 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker TBA Outline:TBA  6:55 pm - 7:05 pmTalk "Letting AI agents use credentials they never see" Chase Erickson, Solutions Engineer at Infisical Outline:Infisical manages the secrets your Daytona agents depend on. The Daytona secret sync pushes them from Infisical to your Daytona organization & keeps them current, rotations included. Infisical's Agent Vault, a proxy, adds the credential to requests bound for the services you configure, so the agent never sees it. In this talk, we'll show how an agent in a Daytona sandbox calls an API without ever holding the secret.  7:05 pm - 8:30 pmNetworkingWith pizzas & beverages About event This is dynamic gathering for AI enthusiasts, innovators, & professionals to collaborate, share ideas, & explore the latest advancements in artificial intelligence. Whether you're building AI products, researching cutting-edge algorithms, or simply passionate about the field, join us to connect, learn, & drive the future of AI forward.

events.name: Future Of Storytelling Salon
events.description: A curated dinner where we discuss the future of marketing & storytelling.Join Fibe & Generated for a conversation-led dinner for DTC brand & creative leaders, with a focus on fashion, apparel & athleisure. We'll talk about generative storytelling & how brand content might play out as a mini-series. The goal is for guests to leave knowing who they can speak with about generative storytelling. There are twelve seats available for marketing leaders who are interested in having a conversation about about what's actually working, what's overhyped, & where the puck is heading next.  Who's in the room?Twelve CMOs, VPs, & Directors of Marketing from mid-market enterprise tech companies & legendary consumer brands. events.description: Every AI model you've ever used is stuck in the past. Ground Truth is a one-day hackathon where you fix that. Join localhost:nyc, The Builder Series & You.com for 10 hours of building AI agents grounded in the live web. Real-time data, deep research, verifiable answers. Come build the kind of agent people would trust with a real decision. Problem StatementEvery LLM is frozen at its training cutoff. It doesn't know what happened this morning, & when it doesn't know, it guesses, confidently. That's the gap between a cool demo & a product people rely on. Your challenge: build an AI agent that knows what's true right now. It searches the live web through the You.com API, reads the sources, reasons over them & shows its receipts. The Challenge TracksLive Wire (real-time agents): agents that wake up when the world changes. Price moves, breaking news, a competitor launch, a policy change, a new job posting. If it happened in the last hour, your agent already knows & already acted. The Analyst (deep research): pick a profession (VCs, lawyers, journalists, recruiters, doctors, policy staffers) & replace its 40-hour research memo with a 4-minute one, every claim cited. Receipts (trust & verification): agents that fact-check claims, catch AI hallucinations, verify sources & show their work. Best Content (open to every team): post about what you built, tag You.com, & win a dedicated prize. What to ExpectA kickoff walkthrough of the You.com API: Search, Contents, Research & the hosted MCP server Free You.com API credits for every builder 6 hours of building Teams of up to 4, or solo if that's your thing Team matching at kickoff if you're coming alone Mentors from You.com on the floor all day Live demos to judges at the end, plus food all day Prizes1st Place Overall: $500 cash Best Content: TBD JudgesTBD Who Should AttendEngineers (full stack, backend, AI/ML) Founders & aspiring founders building with AI Designers & product people who want to ship something real Researchers & analysts who know exactly what a great research agent should do You don't need a finished idea. events.name: Powering The Transition - Closing Skills Gap In New Energy Infrastructure
events.description: In partnership with Schneider Electric, Google, Barclays, LACI & IYF The energy transition is underway - but the workforce needed to deliver it is not keeping pace. Across the full arc of how energy is generated, moved, stored, serviced, & used - spanning utilities, power generation, advanced manufacturing, fleet electrification, data centers, & industrial infrastructure - a persistent & structural challenge has emerged: the skilled trades & technician roles most critical to new energy infrastructure face serious & growing skills gaps, & too often the employers, training providers, & talent leaders working to close them are doing so in isolation. NationSwell, in partnership with Barclays, LACI, IYF, Schneider Electric, & Google is convening a working session at Brooklyn Army Terminal - home to BATWorks, NYC's emerging climate innovation hub - to change that. Bringing together talent leaders, hiring managers, & workforce training providers, this in-person convening will use IYF's proven industry competency framework to surface & validate the most critical skills gaps across the skilled trades workforce driving new energy infrastructure.  The day will move from insight to action. The goal is a shared vocabulary & shared priorities that attendees can take back to their organizations, & use to advocate for the training investments, certifications, & systems changes the new energy infrastructure demands. BATWorks offers a uniquely fitting backdrop: a place where growth-stage climate companies, workforce development, & hands-on innovation converge. Where employers are growing & talent supply can grow with them. Attendees will leave knowing they are not alone in this challenge - & with concrete, validated priorities to guide the next steps.

events.description: Join us on Thursday, November 5th at Solana Skyline for an invite-only evening bringing together leading founders, VCs, & operators from across New York's Solana ecosystem ahead of Breakpoint London. The evening will include a happy hour with light bites & drinks, along with a showcase of what our Cohort 5 teams have built during the Solana Incubator. Come connect with the people building, backing, & shaping the future of Solana. Meet Cohort 5 Six teams have been building alongside Solana Labs, spanning AI, robotics, trading infrastructure, & new onchain markets. ClawPump - A launchpad for tokenizing & monetizing AI products & autonomous agents. Already powered 8,000+ agents & generated over $270M in trading volume. CrowdBrain - Building distributed infrastructure for robot learning & operations. Grand champion of the Colosseum Frontier Hackathon. Lavarage - A decentralized spot-margin & lending protocol driving capital efficiency across Solana, with $200M+ in volume & 10,000+ traders. Morfi Markets - An opinion market where users can trade subjective debates that traditional prediction markets can't price. OwnIt - Bringing onchain verification to trading relationships traditionally built on trust, with every trade settling transparently on Solana. ProjectSolo - Connecting AI agents with humans for real-world judgment & feedback, powered by a privacy-preserving proof-of-humanity protocol. Backed by Draper Associates. About Solana Incubator Solana Incubator is a three-month intensive program in New York City where a select group of founders build & grow their companies directly alongside Solana Labs. Through hands-on support across development, go-to-market, fundraising, & strategic partnerships, the program helps promising teams build the next generation of companies in the Solana ecosystem. Follow Solana Incubator on X for the latest updates.
