events.name: The Deployment Room: 6 Active Funds, Funding Founders (Seed to Series A+)
events.description: The Builder Series: A 60,000+ member community redefining what networking looks like curating founders, investors into intentional rooms built for experiences people remember & relationships that last. It's a direct line to the most ambitious builders. Find us here: Instagram  LinkedIn  TikTok  Facebook  X : WhatsApp Broad Channel (Not a GC) August was our pilot. Here's how it performed. Our intent 20 founders, 6 investors. The real turnout: 30 guests: 20 founders, 10 capital allocators $70M+ raised collectively by the founders present $3.5M average raised per founder $2.3B+ combined AUM across the investors $1M average check, $100K minimum $10M+ in live check capacity This is today objective: Every founder in the room is doing $1M+ in ARR or has raised a round of $1M or more. Raised your 1st round, onto your 2nd, or bootstrapped to $1M ARR? You're in the right place. Every investor here is from our network. We're curating this room deliberately, matching founders to the investors most likely to be a fit, & making the introduction ourselves. The goal here: Getting founders funded by our investor network. The 6 Investors joining us from our network: (More will be joining) Francesca Poupel: F&G Capital Partners (Managing Partner): Backing founders from pre-seed to Series A in AI, fintech, & blockchain, writing $300K-$500K checks & partnering closely with teams as they scale. Mahir Laul (Partner) representing Laul Global a family office & holding company operating four interconnected pillars: Education Engine, Real Assets, Future Ventures, & Acquisitions. One integrated system. One long-term vision. Laul Global is owned & operated by the Laul family. We started with a single student recruitment company. We built it into one of Canada's most diversified education holding groups. Today the portfolio spans institutions, edtech, real estate, & a tech venture studio, with reach across 20+ countries & no plans to slow down.  Triet Leminh: Principal, LMT Partners: Lawyer, founder, & investor backing pre-seed to Series A founders building in enterprise & regulated industries. Writing $200K-$300K checks.  Andrew Antar (General Partner, AG Venture Capital): A generalist fund backing extraordinary founders, sector agnostic. Also a Venture Partner at Arcadian Capital, focused on late-stage secondaries & pre-IPO tech, & served as Crypto Policy Advisor to the NYC Office of the Mayor - advising on the city's crypto regulatory framework & organizing the NYC Crypto Summit at Gracie Mansion. He is also founder of Tune.FM, a tokenized music streaming platform & digital asset marketplace, & co-founded Clear Quantum, a stealth quantum AI startup. Gonzalo Quincot (Founder, Sinober): Sinober is a financial intelligence platform that combines public & private market intelligence with institutional-grade methodology, corporate finance & proprietary AI tools to sharpen investment & capital decisions for individuals & businesses. Invests in automation, robotics, data centers & applied AI.  Shilpi Nayak: (Founder & General Partner, 434 VC): Invests in early-stage technical founders across AI, infrastructure, physical AI & emerging technology. She is also the founder of House of 434, a community bringing together founders, investors & industry leaders.  Pranav Jajapur (Co-Founder, ZERON Ventures): ZERON is an early-stage venture fund with an execution platform behind it, backing real-world technology, AI, healthcare, deep tech & climate companies building in the physical world, inside biology. Pre-seed through Series A with core deployment at seed, writing $400K-$500k checks. Preferred focus is institutionally-anchored AI: structural research relationships at academic institutions, spinouts, & founder-led research programs. Fund I in formation. Deploying Q1  All 6 senior investors confirmed. Part of building rooms is making sure real capital is present. Six investors actively deploying writing capital will be joining. Our first confirmed: Why we do this: Putting active investors in the same room as exceptional founders, & keeps the room small enough to ensure everyone actually meets. We value intentional networking & community. If you're here to meet the best of the best, this is the room. Our Sponsor: Composition WealthYour seat at the table is waiting. Your life is shaped by new beginnings, major decisions, & milestones. That's why when it comes to developing the strategies to achieve your financial goals, we make sure you have a seat at the table & are empowered with the knowledge & tools to shape your own future. At Composition Wealth, our goal is to empower you to reach YOUR goals. Chris Guarino, CFPBook some time: Calendly link What to expect for this: A Greek style lunch, courtesy of our team Conversations with fellow high-performing startup leaders An experience designed to facilitate new meaningful connections conversations with ambitious peers solving similar problems Event to be hosted at a beautiful private Soho loft Our intent is to bring good, smart humans together, & active investors together to fun incredible founders. Community has been lost & we are rebuilding it. Our Greek Inspired Menu: About the meal A three-course Greek menu. Appetizers & dessert are shared & open to everyone; each will get one entre. The format is intentionally part standing, part seated so you can enjoy incredible food without being anchored to a single table or a single conversation. Why we do this Our intent is simple: bring good, smart humans together, put active investors in the same room as incredible founders. Intentional community has been lost. We're rebuilding it.

events.name: Startup Pitch Mixer
events.description: Join our event in New York! We design Pitch & Networking nights to help founders sharpen their thinking through direct, candid feedback & to give strong investors access to serious teams. Our pitch night is complemented by a structured networking session before & after the pitch session.  What to expect: Startups pitch live & receive focused feedback from angels & VC partners Structured networking session before & after the pitches Entrepreneurs, startup founders, & operators are joining to network, exchange ideas, & build strong connections Active investors & venture scouts joining to discover the best startups early  Who you will meet at the event: Founders Investors, VC partners, Venture Scouts Marketers, Salespeople, Business Advisors Industry Disruptors AI Experts Entrepreneurs from Europe, Asia, & the United Kingdom  We Welcome New Investors: We invite investors to our event to expand their network, get acquainted with new startups, evaluate them, share feedback, & participate in discussions with early-stage & serial founders. We offer complimentary tickets to institutional investors, angels, & venture scouts with a proven track record. If you'd like to access our database of promising startups or provide mentorship support to our best startups, please fill out this short Investor Application Form, & our team will contact you.  Want to Pitch? A limited number of founders will have the opportunity to pitch their startup or business to a panel of investors & experts. 4-6 selected founders will pitch their startup, followed by a short Q&A where participants can ask questions & share feedback. Apply by filling out the Pitch Application Form & sending us your pitch deck. Spots are limited, & we select founders in advance. To maintain high-quality pitches, you are required to present with a pitch deck. We will share our pitching guide and, if you'd like, coach you so you're fully prepared for pitch night.  The best startups will be featured across our social media & included in our investor newsletter. Requirements for attendees: Dress code: smart casual. Bring good energy.  Join our event & secure your ticket today! About us: Startup Valley is a global event organizer hosting pitch nights in 25 cities since 2023. Since then, we have hosted 850 events for 40,000 attendees. Over these years, we connected countless outstanding early-stage startups to serious investors, & we are not planning to stop. We maintain strategic partnerships with VC funds in the US, Europe, & Asia to support our community. Do you have a question, a partnership proposal, or want to clarify something? Reach us at hello@startupvalley.club Agenda 18:00-18:30 - Registration: Guests register, receive badges, & event programs. This is an opportunity for casual networking, making first connections, & preparing for the event. 18:30-19:00 - Event Kickoff & Interactive Networking: Official welcome from the organizers with a brief overview of the event goals & schedule. Interactive networking session to connect with key contacts. 19:00-19:50 - Startup Pitch Session: Startups present their projects to investors & experts. Each team has 5 minutes to pitch, covering the project's core idea, business model, & target market. 19:50-21:00 - Chill & Networking: Participants enjoy casual conversations with investors, discuss collaboration opportunities, & exchange ideas over refreshments. FAQ Can I pitch? Yes! To pitch, please purchase a Pitch Ticket & fill out the Pitch Application Form. We will contact you to discuss & approve your pitch. The pitch duration is 5 minutes. You will also have some time to answer questions from the audience. How does the pitch go? Selected founders present on stage to the audience & the investors in the room. You get 5 minutes to pitch your idea, business model, target market, & investment ask, followed by a short Q&A. The best startups are featured across our social media channels & in the investor newsletter. Who will I meet? Founders, angel investors, VC partners, venture scouts, AI experts, engineers, operators, marketing & sales experts, & international entrepreneurs from across Europe, Asia, & the US. Do investors get free tickets? Yes! Please apply above or email hello@startupvalley.club, & we will issue a complimentary ticket for you & your team. Can I request a refund? Yes. Refunds are available if requested at least 1 day before the event start time. Please submit the refund request on the platform where you purchased your ticket, or email us at hello@startupvalley.club

events.name: AI, Human Expertise & Future Of People's Health
events.description: AI, Human Expertise, & the Future of the People's Health Artificial intelligence is transforming how we learn, make decisions, & address challenges in healthcare & population health. How can we ensure these technologies actually improve people's lives? Drawing on research & collaborations across healthcare, government, industry, & education, this talk examines the relationship between AI, human expertise, & population health. Through examples from clinical practice, public health decision-making, & education, we explore how AI reshapes professional judgment, how we develop the expertise needed to evaluate these technologies, & what individuals & institutions need to ensure AI contributes to better health. SpeakerRumi Chunara, Associate Professor of Computer Science & Engineering, NYU Tandon School of Engineering; Director, Center for Health Data Science, NYU

events.name: Six Math Essentials w/ Terence Tao
events.description: Book Launch & Conversation with Janna Levin Widely regarded as the world's greatest living mathematician, Fields Medalist Terence Tao approaches mathematics as a sublime art-a quiet, rigorous effort to map the hidden scaffolding of reality. To mark the publication of his first popular book, Six Math Essentials, join us for an evening with Tao in conversation with Pioneer Works Director of Sciences Janna Levin. Tracing the central pillars of his book-from algebra as abstraction & geometry beyond sight, to navigating uncertainty & the mathematics of change-they will reveal math not as obscure magic, but as a deeply creative, interconnected way of thinking. Often referred to as the Mozart of mathematics, Tao will also explore how AI is transforming his own practice, the frontier of research, & our collective future. Together, we will consider what becomes of human intuition & creativity when the tools of thought are no longer uniquely human-and whether the true beauty of math lies not in the answers we find, but in the human mind reaching for them. Tao will sign copies of Six Math Essentials following the conversation, with books available for purchase on site. (Unable to attend? Order a signed copy here.) Please note that seating is limited & will be available on a first-come, first-served basis.   About the speakersTerence Tao is an Australian-American professor of mathematics at UCLA whose work focuses primarily on harmonic analysis, partial differential equations, combinatorics, & analytic number theory. The recipient of a Fields Medal, a MacArthur Genius Grant, & a Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics, among many other accolades, he is one of the most decorated & prolific mathematicians working today. Tao is the author of several academic books including Solving Mathematical Problems: A Personal Perspective & Additive Combinatorics, as well as his first popular math book, Six Math Essentials. He lives in Los Angeles. Janna Levin is the Claire Tow Professor of physics & astronomy at Barnard College of Columbia University. A Guggenheim Fellow, she has contributed to our understanding of black holes, extra dimensions, & cosmology. She is the founding director of sciences at Pioneer Works & the founding editor-in-chief of the magazine Pioneer Works Broadcast. She often contributes to news, documentaries, & radio, including as the presenter of the NOVA feature Black Hole Apocalypse on PBS & as a contributor to CBS, CNN, BBC, & NBC. She has authored books on black holes & the universe-Black Hole Blues, How the Universe Got its Spots, & Black Hole Survival Guide-as well as a PEN award-winning novel, A Madman Dreams of Turing Machines. You can find her current writings in Higher Dimensions. This program is funded by the Simons Foundation International & administered by the Simons Foundation's Science, Society & Culture division.

events.name: AI & Future Of Community
events.description: At a moment when loneliness, social isolation, & declining trust are contributing to a growing crisis of community, artificial intelligence is rapidly changing how we communicate & connect with one another. Can AI help strengthen human connection, or could it deepen the forces pulling us apart? Pioneering AI researcher David Blei, Central Synagogue Senior Rabbi Angela Buchdahl, & technologist Jamie Metzl - author of The AI Ten Commandments - talk to constitutional scholar Noah Feldman in a wide-ranging conversation exploring one of the defining questions of our age. Artificial intelligence is transforming our world at breathtaking speed. This is the one where you build something physical. Silicon Alley Hack is a one-day, in-person sprint for builders who'd rather solder than ship a vibe-coded app. Microcontrollers. Sensors. Connected devices. Real hardware that runs in the real world & has to work when we plug it in on stage. Application-based. Teams of 4. Every team gets an STM32 development board & peripherals on arrival. The interesting frontier moved back to atoms - robots that navigate a room, drones that deliver, sensors that make a physical space legible to a machine. All of it runs on constrained silicon, in real time, in places where the cloud is too slow, too far, or not there at all. So that's the terrain: edge intelligence. events.name: Growth Council - Off-The-Record Problem Solving For Scaling Founders
events.description: Are you a founder or entrepreneur? If so, you know that scaling your business past Seed & Series A can expose many gaps in your business all at once - talent/employee friction, messy positioning, legal nuances, capital efficiency...and the list goes on. And while most founder events only focus on panels with generic advice, our new event "The Growth Council" aims to do something different. The mission of this event is to give the founder community access to experts who can help you at your specific stage of growth. The Growth Council is a small-group, peer-to-peer advisory session built specifically for Seed to Series B founders who want to explore their challenges with experts from across the industry & outside their network. Founders will have access to experts in various areas, rotating at specific intervals to ensure they meet with as many experts as possible (think speed dating, but less awkward). These conversations are meant to challenge assumptions & empower founders with new perspectives on their most pressing problems. You'll walk away with fresh perspectives, a bigger network, & connections who can help facilitate you on your journey towards success. The Expert Council Bring us your founder questions, your bottlenecks, or gut-check a current decision & get actionable takeaways from those who have been there before. You'll meet with cross-functional leaders such as: TJ Allison (Sales Advisor & Executive Coach, TJAllison.com) - Sales expert who focuses on revenue & the "Inner Game" to grow revenue & sense of self. Simon Gibson (Fractional VP of Marketing, Formerly GIPHY) - Marketing leader who blends creative storytelling & data-driven strategy to build culturally relevant brands & scale businesses. Rebekah Huber (Cofounder, Kindred Works) - Ops specialist who builds the systems that give founders their time back. Anna Kaplan (Founder & CEO, Narrativ By AK) - Narrative & messaging specialist who helps founders craft a story that wins the room. Marc Kaufman (Partner, Potomac Law Group) - Intellectual property attorney specializing in creating IP assets that increase funding. Fractional CFO TBD Agenda 6:00 PM - 6:30 PM | Arrivals & Light BitesCasual networking over food & drinks before we kick off. 6:30 PM - 6:45 PM | Council & Sponsor IntrosQuick, 60-second introductions from each expert on the specific fires they help extinguish. 6:45 PM - 7:45 PM | Growth Council HuddlesRotate at regular intervals. At each table, state your burning question, get sharp direct feedback from the functional expert, & compare notes with peer founders. 7:45 PM - 8:30 PM | Drinks & Direct ConnectionsInformal wrap-up to continue conversations with experts & founders. Who Should Apply This event is strictly curated for Seed, Series A, & Series B founders / co-founders leading venture-backed tech startups. Capacity is strictly capped at 35 founders to maintain small group sizes & high-signal discussions. Requests to join will be reviewed to preserve the peer dynamic. Hosted By: Kindred Works - Fractional operations & employee engagement partners for high-growth startups. Narrativ by AK - Strategic positioning & narrative development for founders. Tavern - A Physical Social Network Want to host your own event? events.name: Drinks & Hacking: IT Happy Hour with The Objective-See Foundation
events.description: Join Rippling IT & The Objective-See Foundation for a happy hour at the Rippling NYC office. Over drinks & light bites, enjoy networking with your fellow IT pros & enjoy a presentation from Patrick Wardle, Co-Founder of the Objective-See Foundation, titled: Your Agent, My Orders: Hacking ChatGPT. A bit more about Patrick's presentation: AI agents need broad access to our files, accounts, & devices, making them prime targets for hackers. We took a closer look at ChatGPT's macOS desktop app & uncovered vulnerabilities that allow attackers to turn your trusted AI assistant against you. The impact? Attackers could hijack your Dot, take over your OpenAI account, access protected files, & more. Worse, these attacks present new challenges for traditional security tools: when an AI agent is compromised, malicious activity can look just like the agent doing its job. We'll demo what happens when ChatGPT gets hacked, discuss why AI agents pose new security challenges, & explore what all this means for Mac admins & the future of endpoint security. You can read more about this in NYT & Wired - & we hope to see you in-person for the full presentation. See you soon! A bit about us: Rippling IT amplifies your abilities & supercharges your skills. Control the entire user lifecycle in one system with fully built Identity, Device, & Inventory management tools, & 500+ integrations-including custom SCIM & SAML. Simplify, secure, & scale all from one single platform. Objective-See is a non-profit foundation focused on macOS security, driven by the mission to create free tools, grow & support a global community of students, researchers, & defenders, & advance Apple security through education, research, collaboration, & opportunity, around the world.

events.description: What if a museum ran like a lab, with the experiment still in progress? Ann Neumann is Director of Galleries & Exhibitions at the MIT Museum. Each one works as a prototype for engaging the public with technologies like CRISPR, machine learning, & sensory neuroscience. Reserve your spot & arrive early. events.name: The AI Briefing By Startup Grind: Who Owns The Data Layer Behind Enterprise AI
events.description: The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise.  This month's source: The Formula for Agentic AI Value: Applied AI Index 2026 (Boston Consulting Group - Sep 2026) Secondary sources: 5 Emerging Trends in Enterprise Data & AI (The Modern Data Company - Aug 2026) Agentic context layers (VentureBeat Intelligence - Oct 2026) Most of the money behind enterprise AI no longer runs through IT. BCG surveyed 1,330 CxOs & senior executives. AI spending has more than tripled, to 3.3% of revenue, & 2.8 points of it sit outside the enterprise IT budget. Business units generate about two-thirds of the value AI creates. So who owns the data their agents run on? BCG says the gap between leaders & everyone else has moved up the stack, to whether a company's data is current, consistently defined, trustworthy, & managed with clear ownership. It tells companies to keep their definitions, business rules & decision logic in a layer they control & could move to another vendor. VentureBeat's August survey points the other way. 98% of companies running retrieval in production use at least one system someone else built, & 2% name building & owning their context layer as their likely direction. 64% have already caught an AI agent giving a confidently wrong answer because of their own company's data.  The Mission: Deciding who owns the definitions, rules & context your AI runs on This series has spent the year on readiness: how fast enterprises adopted, where leadership's confidence outran results, how governance fell behind agents, & whether the workforce was ready. October's discussion turned to a question none of those sessions answered: who owns the data layer? We'll test BCG's advice against what data teams report from the inside. 61% call a reliable context layer critical for AI agents, & 16% engineer one on purpose.  The Format: The numbers: BCG's spending & ownership data, & where a self-reported executive survey stops being evidence. Cross-pollinated debate: Who owns it in your org? IT, the data team, the business unit paying for the agent, or the model vendor whose stack holds the context. The semantic layer problem: In VentureBeat's survey, companies running or building a semantic layer were about twice as likely to report a confidently wrong agent answer (78% vs. 37%). We'll work through why, & what it means for anyone about to fund one.  Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: See where AI budgets & accountability sit at the 7.5% of companies BCG calls future-built (all of them have clear ownership of the AI agenda), & decide whose name goes on the data layer before a vendor's does. Founders & Builders: Hear what buyers mean when they ask about lock-in. 37% of VentureBeat's respondents plan to keep standalone tools alongside the model, & 22% expect to consolidate onto one model provider's stack. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Compare notes on the work underneath. 46% of respondents say their teams spend more than a quarter of their time maintaining & integrating tools, & 8.4% say the data feeding their AI is trustworthy enough for production.  The Prep: This is a working session, not a lecture. Read the report here. Bring one wrong answer your AI gave & where the bad data came from.

events.description: IT IS BACK! CALLING ALL FOUNDERS! Hosted by Plug & Play NYC & Pioneering Minds AI Apply to pitch here:https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScOGgbEqUmtEHmKrhqpzynRzYX4Lk4EUC8qrYvSt6YZhXrGvg Pitching is one of the most important skills a founder develops, yet it's rarely practiced in a setting where you can iterate in real time. In this interactive workshop, founders will present their pitch, receive direct feedback, & immediately refine it live. This is a hands-on pitch masterclass where builders learn by doing, & by watching other founders sharpen their story. For founders, few people have a better perspective on how to communicate complex technology simply & convincingly. In this session, Anthony & Anna will work directly with founders in a live pitch lab, helping them sharpen their narrative & strengthen how they present their ideas. Come have a sales pitch, demo pitch, or even a VC pitch! Anthony RoseAnthony Rose is a pioneering technology entrepreneur best known as the co-creator & former CTO of the BBC iPlayer, one of the world's first large-scale streaming platforms that fundamentally changed how millions consume television. He has spent decades building technology at the intersection of consumer platforms, developer ecosystems, & emerging tech. His experience spans founding companies, leading engineering teams, & scaling global products. Nate HinmanNate Hinman is Senior Director at Plug & Play Tech Center. He works closely with startups, corporate partners, & investors to identify promising companies, accelerate growth, & create opportunities for founders to connect with some of the world's leading organizations. With extensive experience across Plug & Play's enterprise technology & AI ecosystem, Nate has seen hundreds of startups present, position, & refine their businesses. At this Pitch Masterclass, he will share an investor & accelerator perspective on what makes a pitch stand out, common mistakes founders make, & how to communicate a startup's story with greater clarity & impact. Workshop Format: Live Pitch Master Class 4-5 selected founders will pitch their startup & iterate live with Anthony. Each founder will go through the following format:  5-minute pitch 5 minutes of feedback 2-minute revised pitch incorporating feedback Watching this process unfold live helps everyone in the room see how small narrative adjustments can dramatically improve clarity, persuasion, & impact. Agenda:6:00 p.m. - Doors open6:25 p.m. - Pitches begin & live workshop7:30 p.m. - Networking session Who Should Attend This event is designed for:  AI founders preparing to raise funding Builders refining how they communicate their product Early-stage startups preparing for demo days or investor meetings Anyone interested in how strong startup narratives are built Apply to Pitch We will select 4-5 founders from the community to present during the session. If you would like to pitch your startup & receive live feedback, apply at this link! Selected founders will be notified ahead of the event. About Plug & PlayPlug & Play is the leading innovation platform, connecting startups, corporations, venture capital firms, universities, & government agencies. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, we're present in 60+ locations across 25+ industries. We offer corporate innovation programs, helping our partners in every stage of their innovation journey, from education to execution. We also run startup acceleration programs & have built an in-house VC where we've invested in hundreds of successful companies including Dropbox, Guardant Health, Honey, Lending Club, N26, PayPal, & Rappi. For more information, visit Plug & Play. About SeedLegalsSeedLegals is your full-stack legal platform from incorporation to Series A & beyond. Whether you're just starting out or gearing up for your next raise, SeedLegals is built to help founders move faster & smarter. Our tools make it simple to create & sign essential legal docs, close funding rounds, & reward your team - without burning time or cash on admin. There are over 50,000 startups on SeedLegals. If you're looking to incorporate, convert your to a C Corp, do a SAFE or a priced round, or manage your cap table, head over to SeedLegals, we're here to help you get there faster. About PRIMARYWelcome to PRIMARY, where 50,000 square feet of thoughtfully designed private & community spaces redefine coworking in downtown NYC. As the largest coworking space in FiDi, we combine premium private offices, shared workspaces, & an exclusive Lounge with top-tier amenities & exceptional service, creating the ultimate environment for your business to thrive. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: 122nd NY Hardware Meetup
events.description: The Hardware Meetup community is excited to announce our next event at Parter's NYC office. Hardware Meetups happen across 35+ cities around the world, bringing together hardware professionals to network & learn from each other. You might not realize it, but NYC is a hotbed for this kind of innovation & tonight you'll meet two companies working at the cutting edge of this technology. THANK YOU TO OUR HOST PARTER Parter is the AI-native BOM optimization platform that takes hardware from design to production without supply chain surprises. It continuously monitors every part on the BOM & flags shortages, EOL & lead time risks early, so issues are caught in prototyping, not on the production line. When a part is at risk or overpriced, Parter proactively finds drop-in alternates & cross-references, validated for fit, form & function, so teams can cut cost & lead time without a redesign. Datasheets & PCNs are parsed automatically, & every affected BOM is flagged the moment a change is announced. AGENDA6:30 - Arrival 7:00 - Welcome & introduction 7:15 - Speakers 8:00 - Mingling 9:00 - Event concludes SPEAKERSStay tuned for speaker announcement WANT TO GET INVOLVED?Sponsorship: We offer exclusive access to our 10,000+ member community through sponsorships. Host an event at your space: We are always looking for host sponsors to provide access to unique spaces from cool hardware companies building interesting things. Want to open up your office? Speaker: Do you have something interesting to share with our community? We're on the lookout for fresh faces to talk about their journey & experiences. If you want to get involved, head here: https://linktr.ee/nyhardware

events.name: Ugly Talks - Failure Is Key To Success
events.description: Failure gets talked about like it is part of the journey. That is the lie. The real thing is messier. Missed bets. Wrong hires. Near-breakdowns. The week you stop sleeping & start doing math at 3:00 AM. Founders are expected to eat it quietly & keep moving. No language for what happened. No playbook for what to do next. Ugly Talk is a founder room for the part nobody posts. No fluff. No consultants. Just builders with scars, talking about the call that cost them.  Why you should be in this room.Hear what failure cost them. Then hear what they did next. Learn how experienced founders separate self-worth from outcomes when things go sideways. Spot the patterns behind repeat mistakes. And the early signals you should not ignore. Leave with a few concrete moves for the next hard week. Not inspiration. Meet other founders in the thick of it. The ones who are still building.  What's on the table.Dare to suck: how permission to fail unlocks real progress The moment things broke: missed opportunities, wrong turns, near-breakdowns, & what changed afterward Failure vs identity: separating self-worth from outcomes Treating setbacks as data: what to measure, what to ignore, & how to decide fast Rejection as redirection: how founders find the signal in the no Habits for staying focused & resilient when everything feels uncertain  Run of show6:00 - 6:30 PM: Reception (check-in & light drinks) 6:30 - 6:40 PM: Welcome remarks 6:40 - 6:50 PM: Keynote Speech by Ben McKean 6:50 - 7:30 PM: Panel Discussion 7:30 - 7:45 PM: Audience Q&A 7:45 - 8:00 PM: Mixer + snacks & drinks  Featured speakers.Ben McKean - Founder & Chief Executive Officer, Hungryroot Ben McKean is the Founder & CEO of Hungryroot, a personalized healthy eating assistant that uses AI to make meal planning, food shopping, & nutrition effortless & enjoyable. Prior to Hungryroot, Ben was a Vice President & General Manager at Groupon, overseeing their food & beverage business. Ben came to Groupon through the acquisition of Savored, which he founded in 2009. Savored was the nation's leading provider of yield management technology to the restaurant industry, used by over two thousand restaurants nationwide & nearly one million diners. Prior to Savored, Ben worked in Merrill Lynch's technology investment banking group. Ben is a graduate of Georgetown University & currently lives in North Carolina with his wife & kids. Stephen McKinney - Founder & CEO, Bizbe Stephen McKinney is a serial entrepreneur with over a decade of experience across tech, marketing, & logistics. He's the founder & CEO of Bizbe.com, an AI-native business brokerage & lower middle market M&A firm based in New York & Miami. A former contestant on ABC's Shark Tank, Steve previously founded & led Retty Logistics, a seven-figure last-mile delivery company acquired by DXP Logistics & Webster Logistics. Dmitry Koltunov - Founder & CEO, Arbor Dmitry Koltunov is a serial entrepreneur, technologist, educator, & storyteller. He is the founder & CEO of Arbor, an AI-powered content engine that helps enterprises scale their communications with video & beyond. Previously, he co-founded & served as CTO of ALICE, a hospitality technology company that grew into a global industry leader before being acquired by Expedia Group. Dmitry also leads the New York City chapter of the Startup Leadership Program, New York's oldest startup fellowship, whose 500+ alumni have collectively raised more than $1 billion in funding across every industry imaginable. He is passionate about helping founders navigate the challenges of building & scaling companies. Outside of technology, Dmitry is an award-winning songwriter & theater producer currently developing a new musical for Broadway. He holds degrees in Computer Science & Economics from the University of Pennsylvania & is a CFA charterholder. Gwendolyn von Rahn - Co-Founder & CEO, Sweetling Health Gwendolyn von Rahn is the Co-Founder & CEO of Sweetling Health, an postpartum intelligence platform built for at-risk & hard-to-reach populations. She's a second-time exited founder, an award-winning marketer with over a decade of experience building consumer brands for women, Gwen led creative & brand teams at Vogue, InStyle, & POPSUGAR before founding & scaling a mission-driven consumer brand into Nordstrom distribution that raised over $1M for melanoma research through the Melanoma Research Foundation. She holds a Cornell Johnson MBA & founded Sweetling from her own lived experience with the postpartum care gap.  Who's hosting it.Victoria Yampolsky - President, The Startup Station Victoria Yampolsky is the Founder & President of The Startup Station, a strategic CFO advisory firm & financial education platform for startups. She partners with founders on financial strategy, modeling, & fundraising, having supported over 150 companies across 15 industries in raising more than $50M in venture capital. Victoria is also an advocate for female founders & access to capital, & has taught finance to more than 20,000 entrepreneurs through programs including the Bank of America Institute for Women's Entrepreneurship at Cornell. She began her career at Deutsche Bank & Capgemini, & holds a BS in Computer Science from Cornell University & an MBA from Columbia Business School.  Who's getting in.Early-stage tech founders & operators navigating uncertainty, setbacks, or the emotional weight of building a company. Expected roles may include: Founders & co-founders (pre-seed to Series A) Operators (COO, Head of Ops, Chief of Staff) Product & Engineering leads building through ambiguity Growth & GTM leads working through missed targets & pivots Finance & strategy leaders supporting founder decision-making  Who's backing this.The Startup Station The Startup Station - is a CFO advisory & financial education platform for early-stage startups. We help early-stage founders build investor-ready financials & tell their funding story with confidence. In the past decade, we've helped 150+ founders raise over $50M & educated 20,000+ entrepreneurs worldwide. The Startup Station also runs Speed Pitch, an exclusive investor-founder matchmaking event series for early-stage startups where founders are matched with 3 investors by sector, stage, & check size. Mind Your Business Every attendee will receive a free copy of keynote speaker Ben McKean's Mind Your Business. Mind Your Business is a practical parable for people rethinking work as AI advances. Set over a four-day retreat, it follows six participants competing for funding to bring one vision to life. As they evaluate six competing proposals, they begin to confront deeper questions about what gives them energy, who they serve, & what they uniquely contribute. Those patterns form what the book calls their Soulcode-the way purpose, belonging, imagination, & courage shape how they work. Told with humor & warmth, the story turns familiar workplace tensions into practical lessons for contributing more deeply, seeing new possibilities, & acting with greater conviction. At its core, the book argues that the opportunity of the AI era isn't doing more work-it's knowing what work is worth doing. GREY Journal GREY Journal - Media partner spotlighting modern entrepreneurs (featured on Apple News + Google News).  About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough "aha!" moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons & insights. With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami, we've built a vibrant community of thousands of founders & industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape. Official Website: UglyTalk.com Important Notice for Ugly Talk AttendeesAdmission & Confirmation Attendance is by approval only. Approved guests will receive a confirmation email along with a calendar invite. Invitations are non-transferable. Additional event details will be shared as the event approaches. Code of Conduct By attending, you agree to: Maintain respect & professionalism, adhering to all venue rules, policies, & applicable laws. Refrain from harassment, discrimination, unwelcome sexual advances (verbal or physical), intimidation, or inappropriate photography/recording. Report any violations to the event hosts immediately. Violations may result in immediate removal from the event & exclusion from future invitations. Liability & Risk Participation is voluntary & at your own risk. The event organizers, hosts, sponsors, & venue are not liable for personal injury, lost or stolen belongings, or any other damages incurred during the event. Media Consent By attending, you grant the event organizers & affiliated entities the right to capture, use, & distribute photos, videos, & audio recordings of you for promotional, marketing, & other lawful purposes, including digital & print media, advertising, & social media. You waive any right to inspect or approve the final materials & release all claims related to their use. Communications By registering, you agree to receive marketing & promotional communications from Ugly Talk & its co-hosts, partners, & sponsors. You may unsubscribe at any time. Agreement If you do not agree to this Code of Conduct, please refrain from attending the event.  Join us to stay updated on upcoming Ugly Talk events! Join the newsletter  Follow us on IG  Official website

events.name: Monday Founders Coworking Pod
events.description: If you're an early stage founder, building alone is hard. You lose momentum, get stuck with no one to ask, & there's no one checking if you actually did what you said you'd do this week. We're a small group of founders working together for the month - think study group, but for building. We help each other, check in, & keep each other on track. Now we're opening it up to more people, in pods of 3-5. Here's how it works: you tell your pod what you're trying to get done, & they hold you to it. Stuck on something? Someone in the pod probably knows the answer. Starting to slip? Someone notices. Same faces every week, so you're never starting over with strangers. This is an outgrowth of our Wednesday coworking events - just smaller. We're here to build the idea & building culture NYC deserves. We focus on that foundational layer of relationships & community that allows for ideas to spread & building to happen. Enough of the transactional networking. Product first, business second. Cohort is a community of founders, builders, creatives, & researchers in NYC, & the Monday pod is our small-group coworking ritual. Let's build. More from CohortKeep building, exploring ideas, & meeting the community. Find your next gathering below. Explore & connect The Crawling Dead: Halloween Food CrawlSat, Oct 31A Halloween afternoon food walk through Brownstone Brooklyn, with local bites & spooky stoops. Build together Monday Founders Coworking PodsSmall groups, shared goals, weekly accountability.Nov 2  Nov 9  Nov 16 Wednesday CoworkingWork alongside founders, builders, creatives, & researchers.Oct 28  Nov 4  Nov 11 Check our full calendar for more events

events.name: The Next Wave: AI & The Future Of Ocean Conservation, with Ocean Agentics
events.description: The world has committed to protecting 30% of the ocean by 2030, a target scientists see as the minimum for a healthy ocean. With four years to go, only about 3% is effectively protected. Countries & communities pursuing the 30x30 goal often lack the data, tools & technical teams to propose & implement conservation efforts at the speed & scale needed to get there. AI is starting to help with some of the hardest parts of that work. It can map where whales & other wildlife gather so countries know which waters to protect, & help coast guards catch illegal fishing vessels inside protected areas. However, most of these tools still sit out of reach of the small island nations & coastal communities with the most at stake. Whether AI narrows that gap or widens it depends on whether it's built with & for the people who will use it. Join Anew & Ocean Agentics for an evening of conversation with people leading this work across ocean technology, science, philanthropy & policy. We'll talk about what responsible AI for the ocean could look like, & what it would take for these tools to reach the people who need them. Drinks & mingling to follow. Ocean Agentics is a nonprofit building open tools that put frontier technology & marine data in the hands of people protecting the ocean. Our current focus is on providing engineering support to the countries & stakeholders implementing the High Seas Treaty, which covers two-thirds of the ocean. Anew is a gathering space & discovery center for social transformation located in NYC. We host interactive events & workshops, an accelerator program for nonprofits, & a retail lab featuring ethically-sourced coffee & gifts.

events.name: Silicon Alley Hack | Build Cool Hardware
events.description: Everyone & their grandma is hosting a hackathon. This is the one where you build something physical. Silicon Alley Hack is a one-day, in-person sprint for builders who'd rather solder than ship a vibe-coded app. Microcontrollers. Sensors. Connected devices. Real hardware that runs in the real world & has to work when we plug it in on stage. Application-based. Teams of 4. Every team gets an STM32 development board & peripherals on arrival. Bring your laptop, your wits, & your soldering instincts.  The Problem StatementSoftware ate the world & then got bored. The interesting frontier moved back to atoms - robots that navigate a room, drones that deliver, sensors that make a physical space legible to a machine. All of it runs on constrained silicon, in real time, in places where the cloud is too slow, too far, or not there at all. So that's the terrain: edge intelligence. Machines that sense the world & act on it, on-device.  The Challenge ThemeThe sealed spec will live somewhere in here: Sense  decide  act, running on-device IoT, sensors, & connected devices Physical/digital interaction - things that move, respond, or react Anything that runs on hardware, not just in a browser Constraints you can count on: You'll be working on an STM32 development board & peripherals - get familiar before you show up It has to run live. Slides don't win. Working hardware wins. First team to solve it take the prizes. This is a race, not a showcase.  What to ExpectA live race-to-win challenge dropped at kickoff An STM32 dev kit + peripherals for every team, free 5 hours of focused build time Team formation on-site, or come with your crew Breakfast & lunch provided Exciting prizes for the winning A room full of NYC's hardware people - embedded engineers, drone builders, robotics founders, spatial-data folks  Schedule10:00 - 11:00 AM - Doors open. Breakfast, networking mixer, team formation. 11:00 - 11:30 AM - Partner intros, Root Access demo, challenge drop, rules & judging criteria. 11:30 AM - 4:30 PM - Build sprint. Lunch provided. Clock does not stop. 4:30 - 5:15 PM - Live hardware demos to the judges. 5:15 - 6:00 PM - Photos & Mixer.  PrizesA mix of cash, credits, & perks for the winning team. Sponsors are getting locked in - full breakdown announced before doors.  Who Should AttendEmbedded & firmware engineers Robotics, drone, & hardware builders EE / CE students & anyone who's ever blown up a dev board Founders building physical products Software engineers who want to get their hands on real silicon Anyone curious, ambitious, & hands-on  Sponsors[Sponsor TBD - reach out to somyag00@gmail.com to sponsor]  Hosts & PartnersSomya Gupta - The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Pulse NYC AI - A community, incubator, & venture fund built for founders, researchers, & technologists shaping the future of AI in New York City. ConnNext - A next-gen mobile app & community built for career growth.

events.name: Is Everything Predictable - AI, Prediction Markets & Philosophy Of Foresight
events.description: In this six-week course, explore works from philosophy, cultural studies, & journalism to understand how technologies that predict the future also shape the present.The age of AI, prediction markets, & real-time data analysis brings predictive reasoning into all corners of human life. Once considered a niche academic interest area, the philosophy & politics of prediction is now relevant to everybody. Is Everything Predictable?: AI, Prediction Markets, & the Philosophy of Foresight presents scholarly material on forecasting technologies in a rigorous but highly accessible format.Drawing from a range of sources, we center scholarly texts & deeply-researched journalism that uncover the links between digital calculation, philosophical notions of time & free will, & the reality of living in an age where everything seems reducible to calculation.Guest speakers from academia & tech journalism will round out our seminar sessions, & for our final meeting, students have the option of presenting original research or creative work in an event open to the general public.SyllabusIn the early weeks of the course, we read texts from contemporary media studies & political theory that construe prediction & speculation as forms of governance. We also address probabilistic reasoning as a key feature of artificial intelligence & prediction market mechanisms, using frameworks suitable for participants without any background in STEM. As we will see, the similarities & differences between how probability works in AI versus prediction markets have much to tell us about these tools effects on everything from global warfare & the environment to creativity & personal relationships.After establishing a strong practical & theoretical foundation in AI & prediction markets, we turn to philosophical writing on the nature of freedom, self-expression, & power. These texts urge us to ask whether predictive technologies empower us with highly advanced forms of knowledge; if they inhibit us by constraining our imagination of whats possible; or if both of these outcomes might be true at once. We also read articles & listen to podcast interviews with our guest speakers in anticipation of their visits.Throughout our sessions, we examine case studies related to tech companies, specific applications, & major actors in the AI & prediction market space. The courses culminating event  a salon open to the general public  reflects our interest in connecting questions & concerns that seem highly academic to current events & everyday life. Students who choose to give presentations will participate in an additional workshop or one-on-one advising session to help them prepare. By the courses end, we will be able to navigate a world driven by predictive technologies with greater clarity, confidence, & wisdom, & to share our perspectives on them in a way that empowers those around us.Learning OutcomesConnect AI & prediction market functionalities to political & cultural affairsDevelop critical reading skills applicable to philosophy & journalismApply frameworks from the theoretical humanities to real-world developments in politics & technologyMake scholarly ideas accessible to a wide range of audiencesScholarshipsIndex scholarships are designed to benefit underrepresented groups, BIPOC members of our community, & those for whom the class price is not accessible. These need-based scholarships will go to the candidates who best demonstrate why they should be chosen for the free spot to our class. You can apply for a scholarship here.Instructor BioEmma Stamm is a writer & professor with a background in philosophy & the social study of science & technology (STS). She holds a PhD in Interdisciplinary Studies from Virginia Tech & has taught courses on the philosophy & social implications of technology at Villanova University, Virginia Tech, the Acid Horizon Research Commons, New York University, where she currently teaches for the Department of Media, Culture, & Communication. As a public-facing scholar, she has written for Vice Motherboard, Real Life Mag, & Communications of the Association for Computing Machinery, in addition to co-hosting the LEPHT HAND podcast. She is the co-founder & Executive Director of theLenox Institute for Advanced Study, which makes critical science & tech education accessible beyond academia.RefundsWe get that things come up, but we rely on headcounts to make our programs viable. If you request a refund...More than 4 weeks before the program begins  100% refundMore than 2 weeks before the program begins  50% refundFewer than 2 weeks before the program begins  No refundThanks for understanding & for supporting our ability to provide cool offerings through your purchase.Media Release ClauseBy attending this event, you consent to being photographed, filmed, or recorded, & grant Index Space permission to use this content for promotional or informational purposes.

Is Everything Predictable?: AI, Prediction Markets, & the Philosophy of Foresight presents scholarly material on forecasting technologies in a rigorous but highly accessible format.Drawing from a range of sources, we center scholarly texts & deeply-researched journalism that uncover the links between digital calculation, philosophical notions of time & free will, & the reality of living in an age where everything seems reducible to calculation.Guest speakers from academia & tech journalism will round out our seminar sessions, & for our final meeting, students have the option of presenting original research or creative work in an event open to the general public.SyllabusIn the early weeks of the course, we read texts from contemporary media studies & political theory that construe prediction & speculation as forms of governance. We also address probabilistic reasoning as a key feature of artificial intelligence & prediction market mechanisms, using frameworks suitable for participants without any background in STEM. As we will see, the similarities & differences between how probability works in AI versus prediction markets have much to tell us about these tools effects on everything from global warfare & the environment to creativity & personal relationships.After establishing a strong practical & theoretical foundation in AI & prediction markets, we turn to philosophical writing on the nature of freedom, self-expression, & power. These texts urge us to ask whether predictive technologies empower us with highly advanced forms of knowledge; if they inhibit us by constraining our imagination of whats possible; or if both of these outcomes might be true at once. We also read articles & listen to podcast interviews with our guest speakers in anticipation of their visits.Throughout our sessions, we examine case studies related to tech companies, specific applications, & major actors in the AI & prediction market space. The courses culminating event  a salon open to the general public  reflects our interest in connecting questions & concerns that seem highly academic to current events & everyday life. Students who choose to give presentations will participate in an additional workshop or one-on-one advising session to help them prepare. By the courses end, we will be able to navigate a world driven by predictive technologies with greater clarity, confidence, & wisdom, & to share our perspectives on them in a way that empowers those around us.Learning OutcomesConnect AI & prediction market functionalities to political & cultural affairsDevelop critical reading skills applicable to philosophy & journalismApply frameworks from the theoretical humanities to real-world developments in politics & technologyMake scholarly ideas accessible to a wide range of audiencesScholarshipsIndex scholarships are designed to benefit underrepresented groups, BIPOC members of our community, & those for whom the class price is not accessible. These need-based scholarships will go to the candidates who best demonstrate why they should be chosen for the free spot to our class. You can apply for a scholarship here.Instructor BioEmma Stamm is a writer & professor with a background in philosophy & the social study of science & technology (STS). She holds a PhD in Interdisciplinary Studies from Virginia Tech & has taught courses on the philosophy & social implications of technology at Villanova University, Virginia Tech, the Acid Horizon Research Commons, New York University, where she currently teaches for the Department of Media, Culture, & Communication. As a public-facing scholar, she has written for Vice Motherboard, Real Life Mag, & Communications of the Association for Computing Machinery, in addition to co-hosting the LEPHT HAND podcast. She is the co-founder & Executive Director of theLenox Institute for Advanced Study, which makes critical science & tech education accessible beyond academia.RefundsWe get that things come up, but we rely on headcounts to make our programs viable. events.name: The AI Briefing By Startup Grind: Who Owns The Data Layer Behind Enterprise AI
events.description: The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise.  This month's source: The Formula for Agentic AI Value: Applied AI Index 2026 (Boston Consulting Group - Sep 2026) Secondary sources: 5 Emerging Trends in Enterprise Data & AI (The Modern Data Company - Aug 2026) Agentic context layers (VentureBeat Intelligence - Oct 2026) Most of the money behind enterprise AI no longer runs through IT. BCG surveyed 1,330 CxOs & senior executives. AI spending has more than tripled, to 3.3% of revenue, & 2.8 points of it sit outside the enterprise IT budget. Business units generate about two-thirds of the value AI creates. So who owns the data their agents run on? BCG says the gap between leaders & everyone else has moved up the stack, to whether a company's data is current, consistently defined, trustworthy, & managed with clear ownership. It tells companies to keep their definitions, business rules & decision logic in a layer they control & could move to another vendor. VentureBeat's August survey points the other way. 98% of companies running retrieval in production use at least one system someone else built, & 2% name building & owning their context layer as their likely direction. 64% have already caught an AI agent giving a confidently wrong answer because of their own company's data.  The Mission: Deciding who owns the definitions, rules & context your AI runs on This series has spent the year on readiness: how fast enterprises adopted, where leadership's confidence outran results, how governance fell behind agents, & whether the workforce was ready. October's discussion turned to a question none of those sessions answered: who owns the data layer? We'll test BCG's advice against what data teams report from the inside. 61% call a reliable context layer critical for AI agents, & 16% engineer one on purpose.  The Format: The numbers: BCG's spending & ownership data, & where a self-reported executive survey stops being evidence. Cross-pollinated debate: Who owns it in your org? IT, the data team, the business unit paying for the agent, or the model vendor whose stack holds the context. The semantic layer problem: In VentureBeat's survey, companies running or building a semantic layer were about twice as likely to report a confidently wrong agent answer (78% vs. 37%). We'll work through why, & what it means for anyone about to fund one.  Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: See where AI budgets & accountability sit at the 7.5% of companies BCG calls future-built (all of them have clear ownership of the AI agenda), & decide whose name goes on the data layer before a vendor's does. Founders & Builders: Hear what buyers mean when they ask about lock-in. 37% of VentureBeat's respondents plan to keep standalone tools alongside the model, & 22% expect to consolidate onto one model provider's stack. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Compare notes on the work underneath. 46% of respondents say their teams spend more than a quarter of their time maintaining & integrating tools, & 8.4% say the data feeding their AI is trustworthy enough for production.  The Prep: This is a working session, not a lecture. Read the report here. Bring one wrong answer your AI gave & where the bad data came from.

Read the report here. Bring one wrong answer your AI gave & where the bad data came from.

events.name: NY Tech Meetup - Climate Tech Edition
events.description: NY Tech Meetup  Columbia University SPSM.S. Technology Management Program We're excited to welcome back Columbia University's School of Professional Studies M.S. Technology Management program for another special edition of the NY Tech Meetup! Join us on Monday, November 9, as we spotlight emerging innovators from Columbia's Technology Management program who are turning bold ideas into promising technologies & real-world solutions. From fresh approaches to everyday challenges to innovations with the potential to transform industries, this edition offers a unique opportunity to discover what's next, hear directly from the innovators, & connect with NYC's vibrant tech community. As always, expect live demos, engaging conversations, new connections, & the energy that makes NY Tech Meetup a cornerstone of New York's tech ecosystem. Presenting innovators & their demos will be announced soon. Stay tuned! Program 6:00 PM - Doors Open 6:30 PM - Welcome & Live Demos 8:00 PM - Community Ask / Offer 8:15 PM - After-Party & Networking Come for the demos. Stay for the connections. Seats are limited - register now to secure your spot! About the NY Tech Meetup The NY Tech Meetup (NYTM) is a signature event of theNY Tech Alliance that has been a monthly staple for the NYC tech ecosystem since 2004. It is the world's largest meetup group of its kind with over 50,000 members who have a common interest in learning from & helping one another. At each event, entrepreneurs, founders, CEOs, & their teams demo cutting edge & transformative tech, answer questions from attendees & network with all in a welcoming & fun-filled space. Since its creation, over 1,200 companies have participated & have been a driving force of innovation & job creation in NYC & the greater NY area. About Columbia University's M.S. in Technology Management Columbia University's M.S. in Technology Management (TMGT) equips graduates with applied technology skills through research & industry insights to lead digital transformations & innovation in organizations across industries with an ethical leadership lens to achieve high impact & measurable results for today & to prepare for the future. Guided by Columbia's School of Professional Studies Scholar-Practitioner model, the program bridges theory & practice by integrating cutting-edge, real-world applications into the classroom experience & offers flexible pathways to the Masters of Science in Technology Management degree. The In-Person STEM-designated pathway offers full-time & part-time options & the Online part-time option is designed for working professionals who want the rigor & community of Columbia University from anywhere in the world. Through the School of Professional Studies' immersive digital learning environment, students engage in live, interactive classes led by Columbia faculty & industry experts.

Through curated events, live demonstrations, & meaningful conversations, Breakline Society creates opportunities for collaboration, investment, & innovation across emerging industries. 99 YARDS 99 YARDS is an AI-powered fashion technology platform that connects brands, creative professionals, manufacturers, & service providers in a single ecosystem. Built to modernize how the fashion industry operates, 99 YARDS leverages AI to streamline discovery, collaboration, & production-from concept to market. Together, Breakline Society  99 YARDS are bringing New York's technology, investment, & creative communities together to explore how Physical AI, robotics, & intelligent automation are transforming industries & creating new opportunities. Meet the founders building intelligent machines & the investors exploring what comes next. Join us in New York in Nov. for an evening of robotics demos, candid conversations, & connections across Physical AI. Whether you're building a product, investing in the space, or exploring your next opportunity, see the technology up close & meet the people behind it.  Speaker Spotlight Ned Lomigora - Founder, 387labs  User Uploaded ImageA serial entrepreneur with an MIT engineering background, Ned helps businesses turn AI capabilities into practical applications. events.name: AI Build Lab For Founders: Launch & Read The Signal
events.description: AI Build Lab for Founders SeriesTake your idea from concept to launch in a series of interactive sessions. Leverage AI tools to build a live product, put it in front of users, & leave with honest feedback, concrete next steps, & the tools to keep going - no coding background required. Session 3: LaunchAcquire users, analyze the data, & make the call. Compare your live user engagement against pre-set targets, locate your audience's online channels, & run live outreach during the session. Evaluate the evidence to decide whether to persevere, pivot, or pause, & map out your next test. Who it is forCurrent NYU students, Alumni, & Faculty Coders & non-coders are welcome. Anyone who wants to explore ideas, is curious about entrepreneurship, or has started building. Deliverables for Session 3: LaunchGet to your first users, a plan to market, or a path to pivot An evidence scorecard for your product, or MVP A decision: continue, change, or stop A 14-day plan for the next test Full series highlightsHands-on from start to finish. Every session ends with something real in hand, not just notes. Real customers, not guesses. Founders talk to 5 to 10 potential users & put a working product in front of them. Two tracks. No-code founders build with tools like Lovable, Replit, v0, & Bolt. Founders who code use Claude Code or Cursor. Honest checks built in. Founders open & verify every source, set their success target before the results come in, & have a second tool test every build. A live product with a real ask. Each product goes live with a waitlist, pre-order, or booking option. Demo day. The series ends with founders presenting to guest founders & investors. Tools they keep. Every founder leaves with the full Leverage kit & their own working setup. What founders walk away withA tested idea. Assumptions checked against real conversations & real data. A live product MVP. Reviewed, tested, & in front of first users, or a clear & cheap "no." A decision & a plan. Continue, change, or stop, backed by evidence, with the next 14-day test written out. Their own working toolkit. Research, idea testing, building & review tools, set up & ready to use. The Leverage kit. Every prompt & tool used in the series. Entrepreneurship mindset. Check the sources. Set the target first. Never let the builder grade its own work. A cohort. A group of founders who built alongside them.

events.name: Can Your Agents Actually Ship?
events.description: Can your agents actually ship?Compose your AI-native SDLCYour AI agents can't be trusted with data they can't find, can't understand, & aren't sure they're allowed to touch. And even when they get it right, the code they write still stalls in a delivery pipeline built for human speed. On Nov2 we will tackle both: first the data foundations agents need to trust, then the SDLC they need to ship through. Opening talk: From a Data Swamp to a Data Agent You Can Trust The evening opens with Grzegorz Krl on the data foundations AI agents need to find, understand & safely access your data. We've run this talk at Boston & San Francisco Tech Week, & both times it ran long because nobody wanted to stop asking questions. Full session details: https://luma.com/il0xoz9a Main session: Can your agents actually ship? AI can write code. Getting that code to production is another matter. Most engineering organizations hit the same wall: the bottleneck isn't the agent, it's everything downstream of it. Pipelines, CI, reviews, security gates, release processes: all of it was built for human speed, not AI. Visdom, built by VirtusLab, is the missing layer between AI coding & production. It lets you compose an AI-native SDLC, piece by piece: the context, validation, governance & orchestration agents need to ship safely & at scale. Come see what that looks like in practice. We'll cover: Why AI adoption stalls after the first wave of excitement What infrastructure an AI-native SDLC actually requires How Visdom connects agents to your SDLC, component by component Live demos of AI agents shipping production-ready code Q&A with the Visdom team Evaluating AI coding assistants or already rolling them out across teams? This session is about what happens after the code is written.  What you'll see liveA hands-on walkthrough of how Visdom removes friction across context, execution, & validation, turning your SDLC into a system AI agents can reliably operate on: Deep repository scanning that builds the semantic context AI agents actually need: not just open files, but the full dependency & intent graph across your codebase Blast radius scoring on an AI-generated PR before it touches CI, catching what code review misses when your team merges 3x more than last quarter Governed sandbox execution with full audit trails: the missing layer between the AI suggested it & it's running in production A live maturity assessment on a real delivery pipeline: where it stands today, & the smallest concrete step that unlocks the next level Who should join?CTOs, CDOs, VPs of Engineering & Data, Heads of Platform & AI, & senior engineers responsible for developer productivity, data platforms & AI adoption strategy. Especially if your AI tools shine in demos but stall in your CI/CD pipeline, or your agents can't tell which table is the right one. Why it's worth your time Get a practical diagnostic for making your data usable by AI agents See what an AI-native SDLC looks like in practice (live demo) Learn how to assess your AI maturity, step by step Learn how to start small, validate quickly, & evolve without big upfront risk Agenda6:00 PM - Doors open, drinks & networking6:30 PM - Opening talk: From a Data Swamp to a Data Agent You Can Trust (incl. Q&A)7:00 PM - Panel: real stories from AI adoption7:45 PM - Live demo: Visdom8:15 - 9:00 PM - Q&A & networking SpeakersPractitioners working hands-on with AI-driven delivery, data platforms, developer tooling, & real-world implementation: Grzegorz Krl, Tech Lead & Data Architect at VirtusLabGrzegorz believes that solid data systems start with a deep understanding of what the business actually needs. He works closely with organizations to put their business domains at the center of every data initiative, so that architectures, models & pipelines reflect how the business really operates. Artur Skowroski, Head of Application Development at VirtusLabArtur has spent more than ten years in the industry, on everything from greenfield builds to systems older than he is. He has worked as a Software Engineer, Tech Lead, Architect & Technical Product Manager, which gives him a broad view of the problems he tackles. He still likes to stay hands-on & has been writing a weekly roundup of the JVM ecosystem at jvm-weekly.com for over two years. Hosted by VirtusLabWe work with organizations ranging from global brands (including top-tier investment banks, Databricks, Airbnb, & DHL) to fast-growing startups, helping them build data platforms & AI systems that actually scale. At our core, we're engineers working with engineers, & we actively support the community through meetups, events, & shared learning. If you're working on AI in software delivery, this is where it starts to actually work.

events.name: AI & Future Of Community
events.description: At a moment when loneliness, social isolation, & declining trust are contributing to a growing crisis of community, artificial intelligence is rapidly changing how we communicate & connect with one another. Can AI help strengthen human connection, or could it deepen the forces pulling us apart? Pioneering AI researcher David Blei, Central Synagogue Senior Rabbi Angela Buchdahl, & technologist Jamie Metzl - author of The AI Ten Commandments - talk to constitutional scholar Noah Feldman in a wide-ranging conversation exploring one of the defining questions of our age. Artificial intelligence is transforming our world at breathtaking speed. It promises extraordinary breakthroughs in medicine, science, education, & human creativity while raising profound questions about truth, justice, freedom, meaning, & the future of our civilization. Can these technologies help us become not only more productive, but wiser, more compassionate, & more ethical? What values should guide the creation of increasingly powerful intelligent systems, & what choices must we make today to shape the future we want? Representing wide-ranging, divergent viewpoints on this transformative technology, Blei, Buchdahl, Metzl, & Feldman gather to explore the legal, ethical, philosophical, scientific, & spiritual dimensions of how AI stands to change our world. Can intelligent machines help us become more ethical? How should democratic societies govern increasingly powerful AI systems? Most importantly, what can we do today to ensure that AI strengthens, rather than diminishes, our communities? Join us for a timely conversation offering fresh insight into the choices that are shaping the future of humanity. Copies of The AI Ten Commandments: A New Moral Code for Humanity by Jamie Metzl, To Be a Jew Today by Noah Feldman, & Heart of a Stranger: An Unlikely Rabbi's Story of Faith, Identity, & Belonging by Rabbi Angela Buchdahl will be available for purchase; the authors will sign books following the program. An initiative of the 92NY Belfer Center for Innovation & Social Impact.

events.name: What Makes A Good Life? A Guided Public Discussion On AI
events.description: The oldest question philosophers have asked is: What makes a good life? This inquiry has been important not only for guiding individual decisions, but also for shaping institutions & public policy. Now, amid the rapid changes AI is bringing to every aspect of our lives, & the growing debate about its risks & benefits, we must ask: What makes a good life, & how does AI enable or hinder it? Together, we will explore this question through prompts & shared reflection. Dr. Ece Tekbulut is a political philosopher & the founder of Thinking Through. She earned her Ph.D. from Columbia University. Through Thinking Through, she brings rigorous philosophical inquiry into everyday life, convening groups to engage with themes central to contemporary society, especially where people feel at an impasse. One such focus is AI's impact on human flourishing. Her work fosters public discourse on AI's implications & the ethical questions that surround it, & she writes on AI & society for Medyascope. Wissam Kahi is the founder of Odyssey Lead, where he helps companies capture the value of AI that usually gets lost between the boardroom & the front line. For seven years he led digital transformation across United Rentals' network of more than 1,500 locations, & he learned there that AI only sticks when the people who do the work help shape it. His essays on Substack & his novella The Panama Dilemma explore the question at the heart of tonight's discussion: what makes a good life when the machine is doing the living? Matt Konwiser is an Ecosystem Leader & Field CTO at IBM. He serves on the AI Advisory Council at the Global Technology Industry Association (GTIA) & writes a regular column on AI for CFO Intelligence Magazine. He also co-hosts AI Diatribe, a podcast built around direct, practical conversations about where AI is headed & what organizations should do about it. Anew is a gathering space & discovery center for social transformation located in NYC. We host interactive events & workshops, an accelerator program for nonprofits, & a retail lab featuring ethically-sourced coffee & gifts.

events.name: Convergence Exhibition Opening Reception
events.description: Converse with creators blurring the lines of form & function while enjoying lite bites & seasonal drinks! Convergence: Art & Industry at the Yard Exhibition Opening Reception Friday, November 6, 2026 5:00 p.m. - 8:00 p.m. Yard Work Gallery @ Building 92 Free  Featuring work that blurs the boundaries between fine art & industrial production, the exhibition highlights the ways in which processes, materials, & innovation connect artists, designers, & fabricators. Featuring a dozen works on view, visitors will enjoy examining the ways in which form & function come together, while engaging directly with the creators behind the objects. Join us for light bites, drinks, & lively conversations.   ///   BNYDC RULES, PROTOCOLS & ACKNOWLEDGEMENT  Check-In Procedure All visitors must check-in at Building 92. Visitors arriving through other entry points will be redirected to enter through official entry locations.All visitors must register for the event. No one will be admitted without an official RSVP. It is highly recommended that you RSVP in advance although day of registration is permitted.A valid photo ID is required for entry.
