events.name: Climate Scaling Summit
events.description: The true entry points for startups working with government Join LACI at BATWorks & The Trust for Governors Island for a Climate Scaling Summit focused on one critical inflection point: how climate startups break into government as a customer, regulator, & partner. Securing contracts with the government can feel opaque to founders, but true entry points exist even if they are not always obvious to a first-time founder. This session demystifies how startups can work with government agencies & offers a valuable opportunity for founders to ask agencies & entities for feedback, technical support, & opportunities to scale. The morning opens with a fireside chat/panel, followed by five hands-on workshops covering: LegislationPermitting & CodePilot KPIs for Government AgenciesCapital Projects & Public-Private DevelopmentEducation & Workforce This is the final of four Climate Scaling Summits hosted by LACI at BATWorks in 2026, all under the theme of accelerating commercialization of clean energy innovation in NY by focusing on common problems faced by startups after the pilot stage. About LACI & The Trust for Governors Island LACI has deployed $25M in cleantech pilots over the past four years, from first commercial deployments to the nation's first zero-emissions delivery zone & is now supercharging the Pilots at BAT program & deeper deployment of the LACI Cleantech Debt Fund.  The Trust for Governors Island's Climate Piloting Program offers early-stage companies & innovators the opportunity to test & scale climate products & services in a real-world environment. Since its launch in 2023, the program has advanced projects in living shorelines, clean water, circular economy, buildings, energy, air quality, & urban agriculture-opening doors to new customers, suppliers, talent, investors, & public agency partnerships. The program is a core initiative of the Trust's Center for Climate Solutions, an initiative dedicated to accelerating equitable climate solutions for cities on Governors Island. Visit www.govisland.org/climate to learn more.

events.name: Agentic Finance Hack
events.description: Money never sleeps. Neither do agents.Right now, a human still approves every trade, every payment, every flagged account. How much longer can finance work that way?Agents can already execute. They place trades, pay invoices, and chase late payments without waiting for sign-off. The big concern is trust. Give an agent too little authority and its useless. Give it too much and its dangerous. Getting that balance right is the whole game.Were looking for agents bold enough to act and safe enough to trust.What you can build for Markets & Trading: research, strategies, and prediction markets Agentic Payments: moving money safely, within limits Compliance & Financial Crime: catching fraud and managing risk Finance Ops: automating invoicing, collections, and treasuryWe bring the venue, the compute credits, and the food. You bring the idea.JudgesPradeep Dhananjaya - Tech lead @ AWSWho is it for?Engineers, quant builders, fintech founders, and anyone working in finance who wants to build. events.name: Responsible Tech Summit - Embedding Accountability AI Era
events.description: At a time when artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping society, the conversation is shifting from broad principles to real-world accountability. The 2026 summit will explore the theme of Principles to Power: Embedding Accountability in the AI Era. For years, the Responsible Tech field has been guided by ethical frameworks, voluntary commitments, & emerging standards. Today, the challenge is clear: how do we translate those ideas into systems of governance, oversight, & design that ensure innovation does not come at the expense of safety, rights, or trust? The Responsible Tech Summit is designed as a curated convening for 375 leaders that helps align & shape the direction of the movement. Participants will include global governance leaders, AI researchers, industry practitioners, policy experts, civil society advocates, & philanthropic leaders who are building the infrastructure of accountability for the digital age. Through keynotes, panels, & conversations, attendees will explore topics such as accountability by design, platform oversight, youth online safety, the Responsible Tech economy, & the evolving global regulatory landscape. All ticket proceeds fund free resources & services for the Responsible Tech community that our organization provides. Can't make it in person? The event will be livestreamed for free on All Tech Is Human's YouTube page, where recordings will also be available afterward. - Are you a journalist looking to potentially cover the Responsible Tech Summit? Reach out to Hello@AllTechIsHuman.org. Speakers for the Responsible Tech Summit 2026 Camille Francois - President, ROOST Eli Pariser - Co-Director, New_ Public Cathy O'Neil, Founder, Author, Mathematician & Data Scientist, O'Neil Risk Consulting & Algorithmic Auditing Rumman Chowdhury, CEO, Humane Intelligence PBC Alex Bores, Assembly Member, New York City's 73rd District Beth Goldberg, Founding Executive Director of Humanity AI Sinead Bovell, Founder, WAYE Alexis Wales, Chief Information Security Officer, GitHub Alison Lee, Chief R&D Officer, The Rithm Project Amanda Craig, General Manager of Responsible AI Public Policy, Microsoft Anya Schiffrin, Director, Media Program, Columbia University (SIPA) Carrie Varoquiers, Chief Impact Officer, Workday Joshua Elder, Senior Vice President & Head of Grantmaking, Siegel Family Endowment Julie Cordua, CEO, Thorn Fernanda Del Castillo, Director of AI Governance, Mastercard Kathy Pham, Faculty & Senior Fellow, Product & Responsible AI, Harvard University Kristin Hansen, Executive Director, Civic Health Project J. Trevor Hughes, President & CEO of IAPP Shreya Singh Hernndez, Senior Manager, Aspen Digital, The Aspen Institute Melanie Plaza, Chief Technology Officer, AE Studio Courtney Radsch, Director of the Center for Media & Digital Governance, Open Markets Institute; Fellow, Brookings Institution Andrew Rasiej, Founder, Civic Hall Clement Wolf, Director, Responsible AI Strategy, Google Hale Sirin, Program Scientist, Schmidt Sciences AI & Advanced Computing Institute Jeff Collins, Director of Trust & Safety, Amazon Web Services Alisar Mustafa, Head of AI Safety, Duco Experts   Agenda10:00 - 11:00 am ET | Check-in & Networking 11:00 - 11:10 am | Welcome remarks 11:15 - 11:45 am | Panel: Beyond Benchmarks: Turning Evaluations into Enforceable Standards 11:50 - 12:00 pm | Lightning talk 12:05 - 12:35 pm | Panel: Safety by Design: Accountability at the Intersection of AI, Industry, & Advocacy 12:40 - 1:40 pm | Lunch 1:45 - 2:05 pm | Fireside Chat: Open-Source, Open Questions: Transparency in the Age of AI 2:10 - 2:40 pm | Panel: Shared Risk, Shared Responsibility: Rethinking Responsible AI Governance 2:45 - 3:05 pm | Fireside Chat: Alignment in Practice: Building AI That Wants to be Good 3:05 - 3:30 pm | Networking break 3:30 - 4:00 pm | Panel: Trust as Strategy & the Fight Against AI-Enabled Fraud 4:05 - 4:15 pm | Keynote 4:15 - 4:25 pm | Lightning Talk 4:30 - 5:00 pm | Panel: Rebuilding the Commons: Community & Pluralism in the AI Era 5:05 - 5:25 pm | Fireside Chat: Looking Back to Look Ahead: Co-Designing AI After a Decade of Tech Lessons 5:25 - 5:30 pm | Closing remarks *See the full agenda & bios of our speakers here.   Sponsors for the Responsible Tech Summit 2026Special thanks to our strategic partners, Columbia World Projects, Forum One, & Highspring, for helping bring this critical conversation to life. WorkdayWorkday operates at the heart of the enterprise - HR, finance, & IT - where the margin for error is effectively zero. By tightly coupling AI with the context, guardrails, & trusted processes that run the business, Workday goes beyond AI that assists work to agents that do the work & drive measurable outcomes. More than 11,500 organizations worldwide, including more than 65% of the Fortune 500, trust Workday to deliver. MastercardMastercard is a global technology company in the payments industry, connecting consumers, financial institutions, merchants, & governments in more than 200 countries & territories. The company is committed to building a sustainable, inclusive digital economy that benefits everyone, everywhere. PinterestPinterest is a visual search & discovery platform where people find inspiration, curate ideas & shop products - all in a positive place online. Headquartered in San Francisco, Pinterest has over 600 million monthly active users worldwide. MicrosoftMicrosoft is a global technology leader empowering every person & organization on the planet to achieve more through its platforms & productivity tools. The company is committed to advancing responsible AI & ensuring emerging technologies are developed & deployed safely & ethically. Siegel Family EndowmentSiegel Family Endowment takes an inquiry-driven approach to grantmaking, informed by the scientific method. As technology reshapes society, we fund organizations asking critical questions about its impact on learning, work, & infrastructure. Founded in 2011 by David Siegel, co-founder & co-chairman of Two Sigma, we advance technology in the public interest, supporting research & initiatives that imagine a more inclusive, resilient technology-driven society. AE StudioAE Studio is an applied AI & AI alignment company that builds software products for clients while advancing research on making advanced AI systems safe & beneficial. Its recent work with Anthropic, GRAM, trains dangerous knowledge into removable modules so it can be stripped from a model before release. AE Studio reinvests its commercial success into neglected approaches to AI alignment research. Learn more at ae.studio. GoogleGoogle's mission is to organize the world's information & make it universally accessible & useful. As a leader in AI & computing, the company is focused on developing technology responsibly to benefit people & society. Kapor FoundationThe Kapor Foundation works at the intersection of racial equity & technology to expand access to K-12 computer science & postsecondary tech pathways, improve tech accountability & worker protections, & increase investments in infrastructure & innovation. We advocate for policy changes, build the capacity of partners, conduct research, support partners through grantmaking, & invest in entrepreneurship & VC. We believe that when technology includes diverse perspectives & is harnessed to address societal challenges, we can transform the tech ecosystem for Black, Latine, & Native communities, & society as a whole. Kapor Foundation works collectively with the Kapor Center family of organizations, Kapor Capital, & SMASH to reimagine & reconstruct a more inclusive & equitable technology sector. Check out Kapor Foundation's Responsible AI Principles for Advancing a More Equitable Innovation Future. IAPPThe IAPP is a policy-neutral, not-for-profit association founded in 2000 with a mission to define, promote & improve the professions of privacy, AI governance & digital responsibility globally. Civic Health ProjectCivic Health Project is a nonpartisan nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing scalable solutions to the dangerous divisions that threaten American democracy. Since our founding in 2019, we have supported more than 75 academic researchers, grassroots practitioners, creatives, & technologists who are helping reduce polarization, strengthen civic norms, & foster social cohesion. Today, Civic Health Project focuses primarily on exploring the vast potential of promising new technologies to help resolve conflict, improve civil discourse & deliberation, foster social cohesion, & uphold societal norms. Normsy.ai, our flagship in-house project, brings this mission to life. It identifies toxic content in real time & equips users to respond with respectful, trust-building messages grounded in social science & supported by artificial intelligence. We are also part of the initiative The Forum, a new model for civic leadership at a time when trust is low, division is high, & the need for credible, citizen-led solutions has never been greater. GitHubGitHub is the world's leading platform for agentic software development - powered by Copilot to build, scale, & deliver secure software. Over 225 million developers, including more than 90% of the Fortune 100 companies, use GitHub to collaborate, & more than 140,000 organizations have adopted GitHub Copilot. CinderCinder is the industry's first Trust & Safety operations platform to help organizations combat Internetabuse at scale. We provide Trust & Safety teams with a single system to manage complex integrityoperations & investigations to create a safe environment for their users. Interested in sponsoring our summit or forming a strategic partnership? Email us at hello@alltechishuman.org.   About All Tech Is HumanAll Tech Is Human is the coordination layer & connective tissue for the Responsible Tech ecosystem. By uniting key individuals across civil society, government, industry, academia, & philanthropy, we provide a sandbox for solution-building & socialization to influence key levers of change. We specialize in taking a whole-of-ecosystem approach to tackling thorny tech & society issues, shaping the Responsible Tech movement, & ensuring that our tech future is aligned with the public interest. We are the premier gathering for the Responsible Tech community, convening thousands of people globally. We curate the defining resource for the movement, the Responsible Tech Guide, used by academia, industry, civil society, & policy professionals. We have the largest online community for the Responsible Tech movement hosted on Slack with over 15,000 members across 117 countries. We have the go-to job board for the community, our curated Responsible Tech Job Board & related talent pool. Refund Policy & Billing DetailsRefund requests made before October 1 at 5:00 pm ET are subject to a $50 administrative fee. Refund requests made between October 2 & the final refund deadline of October 16 at 5:00 pm ET face a late cancellation fee of $100. No refunds or ticket transfers are permitted after October 16. Please note: credit card statements for this purchase will show a charge from "Social Science Research Council (SSRC)," All Tech Is Human's fiscal sponsor.

events.name: Spatial Analytics w/ Python
events.description: Join PyData NYC on October 27th at 6:30 PM for an evening exploring geospatial data science with Python, featuring Brendan Collins, Founder & CTO at Makepath & creator of Xarray-Spatial! Discover how Python can transform spatial data into powerful insights, from terrain analysis & hydrology to scalable CPU- & GPU-accelerated computing. Please bring your  to follow along & sign up using your official government-issued name.  Pizza & drinks will be provided - Thank you, Makepath! Agenda xarray-spatial: In & Out of the Raster-verseSpeaker: Brendan Collins (Founder & CTO at Makepath)Spatial data comes in many shapes & sizes, but some of the most powerful spatial analysis techniques begin by viewing the world as a grid.Led by the library's creator & maintainer, this talk introduces Xarray-Spatial, an open-source Python library for scalable raster analysis with CPU & GPU acceleration.We'll learn how to enter the Raster-verse by bringing spatial data into Xarray, explore the Raster-verse using algorithms for terrain analysis, hydrology, proximity, & more, & escape the Raster-verse through techniques like zonal statistics & polygonization.Finally, we'll discuss contributing to the Raster-verse, sharing lessons from maintaining Xarray-Spatial & how AI-augmented development is transforming open-source contributions, code quality, & scientific software engineering.Whether you're a GIS practitioner, data scientist, or Python developer, you'll leave with practical ideas for working with spatial data & contributing to open source.  About the SpeakerBrendan Collins is the Founder & CTO of Makepath, where he helps early-stage startups & Fortune 500 engineering teams realize their product ambitions.A former employee of Anaconda, Brendan has spent the past decade applying PyData technologies, including NumPy, Xarray, & Numba, to engineering challenges across the public, private, & nonprofit sectors.When not writing in the third person, Brendan enjoys swimming, playing the banjo, & gardening.  NetworkingConnect with fellow data enthusiasts, Python developers, researchers, & community leaders. Build meaningful connections, exchange ideas, & explore opportunities for collaboration.

Thank you, Makepath! Agenda xarray-spatial: In & Out of the Raster-verseSpeaker: Brendan Collins (Founder & CTO at Makepath)Spatial data comes in many shapes & sizes, but some of the most powerful spatial analysis techniques begin by viewing the world as a grid.Led by the library's creator & maintainer, this talk introduces Xarray-Spatial, an open-source Python library for scalable raster analysis with CPU & GPU acceleration.We'll learn how to enter the Raster-verse by bringing spatial data into Xarray, explore the Raster-verse using algorithms for terrain analysis, hydrology, proximity, & more, & escape the Raster-verse through techniques like zonal statistics & polygonization.Finally, we'll discuss contributing to the Raster-verse, sharing lessons from maintaining Xarray-Spatial & how AI-augmented development is transforming open-source contributions, code quality, & scientific software engineering.Whether you're a GIS practitioner, data scientist, or Python developer, you'll leave with practical ideas for working with spatial data & contributing to open source.  About the SpeakerBrendan Collins is the Founder & CTO of Makepath, where he helps early-stage startups & Fortune 500 engineering teams realize their product ambitions.A former employee of Anaconda, Brendan has spent the past decade applying PyData technologies, including NumPy, Xarray, & Numba, to engineering challenges across the public, private, & nonprofit sectors.When not writing in the third person, Brendan enjoys swimming, playing the banjo, & gardening.  NetworkingConnect with fellow data enthusiasts, Python developers, researchers, & community leaders. Build meaningful connections, exchange ideas, & explore opportunities for collaboration.

events.name: Tech Table Talk: Career, Family & Life On Your Terms
events.description: Tech Table Talk: Career, Family & Life on Your Terms is an intimate dinner bringing together women in tech for an honest conversation about career, fertility, family planning, & building a life on their own terms. Hosted by Baddies in Tech in partnership with Spring Fertility, the evening will create space for women to have the kinds of conversations we don't often have: How do you think about growing your career while also considering a future family? What options are available if your personal & professional timelines do not align perfectly? And how can having more information today create more choices tomorrow? We're setting the Tech Table to create space for a conversation you may have been thinking about but have not had anyone to talk to about. You'll walk away not just with a great meal & new professional connections, but also more information, more context, & more confidence to make decisions that feel right for the life you're building! What to ExpectWelcome & Opening ToastBaddies in Tech & Spring Fertility will welcome the group & set the tone for an open, judgment-free conversation about career, fertility, family planning, & the life you're building. Dinner & Tech Table TalkOver dinner, guests will have the opportunity to connect more deeply with one another through thoughtful conversation & curated table prompts, exploring the realities of building a career while also thinking about relationships, motherhood, fertility, timing, & what it means to make decisions on your own terms. Fertility Planning Q&A with Dr. Shante Sullivan-PikeThroughout the evening, Dr. Shante Sullivan-Pike of Spring Fertility will help answer questions & demystify fertility, fertility preservation, & family-planning options. Dr. Chantae Sullivan-Pyke is a double board certified Fertility Specialist & Site Director of Spring Fertility Long Island. She completed her medical training at Yale University, Columbia University, & the University of Pennsylvania. Dr. Sullivan-Pyke brings a thoughtful & compassionate approach to fertility care, rooted in deep clinical experience & a genuine connection with her patients. She combines her expertise with a strong commitment to the patient experience, creating a supportive & empowering atmosphere throughout the process. Her areas of clinical focus include IVF, fertility preservation, & oncofertility, & she is particularly passionate about helping her patients navigate complex fertility decisions with clarity & confidence. What You'll Leave WithFresh perspective on navigating career goals alongside personal & family plans New relationships with women thinking through many of the same questions A better understanding of your fertility & family-planning options More clarity around fertility preservation & when it may be worth exploring Greater confidence asking questions about your reproductive health A stronger connection to the Baddies in Tech & Spring Fertility communitie Attendance is complimentary & curated. Because this dinner is intentionally intimate & limited to approximately 20-25 guests, registrations will be reviewed to create a group that aligns with the purpose of the evening. Submitting the registration form expresses your interest in attending & does not guarantee an invitation. Confirmed guests will be notified approximately one week before the event.

events.name: AI & Future Of Life Sciences
events.description: Join UJA Healthcare for our kickoff event:a timely talk featuring Mikael Dolsten, M.D., Ph.D., former chief scientific officer at Pfizer, on how artificial intelligence is advancing medicine & reshaping the life sciences industry. After a reception with light bites & mingling,you'll hear from Dr. Dolsten in conversation with Avi Kometz, M.D., a partner at Deerfield Management, about how AI is accelerating drug discovery, advancing cancer treatment & gene therapies, impacting clinical trials, & opening new possibilities for public health. You'll also hear about UJA's powerful work improving the lives of people in need here in New York, in Israel, & around the world. Dr. Mikael DolstenMikael Dolsten, M.D., Ph.D., is a physician-scientist & investment advisor who serves on several public & private boards as a director or chairman & as strategic advisor to leading business groups in biomedicine & AI TechBio. Dr. Dolsten is the former chief scientific officer & president of Research & Development at Pfizer During his 16-year tenure at Pfizer, he led the approval of more than 36 medicines & vaccines. Dr. Dolsten holds an M.D. & a Ph.D. in tumor immunology from Lund University, where he is a visiting adjunct professor, & has published more than 160 scientific papers. Avi Kometz, M.D., is a partner on Deerfield Management's Medical Technologies team. He was a partner at Ascent Biomedical Ventures, leading investments in biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, & health IT. He also led corporate development at a pediatric pharmaceutical company & advised healthcare clients at McKinsey. He began as a clinician in South Africa & went on to found & build a group of clinics.

events.name: Your Investor Pitch - What To Say & How To Say It
events.description: A free, two-hour workshop for founders who want to build a stronger investor pitch & deliver it with confidence.You know your business. You know the opportunity. But can you communicate it in a way that makes investors understand the potential, believe in you, & want to continue the conversation? On October 30, join a group of founders for a focused working session to assess the pitch you have today, identify what's missing, & turn it into a sharper, more compelling investor presentation. Anthony Rose, CEO of SeedLegals.com, tells you exactly what investors need to hear. David Goldberg, CEO of Prosody.center, shows you exactly how they need to hear it. Two hours, both experts, free. What you'll work on1. Build the right investor storyStructure your pitch around what investors need to understand: opportunity, differentiation, competition, financials, traction, scalability, & why now. Cut unnecessary information, close narrative gaps, & make the value easier to grasp. 2. Deliver it with confidence & credibilityA strong deck isn't enough. Learn to make a strong first impression, create buy-in, use pace & pauses to make key numbers land, stress the words that carry value, & steady your voice under pressure. Use your voice to communicate with the composure & authority investors expect. 3. Test & refine your pitchPitch in front of others & discover where the room leans in, where you lose them, & what needs to change. Use live feedback to tighten your messaging & delivery. 4. The live-feedback experienceEach hour includes 15 minutes of tips, first from Anthony Rose on creating compelling content, then from David Goldberg on delivering it with conviction, followed by 45 minutes of live, instructive feedback so founders can improve their pitches on the spot. What you'll leave withA sharper, more focused investor pitch A clearer understanding of your strengths & gaps Practical techniques for presenting with confidence Real-world feedback on your messaging & delivery Specific next steps for continuing to improve Greater insight into what can move an investor from listening to wanting to know more Who should attendFounders & startup leaders at different stages of the fundraising journey. Whether you're preparing to pitch for the first time or you've pitched before & know it could be stronger, the goal is the same: leave with a better pitch than the one you walked in with. Your facilitatorsAnthony Rose, CEO, SeedLegalsFounder & CEO of SeedLegals, the legaltech platform that helps startups get investment-ready, run a funding round, & handle their legals, used by over 60,000 startups. Before SeedLegals, his career spanned 3D graphics, peer-to-peer music, internet video, & social TV, including heading up BBC iPlayer. Wired Magazine's 2009 cover story called him "The Man Who Saved the BBC." David Goldberg, CEO, Prosody.center & Edge StudioFounder of Prosody.center & EdgeStudio.com, an international voiceover recording center. He has directed, coached, & trained over 10,000 celebrities, politicians, CEOs, & founders on more than 13,000 spoken-word projects over 38 years. He identifies the blind spots that hold founders back when they pitch (pacing, phrasing, wording, emphasis, tone, body language, composure, nonverbal cues), then shows the precise adjustments that change how investors experience & respond to you. DetailsWhen: Friday, October 30, 1-3pm ET, in person, Times Square, NYCCost: Free to join. Co-founders are welcome too.Capacity: Seating is limited, & registrations are approved individually. Come prepared to work on your business, test your ideas, & practice your pitch, not simply take notes.

events.description: Join Propel Earth for a private dinner with funded early-stage founders in NYC focused on IP law, patents, AI, ownership, and investor diligence.This is not a webinar.This is an intimate founder dinner for people building real companies who want to better understand how intellectual property affects fundraising, product development, defensibility, and long-term company value.Most founders do not think about IP until it becomes a problem.A competitor files first.An investor flags a gap in diligence.A contractor owns code the company thought it owned.An AI tool creates uncertainty around who actually owns the core product.This dinner is designed to help founders avoid those mistakes early while meeting other high-quality founders in the same stage of building.Over dinner, well discuss the IP decisions that matter in the first few years of a startup, including patents, trademarks, trade secrets, AI-generated work, contractor ownership, fundraising diligence, and what founders should have documented before the stakes get higher.Expect a curated room, real conversation, and a chance to build relationships with other early-stage funded founders in events.name: The Deployment Room: 6 Active Funds, Funding Founders (Seed to Series B)
events.description: The Builder Series: A 60,000+ member community redefining what networking looks like - curating founders, operators, investors & more into intentional rooms built for experiences people remember & relationships that last. It's a direct line to the most ambitious builders, with a community that actually shows up. Link to apply for membership: Link For more info please message me 917-242-2821, dylan@thebuilderseries.co Find us here: Instagram  LinkedIn  TikTok  Facebook  X : WhatsApp Broad Channel This is the 4rd edition of our luncheon. This time, we're hosting it in an $8.5M townhouse, because we believe in high-class experiences, & incredible people. Every room has been bigger than the last. Our 2nd edition versus the 1st: Founder revenue: $90M+ a year, up from $18M+ in August. Money being raised: $197M+ across 19 founders, up from $95M+ across 14 in August. Capital already raised: $43M+, up from $35M+ in August. The investors at the table: We feature 6 investors from our network, & we always end up with more. 1st edition: We expected 6. We brought 10. 2nd edition: We expected 10. We brought 12. $2B+ combined AUM across both events. $1M average check, $100K minimum. $10M+ in live check capacity. Who this room is for To get into this room, you should to have raised at least $1M or be doing $1M+ in ARR. Our last edition averaged $3.8M+ ARR per founder. Raised your first round, onto your second, or bootstrapped to $1M or 15M ARR? You're in the right place. If you're an exited founder, LP/GP, dealmaker or capital raiser, you belong in this room too. Every investor here is from our network. We're curating this room deliberately, matching founders to the investors most likely to be a fit, & making the introduction ourselves. The goal: getting founders funded by our investor network. The 6 Investors joining us from our network: (More will be joining) Jay Spindel: Jay Spindel (Managing Director) of INTE Securities & (Special Advisor) to SOJA Ventures. With decades of experience in capital formation & investing, he has helped numerous emerging-growth companies secure funding & pursue their strategic objectives. Jay brings a broad, cross-sector perspective, with experience supporting companies in agentic AI, advertising technology, healthcare services, & renewable energy. Through INTE Securities, an SEC-registered & FINRA-member broker-dealer, he advises companies & family offices on capital-raising initiatives. As a Special Advisor to SOJA Ventures, he plays a key role in securing capital for the firm's portfolio companies & supporting their long-term growth., FINRA member broker-dealer connecting issuers with accredited & institutional capital. Moshe Neuman (Founder, MN Ventures): Moshe is an angel investor, advisor & startup guru who has mentored more than 100 founders. He's now building MN Ventures, a new VC fund raising $100M, as he moves from angel investing into running his own fund. He backs companies at the very earliest stages.  Triet Leminh: Principal, LMT Partners: Lawyer, founder, & investor backing pre-seed to Series A founders building in enterprise & regulated industries. Writing $200K-$300K checks.  DJ Patel (Head of Direct Investing, UV: DJ leads direct investments at UV, which manages $75M-$100M. He backs Seed to Series A companies in healthtech, fintech & AI infrastructure, with typical checks of $500K-$600K.  Gonzalo Quincot (Founder, Sinober): Sinober is a financial intelligence platform that combines public & private market intelligence with institutional-grade methodology, corporate finance & proprietary AI tools to sharpen investment & capital decisions for individuals & businesses. Invests in automation, robotics, data centers & applied AI.  Dr. David Cunic (Serial Entrepreneur & Investor, UCS Advisor [confirm]): A 17-time founder who has built companies across 3 countries & 8 states, with 7 exits. He represents a network of more than 1,000 angel investors who are always looking for quality deal flow. He also helps companies at the friends-and-family, pre-seed & seed stages raise capital, writing checks himself.  All 6 senior investors confirmed. Part of building rooms is making sure real capital is present. Six investors actively deploying writing capital will be joining. Our first confirmed: Why we do this: Putting active investors in the same room as exceptional founders, & keeps the room small enough to ensure everyone actually meets. We value intentional networking & community. If you're here to meet the best of the best, this is the room. Why we do this Our intent is simple: bring good, smart humans together, put active investors in the same room as incredible founders. Intentional community has been lost. We're rebuilding it. What to expect A Korean-style small bites lunch, courtesy of our team, with dishes shared family style Conversations with fellow high-performing startup leaders & investors An experience designed for meaningful connections with ambitious peers solving similar problems A beautiful private townhouse, with room to move between the kitchen, the deck & the garden The format is intentionally part standing, part seated, so you can enjoy incredible food without being anchored to a single table or a single conversation.

events.description: Join us for a special conversation with Priya Parker, acclaimed author of The Art of Gathering & her new New York Times bestseller, The Art of Fighting. In conversation with Kwaku Aning, Founder & Principal of Retro Futurism, Priya will explore how we can rethink conflict, navigate difficult conversations, & turn moments of disagreement into opportunities for deeper understanding & connection. About Priya Parker Priya Parker is a facilitator, strategic advisor, & acclaimed author of The Art of Gathering: How We Meet & Why It Matters. Her new book, THE ART OF FIGHTING: The Transformative Power of Conflict, is a New York Times bestseller & is out now. Trained in the field of conflict resolution, she is sought after by Fortune 500 companies, nonprofits, universities, civic organizations, & various groups around the world to resolve issues & come together more intentionally. She studied organizational design at MIT, public policy at the Harvard Kennedy School, & political & social thought at the University of Virginia. She is the host of the popular Substack GROUP LIFE where she teaches regularly. About Kwaku Aning Kwaku Aning is the Founder & Principal of Retro Futurism Consulting, where he draws on 25 years of experience across education, corporate, & nonprofit sectors to help organizations build powerful networks, maximize conferences & gatherings, & form partnerships that drive change.

events.name: Business Funding - An International Perspective
events.description: Every stage of growing a business is a funding decision, even when it doesn't feel like one. How you pay for the next market, the next hire, the next acquisition quietly shapes what the business is worth years later, & who you can sell it to. Across the Atlantic, the options multiply & the advice gets thinner. During the evening, hear from speakers across the corporate lifecycle, sharing their different funding, expansion & exit stories, so you leave with greater insight & awareness of the opportunities, & the pitfalls to avoid. Designed for international founders & business executives planning to grow in New York City, the discussion will cover the advantages, tradeoffs, & tactics involved in raising capital from VC & PE sources.  Speakers Dan Jaeck is a Principal at Crane VC, based between New York & London, where he partners with founders building transformational software companies.Before joining Crane, he spent four years at Eniac Ventures in NYC, investing in AI application-layer & infrastructure companies. Prior to Eniac, Dan began his career at Goldman Sachs in London on the Emerging Market Equities desk. Joel Goschalk is a Senior Director at Dundon Advisers, advising middle-market companies on recapitalizations, restructurings & credit. He started as a London insolvency practitioner, co-founded & scaled a UK litigation funding & private equity business (Cavendish IP Solutions), & has spent over a decade as COO of a family office, advising on fundraising rounds, fund formation across the UK, US & offshore, & cross-border expansion.  Co-host: The Transatlantic Innovation Hub, is New York's launch pad for Italian & European companies, to help them successfully enter & scale in the U.S. market. Located in the heart of Manhattan, TIH serves as a landing pad for innovation ecosystems, providing companies with both a physical presence in New York & a structured set of market access services to accelerate their U.S. expansion. The Knowledge Shop is the founder community in NYC. We are industry & stage agnostic, helping not just startups grow, but supporting the founders building them.  Founding Partner: Sabre Integrated has been providing commercial security systems in NYC since 2000.From access control & video surveillance to fully integrated security systems, they design, install & support your business every step of the way  Charity Partner: The St George's Society of New York, provides life-changing support to immigrants from Britain & the Commonwealth in New York. Established in 1770, we're the second-oldest charity in the city. We hold events year round - join us for Pancake day   Find even more Tech events at: www.foundereventsnyc.com

events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: Did Maha Maha?
events.description: Has the MAHA movement made Americans healthier than the establishment? Americans spend more on healthcare than anyone else in the world. Yet we have soaring rates of obesity, diabetes, & chronic disease. So is the medical establishment failing us? And is MAHA actually doing any better? RFK's MAHA movement has put ultra-processed foods, environmental toxins, & chronic disease at the center of the national conversation. Supporters say it's finally challenging a healthcare system that profits from treating illness instead of preventing it. Critics say it's undermining trust in vaccines, established science, & the institutions responsible for keeping Americans healthy. So who's right? Is MAHA forcing a long-overdue reckoning with a broken healthcare system? Or is it replacing imperfect science with something far more dangerous? Kerry Semle is a biomedical engineer, former medical technology executive, & women's health advocate with 15 years of experience in medical devices & diagnostics. She's advocated for greater investment in women's health research & improved access to care. Emily Kaplan is the CEO & co-founder of the Broken Science Initiative, an organization challenging the scientific establishment & questioning how medical research is conducted, evaluated, & trusted. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

events.name: Drinks & Hacking: IT Happy Hour with The Objective-See Foundation
events.description: Join Rippling IT & The Objective-See Foundation for a happy hour at the Rippling NYC office. Over drinks & light bites, enjoy networking with your fellow IT pros & enjoy a presentation from Patrick Wardle, Co-Founder of the Objective-See Foundation, titled: Your Agent, My Orders: Hacking ChatGPT. A bit more about Patrick's presentation: AI agents need broad access to our files, accounts, & devices, making them prime targets for hackers. We took a closer look at ChatGPT's macOS desktop app & uncovered vulnerabilities that allow attackers to turn your trusted AI assistant against you. The impact? Attackers could hijack your Dot, take over your OpenAI account, access protected files, & more. Worse, these attacks present new challenges for traditional security tools: when an AI agent is compromised, malicious activity can look just like the agent doing its job. We'll demo what happens when ChatGPT gets hacked, discuss why AI agents pose new security challenges, & explore what all this means for Mac admins & the future of endpoint security. You can read more about this in NYT & Wired - & we hope to see you in-person for the full presentation. See you soon! A bit about us: Rippling IT amplifies your abilities & supercharges your skills. Control the entire user lifecycle in one system with fully built Identity, Device, & Inventory management tools, & 500+ integrations-including custom SCIM & SAML. Simplify, secure, & scale all from one single platform. Objective-See is a non-profit foundation focused on macOS security, driven by the mission to create free tools, grow & support a global community of students, researchers, & defenders, & advance Apple security through education, research, collaboration, & opportunity, around the world.

events.name: Startup Pitch Mixer
events.description: Join our event in New York! We design Pitch & Networking nights to help founders sharpen their thinking through direct, candid feedback & to give strong investors access to serious teams. Our pitch night is complemented by a structured networking session before & after the pitch session.  What to expect: Startups pitch live & receive focused feedback from angels & VC partners Structured networking session before & after the pitches Entrepreneurs, startup founders, & operators are joining to network, exchange ideas, & build strong connections Active investors & venture scouts joining to discover the best startups early  Who you will meet at the event: Founders Investors, VC partners, Venture Scouts Marketers, Salespeople, Business Advisors Industry Disruptors AI Experts Entrepreneurs from Europe, Asia, & the United Kingdom  We Welcome New Investors: We invite investors to our event to expand their network, get acquainted with new startups, evaluate them, share feedback, & participate in discussions with early-stage & serial founders. We offer complimentary tickets to institutional investors, angels, & venture scouts with a proven track record. If you'd like to access our database of promising startups or provide mentorship support to our best startups, please fill out this short Investor Application Form, & our team will contact you.  Want to Pitch? A limited number of founders will have the opportunity to pitch their startup or business to a panel of investors & experts. 4-6 selected founders will pitch their startup, followed by a short Q&A where participants can ask questions & share feedback. Apply by filling out the Pitch Application Form & sending us your pitch deck. Spots are limited, & we select founders in advance. To maintain high-quality pitches, you are required to present with a pitch deck. We will share our pitching guide and, if you'd like, coach you so you're fully prepared for pitch night.  The best startups will be featured across our social media & included in our investor newsletter. Requirements for attendees: Dress code: smart casual. Bring good energy.  Join our event & secure your ticket today! About us: Startup Valley is a global event organizer hosting pitch nights in 25 cities since 2023. Since then, we have hosted 850 events for 40,000 attendees. Over these years, we connected countless outstanding early-stage startups to serious investors, & we are not planning to stop. We maintain strategic partnerships with VC funds in the US, Europe, & Asia to support our community. Do you have a question, a partnership proposal, or want to clarify something? Reach us at hello@startupvalley.club Agenda 18:00-18:30 - Registration: Guests register, receive badges, & event programs. This is an opportunity for casual networking, making first connections, & preparing for the event. 18:30-19:00 - Event Kickoff & Interactive Networking: Official welcome from the organizers with a brief overview of the event goals & schedule. Interactive networking session to connect with key contacts. 19:00-19:50 - Startup Pitch Session: Startups present their projects to investors & experts. Each team has 5 minutes to pitch, covering the project's core idea, business model, & target market. 19:50-21:00 - Chill & Networking: Participants enjoy casual conversations with investors, discuss collaboration opportunities, & exchange ideas over refreshments. FAQ Can I pitch? Yes! To pitch, please purchase a Pitch Ticket & fill out the Pitch Application Form. We will contact you to discuss & approve your pitch. The pitch duration is 5 minutes. You will also have some time to answer questions from the audience. How does the pitch go? Selected founders present on stage to the audience & the investors in the room. You get 5 minutes to pitch your idea, business model, target market, & investment ask, followed by a short Q&A. The best startups are featured across our social media channels & in the investor newsletter. Who will I meet? Founders, angel investors, VC partners, venture scouts, AI experts, engineers, operators, marketing & sales experts, & international entrepreneurs from across Europe, Asia, & the US. Do investors get free tickets? Yes! Please apply above or email hello@startupvalley.club, & we will issue a complimentary ticket for you & your team. Can I request a refund? Yes. Refunds are available if requested at least 1 day before the event start time. Please submit the refund request on the platform where you purchased your ticket, or email us at hello@startupvalley.club

events.name: An Unmuted Debate: Primary Party Crashers
events.description: Should primaries be open to every voter? More Americans now identify as independent than as Democrat or Republican. Yet in New York & many other states, those voters are shut out of the primaries that often decide who actually wins. So are closed primaries locking out the voters our politics needs most? And would opening them make anything better? Open primaries let any registered voter participate, regardless of party. Supporters say they force candidates to campaign to the whole electorate, reward problem-solvers over partisans, & give millions of independents a real voice. Critics say parties have the right to choose their own nominees, that open systems invite strategic crossover voting & voter confusion, & that the evidence they reduce polarization is thin. So who's right? Are open primaries the fix for a system that rewards the extremes? Or are they a reform that promises more than it delivers? John Opdycke is the founder & president of Open Primaries, a national organization working to enact & protect open & nonpartisan primaries. He has spent three decades in independent & reform politics, helped found the New York State Independence Party, & writes the monthly column Brash Tacks for The Fulcrum. Lindsey Cormack is an associate professor of political science & director of the Diplomacy Lab at Stevens Institute of Technology. She is the author of How to Raise a Citizen (And Why It's Up to You to Do It) & Congress & U.S. Veterans, created the DCInbox database of congressional newsletters, & serves as Secretary of Manhattan Community Board 8. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

events.name: Awake & Alive
events.description: What helps us feel fully present, engaged, & alive? In this experiential somatic workshop, we'll explore flow as a state of deep engagement, connection, & ease, & look at what helps us move toward it more often. For people living with chronic stress, burnout, or the effects of trauma, moments of flow can be especially restorative. They can help us shift out of constant vigilance or depletion & reconnect with curiosity, creativity, agency, pleasure, & a sense of being fully in our lives. Deborah Lee is a somatic executive coach & founder of Creaturae, supporting founders, leaders, creatives, & changemakers who feel stretched thin, caught in familiar patterns, or disconnected from themselves. She helps people notice how stress & emotions show up physically in order to understand the patterns behind the responses, & helps people explore new ways to navigate pressure, relationships, & everyday life. Deborah is also the Founder & CEO of AI Empath, an AI-powered somatic coaching platform informed by her practice & research. She is completing her M.A in Clinical Psychology at Columbia University. Want to host your own event? Click here to learn more.

events.name: PMAI - Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Learn How to SellSales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. - Bring a computer. You're writing three things tonight.- Most founders can get meetings. The deals die after meeting one.- You'll leave with your buyer in one sentence, a cold email written to a real person, & five questions for your next call. About Farzad, the speaker Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding & generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: Worn: Smart Glasses Hackathon
events.description: Two days, one overnight build, & real smart glasses on your face. Join us at Cornell Tech with MicroLumin, the Shenzhen team behind the CES 2026 award-winning M6 display glasses, & build the first wave of apps for waveguide display glasses. This is a hands-on hardware hackathon for engineers & builders who would rather ship on real devices than talk about the future of spatial computing. Problem StatementSmart glasses are finally light enough to wear all day. What's missing is software that feels natural to use. Your challenge is to build anthropocentric interfaces: apps that start from how people see, move, talk & pay attention, not from how phones work. These should be things you'd actually keep on your face. The Challenge ThemeHeads-up assistants that show the right info at the right moment Live captioning, translation & conversation memory Navigation & wayfinding without looking down at a phone Accessibility for low-vision, hard-of-hearing & neurodivergent users Hands-free workflows for field techs, clinicians, chefs & mechanics New input patterns: voice, ring, head motion & glanceable UI Making the glasses useful with AI on what the camera sees What to ExpectMicroLumin AR glasses handed out to teams for the build SDK access & docs shared before the event so you can start early A workshop from Dr. Zhaoen Dai, MicroLumin's founder & CEO, on AR & where the AI industry is heading An overnight build from Friday evening into Saturday Teams of up to 4, or match with teammates at kickoff Food, caffeine & other builders who care about hardware Live demos on the device, worn by your team, in front of the judges ScheduleFriday, Nov 20 5:30 PM: Doors open, check-in, dinner 6:15 PM: Welcome & kickoff with the organizers, Cornell Tech & MicroLumin 6:35 PM: Challenge brief & a walkthrough of the MicroLumin SDK 7:00 PM: Team formation: 30-second idea pitches, then a mixer to find teammates 7:45 PM: Teams locked, hardware handed out, devices set up 8:00 PM: Hacking begins 9:00 PM: SDK help desk & mentor office hours open 11:30 PM: Late-night snacks Overnight 12:00 AM to 8:00 AM: Overnight build, with a quiet rest area for anyone who needs a nap All night: A MicroLumin engineer is online for live SDK support (it's afternoon in Shenzhen) Saturday, Nov 21 8:00 AM: Breakfast & coffee 9:00 AM: Morning check-in: each team shares where they are & what's blocking them 10:00 AM: Workshop with Dr. Zhaoen Dai, MicroLumin's founder & CEO, on designing for AR & waveguide displays 11:00 AM: Workshop: [Topic & speaker TBD] 12:30 PM: Lunch 2:00 PM: Code freeze, project submissions due 2:15 PM: Demo expo: judges go table to table & teams demo on the device 3:45 PM: Finalists announced 4:00 PM: Finalists demo on stage: 3 minutes, worn by the team, plus 2 minutes of Q&A 4:45 PM: Talk by Dr. Dai on AR & where the AI industry is heading, while judges deliberate 5:30 PM: Awards 6:00 PM: Hardware return & wrap PrizesTBD JudgesTBD Who Should AttendHardware Founders Engineers at companies like Meta, Amazon & Google who want to build on AR hardware iOS & Android developers Hardware tinkerers, embedded & computer vision engineers Product designers interested in spatial & glanceable UI Spots are limited & approval is required. You don't need prior AR experience, just the drive to build something real overnight. SponsorsMicroLumin: Shenzhen-based maker of AR display glasses, including the M6 series & several CES 2026 award winners. MicroLumin is providing the hardware & SDK support for teams. HostsSomya Gupta: The face of the NYC startup ecosystem. Stephen Jin: Johnson MBA '27 at Cornell, board director at Gona Semiconductor, Angel Investing Waftech - Founded in 2007 & based in Penang, Malaysia, Waftech designs & manufactures wafer-handling & automation equipment for semiconductor manufacturing. Waftech delivers end-to-end, from R&D & design through manufacturing & after-sales service, & is ISO 9001:2015 certified. Waftech is a subsidiary of Gona Semiconductor, a Shanghai-headquartered equipment group. Olivia Iarmak: AI Quality Ops Lead at Meta Reality Labs working on Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses, & co-founder of HQ Labs. Vishal Kharker: Lead Product Manager at RTX Fintech & Research, previously at Barclays & RBC Capital Markets. Info site: https://worn-hacks.com

events.name: Post Human Investment Summit
events.description: In the 1980s, Renaissance Technologies pioneered a new way to beat the markets: computing power, statistics, & signal processing. Today that approach anchors a $1.2 trillion asset class, but one built almost entirely on short-horizon trades. The holy grail has always been the opposite: long-horizon investing, fully automated. An agentic Warren Buffett. With the tools we had, it felt out of reach. Agentic reasoning systems may finally change that. A new wave of frontier researchers, 6 newly launched fully agentic funds, & tiger teams inside established funds are setting out to build it. Join us for a one day summit alongside many of the early leaders in this space, to share ideas, challenge assumptions, & brainstorm the various paths ahead for this burgeoning space. The event will be a tightly curated group of researchers, builders, investment professionals, & LPs. Please apply below to be included.   Hosted by Pillar VC Pillar VC is a Boston-based seed-stage venture capital firm. We invest in engineers, researchers, & scientists building solutions to the world's greatest challenges, including Circle, Abridge, Algorand, PillPack, Jellyfish, Neural Magic, Hometap, Asimov, & PathAI, & others.

events.name: SOSV Deep Tech Summit
events.description: SOSV DEEP TECH SUMMIT Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. The producers of the Summit are SOSV's Ned Desmond, Ben Joffe, & Norm Amandi. More DetailsSOSV's mission is to invest in deep tech companies that advance human & planetary health, & embedded in building an 800+ company portfolio with a remarkable array of companies applying AI in the physical world. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

events.name: Data By Design
events.description: In conversation with Shannon Mattern. P&T Knitwear is pleased to welcome Lauren Klein, Tanvi Sharma, & Silas Munro to celebrate & discuss the release of their book Data by Design, which explores how the history of data visualization holds the key to designing a more just future. They will be in conversation with Shannon Mattern, & will sign books after the talk! Doors open at 6:30pm with the talk starting closer to 7:00pm. Come early & grab a drink from the P&T Cafe! Tickets & books are available both on eventbrite & at the door. Housekeeping notes: This is a ticketed in-store event with limited amphitheater-style seating.Doors open at 6:30pm, with the talk starting around 7:00pm.Cost of a book bundle ticket reflects the total cost of the feature event book (MSRP plus tax). Each book bundle ticket guarantees ticket holders one (1) copy of the feature event book.The talk will be followed by a book signing. Books signed at P&T Knitwear events must be purchased from P&T Knitwear.If you would like a signed copy & cannot attend the event, we're happy to take your pre-order. We ship most places!About the authors:Lauren Klein is Professor of Data & Decision Sciences & English at Emory University, where she also directs the Digital Humanities Lab & the Atlanta Interdisciplinary AI Network. Her research brings together computational & critical methods to explore questions of gender, race, & justice, both in early America & today. Klein is the author (with Catherine D'Ignazio) of the award-winning Data Feminism (MIT Press, 2020), & the editor (with Matthew K. Gold) of Debates in the Digital Humanities (Univ. of Minnesota Press), among other books & papers. Her next book, Data by Design: Visualization & Power from Abolition to the Dawn of Data Science (MIT Press), will be out in October 2026.  Silas Munro is a designer, artist, writer, curator, surfer, & descendant of the Banyole people of Eastern Uganda. He founded the design studio Polymode, whose clients include MoMA, the MET, Nike, & the Hammer. Munro is the curator & author of Strikethrough: Typographic Messages of Protest at Letterform Archive & the co-curator of Reverberations: Lineages in Design History at the Ford Foundation Gallery. He contributed to W. E. B. Du Bois's Data Portraits: Visualizing Black America, & co-authored the first BIPOC-centered design history course, Black Design in America: African Americans & the African Diaspora in Graphic Design 19th-21st Century. His visual art was recently exhibited at Data Consciousness: Reframing Blackness in Contemporary Print at Print Center New York. Tanvi Sharma is a design technologist working at the intersection of data, aesthetics, & the humanities. She is currently an Art Director at Apple & co-author of Data by Design (MIT Press, 2026). She has previously worked at Pentagram, Public Policy Lab, & Spotify. She lives in Harlem, NY, with her two cats, Yuchi & Bubbles. More at tanvi.network.   About the moderator:Shannon Mattern is the Director of Creative Research at the Metropolitan New York Library Council, a state-founded, member-supported non-profit linking hundreds of libraries & archives across the city. Previously, she held tenured full professorships in media studies, anthropology, & art history at The New School & the University of Pennsylvania. She is the author of four books, the (co-)editor of six collections, & the author of over 100 articles & chapters about urban technology, knowledge infrastructures, maps, maintenance, data art, & other heterogenous subjects. She was the 2025 Kluge Chair in Modern Culture at the Library of Congress & the 2025 Design Indexer in residence at the Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum. You can find her at wordsinspace.net.

events.name: Unmuted  Debate - AI & China
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In July, a Chinese lab you'd probably never heard of published Kimi K3: 2.8 trillion parameters, billed as the largest open model on earth, weights posted free on Hugging Face for anyone to download. It's one of four Chinese labs that spent the last year closing the gap with the American frontier, then giving the result away. Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi. Four of the five most-used open models in the world now come out of Beijing, & American developers are running them inside hospitals, law firms, & startups because they're the cheapest, fastest tools available. No API someone in Washington controls. No off switch. Just download & go. One camp says a model is just math. Open weights run on a consumer's machine, the code is right there to inspect, & cutting Americans off from the best tools on the planet is how you lose a technology race. The other camp says the giveaway is the strategy. China seeds the world's infrastructure with their standards, their defaults, their assumptions, & the dependency follows once switching costs become unbeatable. So: should Americans be allowed to build on Chinese open-weight models or is this the new Cold War's Monkey's Paw? Arguing for, Rob Li is Managing Partner of Amont Partners, a New York global equity firm that invests across the US & Asia. He has spent his career putting capital on both sides of the Pacific, from Yum China to Alibaba deals, & he thinks the country that walls itself off from the best tools available loses. Arguing against, Will McKelvey is a Principal at Lerer Hippeau, one of New York's oldest venture firms, where he backs early-stage founders & spends his days watching for the future of AI, especially in consumer. He got his start by way of a congressional office, & he thinks the cheapest model on the market is the one you pay for slowly. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. events.name: 1st Annual Antitrust Summit
events.description: A global focus on competition law, policy & enforcement comes to New YorkAfter two years of leading the competition debate in London, the Antitrust Summit is crossing the Atlantic. Our London forum brought together more than 385 leading enforcers, economists & corporate executives to discuss the plot twists of modern antitrust law, policy & enforcement. Now, we bring that same rigorous discussion to the US at a particularly consequential moment. The administration in Washington, DC quickly signalled a departure from the neo-Brandeisian period. Dealmaking activity continues to surge. Yet for all the enthusiasm around M&A, the antitrust environment remains unpredictable. Heightened scrutiny of sectors central to the cost of living, increased state intervention in transactions & firms, & a growing role for state attorneys-general in enforcement are contributing to uncertainty. At the same time, AI is reshaping competition & investment dynamics as long-running antitrust cases against technology companies move forward. Against this backdrop, ahead of the November midterm elections, the Antitrust Summit will provide the insights & clarity needed to navigate a changing landscape. Join us in New York on October 28th for the latest edition of our Antitrust Summit series.

events.description: A bigger order can leave you with a smaller margin. That is an ugly way to learn what growth costs. CPG founders will unpack the calls shaping their brands in 2026. Hear what these founders are changing as they finish Q4 & plan for 2027.  Why you should be in this room.Hear which channels moved product & which ate margin. Learn what founders wish they had asked before choosing a co-packer or distributor. Explore where food service & alternative distribution could fit your brand. Hear how founders responded when their customers, markets, or plans changed. Pressure-test your 2027 assumptions against what these founders are seeing in 2026.  What's on the table.Production & partners. Refining the recipe, choosing co-manufacturers, & finding partners who deliver what they promise. Distribution & margin. Where founders are looking beyond familiar shelves to move product. The 2027 calls. Which trends held up, which missed, & what founders are carrying into next year.  Featured speakers.Liv Truesdell - Founder, FROST Buttercream Liv Truesdell started her career in consumer investment banking, working with food & beverage companies, which ultimately led her to launch FROST Buttercream. From naming, logo design, & packaging to pricing architecture & true ICP targeting, Glenn nails how your brand looks, feels, & scales. A former Madison Avenue VP/Creative Director specializing in luxury & bespoke audiences, Glenn is the trusted sounding board founders rely on to turn complex ideas into scalable brand equity. Moderating Ugly Talks for me is about unpacking the messy truths & hard lessons of entrepreneurship-sharing insights in an engaged & entertaining way.  Who's getting in.Food & beverage founders building in crowded categories. Early-stage CPG founders moving from commercial kitchens to co-manufacturing. Operators working through production, distribution, pricing, & margin decisions. Buyers & investors who want to understand what helps a brand move product & stay in business.  About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough "aha!" moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons & insights. With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami, we've built a vibrant community of thousands of founders & industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape. Official Website: UglyTalk.com  Important Notice for Ugly Talk AttendeesAdmission & Confirmation Attendance is by approval only. events.name: An UNMUTED Book Club: The 100 Years War On Palestine
events.description: READING NOT REQUIRED - just be curious! Next up: Rashid Khalidi's The Hundred Years' War on Palestine, the 2020 book that argues the Israeli-Palestinian conflict isn't simply a tragic struggle between two peoples claiming the same land, but a century-long colonial campaign against Palestinians, backed first by Britain & later by the United States. Khalidi, a Palestinian-American historian at Columbia, tells the story through six turning points, beginning with the 1917 Balfour Declaration & moving through the creation of Israel, the wars that followed, & the failures of the peace process. Drawing on historical archives & his own family's experiences, he makes a provocative argument: that Palestinians have never been negotiating on equal terms, & that understanding the conflict as a dispute between two competing national movements obscures the enormous imbalance of power between them. It's a forceful challenge to conventional accounts of Israel's founding, Zionism, & America's role in the region, & one that raises uncomfortable questions about nationalism, colonialism, & self-determination. Show up even if you only got through a chunk. We'll talk about where Khalidi's account is most convincing, where it leaves out important context, whether Zionism is best understood as a colonial movement or a national liberation movement, & what his interpretation of the past means for the possibility of peace today. UNMUTED is a discussion forum for the politically curious. Accessible. Engaging. Social. Open-minded is the name of the game. Join your people.

events.name: Ground Truth: The Live Agents Hackathon
events.description: Every AI model you've ever used is stuck in the past. Ground Truth is a one-day hackathon where you fix that. Join localhost:nyc, The Builder Series & You.com for 10 hours of building AI agents grounded in the live web. Real-time data, deep research, verifiable answers. Come build the kind of agent people would trust with a real decision. Problem StatementEvery LLM is frozen at its training cutoff. It doesn't know what happened this morning, & when it doesn't know, it guesses, confidently. That's the gap between a cool demo & a product people rely on. Your challenge: build an AI agent that knows what's true right now. It searches the live web through the You.com API, reads the sources, reasons over them & shows its receipts. The Challenge TracksLive Wire (real-time agents): agents that wake up when the world changes. Price moves, breaking news, a competitor launch, a policy change, a new job posting. If it happened in the last hour, your agent already knows & already acted. The Analyst (deep research): pick a profession (VCs, lawyers, journalists, recruiters, doctors, policy staffers) & replace its 40-hour research memo with a 4-minute one, every claim cited. Receipts (trust & verification): agents that fact-check claims, catch AI hallucinations, verify sources & show their work. Best Content (open to every team): post about what you built, tag You.com, & win a dedicated prize. What to ExpectA kickoff walkthrough of the You.com API: Search, Contents, Research & the hosted MCP server Free You.com API credits for every builder 6 hours of building Teams of up to 4, or solo if that's your thing Team matching at kickoff if you're coming alone Mentors from You.com on the floor all day Live demos to judges at the end, plus food all day Prizes1st Place Overall: $500 cash Best Content: TBD JudgesTBD Who Should AttendEngineers (full stack, backend, AI/ML) Founders & aspiring founders building with AI Designers & product people who want to ship something real Researchers & analysts who know exactly what a great research agent should do You don't need a finished idea. events.name: PMAI: Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Sales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. - Bring a computer. You're writing three things tonight.- Most founders can get meetings. The deals die after meeting one.- You'll leave with your buyer in one sentence, a cold email written to a real person, & five questions for your next call. About Farzad, the speaker Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding & generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.description: October 2026 | In-Person at Pier 57 (Livestream TBA)Hype vs. Reality: An AI Debunk Night Every week there's a new AI headline designed to make your heart race. "700 agents went rogue." "AI just crossed the terrifying line." "Your job is next." This month, we're slowing down & reading the receipts. No outside food allowed. events.name: Powering The Transition - Closing Skills Gap In New Energy Infrastructure
events.description: In partnership with Schneider Electric, Google, Barclays, LACI & IYF The energy transition is underway - but the workforce needed to deliver it is not keeping pace. Across the full arc of how energy is generated, moved, stored, serviced, & used - spanning utilities, power generation, advanced manufacturing, fleet electrification, data centers, & industrial infrastructure - a persistent & structural challenge has emerged: the skilled trades & technician roles most critical to new energy infrastructure face serious & growing skills gaps, & too often the employers, training providers, & talent leaders working to close them are doing so in isolation. NationSwell, in partnership with Barclays, LACI, IYF, Schneider Electric, & Google is convening a working session at Brooklyn Army Terminal - home to BATWorks, NYC's emerging climate innovation hub - to change that. Bringing together talent leaders, hiring managers, & workforce training providers, this in-person convening will use IYF's proven industry competency framework to surface & validate the most critical skills gaps across the skilled trades workforce driving new energy infrastructure.  The day will move from insight to action. The goal is a shared vocabulary & shared priorities that attendees can take back to their organizations, & use to advocate for the training investments, certifications, & systems changes the new energy infrastructure demands. BATWorks offers a uniquely fitting backdrop: a place where growth-stage climate companies, workforce development, & hands-on innovation converge. Where employers are growing & talent supply can grow with them. Attendees will leave knowing they are not alone in this challenge - & with concrete, validated priorities to guide the next steps.
