events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Plan Your Best Year With AI
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back  In Person at SalesforceWe're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City and sponsored by Boldforce.This Month We Present...Plan Your Best Year With AIJoin the community for an interactive planning session to reflect on the past year, identify your biggest opportunities, and build an AI-powered roadmap for the year ahead.Before we rush into a new year with another list of goals, lets get clear about what were actually building.What worked this year? What didnt? What deserves more of your energy? And where could AI help you turn those intentions into action?For our final AI & The Culture meetup of the year, were bringing the community together for an interactive planning and reflection session designed to help you look back, think forward, and build a roadmap for what comes next.This isnt about asking AI to magically plan your life. Its about using these tools as thought partnersto help you reflect, uncover patterns, explore possibilities, make decisions, and turn big ambitions into actionable next steps.Together well explore: How to use AI to reflect on your wins, lessons, challenges, and unfinished business from the past year Prompts that help you identify opportunities you might be overlooking How to turn big goals into realistic projects, milestones, and next steps Ways to use AI as a strategic thought partner for your creative work, career, business, or personal projects How to identify where AI and automation can give you back time in the year ahead Building a personalized AI-powered roadmap you can actually use after you leave the roomAnd because this is AI & The Culture, were making space for something AI cant replace: community.Youll have an opportunity to reflect alongside other creatives, founders, educators, artists, technologists, and curious mindsto exchange ideas, share what youre building, and potentially meet the people who can help you move it forward.The goal isnt to leave with 47 resolutions.Its to leave with clarity, priorities, and a plan.Who Should Attend? Creators and content makers Filmmakers, writers, artists, and storytellers Educators and community builders Entrepreneurs, founders, and solopreneurs Marketers, strategists, and creative professionals Technologists and AI enthusiasts Anyone ready to be more intentional about what theyre building nextWhether you already have your next year mapped out or youre still staring at a blank page wondering where to begin, youre welcome here.Come Ready to BuildThis one is especially hands-on, so come prepared to participate. Bring your laptop Bring a notebook or something to write with Bring a few goals, ideas, or questions youve been thinking about for the year ahead Bring your curiosity and a willingness to shareWell be working through reflection exercises, AI prompts, and planning activities togetherso you can leave with the beginnings of a roadmap, not just another page of notes.Come ready to reflect. Come ready to plan. Come ready to build.About AI & The CultureAI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, and culture.Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams and King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, and culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, and community.Were building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI.This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture  grounded in community, focused on real-world use, and centered on learning together in the room.Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Lets build  together. About Your HostsShirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, and co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, and creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, and real-world execution.About King WilloniusKing Willonius is a creative technologist and cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, and creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, and community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable and useful  especially for creatives and innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm. Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio)#AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: Vibecoding 101
events.description: A 4-week scaffolded, hands-on introduction to vibecoding for beginners.Vibecoding, or AI-assisted software development, is the practice of guiding coding agents to translate your ideas into working software - without writing code yourself. We see vibecoding as 4 different product skills in a trench coat. While they may not write code, effective vibecoders mobilize concepts & workflows across software engineering, design, quality assurance, & product management. This course is a scaffolded, hands-on introduction to the fundamental skills & concepts required for a sustainable vibecoding practice. Students will learn through a combination of short lectures, applied exercises, personalized feedback, & demos to peers. We begin by working with coding agents in a multiplayer environment designed for beginners. We will create interactive frontends, learn the basics of the terminal, build integrations with APIs, & create stateful, full-stack applications with a database & user authentication. By the end of the course, students will transition to state-of-the-art coding agents installed on their personal machines, which they will use to build & deploy a working prototype to the web. SyllabusSession 1: Coding agents & frontends We introduce the course & core concepts of vibecoding. We introduce a basic taxonomy of web architecture. Students practice creating basic interactive frontends. Session 2: CLIs, APIs, & the terminal We cover core backend & data concepts. We gently introduce the terminal. Students practice writing simple CLI programs, & integrating with an API. Session 3: Stateful full-stack applications We cover databases & user authentication; students build a full stack app. Session 4: Deployment & demos The final session covers deployment. Students demo their prototypes for the class. Learning OutcomesAcquire core vocabulary & mental models for software development. Prompt coding agents to create frontends, API integrations, & stateful applications. Be able to translate your ideas into working prototypes using AI. Practice presenting your product ideas to peers & colleagues. ResourcesThis new world of ours rewards being a dilettante with a vague mental map of vast territories.- Ted Underwood There is a new kind of coding I call vibecoding,' where you fully give in to the vibes, embrace exponentials, & forget that the code even exists. It's possible because the LLMs (e.g. Cursor Composer w Sonnet) are getting too good it's not really coding - I just see stuff, say stuff, run stuff, & copy paste stuff, & it mostly works.- Andrej Karpathy Slow is smooth, & smooth is fast.- Anonymous ScholarshipIndex scholarships are designed to benefit members of our community who do not have expendable cash to pay for the course, & those for whom the class price is not accessible. These need-based scholarships will go to the candidates who best demonstrate why they should be chosen for the free spot to our class based on the following criteria: Belong to groups that are traditionally underrepresented in the graphic design & creative industries Do not have jobs that would pay for these courses as professional development Cannot independently afford the class at list price Share our value of intentional community The number of selected applicants chosen is subject to the discretion of Index & the instructor, but every course will select at least one. Apply for a scholarship here. Applications close October 20th. Instructor Bio Bill Roberts is an independent technologist based in Brooklyn. Drawn to socially beneficial uses of technology, he has 10 years of software engineering experience on teams spanning healthcare, climate, politics, & education. He runs Legible Labs, a product studio that helps clients design & build AI applications. As a research engineer, he has coauthored papers in peer-reviewed journals & conferences that empirically evaluate the capabilities of AI in educational settings. Bill holds a BA in Computer Science & Sociology from Columbia University.   Refunds We get that things come up, but we rely on headcounts to make our programs viable. If you request a refund... More than 4 weeks before the program begins  100% refundMore than 2 weeks before the program begins  50% refundFewer than 2 weeks before the program begins  No refund Thanks for understanding & for supporting our ability to provide cool offerings through your purchase. Media Release Clause By attending this event, you consent to being photographed, filmed, or recorded, & grant Index Space permission to use this content for promotional or informational purposes.

events.name: GILD AI Forum: AI & Engineering Leaders Dinner
events.description: This GILD AI Forum brings together CTOs, VPs of Engineering, Heads of AI, & senior technical leaders for candid conversations about building, scaling, & implementing AI inside their companies. This isn't a conference. It's not a panel. It's a small, curated room of technical leaders sharing what's actually working, what's not, & the real challenges of shipping AI in the AI era. Each Forum opens with a Conversation Starter, a practitioner sharing what their team is building with AI, followed by open Q&A. From there, the room breaks into intimate discussions where everyone has a seat at the table. Every attendee brings their own experience. Every attendee contributes. No pitches. No performative networking. Just senior technical leaders being honest about the architectures they're choosing, the tradeoffs they're making, & what they wish they'd figured out sooner. TRENDING THEMES FOR THIS SESSION Conversations at the Forum are shaped by what technical leaders bring to the table. Themes likely to surface this evening include: From AI pilots to AI in production: breaking out of the proof-of-concept trap & scaling agents into real workflows Connecting AI to legacy systems: architectural patterns for integrating modern AI with 20-year-old stacks without breaking everything The AI tooling budget problem: balancing experimentation with unsustainable spend as engineers blow through AI tool budgets Engineers as curators, not creators: the shift from writing code to orchestrating AI agents, reusable components, & external services MCP, multi-agent systems, & the orchestration layer: what's working, what's overhyped, & what technical leaders are actually building Guardrails & governance for AI-generated code: who's accountable when the AI writes it, & what review processes actually hold up in production Presented in partnership with Tecla Tecla gives companies flexible access to vetted talent across the US & Latin America, developed for AI-native work & available from fractional engagements to dedicated nearshore pods. Learn more at www.tecla.io THE FORMAT Intentionally small & highly curated, 20 to 25 max. A seated round-table dinner, private & off the record under Chatham House Rules. AGENDA 6:00 - 6:30 PM  Cocktails & passed appetizers 6:30 - 7:00 PM  Dinner is served Find a seat & get comfortable. 6:45 - 6:50 PM  GILD & Partner Welcome A few words from the GILD team & our partners on what the night holds & how we'll spend it together. 6:50 - 7:00 PM  Conversation Starter A fellow engineering leader opens the discussion with a candid perspective on AI, with a brief Q&A. 7:00 - 8:00 PM  Table discussions 8:00 - 8:30 PM  Open mingling WHO THIS IS FOR Founders  CEOs  CTOs  VPs of Engineering  Heads of AI  Technical Leaders  Product Leaders This session is for leaders responsible for building, deploying, & maintaining AI systems in production. Chatham House Rules apply. Discussion stays private.

events.name: Six Math Essentials w/ Terence Tao
events.description: Book Launch & Conversation with Janna Levin Widely regarded as the world's greatest living mathematician, Fields Medalist Terence Tao approaches mathematics as a sublime art-a quiet, rigorous effort to map the hidden scaffolding of reality. To mark the publication of his first popular book, Six Math Essentials, join us for an evening with Tao in conversation with Pioneer Works Director of Sciences Janna Levin. Tracing the central pillars of his book-from algebra as abstraction & geometry beyond sight, to navigating uncertainty & the mathematics of change-they will reveal math not as obscure magic, but as a deeply creative, interconnected way of thinking. Often referred to as the Mozart of mathematics, Tao will also explore how AI is transforming his own practice, the frontier of research, & our collective future. Together, we will consider what becomes of human intuition & creativity when the tools of thought are no longer uniquely human-and whether the true beauty of math lies not in the answers we find, but in the human mind reaching for them. Tao will sign copies of Six Math Essentials following the conversation, with books available for purchase on site. (Unable to attend? Order a signed copy here.) Please note that seating is limited & will be available on a first-come, first-served basis.   About the speakersTerence Tao is an Australian-American professor of mathematics at UCLA whose work focuses primarily on harmonic analysis, partial differential equations, combinatorics, & analytic number theory. The recipient of a Fields Medal, a MacArthur Genius Grant, & a Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics, among many other accolades, he is one of the most decorated & prolific mathematicians working today. Tao is the author of several academic books including Solving Mathematical Problems: A Personal Perspective & Additive Combinatorics, as well as his first popular math book, Six Math Essentials. He lives in Los Angeles. Janna Levin is the Claire Tow Professor of physics & astronomy at Barnard College of Columbia University. A Guggenheim Fellow, she has contributed to our understanding of black holes, extra dimensions, & cosmology. She is the founding director of sciences at Pioneer Works & the founding editor-in-chief of the magazine Pioneer Works Broadcast. She often contributes to news, documentaries, & radio, including as the presenter of the NOVA feature Black Hole Apocalypse on PBS & as a contributor to CBS, CNN, BBC, & NBC. She has authored books on black holes & the universe-Black Hole Blues, How the Universe Got its Spots, & Black Hole Survival Guide-as well as a PEN award-winning novel, A Madman Dreams of Turing Machines. You can find her current writings in Higher Dimensions. This program is funded by the Simons Foundation International & administered by the Simons Foundation's Science, Society & Culture division.

events.description: Overdrive AIHosted by TechUnited:NJ, creators of Propelify, heralded by Forbes as the "SXSW of the Northeast," OverdriveAI is back, & this year it's a debate. The hottest topics in AI, argued live, both sides on stage. Jobs, energy, education, & more. Sharp thinkers go head to head, you hear the case for & against, & you decide where you land. Taking place this year at the Newark Museum of Art, where tech & culture share a roof, OverdriveAI brings together founders, operators, investors, & researchers from across the Northeast for a day built around one idea: the biggest questions in AI don't have easy answers, so let's actually argue about them. TICKETS ARE NOW LIVE!EXPLORE THE FULL OVERDRIVEAI EXPERIENCE Community AI TrainingHands-on morning AI training at EqualSpace designed for all experience levels. No prior AI experience required. Reserve Your Spot Executive AI TrainingA focused, practical AI training designed for executives & business leaders ready to better understand & apply AI within their organizations. Reserve Your Spot Pitch Roast LiveStartups pitch. Comedians roast. Everyone wins. Close out OverdriveAI with an evening of bold ideas, founder pitches, comedy, & connection. Reserve Your Spot   What to Expect Community AI Training A hands-on morning (10a-12p ET) AI training at EqualSpace designed for all experience levels. Come ready to learn, explore, & put AI into practice. No prior experience required. Executive AI Training Turn AI into practical business advantage. Start your morning with a focused AI training session designed for executives, business leaders, & decision-makers navigating the rapidly evolving AI landscape. This interactive session will explore practical ways leaders can better understand, evaluate, & apply AI within their organizations helping you move from conversation to action. The AI Debates The main event at the Newark Museum of Art. Will AI take your job or grow the economy? Who pays for AI's energy appetite? Does AI belong in the classroom? Can you still trust what you see? Startup demos will be featured between rounds & the afternoon will roll into TechUnited:NJ Birthday Party! Final topics & speakers are still being locked in, ticket holders hear every name first. Here's what's on the table so far: AI takes jobs vs. AI grows the economy - does automation erase more work than it creates? Is AI raising your energy bill? - the data center buildout is reshaping the grid, & New Jersey's in the middle of it. Does AI belong in the classroom? - a tutor for every student, or the end of learning how to think? Is it time for universal basic income? - if productivity keeps compounding, someone decides where the gains go. Can we handle deepfakes? - synthetic media's getting cheap & convincing, what's the real defense? Got a debate we missed? Suggest it, & if it makes the stage, you'll know it was yours. Live debates. Experts, opposing sides of one question, no hedging.Hot takes. Short, sharp presentations from speakers with a strong point of view.Networking. 300+ founders, researchers, & investors in one room, this year in a new venue built for it. Pitch Roast Live Closing the night at Newark Culture Club Close with startup pitches & a high-energy evening experience. Four founders pitch, three comedians & two investors roast. One walks out a winner! Last Year, at Nokia Bell Labs Speakers joined us from OpenAI, IBM, CoreWeave, Verizon, Perplexity, Nokia Bell Labs, BetterFutureLabs, NJEDA, & the NJ AI Hub. 16 speakers, 300+ attendees, a packed house. This year's lineup is coming together now, & it's bigger. OverdriveAI is one of many events TechUnited:NJ runs for its 13,000+ member community, from AI Demo Night to Propelify. Inquire about membership to hear about what's next. TechUnited:NJ members receive complimentary admission to OverdriveAI as part of their membership. Not a member yet? events.name: AI Founders Supper Club

It has since grown to a global community of 20,000 AI founders, operators & researchers & has since organized events in 4 countries & 7 cities including NYC, London, Paris, Dubai, Boston, DC, & Philly. Fidelity Private Shares brings certainty to startup founders with their cap table platform to help automate equity management operations & financings in a single collaborative hub. Whether it be in connection with a Series A capital raise, a later-stage VC or PE firm investment, leading up to, during & subsequent to an IPO, PwC's ECS practice is uniquely positioned to be with you every step of the way, helping you achieve your business goals while minimizing risk. Niural is an AI-native, end-to-end HR & finance platform transforming global payroll, PEO, & compliance. Powered by EMMA, our intelligent AI coworker, Niural brings payroll, HR, & finance into a single, streamlined ecosystem. We make global operations smarter, faster, & more efficient. Ramp is an all-in-one financial operations platform designed to save businesses time & money. Combining corporate cards, expense management, bill payments, accounting automation, procurement, travel, treasury, & more, Ramp empowers finance teams to do their best work. More than 70,000 companies, from family-owned farms to space startups, have saved $10B & 27.5M hours with Ramp since its founding in 2019. Investors include Founders Fund, Thrive Capital, Khosla Ventures, Sequoia, Greylock, Stripe, Goldman Sachs, Coatue, & Redpoint, as well as over 100 angel investors who were founders or executives of leading companies.

events.name: Creator Economy Hack
events.description: Creators are the fastest-growing small businesses on the internet, & most of them still run on spreadsheets, DMs & vibes. Come build the tools that fix that. Join GenZtea & localhost:nyc for a one-day, in-person hackathon where builders & creators team up to ship AI products for the creator economy, powered by You.com's real-time web search APIs. Problem StatementEvery creator is a one-person media company: researcher, writer, editor, marketer & sales team. The tools haven't caught up. Build an AI product that helps creators make better content, grow faster, or get paid, using You.com to ground it in what's happening on the internet right now. The Challenge ThemeIdea to Post: turn a voice note, a messy idea or a link into a post, script or thread, informed by what's trending right now Trend Radar: spot what's about to blow up in a niche & tell creators what to make before everyone else Creator Business: brand deal finders, sponsor pitch writers, rate card builders, media kits that write themselves Research Desk: research agents for video essays, podcasts & newsletters, with real citations so creators never post something false Anything else that helps creators make, grow or get paid What to ExpectA kickoff demo on building with the You.com APIs (search, research & live web context for your app) 6 hours of high-energy building Builder + creator teams: creators from the GenZtea community join teams, bring real problems & test your product live Teams of 2 to 4, or come solo & we'll match you Food, drinks & good energy all day Live demos at the end in front of creators & investors. Prizes  1st Place: $500 cash More prizes & You.com API credits to be announced To qualify, every project must use the You.com API, live in a public GitHub repo, & be shared in a demo post on LinkedIn or X tagging You.com, localhost:nyc & GenZtea. JudgesTBD Who Should AttendCreators who want to build the tools they wish they had Engineers (full stack, backend, frontend, AI) Founders & aspiring founders in media, consumer & creator tools Designers & product people who ship fast Anyone curious, ambitious & hands-on You don't need a finished idea. Just show up ready to build. SponsorsYou.com is the leading AI search infrastructure - built for developers. Our APIs let you build intelligent agents & applications that use live, factual data from the web, news, & research, in real time. With just a few lines of code, you can power your LLMs with up-to-date, citation-backed results instead of static training data. [More sponsors to be announced. Want to sponsor? Email somyag00@gmail.com] Hostslocalhost:nyc: Making NYC the biggest startup ecosystem in the world. GenZtea: A community for Gen Z founders, creators & investors.

events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back - In Person at Salesforce We're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City & sponsored by Boldforce. This Month We Present...Build Your Creative Operating SystemBuild a personalized AI workflow that supports your entire creative process-from capturing ideas to publishing finished work-so you're never starting from scratch. Most of us don't have an idea problem. We have a system problem. Ideas live in our Notes app. Research is scattered across browser tabs. Drafts are hiding in Google Docs. Inspiration gets screenshotted & forgotten. And every new project somehow feels like we're starting all over again. What if your creative process actually remembered how you work? At this month's AI & The Culture meetup, we're exploring how to build your own Creative Operating System-a personalized workflow that uses AI to help you capture ideas, organize knowledge, research, create, refine, & publish your work. Instead of collecting more AI tools, we'll focus on connecting the ones that actually support your process. Together we'll explore:  How to map your creative process from idea to finished work  Ways to capture & organize ideas so they don't disappear into the digital abyss  How AI can help you research, brainstorm, draft, edit, & refine your work  Building a personal knowledge base that makes past ideas & research useful again  How to connect AI tools into repeatable workflows instead of using them one at a time  Where automation can save time-and where your human judgment should stay firmly in the driver's seat  How to create a system that gets smarter & more useful the more you use it The goal isn't to automate your creativity. It's to build the infrastructure around your creativity so you have more time & energy for the work only you can do. Expect a welcoming room filled with creators, technologists, educators, founders, artists, & curious minds ready to rethink how we organize & support our creative lives. Who Should Attend?  Creators & content makers  Filmmakers, writers, artists, & storytellers  Educators & community builders  Entrepreneurs, founders, & solopreneurs  Marketers, strategists, & creative professionals  Technologists & AI enthusiasts  Anyone with too many ideas, too many tabs, & not enough systems  Whether your creative process is already organized or currently held together by screenshots, open tabs, & vibes, you're welcome here. Come Ready to Build This won't be a sit-back-and-scroll kind of evening. Bring your laptop, something to write with, & a mindset ready to learn, experiment, & share. We'll be exploring ideas, tools, & workflows you can begin applying to your own creative process.  Bring your laptop  Bring a notebook or something to take notes with  Bring your curiosity & questions Come ready to learn. Come ready to contribute. Come ready to build. About AI & The Culture AI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, & culture. Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams & King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, & culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, & community. We're building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI. This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture - grounded in community, focused on real-world use, & centered on learning together in the room. Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Let's build - together.  About Your Hosts Shirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, & co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, & creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, & real-world execution. About King Willonius King Willonius is a creative technologist & cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, & creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, & community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable & useful - especially for creatives & innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm.  Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio) #AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: AI Content System
events.description: Time Rich presents a working session, hosted by Ella Molony Cook, with co-hosting partner Wispr Flow & presenting partner Stanley. It opens with a short panel on why trust + distribution is now your moat. Then you build your content system in three parts: capture, context, create. You schedule your posts before you leave, so next week is handled. Every guest gets six months of Wispr Pro & Stanley. WHO IT'S FORFounders, business owners & investors who post in bursts, or know they should post more, & want content that sounds like them without writing every word. THE PANEL: YOUR MOAT IS YOUR DISTRIBUTIONA short conversation with investors, founders & ex-Google/YouTube on why visibility, trust & authority matter more than ever. WHAT GETS BUILTCapture. You'll set up Wispr Flow & brief your agent by voice instead of typing. Your best ideas sit in voice notes that never turn into posts, because nothing keeps running when you're busy. Your calls, voice notes & talks become raw material, & we pull ten stories out of your own words.Context. A tone of voice brief, the words you never use, & a call to action matched to each story.Create. Content agents that draft, repurpose across platforms & schedule. By the end, a week of posts is scheduled & the system is set up to fill the next one. Rather have it built for you? The Stanley team will be in the room. Just ask. WHAT TO BRING Laptop, charger & phone. Setup runs on iMessage or WhatsApp. One recording: a talk, a podcast, a call or a voice note Your three best published posts The one thing you want every post to drive: a booked call, a newsletter sign-up or a product AGENDA6:00-6:30 PM  Doors open, meet other founders6:30-6:35 PM  Welcome from Ella6:35-6:55 PM  Panel: your moat is your distribution6:55-8:20 PM  The build: capture, context, create8:20-9:00 PM  Q&A, drinks & mingling POWERED BY STANLEYStanley is an AI Head of Content. You text it a voice note, it drafts in your voice, & it repurposes whatever already performed. Stanley is our presenting partner for the night, so everyone builds on it live. OUR PARTNERTime Rich runs on voice, powered by Wispr FlowWispr Flow is our co-hosting partner. You'll talk to your agents instead of typing to them, & every guest leaves with six months of Wispr Pro. THE ROOMElla Molony Cook is an Australian 4x founder with 1 exit & an investor in Anthropic. Founder of Time Rich a media & AI education platform. Has a community of over 63K+ subscribers on Substack filled with founders, SMBs, angel investors, leaders & has hosted 250+ founder & investor experiences. Max Rivera is an angel investor & GP at GHOST Angels, a fund of Snapchat alumni backing early-stage consumer AI startups. He led global partnerships at Snap from pre-IPO to a $120B public company. Today he leads partnerships for Microsoft AI. Aishwarya Balaji is a 2x founder, venture fund advisor, investor & global speaker. She has spotted & built for emerging markets again & again, from ed-tech & Web3 to non-alc & the creator economy. Rodolphe Kdderitzsch is on the Stanley team. He's ex-Google/YouTube & Squarespace, & a startup founder. TIME RICH CLUBWhere founders, creators & investors come to invest in themselves, their relationships, & building a system to become Time Rich. Whether you're building a company, backing your next deal, or just getting started, this is where you do it alongside people who are building too. Inside the Club: Private conversations on investing, entrepreneurship, building your brand, time hacks & running your life on AI Fireside chats with family offices, exited founders & thought leaders A network of founders, creators & investors who build companies & allocate capital Seats are limited & we read every application.

events.name: Daytona AI Builders
events.description: An event dedicated to exploring all things AI Engineering! Event partners: AWS & Antimetal Agenda 5:30 pm - 6:00 pmWelcome Gathering & Opening Remarks Marijan Cipcic, Principal Events Manager at Daytona  6:00 pm - 6:15 pmTalk "Forkable Sandboxes for Long-Running Agents" Muhammad Annas Hashmi, DevRel at Daytona Outline:Agents are starting to do real software work: installing dependencies, editing files, running tests, starting servers, & debugging over long sessions. But most AI systems still treat each run like a disposable prompt-response loop. That breaks down once the useful state lives not just in tokens, but in the actual machine. This talk is about the runtime layer agents need to become reliable builders. I'll show how forkable Daytona sandboxes let you pause at important moments in an agent run, branch the environment, & sample multiple continuations from the same machine state. For builders, this turns long-running agent workflows into something you can inspect, compare, recover, & eventually optimize.  6:15 pm - 6:30 pmTalk "Multi-Agent Investment AI Assistant built on Amazon Bedrock Agentcore" Sam Farber, Sr. Solutions Architect at AWS Outline:Investment research teams spend days manually gathering data across markets, risk metrics, sentiment indicators, financial statements, & alternative data sources before synthesizing findings into actionable reports. This talk will show how a multi-agent AI system can automate that workflow. A supervisor agent breaks down a research question, delegates to 10 domain-specific specialists running in parallel, & compiles their findings into a comprehensive investment report. The system maintains conversation memory across each agent, allowing researchers to have targeted conversations & follow-ups with each specialized agent.  6:30 pm - 6:45 pmTalk "Building a World Model for Production Agents" Shreyas Iyer, Co-founder & CTO of Antimetal Outline:Production systems are increasingly complex, with critical knowledge scattered across code, infrastructure, telemetry, & people's heads. In this talk, we'll explore how to build a persistent world model that gives AI agents a shared understanding of production. We'll break down four foundational layers: physical topology, temporal changes, causal relationships, & organizational context to show how they enable agents to investigate incidents, assess changes, & proactively manage production, building on what they've learned across tasks.  6:45 pm - 6:55 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker TBA Outline:TBA  6:55 pm - 7:05 pmTalk "Letting AI agents use credentials they never see" Chase Erickson, Solutions Engineer at Infisical Outline:Infisical manages the secrets your Daytona agents depend on. The Daytona secret sync pushes them from Infisical to your Daytona organization & keeps them current, rotations included. Infisical's Agent Vault, a proxy, adds the credential to requests bound for the services you configure, so the agent never sees it. In this talk, we'll show how an agent in a Daytona sandbox calls an API without ever holding the secret.  7:05 pm - 8:30 pmNetworkingWith pizzas & beverages About event This is dynamic gathering for AI enthusiasts, innovators, & professionals to collaborate, share ideas, & explore the latest advancements in artificial intelligence. Whether you're building AI products, researching cutting-edge algorithms, or simply passionate about the field, join us to connect, learn, & drive the future of AI forward.

events.name: Health2Tech - MedTech Edition
events.description: Health2Tech - a series of digital health events.Join us on November 5th for an exclusive gathering that brings together the brightest minds in the digital health space. Hosted by Bailey Morgan, Audrey Guazzone, Maria Putilina & Alex Koshykov, this evening promises to be a confluence of innovation, inspiration, & invaluable networking.  Important!  To keep this session highly focused, priority will be given to MedTech experts, device founders, bioengineers, clinicians, & specialized investors. If you work outside the MedTech space, we appreciate your understanding - we'll review your application & confirm attendance based on remaining capacity.  Want to Showcase Your Medical Device Live?If you are building a medical device or physical HealthTech product, we have live demo spots available to feature your innovation in front of NYC investors, healthcare leaders, & potential partners. How to apply: Fill out the form - Open Google Form Register on this Luma page. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, so please apply early!  Event Schedule: 5:30 PM - 6:00 Doors Open. Begin the evening with a warm welcome & a chance to settle in. 6:00 - 6:45 Panel on: "What Makes a MedTech Company Investable?". 6:45 - 8:30 Networking. Connect, converse, & collaborate with peers driven by a common passion for advancing healthcare through technology.  About our Panelists: Steven Levy Steven is a Partner at Unorthodox Ventures where he focuses on investing in venture stage MedTech companies. Before joining Unorthodox Ventures, Steven worked for the prior 23 years as an investment banker, having held senior roles at Lehman Brothers, Stifel Financial & Cowen & Co. Steven has executed over 100 transactions with aggregate deal value in excess of $30 billion. Steven headed the M&A efforts for the Financial Sponsors practice at Lehman Brothers, covered Financial sponsors & headed the Consumer M&A efforts at Cowen & covered Financial Sponsors, led execution on technology & consumer M&A transactions & headed up the firm's investment banking efforts in Israel at Stifel. Steven received his B.A. from Binghamton University & graduated as a member of Phi Beta Kappa & received his M.B.A. from the Wharton School, at the University of Pennsylvania. Bryan Spielman is a Managing Partner at Northwell Health Equity Partners. He is a seasoned C-suite executive with a track record of driving multi-billion-dollar value creation across the healthcare & technology sectors. Most recently, as Chief Growth Officer at Advarra, he spearheaded the company's $5 billion sale to Blackstone & CPPIB. Prior to that, at Medidata, he helped scale the company from a $400 million to over $2.3 billion market valuation. events.name: AI Build Lab For Founders: Discover
events.description: Take your idea from concept to launch in a series of interactive sessions. Leverage AI tools to build a live product, put it in front of users, & leave with honest feedback, concrete next steps, & the tools to keep going - no coding background required. Who it is forCurrent NYU students, Alumni, & Faculty People who code & people who don't. Anyone who wants to test an idea quickly & cheaply before committing time & money to it. Key highlightsHands-on from start to finish. Every session ends with something real in hand, not just notes. Real customers, not guesses. Founders talk to 5 to 10 potential users & put a working product in front of them. Two tracks. No-code founders build with tools like Lovable, Replit, v0 & Bolt. Founders who code use Claude Code or Cursor. Honest checks built in. Founders open & verify every source, set their success target before the results come in, & have a second tool test every build. A live product with a real ask. Each product goes live with a waitlist, pre-order or booking option. Demo day. The series ends with founders presenting to guest founders & investors. Tools they keep. Every founder leaves with the full Leverage kit & their own working setup. What founders walk away withA tested idea. Assumptions checked against real conversations & real data. A live product MVP. Reviewed, tested, & in front of first users, or a clear & cheap "no." A decision & a plan. Continue, change, or stop, backed by evidence, with the next 14-day test written out. Their own working toolkit. Research, idea testing, building & review tools, set up & ready to use. The Leverage kit. Every prompt & tool used in the series. Good habits. Check the sources. Set the target first. Never let the builder grade its own work. A cohort. A group of founders who built alongside them. Session 1: DiscoverValidate the problem before writing a single line of code. Turn your idea into clear hypotheses around target users, existing workarounds, & willingness to pay. Use AI to mine real customer complaints across online forums, fact-check the findings, stress-test your concept against multiple AI models, & draft your customer interview plan. PARTICIPANTS LEAVE WITH Written assumptions about the customer, problem, & willingness to pay A problem report with sources they checked themselves The three riskiest assumptions An interview script A list of 20 people to talk to, with 5 messages already sent BETWEEN SESSIONS Founders interview 5 to 10 potential users & sort what they hear into evidence for or against each assumption.

events.name: Startup Networking Founders, Investors & Talent Mixer
events.description: New York Startup Networking Event. Meet Founders, Investors, & Talent - Build or Scale Your Startup  Bring a business question to the room Meet founders, entrepreneurs, builders, operators & investors at Ascent Valley's NYC mixer. Talk through business decisions & meet people you could work with. Locals & visitors are equally welcome. Bring a question about finding customers, building your team or growing your business. Share what you're working on & hear how others approach similar challenges. Join small-group discussions before the pitches, then hear company representatives present their businesses. There's time for open networking to get to know each other & explore where you could help one another. Who you'll meet Founders & entrepreneurs starting or growing a business, working through decisions you may be facing too.Builders turning ideas into products & services, including developers & designers.Operators with experience in product, growth, marketing, sales & running teams.Investors interested in understanding a business by meeting the people behind it.  Why This Event Is Different Compare customer acquisition approaches with another entrepreneur, discuss a product decision with a builder or hear how an investor looks at a business. Smaller discussions give you time to ask follow-up questions & understand each other's work. When you find a reason to stay in touch, you can continue the conversation through Ascent Valley after the evening. What to Expect Product & growth: discuss finding customers, product decisions & growing a business. Talent & hiring: meet builders & operators, talk about team needs & explore working together. Fundraising: share what you've learned about preparing a pitch & raising capital. Company pitches: discover what other companies are building & ask their representatives questions. Want to Pitch? Present your company to the room & walk guests through your pitch deck, followed by a short Q&A. Our team reviews applications & confirms speaking slots in advance. Your application creates a public company profile in our Startup Directory. After the event, your company's details enter our private company database for investor matching. With your consent, your company can also be featured in our Weekly Founder Digest. Our team arranges introductions when both sides want to connect.

events.name: AI Build Lab For Founders: Build
events.description: Take your idea from concept to launch in a series of interactive sessions. Leverage AI tools to build a live product, put it in front of users, & leave with honest feedback, concrete next steps, & the tools to keep going - no coding background required. Who it is forCurrent NYU students, Alumni, & Faculty People who code & people who don't. Anyone who wants to test an idea quickly & cheaply before committing time & money to it. Key highlightsHands-on from start to finish. Every session ends with something real in hand, not just notes. Real customers, not guesses. Founders talk to 5 to 10 potential users & put a working product in front of them. Two tracks. No-code founders build with tools like Lovable, Replit, v0 & Bolt. Founders who code use Claude Code or Cursor. Honest checks built in. Founders open & verify every source, set their success target before the results come in, & have a second tool test every build. A live product with a real ask. Each product goes live with a waitlist, pre-order or booking option. Demo day. The series ends with founders presenting to guest founders & investors. Tools they keep. Every founder leaves with the full Leverage kit & their own working setup. What founders walk away withA tested idea. Assumptions checked against real conversations & real data. A live product MVP. Reviewed, tested, & in front of first users, or a clear & cheap "no." A decision & a plan. Continue, change, or stop, backed by evidence, with the next 14-day test written out. Their own working toolkit. Research, idea testing, building & review tools, set up & ready to use. The Leverage kit. Every prompt & tool used in the series. Good habits. Check the sources. Set the target first. Never let the builder grade its own work. A cohort. A group of founders who built alongside them. Session 2: BuildMove from validation to a working product. Founders write a focused one-page plan based on customer interviews, building exclusively to test their biggest assumption. An AI verification tool tests the build against the plan before launch, followed by rapid 60-second live demos & peer critiques. PARTICIPANTS LEAVE WITH A live product at a link A real ask on it: waitlist, pre-order or booking A build reviewed & tested independently BETWEEN SESSIONS Founders share the link with everyone they interviewed & post it where their users gather. They track visits, signups, return use & payments.

events.name: Borderless Office - Identity & Access In World Of Remote-First Growth
events.description: Join Antoine Jebara (Co-founder, JumpCloud) & Noah Landow (Founder & CEO, Macktez) for an informal conversation between an expert on scaling global technology companies & the evolution of identity & access management & the founder of a technology consulting firm. In an era defined by remote work & the rapid rise of agentic AI, the concepts of identity & security are shifting beneath our feet. As AI agents begin to act on our behalf, how do we maintain control, responsibility, & security? If an AI agent executes a transaction or accesses a database, who is truly holding the keys? Antoine brings a unique perspective from the front lines of this transition, from pioneering decentralized 2FA & password management at MYKI to driving global strategy & partner ecosystems at JumpCloud. Join us at the Macktez office, after work, over light snacks & sips, for an exploratory conversation on the challenges of scaling fast-growing global companies & how different security architectures impact our long-term safety in a cloud-first world. We will dive into the shifting landscape of encryption, the unique hurdles of managing remote-first organizations, & what it truly means to "identity" ourselves in the age of AI. Photography, audio, & video recording may occur at this event & by attending you consent to such recording media & its release, publication, exhibition, or reproduction. Event StructureWe ask that guests arrive between 7-7:30 pm to minimize disruption during the talk. 7 pm - Doors open, opportunity to mingle over snacks & sips with other attendees7:30 pm - Guests take their seats for the talk8:15 pm - Informal mixer resumes On AttendanceWe have a limited capacity. If your plans change, please update your registration so someone else can join. A bit about Macktez, & why we host this seriesMacktez is a technology consultancy collaborating with organizations going through dynamic change. Our goal is to form a lasting partnership between our team & our clients, so we can anticipate their technology challenges & help them navigate growth, disruption, & other evolving conditions. Each event in our Tte--Tech series is an opportunity to explore a specific cultural, scientific, historical, & personal issue. We fire at the synapses that connect each topic to other fields of interest & to our individual lives. And we do so in a comfortable environment to facilitate conversation that can be casual, surprising, & illuminating. To learn more, visit us at macktez.com.

events.name: Alpha Agentic Economy Summit
events.description: The Alpha Agentic Economy Summit is the gathering for leaders building the agentic enterprise & those accountable for its decisions. On November 6, 2026, at Nasdaq MarketSite in New York City, Alpha brings together board directors, management teams, investors, & technology leaders to address a defining challenge: enterprises are delegating authority to AI faster than their governance can adapt. AI agents are already executing transactions, writing & deploying code, & making operational decisions between board meetings. As their authority expands, so does the exposure: financial loss, operational disruption, legal liability, & reputational damage. Boards need to understand where that authority sits, how it is controlled, & what evidence demonstrates that oversight is working. The Summit connects the boardroom with the people shaping this shift. Confirmed speakers include Gary Vaynerchuk, Chairman of VaynerX; Stacy Brown-Philpot, Founder & Managing Partner of Cherryrock Capital; Ann Miura-Ko, Co-Founding Partner of Floodgate; Laura Desmond, CEO of Smartly; Al Zollar, board director at BNY, IBM, & Nasdaq; & Madhu Muthukumar, Chief Product Officer of SoFi. They join leaders including Navrina Singh of Credo AI, Philip Rathle of Neo4j, Wasim Khaled of Blackbird.AI, Ned Koh of Aaru, Dara Ladjevardian of Delphi, Bri Treece of Fathom, & Andrew Yang of Noble Mobile. alpha.ac These leaders bring perspectives across enterprise deployment, venture investment, corporate oversight, AI governance, & the technologies changing how companies operate. Directors with oversight responsibility & executives with execution responsibility will engage directly with the builders & investors advancing the agentic economy. Attendance is curated to keep the room senior, focused, & conducive to substantive conversation. Working conversations take place under the Chatham House Rule, creating space for candid discussion of architectures, incidents, controls, & consequential decisions. Sessions give speakers time to examine the material in depth. Questions continue during deliberate intermissions, where delegates can connect directly with speakers & peers in smaller conversations. The format is built for practical outcomes. There are no vendor pitches. The focus is on real systems, delegated authority, & the decisions leaders must make: what agents may do, who owns their actions, when humans must intervene, & how performance & accountability can be verified. Delegates leave with a clearer view of where agents are entering the enterprise, relationships with the people shaping that transition, & concrete priorities for their next board, committee, or management meeting. In the agentic economy, every decision to delegate authority is a governance decision. Growth depends on getting it right. Governance is Alpha.

events.name: Trajectories - Facts, Fictions & Futures Of Spacefaring Societies
events.description: Science fiction has long imagined humanity's path beyond Earth, from post-scarcity utopias to contested frontiers to desperate exoduses. Which way are we headed? This week's interactive community conversation tests those visions against the technological, economic, societal, & cultural forces shaping our spacefaring future right now. Because the future isn't something we predict but something we choose, the question isn't just where we're headed, but where we dare to go. OUR FACILITATORVince Lucich, an engineer & startup founder whose work involves building spacecraft for the emerging orbital economy, will lead us on this idea exploration of the future. WHO'S IT FOR?Idea people. Founders. Builders. Creatives. Researchers. The Curious. And their Supporters --------------FORMATOur format explores ideas together through our diverse backgrounds, while building relationships & community through the process. We want you to talk to each other, instead of just being talked at. 6:00PM - Settle in, grab a drink & some food at the bar, & meet some new people before we start our event. 6:30PM - Our conversation begins with our facilitator presenting the knowledge & context for the conversation along the way. The conversation between attendees will explore from surface level understandings, to deep implications & future iterations. 7:45PM - Meet & connect with new people, catch up with people you haven't seen in a while, discover all the different ways you overlap. And then just hang out, grab a drink, play some pool or ping pong! Or stay for the band afterwards! Our desire is to be the antithesis of NYC's corporate panel & transactional networking culture. We aim to create a vibrant idea & build space in NYC that focuses on the passion & values beyond the money & the hustle.

events.name: Ugly Talk - Building Fandoms In 2027
events.description: A customer buys once. A fan brings people with them. Getting there takes months of showing up. Listening. Keeping promises. Giving people a reason to care when you are no longer in their feed. This Ugly Talk gets into the work behind real fandom. The creator calls that went nowhere. The community plays that looked dead for months. The moment loyal customers pushed back & the brand had to answer. No follower-count victory laps. Just the decisions, mistakes, & proof behind communities that stick.  Why you should be in this room.Hear how consumer brands turn one-time buyers into people who recruit other buyers. Learn which signals reveal loyalty before revenue catches up. See how brands build with creators from the first idea through launch. Learn what to keep doing when the community looks quiet. Hear how leaders respond when their biggest supporters become their loudest critics.  What's on the table.Building superfans at scale: What makes customers care enough to bring other people in. Creators & co-creation: How brands share the build instead of buying a post at the end. Measuring fandom: The numbers that matter after likes & reach stop telling the truth. The slow build: What to do when months of work look like nothing is happening. When fandom turns: What community pushback reveals about the trust you built. Managing a crisis: How to respond fast, own the miss, & keep trust intact.  Who's hosting it. Rob Fajardo - Founder, LeaveNormalBehind Rob Fajardo is an entrepreneur, operator, & cultural architect whose work centers on a simple question: what does winning look like? Early in his career, Rob helped drive the fidget spinner phenomenon by building & activating an influencer network across Instagram & Facebook, reaching over 150 million people. Since then, he has worked with brands including DoorDash, Lowe's, FedEx, Converse, Red Bull, & Wyndham Resort Group, & has been featured in Forbes, Entrepreneur, Thrive Global, & BuzzFeed. Rob is the founder of Leave Normal Behind, a global network of purpose-driven leaders, creators, & investors built around meaningful connection, personal growth, & human flourishing. Over the past decade, he has brought together people across industries & generations through designed gatherings & strategic collaborations. He also serves as Head of Operations for the School of Content at The School of Hard Knocks, one of the world's largest business media platforms with 26M+ followers, where he coaches business owners generating six to nine figures on go-to-market. In addition, he is a Strategic Advisor to The AI Collective, the world's largest AI community, with 70,000+ members across 25+ global chapters.  Who's getting in.CPG & consumer-brand founders building a customer base that sticks. Brand & community leaders responsible for loyalty & retention. Creators building their own audience or working with consumer brands. Marketers who care about advocacy, repeat purchases, & long-term growth.  About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough "aha!" moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons & insights. With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami, we've built a vibrant community of thousands of founders & industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape. Official Website: UglyTalk.com Important Notice for Ugly Talk AttendeesAdmission & Confirmation Attendance is by approval only. Approved guests will receive a confirmation email along with a calendar invite. Invitations are non-transferable. Additional event details will be shared as the event approaches. Code of Conduct By attending, you agree to: Maintain respect & professionalism, adhering to all venue rules, policies, & applicable laws. Refrain from harassment, discrimination, unwelcome sexual advances (verbal or physical), intimidation, or inappropriate photography/recording. Report any violations to the event hosts immediately. Violations may result in immediate removal from the event & exclusion from future invitations. Liability & Risk Participation is voluntary & at your own risk. You waive any right to inspect or approve the final materials & release all claims related to their use. Communications By registering, you agree to receive marketing & promotional communications from Ugly Talk & its co-hosts, partners, & sponsors. events.name: Red Carpet Room Launch Party
events.description: If you show up with a backpack or your laptop you will be banned from the event. Please leave backpacks at home. RED CARPET ROOM Formerly Fun HouseHosted by Anwar EnterprisesSaturday, October 31, 2026 Exact address released to confirmed guests 24 hours before doors. About the Event Red Carpet Room is the next chapter of Fun House, rebuilt around a single idea: the people building brands should be building them together. This is a mixer for founders, creators, & investors from the Anwar Events community, gathered in one room with a shared reason to be there. Everyone in attendance is constructing something with their name attached to it. The night is designed so the person who can unblock you is standing a few feet away. We are doing it on Halloween on purpose. The city will be full of parties where nothing happens beyond the party itself. This one gives you a panel worth sitting through, a room worth working, & footage of yourself that you will actually use. Run of Show [7pm] - Doors, check-in, & open networking to start the night[8pm] - Panel: operators who built audiences, companies, & reputations from nothing   SPECIAL GUESTS BEING REVEALED NEXT WEEK [9pm] - Open mixer, with Red Carpet Show interviews running in the back room Who's Coming The typical guest is a founder raising or building, a creator monetizing an audience, or an investor looking for both. Expect crossover from fashion, music, media, tech, art & consumer brands, since that is who the Anwar Events community actually contains. Whether you are hiring, raising, pitching a collaboration, or looking for people who take their work as seriously as you do, you will be in the right room. The Red Carpet Show Throughout the night, Ilias will pull guests aside for on-camera interviews for The Red Carpet Show. There is one question at the center of every interview: how can he help you. Those conversations get cut into content that reaches an audience of 70,000 plus founders, investors, & creators. Sitting down costs you four minutes & can put your company in front of people you would never cold email. Dress Code Halloween night calls for more than a costume assembled at the last minute. Come dressed as the version of yourself the press would photograph, whether that means black tie, full character, or your own blend of both. Cameras run from the door onward, so arrive accordingly. Capacity & Entry Space is limited & the guest list is curated. A confirmed RSVP secures your place only until capacity fills, so arriving early is strongly recommended. Bring a valid ID for check-in at the door. About the Host Ilias Anwar is an entrepreneur, marketer, & community builder based in New York City. He has produced more than 600 events across NYC, LA, & San Francisco, cultivating a network of over 70,000 founders, investors, & creators. His work includes brand partnerships with Google, Red Bull, Andreessen Horowitz, & Universal Music Group, along with activations at NFL Super Bowl Weekend & New York Fashion Week. Today he runs Anwar Enterprises, a venture studio that launches & scales consumer & tech companies through distribution first. If you need to meet someone in this city, they have probably attended one of his events. Partners & Sponsors Creatorsarethenewstudios.comCanvas helps creators, founders, & brands turn ideas into media IP they own. AI agents handle the story, production plan, budget, & distribution, & your first IP is free. Happyboards.comHappyBoards makes chef-built charcuterie boards & grazing tables from locally sourced ingredients. It delivers same-day across 27+ Northeast cities, & HappyBoards is feeding the room tonight.Stay Connected Future Anwar Events drop to the community first. Get on the list at luma.com/iliasanwar & follow along on Instagram, X, & LinkedIn for everything we run next. Community Standards Red Carpet Room is inclusive of gender, sexuality, race, religion, & ability. Discrimination or harassment of any kind will not be tolerated on site. For urgent security concerns during the event, please contact venue staff directly. Disclaimers By attending this event, you agree to the following terms. Photography, Video, & Recording: This event will be photographed, filmed, live-streamed, & audio recorded. By entering the venue, you consent to being captured on camera & to the use of your name, image, voice, statements, & likeness by Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, The Red Carpet Show, & their affiliated partners & sponsors. Marketing & Promotional Use: Any material captured at this event may appear in promotional content, social media, websites, newsletters, press coverage, paid advertising, sponsor recap materials, & future marketing assets, worldwide & in perpetuity, without compensation. Guests waive any right to inspect or approve the finished material before publication. On-Camera Interviews: Participation in The Red Carpet Show is entirely voluntary. Sitting for an interview grants Anwar Enterprises the full right to edit, distribute, & monetize that footage across any platform, in any format, without further approval. Opting Out: If you do not wish to be photographed or filmed, please notify event staff upon arrival & avoid the designated filming areas. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to accommodate your request, though appearance in wide or crowd shots cannot be fully prevented. Guest Policy: This is a private, invitation-only event. RSVPs are non-transferable & entry is subject to ID verification. Organizers reserve the right to refuse entry at their discretion. Capacity & Access: This event has a strict capacity limit. A confirmed RSVP does not guarantee entry once capacity has been reached, so early arrival is strongly encouraged. Code of Conduct: All attendees are expected to conduct themselves professionally & respectfully. Organizers reserve the right to remove any guest whose behavior is disruptive or inappropriate, without refund or recourse. Liability: Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, & the venue are not responsible for loss, theft, or damage to personal property. Attendance is at your own risk. Data & Registration: Information submitted at registration may be shared with event sponsors & partners in accordance with their respective privacy policies. Guests may opt out of sponsor communications at any time. Changes & Cancellations: Event details including time, venue, panelists, & programming are subject to change. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to notify registered guests of any material changes.

events.name: PMAI: Vibe Coding Workshop
events.description: Curious about coding with AI? This is the perfect place to start. If you are a: Non-technical founder/operator SME who wants to incorporate AI Someone who feel left behind by AI Aspiring builders/students Working professionals looking to 10x productivity Generally curious about agentic AI You have to come! In this beginner-friendly workshop, we'll walk you through everything you need to go from zero to building. We will cover: Setting up & installing Claude Code or Codex on your machine step by step Understanding the basics of how vibe coding works in your terminal Building a real project from scratch using natural language commands Learning how to prompt effectively so the tools do what you actually want No prior experience with AI coding tools is required, just bring your laptop & an active Anthropic or Open AI subscription. Participants are responsible for their own subscriptions. By the end of this session, you'll have a working project & the confidence to keep building on your own. Agenda 10:00 a.m. - Doors open & networking10:30 a.m. - workshop begins11:30 a.m. - Q&As & networking About Narra Collective: Narra Collective is a community-driven coworking & flex workspace in Jersey City serving founders, small business owners, & corporate teams. Through thoughtfully designed space & programming, Narra facilitates meaningful relationships, knowledge exchange, & business growth within a highly engaged local ecosystem. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: NY Tech Meetup - Climate Tech Edition
events.description: NY Tech Meetup  Columbia University SPSM.S. Technology Management Program We're excited to welcome back Columbia University's School of Professional Studies M.S. Technology Management program for another special edition of the NY Tech Meetup! Join us on Monday, November 9, as we spotlight emerging innovators from Columbia's Technology Management program who are turning bold ideas into promising technologies & real-world solutions. From fresh approaches to everyday challenges to innovations with the potential to transform industries, this edition offers a unique opportunity to discover what's next, hear directly from the innovators, & connect with NYC's vibrant tech community. As always, expect live demos, engaging conversations, new connections, & the energy that makes NY Tech Meetup a cornerstone of New York's tech ecosystem. Presenting innovators & their demos will be announced soon. Stay tuned! Program 6:00 PM - Doors Open 6:30 PM - Welcome & Live Demos 8:00 PM - Community Ask / Offer 8:15 PM - After-Party & Networking Come for the demos. Stay for the connections. Seats are limited - register now to secure your spot! About the NY Tech Meetup The NY Tech Meetup (NYTM) is a signature event of theNY Tech Alliance that has been a monthly staple for the NYC tech ecosystem since 2004. It is the world's largest meetup group of its kind with over 50,000 members who have a common interest in learning from & helping one another. At each event, entrepreneurs, founders, CEOs, & their teams demo cutting edge & transformative tech, answer questions from attendees & network with all in a welcoming & fun-filled space. Since its creation, over 1,200 companies have participated & have been a driving force of innovation & job creation in NYC & the greater NY area. About Columbia University's M.S. in Technology Management Columbia University's M.S. in Technology Management (TMGT) equips graduates with applied technology skills through research & industry insights to lead digital transformations & innovation in organizations across industries with an ethical leadership lens to achieve high impact & measurable results for today & to prepare for the future. Guided by Columbia's School of Professional Studies Scholar-Practitioner model, the program bridges theory & practice by integrating cutting-edge, real-world applications into the classroom experience & offers flexible pathways to the Masters of Science in Technology Management degree. The In-Person STEM-designated pathway offers full-time & part-time options & the Online part-time option is designed for working professionals who want the rigor & community of Columbia University from anywhere in the world. Through the School of Professional Studies' immersive digital learning environment, students engage in live, interactive classes led by Columbia faculty & industry experts.

events.name: Ahead Of The Curve
events.description: Ahead of the Curve with Penny Pritzker & Alexa von TobelWhat's taking shape today that will define the companies of tomorrow? Penny Pritzker has built businesses across industries & served as U.S. Secretary of Commerce. Alexa von Tobel founded LearnVest & went on to launch Inspired Capital alongside Penny. Together, they bring a perspective that spans startups, established businesses, investing, & public policy. They join Nami Baral, CEO & Co-Founder of Niural AI, for a candid, forward-looking conversation about: Where AI is opening up new business opportunities. How the workforce is changing & what tomorrow's teams might look like. Where capital, customer demand, & emerging markets are heading. Which shifts founders should prepare for now. Our fireside series has explored the teams that help companies grow & the products that earn conviction. This time, we're looking ahead. Come with questions about the future you're building for.  Date: Wednesday, October 28 Time: 8AM - 11AM Location: New York City Hosted by Niural AINiural is building the future of work by bringing payroll, payments, compliance, & workforce management into one AI-native platform. Beyond the software we're committed to creating spaces where founders can build meaningful relationships with one another. Sponsored by PwCPwC is dedicated to empowering the tech startup ecosystem through deep industry expertise & trusted advisory services. From funding stages to preparing for the capital markets, our team brings world class expertise in key focus areas for emerging growth companies. We deliver tailored solutions that support your business transformation from a high growth tech startup to a sector-defining public company. Our focus is to meet you where you are as an organization, growing with the Company as you IPO & beyond. Whether you're a founder, CEO, or CFO, PwC is here to support your journey toward sustainable growth & innovation. To get connected, please contact Christina White at Christina.m.white@pwc.com.

events.name: Startup Pitch Mixer
events.description: Join our event in New York! We design Pitch & Networking nights to help founders sharpen their thinking through direct, candid feedback & to give strong investors access to serious teams. Our pitch night is complemented by a structured networking session before & after the pitch session.  What to expect: Startups pitch live & receive focused feedback from angels & VC partners Structured networking session before & after the pitches Entrepreneurs, startup founders, & operators are joining to network, exchange ideas, & build strong connections Active investors & venture scouts joining to discover the best startups early  Who you will meet at the event: Founders Investors, VC partners, Venture Scouts Marketers, Salespeople, Business Advisors Industry Disruptors AI Experts Entrepreneurs from Europe, Asia, & the United Kingdom  We Welcome New Investors: We invite investors to our event to expand their network, get acquainted with new startups, evaluate them, share feedback, & participate in discussions with early-stage & serial founders. We offer complimentary tickets to institutional investors, angels, & venture scouts with a proven track record. If you'd like to access our database of promising startups or provide mentorship support to our best startups, please fill out this short Investor Application Form, & our team will contact you.  Want to Pitch? A limited number of founders will have the opportunity to pitch their startup or business to a panel of investors & experts. 4-6 selected founders will pitch their startup, followed by a short Q&A where participants can ask questions & share feedback. Apply by filling out the Pitch Application Form & sending us your pitch deck. Spots are limited, & we select founders in advance. To maintain high-quality pitches, you are required to present with a pitch deck. We will share our pitching guide and, if you'd like, coach you so you're fully prepared for pitch night.  The best startups will be featured across our social media & included in our investor newsletter. Requirements for attendees: Dress code: smart casual. Bring good energy.  Join our event & secure your ticket today! About us: Startup Valley is a global event organizer hosting pitch nights in 25 cities since 2023. Since then, we have hosted 850 events for 40,000 attendees. Over these years, we connected countless outstanding early-stage startups to serious investors, & we are not planning to stop. We maintain strategic partnerships with VC funds in the US, Europe, & Asia to support our community. Do you have a question, a partnership proposal, or want to clarify something? Reach us at hello@startupvalley.club Agenda 18:00-18:30 - Registration: Guests register, receive badges, & event programs. This is an opportunity for casual networking, making first connections, & preparing for the event. 18:30-19:00 - Event Kickoff & Interactive Networking: Official welcome from the organizers with a brief overview of the event goals & schedule. Interactive networking session to connect with key contacts. 19:00-19:50 - Startup Pitch Session: Startups present their projects to investors & experts. Each team has 5 minutes to pitch, covering the project's core idea, business model, & target market. 19:50-21:00 - Chill & Networking: Participants enjoy casual conversations with investors, discuss collaboration opportunities, & exchange ideas over refreshments. FAQ Can I pitch? Yes! To pitch, please purchase a Pitch Ticket & fill out the Pitch Application Form. We will contact you to discuss & approve your pitch. The pitch duration is 5 minutes. You will also have some time to answer questions from the audience. How does the pitch go? Selected founders present on stage to the audience & the investors in the room. You get 5 minutes to pitch your idea, business model, target market, & investment ask, followed by a short Q&A. The best startups are featured across our social media channels & in the investor newsletter. Who will I meet? Founders, angel investors, VC partners, venture scouts, AI experts, engineers, operators, marketing & sales experts, & international entrepreneurs from across Europe, Asia, & the US. Do investors get free tickets? Yes! Please apply above or email hello@startupvalley.club, & we will issue a complimentary ticket for you & your team. Can I request a refund? Yes. Refunds are available if requested at least 1 day before the event start time. Please submit the refund request on the platform where you purchased your ticket, or email us at hello@startupvalley.club

events.name: Trajectories - Facts, Fictions & Futures Of Spacefaring Societies
events.description: Science fiction has long imagined humanity's path beyond Earth, from post-scarcity utopias to contested frontiers to desperate exoduses. Which way are we headed? This week's interactive community conversation tests those visions against the technological, economic, societal, & cultural forces shaping our spacefaring future right now. Because the future isn't something we predict but something we choose, the question isn't just where we're headed, but where we dare to go. OUR FACILITATORVince Lucich, an engineer & startup founder whose work involves building spacecraft for the emerging orbital economy, will lead us on this idea exploration of the future. WHO'S IT FOR?Idea people. Founders. Builders. Creatives. Researchers. The Curious. And their Supporters --------------FORMATOur format explores ideas together through our diverse backgrounds, while building relationships & community through the process. We want you to talk to each other, instead of just being talked at. 6:00PM - Settle in, grab a drink & some food at the bar, & meet some new people before we start our event. 6:30PM - Our conversation begins with our facilitator presenting the knowledge & context for the conversation along the way. The conversation between attendees will explore from surface level understandings, to deep implications & future iterations. 7:45PM - Meet & connect with new people, catch up with people you haven't seen in a while, discover all the different ways you overlap. And then just hang out, grab a drink, play some pool or ping pong! Or stay for the band afterwards! Our desire is to be the antithesis of NYC's corporate panel & transactional networking culture. We aim to create a vibrant idea & build space in NYC that focuses on the passion & values beyond the money & the hustle.
