events.name: SOSV Deep Tech Summit
events.description: SOSV DEEP TECH SUMMIT Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. The producers of the Summit are SOSV's Ned Desmond, Ben Joffe, & Norm Amandi. More DetailsSOSV's mission is to invest in deep tech companies that advance human & planetary health, & embedded in building an 800+ company portfolio with a remarkable array of companies applying AI in the physical world. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

events.name: Business Funding - An International Perspective
events.description: Every stage of growing a business is a funding decision, even when it doesn't feel like one. How you pay for the next market, the next hire, the next acquisition quietly shapes what the business is worth years later, & who you can sell it to. Across the Atlantic, the options multiply & the advice gets thinner. During the evening, hear from speakers across the corporate lifecycle, sharing their different funding, expansion & exit stories, so you leave with greater insight & awareness of the opportunities, & the pitfalls to avoid. Designed for international founders & business executives planning to grow in New York City, the discussion will cover the advantages, tradeoffs, & tactics involved in raising capital from VC & PE sources.  Speakers Dan Jaeck is a Principal at Crane VC, based between New York & London, where he partners with founders building transformational software companies.Before joining Crane, he spent four years at Eniac Ventures in NYC, investing in AI application-layer & infrastructure companies. Prior to Eniac, Dan began his career at Goldman Sachs in London on the Emerging Market Equities desk. Joel Goschalk is a Senior Director at Dundon Advisers, advising middle-market companies on recapitalizations, restructurings & credit. He started as a London insolvency practitioner, co-founded & scaled a UK litigation funding & private equity business (Cavendish IP Solutions), & has spent over a decade as COO of a family office, advising on fundraising rounds, fund formation across the UK, US & offshore, & cross-border expansion.  Co-host: The Transatlantic Innovation Hub, is New York's launch pad for Italian & European companies, to help them successfully enter & scale in the U.S. market. Located in the heart of Manhattan, TIH serves as a landing pad for innovation ecosystems, providing companies with both a physical presence in New York & a structured set of market access services to accelerate their U.S. expansion. The Knowledge Shop is the founder community in NYC. We are industry & stage agnostic, helping not just startups grow, but supporting the founders building them.  Founding Partner: Sabre Integrated has been providing commercial security systems in NYC since 2000.From access control & video surveillance to fully integrated security systems, they design, install & support your business every step of the way  Charity Partner: The St George's Society of New York, provides life-changing support to immigrants from Britain & the Commonwealth in New York. Established in 1770, we're the second-oldest charity in the city. We hold events year round - join us for Pancake day   Find even more Tech events at: www.foundereventsnyc.com

events.name: Your Investor Pitch: What To Say & How To Say It
events.description: A free, two-hour workshop for founders who want to build a stronger investor pitch & deliver it with confidence.You know your business. You know the opportunity. But can you communicate it in a way that makes investors understand the potential, believe in you, & want to continue the conversation? On October 30, join a group of founders for a focused working session to assess the pitch you have today, identify what's missing, & turn it into a sharper, more compelling investor presentation. Anthony Rose, CEO of SeedLegals.com, tells you exactly what investors need to hear. David Goldberg, CEO of Prosody.center, shows you exactly how they need to hear it. Two hours, both experts, free. What you'll work on1. Build the right investor storyStructure your pitch around what investors need to understand: opportunity, differentiation, competition, financials, traction, scalability, & why now. Cut unnecessary information, close narrative gaps, & make the value easier to grasp. 2. Deliver it with confidence & credibilityA strong deck isn't enough. Learn to make a strong first impression, create buy-in, use pace & pauses to make key numbers land, stress the words that carry value, & steady your voice under pressure. Use your voice to communicate with the composure & authority investors expect. 3. Test & refine your pitchPitch in front of others & discover where the room leans in, where you lose them, & what needs to change. Use live feedback to tighten your messaging & delivery. 4. The live-feedback experienceEach hour includes 15 minutes of tips, first from Anthony Rose on creating compelling content, then from David Goldberg on delivering it with conviction, followed by 45 minutes of live, instructive feedback so founders can improve their pitches on the spot. What you'll leave withA sharper, more focused investor pitch A clearer understanding of your strengths & gaps Practical techniques for presenting with confidence Real-world feedback on your messaging & delivery Specific next steps for continuing to improve Greater insight into what can move an investor from listening to wanting to know more Who should attendFounders & startup leaders at different stages of the fundraising journey. Whether you're preparing to pitch for the first time or you've pitched before & know it could be stronger, the goal is the same: leave with a better pitch than the one you walked in with. Your facilitatorsAnthony Rose, CEO, SeedLegalsFounder & CEO of SeedLegals, the legaltech platform that helps startups get investment-ready, run a funding round, & handle their legals, used by over 60,000 startups. Before SeedLegals, his career spanned 3D graphics, peer-to-peer music, internet video, & social TV, including heading up BBC iPlayer. Wired Magazine's 2009 cover story called him "The Man Who Saved the BBC." David Goldberg, CEO, Prosody.center & Edge StudioFounder of Prosody.center & EdgeStudio.com, an international voiceover recording center. He has directed, coached, & trained over 10,000 celebrities, politicians, CEOs, & founders on more than 13,000 spoken-word projects over 38 years. He identifies the blind spots that hold founders back when they pitch (pacing, phrasing, wording, emphasis, tone, body language, composure, nonverbal cues), then shows the precise adjustments that change how investors experience & respond to you. DetailsWhen: Friday, October 30, 1-3pm ET, in person, Times Square, NYCCost: Free to join. Co-founders are welcome too.Capacity: Seating is limited, & registrations are approved individually. Come prepared to work on your business, test your ideas, & practice your pitch, not simply take notes.

events.name: AI Content System + Investor Fireside Chat
events.description: Time Rich presents a working session, hosted by Ella Molony Cook, with co-hosting partner Wispr Flow & presenting partner Stanley. It opens with a short panel on why trust + distribution is now your moat. Then you build your content system in three parts: capture, context, create. You schedule your posts before you leave, so next week is handled. Every guest gets six months of Wispr Pro & Stanley. WHO IT'S FORFounders, business owners & investors who post in bursts, or know they should post more, & want content that sounds like them without writing every word. THE PANEL: YOUR MOAT IS YOUR DISTRIBUTIONA short conversation with investors, founders & ex-Google/YouTube on why visibility, trust & authority matter more than ever. WHAT GETS BUILTCapture. You'll set up Wispr Flow & brief your agent by voice instead of typing. Your best ideas sit in voice notes that never turn into posts, because nothing keeps running when you're busy. Your calls, voice notes & talks become raw material, & we pull ten stories out of your own words.Context. A tone of voice brief, the words you never use, & a call to action matched to each story.Create. Content agents that draft, repurpose across platforms & schedule. By the end, a week of posts is scheduled & the system is set up to fill the next one. Rather have it built for you? The Stanley team will be in the room. Just ask. WHAT TO BRING Laptop, charger & phone. Setup runs on iMessage or WhatsApp. One recording: a talk, a podcast, a call or a voice note Your three best published posts The one thing you want every post to drive: a booked call, a newsletter sign-up or a product AGENDA6:00-6:30 PM  Doors open, meet other founders6:30-6:35 PM  Welcome from Ella6:35-6:55 PM  Panel: your moat is your distribution6:55-8:20 PM  The build: capture, context, create8:20-9:00 PM  Q&A, drinks & mingling POWERED BY STANLEYStanley is an AI Head of Content. You text it a voice note, it drafts in your voice, & it repurposes whatever already performed. Stanley is our presenting partner for the night, so everyone builds on it live. OUR PARTNERTime Rich runs on voice, powered by Wispr FlowWispr Flow is our co-hosting partner. You'll talk to your agents instead of typing to them, & every guest leaves with six months of Wispr Pro. THE ROOMElla Molony Cook is an Australian 4x founder with 1 exit & an investor in Anthropic. Founder of Time Rich a media & AI education platform. Has a community of over 63K+ subscribers on Substack filled with founders, SMBs, angel investors, leaders & has hosted 250+ founder & investor experiences. Max Rivera is an angel investor & GP at GHOST Angels, a fund of Snapchat alumni backing early-stage consumer AI startups. He led global partnerships at Snap from pre-IPO to a $120B public company. Today he leads partnerships for Microsoft AI. Aishwarya Balaji is a 2x founder, venture fund advisor, investor & global speaker. She has spotted & built for emerging markets again & again, from ed-tech & Web3 to non-alc & the creator economy. Rodolphe Kdderitzsch is on the Stanley team. He's ex-Google/YouTube & Squarespace, & a startup founder. TIME RICH CLUBWhere founders, creators & investors come to invest in themselves, their relationships, & building a system to become Time Rich. Whether you're building a company, backing your next deal, or just getting started, this is where you do it alongside people who are building too. Inside the Club: Private conversations on investing, entrepreneurship, building your brand, time hacks & running your life on AI Fireside chats with family offices, exited founders & thought leaders A network of founders, creators & investors who build companies & allocate capital Seats are limited & we read every application.

events.name: Agent Evaluation Science
events.description: Presented by EvalScience, Agent Evaluation Science NYC 2026 is a one-day symposium bringing together researchers & practitioners working on how AI agents should be evaluated. Featured speakers & contributors include Hanna Wallach (Microsoft Research), Jason Weston (Meta / NYU), Yoav Artzi (Cornell Tech), Nouha Dziri (Cohere Labs), Peter Henderson (Princeton), Olawale Salaudeen (UIUC), Rachneet Kaur (J.P. Morgan), Ida Momennejad (Microsoft Research), & Saurabh Jha (IBM Research). We will discuss what agent evaluations should measure, how reliability & validity should be established, where benchmarks & graders fail, how evaluation infrastructure should be built, & what changes when agents are evaluated in interactive & real-world settings. The program includes invited talks, contributed research presentations, posters, a fireside conversation, & extended discussion & networking. November 20, 2026  New York City Registration is free & approval-based. We welcome researchers, builders, & practitioners working on evaluation methods, benchmarks, agent behavior, evaluation infrastructure, & real-world evaluation problems. We are also accepting contributions including ongoing or published research, evaluation studies, tools, failure analyses, & lessons from evaluating deployed systems. Learn more: https://evalscience.org/2026fall-nyc/

events.name: Spooky Civic AI Hackathon - Build Weekend
events.description: Demos are Sunday at Demo Day. RSVP for that separately: luma.com/3perce-pi2u Spooky Civic AI Hackathon: Build AI Tools for NYC Free. Open to everyone. No approval needed, just RSVP.Fri Oct 23 - Sat Oct 24, in person in NYC or on Zoom.Come solo & we'll help you find a team. Free food for in-person builders. Who can come? Anyone who wants to build something for New York City: engineers, product managers, designers, people who used to code, & people who never have. The best teams pair people who know a problem with people who can build the tech. Builders write the code & ship the tool. Problem-solvers (PMs, designers, policy & community folks) pick the problem, shape how people will use it, & lead the pitch. No team? No problem. Most people come solo. You can meet teammates at our Oct 14 & Oct 15 classes, or at Friday's kickoff. Pick a track The Existential Track: Climate & Sustainability. Heat, waste, food access, cleaner air. Urban Nightmares: Housing, Healthcare, Education & Justice. Tenant rights, benefits, school help, legal info in plain English. Ghost in the Machine: AI infrastructure & scaling. Build the parts under civic AI tools, like search, data, & agents that keep them running. Physical AI for Good: Build AI that moves, with robot arm kits on site. No robotics experience needed. You leave with a working prototype, a demo video, & a real project for your portfolio. Mentors will be on hand all weekend. Where: NYC venue announced soon. The Zoom link goes to everyone who RSVPs. Partners: Robot arm kits & on-site mentors from Viam. Food & builder API credits from Vonage. Costumes encouraged. In-person spots are limited, so RSVP now. Sponsorship inquiries: Partner with 3percentclub About Viam: Viam is a New York-based software platform for building, deploying, & managing robotics & AI in the physical world. Viam is supplying robot arm kits & on-site mentors for this hackathon. About Vonage: Vonage, part of Ericsson, builds communications APIs for voice, video, messaging, & verification that developers put into their apps. Vonage is providing food & builder API credits for this hackathon. About 3percentclub: 3percentclub is an NYC nonprofit that teaches free AI classes for underrepresented builders: engineers, career changers, product managers, designers, & people who have never coded. This event is open to everyone. Want to go deeper with AI? Apply to the free AI Architect Fellowship for weekly classes, mentorship, & a community to build with. The AI Collective is a global non-profit building the human layer for the AI era. We unite 1,000,000+ leaders, builders, & stakeholders across 300+ forums worldwide to democratize the frontier, build trust, & coordinate how society navigates the rapid acceleration of technological progress. All attendees & organizers at events affiliated with The AI Collective agree to our privacy policy & are subject to our code of conduct.

events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: Did Maha Maha?
events.description: Has the MAHA movement made Americans healthier than the establishment? Americans spend more on healthcare than anyone else in the world. Yet we have soaring rates of obesity, diabetes, & chronic disease. So is the medical establishment failing us? And is MAHA actually doing any better? RFK's MAHA movement has put ultra-processed foods, environmental toxins, & chronic disease at the center of the national conversation. Supporters say it's finally challenging a healthcare system that profits from treating illness instead of preventing it. Critics say it's undermining trust in vaccines, established science, & the institutions responsible for keeping Americans healthy. So who's right? Is MAHA forcing a long-overdue reckoning with a broken healthcare system? Or is it replacing imperfect science with something far more dangerous? Kerry Semle is a biomedical engineer, former medical technology executive, & women's health advocate with 15 years of experience in medical devices & diagnostics. She's advocated for greater investment in women's health research & improved access to care. Emily Kaplan is the CEO & co-founder of the Broken Science Initiative, an organization challenging the scientific establishment & questioning how medical research is conducted, evaluated, & trusted. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

events.name: TransportationCamp 2026
events.description: Join us on Saturday, October 24, for TransportationCamp NYC 2026! TransportationCamp NYC will be held on Saturday, October 24 at NYU's Tandon School of Engineering in Downtown Brooklyn. Join us to discuss all things transportation & connect with professionals, students, & enthusiasts alike! TransportationCamp is an unconference - every session is planned, proposed, & led by attendees like you. It's the perfect opportunity to share your transportation passion with a diverse gathering of individuals from our multidisciplinary industry. TransportationCamp welcomes all attendees, whether you're a planner, software developer, engineer, student, transportation professional, community member, policymaker, or just excited about mobility! Register here to join us for a fun day of transportation learning & networking on October 24! Interested in sponsoring?We are seeking sponsorship from engineering firms, research centers, planning organizations, & more to make TCNYC26 extra special! To learn about sponsorship packages, contact TCampNYC@gmail.com. Put your organization's name in front of the people who are working on the latest & greatest at the intersection of transportation & technology. Student ScholarshipApplications are now open for our student scholarship! TransportationCamp NYC will award one $500 scholarship this year thanks to the support of VHB! All undergraduate students, as well as full-time master's degree students, are eligible to apply. The deadline for scholarship applications is Sunday, October 18, at 11:59pm ET! Presenting?Thinking about presenting at a session? Sessions may come in a variety of formats: informal discussions, birds-of-a-feather, lightning talks, presentations, & others. We welcome experts, but really you just need to care about transportation issues or be nerds about it like us. The important thing is that you bring your ideas & enthusiasm, & engage! All the breakout rooms are equipped with a projector or whiteboard. We will be handing out session idea cards throughout registration. If you have an idea for a session, feel free to write it down in advance & bring it with you to the event. First time at a TransportationCamp?How To TransportationCamp: Review the TransportationCamp 101 guide that explains all aspects of the event.Participation Encouraged: Sessions are formed as the day goes on, so be sure to come with topics for discussion. If you have an idea, feel free to share & add your thoughts.Rule of Two Feet: Never hesitate to leave a session if you suddenly find it's not for you, or if there's another session that you want to check out, too!Social mediaMake sure you're up to date by following us on LinkedIn & by subscribing to our email updates. And keep the conversation going! Tag your tweets, Instagram photos, & more with the official event hashtag: #TCNYC26

events.description: Join us at Fabrik NYC in DUMBO, Brooklyn for an in-person, hands-on pitch clinic designed to help founders become more confident on stage & sharpen the way they pitch to investors. Whether you are preparing for a fundraising round, an investor meeting, or your next demo day, you will learn practical tools to communicate your story with greater confidence, clarity, & impact. The clinic features two focused, 30-minute workshops covering how you show up & what you say. Don't Calm Down with Dave Wolovsky In this interactive workshop, Dave will share practical exercises to help you compose yourself when pitching, work with pressure rather than against it, & perform with greater presence in high-stakes moments. Dave is a Cognitive Performance Coach with an MS in Neuroscience & Education from Columbia University. He coaches founders on focus & daily energy management & serves as a StartX accelerator mentor. Learn more at https://effortwise.com/founders. The Art of Pitching to Attract Investors with Anthony Rose Anthony will break down how to communicate your vision & opportunity & present your business in a way that resonates with investors. Anthony is the founder & CEO of SeedLegals, the legaltech platform used by more than 50,000 startups to get investment-ready, run funding rounds, & handle legal needs. Before SeedLegals, his career included leading BBC iPlayer. Wired Magazine's 2009 cover story called him The Man Who Saved the BBC. Come ready to learn, practice, & leave with techniques you can use in your next pitch. The room seats 100. Hosted by SeedLegals, Meera Mawkin, Dave Wolovsky, & Fabrik NYC. Presented with Propel Earth Original event & registration details https://luma.com/dehgirvb The exact address is available after registering on the original Luma page.

events.name: Six Math Essentials w/ Terence Tao
events.description: Book Launch & Conversation with Janna Levin Widely regarded as the world's greatest living mathematician, Fields Medalist Terence Tao approaches mathematics as a sublime art-a quiet, rigorous effort to map the hidden scaffolding of reality. To mark the publication of his first popular book, Six Math Essentials, join us for an evening with Tao in conversation with Pioneer Works Director of Sciences Janna Levin. Tracing the central pillars of his book-from algebra as abstraction & geometry beyond sight, to navigating uncertainty & the mathematics of change-they will reveal math not as obscure magic, but as a deeply creative, interconnected way of thinking. Often referred to as the Mozart of mathematics, Tao will also explore how AI is transforming his own practice, the frontier of research, & our collective future. Together, we will consider what becomes of human intuition & creativity when the tools of thought are no longer uniquely human-and whether the true beauty of math lies not in the answers we find, but in the human mind reaching for them. Tao will sign copies of Six Math Essentials following the conversation, with books available for purchase on site. (Unable to attend? Order a signed copy here.) Please note that seating is limited & will be available on a first-come, first-served basis.   About the speakersTerence Tao is an Australian-American professor of mathematics at UCLA whose work focuses primarily on harmonic analysis, partial differential equations, combinatorics, & analytic number theory. The recipient of a Fields Medal, a MacArthur Genius Grant, & a Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics, among many other accolades, he is one of the most decorated & prolific mathematicians working today. Tao is the author of several academic books including Solving Mathematical Problems: A Personal Perspective & Additive Combinatorics, as well as his first popular math book, Six Math Essentials. He lives in Los Angeles. Janna Levin is the Claire Tow Professor of physics & astronomy at Barnard College of Columbia University. A Guggenheim Fellow, she has contributed to our understanding of black holes, extra dimensions, & cosmology. She is the founding director of sciences at Pioneer Works & the founding editor-in-chief of the magazine Pioneer Works Broadcast. She often contributes to news, documentaries, & radio, including as the presenter of the NOVA feature Black Hole Apocalypse on PBS & as a contributor to CBS, CNN, BBC, & NBC. She has authored books on black holes & the universe-Black Hole Blues, How the Universe Got its Spots, & Black Hole Survival Guide-as well as a PEN award-winning novel, A Madman Dreams of Turing Machines. You can find her current writings in Higher Dimensions. This program is funded by the Simons Foundation International & administered by the Simons Foundation's Science, Society & Culture division.

events.name: The Next Wave: AI & The Future Of Ocean Conservation, with Ocean Agentics
events.description: The world has committed to protecting 30% of the ocean by 2030, a target scientists see as the minimum for a healthy ocean. With four years to go, only about 3% is effectively protected. Countries & communities pursuing the 30x30 goal often lack the data, tools & technical teams to propose & implement conservation efforts at the speed & scale needed to get there. AI is starting to help with some of the hardest parts of that work. It can map where whales & other wildlife gather so countries know which waters to protect, & help coast guards catch illegal fishing vessels inside protected areas. However, most of these tools still sit out of reach of the small island nations & coastal communities with the most at stake. Whether AI narrows that gap or widens it depends on whether it's built with & for the people who will use it. Join Anew & Ocean Agentics for an evening of conversation with people leading this work across ocean technology, science, philanthropy & policy. We'll talk about what responsible AI for the ocean could look like, & what it would take for these tools to reach the people who need them. Drinks & mingling to follow. Ocean Agentics is a nonprofit building open tools that put frontier technology & marine data in the hands of people protecting the ocean. Our current focus is on providing engineering support to the countries & stakeholders implementing the High Seas Treaty, which covers two-thirds of the ocean. Anew is a gathering space & discovery center for social transformation located in NYC. We host interactive events & workshops, an accelerator program for nonprofits, & a retail lab featuring ethically-sourced coffee & gifts.

events.name: OverdriveAI Summit
events.description: Overdrive AIHosted by TechUnited:NJ, creators of Propelify, heralded by Forbes as the "SXSW of the Northeast," OverdriveAI is back, & this year it's a debate. The hottest topics in AI, argued live, both sides on stage. Jobs, energy, education, & more. Sharp thinkers go head to head, you hear the case for & against, & you decide where you land. Taking place this year at the Newark Museum of Art, where tech & culture share a roof, OverdriveAI brings together founders, operators, investors, & researchers from across the Northeast for a day built around one idea: the biggest questions in AI don't have easy answers, so let's actually argue about them. TICKETS ARE NOW LIVE!EXPLORE THE FULL OVERDRIVEAI EXPERIENCE Community AI TrainingHands-on morning AI training at EqualSpace designed for all experience levels. No prior AI experience required. Reserve Your Spot Executive AI TrainingA focused, practical AI training designed for executives & business leaders ready to better understand & apply AI within their organizations. Reserve Your Spot Pitch Roast LiveStartups pitch. Comedians roast. Everyone wins. Close out OverdriveAI with an evening of bold ideas, founder pitches, comedy, & connection. Reserve Your Spot   What to Expect Community AI Training A hands-on morning (10a-12p ET) AI training at EqualSpace designed for all experience levels. Come ready to learn, explore, & put AI into practice. No prior experience required. Executive AI Training Turn AI into practical business advantage. Start your morning with a focused AI training session designed for executives, business leaders, & decision-makers navigating the rapidly evolving AI landscape. This interactive session will explore practical ways leaders can better understand, evaluate, & apply AI within their organizations helping you move from conversation to action. The AI Debates The main event at the Newark Museum of Art. Will AI take your job or grow the economy? Who pays for AI's energy appetite? Does AI belong in the classroom? Can you still trust what you see? Startup demos will be featured between rounds & the afternoon will roll into TechUnited:NJ Birthday Party! Final topics & speakers are still being locked in, ticket holders hear every name first. Here's what's on the table so far: AI takes jobs vs. AI grows the economy - does automation erase more work than it creates? Is AI raising your energy bill? - the data center buildout is reshaping the grid, & New Jersey's in the middle of it. Does AI belong in the classroom? - a tutor for every student, or the end of learning how to think? Is it time for universal basic income? - if productivity keeps compounding, someone decides where the gains go. Can we handle deepfakes? - synthetic media's getting cheap & convincing, what's the real defense? Got a debate we missed? Suggest it, & if it makes the stage, you'll know it was yours. Live debates. Experts, opposing sides of one question, no hedging.Hot takes. Short, sharp presentations from speakers with a strong point of view.Networking. 300+ founders, researchers, & investors in one room, this year in a new venue built for it. Pitch Roast Live Closing the night at Newark Culture Club Close with startup pitches & a high-energy evening experience. Four founders pitch, three comedians & two investors roast. One walks out a winner! Last Year, at Nokia Bell Labs Speakers joined us from OpenAI, IBM, CoreWeave, Verizon, Perplexity, Nokia Bell Labs, BetterFutureLabs, NJEDA, & the NJ AI Hub. 16 speakers, 300+ attendees, a packed house. This year's lineup is coming together now, & it's bigger. OverdriveAI is one of many events TechUnited:NJ runs for its 13,000+ member community, from AI Demo Night to Propelify. events.name: An UNMUTED Book Club: The 100 Years War On Palestine
events.description: READING NOT REQUIRED - just be curious! Next up: Rashid Khalidi's The Hundred Years' War on Palestine, the 2020 book that argues the Israeli-Palestinian conflict isn't simply a tragic struggle between two peoples claiming the same land, but a century-long colonial campaign against Palestinians, backed first by Britain & later by the United States. Khalidi, a Palestinian-American historian at Columbia, tells the story through six turning points, beginning with the 1917 Balfour Declaration & moving through the creation of Israel, the wars that followed, & the failures of the peace process. Drawing on historical archives & his own family's experiences, he makes a provocative argument: that Palestinians have never been negotiating on equal terms, & that understanding the conflict as a dispute between two competing national movements obscures the enormous imbalance of power between them. It's a forceful challenge to conventional accounts of Israel's founding, Zionism, & America's role in the region, & one that raises uncomfortable questions about nationalism, colonialism, & self-determination. Show up even if you only got through a chunk. We'll talk about where Khalidi's account is most convincing, where it leaves out important context, whether Zionism is best understood as a colonial movement or a national liberation movement, & what his interpretation of the past means for the possibility of peace today. UNMUTED is a discussion forum for the politically curious. Accessible. Engaging. Social. Open-minded is the name of the game. Join your people.

events.name: Alpha Agentic Economy Summit
events.description: The Alpha Agentic Economy Summit is the gathering for leaders building the agentic enterprise & those accountable for its decisions. On November 6, 2026, at Nasdaq MarketSite in New York City, Alpha brings together board directors, management teams, investors, & technology leaders to address a defining challenge: enterprises are delegating authority to AI faster than their governance can adapt. AI agents are already executing transactions, writing & deploying code, & making operational decisions between board meetings. As their authority expands, so does the exposure: financial loss, operational disruption, legal liability, & reputational damage. Boards need to understand where that authority sits, how it is controlled, & what evidence demonstrates that oversight is working. The Summit connects the boardroom with the people shaping this shift. Confirmed speakers include Gary Vaynerchuk, Chairman of VaynerX; Stacy Brown-Philpot, Founder & Managing Partner of Cherryrock Capital; Ann Miura-Ko, Co-Founding Partner of Floodgate; Laura Desmond, CEO of Smartly; Al Zollar, board director at BNY, IBM, & Nasdaq; & Madhu Muthukumar, Chief Product Officer of SoFi. They join leaders including Navrina Singh of Credo AI, Philip Rathle of Neo4j, Wasim Khaled of Blackbird.AI, Ned Koh of Aaru, Dara Ladjevardian of Delphi, Bri Treece of Fathom, & Andrew Yang of Noble Mobile. alpha.ac These leaders bring perspectives across enterprise deployment, venture investment, corporate oversight, AI governance, & the technologies changing how companies operate. Directors with oversight responsibility & executives with execution responsibility will engage directly with the builders & investors advancing the agentic economy. Attendance is curated to keep the room senior, focused, & conducive to substantive conversation. Working conversations take place under the Chatham House Rule, creating space for candid discussion of architectures, incidents, controls, & consequential decisions. Sessions give speakers time to examine the material in depth. Questions continue during deliberate intermissions, where delegates can connect directly with speakers & peers in smaller conversations. The format is built for practical outcomes. There are no vendor pitches. The focus is on real systems, delegated authority, & the decisions leaders must make: what agents may do, who owns their actions, when humans must intervene, & how performance & accountability can be verified. Delegates leave with a clearer view of where agents are entering the enterprise, relationships with the people shaping that transition, & concrete priorities for their next board, committee, or management meeting. In the agentic economy, every decision to delegate authority is a governance decision. Growth depends on getting it right. Governance is Alpha.

events.name: PMAI: Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Sales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. - Bring a computer. You're writing three things tonight.- Most founders can get meetings. The deals die after meeting one.- You'll leave with your buyer in one sentence, a cold email written to a real person, & five questions for your next call. About Farzad, the speaker Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding & generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: Worn: Smart Glasses Hackathon
events.description: Two days, one overnight build, & real smart glasses on your face. Join us at Cornell Tech with MicroLumin, the Shenzhen team behind the CES 2026 award-winning M6 display glasses, & build the first wave of apps for waveguide display glasses. This is a hands-on hardware hackathon for engineers & builders who would rather ship on real devices than talk about the future of spatial computing. Problem StatementSmart glasses are finally light enough to wear all day. What's missing is software that feels natural to use. Your challenge is to build anthropocentric interfaces: apps that start from how people see, move, talk & pay attention, not from how phones work. These should be things you'd actually keep on your face. The Challenge ThemeHeads-up assistants that show the right info at the right moment Live captioning, translation & conversation memory Navigation & wayfinding without looking down at a phone Accessibility for low-vision, hard-of-hearing & neurodivergent users Hands-free workflows for field techs, clinicians, chefs & mechanics New input patterns: voice, ring, head motion & glanceable UI Making the glasses useful with AI on what the camera sees What to ExpectMicroLumin AR glasses handed out to teams for the build SDK access & docs shared before the event so you can start early A workshop from Dr. Zhaoen Dai, MicroLumin's founder & CEO, on AR & where the AI industry is heading An overnight build from Friday evening into Saturday Teams of up to 4, or match with teammates at kickoff Food, caffeine & other builders who care about hardware Live demos on the device, worn by your team, in front of the judges ScheduleFriday, Nov 20 5:30 PM: Doors open, check-in, dinner 6:15 PM: Welcome & kickoff with the organizers, Cornell Tech & MicroLumin 6:35 PM: Challenge brief & a walkthrough of the MicroLumin SDK 7:00 PM: Team formation: 30-second idea pitches, then a mixer to find teammates 7:45 PM: Teams locked, hardware handed out, devices set up 8:00 PM: Hacking begins 9:00 PM: SDK help desk & mentor office hours open 11:30 PM: Late-night snacks Overnight 12:00 AM to 8:00 AM: Overnight build, with a quiet rest area for anyone who needs a nap All night: A MicroLumin engineer is online for live SDK support (it's afternoon in Shenzhen) Saturday, Nov 21 8:00 AM: Breakfast & coffee 9:00 AM: Morning check-in: each team shares where they are & what's blocking them 10:00 AM: Workshop with Dr. Zhaoen Dai, MicroLumin's founder & CEO, on designing for AR & waveguide displays 11:00 AM: Workshop: [Topic & speaker TBD] 12:30 PM: Lunch 2:00 PM: Code freeze, project submissions due 2:15 PM: Demo expo: judges go table to table & teams demo on the device 3:45 PM: Finalists announced 4:00 PM: Finalists demo on stage: 3 minutes, worn by the team, plus 2 minutes of Q&A 4:45 PM: Talk by Dr. Dai on AR & where the AI industry is heading, while judges deliberate 5:30 PM: Awards 6:00 PM: Hardware return & wrap PrizesTBD JudgesTBD Who Should AttendHardware Founders Engineers at companies like Meta, Amazon & Google who want to build on AR hardware iOS & Android developers Hardware tinkerers, embedded & computer vision engineers Product designers interested in spatial & glanceable UI Spots are limited & approval is required. You don't need prior AR experience, just the drive to build something real overnight. SponsorsMicroLumin: Shenzhen-based maker of AR display glasses, including the M6 series & several CES 2026 award winners. MicroLumin is providing the hardware & SDK support for teams. HostsSomya Gupta: The face of the NYC startup ecosystem. Stephen Jin: Johnson MBA '27 at Cornell, board director at Gona Semiconductor, Angel Investing Waftech - Founded in 2007 & based in Penang, Malaysia, Waftech designs & manufactures wafer-handling & automation equipment for semiconductor manufacturing. Waftech delivers end-to-end, from R&D & design through manufacturing & after-sales service, & is ISO 9001:2015 certified. Waftech is a subsidiary of Gona Semiconductor, a Shanghai-headquartered equipment group. Olivia Iarmak: AI Quality Ops Lead at Meta Reality Labs working on Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses, & co-founder of HQ Labs. Vishal Kharker: Lead Product Manager at RTX Fintech & Research, previously at Barclays & RBC Capital Markets. Info site: https://worn-hacks.com

events.name: Deal Flow - NYC's First VC Hackathon
events.description: Event DescriptionNew York is getting its first VC hackathon, & you're building for the people who write the checks. Deal Flow is a one-day, in-person hackathon hosted by localhost:nyc & VCLab. You get 9 hours to build working products for the real problems VCs face every day. Partners from NYC's top funds judge live, & the best teams leave with intros to those funds. Problem StatementVenture capital runs on spreadsheets, gut feel & endless inbox triage. Firms move billions of dollars with tools that haven't changed in a decade. Your challenge is to build software that helps VCs find better companies, make faster decisions & support their founders after the check clears. The Challenge ThemeSourcing: finding breakout founders before everyone else does Diligence: market maps, competitive analysis & memo drafting Portfolio ops: helping funds support their companies at scale LP reporting: making fund updates less painful & more useful Deal pipeline & CRM workflows that VCs will actually use What to Expect9 hours of focused building, 9 AM to 6 PM Real VC problems, with investors in the room to test your ideas against Teams of 4 Time to meet founders, engineers & investors from across NYC Live demos to a panel of VC judges at the end of the day Food & drinks all day PrizesTo Be Announced. JudgesAbeera Saeed is the Ventures Principal at Plug & Play, investing in Enterprise & AI B2B SaaS companies from Pre-Seed to Series A. Michael Barone - Associate at Everywhere Ventures, a global pre-seed venture capital firm. D. J. Patel - VC | 3x exited founder. Garrett Higgins is a skilled operator with experience running Finance & GTM Operations at high growth companies & an angel investor. He loves helping founders win & drive growth. Radhika Khandelwal builds AI agents for a living as a product leader at Wand AI, & she's spent years in the VC world seeing what makes startups stick. She'll want to see both slick code & a real business. Bettina Sosa is co-founder & CEO of Yaven, building a local-first AI workforce for independent businesses. Who Should AttendPre-seed & seed founders Engineers Builders who have felt the pain of fundraising firsthand Anyone curious about how venture capital actually works from the inside You don't need VC experience or a finished idea. Just show up ready to build. SponsorsSeedLegals is your one-stop legal platform from idea to Series A & beyond. Incorporate your Delaware C Corp or convert your to a C Corp, raise with SAFEs, manage your cap table, give stock options to your team, do a priced round, all on one platform, for way less than paying lawyers, with an amazing team to help. Hostslocalhost:nyc: Making NYC the biggest startup ecosystem in the world. Tracy Huang: VC Lab & CEO of Interlink IQ Olivia Iarmak - Researcher | Meta Reality Labs. ConnNext is a next-gen mobile app & community built for career growth. Visionbrew helps people be 2 places at once with 3D AI avatars. Pulse NYC AI - A community, incubator, & venture fund built for founders, researchers, & technologists shaping the future of AI in New York City.

events.name: Ugly Talk - Building Fandoms In 2027
events.description: A customer buys once. A fan brings people with them. Getting there takes months of showing up. Listening. Keeping promises. Giving people a reason to care when you are no longer in their feed. This Ugly Talk gets into the work behind real fandom. The creator calls that went nowhere. The community plays that looked dead for months. The moment loyal customers pushed back & the brand had to answer. No follower-count victory laps. Just the decisions, mistakes, & proof behind communities that stick.  Why you should be in this room.Hear how consumer brands turn one-time buyers into people who recruit other buyers. Learn which signals reveal loyalty before revenue catches up. See how brands build with creators from the first idea through launch. Learn what to keep doing when the community looks quiet. Hear how leaders respond when their biggest supporters become their loudest critics.  What's on the table.Building superfans at scale: What makes customers care enough to bring other people in. Creators & co-creation: How brands share the build instead of buying a post at the end. Measuring fandom: The numbers that matter after likes & reach stop telling the truth. The slow build: What to do when months of work look like nothing is happening. When fandom turns: What community pushback reveals about the trust you built. Managing a crisis: How to respond fast, own the miss, & keep trust intact.  Who's hosting it. Rob Fajardo - Founder, LeaveNormalBehind Rob Fajardo is an entrepreneur, operator, & cultural architect whose work centers on a simple question: what does winning look like? Early in his career, Rob helped drive the fidget spinner phenomenon by building & activating an influencer network across Instagram & Facebook, reaching over 150 million people. Since then, he has worked with brands including DoorDash, Lowe's, FedEx, Converse, Red Bull, & Wyndham Resort Group, & has been featured in Forbes, Entrepreneur, Thrive Global, & BuzzFeed. Rob is the founder of Leave Normal Behind, a global network of purpose-driven leaders, creators, & investors built around meaningful connection, personal growth, & human flourishing. Over the past decade, he has brought together people across industries & generations through designed gatherings & strategic collaborations. He also serves as Head of Operations for the School of Content at The School of Hard Knocks, one of the world's largest business media platforms with 26M+ followers, where he coaches business owners generating six to nine figures on go-to-market. In addition, he is a Strategic Advisor to The AI Collective, the world's largest AI community, with 70,000+ members across 25+ global chapters.  Who's getting in.CPG & consumer-brand founders building a customer base that sticks. Brand & community leaders responsible for loyalty & retention. Creators building their own audience or working with consumer brands. Marketers who care about advocacy, repeat purchases, & long-term growth.  About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough "aha!" moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons & insights. With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami, we've built a vibrant community of thousands of founders & industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape. Official Website: UglyTalk.com Important Notice for Ugly Talk AttendeesAdmission & Confirmation Attendance is by approval only. Approved guests will receive a confirmation email along with a calendar invite. Invitations are non-transferable. Additional event details will be shared as the event approaches. Code of Conduct By attending, you agree to: Maintain respect & professionalism, adhering to all venue rules, policies, & applicable laws. Refrain from harassment, discrimination, unwelcome sexual advances (verbal or physical), intimidation, or inappropriate photography/recording. Report any violations to the event hosts immediately. Violations may result in immediate removal from the event & exclusion from future invitations. Liability & Risk Participation is voluntary & at your own risk. The event organizers, hosts, sponsors, & venue are not liable for personal injury, lost or stolen belongings, or any other damages incurred during the event. Media Consent By attending, you grant the event organizers & affiliated entities the right to capture, use, & distribute photos, videos, & audio recordings of you for promotional, marketing, & other lawful purposes, including digital & print media, advertising, & social media. You waive any right to inspect or approve the final materials & release all claims related to their use. Communications By registering, you agree to receive marketing & promotional communications from Ugly Talk & its co-hosts, partners, & sponsors. You may unsubscribe at any time. Agreement If you do not agree to this Code of Conduct, please refrain from attending the event.  Join us to stay updated on upcoming Ugly Talk events! Join the newsletter  Follow us on IG  Official website

events.name: Responsible Tech Summit - Embedding Accountability AI Era
events.description: At a time when artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping society, the conversation is shifting from broad principles to real-world accountability. The 2026 summit will explore the theme of Principles to Power: Embedding Accountability in the AI Era. For years, the Responsible Tech field has been guided by ethical frameworks, voluntary commitments, & emerging standards. Today, the challenge is clear: how do we translate those ideas into systems of governance, oversight, & design that ensure innovation does not come at the expense of safety, rights, or trust? The Responsible Tech Summit is designed as a curated convening for 375 leaders that helps align & shape the direction of the movement. Participants will include global governance leaders, AI researchers, industry practitioners, policy experts, civil society advocates, & philanthropic leaders who are building the infrastructure of accountability for the digital age. Through keynotes, panels, & conversations, attendees will explore topics such as accountability by design, platform oversight, youth online safety, the Responsible Tech economy, & the evolving global regulatory landscape. All ticket proceeds fund free resources & services for the Responsible Tech community that our organization provides. Can't make it in person? The event will be livestreamed for free on All Tech Is Human's YouTube page, where recordings will also be available afterward. - Are you a journalist looking to potentially cover the Responsible Tech Summit? Reach out to Hello@AllTechIsHuman.org. Speakers for the Responsible Tech Summit 2026 Camille Francois - President, ROOST Eli Pariser - Co-Director, New_ Public Cathy O'Neil, Founder, Author, Mathematician & Data Scientist, O'Neil Risk Consulting & Algorithmic Auditing Rumman Chowdhury, CEO, Humane Intelligence PBC Alex Bores, Assembly Member, New York City's 73rd District Beth Goldberg, Founding Executive Director of Humanity AI Sinead Bovell, Founder, WAYE Alexis Wales, Chief Information Security Officer, GitHub Alison Lee, Chief R&D Officer, The Rithm Project Amanda Craig, General Manager of Responsible AI Public Policy, Microsoft Anya Schiffrin, Director, Media Program, Columbia University (SIPA) Carrie Varoquiers, Chief Impact Officer, Workday Joshua Elder, Senior Vice President & Head of Grantmaking, Siegel Family Endowment Julie Cordua, CEO, Thorn Fernanda Del Castillo, Director of AI Governance, Mastercard Kathy Pham, Faculty & Senior Fellow, Product & Responsible AI, Harvard University Kristin Hansen, Executive Director, Civic Health Project J. Trevor Hughes, President & CEO of IAPP Shreya Singh Hernndez, Senior Manager, Aspen Digital, The Aspen Institute Melanie Plaza, Chief Technology Officer, AE Studio Courtney Radsch, Director of the Center for Media & Digital Governance, Open Markets Institute; Fellow, Brookings Institution Andrew Rasiej, Founder, Civic Hall Clement Wolf, Director, Responsible AI Strategy, Google Hale Sirin, Program Scientist, Schmidt Sciences AI & Advanced Computing Institute Jeff Collins, Director of Trust & Safety, Amazon Web Services Alisar Mustafa, Head of AI Safety, Duco Experts   Agenda10:00 - 11:00 am ET | Check-in & Networking 11:00 - 11:10 am | Welcome remarks 11:15 - 11:45 am | Panel: Beyond Benchmarks: Turning Evaluations into Enforceable Standards 11:50 - 12:00 pm | Lightning talk 12:05 - 12:35 pm | Panel: Safety by Design: Accountability at the Intersection of AI, Industry, & Advocacy 12:40 - 1:40 pm | Lunch 1:45 - 2:05 pm | Fireside Chat: Open-Source, Open Questions: Transparency in the Age of AI 2:10 - 2:40 pm | Panel: Shared Risk, Shared Responsibility: Rethinking Responsible AI Governance 2:45 - 3:05 pm | Fireside Chat: Alignment in Practice: Building AI That Wants to be Good 3:05 - 3:30 pm | Networking break 3:30 - 4:00 pm | Panel: Trust as Strategy & the Fight Against AI-Enabled Fraud 4:05 - 4:15 pm | Keynote 4:15 - 4:25 pm | Lightning Talk 4:30 - 5:00 pm | Panel: Rebuilding the Commons: Community & Pluralism in the AI Era 5:05 - 5:25 pm | Fireside Chat: Looking Back to Look Ahead: Co-Designing AI After a Decade of Tech Lessons 5:25 - 5:30 pm | Closing remarks *See the full agenda & bios of our speakers here.   Sponsors for the Responsible Tech Summit 2026Special thanks to our strategic partners, Columbia World Projects, Forum One, & Highspring, for helping bring this critical conversation to life. WorkdayWorkday operates at the heart of the enterprise - HR, finance, & IT - where the margin for error is effectively zero. By tightly coupling AI with the context, guardrails, & trusted processes that run the business, Workday goes beyond AI that assists work to agents that do the work & drive measurable outcomes. More than 11,500 organizations worldwide, including more than 65% of the Fortune 500, trust Workday to deliver. MastercardMastercard is a global technology company in the payments industry, connecting consumers, financial institutions, merchants, & governments in more than 200 countries & territories. The company is committed to building a sustainable, inclusive digital economy that benefits everyone, everywhere. PinterestPinterest is a visual search & discovery platform where people find inspiration, curate ideas & shop products - all in a positive place online. Headquartered in San Francisco, Pinterest has over 600 million monthly active users worldwide. MicrosoftMicrosoft is a global technology leader empowering every person & organization on the planet to achieve more through its platforms & productivity tools. The company is committed to advancing responsible AI & ensuring emerging technologies are developed & deployed safely & ethically. Siegel Family EndowmentSiegel Family Endowment takes an inquiry-driven approach to grantmaking, informed by the scientific method. As technology reshapes society, we fund organizations asking critical questions about its impact on learning, work, & infrastructure. Founded in 2011 by David Siegel, co-founder & co-chairman of Two Sigma, we advance technology in the public interest, supporting research & initiatives that imagine a more inclusive, resilient technology-driven society. AE StudioAE Studio is an applied AI & AI alignment company that builds software products for clients while advancing research on making advanced AI systems safe & beneficial. Its recent work with Anthropic, GRAM, trains dangerous knowledge into removable modules so it can be stripped from a model before release. AE Studio reinvests its commercial success into neglected approaches to AI alignment research. Learn more at ae.studio. GoogleGoogle's mission is to organize the world's information & make it universally accessible & useful. As a leader in AI & computing, the company is focused on developing technology responsibly to benefit people & society. Kapor FoundationThe Kapor Foundation works at the intersection of racial equity & technology to expand access to K-12 computer science & postsecondary tech pathways, improve tech accountability & worker protections, & increase investments in infrastructure & innovation. We advocate for policy changes, build the capacity of partners, conduct research, support partners through grantmaking, & invest in entrepreneurship & VC. We believe that when technology includes diverse perspectives & is harnessed to address societal challenges, we can transform the tech ecosystem for Black, Latine, & Native communities, & society as a whole. Kapor Foundation works collectively with the Kapor Center family of organizations, Kapor Capital, & SMASH to reimagine & reconstruct a more inclusive & equitable technology sector. Check out Kapor Foundation's Responsible AI Principles for Advancing a More Equitable Innovation Future. IAPPThe IAPP is a policy-neutral, not-for-profit association founded in 2000 with a mission to define, promote & improve the professions of privacy, AI governance & digital responsibility globally. Civic Health ProjectCivic Health Project is a nonpartisan nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing scalable solutions to the dangerous divisions that threaten American democracy. Since our founding in 2019, we have supported more than 75 academic researchers, grassroots practitioners, creatives, & technologists who are helping reduce polarization, strengthen civic norms, & foster social cohesion. Today, Civic Health Project focuses primarily on exploring the vast potential of promising new technologies to help resolve conflict, improve civil discourse & deliberation, foster social cohesion, & uphold societal norms. Normsy.ai, our flagship in-house project, brings this mission to life. It identifies toxic content in real time & equips users to respond with respectful, trust-building messages grounded in social science & supported by artificial intelligence. events.description: An Exclusive Executive Dinner for Growth & Performance Leaders in SoHo  An evening at a standout Soho restaurant for a small group of senior marketing leaders responsible for growth, acquisition, & paid media across social media channels like Meta, TikTok, YouTube, & CTV. The conversation for the evening: The Future of Video Ads in the Age of AI: As AI automates media buying & makes video production nearly unlimited, creative decisioning becomes the new performance advantage. Just an off-the-record conversation with senior peers over dinner in SoHo. Who it's for Senior in-house marketing leaders only: CMO, VP, Head of, Director roles in User Acquisition, Growth, Performance Marketing, or Paid Social at consumer brands actively investing on video. events.description: Making Sense of Purpose in the Age of AIA fireside chat with Suneet Bhatt When AI can do more of our work, what do we want to do with our lives? It's easy to get caught up in keeping up. But between learning the next tool & planning the next career move, it's worth pausing to ask: What am I moving toward? Join us at Bang & Olufsen for a fireside conversation with Suneet Bhatt, author of Making Sense of Purpose. Together, we'll explore what gives us direction, what matters beyond our job titles, & how to build a meaningful life as AI changes the way we work. We'll talk about finding clarity when the future feels uncertain, building momentum without having every answer, & discovering your kiran, or ray of light. Not a perfect five-year plan, but a clearer sense of what matters to you & a first step toward it. Expect personal stories, practical ideas, & room for your questions. Whether you're rethinking your career, starting something new, or simply wondering what comes next, you'll be in good company. Come enjoy light food, drinks, & thoughtful conversation in a beautiful space. You don't need to have it all figured out to be part of the conversation. A little light, passed on Contribute what you can. Donations of $20 or more include a complimentary signed copy of Making Sense of Purpose & we'll match a gift copy of the book to people who need them, helping a little clarity & encouragement reach beyond the room. Please be advised: Unfortunately, space is very limited at these community events & we can not always accept everyone we would like to. If you are not accepted to this event, please keep applying! events.name: The Growth Council - Off-the-Record Problem Solving For Scaling Founders
events.description: Are you a founder or entrepreneur? If so, you know that scaling your business past Seed & Series A can expose many gaps in your business all at once - talent/employee friction, messy positioning, legal nuances, capital efficiency...and the list goes on. And while most founder events only focus on panels with generic advice, our new event "The Growth Council" aims to do something different. The mission of this event is to give the founder community access to experts who can help you at your specific stage of growth. The Growth Council is a small-group, peer-to-peer advisory session built specifically for Seed to Series B founders who want to explore their challenges with experts from across the industry & outside their network. Founders will have access to experts in various areas, rotating at specific intervals to ensure they meet with as many experts as possible (think speed dating, but less awkward). These conversations are meant to challenge assumptions & empower founders with new perspectives on their most pressing problems. You'll walk away with fresh perspectives, a bigger network, & connections who can help facilitate you on your journey towards success. The Expert Council Bring us your founder questions, your bottlenecks, or gut-check a current decision & get actionable takeaways from those who have been there before. You'll meet with cross-functional leaders such as: TJ Allison (Sales Advisor & Executive Coach, TJAllison.com) - Sales expert who focuses on revenue & the "Inner Game" to grow revenue & sense of self. Simon Gibson (Fractional VP of Marketing, Formerly GIPHY) - Marketing leader who blends creative storytelling & data-driven strategy to build culturally relevant brands & scale businesses. Rebekah Huber (Cofounder, Kindred Works) - Ops specialist who builds the systems that give founders their time back. Anna Kaplan (Founder & CEO, Narrativ By AK) - Narrative & messaging specialist who helps founders craft a story that wins the room. Marc Kaufman (Partner, Potomac Law Group) - Intellectual property attorney specializing in creating IP assets that increase funding. Fractional CFO TBD Agenda 6:00 PM - 6:30 PM | Arrivals & Light BitesCasual networking over food & drinks before we kick off. 6:30 PM - 6:45 PM | Council & Sponsor IntrosQuick, 60-second introductions from each expert on the specific fires they help extinguish. 6:45 PM - 7:45 PM | Growth Council HuddlesRotate at regular intervals. At each table, state your burning question, get sharp direct feedback from the functional expert, & compare notes with peer founders. 7:45 PM - 8:30 PM | Drinks & Direct ConnectionsInformal wrap-up to continue conversations with experts & founders. Who Should Apply This event is strictly curated for Seed, Series A, & Series B founders / co-founders leading venture-backed tech startups. Capacity is strictly capped at 35 founders to maintain small group sizes & high-signal discussions. Requests to join will be reviewed to preserve the peer dynamic. Hosted By: Kindred Works - Fractional operations & employee engagement partners for high-growth startups. Narrativ by AK - Strategic positioning & narrative development for founders. Tavern - A Physical Social Network Want to host your own event? events.name: Vibecoding 101
events.description: A 4-week scaffolded, hands-on introduction to vibecoding for beginners.Vibecoding, or AI-assisted software development, is the practice of guiding coding agents to translate your ideas into working software - without writing code yourself. We see vibecoding as 4 different product skills in a trench coat. While they may not write code, effective vibecoders mobilize concepts & workflows across software engineering, design, quality assurance, & product management. This course is a scaffolded, hands-on introduction to the fundamental skills & concepts required for a sustainable vibecoding practice. Students will learn through a combination of short lectures, applied exercises, personalized feedback, & demos to peers. We begin by working with coding agents in a multiplayer environment designed for beginners. We will create interactive frontends, learn the basics of the terminal, build integrations with APIs, & create stateful, full-stack applications with a database & user authentication. By the end of the course, students will transition to state-of-the-art coding agents installed on their personal machines, which they will use to build & deploy a working prototype to the web. SyllabusSession 1: Coding agents & frontends We introduce the course & core concepts of vibecoding. We introduce a basic taxonomy of web architecture. Students practice creating basic interactive frontends. Session 2: CLIs, APIs, & the terminal We cover core backend & data concepts. We gently introduce the terminal. Students practice writing simple CLI programs, & integrating with an API. Session 3: Stateful full-stack applications We cover databases & user authentication; students build a full stack app. Session 4: Deployment & demos The final session covers deployment. Students demo their prototypes for the class. Learning OutcomesAcquire core vocabulary & mental models for software development. Prompt coding agents to create frontends, API integrations, & stateful applications. Be able to translate your ideas into working prototypes using AI. Practice presenting your product ideas to peers & colleagues. ResourcesThis new world of ours rewards being a dilettante with a vague mental map of vast territories.- Ted Underwood There is a new kind of coding I call vibecoding,' where you fully give in to the vibes, embrace exponentials, & forget that the code even exists. It's possible because the LLMs (e.g. Cursor Composer w Sonnet) are getting too good it's not really coding - I just see stuff, say stuff, run stuff, & copy paste stuff, & it mostly works.- Andrej Karpathy Slow is smooth, & smooth is fast.- Anonymous ScholarshipIndex scholarships are designed to benefit members of our community who do not have expendable cash to pay for the course, & those for whom the class price is not accessible. These need-based scholarships will go to the candidates who best demonstrate why they should be chosen for the free spot to our class based on the following criteria: Belong to groups that are traditionally underrepresented in the graphic design & creative industries Do not have jobs that would pay for these courses as professional development Cannot independently afford the class at list price Share our value of intentional community The number of selected applicants chosen is subject to the discretion of Index & the instructor, but every course will select at least one. Apply for a scholarship here. Applications close October 20th. Instructor Bio Bill Roberts is an independent technologist based in Brooklyn. Drawn to socially beneficial uses of technology, he has 10 years of software engineering experience on teams spanning healthcare, climate, politics, & education. He runs Legible Labs, a product studio that helps clients design & build AI applications. As a research engineer, he has coauthored papers in peer-reviewed journals & conferences that empirically evaluate the capabilities of AI in educational settings. Bill holds a BA in Computer Science & Sociology from Columbia University.   Refunds We get that things come up, but we rely on headcounts to make our programs viable. If you request a refund... More than 4 weeks before the program begins  100% refundMore than 2 weeks before the program begins  50% refundFewer than 2 weeks before the program begins  No refund Thanks for understanding & for supporting our ability to provide cool offerings through your purchase. Media Release Clause By attending this event, you consent to being photographed, filmed, or recorded, & grant Index Space permission to use this content for promotional or informational purposes.

events.name: Ugly Talk: Collecting Skills To Be An Operator
events.description: You got here on the skills you already had. Building, selling, whatever you happen to be good at. That is what got the thing off the ground. Then the business starts asking for skills nobody taught you. Not the parts that made the company exist. The parts that keep it running. You don't have to do all of it yourself. You have a network, you can hire fractional, the tools are actually good now. But you can't direct what you don't understand. That is where founders get hurt. This Ugly Talk names the gaps - sales & marketing, money, people, process - & how founders who collected those skills the hard way actually did it.  Why you should be in this room.Hear which operator skills founders wish they had picked up sooner. Learn how much you need to know about a function to hire for it & direct it. Get the tells that a part of your business is running on hope. Find out what people got wrong first, & what it cost them. Leave with a short list of what to learn next & what to hand off.  What's on the table.Collecting the skills: how the jobs you already did quietly trained you, & where they left holes. Sales & marketing: what a founder still has to own after hiring help. Money: the numbers to watch weekly, & the shortcuts that get expensive. People: the first few hires, & what a bad one actually costs. Directing help: network, fractional, AI - how much you have to understand to use any of it well.  Featured speakers.Sarah Larson - Founder, People Magnets Sarah is a People Expert with over 25 years of experience in HR, Life Sciences, & venture capital. She specializes in helping companies identify people challenges, build strong teams, & develop strategies that support growth. She has served as Head of HR for several Life Sciences companies, including Foundation Medicine, where she joined as the second employee & helped grow the team to over 600 people. Sarah also spent eight years in venture capital as Partner & Chief People Officer at Third Rock Ventures & Chief People Officer at S32. She has advised CEOs, boards, & growing companies as a strategic advisor & interim HR leader. At Magnet, she combines her deep HR experience with a people-first approach to help organizations build strong cultures & thrive. Jeremy Chow - Founder & CEO, Tactus Jeremy Chow is the Founder & CEO of Tactus, an accessibility technology company that has built a wearable device that translates music into vibrations, making music more inclusive & accessible for the Deaf community. As a technical founder with a background in Mechanical Engineering, he started this project through a collaboration with a Deaf dancer & has built & designed the technology from prototype to a product on the market. What began in Boston has since grown into a global venture, with active involvement in innovation ecosystems across Tokyo & Hong Kong. Phil Slabine - Founder, Not Dorks Accounting & Finance Phil Slabine is co-founder of Not Dorks Accounting & Finance, a managed service firm providing early-stage & growth companies with the support they need. He spent 15 years in corporate accounting, most recently as corporate controller at a fast-growing robotics company, before leaving to build his own business. He spends most of his time on the unglamorous parts of building a business - cash runway, pricing, & the plumbing of your financial model - & thinks that since founders have to do accounting anyway, they might as well get amazing value out of it. Based in Boston.  Who's getting in.Boston founders past the idea stage, with real money on the line. First-time founders suddenly running functions they have never run. Operators who inherited sales, finance, or people because somebody had to. Anyone who has said "I'll figure that part out later," & later showed up.  About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough "aha!" moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons & insights. With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami, we've built a vibrant community of thousands of founders & industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape. Official Website: UglyTalk.com  Important Notice for Ugly Talk AttendeesAdmission & Confirmation Attendance is by approval only. Approved guests will receive a confirmation email along with a calendar invite. Invitations are non-transferable. Additional event details will be shared as the event approaches. Code of Conduct By attending, you agree to: Maintain respect & professionalism, adhering to all venue rules, policies, & applicable laws. Refrain from harassment, discrimination, unwelcome sexual advances (verbal or physical), intimidation, or inappropriate photography/recording. Report any violations to the event hosts immediately. Violations may result in immediate removal from the event & exclusion from future invitations. Liability & Risk Participation is voluntary & at your own risk. The event organizers, hosts, sponsors, & venue are not liable for personal injury, lost or stolen belongings, or any other damages incurred during the event. Media Consent By attending, you grant the event organizers & affiliated entities the right to capture, use, & distribute photos, videos, & audio recordings of you for promotional, marketing, & other lawful purposes, including digital & print media, advertising, & social media. You waive any right to inspect or approve the final materials & release all claims related to their use. Communications By registering, you agree to receive marketing & promotional communications from Ugly Talk & its co-hosts, partners, & sponsors. You may unsubscribe at any time. Agreement If you do not agree to this Code of Conduct, please refrain from attending the event.  Join us to stay updated on upcoming Ugly Talk events! Join the newsletter  Follow us on IG  Official website
