events.name: Rooms That Pay
events.description: ROOMS THAT PAYThe Presence-to-Pipeline Workshop A 90-minute live workshop for established business owners to leave every event with paying clients, without feeling salesy. You showed up. You spent the money. So why aren't events paying you back? You shook 50 hands, had a few great conversations, & sent the follow-ups. Then nothing. The "let's stay in touch" went nowhere, & another event quietly became another expense. Your next clients, partners, & investors are already in those rooms. This workshop shows you what to do once you're inside, & after you leave. Rooms That Pay is a 90-minute live workshop for established business owners & execs to go from polite networkers to people magnets, & leave every event with paying clients, without feeling salesy. This is for you if you're: Successful, but stuck at a plateau & ready for the next level Growing through trust, referrals, & face-to-face relationships Great 1-on-1, but rooms full of strangers still feel like work The Presence-to-Pipeline Method Show Up: Drop the work persona & walk in as fully you Connect: Have easy, genuinely helpful conversations that make hiring you the obvious next step Convert: Capture leads, follow up effectively, & turn every event into paying clients Why it works: People buy from people they trust. When they can see who you are & that you know your stuff, you never have to pitch. Personality + expertise = sales. You'll walk out with: Ease in every conversation, no scripts or rehearsed pitches A way to lead with help instead of selling Permission to bring your real personality into the room A simple system to turn "nice to meet you" into signed business Your hostsGal BePole, founders' mentor & creator of Dance Speak, has spent 15 years training people across 13+ countries to step onto stages & into rooms as fully themselves.Greg Bumble, EventReps, helps businesses capture, organize, & convert event conversations into measurable pipeline. If even 2 new clients from your next event are worth $10,000 to $100,000, this is the highest-ROI 90 minutes you'll spend this quarter. Seats are limited to 20. Early-bird pricing of $50 ends November 1. Reserve your seat & make your next room highest conversion event you've had all year.

events.name: Daytona AI Builders
events.description: An event dedicated to exploring all things AI Engineering! Event partners: AWS & Antimetal Agenda 5:30 pm - 6:00 pmWelcome Gathering & Opening Remarks Marijan Cipcic, Principal Events Manager at Daytona  6:00 pm - 6:15 pmTalk "Forkable Sandboxes for Long-Running Agents" Muhammad Annas Hashmi, DevRel at Daytona Outline:Agents are starting to do real software work: installing dependencies, editing files, running tests, starting servers, & debugging over long sessions. But most AI systems still treat each run like a disposable prompt-response loop. That breaks down once the useful state lives not just in tokens, but in the actual machine. This talk is about the runtime layer agents need to become reliable builders. I'll show how forkable Daytona sandboxes let you pause at important moments in an agent run, branch the environment, & sample multiple continuations from the same machine state. For builders, this turns long-running agent workflows into something you can inspect, compare, recover, & eventually optimize.  6:15 pm - 6:30 pmTalk "Multi-Agent Investment AI Assistant built on Amazon Bedrock Agentcore" Sam Farber, Sr. Solutions Architect at AWS Outline:Investment research teams spend days manually gathering data across markets, risk metrics, sentiment indicators, financial statements, & alternative data sources before synthesizing findings into actionable reports. This talk will show how a multi-agent AI system can automate that workflow. A supervisor agent breaks down a research question, delegates to 10 domain-specific specialists running in parallel, & compiles their findings into a comprehensive investment report. The system maintains conversation memory across each agent, allowing researchers to have targeted conversations & follow-ups with each specialized agent.  6:30 pm - 6:45 pmTalk "Building a World Model for Production Agents" Shreyas Iyer, Co-founder & CTO of Antimetal Outline:Production systems are increasingly complex, with critical knowledge scattered across code, infrastructure, telemetry, & people's heads. In this talk, we'll explore how to build a persistent world model that gives AI agents a shared understanding of production. We'll break down four foundational layers: physical topology, temporal changes, causal relationships, & organizational context to show how they enable agents to investigate incidents, assess changes, & proactively manage production, building on what they've learned across tasks.  6:45 pm - 6:55 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker TBA Outline:TBA  6:55 pm - 7:05 pmTalk "Letting AI agents use credentials they never see" Chase Erickson, Solutions Engineer at Infisical Outline:Infisical manages the secrets your Daytona agents depend on. The Daytona secret sync pushes them from Infisical to your Daytona organization & keeps them current, rotations included. Infisical's Agent Vault, a proxy, adds the credential to requests bound for the services you configure, so the agent never sees it. In this talk, we'll show how an agent in a Daytona sandbox calls an API without ever holding the secret.  7:05 pm - 8:30 pmNetworkingWith pizzas & beverages About event This is dynamic gathering for AI enthusiasts, innovators, & professionals to collaborate, share ideas, & explore the latest advancements in artificial intelligence. Whether you're building AI products, researching cutting-edge algorithms, or simply passionate about the field, join us to connect, learn, & drive the future of AI forward.

events.name: The Deployment Room: 6 Active Funds, Funding Founders (Seed to Series A+)
events.description: The Builder Series: A 60,000+ member community redefining what networking looks like curating founders, investors into intentional rooms built for experiences people remember & relationships that last. It's a direct line to the most ambitious builders. Find us here: Instagram  LinkedIn  TikTok  Facebook  X : WhatsApp Broad Channel (Not a GC) August was our pilot. Here's how it performed. Our intent 20 founders, 6 investors. The real turnout: 30 guests: 20 founders, 10 capital allocators $70M+ raised collectively by the founders present $3.5M average raised per founder $2.3B+ combined AUM across the investors $1M average check, $100K minimum $10M+ in live check capacity This is today objective: Every founder in the room is doing $1M+ in ARR or has raised a round of $1M or more. Raised your 1st round, onto your 2nd, or bootstrapped to $1M ARR? You're in the right place. Every investor here is from our network. We're curating this room deliberately, matching founders to the investors most likely to be a fit, & making the introduction ourselves. The goal here: Getting founders funded by our investor network. The 6 Investors joining us from our network: (More will be joining) Francesca Poupel: F&G Capital Partners (Managing Partner): Backing founders from pre-seed to Series A in AI, fintech, & blockchain, writing $300K-$500K checks & partnering closely with teams as they scale. Mahir Laul (Partner) representing Laul Global a family office & holding company operating four interconnected pillars: Education Engine, Real Assets, Future Ventures, & Acquisitions. One integrated system. One long-term vision. Laul Global is owned & operated by the Laul family. We started with a single student recruitment company. We built it into one of Canada's most diversified education holding groups. Today the portfolio spans institutions, edtech, real estate, & a tech venture studio, with reach across 20+ countries & no plans to slow down.  Triet Leminh: Principal, LMT Partners: Lawyer, founder, & investor backing pre-seed to Series A founders building in enterprise & regulated industries. Writing $200K-$300K checks.  Andrew Antar (General Partner, AG Venture Capital): A generalist fund backing extraordinary founders, sector agnostic. Also a Venture Partner at Arcadian Capital, focused on late-stage secondaries & pre-IPO tech, & served as Crypto Policy Advisor to the NYC Office of the Mayor - advising on the city's crypto regulatory framework & organizing the NYC Crypto Summit at Gracie Mansion. He is also founder of Tune.FM, a tokenized music streaming platform & digital asset marketplace, & co-founded Clear Quantum, a stealth quantum AI startup. Gonzalo Quincot (Founder, Sinober): Sinober is a financial intelligence platform that combines public & private market intelligence with institutional-grade methodology, corporate finance & proprietary AI tools to sharpen investment & capital decisions for individuals & businesses. Invests in automation, robotics, data centers & applied AI.  Shilpi Nayak: (Founder & General Partner, 434 VC): Invests in early-stage technical founders across AI, infrastructure, physical AI & emerging technology. She is also the founder of House of 434, a community bringing together founders, investors & industry leaders.  Pranav Jajapur (Co-Founder, ZERON Ventures): ZERON is an early-stage venture fund with an execution platform behind it, backing real-world technology, AI, healthcare, deep tech & climate companies building in the physical world, inside biology. Pre-seed through Series A with core deployment at seed, writing $400K-$500k checks. Preferred focus is institutionally-anchored AI: structural research relationships at academic institutions, spinouts, & founder-led research programs. Fund I in formation. Deploying Q1  All 6 senior investors confirmed. Part of building rooms is making sure real capital is present. Six investors actively deploying writing capital will be joining. Our first confirmed: Why we do this: Putting active investors in the same room as exceptional founders, & keeps the room small enough to ensure everyone actually meets. We value intentional networking & community. If you're here to meet the best of the best, this is the room. Our Sponsor: Composition WealthYour seat at the table is waiting. Your life is shaped by new beginnings, major decisions, & milestones. That's why when it comes to developing the strategies to achieve your financial goals, we make sure you have a seat at the table & are empowered with the knowledge & tools to shape your own future. At Composition Wealth, our goal is to empower you to reach YOUR goals. Chris Guarino, CFPBook some time: Calendly link What to expect for this: A Greek style lunch, courtesy of our team Conversations with fellow high-performing startup leaders An experience designed to facilitate new meaningful connections conversations with ambitious peers solving similar problems Event to be hosted at a beautiful private Soho loft Our intent is to bring good, smart humans together, & active investors together to fun incredible founders. Community has been lost & we are rebuilding it. Our Greek Inspired Menu: About the meal A three-course Greek menu. Appetizers & dessert are shared & open to everyone; each will get one entre. The format is intentionally part standing, part seated so you can enjoy incredible food without being anchored to a single table or a single conversation. Why we do this Our intent is simple: bring good, smart humans together, put active investors in the same room as incredible founders. Intentional community has been lost. We're rebuilding it.

events.name: Ugly Talk: CPG Founders What Worked, What Didn't & The 2027 Outlook
events.description: A bigger order can leave you with a smaller margin. That is an ugly way to learn what growth costs. CPG founders will unpack the calls shaping their brands in 2026. The channels that moved product. The partners that mattered. The pivots they had to make. Bring the decisions you are still wrestling with. Hear what these founders are changing as they finish Q4 & plan for 2027.  Why you should be in this room.Hear which channels moved product & which ate margin. Learn what founders wish they had asked before choosing a co-packer or distributor. Explore where food service & alternative distribution could fit your brand. Hear how founders responded when their customers, markets, or plans changed. Pressure-test your 2027 assumptions against what these founders are seeing in 2026.  What's on the table.Production & partners. Refining the recipe, choosing co-manufacturers, & finding partners who deliver what they promise. Distribution & margin. Which channels earned their place, which disappointed, & what founders changed in response. Finding the customer. What urban & suburban markets taught founders about who actually buys their products. Food service & other routes. Where founders are looking beyond familiar shelves to move product. The 2027 calls. Which trends held up, which missed, & what founders are carrying into next year.  Featured speakers.Liv Truesdell - Founder, FROST Buttercream Liv Truesdell started her career in consumer investment banking, working with food & beverage companies, which ultimately led her to launch FROST Buttercream. FROST is an all-natural Italian Meringue Buttercream made with real butter & egg whites, with ~57% less sugar than a leading buttercream & no palm oils, artificial dyes or preservatives. After hundreds of iterations, Liv created a new premium, refrigerated frosting segment in a category unchanged for ~71 years. FROST launched in NY/NJ retail in 2025, has since expanded across the country, & won the Startup CPG Shelfie Award within its first six months. Glenn Johnson - Marketing Consultant/Fractional CMO As a fractional CMO, Glenn Johnson works on a scalable basis with founders who are tired of bad execution, broken strategies, & agencies that just don't get it. Whether launching from scratch or fixing a brand, packaging, & positioning that fails to translate, Glenn steps in to repair what's broken & build what's next. Operating as Chief Storyteller, Creative Director, & Brand Strategist, he bridges high-level strategy with hands-on execution. From naming, logo design, & packaging to pricing architecture & true ICP targeting, Glenn nails how your brand looks, feels, & scales. A former Madison Avenue VP/Creative Director specializing in luxury & bespoke audiences, Glenn is the trusted sounding board founders rely on to turn complex ideas into scalable brand equity. Moderating Ugly Talks for me is about unpacking the messy truths & hard lessons of entrepreneurship-sharing insights in an engaged & entertaining way.  Who's getting in.Food & beverage founders building in crowded categories. Early-stage CPG founders moving from commercial kitchens to co-manufacturing. Operators working through production, distribution, pricing, & margin decisions. Buyers & investors who want to understand what helps a brand move product & stay in business.  About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough "aha!" moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons & insights. With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami, we've built a vibrant community of thousands of founders & industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape. Official Website: UglyTalk.com  Important Notice for Ugly Talk AttendeesAdmission & Confirmation Attendance is by approval only. Approved guests will receive a confirmation email along with a calendar invite. Invitations are non-transferable. Additional event details will be shared as the event approaches. Code of Conduct By attending, you agree to: Maintain respect & professionalism, adhering to all venue rules, policies, & applicable laws. Refrain from harassment, discrimination, unwelcome sexual advances (verbal or physical), intimidation, or inappropriate photography/recording. Report any violations to the event hosts immediately. Violations may result in immediate removal from the event & exclusion from future invitations. Liability & Risk Participation is voluntary & at your own risk. The event organizers, hosts, sponsors, & venue are not liable for personal injury, lost or stolen belongings, or any other damages incurred during the event. Media Consent By attending, you grant the event organizers & affiliated entities the right to capture, use, & distribute photos, videos, & audio recordings of you for promotional, marketing, & other lawful purposes, including digital & print media, advertising, & social media. events.name: Plug & Play x PMAI - Pitching Masterclass
events.description: IT IS BACK! CALLING ALL FOUNDERS! Hosted by Plug & Play NYC & Pioneering Minds AI Apply to pitch here:https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScOGgbEqUmtEHmKrhqpzynRzYX4Lk4EUC8qrYvSt6YZhXrGvg Pitching is one of the most important skills a founder develops, yet it's rarely practiced in a setting where you can iterate in real time. In this interactive workshop, founders will present their pitch, receive direct feedback, & immediately refine it live. This is a hands-on pitch masterclass where builders learn by doing, & by watching other founders sharpen their story. For founders, few people have a better perspective on how to communicate complex technology simply & convincingly. In this session, Anthony & Anna will work directly with founders in a live pitch lab, helping them sharpen their narrative & strengthen how they present their ideas. Come have a sales pitch, demo pitch, or even a VC pitch! Anthony RoseAnthony Rose is a pioneering technology entrepreneur best known as the co-creator & former CTO of the BBC iPlayer, one of the world's first large-scale streaming platforms that fundamentally changed how millions consume television. He has spent decades building technology at the intersection of consumer platforms, developer ecosystems, & emerging tech. His experience spans founding companies, leading engineering teams, & scaling global products. Nate HinmanNate Hinman is Senior Director at Plug & Play Tech Center. He works closely with startups, corporate partners, & investors to identify promising companies, accelerate growth, & create opportunities for founders to connect with some of the world's leading organizations. With extensive experience across Plug & Play's enterprise technology & AI ecosystem, Nate has seen hundreds of startups present, position, & refine their businesses. At this Pitch Masterclass, he will share an investor & accelerator perspective on what makes a pitch stand out, common mistakes founders make, & how to communicate a startup's story with greater clarity & impact. Workshop Format: Live Pitch Master Class 4-5 selected founders will pitch their startup & iterate live with Anthony. Each founder will go through the following format:  5-minute pitch 5 minutes of feedback 2-minute revised pitch incorporating feedback Watching this process unfold live helps everyone in the room see how small narrative adjustments can dramatically improve clarity, persuasion, & impact. Agenda:6:00 p.m. - Doors open6:25 p.m. - Pitches begin & live workshop7:30 p.m. - Networking session Who Should Attend This event is designed for:  AI founders preparing to raise funding Builders refining how they communicate their product Early-stage startups preparing for demo days or investor meetings Anyone interested in how strong startup narratives are built Apply to Pitch We will select 4-5 founders from the community to present during the session. If you would like to pitch your startup & receive live feedback, apply at this link! Selected founders will be notified ahead of the event. About Plug & PlayPlug & Play is the leading innovation platform, connecting startups, corporations, venture capital firms, universities, & government agencies. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, we're present in 60+ locations across 25+ industries. We offer corporate innovation programs, helping our partners in every stage of their innovation journey, from education to execution. We also run startup acceleration programs & have built an in-house VC where we've invested in hundreds of successful companies including Dropbox, Guardant Health, Honey, Lending Club, N26, PayPal, & Rappi. For more information, visit Plug & Play. About SeedLegalsSeedLegals is your full-stack legal platform from incorporation to Series A & beyond. Whether you're just starting out or gearing up for your next raise, SeedLegals is built to help founders move faster & smarter. Our tools make it simple to create & sign essential legal docs, close funding rounds, & reward your team - without burning time or cash on admin. There are over 50,000 startups on SeedLegals. If you're looking to incorporate, convert your to a C Corp, do a SAFE or a priced round, or manage your cap table, head over to SeedLegals, we're here to help you get there faster. About PRIMARYWelcome to PRIMARY, where 50,000 square feet of thoughtfully designed private & community spaces redefine coworking in downtown NYC. As the largest coworking space in FiDi, we combine premium private offices, shared workspaces, & an exclusive Lounge with top-tier amenities & exceptional service, creating the ultimate environment for your business to thrive. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

Tickets on NYC Ferry are $4.50 each way. Once you get to Governors Island, you will either get out at Soissons Landing (from Manhattan) or Yankee Pier (from Brooklyn). You can use this map of Governors Island to locate Colonels Row. The Climate Imaginarium is in Building 406A, in the middle of Colonels Row, & will have a visible sign outside the doorway. Our address is 406A Comfort Road.

events.name: What Makes A Good Life? A Guided Public Discussion On AI
events.description: The oldest question philosophers have asked is: What makes a good life? This inquiry has been important not only for guiding individual decisions, but also for shaping institutions & public policy. Now, amid the rapid changes AI is bringing to every aspect of our lives, & the growing debate about its risks & benefits, we must ask: What makes a good life, & how does AI enable or hinder it? Together, we will explore this question through prompts & shared reflection. Dr. Ece Tekbulut is a political philosopher & the founder of Thinking Through. She earned her Ph.D. from Columbia University. Through Thinking Through, she brings rigorous philosophical inquiry into everyday life, convening groups to engage with themes central to contemporary society, especially where people feel at an impasse. One such focus is AI's impact on human flourishing. Her work fosters public discourse on AI's implications & the ethical questions that surround it, & she writes on AI & society for Medyascope. Wissam Kahi is the founder of Odyssey Lead, where he helps companies capture the value of AI that usually gets lost between the boardroom & the front line. For seven years he led digital transformation across United Rentals' network of more than 1,500 locations, & he learned there that AI only sticks when the people who do the work help shape it. His essays on Substack & his novella The Panama Dilemma explore the question at the heart of tonight's discussion: what makes a good life when the machine is doing the living? Matt Konwiser is an Ecosystem Leader & Field CTO at IBM. He serves on the AI Advisory Council at the Global Technology Industry Association (GTIA) & writes a regular column on AI for CFO Intelligence Magazine. He also co-hosts AI Diatribe, a podcast built around direct, practical conversations about where AI is headed & what organizations should do about it. Anew is a gathering space & discovery center for social transformation located in NYC. We host interactive events & workshops, an accelerator program for nonprofits, & a retail lab featuring ethically-sourced coffee & gifts.

events.name: Borderless Office - Identity & Access In World Of Remote-First Growth
events.description: Join Antoine Jebara (Co-founder, JumpCloud) & Noah Landow (Founder & CEO, Macktez) for an informal conversation between an expert on scaling global technology companies & the evolution of identity & access management & the founder of a technology consulting firm. In an era defined by remote work & the rapid rise of agentic AI, the concepts of identity & security are shifting beneath our feet. As AI agents begin to act on our behalf, how do we maintain control, responsibility, & security? If an AI agent executes a transaction or accesses a database, who is truly holding the keys? Antoine brings a unique perspective from the front lines of this transition, from pioneering decentralized 2FA & password management at MYKI to driving global strategy & partner ecosystems at JumpCloud. Join us at the Macktez office, after work, over light snacks & sips, for an exploratory conversation on the challenges of scaling fast-growing global companies & how different security architectures impact our long-term safety in a cloud-first world. We will dive into the shifting landscape of encryption, the unique hurdles of managing remote-first organizations, & what it truly means to "identity" ourselves in the age of AI. Photography, audio, & video recording may occur at this event & by attending you consent to such recording media & its release, publication, exhibition, or reproduction. Event StructureWe ask that guests arrive between 7-7:30 pm to minimize disruption during the talk. 7 pm - Doors open, opportunity to mingle over snacks & sips with other attendees7:30 pm - Guests take their seats for the talk8:15 pm - Informal mixer resumes On AttendanceWe have a limited capacity. If your plans change, please update your registration so someone else can join. A bit about Macktez, & why we host this seriesMacktez is a technology consultancy collaborating with organizations going through dynamic change. Our goal is to form a lasting partnership between our team & our clients, so we can anticipate their technology challenges & help them navigate growth, disruption, & other evolving conditions. Each event in our Tte--Tech series is an opportunity to explore a specific cultural, scientific, historical, & personal issue. We fire at the synapses that connect each topic to other fields of interest & to our individual lives. And we do so in a comfortable environment to facilitate conversation that can be casual, surprising, & illuminating. To learn more, visit us at macktez.com.

events.name: SOSV Deep Tech Summit
events.description: Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. The producers of the Summit are SOSV's Ned Desmond, Ben Joffe, & Norm Amandi. SOSV's mission is to invest in deep tech companies that advance human & planetary health, & embedded in building an 800+ company portfolio with a remarkable array of companies applying AI in the physical world. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

events.description: 4 part workshop hosted by Healing Healthtech on "How to Raise Your First Priced Round." Raising your first priced round is a completely different undertaking than stacking safe notes. I want to help you skip the avoidable mistakes.  The diligence is deeper, the relevant terms are completely different, & the stakes for getting it wrong are much higher as priced round investors will almost always take board seats & protective provisions.  I've taught founders how to navigate a priced round for years & on October 27th in NYC will be conducting a public bootcamp / workshop with the highest impact aspects. Generously sponsored by Jose Rivera & Tonna Obaze of Gunderson Dettmer, Kelly Caviglia of Mercury, & Paul Brezovsky III of Qapita. Session 1: Taught by Ramesh Karra & Paul Brezovsky III's team at Qapita will focus on Data Room. What goes in, what doesn't, what investors are looking for, & how not get get tripped up. Session 2: Taught by Jose Rivera of Gunderson Dettmer will focus on the term sheet negotiation. What terms matter & which don't. How to affect outcomes that are durable & beneficial for your business. Session 3: Taught by me will focused on how to find, pitch, & close priced round investors. Session 4: Will be a panel discussion & fireside chat with 3 partners at NYC VC firms. I've purposely chosen folks who represent software & hardware investors as well as funds that operate outside of healthcare. Mat Kaliski of Acronym Venture CapitalBrian Laung Aoaeh, CFA of REFASHIOND Ventures: The Industrial Transformation FundOwen Willis of Opal Ventures & Primary Venture Partners

events.name: Hype vs Reality - AI Debunk Night
events.description: October 2026 | In-Person at Pier 57 (Livestream TBA)Hype vs. Reality: An AI Debunk Night Every week there's a new AI headline designed to make your heart race. "700 agents went rogue." "AI just crossed the terrifying line." "Your job is next." This month, we're slowing down & reading the receipts. No outside food allowed. The venue has food for sale.   The format: We take the biggest AI stories of the year & break each one down in three moves:  What the headline said  What the primary sources actually show  What's genuinely still unknown The main event: The July 2026 Hugging Face breach - the "rogue agent swarm" story that's been viewed 15M+ times. We'll walk through OpenAI's own incident report & the independent METR investigation to show what really happened (spoiler: it's less "machine uprising," more "someone didn't patch an internal proxy"). "AI will kill us all" - who's selling the timelines, & what the technical critics actually claim Apply to give a presentation here. --- Speakers:Norman BBernie T(More TBA) Sponsors:Current Sponsor list still being compiled. If you'd like to sponsor the event, please reach out to us at speaking@thoughtful.events

events.name: Is Everything Predictable - AI, Prediction Markets & Philosophy Of Foresight
events.description: In this six-week course, explore works from philosophy, cultural studies, & journalism to understand how technologies that predict the future also shape the present.The age of AI, prediction markets, & real-time data analysis brings predictive reasoning into all corners of human life. Once considered a niche academic interest area, the philosophy & politics of prediction is now relevant to everybody. Is Everything Predictable?: AI, Prediction Markets, & the Philosophy of Foresight presents scholarly material on forecasting technologies in a rigorous but highly accessible format.Drawing from a range of sources, we center scholarly texts & deeply-researched journalism that uncover the links between digital calculation, philosophical notions of time & free will, & the reality of living in an age where everything seems reducible to calculation.Guest speakers from academia & tech journalism will round out our seminar sessions, & for our final meeting, students have the option of presenting original research or creative work in an event open to the general public.SyllabusIn the early weeks of the course, we read texts from contemporary media studies & political theory that construe prediction & speculation as forms of governance. We also address probabilistic reasoning as a key feature of artificial intelligence & prediction market mechanisms, using frameworks suitable for participants without any background in STEM. As we will see, the similarities & differences between how probability works in AI versus prediction markets have much to tell us about these tools effects on everything from global warfare & the environment to creativity & personal relationships.After establishing a strong practical & theoretical foundation in AI & prediction markets, we turn to philosophical writing on the nature of freedom, self-expression, & power. These texts urge us to ask whether predictive technologies empower us with highly advanced forms of knowledge; if they inhibit us by constraining our imagination of whats possible; or if both of these outcomes might be true at once. We also read articles & listen to podcast interviews with our guest speakers in anticipation of their visits.Throughout our sessions, we examine case studies related to tech companies, specific applications, & major actors in the AI & prediction market space. The courses culminating event  a salon open to the general public  reflects our interest in connecting questions & concerns that seem highly academic to current events & everyday life. Students who choose to give presentations will participate in an additional workshop or one-on-one advising session to help them prepare. By the courses end, we will be able to navigate a world driven by predictive technologies with greater clarity, confidence, & wisdom, & to share our perspectives on them in a way that empowers those around us.Learning OutcomesConnect AI & prediction market functionalities to political & cultural affairsDevelop critical reading skills applicable to philosophy & journalismApply frameworks from the theoretical humanities to real-world developments in politics & technologyMake scholarly ideas accessible to a wide range of audiencesScholarshipsIndex scholarships are designed to benefit underrepresented groups, BIPOC members of our community, & those for whom the class price is not accessible. These need-based scholarships will go to the candidates who best demonstrate why they should be chosen for the free spot to our class. You can apply for a scholarship here.Instructor BioEmma Stamm is a writer & professor with a background in philosophy & the social study of science & technology (STS). She holds a PhD in Interdisciplinary Studies from Virginia Tech & has taught courses on the philosophy & social implications of technology at Villanova University, Virginia Tech, the Acid Horizon Research Commons, New York University, where she currently teaches for the Department of Media, Culture, & Communication. As a public-facing scholar, she has written for Vice Motherboard, Real Life Mag, & Communications of the Association for Computing Machinery, in addition to co-hosting the LEPHT HAND podcast. She is the co-founder & Executive Director of theLenox Institute for Advanced Study, which makes critical science & tech education accessible beyond academia.RefundsWe get that things come up, but we rely on headcounts to make our programs viable. If you request a refund...More than 4 weeks before the program begins  100% refundMore than 2 weeks before the program begins  50% refundFewer than 2 weeks before the program begins  No refundThanks for understanding & for supporting our ability to provide cool offerings through your purchase.Media Release ClauseBy attending this event, you consent to being photographed, filmed, or recorded, & grant Index Space permission to use this content for promotional or informational purposes.

Join us to engage with leading innovators tackling climates most complex challenges with bold, next-generation solutions.Refreshments & light hors d'oeuvres will be provided.AgendaDoors OpenKeynote + Welcome RemarksAlso on stage:  Tone Sndergaard, Director, Offshore Wind Innovation Hub at NYU Tandon Urban Future LabInnovator Lightning Pitches by the 2026 CohortEach of our Offshore Wind Innovation Hub partners has sent their most experienced innovation experts to provide feedback for each of the selected cohort companies.Sam Jung, SVP, Green Economy, New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYC EDC)Lyndie Hice-Dunton, Executive Director, National Offshore Wind Research & Development Consortium (NOWRDC)Robert Fenton, Head of Americas Generation Procurement, rstedStephan Kremers, Senior Technical Project Manager, VestasFireside Chat on Dual-Use Technology AdaptationNetworking & RefreshmentsMeet our 2026 FinalistsBlue Ocean Transfers Group (BOT) (New York, US) - Multipurpose, hybrid electric support vessel enabling maritime decarbonization.Bubble Robotics (California, US) - Resident fleet of autonomous underwater robots monitoring offshore infrastructure.Clema (New York, US) - Thermoelectric cooling vest for workers in extreme heat.Fleet Robotics (Massachusetts, US) - Data insights powered by submersible, autonomous cleaning & inspection robots.Hefring Marine (Iceland) - Intelligence platform combining onboard hardware with software to optimize marine operations.HiFIT USA (New York, US) - Impact treatment welding to enable life extension & lighter structures.NeuralX (California, US) - Underwater video & computer vision for fisheries monitoring & ecological data.Sail GTX (New York, US) - events.name: Data By Design
events.description: In conversation with Shannon Mattern. P&T Knitwear is pleased to welcome Lauren Klein, Tanvi Sharma, & Silas Munro to celebrate & discuss the release of their book Data by Design, which explores how the history of data visualization holds the key to designing a more just future. They will be in conversation with Shannon Mattern, & will sign books after the talk! Doors open at 6:30pm with the talk starting closer to 7:00pm. Come early & grab a drink from the P&T Cafe! Tickets & books are available both on eventbrite & at the door. Housekeeping notes: This is a ticketed in-store event with limited amphitheater-style seating.Doors open at 6:30pm, with the talk starting around 7:00pm.Cost of a book bundle ticket reflects the total cost of the feature event book (MSRP plus tax). Each book bundle ticket guarantees ticket holders one (1) copy of the feature event book.The talk will be followed by a book signing. Books signed at P&T Knitwear events must be purchased from P&T Knitwear.If you would like a signed copy & cannot attend the event, we're happy to take your pre-order. We ship most places!About the authors:Lauren Klein is Professor of Data & Decision Sciences & English at Emory University, where she also directs the Digital Humanities Lab & the Atlanta Interdisciplinary AI Network. Her research brings together computational & critical methods to explore questions of gender, race, & justice, both in early America & today. Klein is the author (with Catherine D'Ignazio) of the award-winning Data Feminism (MIT Press, 2020), & the editor (with Matthew K. Gold) of Debates in the Digital Humanities (Univ. of Minnesota Press), among other books & papers. Her next book, Data by Design: Visualization & Power from Abolition to the Dawn of Data Science (MIT Press), will be out in October 2026.  Silas Munro is a designer, artist, writer, curator, surfer, & descendant of the Banyole people of Eastern Uganda. He founded the design studio Polymode, whose clients include MoMA, the MET, Nike, & the Hammer. Munro is the curator & author of Strikethrough: Typographic Messages of Protest at Letterform Archive & the co-curator of Reverberations: Lineages in Design History at the Ford Foundation Gallery. He contributed to W. E. B. Du Bois's Data Portraits: Visualizing Black America, & co-authored the first BIPOC-centered design history course, Black Design in America: African Americans & the African Diaspora in Graphic Design 19th-21st Century. His visual art was recently exhibited at Data Consciousness: Reframing Blackness in Contemporary Print at Print Center New York. Tanvi Sharma is a design technologist working at the intersection of data, aesthetics, & the humanities. She is currently an Art Director at Apple & co-author of Data by Design (MIT Press, 2026). She has previously worked at Pentagram, Public Policy Lab, & Spotify. She lives in Harlem, NY, with her two cats, Yuchi & Bubbles. More at tanvi.network.   About the moderator:Shannon Mattern is the Director of Creative Research at the Metropolitan New York Library Council, a state-founded, member-supported non-profit linking hundreds of libraries & archives across the city. Previously, she held tenured full professorships in media studies, anthropology, & art history at The New School & the University of Pennsylvania. She is the author of four books, the (co-)editor of six collections, & the author of over 100 articles & chapters about urban technology, knowledge infrastructures, maps, maintenance, data art, & other heterogenous subjects. She was the 2025 Kluge Chair in Modern Culture at the Library of Congress & the 2025 Design Indexer in residence at the Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum. You can find her at wordsinspace.net.

events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Plan Your Best Year With AI
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back  In Person at SalesforceWe're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City and sponsored by Boldforce.This Month We Present...Plan Your Best Year With AIJoin the community for an interactive planning session to reflect on the past year, identify your biggest opportunities, and build an AI-powered roadmap for the year ahead.Before we rush into a new year with another list of goals, lets get clear about what were actually building.What worked this year? What didnt? What deserves more of your energy? And where could AI help you turn those intentions into action?For our final AI & The Culture meetup of the year, were bringing the community together for an interactive planning and reflection session designed to help you look back, think forward, and build a roadmap for what comes next.This isnt about asking AI to magically plan your life. Its about using these tools as thought partnersto help you reflect, uncover patterns, explore possibilities, make decisions, and turn big ambitions into actionable next steps.Together well explore: How to use AI to reflect on your wins, lessons, challenges, and unfinished business from the past year Prompts that help you identify opportunities you might be overlooking How to turn big goals into realistic projects, milestones, and next steps Ways to use AI as a strategic thought partner for your creative work, career, business, or personal projects How to identify where AI and automation can give you back time in the year ahead Building a personalized AI-powered roadmap you can actually use after you leave the roomAnd because this is AI & The Culture, were making space for something AI cant replace: community.Youll have an opportunity to reflect alongside other creatives, founders, educators, artists, technologists, and curious mindsto exchange ideas, share what youre building, and potentially meet the people who can help you move it forward.The goal isnt to leave with 47 resolutions.Its to leave with clarity, priorities, and a plan.Who Should Attend? Creators and content makers Filmmakers, writers, artists, and storytellers Educators and community builders Entrepreneurs, founders, and solopreneurs Marketers, strategists, and creative professionals Technologists and AI enthusiasts Anyone ready to be more intentional about what theyre building nextWhether you already have your next year mapped out or youre still staring at a blank page wondering where to begin, youre welcome here.Come Ready to BuildThis one is especially hands-on, so come prepared to participate. Bring your laptop Bring a notebook or something to write with Bring a few goals, ideas, or questions youve been thinking about for the year ahead Bring your curiosity and a willingness to shareWell be working through reflection exercises, AI prompts, and planning activities togetherso you can leave with the beginnings of a roadmap, not just another page of notes.Come ready to reflect. Come ready to plan. Come ready to build.About AI & The CultureAI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, and culture.Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams and King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, and culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, and community.Were building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI.This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture  grounded in community, focused on real-world use, and centered on learning together in the room.Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Lets build  together. About Your HostsShirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, and co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, and creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, and real-world execution.About King WilloniusKing Willonius is a creative technologist and cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, and creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, and community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable and useful  especially for creatives and innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm. Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio)#AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: Innovation in Public Mixer 5.0  Year End Capital
events.description: Edition 5.0. Theme, year end capital. The monthly room where founders, investors & operators actually get matched. Capped & curated. Everyone leaves with at least one named introduction & the framing for the conversation. November is when allocators are deploying what is left of the year & family offices are planning the next one. This edition leans toward the capital side of the network. Who we are. Propel Earth has run 100+ events & built a network of 36,000+ founders, investors, operators, & service providers across six continents. We are not an events company. We are an outcomes company that happens to use rooms. You bring the intent. We deliver the outcome. This is not a business card room. We cap it at 40-50 people & we curate it. Tell us what you are building & who you need when you register, & before you walk in we hand you at least one match: a specific person, plus the framing for the conversation. Everyone leaves having met someone who matters to what they are working on. You do not need to apply to the cohort to attend. This room is open. Tickets Early Access - $20. Limited, nearly gone.General Admission - $40.Free for Propel Private Network members. Dinner is highly encouraged - the kitchen at The Wilson is excellent. Come hungry & stay late. What Propel actually does for you 1  Innovation in Public - our GTM accelerator. For founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go-to-market: content, distribution, & more sales. Four weeks, twice a week, building in public, closing with a public showcase in front of the room. Applications open for the August cohort  Apply here 2  The Propel Private Network. Stop networking. Start getting matched. Every month we personally hand you three introductions chosen for what you need right now - someone who can pay you, hire you, or move your company forward. It works both ways: you go into the pool too. Founding rate $200/mo, first 25 members, locked for life  Claim a founding membership 3  Propel Community Coworking x Wayo Club. Come Wednesday night, then come back Thursday & build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, founded by Jason Malefakis. Wayo is a curated community workspace network where members work from premium venues alongside thoughtfully selected founders, operators, & consultants they can collaborate with, refer, hire, or do business with. Attendees typically report being 1.5 to 2x more productive than working from home or a cafe, & leave with 2 to 3 meaningful connections. Lunch is included. Register with us  Propel Community Coworking 1.0  Get a Wayo Community Workday membership  Join the Wayo Anytime waitlist 4  Featured Founder. Build your founder or service-provider profile on Propel & we will give you one additional intro on us  propel.earth/featured-founders On camera: Nik Michael of the Pivot Point podcast is shooting photography, video, & follow-up interviews with select attendees. Want to be featured, reach out to him directly. Newsletter  propelearth.beehiiv.com  Propel Earth  propel.earth  Questions, text Stephen at 516 307 6380. About The WilsonThe Wilson NYC is a popular American comfort-food restaurant & bar located in NoMad/Chelsea. While the restaurant does not hold traditional culinary stars (like Michelin), it acts as a highly-rated, frequent event space for awards shows & local hospitality honors due to its event duplex & outdoor patio. The Wilson has also been celebrated for supporting its employees through the One Fair Wage What Propel does, & what it has produced Nine ways we connect this network. Every one of these is a room we have already run. Founders & Investors. We put founders in rooms with the people who write checks. Demo Night NYC ran in front of 35+ investors. Founders x Investors Night at PhD Lounge, the Funders x Founders High Line Walk, the Harvard Club Investment Dinner, & the NYTW Pitch Competition with 800+ registrations. Every monthly mixer does the same thing at a smaller scale, which is why we cap the room & match you before you arrive. Founders & Service Providers. You tell us what you need & we match you to someone vetted who does it. Legal, tax, engineering, design, growth, operations. Our Founders Meet Providers rooms exist for exactly this, & the Propel Marketplace runs it year round. Featured provider this month is Moshe Cohen, CPA, offering a 30 minute startup tax & finance session for $120. Book a session or browse the marketplace Hiring & Talent. Our Tech Job Fair & Developer Job Fair each brought over 150 engineers & operators into the room. That now runs continuously on Propel Earth Jobs, where employers, candidates, & referrers all work in one place. Post a role or find one Product Launches. We launch products to the whole network. The ConnNext App Launch Party pulled 475 registrations, the largest event we have ever run. BECOMEFAMOUS.AI pulled 222. If you are launching something & you need a room, reply to this & we will build it. Capital & Family Office. The capital side of the network. Our Private Markets Discussion Panel drew 280 registrations & Family Office Crypto with Forum Pay brought allocators into the room. These are smaller rooms with higher stakes. See the next one Masterclasses & Info Sessions. Free, online, & taught by specialists who actually do the work. Our Social Impact Cohort Info Session drew 297 registrations. TRIIBE TALK on branding drew 157. Tax, legal, fundraising, & go to market, taught by operators. See the calendar The GTM Accelerator. Four weeks for founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go to market help: content, distribution, & more sales. You get a dedicated BDR, a custom digital asset kit, & a public showcase in front of the room. Our last cohort presented at Demo Day to 35+ investors. August applications are open & you can see how we represented the last cohort The Social Rooms. Not everything is a pitch. Foundersgiving Party & Pitch Roast drew 381 people. LABYRINTH at Hotel Chelsea drew 309. Above Fridays Rooftop Networking, Holiday Chemistry Night, & Bowling & Business. These are the rooms where relationships actually form, & they are the reason the other eight verticals work. Community Coworking. Come to the mixer on Wednesday, then come back Thursday & actually build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, coffee & lunch included. Register here The Private Network, the thread through all of it. Every vertical above runs on the same engine. You tell us what you need, we find the person, we make the introduction in writing. Members receive three curated introductions every month plus free entry to every mixer & select special events. $200 per month, & the first 25 founding members lock that rate for life. Join here Want to sponsor a room? One sponsor per event so it never feels crowded. Email stephen@propel.earth Media ConsentPhotography & Video Acknowledgement. By registering for & attending this event, you acknowledge that Propel Earth (the "Organizer") may record the session (including video, audio, & chat transcripts). You grant the Organizer a perpetual, royalty-free, worldwide license to use, reproduce, & distribute any such recordings or photographs for promotional, educational, or commercial purposes. You waive any right to inspect or approve the finished product & understand that no compensation will be provided for your appearance in these materials. Attendance at the event shall be deemed as conclusive evidence of your agreement to these terms. Connect with Me Join the Newsletter Join Propel as a Founder Join Propel as a Service Provider Follow Propel Earth Find me here Join the Propel Founder WhatsApp Event Co-Hosting & Sponsorship Partner With Propel Earth

events.name: The AI Briefing By Startup Grind: Who Owns The Data Layer Behind Enterprise AI
events.description: The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise.  This month's source: The Formula for Agentic AI Value: Applied AI Index 2026 (Boston Consulting Group - Sep 2026) Secondary sources: 5 Emerging Trends in Enterprise Data & AI (The Modern Data Company - Aug 2026) Agentic context layers (VentureBeat Intelligence - Oct 2026) Most of the money behind enterprise AI no longer runs through IT. BCG surveyed 1,330 CxOs & senior executives. AI spending has more than tripled, to 3.3% of revenue, & 2.8 points of it sit outside the enterprise IT budget. Business units generate about two-thirds of the value AI creates. So who owns the data their agents run on? BCG says the gap between leaders & everyone else has moved up the stack, to whether a company's data is current, consistently defined, trustworthy, & managed with clear ownership. It tells companies to keep their definitions, business rules & decision logic in a layer they control & could move to another vendor. VentureBeat's August survey points the other way. 98% of companies running retrieval in production use at least one system someone else built, & 2% name building & owning their context layer as their likely direction. 64% have already caught an AI agent giving a confidently wrong answer because of their own company's data.  The Mission: Deciding who owns the definitions, rules & context your AI runs on This series has spent the year on readiness: how fast enterprises adopted, where leadership's confidence outran results, how governance fell behind agents, & whether the workforce was ready. October's discussion turned to a question none of those sessions answered: who owns the data layer? We'll test BCG's advice against what data teams report from the inside. 61% call a reliable context layer critical for AI agents, & 16% engineer one on purpose.  The Format: The numbers: BCG's spending & ownership data, & where a self-reported executive survey stops being evidence. Cross-pollinated debate: Who owns it in your org? IT, the data team, the business unit paying for the agent, or the model vendor whose stack holds the context. The semantic layer problem: In VentureBeat's survey, companies running or building a semantic layer were about twice as likely to report a confidently wrong agent answer (78% vs. 37%). We'll work through why, & what it means for anyone about to fund one.  Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: See where AI budgets & accountability sit at the 7.5% of companies BCG calls future-built (all of them have clear ownership of the AI agenda), & decide whose name goes on the data layer before a vendor's does. Founders & Builders: Hear what buyers mean when they ask about lock-in. 37% of VentureBeat's respondents plan to keep standalone tools alongside the model, & 22% expect to consolidate onto one model provider's stack. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Compare notes on the work underneath. 46% of respondents say their teams spend more than a quarter of their time maintaining & integrating tools, & 8.4% say the data feeding their AI is trustworthy enough for production.  The Prep: This is a working session, not a lecture. Read the report here. Bring one wrong answer your AI gave & where the bad data came from.

events.name: Unmuted  Debate - AI & China
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In July, a Chinese lab you'd probably never heard of published Kimi K3: 2.8 trillion parameters, billed as the largest open model on earth, weights posted free on Hugging Face for anyone to download. It's one of four Chinese labs that spent the last year closing the gap with the American frontier, then giving the result away. Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi. Four of the five most-used open models in the world now come out of Beijing, & American developers are running them inside hospitals, law firms, & startups because they're the cheapest, fastest tools available. No API someone in Washington controls. No off switch. Just download & go. One camp says a model is just math. Open weights run on a consumer's machine, the code is right there to inspect, & cutting Americans off from the best tools on the planet is how you lose a technology race. The other camp says the giveaway is the strategy. China seeds the world's infrastructure with their standards, their defaults, their assumptions, & the dependency follows once switching costs become unbeatable. So: should Americans be allowed to build on Chinese open-weight models or is this the new Cold War's Monkey's Paw? Arguing for, Rob Li is Managing Partner of Amont Partners, a New York global equity firm that invests across the US & Asia. He has spent his career putting capital on both sides of the Pacific, from Yum China to Alibaba deals, & he thinks the country that walls itself off from the best tools available loses. Arguing against, Will McKelvey is a Principal at Lerer Hippeau, one of New York's oldest venture firms, where he backs early-stage founders & spends his days watching for the future of AI, especially in consumer. He got his start by way of a congressional office, & he thinks the cheapest model on the market is the one you pay for slowly. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones. In collaboration with COMMITTEE OF 100Committee of 100 (C100) is a nonprofit U.S. leadership organization of distinguished Chinese Americans dedicated to advancing the full participation of Chinese Americans in American society & fostering constructive U.S.-China relations. For more than 35 years, C100 has brought together leaders across business, government, academia, technology, media, the arts, & other fields to advance its dual mission. Learn more at committee100.org.

events.name: An Unmuted Debate: Primary Party Crashers
events.description: Should primaries be open to every voter? More Americans now identify as independent than as Democrat or Republican. Yet in New York & many other states, those voters are shut out of the primaries that often decide who actually wins. So are closed primaries locking out the voters our politics needs most? And would opening them make anything better? Open primaries let any registered voter participate, regardless of party. Supporters say they force candidates to campaign to the whole electorate, reward problem-solvers over partisans, & give millions of independents a real voice. Critics say parties have the right to choose their own nominees, that open systems invite strategic crossover voting & voter confusion, & that the evidence they reduce polarization is thin. So who's right? Are open primaries the fix for a system that rewards the extremes? Or are they a reform that promises more than it delivers? John Opdycke is the founder & president of Open Primaries, a national organization working to enact & protect open & nonpartisan primaries. He has spent three decades in independent & reform politics, helped found the New York State Independence Party, & writes the monthly column Brash Tacks for The Fulcrum. Lindsey Cormack is an associate professor of political science & director of the Diplomacy Lab at Stevens Institute of Technology. She is the author of How to Raise a Citizen (And Why It's Up to You to Do It) & Congress & U.S. Veterans, created the DCInbox database of congressional newsletters, & serves as Secretary of Manhattan Community Board 8. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

Supporters say they force candidates to campaign to the whole electorate, reward problem-solvers over partisans, & give millions of independents a real voice. Critics say parties have the right to choose their own nominees, that open systems invite strategic crossover voting & voter confusion, & that the evidence they reduce polarization is thin. So who's right? Are open primaries the fix for a system that rewards the extremes? Or are they a reform that promises more than it delivers? John Opdycke is the founder & president of Open Primaries, a national organization working to enact & protect open & nonpartisan primaries. He has spent three decades in independent & reform politics, helped found the New York State Independence Party, & writes the monthly column Brash Tacks for The Fulcrum. Lindsey Cormack is an associate professor of political science & director of the Diplomacy Lab at Stevens Institute of Technology. She is the author of How to Raise a Citizen (And Why It's Up to You to Do It) & Congress & U.S. Veterans, created the DCInbox database of congressional newsletters, & serves as Secretary of Manhattan Community Board 8. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

events.name: Spatial Analytics w/ Python
events.description: Join PyData NYC on October 27th at 6:30 PM for an evening exploring geospatial data science with Python, featuring Brendan Collins, Founder & CTO at Makepath & creator of Xarray-Spatial! Discover how Python can transform spatial data into powerful insights, from terrain analysis & hydrology to scalable CPU- & GPU-accelerated computing. Please bring your  to follow along & sign up using your official government-issued name.  Pizza & drinks will be provided - Thank you, Makepath! Agenda xarray-spatial: In & Out of the Raster-verseSpeaker: Brendan Collins (Founder & CTO at Makepath)Spatial data comes in many shapes & sizes, but some of the most powerful spatial analysis techniques begin by viewing the world as a grid.Led by the library's creator & maintainer, this talk introduces Xarray-Spatial, an open-source Python library for scalable raster analysis with CPU & GPU acceleration.We'll learn how to enter the Raster-verse by bringing spatial data into Xarray, explore the Raster-verse using algorithms for terrain analysis, hydrology, proximity, & more, & escape the Raster-verse through techniques like zonal statistics & polygonization.Finally, we'll discuss contributing to the Raster-verse, sharing lessons from maintaining Xarray-Spatial & how AI-augmented development is transforming open-source contributions, code quality, & scientific software engineering.Whether you're a GIS practitioner, data scientist, or Python developer, you'll leave with practical ideas for working with spatial data & contributing to open source.  About the SpeakerBrendan Collins is the Founder & CTO of Makepath, where he helps early-stage startups & Fortune 500 engineering teams realize their product ambitions.A former employee of Anaconda, Brendan has spent the past decade applying PyData technologies, including NumPy, Xarray, & Numba, to engineering challenges across the public, private, & nonprofit sectors.When not writing in the third person, Brendan enjoys swimming, playing the banjo, & gardening.  NetworkingConnect with fellow data enthusiasts, Python developers, researchers, & community leaders. Build meaningful connections, exchange ideas, & explore opportunities for collaboration.

events.description: Health2Tech - a series of digital health events.Join us on November 5th for an exclusive gathering that brings together the brightest minds in the digital health space. Hosted by Bailey Morgan, Audrey Guazzone, Maria Putilina & Alex Koshykov, this evening promises to be a confluence of innovation, inspiration, & invaluable networking.  Important!  To keep this session highly focused, priority will be given to MedTech experts, device founders, bioengineers, clinicians, & specialized investors. If you work outside the MedTech space, we appreciate your understanding - we'll review your application & confirm attendance based on remaining capacity.  Want to Showcase Your Medical Device Live?If you are building a medical device or physical HealthTech product, we have live demo spots available to feature your innovation in front of NYC investors, healthcare leaders, & potential partners. How to apply: Fill out the form - Open Google Form Register on this Luma page. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, so please apply early!  Event Schedule: 5:30 PM - 6:00 Doors Open. Connect, converse, & collaborate with peers driven by a common passion for advancing healthcare through technology.  About our Panelists: Steven Levy Steven is a Partner at Unorthodox Ventures where he focuses on investing in venture stage MedTech companies. Before joining Unorthodox Ventures, Steven worked for the prior 23 years as an investment banker, having held senior roles at Lehman Brothers, Stifel Financial & Cowen & Co. Steven has executed over 100 transactions with aggregate deal value in excess of $30 billion. Steven headed the M&A efforts for the Financial Sponsors practice at Lehman Brothers, covered Financial sponsors & headed the Consumer M&A efforts at Cowen & covered Financial Sponsors, led execution on technology & consumer M&A transactions & headed up the firm's investment banking efforts in Israel at Stifel. Steven received his B.A. from Binghamton University & graduated as a member of Phi Beta Kappa & received his M.B.A. from the Wharton School, at the University of Pennsylvania. Bryan Spielman is a Managing Partner at Northwell Health Equity Partners. events.name: PMAI - Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Learn How to SellSales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. - Bring a computer. You're writing three things tonight.- Most founders can get meetings. The deals die after meeting one.- You'll leave with your buyer in one sentence, a cold email written to a real person, & five questions for your next call. About Farzad, the speaker Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding & generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: Tech Table Talk: Career, Family & Life On Your Terms
events.description: Tech Table Talk: Career, Family & Life on Your Terms is an intimate dinner bringing together women in tech for an honest conversation about career, fertility, family planning, & building a life on their own terms. Hosted by Baddies in Tech in partnership with Spring Fertility, the evening will create space for women to have the kinds of conversations we don't often have: How do you think about growing your career while also considering a future family? What options are available if your personal & professional timelines do not align perfectly? And how can having more information today create more choices tomorrow? We're setting the Tech Table to create space for a conversation you may have been thinking about but have not had anyone to talk to about. events.name: Ground Truth: The Live Agents Hackathon
events.description: Every AI model you've ever used is stuck in the past. Ground Truth is a one-day hackathon where you fix that. Join localhost:nyc, The Builder Series & You.com for 10 hours of building AI agents grounded in the live web. Real-time data, deep research, verifiable answers. Come build the kind of agent people would trust with a real decision. Problem StatementEvery LLM is frozen at its training cutoff. It doesn't know what happened this morning, & when it doesn't know, it guesses, confidently. That's the gap between a cool demo & a product people rely on. Your challenge: build an AI agent that knows what's true right now. It searches the live web through the You.com API, reads the sources, reasons over them & shows its receipts. The Challenge TracksLive Wire (real-time agents): agents that wake up when the world changes. Price moves, breaking news, a competitor launch, a policy change, a new job posting. If it happened in the last hour, your agent already knows & already acted. The Analyst (deep research): pick a profession (VCs, lawyers, journalists, recruiters, doctors, policy staffers) & replace its 40-hour research memo with a 4-minute one, every claim cited. Receipts (trust & verification): agents that fact-check claims, catch AI hallucinations, verify sources & show their work. Best Content (open to every team): post about what you built, tag You.com, & win a dedicated prize. What to ExpectA kickoff walkthrough of the You.com API: Search, Contents, Research & the hosted MCP server Free You.com API credits for every builder 6 hours of building Teams of up to 4, or solo if that's your thing Team matching at kickoff if you're coming alone Mentors from You.com on the floor all day Live demos to judges at the end, plus food all day Prizes1st Place Overall: $500 cash Best Content: TBD JudgesTBD Who Should AttendEngineers (full stack, backend, AI/ML) Founders & aspiring founders building with AI Designers & product people who want to ship something real Researchers & analysts who know exactly what a great research agent should do You don't need a finished idea. Just show up ready to build. SponsorsYou.com: AI search infrastructure that gives agents real-time, cited access to the web through its Search, Contents & Research APIs. Hostslocalhost:nyc: Making NYC the biggest startup ecosystem in the world. The Builder Series   The Builder Series: A 60,000+ member community redefining what networking looks like - curating founders, operators, investors & more into intentional rooms built for experiences people remember & relationships that last.
