events.name: Startup Pitch & Networking
events.description: Join our event in New York! We design Pitch & Networking nights to help founders sharpen their thinking through direct, candid feedback & to give strong investors access to serious teams. Our pitch night is complemented by a structured networking session before & after the pitch session. What to expect: Startups pitch live & receive focused feedback from angels & VC partners Structured networking session before & after the pitches Entrepreneurs, startup founders, & operators are joining to network, exchange ideas, & build strong connections Active investors & venture scouts joining to discover the best startups early  Who you will meet at the event: Founders Investors, VC partners, Venture Scouts Marketers, Salespeople, Business Advisors Industry Disruptors AI Experts Entrepreneurs from Europe, Asia, & the United Kingdom  We Welcome New Investors: We invite investors to our event to expand their network, get acquainted with new startups, evaluate them, share feedback, & participate in discussions with early-stage & serial founders. We offer complimentary tickets to institutional investors, angels, & venture scouts with a proven track record. If you'd like to access our database of promising startups or provide mentorship support to our best startups, please fill out this short Investor Application Form, & our team will contact you.  Want to Pitch? A limited number of founders will have the opportunity to pitch their startup or business to a panel of investors & experts. 4-6 selected founders will pitch their startup, followed by a short Q&A where participants can ask questions & share feedback. Apply by filling out the Pitch Application Form & sending us your pitch deck. Spots are limited, & we select founders in advance. To maintain high-quality pitches, you are required to present with a pitch deck. We will share our pitching guide and, if you'd like, coach you so you're fully prepared for pitch night.  The best startups will be featured across our social media & included in our investor newsletter. Requirements for attendees: Dress code: smart casual. Bring good energy.  Join our event & secure your ticket today! About us: Startup Valley is a global event organizer hosting pitch nights in 25 cities since 2023. Since then, we have hosted 850 events for 40,000 attendees. Over these years, we connected countless outstanding early-stage startups to serious investors, & we are not planning to stop. We maintain strategic partnerships with VC funds in the US, Europe, & Asia to support our community. Do you have a question, a partnership proposal, or want to clarify something? Reach us at hello@startupvalley.club Agenda 18:00-18:30 - Registration: Guests register, receive badges, & event programs. This is an opportunity for casual networking, making first connections, & preparing for the event. 18:30-19:00 - Event Kickoff & Interactive Networking: Official welcome from the organizers with a brief overview of the event goals & schedule. Interactive networking session to connect with key contacts. 19:00-19:50 - Startup Pitch Session: Startups present their projects to investors & experts. Each team has 5 minutes to pitch, covering the project's core idea, business model, & target market. 19:50-21:00 - Chill & Networking: Participants enjoy casual conversations with investors, discuss collaboration opportunities, & exchange ideas over refreshments. FAQ Can I pitch? Yes! To pitch, please purchase a Pitch Ticket & fill out the Pitch Application Form. We will contact you to discuss & approve your pitch. The pitch duration is 5 minutes. You will also have some time to answer questions from the audience. How does the pitch go? Selected founders present on stage to the audience & the investors in the room. You get 5 minutes to pitch your idea, business model, target market, & investment ask, followed by a short Q&A. The best startups are featured across our social media channels & in the investor newsletter. Who will I meet? Founders, angel investors, VC partners, venture scouts, AI experts, engineers, operators, marketing & sales experts, & international entrepreneurs from across Europe, Asia, & the US. Do investors get free tickets? Yes! Please apply above or email hello@startupvalley.club, & we will issue a complimentary ticket for you & your team. Can I request a refund? Yes. Refunds are available if requested at least 1 day before the event start time. Please submit the refund request on the platform where you purchased your ticket, or email us at hello@startupvalley.club

events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Build Your Creative Operating System
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back - In Person at Salesforce We're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City & sponsored by Boldforce. This Month We Present...Build Your Creative Operating SystemBuild a personalized AI workflow that supports your entire creative process-from capturing ideas to publishing finished work-so you're never starting from scratch. Most of us don't have an idea problem. We have a system problem. Ideas live in our Notes app. Research is scattered across browser tabs. Drafts are hiding in Google Docs. Inspiration gets screenshotted & forgotten. And every new project somehow feels like we're starting all over again. What if your creative process actually remembered how you work? At this month's AI & The Culture meetup, we're exploring how to build your own Creative Operating System-a personalized workflow that uses AI to help you capture ideas, organize knowledge, research, create, refine, & publish your work. Instead of collecting more AI tools, we'll focus on connecting the ones that actually support your process. Together we'll explore:  How to map your creative process from idea to finished work  Ways to capture & organize ideas so they don't disappear into the digital abyss  How AI can help you research, brainstorm, draft, edit, & refine your work  Building a personal knowledge base that makes past ideas & research useful again  How to connect AI tools into repeatable workflows instead of using them one at a time  Where automation can save time-and where your human judgment should stay firmly in the driver's seat  How to create a system that gets smarter & more useful the more you use it The goal isn't to automate your creativity. It's to build the infrastructure around your creativity so you have more time & energy for the work only you can do. Expect a welcoming room filled with creators, technologists, educators, founders, artists, & curious minds ready to rethink how we organize & support our creative lives. Who Should Attend?  Creators & content makers  Filmmakers, writers, artists, & storytellers  Educators & community builders  Entrepreneurs, founders, & solopreneurs  Marketers, strategists, & creative professionals  Technologists & AI enthusiasts  Anyone with too many ideas, too many tabs, & not enough systems  Whether your creative process is already organized or currently held together by screenshots, open tabs, & vibes, you're welcome here. Come Ready to Build This won't be a sit-back-and-scroll kind of evening. Bring your laptop, something to write with, & a mindset ready to learn, experiment, & share. We'll be exploring ideas, tools, & workflows you can begin applying to your own creative process.  Bring your laptop  Bring a notebook or something to take notes with  Bring your curiosity & questions Come ready to learn. Come ready to contribute. Come ready to build. About AI & The Culture AI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, & culture. Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams & King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, & culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, & community. We're building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI. This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture - grounded in community, focused on real-world use, & centered on learning together in the room. Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Let's build - together.  About Your Hosts Shirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, & co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, & creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, & real-world execution. About King Willonius King Willonius is a creative technologist & cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, & creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, & community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable & useful - especially for creatives & innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm.  Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio) #AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: The AI Era & What It Means To Be Human
events.description: The AI Era & What It Means to Be HumanAI is changing how we work, learn, create, & make decisions. But underneath the conversation about models, agents, & automation is a more fundamental question: what does it mean to be human in an age of increasingly capable machines? On October 23rd, The AI Collective is bringing together 100 people in NYC for an evening exploring the human side of the AI era. We'll move beyond the usual conversation about what AI can do & look instead at what its rise asks of us: how we learn, how we maintain agency, how we relate to one another, & which distinctly human capacities become more important as technology advances. The evening will combine conversation, small-group discussion, & experiential mindfulness/wellness exercises. This is not a technical AI event. We're creating a conversation about the human layer: the trust, awareness, connection, & shared understanding we'll need to build alongside the technology. Come curious. Expect to participate. Agenda6:00 PM: Arrival & Welcome6:30 PM: Opening Remarks + Experiential Mindfulness Exercise6:45 PM: Fireside Chat: AI & the Human Condition with Mohan Nair, author of "Unreachable: How to Not Lose Your Mind in an AI-Obsessed Era."7:15 PM: Conversation with Catherine & Manas followed by Breath-work & Meditation.7:45 PM: Small-Group Roundtables8:15 PM: Dessert & Networking Food & beverages provided. Space is limited to 75 participants. Co-hosted by The AI Collective & Manas Ram with support from JQ Consulting, whose work focuses on the science of human wellbeing, resilience, happiness, mindfulness, & the human condition. Please be advised: Unfortunately, space is very limited at these community events & we can not always accept everyone we would like to. If you are not accepted to this event, please keep applying! We appreciate your application tremendously & we are looking forward to seeing you at a future event very soon! The AI Collective is a global non-profit building the human layer for the AI era. We unite 200,000+ leaders, builders, & stakeholders across 100+ forums worldwide to democratize the frontier, build trust, & coordinate how society navigates the rapid acceleration of technological progress. All attendees & organizers at events affiliated with The AI Collective agree to our privacy policy & are subject to our code of conduct.

events.name: GILD AI Forum: AI & Engineering Leaders Dinner
events.description: This GILD AI Forum brings together CTOs, VPs of Engineering, Heads of AI, & senior technical leaders for candid conversations about building, scaling, & implementing AI inside their companies. This isn't a conference. It's not a panel. It's a small, curated room of technical leaders sharing what's actually working, what's not, & the real challenges of shipping AI in the AI era. Each Forum opens with a Conversation Starter, a practitioner sharing what their team is building with AI, followed by open Q&A. From there, the room breaks into intimate discussions where everyone has a seat at the table. Every attendee brings their own experience. Every attendee contributes. No pitches. No performative networking. Just senior technical leaders being honest about the architectures they're choosing, the tradeoffs they're making, & what they wish they'd figured out sooner. TRENDING THEMES FOR THIS SESSION Conversations at the Forum are shaped by what technical leaders bring to the table. Themes likely to surface this evening include: From AI pilots to AI in production: breaking out of the proof-of-concept trap & scaling agents into real workflows Connecting AI to legacy systems: architectural patterns for integrating modern AI with 20-year-old stacks without breaking everything The AI tooling budget problem: balancing experimentation with unsustainable spend as engineers blow through AI tool budgets Engineers as curators, not creators: the shift from writing code to orchestrating AI agents, reusable components, & external services MCP, multi-agent systems, & the orchestration layer: what's working, what's overhyped, & what technical leaders are actually building Guardrails & governance for AI-generated code: who's accountable when the AI writes it, & what review processes actually hold up in production Presented in partnership with Tecla Tecla gives companies flexible access to vetted talent across the US & Latin America, developed for AI-native work & available from fractional engagements to dedicated nearshore pods. Learn more at www.tecla.io THE FORMAT Intentionally small & highly curated, 20 to 25 max. A seated round-table dinner, private & off the record under Chatham House Rules. AGENDA 6:00 - 6:30 PM  Cocktails & passed appetizers 6:30 - 7:00 PM  Dinner is served Find a seat & get comfortable. 6:45 - 6:50 PM  GILD & Partner Welcome A few words from the GILD team & our partners on what the night holds & how we'll spend it together. 6:50 - 7:00 PM  Conversation Starter A fellow engineering leader opens the discussion with a candid perspective on AI, with a brief Q&A. 7:00 - 8:00 PM  Table discussions 8:00 - 8:30 PM  Open mingling WHO THIS IS FOR Founders  CEOs  CTOs  VPs of Engineering  Heads of AI  Technical Leaders  Product Leaders This session is for leaders responsible for building, deploying, & maintaining AI systems in production. Chatham House Rules apply. Discussion stays private.

Located on Governors Island, the Climate Imaginarium is activating a cultural destination at the heart of New York City's burgeoning green economy, where artists, scientists, advocates, & storytellers come together to reimagine & build toward a more resilient future.  Getting to the Climate ImaginariumFor the weekend ferry schedule to Governors Island, please check here. Ferries run every 15 minutes. Take the ferry that's most convenient for you from either Lower Manhattan (10 South Street), Brooklyn Bridge Park (Pier 6), or Red Hook/Atlantic Basin. Please arrive 15 minutes prior to your ferry departure time with your ticket ready to display. Ferry tickets must be purchased at the ferry terminal or online. Fares are $5 for a round trip ticket & free for adults over 65, children 12 & under, Climate Imaginarium summer volunteers, & others. All passengers ride free before 11am on weekends. Cars are not permitted. Governors Island is also accessible from any route via NYC Ferry by transferring at Wall Street/Pier 11. You can find the NYC Ferry schedule here. Tickets on NYC Ferry are $4.50 each way. Once you get to Governors Island, you will either get out at Soissons Landing (from Manhattan) or Yankee Pier (from Brooklyn). You can use this map of Governors Island to locate Colonels Row. The Climate Imaginarium is in Building 406A, in the middle of Colonels Row, & will have a visible sign outside the doorway. Our address is 406A Comfort Road.

events.name: Vibecoding 101
events.description: A 4-week scaffolded, hands-on introduction to vibecoding for beginners.Vibecoding, or AI-assisted software development, is the practice of guiding coding agents to translate your ideas into working software - without writing code yourself. We see vibecoding as 4 different product skills in a trench coat. While they may not write code, effective vibecoders mobilize concepts & workflows across software engineering, design, quality assurance, & product management. This course is a scaffolded, hands-on introduction to the fundamental skills & concepts required for a sustainable vibecoding practice. Students will learn through a combination of short lectures, applied exercises, personalized feedback, & demos to peers. We begin by working with coding agents in a multiplayer environment designed for beginners. We will create interactive frontends, learn the basics of the terminal, build integrations with APIs, & create stateful, full-stack applications with a database & user authentication. By the end of the course, students will transition to state-of-the-art coding agents installed on their personal machines, which they will use to build & deploy a working prototype to the web. SyllabusSession 1: Coding agents & frontends We introduce the course & core concepts of vibecoding. We introduce a basic taxonomy of web architecture. Students practice creating basic interactive frontends. Session 2: CLIs, APIs, & the terminal We cover core backend & data concepts. We gently introduce the terminal. Students practice writing simple CLI programs, & integrating with an API. Session 3: Stateful full-stack applications We cover databases & user authentication; students build a full stack app. Session 4: Deployment & demos The final session covers deployment. Students demo their prototypes for the class. Learning OutcomesAcquire core vocabulary & mental models for software development. Prompt coding agents to create frontends, API integrations, & stateful applications. Be able to translate your ideas into working prototypes using AI. Practice presenting your product ideas to peers & colleagues. ResourcesThis new world of ours rewards being a dilettante with a vague mental map of vast territories.- Ted Underwood There is a new kind of coding I call vibecoding,' where you fully give in to the vibes, embrace exponentials, & forget that the code even exists. It's possible because the LLMs (e.g. Cursor Composer w Sonnet) are getting too good it's not really coding - I just see stuff, say stuff, run stuff, & copy paste stuff, & it mostly works.- Andrej Karpathy Slow is smooth, & smooth is fast.- Anonymous ScholarshipIndex scholarships are designed to benefit members of our community who do not have expendable cash to pay for the course, & those for whom the class price is not accessible. These need-based scholarships will go to the candidates who best demonstrate why they should be chosen for the free spot to our class based on the following criteria: Belong to groups that are traditionally underrepresented in the graphic design & creative industries Do not have jobs that would pay for these courses as professional development Cannot independently afford the class at list price Share our value of intentional community The number of selected applicants chosen is subject to the discretion of Index & the instructor, but every course will select at least one. Apply for a scholarship here. Applications close October 20th. Instructor Bio Bill Roberts is an independent technologist based in Brooklyn. Drawn to socially beneficial uses of technology, he has 10 years of software engineering experience on teams spanning healthcare, climate, politics, & education. He runs Legible Labs, a product studio that helps clients design & build AI applications. As a research engineer, he has coauthored papers in peer-reviewed journals & conferences that empirically evaluate the capabilities of AI in educational settings. Bill holds a BA in Computer Science & Sociology from Columbia University.   Refunds We get that things come up, but we rely on headcounts to make our programs viable. If you request a refund... More than 4 weeks before the program begins  100% refundMore than 2 weeks before the program begins  50% refundFewer than 2 weeks before the program begins  No refund Thanks for understanding & for supporting our ability to provide cool offerings through your purchase. Media Release Clause By attending this event, you consent to being photographed, filmed, or recorded, & grant Index Space permission to use this content for promotional or informational purposes.

events.name: Daytona AI Builders
events.description: An event dedicated to exploring all things AI Engineering! Event partners: AWS & Antimetal Agenda 5:30 pm - 6:00 pmWelcome Gathering & Opening Remarks Marijan Cipcic, Principal Events Manager at Daytona  6:00 pm - 6:15 pmTalk "Forkable Sandboxes for Long-Running Agents" Muhammad Annas Hashmi, DevRel at Daytona Outline:Agents are starting to do real software work: installing dependencies, editing files, running tests, starting servers, & debugging over long sessions. But most AI systems still treat each run like a disposable prompt-response loop. That breaks down once the useful state lives not just in tokens, but in the actual machine. This talk is about the runtime layer agents need to become reliable builders. I'll show how forkable Daytona sandboxes let you pause at important moments in an agent run, branch the environment, & sample multiple continuations from the same machine state. For builders, this turns long-running agent workflows into something you can inspect, compare, recover, & eventually optimize.  6:15 pm - 6:30 pmTalk "Multi-Agent Investment AI Assistant built on Amazon Bedrock Agentcore" Sam Farber, Sr. Solutions Architect at AWS Outline:Investment research teams spend days manually gathering data across markets, risk metrics, sentiment indicators, financial statements, & alternative data sources before synthesizing findings into actionable reports. This talk will show how a multi-agent AI system can automate that workflow. A supervisor agent breaks down a research question, delegates to 10 domain-specific specialists running in parallel, & compiles their findings into a comprehensive investment report. The system maintains conversation memory across each agent, allowing researchers to have targeted conversations & follow-ups with each specialized agent.  6:30 pm - 6:45 pmTalk "Building a World Model for Production Agents" Shreyas Iyer, Co-founder & CTO of Antimetal Outline:Production systems are increasingly complex, with critical knowledge scattered across code, infrastructure, telemetry, & people's heads. In this talk, we'll explore how to build a persistent world model that gives AI agents a shared understanding of production. We'll break down four foundational layers: physical topology, temporal changes, causal relationships, & organizational context to show how they enable agents to investigate incidents, assess changes, & proactively manage production, building on what they've learned across tasks.  6:45 pm - 6:55 pmTalk "TBA" Speaker TBA Outline:TBA  6:55 pm - 7:05 pmTalk "Letting AI agents use credentials they never see" Chase Erickson, Solutions Engineer at Infisical Outline:Infisical manages the secrets your Daytona agents depend on. The Daytona secret sync pushes them from Infisical to your Daytona organization & keeps them current, rotations included. Infisical's Agent Vault, a proxy, adds the credential to requests bound for the services you configure, so the agent never sees it. In this talk, we'll show how an agent in a Daytona sandbox calls an API without ever holding the secret.  7:05 pm - 8:30 pmNetworkingWith pizzas & beverages About event This is dynamic gathering for AI enthusiasts, innovators, & professionals to collaborate, share ideas, & explore the latest advancements in artificial intelligence. Whether you're building AI products, researching cutting-edge algorithms, or simply passionate about the field, join us to connect, learn, & drive the future of AI forward.

events.name: Ugly Talk - Building Fandoms In 2027
events.description: A customer buys once. A fan brings people with them. Getting there takes months of showing up. Listening. Keeping promises. Giving people a reason to care when you are no longer in their feed. This Ugly Talk gets into the work behind real fandom. The creator calls that went nowhere. The community plays that looked dead for months. The moment loyal customers pushed back & the brand had to answer. No follower-count victory laps. Just the decisions, mistakes, & proof behind communities that stick.  Why you should be in this room.Hear how consumer brands turn one-time buyers into people who recruit other buyers. Learn which signals reveal loyalty before revenue catches up. See how brands build with creators from the first idea through launch. Learn what to keep doing when the community looks quiet. Hear how leaders respond when their biggest supporters become their loudest critics.  What's on the table.Building superfans at scale: What makes customers care enough to bring other people in. Creators & co-creation: How brands share the build instead of buying a post at the end. Measuring fandom: The numbers that matter after likes & reach stop telling the truth. The slow build: What to do when months of work look like nothing is happening. When fandom turns: What community pushback reveals about the trust you built. Managing a crisis: How to respond fast, own the miss, & keep trust intact.  Who's hosting it. Rob Fajardo - Founder, LeaveNormalBehind Rob Fajardo is an entrepreneur, operator, & cultural architect whose work centers on a simple question: what does winning look like? Early in his career, Rob helped drive the fidget spinner phenomenon by building & activating an influencer network across Instagram & Facebook, reaching over 150 million people. Since then, he has worked with brands including DoorDash, Lowe's, FedEx, Converse, Red Bull, & Wyndham Resort Group, & has been featured in Forbes, Entrepreneur, Thrive Global, & BuzzFeed. Rob is the founder of Leave Normal Behind, a global network of purpose-driven leaders, creators, & investors built around meaningful connection, personal growth, & human flourishing. Over the past decade, he has brought together people across industries & generations through designed gatherings & strategic collaborations. He also serves as Head of Operations for the School of Content at The School of Hard Knocks, one of the world's largest business media platforms with 26M+ followers, where he coaches business owners generating six to nine figures on go-to-market. In addition, he is a Strategic Advisor to The AI Collective, the world's largest AI community, with 70,000+ members across 25+ global chapters.  Who's getting in.CPG & consumer-brand founders building a customer base that sticks. Brand & community leaders responsible for loyalty & retention. Creators building their own audience or working with consumer brands. Marketers who care about advocacy, repeat purchases, & long-term growth.  About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough "aha!" moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons & insights. With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami, we've built a vibrant community of thousands of founders & industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape. Official Website: UglyTalk.com Important Notice for Ugly Talk AttendeesAdmission & Confirmation Attendance is by approval only. Approved guests will receive a confirmation email along with a calendar invite. Invitations are non-transferable. Additional event details will be shared as the event approaches. Code of Conduct By attending, you agree to: Maintain respect & professionalism, adhering to all venue rules, policies, & applicable laws. Refrain from harassment, discrimination, unwelcome sexual advances (verbal or physical), intimidation, or inappropriate photography/recording. Report any violations to the event hosts immediately. Violations may result in immediate removal from the event & exclusion from future invitations. Liability & Risk Participation is voluntary & at your own risk. The event organizers, hosts, sponsors, & venue are not liable for personal injury, lost or stolen belongings, or any other damages incurred during the event. Media Consent By attending, you grant the event organizers & affiliated entities the right to capture, use, & distribute photos, videos, & audio recordings of you for promotional, marketing, & other lawful purposes, including digital & print media, advertising, & social media. You waive any right to inspect or approve the final materials & release all claims related to their use. Communications By registering, you agree to receive marketing & promotional communications from Ugly Talk & its co-hosts, partners, & sponsors. You may unsubscribe at any time. Agreement If you do not agree to this Code of Conduct, please refrain from attending the event.  Join us to stay updated on upcoming Ugly Talk events! Join the newsletter  Follow us on IG  Official website

events.description: Are you a founder or entrepreneur? If so, you know that scaling your business past Seed & Series A can expose many gaps in your business all at once - talent/employee friction, messy positioning, legal nuances, capital efficiency...and the list goes on. And while most founder events only focus on panels with generic advice, our new event "The Growth Council" aims to do something different. The mission of this event is to give the founder community access to experts who can help you at your specific stage of growth. The Growth Council is a small-group, peer-to-peer advisory session built specifically for Seed to Series B founders who want to explore their challenges with experts from across the industry & outside their network. Founders will have access to experts in various areas, rotating at specific intervals to ensure they meet with as many experts as possible (think speed dating, but less awkward). These conversations are meant to challenge assumptions & empower founders with new perspectives on their most pressing problems. You'll walk away with fresh perspectives, a bigger network, & connections who can help facilitate you on your journey towards success. The Expert Council Bring us your founder questions, your bottlenecks, or gut-check a current decision & get actionable takeaways from those who have been there before. You'll meet with cross-functional leaders such as: TJ Allison (Sales Advisor & Executive Coach, TJAllison.com) - Sales expert who focuses on revenue & the "Inner Game" to grow revenue & sense of self. Simon Gibson (Fractional VP of Marketing, Formerly GIPHY) - Marketing leader who blends creative storytelling & data-driven strategy to build culturally relevant brands & scale businesses. Rebekah Huber (Cofounder, Kindred Works) - Ops specialist who builds the systems that give founders their time back. Anna Kaplan (Founder & CEO, Narrativ By AK) - Narrative & messaging specialist who helps founders craft a story that wins the room. Marc Kaufman (Partner, Potomac Law Group) - Intellectual property attorney specializing in creating IP assets that increase funding. Fractional CFO TBD Agenda 6:00 PM - 6:30 PM | Arrivals & Light BitesCasual networking over food & drinks before we kick off. 6:30 PM - 6:45 PM | Council & Sponsor IntrosQuick, 60-second introductions from each expert on the specific fires they help extinguish. 6:45 PM - 7:45 PM | Growth Council HuddlesRotate at regular intervals. At each table, state your burning question, get sharp direct feedback from the functional expert, & compare notes with peer founders. 7:45 PM - 8:30 PM | Drinks & Direct ConnectionsInformal wrap-up to continue conversations with experts & founders. Who Should Apply This event is strictly curated for Seed, Series A, & Series B founders / co-founders leading venture-backed tech startups. Capacity is strictly capped at 35 founders to maintain small group sizes & high-signal discussions. Requests to join will be reviewed to preserve the peer dynamic. Hosted By: Kindred Works - Fractional operations & employee engagement partners for high-growth startups. Narrativ by AK - Strategic positioning & narrative development for founders. Tavern - A Physical Social Network Want to host your own event? events.name: Six Math Essentials w/ Terence Tao
events.description: Book Launch & Conversation with Janna Levin Widely regarded as the world's greatest living mathematician, Fields Medalist Terence Tao approaches mathematics as a sublime art-a quiet, rigorous effort to map the hidden scaffolding of reality. To mark the publication of his first popular book, Six Math Essentials, join us for an evening with Tao in conversation with Pioneer Works Director of Sciences Janna Levin. Tracing the central pillars of his book-from algebra as abstraction & geometry beyond sight, to navigating uncertainty & the mathematics of change-they will reveal math not as obscure magic, but as a deeply creative, interconnected way of thinking. Often referred to as the Mozart of mathematics, Tao will also explore how AI is transforming his own practice, the frontier of research, & our collective future. Together, we will consider what becomes of human intuition & creativity when the tools of thought are no longer uniquely human-and whether the true beauty of math lies not in the answers we find, but in the human mind reaching for them. Tao will sign copies of Six Math Essentials following the conversation, with books available for purchase on site. (Unable to attend? Order a signed copy here.) Please note that seating is limited & will be available on a first-come, first-served basis.   About the speakersTerence Tao is an Australian-American professor of mathematics at UCLA whose work focuses primarily on harmonic analysis, partial differential equations, combinatorics, & analytic number theory. The recipient of a Fields Medal, a MacArthur Genius Grant, & a Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics, among many other accolades, he is one of the most decorated & prolific mathematicians working today. Tao is the author of several academic books including Solving Mathematical Problems: A Personal Perspective & Additive Combinatorics, as well as his first popular math book, Six Math Essentials. He lives in Los Angeles. Janna Levin is the Claire Tow Professor of physics & astronomy at Barnard College of Columbia University. A Guggenheim Fellow, she has contributed to our understanding of black holes, extra dimensions, & cosmology. She is the founding director of sciences at Pioneer Works & the founding editor-in-chief of the magazine Pioneer Works Broadcast. She often contributes to news, documentaries, & radio, including as the presenter of the NOVA feature Black Hole Apocalypse on PBS & as a contributor to CBS, CNN, BBC, & NBC. She has authored books on black holes & the universe-Black Hole Blues, How the Universe Got its Spots, & Black Hole Survival Guide-as well as a PEN award-winning novel, A Madman Dreams of Turing Machines. You can find her current writings in Higher Dimensions. This program is funded by the Simons Foundation International & administered by the Simons Foundation's Science, Society & Culture division.

events.name: Alpha Agentic Economy Summit
events.description: The Alpha Agentic Economy Summit is the gathering for leaders building the agentic enterprise & those accountable for its decisions. On November 6, 2026, at Nasdaq MarketSite in New York City, Alpha brings together board directors, management teams, investors, & technology leaders to address a defining challenge: enterprises are delegating authority to AI faster than their governance can adapt. AI agents are already executing transactions, writing & deploying code, & making operational decisions between board meetings. As their authority expands, so does the exposure: financial loss, operational disruption, legal liability, & reputational damage. Boards need to understand where that authority sits, how it is controlled, & what evidence demonstrates that oversight is working. The Summit connects the boardroom with the people shaping this shift. Confirmed speakers include Gary Vaynerchuk, Chairman of VaynerX; Stacy Brown-Philpot, Founder & Managing Partner of Cherryrock Capital; Ann Miura-Ko, Co-Founding Partner of Floodgate; Laura Desmond, CEO of Smartly; Al Zollar, board director at BNY, IBM, & Nasdaq; & Madhu Muthukumar, Chief Product Officer of SoFi. They join leaders including Navrina Singh of Credo AI, Philip Rathle of Neo4j, Wasim Khaled of Blackbird.AI, Ned Koh of Aaru, Dara Ladjevardian of Delphi, Bri Treece of Fathom, & Andrew Yang of Noble Mobile. alpha.ac These leaders bring perspectives across enterprise deployment, venture investment, corporate oversight, AI governance, & the technologies changing how companies operate. Directors with oversight responsibility & executives with execution responsibility will engage directly with the builders & investors advancing the agentic economy. Attendance is curated to keep the room senior, focused, & conducive to substantive conversation. Working conversations take place under the Chatham House Rule, creating space for candid discussion of architectures, incidents, controls, & consequential decisions. Sessions give speakers time to examine the material in depth. Questions continue during deliberate intermissions, where delegates can connect directly with speakers & peers in smaller conversations. The format is built for practical outcomes. There are no vendor pitches. The focus is on real systems, delegated authority, & the decisions leaders must make: what agents may do, who owns their actions, when humans must intervene, & how performance & accountability can be verified. Delegates leave with a clearer view of where agents are entering the enterprise, relationships with the people shaping that transition, & concrete priorities for their next board, committee, or management meeting. In the agentic economy, every decision to delegate authority is a governance decision. Growth depends on getting it right. Governance is Alpha.

The Alpha Agentic Economy Summit is the gathering for leaders building the agentic enterprise & those accountable for its decisions. On November 6, 2026, at Nasdaq MarketSite in New York City, Alpha brings together board directors, management teams, investors, & technology leaders to address a defining challenge: enterprises are delegating authority to AI faster than their governance can adapt. AI agents are already executing transactions, writing & deploying code, & making operational decisions between board meetings. As their authority expands, so does the exposure: financial loss, operational disruption, legal liability, & reputational damage. Boards need to understand where that authority sits, how it is controlled, & what evidence demonstrates that oversight is working. The Summit connects the boardroom with the people shaping this shift. Confirmed speakers include Gary Vaynerchuk, Chairman of VaynerX; Stacy Brown-Philpot, Founder & Managing Partner of Cherryrock Capital; Ann Miura-Ko, Co-Founding Partner of Floodgate; Laura Desmond, CEO of Smartly; Al Zollar, board director at BNY, IBM, & Nasdaq; & Madhu Muthukumar, Chief Product Officer of SoFi. They join leaders including Navrina Singh of Credo AI, Philip Rathle of Neo4j, Wasim Khaled of Blackbird.AI, Ned Koh of Aaru, Dara Ladjevardian of Delphi, Bri Treece of Fathom, & Andrew Yang of Noble Mobile. alpha.ac These leaders bring perspectives across enterprise deployment, venture investment, corporate oversight, AI governance, & the technologies changing how companies operate. Directors with oversight responsibility & executives with execution responsibility will engage directly with the builders & investors advancing the agentic economy. Attendance is curated to keep the room senior, focused, & conducive to substantive conversation. Working conversations take place under the Chatham House Rule, creating space for candid discussion of architectures, incidents, controls, & consequential decisions. Sessions give speakers time to examine the material in depth. Questions continue during deliberate intermissions, where delegates can connect directly with speakers & peers in smaller conversations. The format is built for practical outcomes. There are no vendor pitches. The focus is on real systems, delegated authority, & the decisions leaders must make: what agents may do, who owns their actions, when humans must intervene, & how performance & accountability can be verified. Delegates leave with a clearer view of where agents are entering the enterprise, relationships with the people shaping that transition, & concrete priorities for their next board, committee, or management meeting. In the agentic economy, every decision to delegate authority is a governance decision. Growth depends on getting it right. Governance is Alpha.

events.name: Data By Design
events.description: In conversation with Shannon Mattern. P&T Knitwear is pleased to welcome Lauren Klein, Tanvi Sharma, & Silas Munro to celebrate & discuss the release of their book Data by Design, which explores how the history of data visualization holds the key to designing a more just future. They will be in conversation with Shannon Mattern, & will sign books after the talk! Doors open at 6:30pm with the talk starting closer to 7:00pm. Come early & grab a drink from the P&T Cafe! Tickets & books are available both on eventbrite & at the door. Housekeeping notes: This is a ticketed in-store event with limited amphitheater-style seating.Doors open at 6:30pm, with the talk starting around 7:00pm.Cost of a book bundle ticket reflects the total cost of the feature event book (MSRP plus tax). Each book bundle ticket guarantees ticket holders one (1) copy of the feature event book.The talk will be followed by a book signing. Books signed at P&T Knitwear events must be purchased from P&T Knitwear.If you would like a signed copy & cannot attend the event, we're happy to take your pre-order. We ship most places!About the authors:Lauren Klein is Professor of Data & Decision Sciences & English at Emory University, where she also directs the Digital Humanities Lab & the Atlanta Interdisciplinary AI Network. Her research brings together computational & critical methods to explore questions of gender, race, & justice, both in early America & today. Klein is the author (with Catherine D'Ignazio) of the award-winning Data Feminism (MIT Press, 2020), & the editor (with Matthew K. Gold) of Debates in the Digital Humanities (Univ. of Minnesota Press), among other books & papers. Her next book, Data by Design: Visualization & Power from Abolition to the Dawn of Data Science (MIT Press), will be out in October 2026.  Silas Munro is a designer, artist, writer, curator, surfer, & descendant of the Banyole people of Eastern Uganda. He founded the design studio Polymode, whose clients include MoMA, the MET, Nike, & the Hammer. Munro is the curator & author of Strikethrough: Typographic Messages of Protest at Letterform Archive & the co-curator of Reverberations: Lineages in Design History at the Ford Foundation Gallery. He contributed to W. E. B. Du Bois's Data Portraits: Visualizing Black America, & co-authored the first BIPOC-centered design history course, Black Design in America: African Americans & the African Diaspora in Graphic Design 19th-21st Century. His visual art was recently exhibited at Data Consciousness: Reframing Blackness in Contemporary Print at Print Center New York. Tanvi Sharma is a design technologist working at the intersection of data, aesthetics, & the humanities. She is currently an Art Director at Apple & co-author of Data by Design (MIT Press, 2026). She has previously worked at Pentagram, Public Policy Lab, & Spotify. She lives in Harlem, NY, with her two cats, Yuchi & Bubbles. More at tanvi.network.   About the moderator:Shannon Mattern is the Director of Creative Research at the Metropolitan New York Library Council, a state-founded, member-supported non-profit linking hundreds of libraries & archives across the city. Previously, she held tenured full professorships in media studies, anthropology, & art history at The New School & the University of Pennsylvania. She is the author of four books, the (co-)editor of six collections, & the author of over 100 articles & chapters about urban technology, knowledge infrastructures, maps, maintenance, data art, & other heterogenous subjects. She was the 2025 Kluge Chair in Modern Culture at the Library of Congress & the 2025 Design Indexer in residence at the Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum. You can find her at wordsinspace.net.

events.name: An UNMUTED Book Club: The 100 Years War On Palestine
events.description: READING NOT REQUIRED - just be curious! Next up: Rashid Khalidi's The Hundred Years' War on Palestine, the 2020 book that argues the Israeli-Palestinian conflict isn't simply a tragic struggle between two peoples claiming the same land, but a century-long colonial campaign against Palestinians, backed first by Britain & later by the United States. Khalidi, a Palestinian-American historian at Columbia, tells the story through six turning points, beginning with the 1917 Balfour Declaration & moving through the creation of Israel, the wars that followed, & the failures of the peace process. Drawing on historical archives & his own family's experiences, he makes a provocative argument: that Palestinians have never been negotiating on equal terms, & that understanding the conflict as a dispute between two competing national movements obscures the enormous imbalance of power between them. It's a forceful challenge to conventional accounts of Israel's founding, Zionism, & America's role in the region, & one that raises uncomfortable questions about nationalism, colonialism, & self-determination. Show up even if you only got through a chunk. We'll talk about where Khalidi's account is most convincing, where it leaves out important context, whether Zionism is best understood as a colonial movement or a national liberation movement, & what his interpretation of the past means for the possibility of peace today. UNMUTED is a discussion forum for the politically curious. Accessible. Engaging. Social. Open-minded is the name of the game. Join your people.

events.name: Monday Founders Coworking Pod
events.description: If you're an early stage founder, building alone is hard. You lose momentum, get stuck with no one to ask, & there's no one checking if you actually did what you said you'd do this week. We're a small group of founders working together for the month - think study group, but for building. We help each other, check in, & keep each other on track. Now we're opening it up to more people, in pods of 3-5. Here's how it works: you tell your pod what you're trying to get done, & they hold you to it. Stuck on something? Someone in the pod probably knows the answer. Starting to slip? Someone notices. Same faces every week, so you're never starting over with strangers. This is an outgrowth of our Wednesday coworking events - just smaller. We're here to build the idea & building culture NYC deserves. We focus on that foundational layer of relationships & community that allows for ideas to spread & building to happen. events.name: Business Funding - An International Perspective
events.description: Every stage of growing a business is a funding decision, even when it doesn't feel like one. How you pay for the next market, the next hire, the next acquisition quietly shapes what the business is worth years later, & who you can sell it to. Across the Atlantic, the options multiply & the advice gets thinner. During the evening, hear from speakers across the corporate lifecycle, sharing their different funding, expansion & exit stories, so you leave with greater insight & awareness of the opportunities, & the pitfalls to avoid. Designed for international founders & business executives planning to grow in New York City, the discussion will cover the advantages, tradeoffs, & tactics involved in raising capital from VC & PE sources.  Speakers Dan Jaeck is a Principal at Crane VC, based between New York & London, where he partners with founders building transformational software companies.Before joining Crane, he spent four years at Eniac Ventures in NYC, investing in AI application-layer & infrastructure companies. Prior to Eniac, Dan began his career at Goldman Sachs in London on the Emerging Market Equities desk. Joel Goschalk is a Senior Director at Dundon Advisers, advising middle-market companies on recapitalizations, restructurings & credit. He started as a London insolvency practitioner, co-founded & scaled a UK litigation funding & private equity business (Cavendish IP Solutions), & has spent over a decade as COO of a family office, advising on fundraising rounds, fund formation across the UK, US & offshore, & cross-border expansion.  Co-host: The Transatlantic Innovation Hub, is New York's launch pad for Italian & European companies, to help them successfully enter & scale in the U.S. market. Located in the heart of Manhattan, TIH serves as a landing pad for innovation ecosystems, providing companies with both a physical presence in New York & a structured set of market access services to accelerate their U.S. expansion. The Knowledge Shop is the founder community in NYC. We are industry & stage agnostic, helping not just startups grow, but supporting the founders building them.  Founding Partner: Sabre Integrated has been providing commercial security systems in NYC since 2000.From access control & video surveillance to fully integrated security systems, they design, install & support your business every step of the way  Charity Partner: The St George's Society of New York, provides life-changing support to immigrants from Britain & the Commonwealth in New York. Established in 1770, we're the second-oldest charity in the city. We hold events year round - join us for Pancake day   Find even more Tech events at: www.foundereventsnyc.com

events.name: Is Everything Predictable - AI, Prediction Markets & Philosophy Of Foresight
events.description: In this six-week course, explore works from philosophy, cultural studies, & journalism to understand how technologies that predict the future also shape the present.The age of AI, prediction markets, & real-time data analysis brings predictive reasoning into all corners of human life. Once considered a niche academic interest area, the philosophy & politics of prediction is now relevant to everybody. Is Everything Predictable?: AI, Prediction Markets, & the Philosophy of Foresight presents scholarly material on forecasting technologies in a rigorous but highly accessible format.Drawing from a range of sources, we center scholarly texts & deeply-researched journalism that uncover the links between digital calculation, philosophical notions of time & free will, & the reality of living in an age where everything seems reducible to calculation.Guest speakers from academia & tech journalism will round out our seminar sessions, & for our final meeting, students have the option of presenting original research or creative work in an event open to the general public.SyllabusIn the early weeks of the course, we read texts from contemporary media studies & political theory that construe prediction & speculation as forms of governance. We also address probabilistic reasoning as a key feature of artificial intelligence & prediction market mechanisms, using frameworks suitable for participants without any background in STEM. As we will see, the similarities & differences between how probability works in AI versus prediction markets have much to tell us about these tools effects on everything from global warfare & the environment to creativity & personal relationships.After establishing a strong practical & theoretical foundation in AI & prediction markets, we turn to philosophical writing on the nature of freedom, self-expression, & power. These texts urge us to ask whether predictive technologies empower us with highly advanced forms of knowledge; if they inhibit us by constraining our imagination of whats possible; or if both of these outcomes might be true at once. We also read articles & listen to podcast interviews with our guest speakers in anticipation of their visits.Throughout our sessions, we examine case studies related to tech companies, specific applications, & major actors in the AI & prediction market space. The courses culminating event  a salon open to the general public  reflects our interest in connecting questions & concerns that seem highly academic to current events & everyday life. Students who choose to give presentations will participate in an additional workshop or one-on-one advising session to help them prepare. By the courses end, we will be able to navigate a world driven by predictive technologies with greater clarity, confidence, & wisdom, & to share our perspectives on them in a way that empowers those around us.Learning OutcomesConnect AI & prediction market functionalities to political & cultural affairsDevelop critical reading skills applicable to philosophy & journalismApply frameworks from the theoretical humanities to real-world developments in politics & technologyMake scholarly ideas accessible to a wide range of audiencesScholarshipsIndex scholarships are designed to benefit underrepresented groups, BIPOC members of our community, & those for whom the class price is not accessible. These need-based scholarships will go to the candidates who best demonstrate why they should be chosen for the free spot to our class. You can apply for a scholarship here.Instructor BioEmma Stamm is a writer & professor with a background in philosophy & the social study of science & technology (STS). She holds a PhD in Interdisciplinary Studies from Virginia Tech & has taught courses on the philosophy & social implications of technology at Villanova University, Virginia Tech, the Acid Horizon Research Commons, New York University, where she currently teaches for the Department of Media, Culture, & Communication. As a public-facing scholar, she has written for Vice Motherboard, Real Life Mag, & Communications of the Association for Computing Machinery, in addition to co-hosting the LEPHT HAND podcast. She is the co-founder & Executive Director of theLenox Institute for Advanced Study, which makes critical science & tech education accessible beyond academia.RefundsWe get that things come up, but we rely on headcounts to make our programs viable. events.name: Propel Demo Day  Innovation In Public Cohort Showcase
events.description: Ten companies. Twelve minutes each. An investor room in New York. Who we are. Propel Earth has run 100+ events & built a network of 36,000+ founders, investors, operators, & service providers across six continents. We are not an events company. We are an outcomes company that happens to use rooms. You bring the intent. We deliver the outcome. Demo Night NYC is the biggest room we have ever run, 26,666 people on the guest list & 35+ investors in the room. This is that format, built for the companies coming out of our cohort & the investors who back them. Every attendee tells us at registration what they are building & who they need to meet. Before doors open we hand you at least one named introduction plus the framing for the conversation. Founders leave with investor conversations, investors leave with deal flow they did not have to source. The night 6:00 Doors, drinks, & your matches are waiting7:00 Ten companies, twelve minutes each, pitch & questions8:15 Room favourite, voted live8:30 Open floor with the investors in the room9:00 Close Tickets General admission, free. Open to founders, investors, operators & anyone building.Present Your Company, 250 dollars. Ten slots only. Stage time in front of an investor room, professional video of your pitch, & your company in the post event send.Title Sponsor, 5,000 dollars. One per Demo Day. Naming rights, logo on all promotion & the photo backdrop, a brand moment from the stage, & the full registrant list within 48 hours.Free for Propel Private Network members. What Propel actually does for you 1  Innovation in Public, our GTM accelerator. For founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go to market: content, distribution, & more sales. Four weeks, twice a week, building in public, closing with a public showcase at Propel Demo Day in front of an investor room. Applications for the next cohort are open at this link. 2  The Propel Private Network. Stop networking. Start getting matched. Every month we personally hand you three introductions chosen for what you need right now - someone who can pay you, hire you, or move your company forward. It works both ways: you go into the pool too. Founding rate $200/mo, first 25 members, locked for life  Claim a founding membership 3  Propel Community Coworking x Wayo Club. Come Wednesday night, then come back Thursday & build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, founded by Jason Malefakis. Wayo is a curated community workspace network where members work from premium venues alongside thoughtfully selected founders, operators, & consultants they can collaborate with, refer, hire, or do business with. Attendees typically report being 1.5 to 2x more productive than working from home or a cafe, & leave with 2 to 3 meaningful connections. Lunch is included. Register with us  Propel Community Coworking 1.0  Get a Wayo Community Workday membership  Join the Wayo Anytime waitlist 4  Featured Founder. Build your founder or service-provider profile on Propel & we will give you one additional intro on us  propel.earth/featured-founders 5  Providers already in the room. This is not theoretical. Moshe Cohen, CPA of Cohen & Co runs tax strategy, bookkeeping & fractional CFO work for Propel founders & takes bookings through us. Thirty minute paid session, 120 dollars  Book Moshe. Stephen Michael Consulting, a 45 minute strategy call for funded founders raising, investors deploying, & enterprises entering the startup ecosystem, 150 dollars  Book a strategy call. If you provide a service & want a table at the next one, that is what the provider ticket is. On camera: Nik Michael, host of the Pivot Point podcast, is shooting photography, video, & follow up interviews with select attendees. Nik is a licensed clinician with more than thirty years in counseling & decades in business, education, & investing, & his show explores the moments where transformation begins. Watch the show on YouTube  Listen on Spotify or Apple Podcasts  More at counselingtherapy.com/pivotpoint. Want to be featured, reach out to him directly. Newsletter  propelearth.beehiiv.com  Propel Earth  propel.earth  Questions, text Stephen at 516 307 6380. About The WilsonThe Wilson NYC is a popular American comfort-food restaurant & bar located in NoMad/Chelsea. While the restaurant does not hold traditional culinary stars (like Michelin), it acts as a highly-rated, frequent event space for awards shows & local hospitality honors due to its event duplex & outdoor patio. The Wilson has also been celebrated for supporting its employees through the One Fair Wage What Propel does, & what it has produced Nine ways we connect this network. Every one of these is a room we have already run. Founders & Investors. We put founders in rooms with the people who write checks. Demo Night NYC ran in front of 35+ investors. Founders x Investors Night at PhD Lounge, the Funders x Founders High Line Walk, the Harvard Club Investment Dinner, & the NYTW Pitch Competition with 800+ registrations. Every monthly mixer does the same thing at a smaller scale, which is why we cap the room & match you before you arrive. Founders & Service Providers. You tell us what you need & we match you to someone vetted who does it. Legal, tax, engineering, design, growth, operations. events.name: Drinks & Hacking: IT Happy Hour with The Objective-See Foundation
events.description: Join Rippling IT & The Objective-See Foundation for a happy hour at the Rippling NYC office. Over drinks & light bites, enjoy networking with your fellow IT pros & enjoy a presentation from Patrick Wardle, Co-Founder of the Objective-See Foundation, titled: Your Agent, My Orders: Hacking ChatGPT. A bit more about Patrick's presentation: AI agents need broad access to our files, accounts, & devices, making them prime targets for hackers. We took a closer look at ChatGPT's macOS desktop app & uncovered vulnerabilities that allow attackers to turn your trusted AI assistant against you. The impact? Attackers could hijack your Dot, take over your OpenAI account, access protected files, & more. Worse, these attacks present new challenges for traditional security tools: when an AI agent is compromised, malicious activity can look just like the agent doing its job. We'll demo what happens when ChatGPT gets hacked, discuss why AI agents pose new security challenges, & explore what all this means for Mac admins & the future of endpoint security. You can read more about this in NYT & Wired - & we hope to see you in-person for the full presentation. See you soon! A bit about us: Rippling IT amplifies your abilities & supercharges your skills. Control the entire user lifecycle in one system with fully built Identity, Device, & Inventory management tools, & 500+ integrations-including custom SCIM & SAML. Simplify, secure, & scale all from one single platform. Objective-See is a non-profit foundation focused on macOS security, driven by the mission to create free tools, grow & support a global community of students, researchers, & defenders, & advance Apple security through education, research, collaboration, & opportunity, around the world.

events.name: Borderless Office - Identity & Access In World Of Remote-First Growth
events.description: Join Antoine Jebara (Co-founder, JumpCloud) & Noah Landow (Founder & CEO, Macktez) for an informal conversation between an expert on scaling global technology companies & the evolution of identity & access management & the founder of a technology consulting firm. In an era defined by remote work & the rapid rise of agentic AI, the concepts of identity & security are shifting beneath our feet. As AI agents begin to act on our behalf, how do we maintain control, responsibility, & security? If an AI agent executes a transaction or accesses a database, who is truly holding the keys? Antoine brings a unique perspective from the front lines of this transition, from pioneering decentralized 2FA & password management at MYKI to driving global strategy & partner ecosystems at JumpCloud. Join us at the Macktez office, after work, over light snacks & sips, for an exploratory conversation on the challenges of scaling fast-growing global companies & how different security architectures impact our long-term safety in a cloud-first world. We will dive into the shifting landscape of encryption, the unique hurdles of managing remote-first organizations, & what it truly means to "identity" ourselves in the age of AI. Photography, audio, & video recording may occur at this event & by attending you consent to such recording media & its release, publication, exhibition, or reproduction. Event StructureWe ask that guests arrive between 7-7:30 pm to minimize disruption during the talk. 7 pm - Doors open, opportunity to mingle over snacks & sips with other attendees7:30 pm - Guests take their seats for the talk8:15 pm - Informal mixer resumes On AttendanceWe have a limited capacity. If your plans change, please update your registration so someone else can join. A bit about Macktez, & why we host this seriesMacktez is a technology consultancy collaborating with organizations going through dynamic change. Our goal is to form a lasting partnership between our team & our clients, so we can anticipate their technology challenges & help them navigate growth, disruption, & other evolving conditions. Each event in our Tte--Tech series is an opportunity to explore a specific cultural, scientific, historical, & personal issue. We fire at the synapses that connect each topic to other fields of interest & to our individual lives. And we do so in a comfortable environment to facilitate conversation that can be casual, surprising, & illuminating. To learn more, visit us at macktez.com.

events.name: The AI Era & What It Means To Be Human
events.description: The AI Era & What It Means to Be HumanAI is changing how we work, learn, create, & make decisions. But underneath the conversation about models, agents, & automation is a more fundamental question: what does it mean to be human in an age of increasingly capable machines? On October 23rd, The AI Collective is bringing together 100 people in NYC for an evening exploring the human side of the AI era. We'll move beyond the usual conversation about what AI can do & look instead at what its rise asks of us: how we learn, how we maintain agency, how we relate to one another, & which distinctly human capacities become more important as technology advances. The evening will combine conversation, small-group discussion, & experiential mindfulness/wellness exercises. This is not a technical AI event. We're creating a conversation about the human layer: the trust, awareness, connection, & shared understanding we'll need to build alongside the technology. Come curious. Expect to participate. Agenda6:00 PM: Arrival & Welcome6:30 PM: Opening Remarks + Experiential Mindfulness Exercise6:45 PM: Fireside Chat: AI & the Human Condition with Mohan Nair, author of "Unreachable: How to Not Lose Your Mind in an AI-Obsessed Era."7:15 PM: Conversation with Catherine & Manas followed by Breath-work & Meditation.7:45 PM: Small-Group Roundtables8:15 PM: Dessert & Networking Food & beverages provided. Space is limited to 75 participants. Co-hosted by The AI Collective & Manas Ram with support from JQ Consulting, whose work focuses on the science of human wellbeing, resilience, happiness, mindfulness, & the human condition. Please be advised: Unfortunately, space is very limited at these community events & we can not always accept everyone we would like to. If you are not accepted to this event, please keep applying! We appreciate your application tremendously & we are looking forward to seeing you at a future event very soon! The AI Collective is a global non-profit building the human layer for the AI era. We unite 200,000+ leaders, builders, & stakeholders across 100+ forums worldwide to democratize the frontier, build trust, & coordinate how society navigates the rapid acceleration of technological progress. All attendees & organizers at events affiliated with The AI Collective agree to our privacy policy & are subject to our code of conduct.

events.name: Ground Truth: The Live Agents Hackathon
events.description: Every AI model you've ever used is stuck in the past. Ground Truth is a one-day hackathon where you fix that. Join localhost:nyc, The Builder Series & You.com for 10 hours of building AI agents grounded in the live web. Real-time data, deep research, verifiable answers. Come build the kind of agent people would trust with a real decision. Problem StatementEvery LLM is frozen at its training cutoff. It doesn't know what happened this morning, & when it doesn't know, it guesses, confidently. That's the gap between a cool demo & a product people rely on. Your challenge: build an AI agent that knows what's true right now. It searches the live web through the You.com API, reads the sources, reasons over them & shows its receipts. The Challenge TracksLive Wire (real-time agents): agents that wake up when the world changes. Price moves, breaking news, a competitor launch, a policy change, a new job posting. If it happened in the last hour, your agent already knows & already acted. The Analyst (deep research): pick a profession (VCs, lawyers, journalists, recruiters, doctors, policy staffers) & replace its 40-hour research memo with a 4-minute one, every claim cited. Receipts (trust & verification): agents that fact-check claims, catch AI hallucinations, verify sources & show their work. Best Content (open to every team): post about what you built, tag You.com, & win a dedicated prize. What to ExpectA kickoff walkthrough of the You.com API: Search, Contents, Research & the hosted MCP server Free You.com API credits for every builder 6 hours of building Teams of up to 4, or solo if that's your thing Team matching at kickoff if you're coming alone Mentors from You.com on the floor all day Live demos to judges at the end, plus food all day Prizes1st Place Overall: $500 cash Best Content: TBD JudgesTBD Who Should AttendEngineers (full stack, backend, AI/ML) Founders & aspiring founders building with AI Designers & product people who want to ship something real Researchers & analysts who know exactly what a great research agent should do You don't need a finished idea. Just show up ready to build. SponsorsYou.com: AI search infrastructure that gives agents real-time, cited access to the web through its Search, Contents & Research APIs. Hostslocalhost:nyc: Making NYC the biggest startup ecosystem in the world. The Builder Series   The Builder Series: A 60,000+ member community redefining what networking looks like - curating founders, operators, investors & more into intentional rooms built for experiences people remember & relationships that last. It's a direct line to the most ambitious builders, with a community that actually shows up.   Connect with Me: Join 60,000+ people shaping the future  Join the Newsletter  Follow the Builder Series  Find me here

events.name: Unmuted  Debate - AI & China
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In July, a Chinese lab you'd probably never heard of published Kimi K3: 2.8 trillion parameters, billed as the largest open model on earth, weights posted free on Hugging Face for anyone to download. It's one of four Chinese labs that spent the last year closing the gap with the American frontier, then giving the result away. Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi. Four of the five most-used open models in the world now come out of Beijing, & American developers are running them inside hospitals, law firms, & startups because they're the cheapest, fastest tools available. No API someone in Washington controls. No off switch. Just download & go. One camp says a model is just math. Open weights run on a consumer's machine, the code is right there to inspect, & cutting Americans off from the best tools on the planet is how you lose a technology race. The other camp says the giveaway is the strategy. China seeds the world's infrastructure with their standards, their defaults, their assumptions, & the dependency follows once switching costs become unbeatable. So: should Americans be allowed to build on Chinese open-weight models or is this the new Cold War's Monkey's Paw? Arguing for, Rob Li is Managing Partner of Amont Partners, a New York global equity firm that invests across the US & Asia. He has spent his career putting capital on both sides of the Pacific, from Yum China to Alibaba deals, & he thinks the country that walls itself off from the best tools available loses. Arguing against, Will McKelvey is a Principal at Lerer Hippeau, one of New York's oldest venture firms, where he backs early-stage founders & spends his days watching for the future of AI, especially in consumer. He got his start by way of a congressional office, & he thinks the cheapest model on the market is the one you pay for slowly. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones. In collaboration with COMMITTEE OF 100Committee of 100 (C100) is a nonprofit U.S. leadership organization of distinguished Chinese Americans dedicated to advancing the full participation of Chinese Americans in American society & fostering constructive U.S.-China relations. For more than 35 years, C100 has brought together leaders across business, government, academia, technology, media, the arts, & other fields to advance its dual mission. Learn more at committee100.org.

events.name: NY Tech Meetup - Climate Tech Edition
events.description: NY Tech Meetup  Columbia University SPSM.S. Technology Management Program We're excited to welcome back Columbia University's School of Professional Studies M.S. Technology Management program for another special edition of the NY Tech Meetup! Join us on Monday, November 9, as we spotlight emerging innovators from Columbia's Technology Management program who are turning bold ideas into promising technologies & real-world solutions. From fresh approaches to everyday challenges to innovations with the potential to transform industries, this edition offers a unique opportunity to discover what's next, hear directly from the innovators, & connect with NYC's vibrant tech community. As always, expect live demos, engaging conversations, new connections, & the energy that makes NY Tech Meetup a cornerstone of New York's tech ecosystem. Presenting innovators & their demos will be announced soon. Stay tuned! Program 6:00 PM - Doors Open 6:30 PM - Welcome & Live Demos 8:00 PM - Community Ask / Offer 8:15 PM - After-Party & Networking Come for the demos. Stay for the connections. Seats are limited - register now to secure your spot! About the NY Tech Meetup The NY Tech Meetup (NYTM) is a signature event of theNY Tech Alliance that has been a monthly staple for the NYC tech ecosystem since 2004. It is the world's largest meetup group of its kind with over 50,000 members who have a common interest in learning from & helping one another. At each event, entrepreneurs, founders, CEOs, & their teams demo cutting edge & transformative tech, answer questions from attendees & network with all in a welcoming & fun-filled space. Since its creation, over 1,200 companies have participated & have been a driving force of innovation & job creation in NYC & the greater NY area. About Columbia University's M.S. in Technology Management Columbia University's M.S. in Technology Management (TMGT) equips graduates with applied technology skills through research & industry insights to lead digital transformations & innovation in organizations across industries with an ethical leadership lens to achieve high impact & measurable results for today & to prepare for the future. Guided by Columbia's School of Professional Studies Scholar-Practitioner model, the program bridges theory & practice by integrating cutting-edge, real-world applications into the classroom experience & offers flexible pathways to the Masters of Science in Technology Management degree. The In-Person STEM-designated pathway offers full-time & part-time options & the Online part-time option is designed for working professionals who want the rigor & community of Columbia University from anywhere in the world. Through the School of Professional Studies' immersive digital learning environment, students engage in live, interactive classes led by Columbia faculty & industry experts.

events.description: 4 part workshop hosted by Healing Healthtech on "How to Raise Your First Priced Round." Raising your first priced round is a completely different undertaking than stacking safe notes. I want to help you skip the avoidable mistakes.  The diligence is deeper, the relevant terms are completely different, & the stakes for getting it wrong are much higher as priced round investors will almost always take board seats & protective provisions.  I've taught founders how to navigate a priced round for years & on October 27th in NYC will be conducting a public bootcamp / workshop with the highest impact aspects. Location will be the beautiful Gunderson Dettmer NYC offices above Flatiron. Generously sponsored by Jose Rivera & Tonna Obaze of Gunderson Dettmer, Kelly Caviglia of Mercury, & Paul Brezovsky III of Qapita. Session 1: Taught by Ramesh Karra & Paul Brezovsky III's team at Qapita will focus on Data Room. What goes in, what doesn't, what investors are looking for, & how not get get tripped up. Session 2: Taught by Jose Rivera of Gunderson Dettmer will focus on the term sheet negotiation. What terms matter & which don't. How to affect outcomes that are durable & beneficial for your business. Session 3: Taught by me will focused on how to find, pitch, & close priced round investors. Session 4: Will be a panel discussion & fireside chat with 3 partners at NYC VC firms. I've purposely chosen folks who represent software & hardware investors as well as funds that operate outside of healthcare. Mat Kaliski of Acronym Venture CapitalBrian Laung Aoaeh, CFA of REFASHIOND Ventures: The Industrial Transformation FundOwen Willis of Opal Ventures & Primary Venture Partners
