events.description: Tech Table Talk: Career, Family & Life on Your Terms is an intimate dinner bringing together women in tech for an honest conversation about career, fertility, family planning, & building a life on their own terms. Hosted by Baddies in Tech in partnership with Spring Fertility, the evening will create space for women to have the kinds of conversations we don't often have: How do you think about growing your career while also considering a future family? What options are available if your personal & professional timelines do not align perfectly? And how can having more information today create more choices tomorrow? We're setting the Tech Table to create space for a conversation you may have been thinking about but have not had anyone to talk to about. You'll walk away not just with a great meal & new professional connections, but also more information, more context, & more confidence to make decisions that feel right for the life you're building! What to ExpectWelcome & Opening ToastBaddies in Tech & Spring Fertility will welcome the group & set the tone for an open, judgment-free conversation about career, fertility, family planning, & the life you're building. Dinner & Tech Table TalkOver dinner, guests will have the opportunity to connect more deeply with one another through thoughtful conversation & curated table prompts, exploring the realities of building a career while also thinking about relationships, motherhood, fertility, timing, & what it means to make decisions on your own terms. Fertility Planning Q&A with Dr. Shante Sullivan-PikeThroughout the evening, Dr. Shante Sullivan-Pike of Spring Fertility will help answer questions & demystify fertility, fertility preservation, & family-planning options. Dr. Chantae Sullivan-Pyke is a double board certified Fertility Specialist & Site Director of Spring Fertility Long Island. She completed her medical training at Yale University, Columbia University, & the University of Pennsylvania. Dr. Sullivan-Pyke brings a thoughtful & compassionate approach to fertility care, rooted in deep clinical experience & a genuine connection with her patients. She combines her expertise with a strong commitment to the patient experience, creating a supportive & empowering atmosphere throughout the process. Her areas of clinical focus include IVF, fertility preservation, & oncofertility, & she is particularly passionate about helping her patients navigate complex fertility decisions with clarity & confidence. What You'll Leave WithFresh perspective on navigating career goals alongside personal & family plans New relationships with women thinking through many of the same questions A better understanding of your fertility & family-planning options More clarity around fertility preservation & when it may be worth exploring Greater confidence asking questions about your reproductive health A stronger connection to the Baddies in Tech & Spring Fertility communitie Attendance is complimentary & curated. Because this dinner is intentionally intimate & limited to approximately 20-25 guests, registrations will be reviewed to create a group that aligns with the purpose of the evening. Submitting the registration form expresses your interest in attending & does not guarantee an invitation. Confirmed guests will be notified approximately one week before the event.

events.name: OverdriveAI Summit
events.description: Overdrive AIHosted by TechUnited:NJ, creators of Propelify, heralded by Forbes as the "SXSW of the Northeast," OverdriveAI is back, & this year it's a debate. The hottest topics in AI, argued live, both sides on stage. Jobs, energy, education, & more. Sharp thinkers go head to head, you hear the case for & against, & you decide where you land. Taking place this year at the Newark Museum of Art, where tech & culture share a roof, OverdriveAI brings together founders, operators, investors, & researchers from across the Northeast for a day built around one idea: the biggest questions in AI don't have easy answers, so let's actually argue about them. TICKETS ARE NOW LIVE!EXPLORE THE FULL OVERDRIVEAI EXPERIENCE Community AI TrainingHands-on morning AI training at EqualSpace designed for all experience levels. No prior AI experience required. Reserve Your Spot Executive AI TrainingA focused, practical AI training designed for executives & business leaders ready to better understand & apply AI within their organizations. Reserve Your Spot Pitch Roast LiveStartups pitch. Comedians roast. Everyone wins. Close out OverdriveAI with an evening of bold ideas, founder pitches, comedy, & connection. Reserve Your Spot   What to Expect Community AI Training A hands-on morning (10a-12p ET) AI training at EqualSpace designed for all experience levels. Come ready to learn, explore, & put AI into practice. No prior experience required. Executive AI Training Turn AI into practical business advantage. Start your morning with a focused AI training session designed for executives, business leaders, & decision-makers navigating the rapidly evolving AI landscape. This interactive session will explore practical ways leaders can better understand, evaluate, & apply AI within their organizations helping you move from conversation to action. The AI Debates The main event at the Newark Museum of Art. Will AI take your job or grow the economy? Who pays for AI's energy appetite? Does AI belong in the classroom? Can you still trust what you see? Startup demos will be featured between rounds & the afternoon will roll into TechUnited:NJ Birthday Party! Final topics & speakers are still being locked in, ticket holders hear every name first. Here's what's on the table so far: AI takes jobs vs. AI grows the economy - does automation erase more work than it creates? Is AI raising your energy bill? - the data center buildout is reshaping the grid, & New Jersey's in the middle of it. Does AI belong in the classroom? - a tutor for every student, or the end of learning how to think? Is it time for universal basic income? - if productivity keeps compounding, someone decides where the gains go. Can we handle deepfakes? - synthetic media's getting cheap & convincing, what's the real defense? Got a debate we missed? Suggest it, & if it makes the stage, you'll know it was yours. Live debates. Experts, opposing sides of one question, no hedging.Hot takes. Short, sharp presentations from speakers with a strong point of view.Networking. 300+ founders, researchers, & investors in one room, this year in a new venue built for it. Pitch Roast Live Closing the night at Newark Culture Club Close with startup pitches & a high-energy evening experience. Four founders pitch, three comedians & two investors roast. One walks out a winner! Last Year, at Nokia Bell Labs Speakers joined us from OpenAI, IBM, CoreWeave, Verizon, Perplexity, Nokia Bell Labs, BetterFutureLabs, NJEDA, & the NJ AI Hub. 16 speakers, 300+ attendees, a packed house. This year's lineup is coming together now, & it's bigger. OverdriveAI is one of many events TechUnited:NJ runs for its 13,000+ member community, from AI Demo Night to Propelify. Inquire about membership to hear about what's next. TechUnited:NJ members receive complimentary admission to OverdriveAI as part of their membership. Not a member yet? events.description: If you show up with a backpack or your laptop you will be banned from the event. Please leave backpacks at home. RED CARPET ROOM Formerly Fun HouseHosted by Anwar EnterprisesSaturday, October 31, 2026 Exact address released to confirmed guests 24 hours before doors. About the Event Red Carpet Room is the next chapter of Fun House, rebuilt around a single idea: the people building brands should be building them together. This is a mixer for founders, creators, & investors from the Anwar Events community, gathered in one room with a shared reason to be there. Everyone in attendance is constructing something with their name attached to it. The night is designed so the person who can unblock you is standing a few feet away. We are doing it on Halloween on purpose. The city will be full of parties where nothing happens beyond the party itself. This one gives you a panel worth sitting through, a room worth working, & footage of yourself that you will actually use. Run of Show [7pm] - Doors, check-in, & open networking to start the night[8pm] - Panel: operators who built audiences, companies, & reputations from nothing   SPECIAL GUESTS BEING REVEALED NEXT WEEK [9pm] - Open mixer, with Red Carpet Show interviews running in the back room Who's Coming The typical guest is a founder raising or building, a creator monetizing an audience, or an investor looking for both. Expect crossover from fashion, music, media, tech, art & consumer brands, since that is who the Anwar Events community actually contains. Whether you are hiring, raising, pitching a collaboration, or looking for people who take their work as seriously as you do, you will be in the right room. The Red Carpet Show Throughout the night, Ilias will pull guests aside for on-camera interviews for The Red Carpet Show. There is one question at the center of every interview: how can he help you. Those conversations get cut into content that reaches an audience of 70,000 plus founders, investors, & creators. Sitting down costs you four minutes & can put your company in front of people you would never cold email. Dress Code Halloween night calls for more than a costume assembled at the last minute. Come dressed as the version of yourself the press would photograph, whether that means black tie, full character, or your own blend of both. Cameras run from the door onward, so arrive accordingly. Capacity & Entry Space is limited & the guest list is curated. A confirmed RSVP secures your place only until capacity fills, so arriving early is strongly recommended. Bring a valid ID for check-in at the door. About the Host Ilias Anwar is an entrepreneur, marketer, & community builder based in New York City. He has produced more than 600 events across NYC, LA, & San Francisco, cultivating a network of over 70,000 founders, investors, & creators. His work includes brand partnerships with Google, Red Bull, Andreessen Horowitz, & Universal Music Group, along with activations at NFL Super Bowl Weekend & New York Fashion Week. Today he runs Anwar Enterprises, a venture studio that launches & scales consumer & tech companies through distribution first. If you need to meet someone in this city, they have probably attended one of his events. Partners & Sponsors Creatorsarethenewstudios.comCanvas helps creators, founders, & brands turn ideas into media IP they own. AI agents handle the story, production plan, budget, & distribution, & your first IP is free. Happyboards.comHappyBoards makes chef-built charcuterie boards & grazing tables from locally sourced ingredients. It delivers same-day across 27+ Northeast cities, & HappyBoards is feeding the room tonight.Stay Connected Future Anwar Events drop to the community first. Get on the list at luma.com/iliasanwar & follow along on Instagram, X, & LinkedIn for everything we run next. Community Standards Red Carpet Room is inclusive of gender, sexuality, race, religion, & ability. Discrimination or harassment of any kind will not be tolerated on site. For urgent security concerns during the event, please contact venue staff directly. Disclaimers By attending this event, you agree to the following terms. Photography, Video, & Recording: This event will be photographed, filmed, live-streamed, & audio recorded. By entering the venue, you consent to being captured on camera & to the use of your name, image, voice, statements, & likeness by Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, The Red Carpet Show, & their affiliated partners & sponsors. Marketing & Promotional Use: Any material captured at this event may appear in promotional content, social media, websites, newsletters, press coverage, paid advertising, sponsor recap materials, & future marketing assets, worldwide & in perpetuity, without compensation. Guests waive any right to inspect or approve the finished material before publication. On-Camera Interviews: Participation in The Red Carpet Show is entirely voluntary. Sitting for an interview grants Anwar Enterprises the full right to edit, distribute, & monetize that footage across any platform, in any format, without further approval. Opting Out: If you do not wish to be photographed or filmed, please notify event staff upon arrival & avoid the designated filming areas. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to accommodate your request, though appearance in wide or crowd shots cannot be fully prevented. Guest Policy: This is a private, invitation-only event. RSVPs are non-transferable & entry is subject to ID verification. Organizers reserve the right to refuse entry at their discretion. Capacity & Access: This event has a strict capacity limit. A confirmed RSVP does not guarantee entry once capacity has been reached, so early arrival is strongly encouraged. Code of Conduct: All attendees are expected to conduct themselves professionally & respectfully. Organizers reserve the right to remove any guest whose behavior is disruptive or inappropriate, without refund or recourse. Liability: Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, & the venue are not responsible for loss, theft, or damage to personal property. Attendance is at your own risk. Data & Registration: Information submitted at registration may be shared with event sponsors & partners in accordance with their respective privacy policies. Guests may opt out of sponsor communications at any time. Changes & Cancellations: Event details including time, venue, panelists, & programming are subject to change. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to notify registered guests of any material changes.

It's a direct line to the most ambitious builders, with a community that actually shows up. Join The Builder Series membership & network: Apply here Find us here: Instagram  LinkedIn  TikTok  Facebook  X : WhatsApp Broad Channel The goal here:Real lessons from founders who've built & exited, told live & unfiltered, then a room of venture-backed founders & investors to put them to work. The focus of this panel series is relationship capital & with that leveraging relationships as growth capital, Why you should be in this roomLessons you can't get from a podcast: the panel is built around one question founders actually face, how to use relationships as growth capital, answered by people who've done it. The room after the panel: the conversations keep going over with the founders, operators & investors who came for the same reason. Who's speakingAkin Opaleye  Moderator  Founder & CEO, SalesParrot Dylan Oriundo  Host & Panelist  The Builder Series: Built a network of 60K+ in one year. Our panelist: to be announced. Last speaker: Ajay JadhavFounder & CEO, Clouds  Two-time founder, $300M+ in exits Ajay is a two-time founder whose companies have exited for a combined $300M+. His first company built the first internet-enabled advisory platform for American Express. That platform became core infrastructure behind the $10B spinoff of Ameriprise. events.name: Innovation in Public Mixer 5.0  Year End Capital
events.description: Edition 5.0. Theme, year end capital. The monthly room where founders, investors & operators actually get matched. Capped & curated. Everyone leaves with at least one named introduction & the framing for the conversation. November is when allocators are deploying what is left of the year & family offices are planning the next one. This edition leans toward the capital side of the network. Who we are. Propel Earth has run 100+ events & built a network of 36,000+ founders, investors, operators, & service providers across six continents. We are not an events company. We are an outcomes company that happens to use rooms. You bring the intent. We deliver the outcome. This is not a business card room. We cap it at 40-50 people & we curate it. Tell us what you are building & who you need when you register, & before you walk in we hand you at least one match: a specific person, plus the framing for the conversation. Everyone leaves having met someone who matters to what they are working on. You do not need to apply to the cohort to attend. This room is open. Tickets Early Access - $20. Limited, nearly gone.General Admission - $40.Free for Propel Private Network members. Dinner is highly encouraged - the kitchen at The Wilson is excellent. Come hungry & stay late. What Propel actually does for you 1  Innovation in Public - our GTM accelerator. For founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go-to-market: content, distribution, & more sales. Four weeks, twice a week, building in public, closing with a public showcase in front of the room. Applications open for the August cohort  Apply here 2  The Propel Private Network. Stop networking. Start getting matched. Every month we personally hand you three introductions chosen for what you need right now - someone who can pay you, hire you, or move your company forward. It works both ways: you go into the pool too. Founding rate $200/mo, first 25 members, locked for life  Claim a founding membership 3  Propel Community Coworking x Wayo Club. Come Wednesday night, then come back Thursday & build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, founded by Jason Malefakis. Wayo is a curated community workspace network where members work from premium venues alongside thoughtfully selected founders, operators, & consultants they can collaborate with, refer, hire, or do business with. Attendees typically report being 1.5 to 2x more productive than working from home or a cafe, & leave with 2 to 3 meaningful connections. Lunch is included. Register with us  Propel Community Coworking 1.0  Get a Wayo Community Workday membership  Join the Wayo Anytime waitlist 4  Featured Founder. Build your founder or service-provider profile on Propel & we will give you one additional intro on us  propel.earth/featured-founders On camera: Nik Michael of the Pivot Point podcast is shooting photography, video, & follow-up interviews with select attendees. Want to be featured, reach out to him directly. Newsletter  propelearth.beehiiv.com  Propel Earth  propel.earth  Questions, text Stephen at 516 307 6380. About The WilsonThe Wilson NYC is a popular American comfort-food restaurant & bar located in NoMad/Chelsea. While the restaurant does not hold traditional culinary stars (like Michelin), it acts as a highly-rated, frequent event space for awards shows & local hospitality honors due to its event duplex & outdoor patio. The Wilson has also been celebrated for supporting its employees through the One Fair Wage What Propel does, & what it has produced Nine ways we connect this network. Every one of these is a room we have already run. Founders & Investors. We put founders in rooms with the people who write checks. Demo Night NYC ran in front of 35+ investors. Founders x Investors Night at PhD Lounge, the Funders x Founders High Line Walk, the Harvard Club Investment Dinner, & the NYTW Pitch Competition with 800+ registrations. Every monthly mixer does the same thing at a smaller scale, which is why we cap the room & match you before you arrive. Founders & Service Providers. You tell us what you need & we match you to someone vetted who does it. Legal, tax, engineering, design, growth, operations. Our Founders Meet Providers rooms exist for exactly this, & the Propel Marketplace runs it year round. Featured provider this month is Moshe Cohen, CPA, offering a 30 minute startup tax & finance session for $120. Book a session or browse the marketplace Hiring & Talent. events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: Did Maha Maha?
events.description: Has the MAHA movement made Americans healthier than the establishment? Americans spend more on healthcare than anyone else in the world. Yet we have soaring rates of obesity, diabetes, & chronic disease. So is the medical establishment failing us? And is MAHA actually doing any better? RFK's MAHA movement has put ultra-processed foods, environmental toxins, & chronic disease at the center of the national conversation. Supporters say it's finally challenging a healthcare system that profits from treating illness instead of preventing it. Critics say it's undermining trust in vaccines, established science, & the institutions responsible for keeping Americans healthy. So who's right? Is MAHA forcing a long-overdue reckoning with a broken healthcare system? Or is it replacing imperfect science with something far more dangerous? Kerry Semle is a biomedical engineer, former medical technology executive, & women's health advocate with 15 years of experience in medical devices & diagnostics. She's advocated for greater investment in women's health research & improved access to care. Emily Kaplan is the CEO & co-founder of the Broken Science Initiative, an organization challenging the scientific establishment & questioning how medical research is conducted, evaluated, & trusted. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

events.name: GILD AI Forum: AI & Engineering Leaders Dinner
events.description: This GILD AI Forum brings together CTOs, VPs of Engineering, Heads of AI, & senior technical leaders for candid conversations about building, scaling, & implementing AI inside their companies. This isn't a conference. It's not a panel. It's a small, curated room of technical leaders sharing what's actually working, what's not, & the real challenges of shipping AI in the AI era. Each Forum opens with a Conversation Starter, a practitioner sharing what their team is building with AI, followed by open Q&A. From there, the room breaks into intimate discussions where everyone has a seat at the table. Every attendee brings their own experience. Every attendee contributes. No pitches. No performative networking. Just senior technical leaders being honest about the architectures they're choosing, the tradeoffs they're making, & what they wish they'd figured out sooner. TRENDING THEMES FOR THIS SESSION Conversations at the Forum are shaped by what technical leaders bring to the table. Themes likely to surface this evening include: From AI pilots to AI in production: breaking out of the proof-of-concept trap & scaling agents into real workflows Connecting AI to legacy systems: architectural patterns for integrating modern AI with 20-year-old stacks without breaking everything The AI tooling budget problem: balancing experimentation with unsustainable spend as engineers blow through AI tool budgets Engineers as curators, not creators: the shift from writing code to orchestrating AI agents, reusable components, & external services MCP, multi-agent systems, & the orchestration layer: what's working, what's overhyped, & what technical leaders are actually building Guardrails & governance for AI-generated code: who's accountable when the AI writes it, & what review processes actually hold up in production Presented in partnership with Tecla Tecla gives companies flexible access to vetted talent across the US & Latin America, developed for AI-native work & available from fractional engagements to dedicated nearshore pods. Learn more at www.tecla.io THE FORMAT Intentionally small & highly curated, 20 to 25 max. A seated round-table dinner, private & off the record under Chatham House Rules. AGENDA 6:00 - 6:30 PM  Cocktails & passed appetizers 6:30 - 7:00 PM  Dinner is served Find a seat & get comfortable. 6:45 - 6:50 PM  GILD & Partner Welcome A few words from the GILD team & our partners on what the night holds & how we'll spend it together. 6:50 - 7:00 PM  Conversation Starter A fellow engineering leader opens the discussion with a candid perspective on AI, with a brief Q&A. 7:00 - 8:00 PM  Table discussions 8:00 - 8:30 PM  Open mingling WHO THIS IS FOR Founders  CEOs  CTOs  VPs of Engineering  Heads of AI  Technical Leaders  Product Leaders This session is for leaders responsible for building, deploying, & maintaining AI systems in production. Chatham House Rules apply. Discussion stays private.

events.name: An Unmuted Debate: Primary Party Crashers
events.description: Should primaries be open to every voter? More Americans now identify as independent than as Democrat or Republican. Yet in New York & many other states, those voters are shut out of the primaries that often decide who actually wins. So are closed primaries locking out the voters our politics needs most? And would opening them make anything better? Open primaries let any registered voter participate, regardless of party. Supporters say they force candidates to campaign to the whole electorate, reward problem-solvers over partisans, & give millions of independents a real voice. Critics say parties have the right to choose their own nominees, that open systems invite strategic crossover voting & voter confusion, & that the evidence they reduce polarization is thin. So who's right? Are open primaries the fix for a system that rewards the extremes? Or are they a reform that promises more than it delivers? John Opdycke is the founder & president of Open Primaries, a national organization working to enact & protect open & nonpartisan primaries. He has spent three decades in independent & reform politics, helped found the New York State Independence Party, & writes the monthly column Brash Tacks for The Fulcrum. Lindsey Cormack is an associate professor of political science & director of the Diplomacy Lab at Stevens Institute of Technology. She is the author of How to Raise a Citizen (And Why It's Up to You to Do It) & Congress & U.S. Veterans, created the DCInbox database of congressional newsletters, & serves as Secretary of Manhattan Community Board 8. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

events.name: Agent Evaluation Science
events.description: Presented by EvalScience, Agent Evaluation Science NYC 2026 is a one-day symposium bringing together researchers & practitioners working on how AI agents should be evaluated. Featured speakers & contributors include Hanna Wallach (Microsoft Research), Jason Weston (Meta / NYU), Yoav Artzi (Cornell Tech), Nouha Dziri (Cohere Labs), Peter Henderson (Princeton), Olawale Salaudeen (UIUC), Rachneet Kaur (J.P. Morgan), Ida Momennejad (Microsoft Research), & Saurabh Jha (IBM Research). We will discuss what agent evaluations should measure, how reliability & validity should be established, where benchmarks & graders fail, how evaluation infrastructure should be built, & what changes when agents are evaluated in interactive & real-world settings. The program includes invited talks, contributed research presentations, posters, a fireside conversation, & extended discussion & networking. November 20, 2026  New York City Registration is free & approval-based. We welcome researchers, builders, & practitioners working on evaluation methods, benchmarks, agent behavior, evaluation infrastructure, & real-world evaluation problems. We are also accepting contributions including ongoing or published research, evaluation studies, tools, failure analyses, & lessons from evaluating deployed systems. Learn more: https://evalscience.org/2026fall-nyc/

events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Plan Your Best Year With AI
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back  In Person at SalesforceWe're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City and sponsored by Boldforce.This Month We Present...Plan Your Best Year With AIJoin the community for an interactive planning session to reflect on the past year, identify your biggest opportunities, and build an AI-powered roadmap for the year ahead.Before we rush into a new year with another list of goals, lets get clear about what were actually building.What worked this year? What didnt? What deserves more of your energy? And where could AI help you turn those intentions into action?For our final AI & The Culture meetup of the year, were bringing the community together for an interactive planning and reflection session designed to help you look back, think forward, and build a roadmap for what comes next.This isnt about asking AI to magically plan your life. Its about using these tools as thought partnersto help you reflect, uncover patterns, explore possibilities, make decisions, and turn big ambitions into actionable next steps.Together well explore: How to use AI to reflect on your wins, lessons, challenges, and unfinished business from the past year Prompts that help you identify opportunities you might be overlooking How to turn big goals into realistic projects, milestones, and next steps Ways to use AI as a strategic thought partner for your creative work, career, business, or personal projects How to identify where AI and automation can give you back time in the year ahead Building a personalized AI-powered roadmap you can actually use after you leave the roomAnd because this is AI & The Culture, were making space for something AI cant replace: community.Youll have an opportunity to reflect alongside other creatives, founders, educators, artists, technologists, and curious mindsto exchange ideas, share what youre building, and potentially meet the people who can help you move it forward.The goal isnt to leave with 47 resolutions.Its to leave with clarity, priorities, and a plan.Who Should Attend? Creators and content makers Filmmakers, writers, artists, and storytellers Educators and community builders Entrepreneurs, founders, and solopreneurs Marketers, strategists, and creative professionals Technologists and AI enthusiasts Anyone ready to be more intentional about what theyre building nextWhether you already have your next year mapped out or youre still staring at a blank page wondering where to begin, youre welcome here.Come Ready to BuildThis one is especially hands-on, so come prepared to participate. Bring your laptop Bring a notebook or something to write with Bring a few goals, ideas, or questions youve been thinking about for the year ahead Bring your curiosity and a willingness to shareWell be working through reflection exercises, AI prompts, and planning activities togetherso you can leave with the beginnings of a roadmap, not just another page of notes.Come ready to reflect. Come ready to plan. Come ready to build.About AI & The CultureAI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, and culture.Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams and King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, and culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, and community.Were building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI.This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture  grounded in community, focused on real-world use, and centered on learning together in the room.Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Lets build  together. About Your HostsShirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, and co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, and creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, and real-world execution.About King WilloniusKing Willonius is a creative technologist and cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, and creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, and community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable and useful  especially for creatives and innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm. Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio)#AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: Silicon Alley Hack | Build Cool Hardware
events.description: Everyone & their grandma is hosting a hackathon. This is the one where you build something physical. Silicon Alley Hack is a one-day, in-person sprint for builders who'd rather solder than ship a vibe-coded app. Microcontrollers. Sensors. Connected devices. Real hardware that runs in the real world & has to work when we plug it in on stage. Application-based. Teams of 4. Every team gets an STM32 development board & peripherals on arrival. Bring your laptop, your wits, & your soldering instincts.  The Problem StatementSoftware ate the world & then got bored. The interesting frontier moved back to atoms - robots that navigate a room, drones that deliver, sensors that make a physical space legible to a machine. All of it runs on constrained silicon, in real time, in places where the cloud is too slow, too far, or not there at all. So that's the terrain: edge intelligence. Machines that sense the world & act on it, on-device.  The Challenge ThemeThe sealed spec will live somewhere in here: Sense  decide  act, running on-device IoT, sensors, & connected devices Physical/digital interaction - things that move, respond, or react Anything that runs on hardware, not just in a browser Constraints you can count on: You'll be working on an STM32 development board & peripherals - get familiar before you show up It has to run live. Slides don't win. Working hardware wins. First team to solve it take the prizes. This is a race, not a showcase.  What to ExpectA live race-to-win challenge dropped at kickoff An STM32 dev kit + peripherals for every team, free 5 hours of focused build time Team formation on-site, or come with your crew Breakfast & lunch provided Exciting prizes for the winning A room full of NYC's hardware people - embedded engineers, drone builders, robotics founders, spatial-data folks  Schedule10:00 - 11:00 AM - Doors open. Breakfast, networking mixer, team formation. 11:00 - 11:30 AM - Partner intros, Root Access demo, challenge drop, rules & judging criteria. 11:30 AM - 4:30 PM - Build sprint. Lunch provided. Clock does not stop. 4:30 - 5:15 PM - Live hardware demos to the judges. 5:15 - 6:00 PM - Photos & Mixer.  PrizesA mix of cash, credits, & perks for the winning team. Sponsors are getting locked in - full breakdown announced before doors.  Who Should AttendEmbedded & firmware engineers Robotics, drone, & hardware builders EE / CE students & anyone who's ever blown up a dev board Founders building physical products Software engineers who want to get their hands on real silicon Anyone curious, ambitious, & hands-on  Sponsors[Sponsor TBD - reach out to somyag00@gmail.com to sponsor]  Hosts & PartnersSomya Gupta - The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Pulse NYC AI - A community, incubator, & venture fund built for founders, researchers, & technologists shaping the future of AI in New York City. ConnNext - A next-gen mobile app & community built for career growth.

Machines that sense the world & act on it, on-device.  The Challenge ThemeThe sealed spec will live somewhere in here: Sense  decide  act, running on-device IoT, sensors, & connected devices Physical/digital interaction - things that move, respond, or react Anything that runs on hardware, not just in a browser Constraints you can count on: You'll be working on an STM32 development board & peripherals - get familiar before you show up It has to run live. Slides don't win. Working hardware wins. First team to solve it take the prizes. This is a race, not a showcase.  What to ExpectA live race-to-win challenge dropped at kickoff An STM32 dev kit + peripherals for every team, free 5 hours of focused build time Team formation on-site, or come with your crew Breakfast & lunch provided Exciting prizes for the winning A room full of NYC's hardware people - embedded engineers, drone builders, robotics founders, spatial-data folks  Schedule10:00 - 11:00 AM - Doors open. Breakfast, networking mixer, team formation. 11:00 - 11:30 AM - Partner intros, Root Access demo, challenge drop, rules & judging criteria. 11:30 AM - 4:30 PM - Build sprint. Lunch provided. Clock does not stop. 4:30 - 5:15 PM - Live hardware demos to the judges. 5:15 - 6:00 PM - Photos & Mixer.  PrizesA mix of cash, credits, & perks for the winning team. Sponsors are getting locked in - full breakdown announced before doors.  Who Should AttendEmbedded & firmware engineers Robotics, drone, & hardware builders EE / CE students & anyone who's ever blown up a dev board Founders building physical products Software engineers who want to get their hands on real silicon Anyone curious, ambitious, & hands-on  Sponsors[Sponsor TBD - reach out to somyag00@gmail.com to sponsor]  Hosts & PartnersSomya Gupta - The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Pulse NYC AI - A community, incubator, & venture fund built for founders, researchers, & technologists shaping the future of AI in New York City. ConnNext - A next-gen mobile app & community built for career growth.

events.name: Responsible Tech Summit - Embedding Accountability AI Era
events.description: At a time when artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping society, the conversation is shifting from broad principles to real-world accountability. The 2026 summit will explore the theme of Principles to Power: Embedding Accountability in the AI Era. For years, the Responsible Tech field has been guided by ethical frameworks, voluntary commitments, & emerging standards. Today, the challenge is clear: how do we translate those ideas into systems of governance, oversight, & design that ensure innovation does not come at the expense of safety, rights, or trust? The Responsible Tech Summit is designed as a curated convening for 375 leaders that helps align & shape the direction of the movement. Participants will include global governance leaders, AI researchers, industry practitioners, policy experts, civil society advocates, & philanthropic leaders who are building the infrastructure of accountability for the digital age. Through keynotes, panels, & conversations, attendees will explore topics such as accountability by design, platform oversight, youth online safety, the Responsible Tech economy, & the evolving global regulatory landscape. All ticket proceeds fund free resources & services for the Responsible Tech community that our organization provides. Can't make it in person? The event will be livestreamed for free on All Tech Is Human's YouTube page, where recordings will also be available afterward. - Are you a journalist looking to potentially cover the Responsible Tech Summit? Reach out to Hello@AllTechIsHuman.org. Speakers for the Responsible Tech Summit 2026 Camille Francois - President, ROOST Eli Pariser - Co-Director, New_ Public Cathy O'Neil, Founder, Author, Mathematician & Data Scientist, O'Neil Risk Consulting & Algorithmic Auditing Rumman Chowdhury, CEO, Humane Intelligence PBC Alex Bores, Assembly Member, New York City's 73rd District Beth Goldberg, Founding Executive Director of Humanity AI Sinead Bovell, Founder, WAYE Alexis Wales, Chief Information Security Officer, GitHub Alison Lee, Chief R&D Officer, The Rithm Project Amanda Craig, General Manager of Responsible AI Public Policy, Microsoft Anya Schiffrin, Director, Media Program, Columbia University (SIPA) Carrie Varoquiers, Chief Impact Officer, Workday Joshua Elder, Senior Vice President & Head of Grantmaking, Siegel Family Endowment Julie Cordua, CEO, Thorn Fernanda Del Castillo, Director of AI Governance, Mastercard Kathy Pham, Faculty & Senior Fellow, Product & Responsible AI, Harvard University Kristin Hansen, Executive Director, Civic Health Project J. Trevor Hughes, President & CEO of IAPP Shreya Singh Hernndez, Senior Manager, Aspen Digital, The Aspen Institute Melanie Plaza, Chief Technology Officer, AE Studio Courtney Radsch, Director of the Center for Media & Digital Governance, Open Markets Institute; Fellow, Brookings Institution Andrew Rasiej, Founder, Civic Hall Clement Wolf, Director, Responsible AI Strategy, Google Hale Sirin, Program Scientist, Schmidt Sciences AI & Advanced Computing Institute Jeff Collins, Director of Trust & Safety, Amazon Web Services Alisar Mustafa, Head of AI Safety, Duco Experts   Agenda10:00 - 11:00 am ET | Check-in & Networking 11:00 - 11:10 am | Welcome remarks 11:15 - 11:45 am | Panel: Beyond Benchmarks: Turning Evaluations into Enforceable Standards 11:50 - 12:00 pm | Lightning talk 12:05 - 12:35 pm | Panel: Safety by Design: Accountability at the Intersection of AI, Industry, & Advocacy 12:40 - 1:40 pm | Lunch 1:45 - 2:05 pm | Fireside Chat: Open-Source, Open Questions: Transparency in the Age of AI 2:10 - 2:40 pm | Panel: Shared Risk, Shared Responsibility: Rethinking Responsible AI Governance 2:45 - 3:05 pm | Fireside Chat: Alignment in Practice: Building AI That Wants to be Good 3:05 - 3:30 pm | Networking break 3:30 - 4:00 pm | Panel: Trust as Strategy & the Fight Against AI-Enabled Fraud 4:05 - 4:15 pm | Keynote 4:15 - 4:25 pm | Lightning Talk 4:30 - 5:00 pm | Panel: Rebuilding the Commons: Community & Pluralism in the AI Era 5:05 - 5:25 pm | Fireside Chat: Looking Back to Look Ahead: Co-Designing AI After a Decade of Tech Lessons 5:25 - 5:30 pm | Closing remarks *See the full agenda & bios of our speakers here.   Sponsors for the Responsible Tech Summit 2026Special thanks to our strategic partners, Columbia World Projects, Forum One, & Highspring, for helping bring this critical conversation to life. WorkdayWorkday operates at the heart of the enterprise - HR, finance, & IT - where the margin for error is effectively zero. By tightly coupling AI with the context, guardrails, & trusted processes that run the business, Workday goes beyond AI that assists work to agents that do the work & drive measurable outcomes. More than 11,500 organizations worldwide, including more than 65% of the Fortune 500, trust Workday to deliver. MastercardMastercard is a global technology company in the payments industry, connecting consumers, financial institutions, merchants, & governments in more than 200 countries & territories. The company is committed to building a sustainable, inclusive digital economy that benefits everyone, everywhere. PinterestPinterest is a visual search & discovery platform where people find inspiration, curate ideas & shop products - all in a positive place online. Headquartered in San Francisco, Pinterest has over 600 million monthly active users worldwide. MicrosoftMicrosoft is a global technology leader empowering every person & organization on the planet to achieve more through its platforms & productivity tools. The company is committed to advancing responsible AI & ensuring emerging technologies are developed & deployed safely & ethically. Siegel Family EndowmentSiegel Family Endowment takes an inquiry-driven approach to grantmaking, informed by the scientific method. As technology reshapes society, we fund organizations asking critical questions about its impact on learning, work, & infrastructure. Founded in 2011 by David Siegel, co-founder & co-chairman of Two Sigma, we advance technology in the public interest, supporting research & initiatives that imagine a more inclusive, resilient technology-driven society. AE StudioAE Studio is an applied AI & AI alignment company that builds software products for clients while advancing research on making advanced AI systems safe & beneficial. Its recent work with Anthropic, GRAM, trains dangerous knowledge into removable modules so it can be stripped from a model before release. AE Studio reinvests its commercial success into neglected approaches to AI alignment research. Learn more at ae.studio. GoogleGoogle's mission is to organize the world's information & make it universally accessible & useful. As a leader in AI & computing, the company is focused on developing technology responsibly to benefit people & society. Kapor FoundationThe Kapor Foundation works at the intersection of racial equity & technology to expand access to K-12 computer science & postsecondary tech pathways, improve tech accountability & worker protections, & increase investments in infrastructure & innovation. We advocate for policy changes, build the capacity of partners, conduct research, support partners through grantmaking, & invest in entrepreneurship & VC. We believe that when technology includes diverse perspectives & is harnessed to address societal challenges, we can transform the tech ecosystem for Black, Latine, & Native communities, & society as a whole. Kapor Foundation works collectively with the Kapor Center family of organizations, Kapor Capital, & SMASH to reimagine & reconstruct a more inclusive & equitable technology sector. Check out Kapor Foundation's Responsible AI Principles for Advancing a More Equitable Innovation Future. IAPPThe IAPP is a policy-neutral, not-for-profit association founded in 2000 with a mission to define, promote & improve the professions of privacy, AI governance & digital responsibility globally. Civic Health ProjectCivic Health Project is a nonpartisan nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing scalable solutions to the dangerous divisions that threaten American democracy. Since our founding in 2019, we have supported more than 75 academic researchers, grassroots practitioners, creatives, & technologists who are helping reduce polarization, strengthen civic norms, & foster social cohesion. Today, Civic Health Project focuses primarily on exploring the vast potential of promising new technologies to help resolve conflict, improve civil discourse & deliberation, foster social cohesion, & uphold societal norms. Normsy.ai, our flagship in-house project, brings this mission to life. It identifies toxic content in real time & equips users to respond with respectful, trust-building messages grounded in social science & supported by artificial intelligence. We are also part of the initiative The Forum, a new model for civic leadership at a time when trust is low, division is high, & the need for credible, citizen-led solutions has never been greater. GitHubGitHub is the world's leading platform for agentic software development - powered by Copilot to build, scale, & deliver secure software. Over 225 million developers, including more than 90% of the Fortune 100 companies, use GitHub to collaborate, & more than 140,000 organizations have adopted GitHub Copilot. CinderCinder is the industry's first Trust & Safety operations platform to help organizations combat Internetabuse at scale. We provide Trust & Safety teams with a single system to manage complex integrityoperations & investigations to create a safe environment for their users. Interested in sponsoring our summit or forming a strategic partnership? Email us at hello@alltechishuman.org.   About All Tech Is HumanAll Tech Is Human is the coordination layer & connective tissue for the Responsible Tech ecosystem. By uniting key individuals across civil society, government, industry, academia, & philanthropy, we provide a sandbox for solution-building & socialization to influence key levers of change. We specialize in taking a whole-of-ecosystem approach to tackling thorny tech & society issues, shaping the Responsible Tech movement, & ensuring that our tech future is aligned with the public interest. We are the premier gathering for the Responsible Tech community, convening thousands of people globally. We curate the defining resource for the movement, the Responsible Tech Guide, used by academia, industry, civil society, & policy professionals. We have the largest online community for the Responsible Tech movement hosted on Slack with over 15,000 members across 117 countries. We have the go-to job board for the community, our curated Responsible Tech Job Board & related talent pool. Refund Policy & Billing DetailsRefund requests made before October 1 at 5:00 pm ET are subject to a $50 administrative fee. Refund requests made between October 2 & the final refund deadline of October 16 at 5:00 pm ET face a late cancellation fee of $100. No refunds or ticket transfers are permitted after October 16. Please note: credit card statements for this purchase will show a charge from "Social Science Research Council (SSRC)," All Tech Is Human's fiscal sponsor.

events.name: The AI Briefing By Startup Grind: Who Owns The Data Layer Behind Enterprise AI
events.description: The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise.  This month's source: The Formula for Agentic AI Value: Applied AI Index 2026 (Boston Consulting Group - Sep 2026) Secondary sources: 5 Emerging Trends in Enterprise Data & AI (The Modern Data Company - Aug 2026) Agentic context layers (VentureBeat Intelligence - Oct 2026) Most of the money behind enterprise AI no longer runs through IT. BCG surveyed 1,330 CxOs & senior executives. AI spending has more than tripled, to 3.3% of revenue, & 2.8 points of it sit outside the enterprise IT budget. Business units generate about two-thirds of the value AI creates. So who owns the data their agents run on? BCG says the gap between leaders & everyone else has moved up the stack, to whether a company's data is current, consistently defined, trustworthy, & managed with clear ownership. It tells companies to keep their definitions, business rules & decision logic in a layer they control & could move to another vendor. VentureBeat's August survey points the other way. 98% of companies running retrieval in production use at least one system someone else built, & 2% name building & owning their context layer as their likely direction. 64% have already caught an AI agent giving a confidently wrong answer because of their own company's data.  The Mission: Deciding who owns the definitions, rules & context your AI runs on This series has spent the year on readiness: how fast enterprises adopted, where leadership's confidence outran results, how governance fell behind agents, & whether the workforce was ready. October's discussion turned to a question none of those sessions answered: who owns the data layer? We'll test BCG's advice against what data teams report from the inside. 61% call a reliable context layer critical for AI agents, & 16% engineer one on purpose.  The Format: The numbers: BCG's spending & ownership data, & where a self-reported executive survey stops being evidence. Cross-pollinated debate: Who owns it in your org? IT, the data team, the business unit paying for the agent, or the model vendor whose stack holds the context. The semantic layer problem: In VentureBeat's survey, companies running or building a semantic layer were about twice as likely to report a confidently wrong agent answer (78% vs. 37%). We'll work through why, & what it means for anyone about to fund one.  Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: See where AI budgets & accountability sit at the 7.5% of companies BCG calls future-built (all of them have clear ownership of the AI agenda), & decide whose name goes on the data layer before a vendor's does. Founders & Builders: Hear what buyers mean when they ask about lock-in. 37% of VentureBeat's respondents plan to keep standalone tools alongside the model, & 22% expect to consolidate onto one model provider's stack. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Compare notes on the work underneath. 46% of respondents say their teams spend more than a quarter of their time maintaining & integrating tools, & 8.4% say the data feeding their AI is trustworthy enough for production.  The Prep: This is a working session, not a lecture. Read the report here. Bring one wrong answer your AI gave & where the bad data came from.

events.name: PMAI - Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Learn How to SellSales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. - Bring a computer. You're writing three things tonight.- Most founders can get meetings. The deals die after meeting one.- You'll leave with your buyer in one sentence, a cold email written to a real person, & five questions for your next call. About Farzad, the speaker Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding & generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: Trajectories - Facts, Fictions & Futures Of Spacefaring Societies
events.description: Science fiction has long imagined humanity's path beyond Earth, from post-scarcity utopias to contested frontiers to desperate exoduses. Which way are we headed? This week's interactive community conversation tests those visions against the technological, economic, societal, & cultural forces shaping our spacefaring future right now. Because the future isn't something we predict but something we choose, the question isn't just where we're headed, but where we dare to go. OUR FACILITATORVince Lucich, an engineer & startup founder whose work involves building spacecraft for the emerging orbital economy, will lead us on this idea exploration of the future. WHO'S IT FOR?Idea people. Founders. Builders. Creatives. Researchers. The Curious. And their Supporters --------------FORMATOur format explores ideas together through our diverse backgrounds, while building relationships & community through the process. We want you to talk to each other, instead of just being talked at. 6:00PM - Settle in, grab a drink & some food at the bar, & meet some new people before we start our event. 6:30PM - Our conversation begins with our facilitator presenting the knowledge & context for the conversation along the way. The conversation between attendees will explore from surface level understandings, to deep implications & future iterations. 7:45PM - Meet & connect with new people, catch up with people you haven't seen in a while, discover all the different ways you overlap. And then just hang out, grab a drink, play some pool or ping pong! Or stay for the band afterwards! Our desire is to be the antithesis of NYC's corporate panel & transactional networking culture. We aim to create a vibrant idea & build space in NYC that focuses on the passion & values beyond the money & the hustle.

events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Build Your Creative Operating System
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back - In Person at Salesforce We're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City & sponsored by Boldforce. This Month We Present...Build Your Creative Operating SystemBuild a personalized AI workflow that supports your entire creative process-from capturing ideas to publishing finished work-so you're never starting from scratch. Most of us don't have an idea problem. We have a system problem. Ideas live in our Notes app. Research is scattered across browser tabs. Drafts are hiding in Google Docs. Inspiration gets screenshotted & forgotten. And every new project somehow feels like we're starting all over again. What if your creative process actually remembered how you work? At this month's AI & The Culture meetup, we're exploring how to build your own Creative Operating System-a personalized workflow that uses AI to help you capture ideas, organize knowledge, research, create, refine, & publish your work. Instead of collecting more AI tools, we'll focus on connecting the ones that actually support your process. Together we'll explore:  How to map your creative process from idea to finished work  Ways to capture & organize ideas so they don't disappear into the digital abyss  How AI can help you research, brainstorm, draft, edit, & refine your work  Building a personal knowledge base that makes past ideas & research useful again  How to connect AI tools into repeatable workflows instead of using them one at a time  Where automation can save time-and where your human judgment should stay firmly in the driver's seat  How to create a system that gets smarter & more useful the more you use it The goal isn't to automate your creativity. It's to build the infrastructure around your creativity so you have more time & energy for the work only you can do. Expect a welcoming room filled with creators, technologists, educators, founders, artists, & curious minds ready to rethink how we organize & support our creative lives. Who Should Attend?  Creators & content makers  Filmmakers, writers, artists, & storytellers  Educators & community builders  Entrepreneurs, founders, & solopreneurs  Marketers, strategists, & creative professionals  Technologists & AI enthusiasts  Anyone with too many ideas, too many tabs, & not enough systems  Whether your creative process is already organized or currently held together by screenshots, open tabs, & vibes, you're welcome here. Come Ready to Build This won't be a sit-back-and-scroll kind of evening. Bring your laptop, something to write with, & a mindset ready to learn, experiment, & share. We'll be exploring ideas, tools, & workflows you can begin applying to your own creative process.  Bring your laptop  Bring a notebook or something to take notes with  Bring your curiosity & questions Come ready to learn. Come ready to contribute. Come ready to build. About AI & The Culture AI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, & culture. Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams & King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, & culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, & community. We're building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI. This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture - grounded in community, focused on real-world use, & centered on learning together in the room. Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Let's build - together.  About Your Hosts Shirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, & co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, & creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, & real-world execution. About King Willonius King Willonius is a creative technologist & cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, & creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, & community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable & useful - especially for creatives & innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm.  Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio) #AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: Spatial Analytics w/ Python
events.description: Join PyData NYC on October 27th at 6:30 PM for an evening exploring geospatial data science with Python, featuring Brendan Collins, Founder & CTO at Makepath & creator of Xarray-Spatial! Discover how Python can transform spatial data into powerful insights, from terrain analysis & hydrology to scalable CPU- & GPU-accelerated computing. Please bring your  to follow along & sign up using your official government-issued name.  Pizza & drinks will be provided - Thank you, Makepath! Agenda xarray-spatial: In & Out of the Raster-verseSpeaker: Brendan Collins (Founder & CTO at Makepath)Spatial data comes in many shapes & sizes, but some of the most powerful spatial analysis techniques begin by viewing the world as a grid.Led by the library's creator & maintainer, this talk introduces Xarray-Spatial, an open-source Python library for scalable raster analysis with CPU & GPU acceleration.We'll learn how to enter the Raster-verse by bringing spatial data into Xarray, explore the Raster-verse using algorithms for terrain analysis, hydrology, proximity, & more, & escape the Raster-verse through techniques like zonal statistics & polygonization.Finally, we'll discuss contributing to the Raster-verse, sharing lessons from maintaining Xarray-Spatial & how AI-augmented development is transforming open-source contributions, code quality, & scientific software engineering.Whether you're a GIS practitioner, data scientist, or Python developer, you'll leave with practical ideas for working with spatial data & contributing to open source.  About the SpeakerBrendan Collins is the Founder & CTO of Makepath, where he helps early-stage startups & Fortune 500 engineering teams realize their product ambitions.A former employee of Anaconda, Brendan has spent the past decade applying PyData technologies, including NumPy, Xarray, & Numba, to engineering challenges across the public, private, & nonprofit sectors.When not writing in the third person, Brendan enjoys swimming, playing the banjo, & gardening.  NetworkingConnect with fellow data enthusiasts, Python developers, researchers, & community leaders. Build meaningful connections, exchange ideas, & explore opportunities for collaboration.

SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. events.description: New York Startup Networking Event. Meet Founders, Investors, & Talent - Build or Scale Your Startup  Bring a business question to the room Meet founders, entrepreneurs, builders, operators & investors at Ascent Valley's NYC mixer. Talk through business decisions & meet people you could work with. Locals & visitors are equally welcome. Bring a question about finding customers, building your team or growing your business. Share what you're working on & hear how others approach similar challenges. Join small-group discussions before the pitches, then hear company representatives present their businesses. There's time for open networking to get to know each other & explore where you could help one another. Who you'll meet Founders & entrepreneurs starting or growing a business, working through decisions you may be facing too.Builders turning ideas into products & services, including developers & designers.Operators with experience in product, growth, marketing, sales & running teams.Investors interested in understanding a business by meeting the people behind it.  Why This Event Is Different Compare customer acquisition approaches with another entrepreneur, discuss a product decision with a builder or hear how an investor looks at a business. Smaller discussions give you time to ask follow-up questions & understand each other's work. When you find a reason to stay in touch, you can continue the conversation through Ascent Valley after the evening. What to Expect Product & growth: discuss finding customers, product decisions & growing a business. Talent & hiring: meet builders & operators, talk about team needs & explore working together. Fundraising: share what you've learned about preparing a pitch & raising capital. Company pitches: discover what other companies are building & ask their representatives questions. Want to Pitch? Present your company to the room & walk guests through your pitch deck, followed by a short Q&A. events.name: Startup Pitch & Networking
events.description: Join our event in New York! We design Pitch & Networking nights to help founders sharpen their thinking through direct, candid feedback & to give strong investors access to serious teams. Our pitch night is complemented by a structured networking session before & after the pitch session. What to expect: Startups pitch live & receive focused feedback from angels & VC partners Structured networking session before & after the pitches Entrepreneurs, startup founders, & operators are joining to network, exchange ideas, & build strong connections Active investors & venture scouts joining to discover the best startups early  Who you will meet at the event: Founders Investors, VC partners, Venture Scouts Marketers, Salespeople, Business Advisors Industry Disruptors AI Experts Entrepreneurs from Europe, Asia, & the United Kingdom  We Welcome New Investors: We invite investors to our event to expand their network, get acquainted with new startups, evaluate them, share feedback, & participate in discussions with early-stage & serial founders. We offer complimentary tickets to institutional investors, angels, & venture scouts with a proven track record. If you'd like to access our database of promising startups or provide mentorship support to our best startups, please fill out this short Investor Application Form, & our team will contact you.  Want to Pitch? A limited number of founders will have the opportunity to pitch their startup or business to a panel of investors & experts. 4-6 selected founders will pitch their startup, followed by a short Q&A where participants can ask questions & share feedback. Apply by filling out the Pitch Application Form & sending us your pitch deck. Spots are limited, & we select founders in advance. To maintain high-quality pitches, you are required to present with a pitch deck. We will share our pitching guide and, if you'd like, coach you so you're fully prepared for pitch night.  The best startups will be featured across our social media & included in our investor newsletter. Requirements for attendees: Dress code: smart casual. Bring good energy.  Join our event & secure your ticket today! About us: Startup Valley is a global event organizer hosting pitch nights in 25 cities since 2023. Since then, we have hosted 850 events for 40,000 attendees. Over these years, we connected countless outstanding early-stage startups to serious investors, & we are not planning to stop. We maintain strategic partnerships with VC funds in the US, Europe, & Asia to support our community. Do you have a question, a partnership proposal, or want to clarify something? Reach us at hello@startupvalley.club Agenda 18:00-18:30 - Registration: Guests register, receive badges, & event programs. This is an opportunity for casual networking, making first connections, & preparing for the event. 18:30-19:00 - Event Kickoff & Interactive Networking: Official welcome from the organizers with a brief overview of the event goals & schedule. Interactive networking session to connect with key contacts. 19:00-19:50 - Startup Pitch Session: Startups present their projects to investors & experts. Each team has 5 minutes to pitch, covering the project's core idea, business model, & target market. 19:50-21:00 - Chill & Networking: Participants enjoy casual conversations with investors, discuss collaboration opportunities, & exchange ideas over refreshments. FAQ Can I pitch? Yes! To pitch, please purchase a Pitch Ticket & fill out the Pitch Application Form. We will contact you to discuss & approve your pitch. The pitch duration is 5 minutes. You will also have some time to answer questions from the audience. How does the pitch go? Selected founders present on stage to the audience & the investors in the room. You get 5 minutes to pitch your idea, business model, target market, & investment ask, followed by a short Q&A. The best startups are featured across our social media channels & in the investor newsletter. Who will I meet? Founders, angel investors, VC partners, venture scouts, AI experts, engineers, operators, marketing & sales experts, & international entrepreneurs from across Europe, Asia, & the US. Do investors get free tickets? Yes! Please apply above or email hello@startupvalley.club, & we will issue a complimentary ticket for you & your team. Can I request a refund? Yes. Refunds are available if requested at least 1 day before the event start time. Please submit the refund request on the platform where you purchased your ticket, or email us at hello@startupvalley.club

events.name: PMAI: Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Sales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. - Bring a computer. You're writing three things tonight.- Most founders can get meetings. The deals die after meeting one.- You'll leave with your buyer in one sentence, a cold email written to a real person, & five questions for your next call. About Farzad, the speaker Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding & generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: Prototyping In Public - Where Art & Science Get Tested On The Gallery Floor
events.description: What if a museum ran like a lab, with the experiment still in progress? Ann Neumann is Director of Galleries & Exhibitions at the MIT Museum. Her question for the evening: can a museum serve as infrastructure for public experimentation, a place where visitors take part in the work rather than just walk through it? If you build products, run pilots, or spend your days deciding what's ready to put in front of real people, this is a look at how one of the best-known science museums handles prototyping in public. In collaboration with the National Arts Club & its Art & Technology Committee, Ann will walk through the interactive projects she's shepherded at the MIT Museum. Each one works as a prototype for engaging the public with technologies like CRISPR, machine learning, & sensory neuroscience. Reserve your spot & arrive early. Space is limited. Founded in 1898, the National Arts Club is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit with a mission to stimulate, foster, & promote public interest in the arts & to educate the American people in the fine arts. Annually, the Club offers more than 150 free programs-both in-person & virtually-to the public, including exhibitions, theatrical & musical performances, lectures, & readings, attracting an audience of over 30,000 in-person visitors & thousands more online.
