events.name: The AI Era & What It Means To Be Human
events.description: The AI Era & What It Means to Be HumanAI is changing how we work, learn, create, & make decisions. But underneath the conversation about models, agents, & automation is a more fundamental question: what does it mean to be human in an age of increasingly capable machines? On October 23rd, The AI Collective is bringing together 100 people in NYC for an evening exploring the human side of the AI era. We'll move beyond the usual conversation about what AI can do & look instead at what its rise asks of us: how we learn, how we maintain agency, how we relate to one another, & which distinctly human capacities become more important as technology advances. The evening will combine conversation, small-group discussion, & experiential mindfulness/wellness exercises. This is not a technical AI event. We're creating a conversation about the human layer: the trust, awareness, connection, & shared understanding we'll need to build alongside the technology. Come curious. Expect to participate. Agenda6:00 PM: Arrival & Welcome6:30 PM: Opening Remarks + Experiential Mindfulness Exercise6:45 PM: Fireside Chat: AI & the Human Condition with Mohan Nair, author of "Unreachable: How to Not Lose Your Mind in an AI-Obsessed Era."7:15 PM: Conversation with Catherine & Manas followed by Breath-work & Meditation.7:45 PM: Small-Group Roundtables8:15 PM: Dessert & Networking Food & beverages provided. Space is limited to 75 participants. Co-hosted by The AI Collective & Manas Ram with support from JQ Consulting, whose work focuses on the science of human wellbeing, resilience, happiness, mindfulness, & the human condition. Please be advised: Unfortunately, space is very limited at these community events & we can not always accept everyone we would like to. If you are not accepted to this event, please keep applying! We appreciate your application tremendously & we are looking forward to seeing you at a future event very soon! The AI Collective is a global non-profit building the human layer for the AI era. We unite 200,000+ leaders, builders, & stakeholders across 100+ forums worldwide to democratize the frontier, build trust, & coordinate how society navigates the rapid acceleration of technological progress. All attendees & organizers at events affiliated with The AI Collective agree to our privacy policy & are subject to our code of conduct.

events.description: Join CUNY at the Climate Imaginarium!Open to the public! Members of the CUNY community will be joining us for a gallery tour, followed by a meditation & climate cafe. Climate cafes are listening circles for your climate-linked emotions. Get help facing your climate anxiety & connect with impactful local organizers. Vegan snacks provided!  About the Climate ImaginariumThe Climate Imaginarium is a center for climate, community, & culture in New York City. Located on Governors Island, the Climate Imaginarium is activating a cultural destination at the heart of New York City's burgeoning green economy, where artists, scientists, advocates, & storytellers come together to reimagine & build toward a more resilient future.  Getting to the Climate ImaginariumFor the weekend ferry schedule to Governors Island, please check here. Ferries run every 15 minutes. Take the ferry that's most convenient for you from either Lower Manhattan (10 South Street), Brooklyn Bridge Park (Pier 6), or Red Hook/Atlantic Basin. Please arrive 15 minutes prior to your ferry departure time with your ticket ready to display. Ferry tickets must be purchased at the ferry terminal or online. Fares are $5 for a round trip ticket & free for adults over 65, children 12 & under, Climate Imaginarium summer volunteers, & others. All passengers ride free before 11am on weekends. Cars are not permitted. Governors Island is also accessible from any route via NYC Ferry by transferring at Wall Street/Pier 11. You can find the NYC Ferry schedule here. Tickets on NYC Ferry are $4.50 each way. Once you get to Governors Island, you will either get out at Soissons Landing (from Manhattan) or Yankee Pier (from Brooklyn). You can use this map of Governors Island to locate Colonels Row. The Climate Imaginarium is in Building 406A, in the middle of Colonels Row, & will have a visible sign outside the doorway. Our address is 406A Comfort Road.

events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Plan Your Best Year With AI
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back  In Person at SalesforceWe're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City and sponsored by Boldforce.This Month We Present...Plan Your Best Year With AIJoin the community for an interactive planning session to reflect on the past year, identify your biggest opportunities, and build an AI-powered roadmap for the year ahead.Before we rush into a new year with another list of goals, lets get clear about what were actually building.What worked this year? What didnt? What deserves more of your energy? And where could AI help you turn those intentions into action?For our final AI & The Culture meetup of the year, were bringing the community together for an interactive planning and reflection session designed to help you look back, think forward, and build a roadmap for what comes next.This isnt about asking AI to magically plan your life. Its about using these tools as thought partnersto help you reflect, uncover patterns, explore possibilities, make decisions, and turn big ambitions into actionable next steps.Together well explore: How to use AI to reflect on your wins, lessons, challenges, and unfinished business from the past year Prompts that help you identify opportunities you might be overlooking How to turn big goals into realistic projects, milestones, and next steps Ways to use AI as a strategic thought partner for your creative work, career, business, or personal projects How to identify where AI and automation can give you back time in the year ahead Building a personalized AI-powered roadmap you can actually use after you leave the roomAnd because this is AI & The Culture, were making space for something AI cant replace: community.Youll have an opportunity to reflect alongside other creatives, founders, educators, artists, technologists, and curious mindsto exchange ideas, share what youre building, and potentially meet the people who can help you move it forward.The goal isnt to leave with 47 resolutions.Its to leave with clarity, priorities, and a plan.Who Should Attend? Creators and content makers Filmmakers, writers, artists, and storytellers Educators and community builders Entrepreneurs, founders, and solopreneurs Marketers, strategists, and creative professionals Technologists and AI enthusiasts Anyone ready to be more intentional about what theyre building nextWhether you already have your next year mapped out or youre still staring at a blank page wondering where to begin, youre welcome here.Come Ready to BuildThis one is especially hands-on, so come prepared to participate. Bring your laptop Bring a notebook or something to write with Bring a few goals, ideas, or questions youve been thinking about for the year ahead Bring your curiosity and a willingness to shareWell be working through reflection exercises, AI prompts, and planning activities togetherso you can leave with the beginnings of a roadmap, not just another page of notes.Come ready to reflect. Come ready to plan. Come ready to build.About AI & The CultureAI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, and culture.Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams and King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, and culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, and community.Were building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI.This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture  grounded in community, focused on real-world use, and centered on learning together in the room.Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Lets build  together. About Your HostsShirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, and co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, and creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, and real-world execution.About King WilloniusKing Willonius is a creative technologist and cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, and creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, and community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable and useful  especially for creatives and innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm. Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio)#AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: Wind-Win Startup Showdown
events.description: Step into the Future of Ocean Renewables:  An Electrifying Evening with the 2026 Offshore Wind Innovation Hub Innovator Cohort!The 4th annual Wind-Win Startup Showdown offers a pitch experience like no other, spotlighting cutting-edge technology breakthroughs to transform the future of ocean renewables. This is a special year for us: the program set a record high: 118 applications & the strongest competition reviewers have seen to date. In 2026, we also drew in a more diverse cohort than ever before by broadening this year's technology scope  a 123% increase in application numbers compared to last year's, reflecting the parallel growth in industry demand for novel solutions needed in the market.Presented by the Offshore Wind Innovation Hub, this networking & pitch event brings together stakeholders across the climate landscapeinvestors, founders, academia, industry, & thought leadersfor an evening of connection, collaboration, & celebration.Come see it for yourself! Join us to engage with leading innovators tackling climates most complex challenges with bold, next-generation solutions.Refreshments & light hors d'oeuvres will be provided.AgendaDoors OpenKeynote + Welcome RemarksAlso on stage:  Tone Sndergaard, Director, Offshore Wind Innovation Hub at NYU Tandon Urban Future LabInnovator Lightning Pitches by the 2026 CohortEach of our Offshore Wind Innovation Hub partners has sent their most experienced innovation experts to provide feedback for each of the selected cohort companies.Sam Jung, SVP, Green Economy, New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYC EDC)Lyndie Hice-Dunton, Executive Director, National Offshore Wind Research & Development Consortium (NOWRDC)Robert Fenton, Head of Americas Generation Procurement, rstedStephan Kremers, Senior Technical Project Manager, VestasFireside Chat on Dual-Use Technology AdaptationNetworking & RefreshmentsMeet our 2026 FinalistsBlue Ocean Transfers Group (BOT) (New York, US) - Multipurpose, hybrid electric support vessel enabling maritime decarbonization.Bubble Robotics (California, US) - Resident fleet of autonomous underwater robots monitoring offshore infrastructure.Clema (New York, US) - Thermoelectric cooling vest for workers in extreme heat.Fleet Robotics (Massachusetts, US) - Data insights powered by submersible, autonomous cleaning & inspection robots.Hefring Marine (Iceland) - Intelligence platform combining onboard hardware with software to optimize marine operations.HiFIT USA (New York, US) - Impact treatment welding to enable life extension & lighter structures.NeuralX (California, US) - Underwater video & computer vision for fisheries monitoring & ecological data.Sail GTX (New York, US) - Platform for smarter customs workflows for offshore wind components.TMA The Hazardous Goods Companion (Germany) - RFID & AIoT inventory visibility & predictive inventory management solution.Tree Composites (The Netherlands) - Composite joints for offshore support structure to realise material & manufacturing optimization.Vital Ocean (Oregon, US) - Intelligence platform combining ocean data, marine environment, & decision interface.Stay tuned in the next few weeks on our website & LinkedIn for updates on our selected cohort!Innovation in FocusOur 2026 cohort takes the stage to pitch ocean & maritimes most promising technologies. This year's lineup features innovations spanning ports, O&M, environmental monitoring & coexistence, workforce development, installation, construction, & commissioning, maritime applications, among others. The scope doesn't just stop there. The majority of this year's solutions are dual-use, carrying relevance across adjacent industries & global markets, a reflection of just how far the blue economy reaches.Marking the official launch of the 2026 Innovator program, this event offers a unique chance to connect directly with the founders behind these ready-to-scale solutions. Explore their real-world impact, uncover new business opportunities, & spark the kind of strategic partnerships that move ideas forward.The Offshore Wind Innovation Hub Innovator ProgramA world-class program open to global offshore wind innovators. Building on three successful cohorts, this eight-month intensive program provides unparalleled support for innovators looking to develop novel technology & advance commercialization in New York & beyond.The Offshore Wind Innovation Hub is an initiative led by Urban Future Lab at NYU Tandon School of Engineering & the National Offshore Wind R&D Consortium (NOWRDC) in collaboration with the New York State Research & Development Authority (NYSERDA) & New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYC EDC).The Innovator program is also supported by industry partners Equinor, rsted, & Vestas.

events.description: Join us at Fabrik NYC in DUMBO, Brooklyn for an in-person, hands-on pitch clinic designed to help founders become more confident on stage & sharpen the way they pitch to investors. Whether you are preparing for a fundraising round, an investor meeting, or your next demo day, you will learn practical tools to communicate your story with greater confidence, clarity, & impact. The clinic features two focused, 30-minute workshops covering how you show up & what you say. Don't Calm Down with Dave Wolovsky In this interactive workshop, Dave will share practical exercises to help you compose yourself when pitching, work with pressure rather than against it, & perform with greater presence in high-stakes moments. Dave is a Cognitive Performance Coach with an MS in Neuroscience & Education from Columbia University. He coaches founders on focus & daily energy management & serves as a StartX accelerator mentor. Learn more at https://effortwise.com/founders. The Art of Pitching to Attract Investors with Anthony Rose Anthony will break down how to communicate your vision & opportunity & present your business in a way that resonates with investors. Anthony is the founder & CEO of SeedLegals, the legaltech platform used by more than 50,000 startups to get investment-ready, run funding rounds, & handle legal needs. Before SeedLegals, his career included leading BBC iPlayer. Wired Magazine's 2009 cover story called him The Man Who Saved the BBC. Come ready to learn, practice, & leave with techniques you can use in your next pitch. The room seats 100. Hosted by SeedLegals, Meera Mawkin, Dave Wolovsky, & Fabrik NYC. Presented with Propel Earth Original event & registration details https://luma.com/dehgirvb The exact address is available after registering on the original Luma page.

events.name: OverdriveAI Summit
events.description: Overdrive AIHosted by TechUnited:NJ, creators of Propelify, heralded by Forbes as the "SXSW of the Northeast," OverdriveAI is back, & this year it's a debate. The hottest topics in AI, argued live, both sides on stage. Jobs, energy, education, & more. Sharp thinkers go head to head, you hear the case for & against, & you decide where you land. Taking place this year at the Newark Museum of Art, where tech & culture share a roof, OverdriveAI brings together founders, operators, investors, & researchers from across the Northeast for a day built around one idea: the biggest questions in AI don't have easy answers, so let's actually argue about them. TICKETS ARE NOW LIVE!EXPLORE THE FULL OVERDRIVEAI EXPERIENCE Community AI TrainingHands-on morning AI training at EqualSpace designed for all experience levels. No prior AI experience required. Reserve Your Spot Executive AI TrainingA focused, practical AI training designed for executives & business leaders ready to better understand & apply AI within their organizations. Reserve Your Spot Pitch Roast LiveStartups pitch. Comedians roast. Everyone wins. Close out OverdriveAI with an evening of bold ideas, founder pitches, comedy, & connection. Reserve Your Spot   What to Expect Community AI Training A hands-on morning (10a-12p ET) AI training at EqualSpace designed for all experience levels. Come ready to learn, explore, & put AI into practice. No prior experience required. Executive AI Training Turn AI into practical business advantage. Start your morning with a focused AI training session designed for executives, business leaders, & decision-makers navigating the rapidly evolving AI landscape. This interactive session will explore practical ways leaders can better understand, evaluate, & apply AI within their organizations helping you move from conversation to action. The AI Debates The main event at the Newark Museum of Art. Will AI take your job or grow the economy? Who pays for AI's energy appetite? Does AI belong in the classroom? Can you still trust what you see? Startup demos will be featured between rounds & the afternoon will roll into TechUnited:NJ Birthday Party! Final topics & speakers are still being locked in, ticket holders hear every name first. Here's what's on the table so far: AI takes jobs vs. AI grows the economy - does automation erase more work than it creates? Is AI raising your energy bill? - the data center buildout is reshaping the grid, & New Jersey's in the middle of it. Does AI belong in the classroom? - a tutor for every student, or the end of learning how to think? Is it time for universal basic income? - if productivity keeps compounding, someone decides where the gains go. Can we handle deepfakes? - synthetic media's getting cheap & convincing, what's the real defense? Got a debate we missed? Suggest it, & if it makes the stage, you'll know it was yours. Live debates. Experts, opposing sides of one question, no hedging.Hot takes. Short, sharp presentations from speakers with a strong point of view.Networking. 300+ founders, researchers, & investors in one room, this year in a new venue built for it. Pitch Roast Live Closing the night at Newark Culture Club Close with startup pitches & a high-energy evening experience. Four founders pitch, three comedians & two investors roast. One walks out a winner! Last Year, at Nokia Bell Labs Speakers joined us from OpenAI, IBM, CoreWeave, Verizon, Perplexity, Nokia Bell Labs, BetterFutureLabs, NJEDA, & the NJ AI Hub. 16 speakers, 300+ attendees, a packed house. This year's lineup is coming together now, & it's bigger. OverdriveAI is one of many events TechUnited:NJ runs for its 13,000+ member community, from AI Demo Night to Propelify. Inquire about membership to hear about what's next. TechUnited:NJ members receive complimentary admission to OverdriveAI as part of their membership. Not a member yet? Join TechUnited:NJ to unlock complimentary access to OverdriveAI, along with year-round member benefits & opportunities to connect with New Jersey's innovation community.

events.name: Spooky Civic AI Hackathon - Build Weekend
events.description: Demos are Sunday at Demo Day. RSVP for that separately: luma.com/3perce-pi2u Spooky Civic AI Hackathon: Build AI Tools for NYC Free. Open to everyone. No approval needed, just RSVP.Fri Oct 23 - Sat Oct 24, in person in NYC or on Zoom.Come solo & we'll help you find a team. Free food for in-person builders. Who can come? Anyone who wants to build something for New York City: engineers, product managers, designers, people who used to code, & people who never have. The best teams pair people who know a problem with people who can build the tech. Builders write the code & ship the tool. Problem-solvers (PMs, designers, policy & community folks) pick the problem, shape how people will use it, & lead the pitch. No team? No problem. Most people come solo. You can meet teammates at our Oct 14 & Oct 15 classes, or at Friday's kickoff. Pick a track The Existential Track: Climate & Sustainability. Heat, waste, food access, cleaner air. Urban Nightmares: Housing, Healthcare, Education & Justice. Tenant rights, benefits, school help, legal info in plain English. Ghost in the Machine: AI infrastructure & scaling. Build the parts under civic AI tools, like search, data, & agents that keep them running. Physical AI for Good: Build AI that moves, with robot arm kits on site. No robotics experience needed. You leave with a working prototype, a demo video, & a real project for your portfolio. Mentors will be on hand all weekend. Where: NYC venue announced soon. The Zoom link goes to everyone who RSVPs. Partners: Robot arm kits & on-site mentors from Viam. Food & builder API credits from Vonage. Costumes encouraged. In-person spots are limited, so RSVP now. Sponsorship inquiries: Partner with 3percentclub About Viam: Viam is a New York-based software platform for building, deploying, & managing robotics & AI in the physical world. Viam is supplying robot arm kits & on-site mentors for this hackathon. About Vonage: Vonage, part of Ericsson, builds communications APIs for voice, video, messaging, & verification that developers put into their apps. Vonage is providing food & builder API credits for this hackathon. About 3percentclub: 3percentclub is an NYC nonprofit that teaches free AI classes for underrepresented builders: engineers, career changers, product managers, designers, & people who have never coded. This event is open to everyone. Want to go deeper with AI? Apply to the free AI Architect Fellowship for weekly classes, mentorship, & a community to build with. The AI Collective is a global non-profit building the human layer for the AI era. We unite 1,000,000+ leaders, builders, & stakeholders across 300+ forums worldwide to democratize the frontier, build trust, & coordinate how society navigates the rapid acceleration of technological progress. All attendees & organizers at events affiliated with The AI Collective agree to our privacy policy & are subject to our code of conduct.

events.name: Built For Success - The Student Journey w/ AI
events.description: The Frontyard at Pace University Co-hosted by Boostability.live About the Event Every student's journey looks different. Built for Success explores how educators, cutting-edge AI, & holistic support frameworks can meet students where they are. Our focus centers on empowering neurodivergent & diverse learners across the entire pipeline from high school into the workforce. Hosted at by the Front yard by Lubin School of Business, this gathering provides a collaborative space for educators, entrepreneurs, & advocates to bridge the gap between emerging EdTech solutions & sustainable student outcomes. Join us for actionable keynotes, candid founder panels, live startup showcases in Demo Alley, & high-impact networking designed to turn support into long-term success. Agenda:10:00-10:30 | Gathering & Continental BreakfastNetworking & refreshments. 10:30-11:00 | Opening Remarks + Keynote: Built for the Whole JourneyWhat students need at every stage, not just the classroom Dr. Lu Shi, Associate Professor, College of Health Professions, Pace University (opening remarks) Dean Ajay, Dean of the Lubin School of Business, Pace University (keynote) 11:00-11:45 | Panel 1: Managing Expectations in an AI ClassroomHow AI is reshaping what teachers expect, & what students can achieve Moderator: Dr. Jennifer Pankowski, Director of Student Accessibility Services, Pace University Jane De Leon Griffin, Associate Provost for Student Success, Bentley University Dr. Sara Asher, Dean of Students, Yeshiva University Julie Zimmerman, Higher Ed & EdTech Advisor, HEAT Advisory 11:45-12:15 | Design Justice in Practice: Bridging Classroom Theory to Real-World Social Impact Dr. James P. Lawler, Professor of Disability Studies & Information Systems, Pace University 12:15-1:00 | LunchCasual meal with startup displays open for browsing & one-on-one conversations. 1:00-1:45 | Fireside Chat: From Code to ClassroomWhy do great EdTech tools sometimes fail in the classroom, & how do we bridge that gap? Moderator: Efrat Segal, Founder & CEO, Boostability Dr. Karen Ferguson, Chief Strategy Officer, Education Affiliates 2:15-2:25 | Closing Keynote: From Support to SuccessWhat it takes to back students across the full journey Dr. Jennifer Pankowski, Director of Student Accessibility Services, Pace University 2:25-3:00 | NetworkingOpen networking with speakers, startup founders, & fellow educators. Registration Notice: Please complete your registration with your full name, email address, & phone number. This information is required in advance to issue your Pace University building visitor pass.

events.name: An UNMUTED Book Club: The 100 Years War On Palestine
events.description: READING NOT REQUIRED - just be curious! Next up: Rashid Khalidi's The Hundred Years' War on Palestine, the 2020 book that argues the Israeli-Palestinian conflict isn't simply a tragic struggle between two peoples claiming the same land, but a century-long colonial campaign against Palestinians, backed first by Britain & later by the United States. Khalidi, a Palestinian-American historian at Columbia, tells the story through six turning points, beginning with the 1917 Balfour Declaration & moving through the creation of Israel, the wars that followed, & the failures of the peace process. Drawing on historical archives & his own family's experiences, he makes a provocative argument: that Palestinians have never been negotiating on equal terms, & that understanding the conflict as a dispute between two competing national movements obscures the enormous imbalance of power between them. It's a forceful challenge to conventional accounts of Israel's founding, Zionism, & America's role in the region, & one that raises uncomfortable questions about nationalism, colonialism, & self-determination. Show up even if you only got through a chunk. We'll talk about where Khalidi's account is most convincing, where it leaves out important context, whether Zionism is best understood as a colonial movement or a national liberation movement, & what his interpretation of the past means for the possibility of peace today. UNMUTED is a discussion forum for the politically curious. Accessible. Engaging. Social. Open-minded is the name of the game. Join your people.

events.name: Agentic Loops Demo Day
events.description: Agents that keep working while you sleep Join AI Tinkerers NYC for a themed demo night on agentic loops: agents that plan, build, verify, & retry without a human in the loop. Not chat wrappers. Systems that run for hours & hand you a result in the morning. Keynote by Conveo engineer Vincent Vankrunkelsven, author of Nightwatch: how to get your agents to keep working while you sleep. Then a full lineup of community demos on the same theme. Space is strictly limited & we will be screening attendance.  Apply now for an evening of live demos, real PRs, real failures, & a room full of people building the same thing. Keynote: Nightwatch, reviewed liveConveo runs a skill called /nightwatch. An engineer plans a feature in the afternoon, a fleet of agents builds it overnight on a remote box, & one reviewed PR is waiting at breakfast. Every layer is a loop: each worker builds, verifies with a script it can run itself, pushes, & drives its PR until the review agents approve. The orchestrator wakes every 15 minutes, checks progress, & replaces anything that died. The whole thing loops again the next day, with the night's logs feeding the next version of the skill. For this event, Conveo will kick off a real Nightwatch run the afternoon of October 21, then do the morning review live on stage. You'll see what the fleet actually built overnight: the master PR, the generated test plan, the screenshots, & whatever broke. A recorded run is on standby in case the demo gods disagree. What you'll take away: The four capabilities you need to run your own overnight loop: a spawner, a durable message bus, validation agents, & a way to wake a running agentHow to write tickets with a closed verification loop so workers converge instead of driftingThe failure modes that each cost Vincent a night, & the fixesHow the agent mesh keeps messages from getting lost when a laptop closesSpeaker: Vincent Vankrunkelsven, Senior Engineer, Conveo. Joined by Dieter (CEO) & Maarten Claes (CTO). What is AI Tinkerers?AI Tinkerers is a meetup exclusively for practitioners with technical, machine learning, & entrepreneurial backgrounds who are actively building & working with foundation models, such as large language models (LLMs) & generative AI. If you're deeply passionate about creating LLM-enabled applications, have hands-on experience in building such systems, & want to connect with like-minded people who share your level of commitment, then this group is the perfect fit for you. With AI Tinkerers meetings happening in many cities, we support a dedicated global community. Who is this for?We are not just AI enthusiasts, we are AI Tinkerers. The core essence of AI Tinkerers is active collaboration around early-stage discovery & innovation, which requires a high degree of experimentation, vulnerability, openness to sharing challenges & learnings, & collaboration among individuals with a shared level of expertise.

Then a full lineup of community demos on the same theme. Space is strictly limited & we will be screening attendance.  Apply now for an evening of live demos, real PRs, real failures, & a room full of people building the same thing. Keynote: Nightwatch, reviewed liveConveo runs a skill called /nightwatch. An engineer plans a feature in the afternoon, a fleet of agents builds it overnight on a remote box, & one reviewed PR is waiting at breakfast. Every layer is a loop: each worker builds, verifies with a script it can run itself, pushes, & drives its PR until the review agents approve. The orchestrator wakes every 15 minutes, checks progress, & replaces anything that died. The whole thing loops again the next day, with the night's logs feeding the next version of the skill. For this event, Conveo will kick off a real Nightwatch run the afternoon of October 21, then do the morning review live on stage. You'll see what the fleet actually built overnight: the master PR, the generated test plan, the screenshots, & whatever broke. A recorded run is on standby in case the demo gods disagree. What you'll take away: The four capabilities you need to run your own overnight loop: a spawner, a durable message bus, validation agents, & a way to wake a running agentHow to write tickets with a closed verification loop so workers converge instead of driftingThe failure modes that each cost Vincent a night, & the fixesHow the agent mesh keeps messages from getting lost when a laptop closesSpeaker: Vincent Vankrunkelsven, Senior Engineer, Conveo. Joined by Dieter (CEO) & Maarten Claes (CTO). What is AI Tinkerers?AI Tinkerers is a meetup exclusively for practitioners with technical, machine learning, & entrepreneurial backgrounds who are actively building & working with foundation models, such as large language models (LLMs) & generative AI. If you're deeply passionate about creating LLM-enabled applications, have hands-on experience in building such systems, & want to connect with like-minded people who share your level of commitment, then this group is the perfect fit for you. With AI Tinkerers meetings happening in many cities, we support a dedicated global community. Who is this for?We are not just AI enthusiasts, we are AI Tinkerers. The core essence of AI Tinkerers is active collaboration around early-stage discovery & innovation, which requires a high degree of experimentation, vulnerability, openness to sharing challenges & learnings, & collaboration among individuals with a shared level of expertise.

events.name: Agentic AI In The Wild - Open Source Agents In Production
events.description: AI & Open Source Builders Meetup, New York City AI agents are moving into production, & more & more of them are built on open source. The question is no longer whether to use them, but what it takes to make them reliable once the demo is over. This meetup brings together builders, maintainers, & practitioners integrating AI agents into real codebases, CI/CD pipelines, internal developer platforms, cloud native infrastructure, & observability stacks. The evening focuses on the conversations that rarely fit into conference talks: what breaks at scale, how open source tools & standards shape agentic systems, where failure modes hide, & how teams build systems they can trust. Under the theme Open Source in Production, we will explore agentic code review, agent loops in CI/CD, developer platforms, eBPF-powered observability & security, & the role open source communities play in how production AI gets built. No vendor pitches. Just practical lessons from systems running in production. Agenda 5:00 PM Doors Open, Drinks & Networking5:30 PM Welcome & Opening Remarks5:40 PM [Speaker TBD], Qodo Dev Community6:05 PM Break, Food & Networking6:25 PM Panel: Agentic AI in the Wild7:15 PM Ryan Hamilton, Senior Developer & Community Lead, CircleCI AI Lab7:40 PM Closing Remarks7:45 PM Networking until 8:00 PM Speakers & Sessions [Speaker TBD], Qodo[Talk title TBD][Talk abstract TBD] Ryan Hamilton, Senior Developer & Community Lead, CircleCI AI LabOne Take: Engineering Agent Loops That Ship 100% Green PRs on the First PushMost teams optimizing AI-assisted development are focused on the wrong variable: prompting harder, adding rework, dumping larger failure logs into context. The real question isn't how to fix red PRs faster. It's how to stop producing them.Ryan shares findings from three connected Loop Lab experiments, each using the same controlled Snake game benchmark to isolate one variable at a time. Each one reveals something unexpected about where the real leverage lives in an agent loop, & what it means for cutting the cost of agentic development.Together, these experiments map a clear path from "rework is inevitable" to "rework is reserved for the unknowable." The result is a practical harness design that bakes a low Merge Efficiency Ratio (MER, the number of validation cycles it takes to get a change onto main) in from the start, & a new way to think about where validation belongs in the agent loop. Panel: Agentic AI in the WildWhat does it take to move AI agents from proof of concept into systems that operate reliably, & what role does open source play?Practitioners from across the stack will discuss context management, governance, open standards, observability, security, & what changes when agentic systems scale.Expect concrete lessons, not talking points. ModeratorDana Fine, Open Source & Developer Relations Manager, QodoDana leads open source programs & community initiatives at Qodo. She runs the GitHub User Group, CNCF local & GenAI communities, & the Bond AI meetup series. PanelistsBaruch Sadogursky, PortBaruch is a longtime developer advocate & a well-known speaker at developer conferences around the world. He co-authored Liquid Software & DevOps Tools for Java Developers, & focuses on developer productivity, DevOps, & how AI is changing the way software gets built & shipped. [Speaker TBD], Claude Community[Bio TBD] [Speaker TBD], NVIDIA[Bio TBD] Community PartnersAWS User Group NYC, CNCF NYC, Frontend NYC, WeMakeDevs, Bond AI, Qodo Dev Community Join the CommunityQodo Dev Community on Discord: [Discord invite link]Follow us on Meetup: [Meetup group link]

events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: Did Maha Maha?
events.description: Has the MAHA movement made Americans healthier than the establishment? Americans spend more on healthcare than anyone else in the world. Yet we have soaring rates of obesity, diabetes, & chronic disease. So is the medical establishment failing us? And is MAHA actually doing any better? RFK's MAHA movement has put ultra-processed foods, environmental toxins, & chronic disease at the center of the national conversation. Supporters say it's finally challenging a healthcare system that profits from treating illness instead of preventing it. Critics say it's undermining trust in vaccines, established science, & the institutions responsible for keeping Americans healthy. So who's right? Is MAHA forcing a long-overdue reckoning with a broken healthcare system? Or is it replacing imperfect science with something far more dangerous? Kerry Semle is a biomedical engineer, former medical technology executive, & women's health advocate with 15 years of experience in medical devices & diagnostics. She's advocated for greater investment in women's health research & improved access to care. Emily Kaplan is the CEO & co-founder of the Broken Science Initiative, an organization challenging the scientific establishment & questioning how medical research is conducted, evaluated, & trusted. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

events.name: Future Forum - Science For Society
events.description: The 2026 FUTURE FORUM will convene leaders from diverse backgrounds including academia, museums, journalism, media, public engagement, government, industry, & scientific organizations from the United States & Germany to explore how science can more effectively serve society through communication, collaboration, & public engagement. Centered on the theme Science for Society, the meeting will examine how trust in science is built & sustained, how scientific discoveries & long-term research can be communicated more effectively to diverse audiences, & how institutions can demonstrate the societal value of science. A panel discussion will address the roles of museums, journalists, policymakers, & other non-traditional science communicators; strategies for strengthening public confidence in science & evidence-based decision-making; the importance of open & international scientific collaboration amid increasing geopolitical pressures; & approaches to fostering public engagement, scientific literacy, & global collaboration. Through interdisciplinary dialogue & transatlantic relationship-building, the 2026 FUTURE FORUM aims to develop new partnerships, identify best practices, & strengthen the role of science communication in advancing an informed, engaged, & resilient society. About the FUTURE FORUM The FUTURE FORUM brings together experts from Germany, the United States, & beyond to exchange perspectives on emerging issues in science, innovation, & society. Through focused expert dialogue & public engagement, the format creates space to examine shared challenges, identify new perspectives, & strengthen transatlantic exchange. Previous editions have explored themes including Science Diplomacy in an Era of Technological Disruption at the Science Diplomacy Hub at Johns Hopkins University, Washington, D.C. in 2025. Or Health. Tech. Diplomacy., which focused on global health at the Broad Institute of MIT & Harvard in 2025. In 2026, the FUTURE FORUM returns with Science for Society, bringing together transatlantic experts to explore questions around science communication, public trust, scientific literacy, public engagement, & collaboration across disciplines & borders.

events.name: Agentic Loops Demo Day
events.description: Agents that keep working while you sleep Join AI Tinkerers NYC for a themed demo night on agentic loops: agents that plan, build, verify, & retry without a human in the loop. Not chat wrappers. Systems that run for hours & hand you a result in the morning. Keynote by Conveo engineer Vincent Vankrunkelsven, author of Nightwatch: how to get your agents to keep working while you sleep. Then a full lineup of community demos on the same theme. Space is strictly limited & we will be screening attendance.  Apply now for an evening of live demos, real PRs, real failures, & a room full of people building the same thing. Keynote: Nightwatch, reviewed liveConveo runs a skill called /nightwatch. An engineer plans a feature in the afternoon, a fleet of agents builds it overnight on a remote box, & one reviewed PR is waiting at breakfast. Every layer is a loop: each worker builds, verifies with a script it can run itself, pushes, & drives its PR until the review agents approve. The orchestrator wakes every 15 minutes, checks progress, & replaces anything that died. The whole thing loops again the next day, with the night's logs feeding the next version of the skill. For this event, Conveo will kick off a real Nightwatch run the afternoon of October 21, then do the morning review live on stage. You'll see what the fleet actually built overnight: the master PR, the generated test plan, the screenshots, & whatever broke. A recorded run is on standby in case the demo gods disagree. What you'll take away: The four capabilities you need to run your own overnight loop: a spawner, a durable message bus, validation agents, & a way to wake a running agentHow to write tickets with a closed verification loop so workers converge instead of driftingThe failure modes that each cost Vincent a night, & the fixesHow the agent mesh keeps messages from getting lost when a laptop closesSpeaker: Vincent Vankrunkelsven, Senior Engineer, Conveo. Joined by Dieter (CEO) & Maarten Claes (CTO). What is AI Tinkerers?AI Tinkerers is a meetup exclusively for practitioners with technical, machine learning, & entrepreneurial backgrounds who are actively building & working with foundation models, such as large language models (LLMs) & generative AI. If you're deeply passionate about creating LLM-enabled applications, have hands-on experience in building such systems, & want to connect with like-minded people who share your level of commitment, then this group is the perfect fit for you. With AI Tinkerers meetings happening in many cities, we support a dedicated global community. Who is this for?We are not just AI enthusiasts, we are AI Tinkerers. The core essence of AI Tinkerers is active collaboration around early-stage discovery & innovation, which requires a high degree of experimentation, vulnerability, openness to sharing challenges & learnings, & collaboration among individuals with a shared level of expertise.

events.name: For The Firsts Meetup
events.description: For The Firsts is a meetup club for those building without a blueprintExpect an evening of interesting conversation in an inviting space as you meet & mingle with other "firsts" - those who are the first in their family to choose their professional path with intention instead of inertia. This month, we'll be sitting down with Jeanelle Teves, the Chief Commercial Officer of Bugaboo, founder of Work Lunch, creator, mother, & author. Enjoy refreshing drinks, delicious bites, & the chance to connect with other professionals, creatives, students, & founders. Each of our meetups looks something like this: 6:00 - 6:30 PM: Arrival & Open Mixer 6:30 - 7:30 PM: Fireside chat with Jeanelle Teves 7:30 - 9:00 PM: Guided Mixer If you are approved, please try to arrive on time, as our events regularly hit capacity & we have many folks on the waitlist. Here's what to expect:Cringe-Free Conversation: This isn't a networking event. It's a purpose-led meetup where who you are will always be more important than what you do. The dress code is always 'come exactly as you are, meet exactly who you need'. Guided Moments of Connection: This experience is at the core of For The Firsts. We'll have a few rounds of guided connection meant to introduce you to others who share your story. Remember the first rule of For The Firsts: go deeper than your job title! Firsts, not Followers: Each meetup is curated to bring together the best possible group of professionals, creatives, & founders in NYC who are the architects of their own lives. Intention is in everything we do, & you'll find that in the people you meet. Remember, the best way to get to know someone is to get someone to know you. I want to encourage you to connect on who you are & your purpose for your work & life. Remember Rule #1: No job titles, go deeper. Tell us why, how & for whom you do what you do. Disclaimer:*By signing up for the event, you will also be subscribed to our weekly Substack 'First Things First' for additional updates & event announcements. *This event will be photographed, & For the Firsts reserves the right to use photos & video from the event for marketing & communications purposes. By attending the event, you consent to the use of your image for these purposes.

events.description: This GILD AI Forum brings together CTOs, VPs of Engineering, Heads of AI, & senior technical leaders for candid conversations about building, scaling, & implementing AI inside their companies. This isn't a conference. It's not a panel. It's a small, curated room of technical leaders sharing what's actually working, what's not, & the real challenges of shipping AI in the AI era. Each Forum opens with a Conversation Starter, a practitioner sharing what their team is building with AI, followed by open Q&A. From there, the room breaks into intimate discussions where everyone has a seat at the table. Every attendee brings their own experience. Every attendee contributes. No pitches. No performative networking. Just senior technical leaders being honest about the architectures they're choosing, the tradeoffs they're making, & what they wish they'd figured out sooner. TRENDING THEMES FOR THIS SESSION Conversations at the Forum are shaped by what technical leaders bring to the table. Themes likely to surface this evening include: From AI pilots to AI in production: breaking out of the proof-of-concept trap & scaling agents into real workflows Connecting AI to legacy systems: architectural patterns for integrating modern AI with 20-year-old stacks without breaking everything The AI tooling budget problem: balancing experimentation with unsustainable spend as engineers blow through AI tool budgets Engineers as curators, not creators: the shift from writing code to orchestrating AI agents, reusable components, & external services MCP, multi-agent systems, & the orchestration layer: what's working, what's overhyped, & what technical leaders are actually building Guardrails & governance for AI-generated code: who's accountable when the AI writes it, & what review processes actually hold up in production Presented in partnership with Tecla Tecla gives companies flexible access to vetted talent across the US & Latin America, developed for AI-native work & available from fractional engagements to dedicated nearshore pods. Learn more at www.tecla.io THE FORMAT Intentionally small & highly curated, 20 to 25 max. A seated round-table dinner, private & off the record under Chatham House Rules. AGENDA 6:00 - 6:30 PM  Cocktails & passed appetizers 6:30 - 7:00 PM  Dinner is served Find a seat & get comfortable. 6:45 - 6:50 PM  GILD & Partner Welcome A few words from the GILD team & our partners on what the night holds & how we'll spend it together. 6:50 - 7:00 PM  Conversation Starter A fellow engineering leader opens the discussion with a candid perspective on AI, with a brief Q&A. 7:00 - 8:00 PM  Table discussions 8:00 - 8:30 PM  Open mingling WHO THIS IS FOR Founders  CEOs  CTOs  VPs of Engineering  Heads of AI  Technical Leaders  Product Leaders This session is for leaders responsible for building, deploying, & maintaining AI systems in production. Chatham House Rules apply. Discussion stays private.

events.name: The Deployment Room: 6 Active Funds, Funding Founders (Seed to Series A+)
events.description: The Builder Series: A 60,000+ member community redefining what networking looks like curating founders, investors into intentional rooms built for experiences people remember & relationships that last. It's a direct line to the most ambitious builders. Find us here: Instagram  LinkedIn  TikTok  Facebook  X : WhatsApp Broad Channel (Not a GC) August was our pilot. Here's how it performed. Our intent 20 founders, 6 investors. The real turnout: 30 guests: 20 founders, 10 capital allocators $70M+ raised collectively by the founders present $3.5M average raised per founder $2.3B+ combined AUM across the investors $1M average check, $100K minimum $10M+ in live check capacity This is today objective: Every founder in the room is doing $1M+ in ARR or has raised a round of $1M or more. Raised your 1st round, onto your 2nd, or bootstrapped to $1M ARR? You're in the right place. Every investor here is from our network. We're curating this room deliberately, matching founders to the investors most likely to be a fit, & making the introduction ourselves. The goal here: Getting founders funded by our investor network. The 6 Investors joining us from our network: (More will be joining) Francesca Poupel: F&G Capital Partners (Managing Partner): Backing founders from pre-seed to Series A in AI, fintech, & blockchain, writing $300K-$500K checks & partnering closely with teams as they scale. Mahir Laul (Partner) representing Laul Global a family office & holding company operating four interconnected pillars: Education Engine, Real Assets, Future Ventures, & Acquisitions. One integrated system. One long-term vision. Laul Global is owned & operated by the Laul family. We started with a single student recruitment company. We built it into one of Canada's most diversified education holding groups. Today the portfolio spans institutions, edtech, real estate, & a tech venture studio, with reach across 20+ countries & no plans to slow down.  Triet Leminh: Principal, LMT Partners: Lawyer, founder, & investor backing pre-seed to Series A founders building in enterprise & regulated industries. Writing $200K-$300K checks.  Andrew Antar (General Partner, AG Venture Capital): A generalist fund backing extraordinary founders, sector agnostic. Also a Venture Partner at Arcadian Capital, focused on late-stage secondaries & pre-IPO tech, & served as Crypto Policy Advisor to the NYC Office of the Mayor - advising on the city's crypto regulatory framework & organizing the NYC Crypto Summit at Gracie Mansion. He is also founder of Tune.FM, a tokenized music streaming platform & digital asset marketplace, & co-founded Clear Quantum, a stealth quantum AI startup. Gonzalo Quincot (Founder, Sinober): Sinober is a financial intelligence platform that combines public & private market intelligence with institutional-grade methodology, corporate finance & proprietary AI tools to sharpen investment & capital decisions for individuals & businesses. Invests in automation, robotics, data centers & applied AI.  Shilpi Nayak: (Founder & General Partner, 434 VC): Invests in early-stage technical founders across AI, infrastructure, physical AI & emerging technology. She is also the founder of House of 434, a community bringing together founders, investors & industry leaders.  Pranav Jajapur (Co-Founder, ZERON Ventures): ZERON is an early-stage venture fund with an execution platform behind it, backing real-world technology, AI, healthcare, deep tech & climate companies building in the physical world, inside biology. Pre-seed through Series A with core deployment at seed, writing $400K-$500k checks. Preferred focus is institutionally-anchored AI: structural research relationships at academic institutions, spinouts, & founder-led research programs. Fund I in formation. Deploying Q1  All 6 senior investors confirmed. Part of building rooms is making sure real capital is present. Six investors actively deploying writing capital will be joining. Our first confirmed: Why we do this: Putting active investors in the same room as exceptional founders, & keeps the room small enough to ensure everyone actually meets. We value intentional networking & community. If you're here to meet the best of the best, this is the room. Our Sponsor: Composition WealthYour seat at the table is waiting. Your life is shaped by new beginnings, major decisions, & milestones. That's why when it comes to developing the strategies to achieve your financial goals, we make sure you have a seat at the table & are empowered with the knowledge & tools to shape your own future. At Composition Wealth, our goal is to empower you to reach YOUR goals. Chris Guarino, CFPBook some time: Calendly link What to expect for this: A Greek style lunch, courtesy of our team Conversations with fellow high-performing startup leaders An experience designed to facilitate new meaningful connections conversations with ambitious peers solving similar problems Event to be hosted at a beautiful private Soho loft Our intent is to bring good, smart humans together, & active investors together to fun incredible founders. Community has been lost & we are rebuilding it. Our Greek Inspired Menu: About the meal A three-course Greek menu. Appetizers & dessert are shared & open to everyone; each will get one entre. The format is intentionally part standing, part seated so you can enjoy incredible food without being anchored to a single table or a single conversation. Why we do this Our intent is simple: bring good, smart humans together, put active investors in the same room as incredible founders. Intentional community has been lost. We're rebuilding it.

You spent the money. So why aren't events paying you back? You shook 50 hands, had a few great conversations, & sent the follow-ups. Then nothing. The "let's stay in touch" went nowhere, & another event quietly became another expense. Your next clients, partners, & investors are already in those rooms. This workshop shows you what to do once you're inside, & after you leave. Rooms That Pay is a 90-minute live workshop for established business owners & execs to go from polite networkers to people magnets, & leave every event with paying clients, without feeling salesy. This is for you if you're: Successful, but stuck at a plateau & ready for the next level Growing through trust, referrals, & face-to-face relationships Great 1-on-1, but rooms full of strangers still feel like work The Presence-to-Pipeline Method Show Up: Drop the work persona & walk in as fully you Connect: Have easy, genuinely helpful conversations that make hiring you the obvious next step Convert: Capture leads, follow up effectively, & turn every event into paying clients Why it works: People buy from people they trust. When they can see who you are & that you know your stuff, you never have to pitch. Personality + expertise = sales. You'll walk out with: Ease in every conversation, no scripts or rehearsed pitches A way to lead with help instead of selling Permission to bring your real personality into the room A simple system to turn "nice to meet you" into signed business Your hostsGal BePole, founders' mentor & creator of Dance Speak, has spent 15 years training people across 13+ countries to step onto stages & into rooms as fully themselves.Greg Bumble, EventReps, helps businesses capture, organize, & convert event conversations into measurable pipeline. If even 2 new clients from your next event are worth $10,000 to $100,000, this is the highest-ROI 90 minutes you'll spend this quarter. Seats are limited to 20. Jobs, energy, education, & more. Sharp thinkers go head to head, you hear the case for & against, & you decide where you land. Taking place this year at the Newark Museum of Art, where tech & culture share a roof, OverdriveAI brings together founders, operators, investors, & researchers from across the Northeast for a day built around one idea: the biggest questions in AI don't have easy answers, so let's actually argue about them. TICKETS ARE NOW LIVE!EXPLORE THE FULL OVERDRIVEAI EXPERIENCE Community AI TrainingHands-on morning AI training at EqualSpace designed for all experience levels. No prior AI experience required. Reserve Your Spot Executive AI TrainingA focused, practical AI training designed for executives & business leaders ready to better understand & apply AI within their organizations. Reserve Your Spot Pitch Roast LiveStartups pitch. Comedians roast. Everyone wins. Close out OverdriveAI with an evening of bold ideas, founder pitches, comedy, & connection. Reserve Your Spot   What to Expect Community AI Training A hands-on morning (10a-12p ET) AI training at EqualSpace designed for all experience levels. Come ready to learn, explore, & put AI into practice. No prior experience required. Executive AI Training Turn AI into practical business advantage. Start your morning with a focused AI training session designed for executives, business leaders, & decision-makers navigating the rapidly evolving AI landscape. This interactive session will explore practical ways leaders can better understand, evaluate, & apply AI within their organizations helping you move from conversation to action. The AI Debates The main event at the Newark Museum of Art. Will AI take your job or grow the economy? Who pays for AI's energy appetite? Does AI belong in the classroom? Can you still trust what you see? Startup demos will be featured between rounds & the afternoon will roll into TechUnited:NJ Birthday Party! Final topics & speakers are still being locked in, ticket holders hear every name first. Here's what's on the table so far: AI takes jobs vs. AI grows the economy - does automation erase more work than it creates? Is AI raising your energy bill? - the data center buildout is reshaping the grid, & New Jersey's in the middle of it. Does AI belong in the classroom? - a tutor for every student, or the end of learning how to think? Is it time for universal basic income? - if productivity keeps compounding, someone decides where the gains go. Can we handle deepfakes? - synthetic media's getting cheap & convincing, what's the real defense? Got a debate we missed? Suggest it, & if it makes the stage, you'll know it was yours. Live debates. Experts, opposing sides of one question, no hedging.Hot takes. Short, sharp presentations from speakers with a strong point of view.Networking. 300+ founders, researchers, & investors in one room, this year in a new venue built for it. Pitch Roast Live Closing the night at Newark Culture Club Close with startup pitches & a high-energy evening experience. Four founders pitch, three comedians & two investors roast. One walks out a winner! Last Year, at Nokia Bell Labs Speakers joined us from OpenAI, IBM, CoreWeave, Verizon, Perplexity, Nokia Bell Labs, BetterFutureLabs, NJEDA, & the NJ AI Hub. 16 speakers, 300+ attendees, a packed house. This year's lineup is coming together now, & it's bigger. OverdriveAI is one of many events TechUnited:NJ runs for its 13,000+ member community, from AI Demo Night to Propelify. Inquire about membership to hear about what's next. TechUnited:NJ members receive complimentary admission to OverdriveAI as part of their membership. Not a member yet? events.name: Urban Future Summit - 10 Years Of Impact
events.description: The 2026 Urban Future Summit is supported by New York Community Trust, New York State Energy Research & Development Authority, MUFG Bank, & NYU Tandon School of Engineering - this year is extra special as we're celebrating 10 years of supporting climate innovation & the entrepreneurs who have shaped it. 2 PRIZE TRACKS. 8 FINALISTS. HEAR THEM PITCH ON 10/22.Read the full press release  Climate Adaptation Prize: focused on solutions that help communities & ecosystems adapt to & build resilience against the impacts of climate change. Airbuild: Autonomous biological nutrient recovery systems that convert wastewater nutrients into carbon-sequestering biochar fertilizer, helping municipalities meet EPA compliance & cut costs while creating new revenue for farmers. Class 3 Technologies: Engineering-grade, building-level climate risk assessments powered by Iris, a proprietary simulation engine, helping large property owners quantify physical vulnerability & evaluate resilience strategies across their portfolios, while extending that same risk intelligence to underserved communities. Rarefied: A sunlight-driven propulsion mechanism enabling persistent flight in near-space, building a new atmospheric data layer to improve weather forecasting, disaster resilience, & climate risk modeling - data especially valuable in equatorial & developing regions, where sparse observations weaken storm & drought forecasts. Supercool Earth: An end-to-end precipitation enhancement platform that uses biology to increase rain & snowfall on demand for ski resorts, water utilities, hydropower operators, & agriculture, giving water-scarce communities a tool to stabilize supply before rationing or crop failure set in. Climate Mitigation Prize: focused on solutions that reduce greenhouse gas emissions & mitigate the impacts of climate change. Arcticar: An intelligent, clean energy platform for the cold chain, replacing diesel-powered trailer refrigeration with lower-cost electric units & integrated battery storage, eliminating the emissions & noise pollution reefers create. Emulate Cities: AI infrastructure that helps local governments automate permit review, cutting permitting timelines from weeks to minutes to accelerate deployment of housing, clean energy, & climate-resilient infrastructure. Every Electric: Operator of New York City's largest plug-in powerbank network, giving households access to affordable backup power while strengthening grid reliability for all New Yorkers. Ultropia: An ultrasonic mechanical water extraction platform that removes moisture from materials, targeting the energy-intensive gas dryers used across the industrial laundry industry. For more than a decade, the Urban Future Prize Competition has identified & accelerated the founders building the technologies, infrastructure, & systems that cities need to thrive in a changing world. What begins as an early-stage idea has repeatedly become a market-shaping company: 23 startups supported, more than $1 million awarded in non-dilutive funding, & over $515 million in follow-on capital raised - a remarkable 515x return on prize dollars deployed. At this year's Urban Future Summit, attendees will actively participate in the next chapter of that story. The Summit will culminate with presentations from the 2026 Urban Future Prize Competition finalists - founders tackling some of the most urgent challenges we're facing today, from climate resilience & emissions reduction to mobility, energy, & the circular economy. These entrepreneurs are not only competing for funding; they are competing for the opportunity to join ACRE, New York's longest-running climatetech incubator, where breakthrough ideas are transformed into scalable businesses. This year marks an important milestone for the Urban Future Prize Competition. For the first time, four awardees will be selected across the Climate Adaptation & Climate Mitigation prize tracks. Two winners get access to $50k & two runner-up teams in each track will also receive $10k in non-dilutive funding & admission into the ACRE Incubator. By expanding support to a broader cohort of entrepreneurs, we're investing in a larger pipeline of innovators at a moment when climate resilience & decarbonization must advance together.

events.name: Tech Table Talk: Career, Family & Life On Your Terms
events.description: Tech Table Talk: Career, Family & Life on Your Terms is an intimate dinner bringing together women in tech for an honest conversation about career, fertility, family planning, & building a life on their own terms. Hosted by Baddies in Tech in partnership with Spring Fertility, the evening will create space for women to have the kinds of conversations we don't often have: How do you think about growing your career while also considering a future family? What options are available if your personal & professional timelines do not align perfectly? And how can having more information today create more choices tomorrow? We're setting the Tech Table to create space for a conversation you may have been thinking about but have not had anyone to talk to about. You'll walk away not just with a great meal & new professional connections, but also more information, more context, & more confidence to make decisions that feel right for the life you're building! What to ExpectWelcome & Opening ToastBaddies in Tech & Spring Fertility will welcome the group & set the tone for an open, judgment-free conversation about career, fertility, family planning, & the life you're building. Dinner & Tech Table TalkOver dinner, guests will have the opportunity to connect more deeply with one another through thoughtful conversation & curated table prompts, exploring the realities of building a career while also thinking about relationships, motherhood, fertility, timing, & what it means to make decisions on your own terms. Fertility Planning Q&A with Dr. Shante Sullivan-PikeThroughout the evening, Dr. Shante Sullivan-Pike of Spring Fertility will help answer questions & demystify fertility, fertility preservation, & family-planning options. Dr. Chantae Sullivan-Pyke is a double board certified Fertility Specialist & Site Director of Spring Fertility Long Island. She completed her medical training at Yale University, Columbia University, & the University of Pennsylvania. Dr. Sullivan-Pyke brings a thoughtful & compassionate approach to fertility care, rooted in deep clinical experience & a genuine connection with her patients. She combines her expertise with a strong commitment to the patient experience, creating a supportive & empowering atmosphere throughout the process. Her areas of clinical focus include IVF, fertility preservation, & oncofertility, & she is particularly passionate about helping her patients navigate complex fertility decisions with clarity & confidence. What You'll Leave WithFresh perspective on navigating career goals alongside personal & family plans New relationships with women thinking through many of the same questions A better understanding of your fertility & family-planning options More clarity around fertility preservation & when it may be worth exploring Greater confidence asking questions about your reproductive health A stronger connection to the Baddies in Tech & Spring Fertility communitie Attendance is complimentary & curated. Because this dinner is intentionally intimate & limited to approximately 20-25 guests, registrations will be reviewed to create a group that aligns with the purpose of the evening. Submitting the registration form expresses your interest in attending & does not guarantee an invitation. Confirmed guests will be notified approximately one week before the event.

events.name: AI Agents Build Day w/ Genspark
events.description: Turn your curiosity about AI into something you can actually use.Join AI After 5 for a hands-on Genspark AI agent session where we'll explore what's possible, build together, & share what we create. Founder of an RL-environment-as-a-service platform backed by Google AI Fund, Betaworks, Hickory Fall Ventures, & NVIDIA Inception. Sharon Rao, MD - Physician-entrepreneur, exited EdTech founder, ex-COO to the largest MedEd brand (3M+ audience, 300K+ platform subscribers) & NYC Health  Tech community host. She represents healthcare & life sciences at the table.

events.name: Transit Techies
events.description: The Center for Urban Science + Progress (CUSP) at NYU Tandon & Transit Techies welcome you to attend two presentations: Phil Cline on Swiftly & Joe Puccio on WalkNYC. Connect with NYU Tandon CUSP & Transit Techies NYC at this talk; attendees are welcome to bring their own food. The event will be held at 370 Jay Street, Brooklyn, NY in Room 1201. We hope to see you there! About the TalksSwiftly Phil Cline will share some of his work on assisting transit agencies with better drawing & dissemination of bus detours at Swiftly WalkNYC In May, Joe created WalkNYC, an app that tracks which blocks you've walked. He built it as a personal project while trying to walk every block in Manhattan. Since launch over 25,000 New Yorkers have started using WalkNYC to stay active & explore the city. About the SpeakersPhil ClineSoftware Engineer, Swiftly Phil Cline is a Brooklyn-based software engineer originally from Toronto who has worked in the transit industry for over 7 years & has a lot of experience with transit data standards like GTFS & GTFS-RT. Joe PuccioCreator, WalkNYC & Founder Coursicle Joe Puccio is a designer & programmer based in NYC. He is the founder of Coursicle, an app used by millions of college students to manage their class schedules & assignments. A central focus of Joe's work is running his companies ethically & building products that are fundamentally beneficial to people's lives. At Coursicle, all employees receive the same salary, & profits are split among employees at the end of each year. Joe graduated from UNC Chapel Hill in 2016 with degrees in Mathematics & Computer Science. He writes about design, technology, & other ideas at joepuccio.com. Vistor InformationPlease visit the NYU Tandon website for directions & a campus map. Advance registration through Luma is required for campus access at NYU for external guests. Attendees who are not current students, faculty, or staff at NYU, including alumni, are asked to register using a personal email address. About CUSP at NYU TandonThe Center for Urban Science + Progress (CUSP) at NYU Tandon is an interdisciplinary center dedicated to applying science, technology, engineering, math, & social sciences to serve urban communities worldwide. Founded as a partnership between NYU & the City of New York, CUSP leads research, educational, & entrepreneurial initiatives that advance the science of cities. By applying novel insights to urban issues, we develop data- & technology-driven approaches that drive positive impact. With an additional focus on training future leaders, CUSP offers interdisciplinary academic programs in applied urban science & informatics for graduate students & professionals. CUSP also engages with stakeholders across city agencies, start-ups, industry players, community-based organizations, & nonprofits to address urgent socioeconomic, environmental, & infrastructural challenges. The center's ultimate objective is to improve urban quality of life by using data to innovate & refine inclusive, equitable, & sustainable practices for cities everywhere. About Transit Techies NYCBringing together the technologists who love transit & the transit enthusiasts who hack! We'll have speakers present transit-related projects. Presenters may be household hackers, data scientists, researchers, product developers, or you! All presentations will be technical & awesome. Follow our calendar to stay up-to-date on our future events! Learn more on our website.

events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Build Your Creative Operating System
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back - In Person at Salesforce We're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City & sponsored by Boldforce. This Month We Present...Build Your Creative Operating SystemBuild a personalized AI workflow that supports your entire creative process-from capturing ideas to publishing finished work-so you're never starting from scratch. Most of us don't have an idea problem. We have a system problem. Ideas live in our Notes app. Research is scattered across browser tabs. Drafts are hiding in Google Docs. Inspiration gets screenshotted & forgotten. And every new project somehow feels like we're starting all over again. What if your creative process actually remembered how you work? At this month's AI & The Culture meetup, we're exploring how to build your own Creative Operating System-a personalized workflow that uses AI to help you capture ideas, organize knowledge, research, create, refine, & publish your work. Instead of collecting more AI tools, we'll focus on connecting the ones that actually support your process. Together we'll explore:  How to map your creative process from idea to finished work  Ways to capture & organize ideas so they don't disappear into the digital abyss  How AI can help you research, brainstorm, draft, edit, & refine your work  Building a personal knowledge base that makes past ideas & research useful again  How to connect AI tools into repeatable workflows instead of using them one at a time  Where automation can save time-and where your human judgment should stay firmly in the driver's seat  How to create a system that gets smarter & more useful the more you use it The goal isn't to automate your creativity. It's to build the infrastructure around your creativity so you have more time & energy for the work only you can do. Expect a welcoming room filled with creators, technologists, educators, founders, artists, & curious minds ready to rethink how we organize & support our creative lives. Who Should Attend?  Creators & content makers  Filmmakers, writers, artists, & storytellers  Educators & community builders  Entrepreneurs, founders, & solopreneurs  Marketers, strategists, & creative professionals  Technologists & AI enthusiasts  Anyone with too many ideas, too many tabs, & not enough systems  Whether your creative process is already organized or currently held together by screenshots, open tabs, & vibes, you're welcome here. Come Ready to Build This won't be a sit-back-and-scroll kind of evening. Bring your laptop, something to write with, & a mindset ready to learn, experiment, & share. We'll be exploring ideas, tools, & workflows you can begin applying to your own creative process.  Bring your laptop  Bring a notebook or something to take notes with  Bring your curiosity & questions Come ready to learn. Come ready to contribute. Come ready to build. About AI & The Culture AI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, & culture. Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams & King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, & culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, & community. We're building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI. This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture - grounded in community, focused on real-world use, & centered on learning together in the room. Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Let's build - together.  About Your Hosts Shirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, & co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, & creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, & real-world execution. About King Willonius King Willonius is a creative technologist & cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, & creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, & community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable & useful - especially for creatives & innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm.  Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio) #AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

these rapidly evolving industries. What to ExpectArrival & ConnectionEase into the evening with drinks, light bites, & time to connect with fellow guests before dinner begins. Dinner & Tech Table TalkOver dinner, guests will have the opportunity to connect more deeply with one another through thoughtful conversation & curated table prompts. The conversation will invite guests to share what they're building, exploring, questioning, & imagining for the future of technology, media, commerce, & AI. Dessert & Fireside ConversationTo close the evening, Randi Gray, Head of IT at MERIT Beauty, will join Allie Joy Tsahey, CEO of Baddies in Tech, for an intimate fireside conversation exploring the intersection of technology, AI, media, & commerce. Together, they'll unpack how emerging technology is reshaping the way people discover, consume, create, shop, & engage with content & products, & what that evolution means for the women helping shape what comes next. What You'll
