events.name: Propel Demo Day  Innovation In Public Cohort Showcase
events.description: Ten companies. Twelve minutes each. An investor room in New York. Who we are. Propel Earth has run 100+ events & built a network of 36,000+ founders, investors, operators, & service providers across six continents. We are not an events company. We are an outcomes company that happens to use rooms. You bring the intent. We deliver the outcome. Demo Night NYC is the biggest room we have ever run, 26,666 people on the guest list & 35+ investors in the room. This is that format, built for the companies coming out of our cohort & the investors who back them. Every attendee tells us at registration what they are building & who they need to meet. Before doors open we hand you at least one named introduction plus the framing for the conversation. Founders leave with investor conversations, investors leave with deal flow they did not have to source. The night 6:00 Doors, drinks, & your matches are waiting7:00 Ten companies, twelve minutes each, pitch & questions8:15 Room favourite, voted live8:30 Open floor with the investors in the room9:00 Close Tickets General admission, free. Open to founders, investors, operators & anyone building.Present Your Company, 250 dollars. Ten slots only. Stage time in front of an investor room, professional video of your pitch, & your company in the post event send.Title Sponsor, 5,000 dollars. One per Demo Day. Naming rights, logo on all promotion & the photo backdrop, a brand moment from the stage, & the full registrant list within 48 hours.Free for Propel Private Network members. What Propel actually does for you 1  Innovation in Public, our GTM accelerator. For founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go to market: content, distribution, & more sales. Four weeks, twice a week, building in public, closing with a public showcase at Propel Demo Day in front of an investor room. Applications for the next cohort are open at this link. 2  The Propel Private Network. Stop networking. Start getting matched. Every month we personally hand you three introductions chosen for what you need right now - someone who can pay you, hire you, or move your company forward. It works both ways: you go into the pool too. Founding rate $200/mo, first 25 members, locked for life  Claim a founding membership 3  Propel Community Coworking x Wayo Club. Come Wednesday night, then come back Thursday & build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, founded by Jason Malefakis. Wayo is a curated community workspace network where members work from premium venues alongside thoughtfully selected founders, operators, & consultants they can collaborate with, refer, hire, or do business with. Attendees typically report being 1.5 to 2x more productive than working from home or a cafe, & leave with 2 to 3 meaningful connections. Lunch is included. Register with us  Propel Community Coworking 1.0  Get a Wayo Community Workday membership  Join the Wayo Anytime waitlist 4  Featured Founder. Build your founder or service-provider profile on Propel & we will give you one additional intro on us  propel.earth/featured-founders 5  Providers already in the room. This is not theoretical. Moshe Cohen, CPA of Cohen & Co runs tax strategy, bookkeeping & fractional CFO work for Propel founders & takes bookings through us. Thirty minute paid session, 120 dollars  Book Moshe. Stephen Michael Consulting, a 45 minute strategy call for funded founders raising, investors deploying, & enterprises entering the startup ecosystem, 150 dollars  Book a strategy call. If you provide a service & want a table at the next one, that is what the provider ticket is. On camera: Nik Michael, host of the Pivot Point podcast, is shooting photography, video, & follow up interviews with select attendees. Nik is a licensed clinician with more than thirty years in counseling & decades in business, education, & investing, & his show explores the moments where transformation begins. Watch the show on YouTube  Listen on Spotify or Apple Podcasts  More at counselingtherapy.com/pivotpoint. Want to be featured, reach out to him directly. Newsletter  propelearth.beehiiv.com  Propel Earth  propel.earth  Questions, text Stephen at 516 307 6380. About The WilsonThe Wilson NYC is a popular American comfort-food restaurant & bar located in NoMad/Chelsea. While the restaurant does not hold traditional culinary stars (like Michelin), it acts as a highly-rated, frequent event space for awards shows & local hospitality honors due to its event duplex & outdoor patio. The Wilson has also been celebrated for supporting its employees through the One Fair Wage What Propel does, & what it has produced Nine ways we connect this network. Every one of these is a room we have already run. Founders & Investors. We put founders in rooms with the people who write checks. Demo Night NYC ran in front of 35+ investors. Founders x Investors Night at PhD Lounge, the Funders x Founders High Line Walk, the Harvard Club Investment Dinner, & the NYTW Pitch Competition with 800+ registrations. Every monthly mixer does the same thing at a smaller scale, which is why we cap the room & match you before you arrive. Founders & Service Providers. You tell us what you need & we match you to someone vetted who does it. Legal, tax, engineering, design, growth, operations. Our Founders Meet Providers rooms exist for exactly this, & the Propel Marketplace runs it year round. Featured provider this month is Moshe Cohen, CPA, offering a 30 minute startup tax & finance session for $120. Book a session or browse the marketplace Work with Stephen directly. A 45 minute strategy call for funded founders raising, investors deploying, & enterprises trying to get into the startup ecosystem. Book a strategy call, browse the marketplace50 Hiring & Talent. Our Tech Job Fair & Developer Job Fair each brought over 150 engineers & operators into the room. That now runs continuously on Propel Earth Jobs, where employers, candidates, & referrers all work in one place. Post a role or find one Product Launches. We launch products to the whole network. The ConnNext App Launch Party pulled 475 registrations, the largest event we have ever run. BECOMEFAMOUS.AI pulled 222. If you are launching something & you need a room, reply to this & we will build it. Capital & Family Office. The capital side of the network. Our Private Markets Discussion Panel drew 280 registrations & Family Office Crypto with Forum Pay brought allocators into the room. These are smaller rooms with higher stakes. See the next one Masterclasses & Info Sessions. Free, online, & taught by specialists who actually do the work. Our Social Impact Cohort Info Session drew 297 registrations. TRIIBE TALK on branding drew 157. Tax, legal, fundraising, & go to market, taught by operators. See the calendar The GTM Accelerator. Four weeks for founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go to market help: content, distribution, & more sales. You get a dedicated BDR, a custom digital asset kit, & a public showcase in front of the room. Our last cohort presented at Demo Day to 35+ investors. August applications are open & you can see how we represented the last cohort The Social Rooms. Not everything is a pitch. Foundersgiving Party & Pitch Roast drew 381 people. LABYRINTH at Hotel Chelsea drew 309. Above Fridays Rooftop Networking, Holiday Chemistry Night, & Bowling & Business. These are the rooms where relationships actually form, & they are the reason the other eight verticals work. Community Coworking. Come to the mixer on Wednesday, then come back Thursday & actually build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, coffee & lunch included. Register here The Private Network, the thread through all of it. Every vertical above runs on the same engine. You tell us what you need, we find the person, we make the introduction in writing. Members receive three curated introductions every month plus free entry to every mixer & select special events. $200 per month, & the first 25 founding members lock that rate for life. Join here Want to sponsor a room? One sponsor per event so it never feels crowded. Email stephen@propel.earth Media ConsentPhotography & Video Acknowledgement. events.name: Post Human Investment Summit
events.description: In the 1980s, Renaissance Technologies pioneered a new way to beat the markets: computing power, statistics, & signal processing. Today that approach anchors a $1.2 trillion asset class, but one built almost entirely on short-horizon trades. The holy grail has always been the opposite: long-horizon investing, fully automated. An agentic Warren Buffett. With the tools we had, it felt out of reach. Agentic reasoning systems may finally change that. A new wave of frontier researchers, 6 newly launched fully agentic funds, & tiger teams inside established funds are setting out to build it. Join us for a one day summit alongside many of the early leaders in this space, to share ideas, challenge assumptions, & brainstorm the various paths ahead for this burgeoning space. The event will be a tightly curated group of researchers, builders, investment professionals, & LPs. Please apply below to be included.   Hosted by Pillar VC Pillar VC is a Boston-based seed-stage venture capital firm. We invest in engineers, researchers, & scientists building solutions to the world's greatest challenges, including Circle, Abridge, Algorand, PillPack, Jellyfish, Neural Magic, Hometap, Asimov, & PathAI, & others.

Don't miss your chance to learn, connect, & grow with New York's most vibrant startup community.  About Silicon Valley Bank (SVB):Silicon Valley Bank, a division of First Citizens Bank, is the bank of some of the world's most innovative companies & investors. SVB provides commercial banking to companies in the technology, life science & healthcare, private equity & venture capital industries, with a dedicated climate tech & sustainability practice since 2008. SVB operates in centers of innovation throughout the United States, serving the unique needs of its dynamic clients with deep sector expertise, insights & connections. SVB's parent company, First Citizens BancShares (NASDAQ: FCNCA ), is a top 20 U.S. financial institution with more than $200 billion in assets. First Citizens Bank, Member FDIC. events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Plan Your Best Year With AI
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back  In Person at SalesforceWe're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City and sponsored by Boldforce.This Month We Present...Plan Your Best Year With AIJoin the community for an interactive planning session to reflect on the past year, identify your biggest opportunities, and build an AI-powered roadmap for the year ahead.Before we rush into a new year with another list of goals, lets get clear about what were actually building.What worked this year? What didnt? What deserves more of your energy? And where could AI help you turn those intentions into action?For our final AI & The Culture meetup of the year, were bringing the community together for an interactive planning and reflection session designed to help you look back, think forward, and build a roadmap for what comes next.This isnt about asking AI to magically plan your life. Its about using these tools as thought partnersto help you reflect, uncover patterns, explore possibilities, make decisions, and turn big ambitions into actionable next steps.Together well explore: How to use AI to reflect on your wins, lessons, challenges, and unfinished business from the past year Prompts that help you identify opportunities you might be overlooking How to turn big goals into realistic projects, milestones, and next steps Ways to use AI as a strategic thought partner for your creative work, career, business, or personal projects How to identify where AI and automation can give you back time in the year ahead Building a personalized AI-powered roadmap you can actually use after you leave the roomAnd because this is AI & The Culture, were making space for something AI cant replace: community.Youll have an opportunity to reflect alongside other creatives, founders, educators, artists, technologists, and curious mindsto exchange ideas, share what youre building, and potentially meet the people who can help you move it forward.The goal isnt to leave with 47 resolutions.Its to leave with clarity, priorities, and a plan.Who Should Attend? Creators and content makers Filmmakers, writers, artists, and storytellers Educators and community builders Entrepreneurs, founders, and solopreneurs Marketers, strategists, and creative professionals Technologists and AI enthusiasts Anyone ready to be more intentional about what theyre building nextWhether you already have your next year mapped out or youre still staring at a blank page wondering where to begin, youre welcome here.Come Ready to BuildThis one is especially hands-on, so come prepared to participate. Bring your laptop Bring a notebook or something to write with Bring a few goals, ideas, or questions youve been thinking about for the year ahead Bring your curiosity and a willingness to shareWell be working through reflection exercises, AI prompts, and planning activities togetherso you can leave with the beginnings of a roadmap, not just another page of notes.Come ready to reflect. Come ready to plan. Come ready to build.About AI & The CultureAI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, and culture.Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams and King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, and culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, and community.Were building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI.This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture  grounded in community, focused on real-world use, and centered on learning together in the room.Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Lets build  together. About Your HostsShirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, and co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, and creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, and real-world execution.About King WilloniusKing Willonius is a creative technologist and cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, and creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, and community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable and useful  especially for creatives and innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm. Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio)#AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: Climate Cafe w/ CUNY
events.description: Join CUNY at the Climate Imaginarium!Open to the public! Members of the CUNY community will be joining us for a gallery tour, followed by a meditation & climate cafe. Climate cafes are listening circles for your climate-linked emotions. Get help facing your climate anxiety & connect with impactful local organizers. Vegan snacks provided!  About the Climate ImaginariumThe Climate Imaginarium is a center for climate, community, & culture in New York City. Located on Governors Island, the Climate Imaginarium is activating a cultural destination at the heart of New York City's burgeoning green economy, where artists, scientists, advocates, & storytellers come together to reimagine & build toward a more resilient future.  Getting to the Climate ImaginariumFor the weekend ferry schedule to Governors Island, please check here. Ferries run every 15 minutes. Take the ferry that's most convenient for you from either Lower Manhattan (10 South Street), Brooklyn Bridge Park (Pier 6), or Red Hook/Atlantic Basin. Please arrive 15 minutes prior to your ferry departure time with your ticket ready to display. Ferry tickets must be purchased at the ferry terminal or online. Fares are $5 for a round trip ticket & free for adults over 65, children 12 & under, Climate Imaginarium summer volunteers, & others. All passengers ride free before 11am on weekends. Cars are not permitted. Governors Island is also accessible from any route via NYC Ferry by transferring at Wall Street/Pier 11. You can find the NYC Ferry schedule here. Tickets on NYC Ferry are $4.50 each way. Once you get to Governors Island, you will either get out at Soissons Landing (from Manhattan) or Yankee Pier (from Brooklyn). You can use this map of Governors Island to locate Colonels Row. The Climate Imaginarium is in Building 406A, in the middle of Colonels Row, & will have a visible sign outside the doorway. Our address is 406A Comfort Road.

events.name: Junto Founder Dinner
events.description: Hi, Andrew Yeung here. We started the Junto Founder Dinner series two years ago to bring together the top founders + builders. Each month, we invite 24 vetted early-stage founders & CEOs for a 3-hour, multiple-course dinner experience. What to expect:A 3-course meal, courtesy of our partners Conversations with fellow high-performing startup leaders A dinner experience designed to facilitate new connections & conversations, with rotating 6-person table formats Meaningful connections with ambitious peers solving similar problems If you're wondering how our dinners usually go... read this Our only intent is to bring good, smart humans together. Details: Date: Dec 9, 2026  Time: 6:00pm - 8:30pm  Venue: Private Dinner Club in NYC Past attendees of my events include the founders/C-suite of Venmo, Duolingo, Foursquare, Lyft, Goldman Sachs, Compass, Superhuman, Yext, OpenDoor, Chief, LearnVest, DocSend, Vercel, Loom, Morning Brew, The Hustle, Gas, Teachable, Replit, Twitter, Slack, Pinterest, Yahoo, MongoDB, Business Insider, Wonder, Hinge.  Apply to join by filling out the RSVP form. About our Hosts & Sponsors: Andrew Yeung is the founder of Fibe & The Shortlist NYC. He is also an angel investor & Partner at Next Wave NYC, a pre-seed venture fund. Andrew has hosted over 300 events for 50,000 founders, operators, investors, & tech professionals that were featured by Bloomberg, Business Insider, Fast Company, Fortune Magazine, Axios, Newsweek, & Forbes. Business Insider dubbed him the "Gatsby of Silicon Alley." Hubble is NYC's largest online platform for startup office space. We combine Kayak-style browse & search, with our free advisory service that does all the heavy lifting: recommendations, shortlisting, booking tours & negotiating the best rates. Fidelity brings certainty to startup founders & leaders with our automated cap table & equity management platform. No matter where you are on your journey, Fidelity has the expertise & robust support to help guide you. Looking for an alternative to your current equity management solution? Our team will guide you through a smooth transition to our platform. Learn more. Comp AI helps startups get SOC 2 or ISO 27001 audit-ready in just a few days, without slowing down the team. Evidence collection, controls, vendor management, & audit prep run on autopilot, so you stay audit-ready 24/7. Trusted by fast-growing teams like Dub, Better Auth, & Corgi. As a thank-you for joining us tonight, you get $2,000 off compliance. Rho is the all-in-one banking platform for startups. With banking set up in minutes, 2% cashback cards, & powerful tools for managing spend, paying bills, & closing the books, Rho helps high-growth startups move fast & stay focused-with support that goes to the ends of the earth to help you win. Get on the list for future events: Twitter  Instagram  Website

events.name: PMAI: Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Sales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. - Bring a computer. You're writing three things tonight.- Most founders can get meetings. The deals die after meeting one.- You'll leave with your buyer in one sentence, a cold email written to a real person, & five questions for your next call. About Farzad, the speaker Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding & generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: Spatial Analytics w/ Python
events.description: Join PyData NYC on October 27th at 6:30 PM for an evening exploring geospatial data science with Python, featuring Brendan Collins, Founder & CTO at Makepath & creator of Xarray-Spatial! Discover how Python can transform spatial data into powerful insights, from terrain analysis & hydrology to scalable CPU- & GPU-accelerated computing. Please bring your  to follow along & sign up using your official government-issued name.  Pizza & drinks will be provided - Thank you, Makepath! Agenda xarray-spatial: In & Out of the Raster-verseSpeaker: Brendan Collins (Founder & CTO at Makepath)Spatial data comes in many shapes & sizes, but some of the most powerful spatial analysis techniques begin by viewing the world as a grid.Led by the library's creator & maintainer, this talk introduces Xarray-Spatial, an open-source Python library for scalable raster analysis with CPU & GPU acceleration.We'll learn how to enter the Raster-verse by bringing spatial data into Xarray, explore the Raster-verse using algorithms for terrain analysis, hydrology, proximity, & more, & escape the Raster-verse through techniques like zonal statistics & polygonization.Finally, we'll discuss contributing to the Raster-verse, sharing lessons from maintaining Xarray-Spatial & how AI-augmented development is transforming open-source contributions, code quality, & scientific software engineering.Whether you're a GIS practitioner, data scientist, or Python developer, you'll leave with practical ideas for working with spatial data & contributing to open source.  About the SpeakerBrendan Collins is the Founder & CTO of Makepath, where he helps early-stage startups & Fortune 500 engineering teams realize their product ambitions.A former employee of Anaconda, Brendan has spent the past decade applying PyData technologies, including NumPy, Xarray, & Numba, to engineering challenges across the public, private, & nonprofit sectors.When not writing in the third person, Brendan enjoys swimming, playing the banjo, & gardening.  NetworkingConnect with fellow data enthusiasts, Python developers, researchers, & community leaders. Build meaningful connections, exchange ideas, & explore opportunities for collaboration.

events.name: The Human Edge - Founders Cacao Salon
events.description: The Human Edge: A Founders Salon for the Age of AIBreakfast  Cacao  Capital  Curated Connection AI is making it easier than ever to build. But trust, conviction, introductions, & the relationships that actually move companies forward are still deeply human. The Human Edge brings together an intimate group of founders, investors, & operators for a morning in Tribeca designed around useful insight & meaningful connection. The morning is structured so the right conversations have time to actually go somewhere. What you'll walk away withA current read on fundraising & what investors are paying attention to, fresh from San Francisco Tech Week A practical perspective on leading teams & building companies as AI changes how we work Three or four people you'll genuinely want to reconnect with A focused, energizing start to your day The morning9:45 AM  Doors openBreakfast & arrival 10:00 AM  Welcome 10:15 AM  Cacao openingA short guided ritual with Sasha Sakhar to arrive, settle in, & set an intention for the morning. 10:45 AM  What investors are seeing nowTanya Montman shares observations from San Francisco Tech Week: where capital is moving, what investors are asking founders, & how AI is changing the fundraising landscape. 11:00 AM  The human side of building with AIGeoff Scott on building companies, teams, & products where AI amplifies people rather than replaces human leadership. 11:15 AM  Open conversation & Q&A 11:30 AM  Curated connection roundsGuided small-group conversations matched around stage, interests, & goals so the conversation gets past the usual networking script. 11:50 AM  Closing + open networking 12:00 PM  Close In the room Tanya Montman  VC & fundraising advisor. After a decade at J.P. Morgan across leveraged finance & M&A, Tanya founded StartLinkVentures to connect founders with capital & advises companies across New York, Boston, & Silicon Valley.  Geoff Scott  CTO, founder, & advisor. Three companies started, four exits, four AI patents, & still coding. Board member at SIM New York Metro & creator of KindnessFlywheel.org, focused on human-centered leadership in the age of AI.  Sasha Sakhar  Founder of SUGARHAUS, an NYC experiential studio reimagining how people gather. For seven years, Sasha has facilitated cacao rituals, connection experiences, & curated gatherings for founders, teams, & creatives. Why cacao?Ceremonial cacao creates a simple transition from doing to being present. Its naturally occurring theobromine offers a gentler, steadier lift than coffee, while the ritual gives us something rare in founder culture: a moment to arrive before the titles, pitches, & ideas begin. You don't need to know anything about cacao. Just come curious. Who it's forEarly-stage founders with a product in market, particularly those preparing for or currently raising, alongside selected operators, angels, investors, & ecosystem builders. An intimate group. events.name: 122nd NY Hardware Meetup
events.description: The Hardware Meetup community is excited to announce our next event at Parter's NYC office. Hardware Meetups happen across 35+ cities around the world, bringing together hardware professionals to network & learn from each other. You might not realize it, but NYC is a hotbed for this kind of innovation & tonight you'll meet two companies working at the cutting edge of this technology. THANK YOU TO OUR HOST PARTER Parter is the AI-native BOM optimization platform that takes hardware from design to production without supply chain surprises. It continuously monitors every part on the BOM & flags shortages, EOL & lead time risks early, so issues are caught in prototyping, not on the production line. events.name: The AI Era & What It Means To Be Human
events.description: The AI Era & What It Means to Be HumanAI is changing how we work, learn, create, & make decisions. But underneath the conversation about models, agents, & automation is a more fundamental question: what does it mean to be human in an age of increasingly capable machines? On October 23rd, The AI Collective is bringing together 100 people in NYC for an evening exploring the human side of the AI era. We'll move beyond the usual conversation about what AI can do & look instead at what its rise asks of us: how we learn, how we maintain agency, how we relate to one another, & which distinctly human capacities become more important as technology advances. The evening will combine conversation, small-group discussion, & experiential mindfulness/wellness exercises. This is not a technical AI event. We're creating a conversation about the human layer: the trust, awareness, connection, & shared understanding we'll need to build alongside the technology. Come curious. Expect to participate. Agenda6:00 PM: Arrival & Welcome6:30 PM: Opening Remarks + Experiential Mindfulness Exercise6:45 PM: Fireside Chat: AI & the Human Condition with Mohan Nair, author of "Unreachable: How to Not Lose Your Mind in an AI-Obsessed Era."7:15 PM: Conversation with Catherine & Manas followed by Breath-work & Meditation.7:45 PM: Small-Group Roundtables8:15 PM: Dessert & Networking Food & beverages provided. Space is limited to 75 participants. Co-hosted by The AI Collective & Manas Ram with support from JQ Consulting, whose work focuses on the science of human wellbeing, resilience, happiness, mindfulness, & the human condition. Please be advised: Unfortunately, space is very limited at these community events & we can not always accept everyone we would like to. If you are not accepted to this event, please keep applying! We appreciate your application tremendously & we are looking forward to seeing you at a future event very soon! The AI Collective is a global non-profit building the human layer for the AI era. We unite 200,000+ leaders, builders, & stakeholders across 100+ forums worldwide to democratize the frontier, build trust, & coordinate how society navigates the rapid acceleration of technological progress. All attendees & organizers at events affiliated with The AI Collective agree to our privacy policy & are subject to our code of conduct.

events.name: The AI-ndustrial Revolution?
events.description: In the next five years, will AI make the average American's life better or worse? Companies are spending billions on AI. But is it actually making the economy better? And more importantly, will it make the economy better FOR YOU? Right now, the evidence is weird. Only 1 in 8 CEOs says AI is both increasing revenue & cutting costs. At the same time, 77% of CEOs say AI has been overhyped so far-but may actually be underhyped over the next decade. So what happens next? A productivity boom that creates new industries & better jobs? Or enormous investment, displaced workers, & technology that never delivers enough value to justify the hype? Daniel Di Martino, an economist & Fellow at the Manhattan Institute, studies economic growth, labor markets, & the policies that drive American competitiveness. Dr. Cecilia Dones is a Columbia lecturer & longtime data & AI executive who works with organizations trying to turn massive AI investments into actual business value. Luke Strathmann, our opener, runs the funniest (and only) Economics comedy show in NYC. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

events.name: Ugly Talk - Your First $100k Deal
events.description: Your first six-figure deal can expose every weak spot in your sales process. You chased the wrong buyer. Priced from fear. Followed up too late. Let one internal champion carry the whole deal. Then the contract lands. You celebrate. The next question hurts more: can you do it again? This Ugly Talk gets into the hard calls behind closing a major customer. You will hear what founders got wrong. You will see what made the deal move. You will leave with a clearer path from one big win to $1M ARR. Why you should be in this room.Spot the sales mistakes that quietly kill large deals.Find the buyer with budget, urgency, & enough power to move.Learn what changes across pricing, pitching, negotiation, & follow-up.Build a sales motion that can survive beyond one lucky contract.Understand what needs to break before your company reaches $1M ARR.

events.name: Building & Scaling Successful UGC Program w/ Amazing Margins
events.description: A hands-on workshop for app founders.Most app founders are burning UA budget on creative that doesn't convert - & the ones who aren't have figured out something specific about how creator content actually scales.You'll leave with your own UGC program mapped out on paper: what it costs to run, what it should return, & where your current setup is leaking margin.What we'll build together:1. Your unit economics. We'll walk through the real cost stack of a creator program - cost per asset, creator rates by tier, usage rights, editing. Then you'll run your own numbers against benchmarks & see where you land.2. Format over volume. Why most brands scale the wrong thing. We'll break down hooks & formats converting on paid social right now, & you'll identify which map to your product.3. Your creator structure. How to compensate creators so quality holds as you go from 5 to 50. We'll cover flat-rate vs. performance, rights bundling, & the specific terms that keep good creators coming back.4. Failure modes. Where UGC programs break - the stuff that doesn't make it into case studies. Diagnostic checklist so you can spot it early.5. Open working time. Bring a live problem. We'll work through as many as time allows, in the room, with the group.You'll leave with: a completed program worksheet with your own numbers, a creator rate benchmark sheet, & a format checklist you can hand to whoever runs your creative.Who this is for:App founders, growth leads, & heads of UA at consumer or B2C apps, pre-seed through Series B, either running paid social now or about to. Come with your current numbers if you have them  the session works better when you're plugging in real figures.Who this isn't for:Agencies & service providers. We're keeping the room on one side of the market so the conversation stays useful.Hosted by GlossKit as part of New York App Week 2026.

events.name: Agentic AI In The Wild - Open Source Agents In Production
events.description: AI & Open Source Builders Meetup, New York City AI agents are moving into production, & more & more of them are built on open source. The question is no longer whether to use them, but what it takes to make them reliable once the demo is over. This meetup brings together builders, maintainers, & practitioners integrating AI agents into real codebases, CI/CD pipelines, internal developer platforms, cloud native infrastructure, & observability stacks. The evening focuses on the conversations that rarely fit into conference talks: what breaks at scale, how open source tools & standards shape agentic systems, where failure modes hide, & how teams build systems they can trust. Under the theme Open Source in Production, we will explore agentic code review, agent loops in CI/CD, developer platforms, eBPF-powered observability & security, & the role open source communities play in how production AI gets built. No vendor pitches. Just practical lessons from systems running in production. Agenda 5:00 PM Doors Open, Drinks & Networking5:30 PM Welcome & Opening Remarks5:40 PM [Speaker TBD], Qodo Dev Community6:05 PM Break, Food & Networking6:25 PM Panel: Agentic AI in the Wild7:15 PM Ryan Hamilton, Senior Developer & Community Lead, CircleCI AI Lab7:40 PM Closing Remarks7:45 PM Networking until 8:00 PM Speakers & Sessions [Speaker TBD], Qodo[Talk title TBD][Talk abstract TBD] Ryan Hamilton, Senior Developer & Community Lead, CircleCI AI LabOne Take: Engineering Agent Loops That Ship 100% Green PRs on the First PushMost teams optimizing AI-assisted development are focused on the wrong variable: prompting harder, adding rework, dumping larger failure logs into context. The real question isn't how to fix red PRs faster. It's how to stop producing them.Ryan shares findings from three connected Loop Lab experiments, each using the same controlled Snake game benchmark to isolate one variable at a time. Each one reveals something unexpected about where the real leverage lives in an agent loop, & what it means for cutting the cost of agentic development.Together, these experiments map a clear path from "rework is inevitable" to "rework is reserved for the unknowable." The result is a practical harness design that bakes a low Merge Efficiency Ratio (MER, the number of validation cycles it takes to get a change onto main) in from the start, & a new way to think about where validation belongs in the agent loop. Panel: Agentic AI in the WildWhat does it take to move AI agents from proof of concept into systems that operate reliably, & what role does open source play?Practitioners from across the stack will discuss context management, governance, open standards, observability, security, & what changes when agentic systems scale.Expect concrete lessons, not talking points. ModeratorDana Fine, Open Source & Developer Relations Manager, QodoDana leads open source programs & community initiatives at Qodo. She runs the GitHub User Group, CNCF local & GenAI communities, & the Bond AI meetup series. PanelistsBaruch Sadogursky, PortBaruch is a longtime developer advocate & a well-known speaker at developer conferences around the world. He co-authored Liquid Software & DevOps Tools for Java Developers, & focuses on developer productivity, DevOps, & how AI is changing the way software gets built & shipped. [Speaker TBD], Claude Community[Bio TBD] [Speaker TBD], NVIDIA[Bio TBD] Community PartnersAWS User Group NYC, CNCF NYC, Frontend NYC, WeMakeDevs, Bond AI, Qodo Dev Community Join the CommunityQodo Dev Community on Discord: [Discord invite link]Follow us on Meetup: [Meetup group link]

events.name: Solution Smithing - How To Raise & Give A Million Dollars
events.description: Join Anew & pop-up foundation The Haven Fund on October 20th for a brainstorming discussion on an urgent need: how to deploy resources efficiently & quickly towards the most pressing issues of our time. The Haven Fund, part of Anew's Fall 2025 cohort of Entrepreneurs in Residence, was born out of a desire to tackle an urgent problem - the immigration crackdown in NYC - by directing capital quickly to those organizations on the ground with the deepest knowledge of the issue. Since Lisa Cowan started this endeavor at the beginning of this year, it has distributed almost $1 million in funds to organizations throughout New York City, no strings attached. In an era of rolling, overlapping crises, we want to ask the audience & panelists, is this model replicable? If so, what would it take to create a template that anyone can use to tackle issues in their community & in different places? Join us as we together explore why this model was a success & how might The Haven Fund scale this model to address additional urgent issues. Panelists include: Iara Peng, Founder & CEO, JustFund, Emily Shechtman, Founder & Director, South Brooklyn Sanctuary, & Jennifer Ching, Executive Director, North Star Fund Anew is a gathering space & discovery center for social transformation located in NYC. We host interactive events & workshops, an accelerator program for nonprofits, & a retail lab featuring ethically-sourced coffee & gifts. The Haven Fund is a pop-up foundation that is raising $1 million in 1 year to support neighborhood-level immigration organizations in New York City. Lisa Cowan is the founder & Director of the Haven Fund. Formerly the Vice President of the Robert Sterling Clark Foundation, she is an organizer, weaver, writer & New Yorker.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Reality Of Data Centers In Space
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a small, curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for.Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data. No talking, just thinking. 45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: The Reality of Data Centers in SpaceStarcloud just raised $250M to build satellites that run AI workloads in orbit, joining Google's "Project Suncatcher" & a SpaceX effort in a race to solve AI's power problem by moving compute off the planet entirely. The pitch is compelling - unlimited solar power, no water usage - but basic questions about heat dissipation, launch costs, & maintenance remain mostly unanswered. We're decoding: Is space-based computing a real solution to AI's real estate & energy issues? Supporting questions: What would actually have to be true for orbital data centers to beat a terrestrial one on cost? Who's positioned to win this race - the well-funded startups (Starcloud), or the hyperscalers who already have the capital & infrastructure (Google, SpaceX)? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like.

events.name: AI Fraud & Death Of Resume - Restoring Algorithmic Trust
events.description: Conquer the AI job market battleground with elite CISO Dr. Rachel Levitch. Learn to restore algorithmic trust & secure your pipeline!  The 2026 job market is facing an unprecedented security & operational crisis. The recruitment landscape has evolved from a standard talent search into a high-stakes battleground of synthetic data. Candidates are deploying advanced, hyper-automated AI agents to mass-apply to hundreds of open roles instantly, reverse-engineer corporate Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS), auto-generate perfect skill matches, & deploy deepfake technology to bypass initial technical screenings. HR departments & engineering teams are drowning in a sea of algorithmic noise. As talent pipelines become flooded with AI-polished fraud, a staggering percentage of enterprise managers report that total trust in the inbound pipeline has completely eroded. In this high-stakes security & talent briefing, Dr. Rachel Levitch-seasoned Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) & founder of the Cognitive Institute-shifts the conversation from simple recruitment metrics to hard-line Systems Security & Information Integrity. We will move beyond the traditional interview structure to explore the mechanics of modern algorithmic fraud, the vulnerabilities of automated screening systems, & the implementation of secure identity & skill verification frameworks. This session provides human resource executives, tech founders, & venture capitalists with the exact tactical roadmap required to bypass synthetic candidate noise, protect personal data privacy, & restore institutional trust in a market-led crisis. Key Takeaways for Attendees: The AI Vulnerability Audit: A live technical breakdown of how 2026 AI-auto-apply bots actively breach, manipulate, & exploit corporate ATS filters.Detecting the Synthetic Candidate: Concrete, practical strategies for talent acquisition teams to identify AI-forged certifications, deepfake video setups, & automated resume stuffing.Rebuilding the Trust Chain: Transitioning your organization toward zero-trust recruitment frameworks, secure identity verification, & authentic human-sustainability metrics. Purchase Tickets At URL Below or See All Events here: https://www.eventbrite.com/o/121452823948

events.name: SOSV Deep Tech Summit
events.description: SOSV DEEP TECH SUMMIT Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. The producers of the Summit are SOSV's Ned Desmond, Ben Joffe, & Norm Amandi. More DetailsSOSV's mission is to invest in deep tech companies that advance human & planetary health, & embedded in building an 800+ company portfolio with a remarkable array of companies applying AI in the physical world. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

value.Most founders do not think about IP until it becomes a problem.A competitor files first.An investor flags a gap in diligence.A contractor owns code the company thought it owned.An AI tool events.name: Deal Flow - NYC's First VC Hackathon
events.description: Event DescriptionNew York is getting its first VC hackathon, & you're building for the people who write the checks. Deal Flow is a one-day, in-person hackathon hosted by localhost:nyc & VCLab. You get 9 hours to build working products for the real problems VCs face every day. Partners from NYC's top funds judge live, & the best teams leave with intros to those funds. Problem StatementVenture capital runs on spreadsheets, gut feel & endless inbox triage. Firms move billions of dollars with tools that haven't changed in a decade. Your challenge is to build software that helps VCs find better companies, make faster decisions & support their founders after the check clears. The Challenge ThemeSourcing: finding breakout founders before everyone else does Diligence: market maps, competitive analysis & memo drafting Portfolio ops: helping funds support their companies at scale LP reporting: making fund updates less painful & more useful Deal pipeline & CRM workflows that VCs will actually use What to Expect9 hours of focused building, 9 AM to 6 PM Real VC problems, with investors in the room to test your ideas against Teams of 4 Time to meet founders, engineers & investors from across NYC Live demos to a panel of VC judges at the end of the day Food & drinks all day PrizesTo Be Announced. JudgesAbeera Saeed is the Ventures Principal at Plug & Play, investing in Enterprise & AI B2B SaaS companies from Pre-Seed to Series A. Michael Barone - Associate at Everywhere Ventures, a global pre-seed venture capital firm. D. J. Patel - VC | 3x exited founder. Garrett Higgins is a skilled operator with experience running Finance & GTM Operations at high growth companies & an angel investor. He loves helping founders win & drive growth. Radhika Khandelwal builds AI agents for a living as a product leader at Wand AI, & she's spent years in the VC world seeing what makes startups stick. She'll want to see both slick code & a real business. Bettina Sosa is co-founder & CEO of Yaven, building a local-first AI workforce for independent businesses. Who Should AttendPre-seed & seed founders Engineers Builders who have felt the pain of fundraising firsthand Anyone curious about how venture capital actually works from the inside You don't need VC experience or a finished idea. Just show up ready to build. SponsorsSeedLegals is your one-stop legal platform from idea to Series A & beyond. Incorporate your Delaware C Corp or convert your to a C Corp, raise with SAFEs, manage your cap table, give stock options to your team, do a priced round, all on one platform, for way less than paying lawyers, with an amazing team to help. Hostslocalhost:nyc: Making NYC the biggest startup ecosystem in the world. Tracy Huang: VC Lab & CEO of Interlink IQ Olivia Iarmak - Researcher | Meta Reality Labs. ConnNext is a next-gen mobile app & community built for career growth. Visionbrew helps people be 2 places at once with 3D AI avatars. Pulse NYC AI - A community, incubator, & venture fund built for founders, researchers, & technologists shaping the future of AI in New York City.

events.name: Innovation in Public Mixer 5.0  Year End Capital
events.description: Edition 5.0. Theme, year end capital. The monthly room where founders, investors & operators actually get matched. Capped & curated. Everyone leaves with at least one named introduction & the framing for the conversation. November is when allocators are deploying what is left of the year & family offices are planning the next one. This edition leans toward the capital side of the network. Who we are. Propel Earth has run 100+ events & built a network of 36,000+ founders, investors, operators, & service providers across six continents. We are not an events company. We are an outcomes company that happens to use rooms. You bring the intent. We deliver the outcome. This is not a business card room. We cap it at 40-50 people & we curate it. Tell us what you are building & who you need when you register, & before you walk in we hand you at least one match: a specific person, plus the framing for the conversation. Everyone leaves having met someone who matters to what they are working on. You do not need to apply to the cohort to attend. This room is open. Tickets Early Access - $20. Limited, nearly gone.General Admission - $40.Free for Propel Private Network members. Dinner is highly encouraged - the kitchen at The Wilson is excellent. Come hungry & stay late. What Propel actually does for you 1  Innovation in Public - our GTM accelerator. For founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go-to-market: content, distribution, & more sales. Four weeks, twice a week, building in public, closing with a public showcase in front of the room. Applications open for the August cohort  Apply here 2  The Propel Private Network. Stop networking. Start getting matched. Every month we personally hand you three introductions chosen for what you need right now - someone who can pay you, hire you, or move your company forward. It works both ways: you go into the pool too. Founding rate $200/mo, first 25 members, locked for life  Claim a founding membership 3  Propel Community Coworking x Wayo Club. Come Wednesday night, then come back Thursday & build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, founded by Jason Malefakis. Wayo is a curated community workspace network where members work from premium venues alongside thoughtfully selected founders, operators, & consultants they can collaborate with, refer, hire, or do business with. Attendees typically report being 1.5 to 2x more productive than working from home or a cafe, & leave with 2 to 3 meaningful connections. Lunch is included. Register with us  Propel Community Coworking 1.0  Get a Wayo Community Workday membership  Join the Wayo Anytime waitlist 4  Featured Founder. events.name: NAB Creator Connect
events.description: ASUS ProArt Creator Connect: NYCWhere the Future of Creative Workflows Live in New YorkOctober 21, 2026 | 6:00-9:00 PM | Pier59 Studios, New York City Join ASUS ProArt & Pier59 Studios in New York City for an evening bringing together professionals from across film, television, broadcast, production, post-production, VFX & the wider creative industries to explore the technology shaping the future of creative workflows. And we're doing it somewhere pretty special. ProArt Creator Connect: NYC will take place inside Studio C at Pier59 Studios, one of North America's most technically advanced virtual production environments & an incredible opportunity to experience the technology, scale & capabilities of a cutting-edge New York production studio first-hand. With the industry in New York for NAB Show New York, we're bringing together the people creating great work with the people building, specifying, buying & deploying the technology behind it. We'll explore how new technology, AI & increasingly powerful professional tools are changing production & creative workflows, with an ASUS ProArt keynote, an industry fireside conversation, hands-on demonstrations & plenty of opportunity to experience the latest technology in a real production environment. Just as importantly, this is an opportunity to step away from the show floor, grab a drink & spend an evening with other people working across the industry in one of New York's most impressive production spaces. What to expectExperience Pier59's Studio C virtual production environment & get hands-on with the latest ASUS ProArt technology & professional creative workflows. Throughout the evening, you'll be able to explore technology designed for demanding production, post-production & creative environments, hear from industry experts about where professional workflows are heading, & meet people working across film & television production, broadcast, post, VFX, virtual production, AI & content creation. We'll look at the increasingly important role of AI & high-performance computing in professional creative environments, alongside the displays, systems & technologies being used throughout modern production pipelines. There'll be drinks, demonstrations & plenty of time for conversation throughout the evening. Whether you're responsible for creating the content, building the workflow or making the technology decisions behind it, Creator Connect: NYC is designed to bring those worlds together. Who should attend?ProArt Creator Connect: NYC is for professionals working across film, television, broadcast, production, post-production, VFX, virtual production, photography, design, AI & content creation. That includes filmmakers, editors, colorists, VFX artists, DPs, producers & creators, but also the people responsible for the technology behind their work: technical directors, production & post-production leaders, studio teams, technology executives, IT professionals, systems integrators, resellers & those responsible for specifying & investing in creative technology. If you're in New York for NAB Show New York, work within the city's production & post community, or simply want to see where professional creative technology is heading next, come & join us. It's also a rare opportunity to spend an evening inside Pier59's Studio C & experience one of North America's most advanced virtual production environments. Space is limited. Registration is free, but advance registration is required. Presented by ASUS ProArt & hosted with Pier59 Studios. By registering for this event, you agree that your registration details may be shared with ASUS Computer International (ACI) & participating event partners for event administration & relevant follow-up communications. If you would prefer not to have your details shared with event partners, you can opt out at any time by contacting us.

events.name: Six Math Essentials w/ Terence Tao
events.description: Book Launch & Conversation with Janna Levin Widely regarded as the world's greatest living mathematician, Fields Medalist Terence Tao approaches mathematics as a sublime art-a quiet, rigorous effort to map the hidden scaffolding of reality. To mark the publication of his first popular book, Six Math Essentials, join us for an evening with Tao in conversation with Pioneer Works Director of Sciences Janna Levin. Tracing the central pillars of his book-from algebra as abstraction & geometry beyond sight, to navigating uncertainty & the mathematics of change-they will reveal math not as obscure magic, but as a deeply creative, interconnected way of thinking. Often referred to as the Mozart of mathematics, Tao will also explore how AI is transforming his own practice, the frontier of research, & our collective future. Together, we will consider what becomes of human intuition & creativity when the tools of thought are no longer uniquely human-and whether the true beauty of math lies not in the answers we find, but in the human mind reaching for them. Tao will sign copies of Six Math Essentials following the conversation, with books available for purchase on site. (Unable to attend? Order a signed copy here.) Please note that seating is limited & will be available on a first-come, first-served basis.   About the speakersTerence Tao is an Australian-American professor of mathematics at UCLA whose work focuses primarily on harmonic analysis, partial differential equations, combinatorics, & analytic number theory. The recipient of a Fields Medal, a MacArthur Genius Grant, & a Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics, among many other accolades, he is one of the most decorated & prolific mathematicians working today. Tao is the author of several academic books including Solving Mathematical Problems: A Personal Perspective & Additive Combinatorics, as well as his first popular math book, Six Math Essentials. He lives in Los Angeles. Janna Levin is the Claire Tow Professor of physics & astronomy at Barnard College of Columbia University. A Guggenheim Fellow, she has contributed to our understanding of black holes, extra dimensions, & cosmology. She is the founding director of sciences at Pioneer Works & the founding editor-in-chief of the magazine Pioneer Works Broadcast. She often contributes to news, documentaries, & radio, including as the presenter of the NOVA feature Black Hole Apocalypse on PBS & as a contributor to CBS, CNN, BBC, & NBC. She has authored books on black holes & the universe-Black Hole Blues, How the Universe Got its Spots, & Black Hole Survival Guide-as well as a PEN award-winning novel, A Madman Dreams of Turing Machines. You can find her current writings in Higher Dimensions. This program is funded by the Simons Foundation International & administered by the Simons Foundation's Science, Society & Culture division.

events.name: Silicon Alley Hack | Build Cool Hardware
events.description: Everyone & their grandma is hosting a hackathon. This is the one where you build something physical. Silicon Alley Hack is a one-day, in-person sprint for builders who'd rather solder than ship a vibe-coded app. Microcontrollers. Sensors. Connected devices. Real hardware that runs in the real world & has to work when we plug it in on stage. Application-based. Teams of 4. Every team gets an STM32 development board & peripherals on arrival. Bring your laptop, your wits, & your soldering instincts.  The Problem StatementSoftware ate the world & then got bored. The interesting frontier moved back to atoms - robots that navigate a room, drones that deliver, sensors that make a physical space legible to a machine. All of it runs on constrained silicon, in real time, in places where the cloud is too slow, too far, or not there at all. So that's the terrain: edge intelligence. Machines that sense the world & act on it, on-device.  The Challenge ThemeThe sealed spec will live somewhere in here: Sense  decide  act, running on-device IoT, sensors, & connected devices Physical/digital interaction - things that move, respond, or react Anything that runs on hardware, not just in a browser Constraints you can count on: You'll be working on an STM32 development board & peripherals - get familiar before you show up It has to run live. Slides don't win. Working hardware wins. First team to solve it take the prizes. This is a race, not a showcase.  What to ExpectA live race-to-win challenge dropped at kickoff An STM32 dev kit + peripherals for every team, free 5 hours of focused build time Team formation on-site, or come with your crew Breakfast & lunch provided Exciting prizes for the winning A room full of NYC's hardware people - embedded engineers, drone builders, robotics founders, spatial-data folks  Schedule10:00 - 11:00 AM - Doors open. Breakfast, networking mixer, team formation. 11:00 - 11:30 AM - Partner intros, Root Access demo, challenge drop, rules & judging criteria. 11:30 AM - 4:30 PM - Build sprint. Lunch provided. Clock does not stop. 4:30 - 5:15 PM - Live hardware demos to the judges. 5:15 - 6:00 PM - Photos & Mixer.  PrizesA mix of cash, credits, & perks for the winning team. Sponsors are getting locked in - full breakdown announced before doors.  Who Should AttendEmbedded & firmware engineers Robotics, drone, & hardware builders EE / CE students & anyone who's ever blown up a dev board Founders building physical products Software engineers who want to get their hands on real silicon Anyone curious, ambitious, & hands-on  Sponsors[Sponsor TBD - reach out to somyag00@gmail.com to sponsor]  Hosts & PartnersSomya Gupta - The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Pulse NYC AI - A community, incubator, & venture fund built for founders, researchers, & technologists shaping the future of AI in New York City. ConnNext - A next-gen mobile app & community built for career growth.

events.name: An UNMUTED Book Club: The 100 Years War On Palestine
events.description: READING NOT REQUIRED - just be curious! Next up: Rashid Khalidi's The Hundred Years' War on Palestine, the 2020 book that argues the Israeli-Palestinian conflict isn't simply a tragic struggle between two peoples claiming the same land, but a century-long colonial campaign against Palestinians, backed first by Britain & later by the United States. Khalidi, a Palestinian-American historian at Columbia, tells the story through six turning points, beginning with the 1917 Balfour Declaration & moving through the creation of Israel, the wars that followed, & the failures of the peace process. Drawing on historical archives & his own family's experiences, he makes a provocative argument: that Palestinians have never been negotiating on equal terms, & that understanding the conflict as a dispute between two competing national movements obscures the enormous imbalance of power between them. It's a forceful challenge to conventional accounts of Israel's founding, Zionism, & America's role in the region, & one that raises uncomfortable questions about nationalism, colonialism, & self-determination. Show up even if you only got through a chunk. We'll talk about where Khalidi's account is most convincing, where it leaves out important context, whether Zionism is best understood as a colonial movement or a national liberation movement, & what his interpretation of the past means for the possibility of peace today. UNMUTED is a discussion forum for the politically curious. Accessible. Engaging. Social. Open-minded is the name of the game. Join your people.

events.name: Health2Tech
events.description: Health2Tech - a series of digital health events.Join us on October 22nd for an exclusive gathering that brings together the brightest minds in the digital health space. Hosted by Bailey Morgan & Alex Koshykov, this evening promises to be a confluence of innovation, inspiration, & invaluable networking.  Event Schedule: 5:30 PM - 6:00 Doors Open. Begin the evening with a warm welcome & a chance to settle in. 6:00 - 6:45: "Women's Health: Undervalued to Unavoidable" by Marissa Fayer & Bailey Morgan. 6:45 - 8:30 Networking. Connect, converse, & collaborate with peers driven by a common passion for advancing healthcare through technology.  About our Guest Speaker: Marissa Fayer has spent 25+ years operating at the intersection of technology & women's health. She's CEO of DeepLook Medical, an FDA-cleared AI diagnostics company focused on improving cancer detection for patients with dense breast tissue, & CEO/founder of HERhealthEQ, a nonprofit that's improved the health outcomes of 151,000+ women in 13 different countries by expanding access to medical devices & equipment. Marissa approaches women's health as infrastructure: when properly funded & built, it drives measurable returns across economies, workforces, & communities. Previously, Marissa held executive roles at Hologic, Olympus, Maquet Getinge, & has consulted for organizations including Pfizer, the National Institutes of Health (NIH), NuVasive, & Boehringer Ingelheim. She currently serves as an Investment Committee Member of GG Ventures, a 2026-2028 World Economic Forum (WEF) Technology Fellow, is an active founding member of Milken Institute's Women's Health Committee, & advisor to Welwaze Medical, Impact.51, & TechThrive Ventures. Marissa is the author of Undervalued to Unavoidable: Women's Health as Infrastructure. Marissa is a TEDx speaker (2019 TEDxLugano), has delivered keynotes at leading global healthcare conferences, & has been recognized as a Top 100 Women in Medtech & a Medtech Voice to Follow. Marissa can be found at www.marissafayer.com  Why Attend? Meet like-minded individuals who are actively shaping the health tech landscape. Share experiences, discuss challenges, & explore potential solutions with fellow founders. Learn from the journeys of other entrepreneurs, discover something new, seek advice, & perhaps find the mentor or partner you've been looking for.  Who Should Attend? Digital Health Founders at various stages of their startup journey. Healthcare Professionals who are passionate about health innovation. Investors looking to make impactful contributions to the digital health & medtech spaces.  Why This Event Is A Must? Hear from thought leaders & innovators in the digital health domain (at every event, we'll have a new set of speakers). Connect with peers, potential collaborators, & mentors. Participate in engaging Q&As & discussions that can spark new ideas & opportunities.  Venue Details: Great location in the heart of New York, equipped to foster conversations & connections. Venue details will be shared with registered attendees. Because of limited capacity, we won't be able to accommodate everyone, so please register whenever you are sure you can attend. Don't miss this chance to be part of a community that's driving the future of health tech. Reserve your spot now & join us in shaping the landscape of digital health for 2026 & beyond. Partners FINN Partners - more than an agency. Champions of change. FINN Partners is one of the fastest-growing global, independent marketing & communications agencies in the world, serving clients through a powerful combination of bold creativity, informed strategy, hands-on partnership, & highly specialized expertise. About the organizer Bailey Morgan, Based in Astoria, NYC, is a versatile healthtech leader who merges clinical expertise with business acumen to accelerate healthcare innovation & community impact. Having started her career as a medical speech language pathologist working within inpatient facilities throughout the boroughs of NYC, she saw firsthand how behind the healthcare tech ecosystem was compared to industries such as tech or finance. After leaving healthcare to move into the healthtech startup space, Bailey has since raised over $10M in capital, led several successful sales & marketing teams through go-to-market stages in both SaaS & CPG, & has closed over $2M in technology sales herself. She currently serves as Chief of Staff at Groth Pain & Spine, a pain management practice with 10+ locations & 40+ providers, where she leads the change management & technology integrations for the practices acquisitions. In addition to consulting with various healthcare technology companies, Bailey is a Director & the Treasurer for an NYC-based dementia-focused nonprofit that employs individuals living with dementia & supports families & caregivers. Alex Koshykov is a co-founder of BeKey & a digital health expert who constantly shares news, introduces promising technologies, & promotes secure software & hardware for the healthcare industry on his YouTube channel. Additionally to that, he is a co-founder of YODD, a medical device startup. Additional Information By signing up, your email will be automatically added to the Health2Tech newsletter with news & upcoming events - but don't worry, we won't flood your inbox! ;) Also, just a note that this event might be photographed or filmed. If we do capture some moments, Health2Tech may use the photos or videos for marketing & communication purposes. By registering, you're giving us the thumbs up for using your image for these reasons.

events.name: Wind-Win Startup Showdown
events.description: Step into the Future of Ocean Renewables:  An Electrifying Evening with the 2026 Offshore Wind Innovation Hub Innovator Cohort!The 4th annual Wind-Win Startup Showdown offers a pitch experience like no other, spotlighting cutting-edge technology breakthroughs to transform the future of ocean renewables. This is a special year for us: the program set a record high: 118 applications & the strongest competition reviewers have seen to date. In 2026, we also drew in a more diverse cohort than ever before by broadening this year's technology scope  a 123% increase in application numbers compared to last year's, reflecting the parallel growth in industry demand for novel solutions needed in the market.Presented by the Offshore Wind Innovation Hub, this networking & pitch event brings together stakeholders across the climate landscapeinvestors, founders, academia, industry, & thought leadersfor an evening of connection, collaboration, & celebration.Come see it for yourself! Join us to engage with leading innovators tackling climates most complex challenges with bold, next-generation solutions.Refreshments & light hors d'oeuvres will be provided.AgendaDoors OpenKeynote + Welcome RemarksAlso on stage:  Tone Sndergaard, Director, Offshore Wind Innovation Hub at NYU Tandon Urban Future LabInnovator Lightning Pitches by the 2026 CohortEach of our Offshore Wind Innovation Hub partners has sent their most experienced innovation experts to provide feedback for each of the selected cohort companies.Sam Jung, SVP, Green Economy, New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYC EDC)Lyndie Hice-Dunton, Executive Director, National Offshore Wind Research & Development Consortium (NOWRDC)Robert Fenton, Head of Americas Generation Procurement, rstedStephan Kremers, Senior Technical Project Manager, VestasFireside Chat on Dual-Use Technology AdaptationNetworking & RefreshmentsMeet our 2026 FinalistsBlue Ocean Transfers Group (BOT) (New York, US) - Multipurpose, hybrid electric support vessel enabling maritime decarbonization.Bubble Robotics (California, US) - Resident fleet of autonomous underwater robots monitoring offshore infrastructure.Clema (New York, US) - Thermoelectric cooling vest for workers in extreme heat.Fleet Robotics (Massachusetts, US) - Data insights powered by submersible, autonomous cleaning & inspection robots.Hefring Marine (Iceland) - Intelligence platform combining onboard hardware with software to optimize marine operations.HiFIT USA (New York, US) - Impact treatment welding to enable life extension & lighter structures.NeuralX (California, US) - Underwater video & computer vision for fisheries monitoring & ecological data.Sail GTX (New York, US) - Platform for smarter customs workflows for offshore wind components.TMA The Hazardous Goods Companion (Germany) - RFID & AIoT inventory visibility & predictive inventory management solution.Tree Composites (The Netherlands) - Composite joints for offshore support structure to realise material & manufacturing optimization.Vital Ocean (Oregon, US) - Intelligence platform combining ocean data, marine environment, & decision interface.Stay tuned in the next few weeks on our website & LinkedIn for updates on our selected cohort!Innovation in FocusOur 2026 cohort takes the stage to pitch ocean & maritimes most promising technologies. This year's lineup features innovations spanning ports, O&M, environmental monitoring & coexistence, workforce development, installation, construction, & commissioning, maritime applications, among others. The scope doesn't just stop there. The majority of this year's solutions are dual-use, carrying relevance across adjacent industries & global markets, a reflection of just how far the blue economy reaches.Marking the official launch of the 2026 Innovator program, this event offers a unique chance to connect directly with the founders behind these ready-to-scale solutions. Explore their real-world impact, uncover new business opportunities, & spark the kind of strategic partnerships that move ideas forward.The Offshore Wind Innovation Hub Innovator ProgramA world-class program open to global offshore wind innovators. Building on three successful cohorts, this eight-month intensive program provides unparalleled support for innovators looking to develop novel technology & advance commercialization in New York & beyond.The Offshore Wind Innovation Hub is an initiative led by Urban Future Lab at NYU Tandon School of Engineering & the National Offshore Wind R&D Consortium (NOWRDC) in collaboration with the New York State Research & Development Authority (NYSERDA) & New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYC EDC).The Innovator program is also supported by industry partners Equinor, rsted, & Vestas.

events.name: Fandom, Cities & Psychology Of Collective Emotion
events.description: Fandom, Cities, & the Psychology of Collective Emotion Why do sports fans feel so deeply connected to teams, cities, & even complete strangers? This talk explores the science of fandom & the social psychology that transforms spectators into communities. Drawing on research in social identity, belonging, collective emotion, & fan behavior, this talk examines how rituals, rivalries, & shared experiences turn they into we. From a Knicks championship transforming the emotional temperature of New York City to the 2026 FIFA World Cup activating cities around the globe, the talk considers how sport mega-events create collective identity-and whether fandom functions as social infrastructure in an increasingly disconnected world. SpeakerGina Antoniello, Clinical Assistant Professor & Director, Women's Sport Collective, NYU SPS Preston Robert Tisch Institute for Global Sport; Faculty Athletics Representative, NYU

events.name: Zenity AI Agent Security Summit
events.description: Shape the Future of AI Security AI agents are no longer novelties for future consideration - they're scaling across industries & borders at breakneck pace today, bringing with them a security landscape that grows continuously ambiguous. Don't just witness the conversation around agentic security - contribute to it. The AI Agent Security Summit returns to four international cities in 2026. Save your spot now. What You'll LearnWith AI agents becoming integral to many workflows, they introduce unprecedented challenges. This summit navigates the uncharted territories of AI agents with discussions around:  Real RisksLearn how attackers exploit AI Agents & what you need to change in your security strategy to stay ahead.  Deconstructing AI AgentsDive deep into adversarial tactics, prompt manipulation, & unintended behaviors that can turn trusted systems into threats.  Defense Beyond the PerimeterDiscover new defense methods that monitor behavior, detect deviations in intent, & break malicious automation. After launching the AI Agent Security Summit in New York City & San Francisco in 2025, we're taking the Summit global - expanding to NYC, San Francisco, London, & Asia. Each Summit will feature local speakers, fresh content, & original research highlighting emerging vulnerabilities & attack pathways in AI agents. We invite researchers & practitioners to share new findings, tools, & firsthand experiences exploring the security challenges & risks that emerge as AI agents are developed & adopted in enterprise environments.
