events.name: Fandom, Cities & Psychology Of Collective Emotion
events.description: Fandom, Cities, & the Psychology of Collective Emotion Why do sports fans feel so deeply connected to teams, cities, & even complete strangers? This talk explores the science of fandom & the social psychology that transforms spectators into communities. Drawing on research in social identity, belonging, collective emotion, & fan behavior, this talk examines how rituals, rivalries, & shared experiences turn they into we. From a Knicks championship transforming the emotional temperature of New York City to the 2026 FIFA World Cup activating cities around the globe, the talk considers how sport mega-events create collective identity-and whether fandom functions as social infrastructure in an increasingly disconnected world. SpeakerGina Antoniello, Clinical Assistant Professor & Director, Women's Sport Collective, NYU SPS Preston Robert Tisch Institute for Global Sport; Faculty Athletics Representative, NYU

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Reality Of Data Centers In Space
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a small, curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for.Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data. No talking, just thinking. 45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: The Reality of Data Centers in SpaceStarcloud just raised $250M to build satellites that run AI workloads in orbit, joining Google's "Project Suncatcher" & a SpaceX effort in a race to solve AI's power problem by moving compute off the planet entirely. The pitch is compelling - unlimited solar power, no water usage - but basic questions about heat dissipation, launch costs, & maintenance remain mostly unanswered. We're decoding: Is space-based computing a real solution to AI's real estate & energy issues? Supporting questions: What would actually have to be true for orbital data centers to beat a terrestrial one on cost? Who's positioned to win this race - the well-funded startups (Starcloud), or the hyperscalers who already have the capital & infrastructure (Google, SpaceX)? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like.

Today the portfolio spans institutions, edtech, real estate, & a tech venture studio, with reach across 20+ countries & no plans to slow down.  Triet Leminh: Principal, LMT Partners: Lawyer, founder, & investor backing pre-seed to Series A founders building in enterprise & regulated industries. Writing $200K-$300K checks.  Andrew Antar (General Partner, AG Venture Capital): A generalist fund backing extraordinary founders, sector agnostic. Invests in automation, robotics, data centers & applied AI.  Shilpi Nayak: (Founder & General Partner, 434 VC): Invests in early-stage technical founders across AI, infrastructure, physical AI & emerging technology. She is also the founder of House of 434, a community bringing together founders, investors & industry leaders.  Pranav Jajapur (Co-Founder, ZERON Ventures): ZERON is an early-stage venture fund with an execution platform behind it, backing real-world technology, AI, healthcare, deep tech & climate companies building in the physical world, inside biology. Pre-seed through Series A with core deployment at seed, writing $400K-$500k checks. Preferred focus is institutionally-anchored AI: structural research relationships at academic institutions, spinouts, & founder-led research programs. Fund I in formation. Appetizers & dessert are shared & open to everyone; each will get one entre. The format is intentionally part standing, part seated so you can enjoy incredible food without being anchored to a single table or a single conversation. Why we do this Our intent is simple: bring good, smart humans together, put active investors in the same room as incredible founders. Intentional community has been lost. We're rebuilding it.

events.description: Edition 5.0. Theme, year end capital. The monthly room where founders, investors & operators actually get matched. Capped & curated. Everyone leaves with at least one named introduction & the framing for the conversation. November is when allocators are deploying what is left of the year & family offices are planning the next one. This edition leans toward the capital side of the network. Who we are. Propel Earth has run 100+ events & built a network of 36,000+ founders, investors, operators, & service providers across six continents. We are not an events company. We are an outcomes company that happens to use rooms. You bring the intent. We deliver the outcome. This is not a business card room. We cap it at 40-50 people & we curate it. Tell us what you are building & who you need when you register, & before you walk in we hand you at least one match: a specific person, plus the framing for the conversation. Everyone leaves having met someone who matters to what they are working on. You do not need to apply to the cohort to attend. This room is open. Tickets Early Access - $20. Limited, nearly gone.General Admission - $40.Free for Propel Private Network members. Dinner is highly encouraged - the kitchen at The Wilson is excellent. Come hungry & stay late. What Propel actually does for you 1  Innovation in Public - our GTM accelerator. For founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go-to-market: content, distribution, & more sales. Four weeks, twice a week, building in public, closing with a public showcase in front of the room. Applications open for the August cohort  Apply here 2  The Propel Private Network. Stop networking. Start getting matched. Every month we personally hand you three introductions chosen for what you need right now - someone who can pay you, hire you, or move your company forward. It works both ways: you go into the pool too. Founding rate $200/mo, first 25 members, locked for life  Claim a founding membership 3  Propel Community Coworking x Wayo Club. Come Wednesday night, then come back Thursday & build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, founded by Jason Malefakis. Wayo is a curated community workspace network where members work from premium venues alongside thoughtfully selected founders, operators, & consultants they can collaborate with, refer, hire, or do business with. Attendees typically report being 1.5 to 2x more productive than working from home or a cafe, & leave with 2 to 3 meaningful connections. Lunch is included. Founders x Investors Night at PhD Lounge, the Funders x Founders High Line Walk, the Harvard Club Investment Dinner, & the NYTW Pitch Competition with 800+ registrations. Every monthly mixer does the same thing at a smaller scale, which is why we cap the room & match you before you arrive. Founders & Service Providers. You tell us what you need & we match you to someone vetted who does it. Legal, tax, engineering, design, growth, operations. Our Founders Meet Providers rooms exist for exactly this, & the Propel Marketplace runs it year round. Featured provider this month is Moshe Cohen, CPA, offering a 30 minute startup tax & finance session for $120. Book a session or browse the marketplace Hiring & Talent. Our Tech Job Fair & Developer Job Fair each brought over 150 engineers & operators into the room. The ConnNext App Launch Party pulled 475 registrations, the largest event we have ever run. BECOMEFAMOUS.AI pulled 222. If you are launching something & you need a room, reply to this & we will build it. Capital & Family Office. The capital side of the network. Our Private Markets Discussion Panel drew 280 registrations & Family Office Crypto with Forum Pay brought allocators into the room. These are smaller rooms with higher stakes. See the next one Masterclasses & Info Sessions. Free, online, & taught by specialists who actually do the work. Our Social Impact Cohort Info Session drew 297 registrations. TRIIBE TALK on branding drew 157. Tax, legal, fundraising, & go to market, taught by operators. See the calendar The GTM Accelerator. Four weeks for founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go to market help: content, distribution, & more sales. You get a dedicated BDR, a custom digital asset kit, & a public showcase in front of the room. Our last cohort presented at Demo Day to 35+ investors. August applications are open & you can see how we represented the last cohort The Social Rooms. Not everything is a pitch. Foundersgiving Party & Pitch Roast drew 381 people. LABYRINTH at Hotel Chelsea drew 309. Above Fridays Rooftop Networking, Holiday Chemistry Night, & Bowling & Business. These are the rooms where relationships actually form, & they are the reason the other eight verticals work. Community Coworking. events.description: A casual, pay-your-own-way networking event designed for professionals to connect, share ideas, & build lasting relationships across the broader business & technology ecosystem. Meet fellow professionals, expand your network, & enjoy a relaxed evening together. Food & beverages are available for individual purchase. Who Attends: Founders & startups PR & Agency teams Venture Capitalists Consultants Finance professionals Content & social media marketers Marketing technology professionals Attendance is limited to help keep conversations meaningful, so please apply for a spot. We look forward to meeting you! About Our Meet Ups: Our Meet Ups are relaxed, industry-agnostic gatherings built for professionals who want to unplug from the standard corporate routine & connect on a human level. Whether you are looking to exchange fresh perspectives, brainstorm new concepts, or simply meet peers navigating similar spaces, this environment is designed for open-ended conversation & organic relationship-building. What It Is: An open, welcoming community space to meet new connections. An opportunity to exchange industry perspectives & uncover unexpected collaborations. A low-pressure, welcoming atmosphere with no formal agenda or mandatory pitches. What It Isn't: RTM Nexus Meet Up is not a curated buyer/seller event & is not structured around guaranteed access to a specific target audience, vertical, company type, or decision-maker profile (ICP). Looking for something more targeted? If you need to connect with a specific niche-such as retail, fashion, beauty, CPG, or enterprise brand leaders-check out our "Retail Leaders Receptions" & "Nexus Mixers" instead. Those events are intentionally curated & sponsored around targeted audiences to provide a more focused networking experience.

events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: Did Maha Maha?
events.description: Has the MAHA movement made Americans healthier than the establishment? Americans spend more on healthcare than anyone else in the world. Yet we have soaring rates of obesity, diabetes, & chronic disease. So is the medical establishment failing us? And is MAHA actually doing any better? RFK's MAHA movement has put ultra-processed foods, environmental toxins, & chronic disease at the center of the national conversation. Supporters say it's finally challenging a healthcare system that profits from treating illness instead of preventing it. Critics say it's undermining trust in vaccines, established science, & the institutions responsible for keeping Americans healthy. So who's right? Is MAHA forcing a long-overdue reckoning with a broken healthcare system? Or is it replacing imperfect science with something far more dangerous? Kerry Semle is a biomedical engineer, former medical technology executive, & women's health advocate with 15 years of experience in medical devices & diagnostics. She's advocated for greater investment in women's health research & improved access to care. Emily Kaplan is the CEO & co-founder of the Broken Science Initiative, an organization challenging the scientific establishment & questioning how medical research is conducted, evaluated, & trusted. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

events.name: OverdriveAI Summit
events.description: Overdrive AIHosted by TechUnited:NJ, creators of Propelify, heralded by Forbes as the "SXSW of the Northeast," OverdriveAI is back, & this year it's a debate. The hottest topics in AI, argued live, both sides on stage. Jobs, energy, education, & more. Sharp thinkers go head to head, you hear the case for & against, & you decide where you land. Taking place this year at the Newark Museum of Art, where tech & culture share a roof, OverdriveAI brings together founders, operators, investors, & researchers from across the Northeast for a day built around one idea: the biggest questions in AI don't have easy answers, so let's actually argue about them. TICKETS ARE NOW LIVE!EXPLORE THE FULL OVERDRIVEAI EXPERIENCE Community AI TrainingHands-on morning AI training at EqualSpace designed for all experience levels. No prior AI experience required. Reserve Your Spot Executive AI TrainingA focused, practical AI training designed for executives & business leaders ready to better understand & apply AI within their organizations. Reserve Your Spot Pitch Roast LiveStartups pitch. Comedians roast. Everyone wins. Close out OverdriveAI with an evening of bold ideas, founder pitches, comedy, & connection. Reserve Your Spot   What to Expect Community AI Training A hands-on morning (10a-12p ET) AI training at EqualSpace designed for all experience levels. Come ready to learn, explore, & put AI into practice. No prior experience required. Executive AI Training Turn AI into practical business advantage. Start your morning with a focused AI training session designed for executives, business leaders, & decision-makers navigating the rapidly evolving AI landscape. This interactive session will explore practical ways leaders can better understand, evaluate, & apply AI within their organizations helping you move from conversation to action. The AI Debates The main event at the Newark Museum of Art. Will AI take your job or grow the economy? Who pays for AI's energy appetite? Does AI belong in the classroom? Can you still trust what you see? Startup demos will be featured between rounds & the afternoon will roll into TechUnited:NJ Birthday Party! Final topics & speakers are still being locked in, ticket holders hear every name first. Here's what's on the table so far: AI takes jobs vs. AI grows the economy - does automation erase more work than it creates? Is AI raising your energy bill? - the data center buildout is reshaping the grid, & New Jersey's in the middle of it. Does AI belong in the classroom? - a tutor for every student, or the end of learning how to think? Is it time for universal basic income? - if productivity keeps compounding, someone decides where the gains go. Can we handle deepfakes? - synthetic media's getting cheap & convincing, what's the real defense? Got a debate we missed? Suggest it, & if it makes the stage, you'll know it was yours. Live debates. Experts, opposing sides of one question, no hedging.Hot takes. Short, sharp presentations from speakers with a strong point of view.Networking. 300+ founders, researchers, & investors in one room, this year in a new venue built for it. Pitch Roast Live Closing the night at Newark Culture Club Close with startup pitches & a high-energy evening experience. Four founders pitch, three comedians & two investors roast. One walks out a winner! Last Year, at Nokia Bell Labs Speakers joined us from OpenAI, IBM, CoreWeave, Verizon, Perplexity, Nokia Bell Labs, BetterFutureLabs, NJEDA, & the NJ AI Hub. 16 speakers, 300+ attendees, a packed house. This year's lineup is coming together now, & it's bigger. OverdriveAI is one of many events TechUnited:NJ runs for its 13,000+ member community, from AI Demo Night to Propelify. Inquire about membership to hear about what's next. TechUnited:NJ members receive complimentary admission to OverdriveAI as part of their membership. Not a member yet? Join TechUnited:NJ to unlock complimentary access to OverdriveAI, along with year-round member benefits & opportunities to connect with New Jersey's innovation community.

events.name: Solution Smithing - How To Raise & Give A Million Dollars
events.description: Join Anew & pop-up foundation The Haven Fund on October 20th for a brainstorming discussion on an urgent need: how to deploy resources efficiently & quickly towards the most pressing issues of our time. The Haven Fund, part of Anew's Fall 2025 cohort of Entrepreneurs in Residence, was born out of a desire to tackle an urgent problem - the immigration crackdown in NYC - by directing capital quickly to those organizations on the ground with the deepest knowledge of the issue. Since Lisa Cowan started this endeavor at the beginning of this year, it has distributed almost $1 million in funds to organizations throughout New York City, no strings attached. In an era of rolling, overlapping crises, we want to ask the audience & panelists, is this model replicable? If so, what would it take to create a template that anyone can use to tackle issues in their community & in different places? Join us as we together explore why this model was a success & how might The Haven Fund scale this model to address additional urgent issues. Panelists include: Iara Peng, Founder & CEO, JustFund, Emily Shechtman, Founder & Director, South Brooklyn Sanctuary, & Jennifer Ching, Executive Director, North Star Fund Anew is a gathering space & discovery center for social transformation located in NYC. We host interactive events & workshops, an accelerator program for nonprofits, & a retail lab featuring ethically-sourced coffee & gifts. The Haven Fund is a pop-up foundation that is raising $1 million in 1 year to support neighborhood-level immigration organizations in New York City. Lisa Cowan is the founder & Director of the Haven Fund. Formerly the Vice President of the Robert Sterling Clark Foundation, she is an organizer, weaver, writer & New Yorker.

events.description: SOSV DEEP TECH SUMMIT Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. The producers of the Summit are SOSV's Ned Desmond, Ben Joffe, & Norm Amandi. More DetailsSOSV's mission is to invest in deep tech companies that advance human & planetary health, & embedded in building an 800+ company portfolio with a remarkable array of companies applying AI in the physical world. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Build Your Creative Operating System
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back - In Person at Salesforce We're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City & sponsored by Boldforce. This Month We Present...Build Your Creative Operating SystemBuild a personalized AI workflow that supports your entire creative process-from capturing ideas to publishing finished work-so you're never starting from scratch. Most of us don't have an idea problem. We have a system problem. Ideas live in our Notes app. Research is scattered across browser tabs. Drafts are hiding in Google Docs. Inspiration gets screenshotted & forgotten. And every new project somehow feels like we're starting all over again. What if your creative process actually remembered how you work? At this month's AI & The Culture meetup, we're exploring how to build your own Creative Operating System-a personalized workflow that uses AI to help you capture ideas, organize knowledge, research, create, refine, & publish your work. Instead of collecting more AI tools, we'll focus on connecting the ones that actually support your process. Together we'll explore:  How to map your creative process from idea to finished work  Ways to capture & organize ideas so they don't disappear into the digital abyss  How AI can help you research, brainstorm, draft, edit, & refine your work  Building a personal knowledge base that makes past ideas & research useful again  How to connect AI tools into repeatable workflows instead of using them one at a time  Where automation can save time-and where your human judgment should stay firmly in the driver's seat  How to create a system that gets smarter & more useful the more you use it The goal isn't to automate your creativity. It's to build the infrastructure around your creativity so you have more time & energy for the work only you can do. Expect a welcoming room filled with creators, technologists, educators, founders, artists, & curious minds ready to rethink how we organize & support our creative lives. Who Should Attend?  Creators & content makers  Filmmakers, writers, artists, & storytellers  Educators & community builders  Entrepreneurs, founders, & solopreneurs  Marketers, strategists, & creative professionals  Technologists & AI enthusiasts  Anyone with too many ideas, too many tabs, & not enough systems  Whether your creative process is already organized or currently held together by screenshots, open tabs, & vibes, you're welcome here. Come Ready to Build This won't be a sit-back-and-scroll kind of evening. Bring your laptop, something to write with, & a mindset ready to learn, experiment, & share. We'll be exploring ideas, tools, & workflows you can begin applying to your own creative process.  Bring your laptop  Bring a notebook or something to take notes with  Bring your curiosity & questions Come ready to learn. Come ready to contribute. Come ready to build. About AI & The Culture AI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, & culture. Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams & King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, & culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, & community. We're building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI. This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture - grounded in community, focused on real-world use, & centered on learning together in the room. Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Let's build - together.  About Your Hosts Shirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, & co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, & creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, & real-world execution. About King Willonius King Willonius is a creative technologist & cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, & creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, & community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable & useful - especially for creatives & innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm.  Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio) #AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: The AI-ndustrial Revolution?
events.description: In the next five years, will AI make the average American's life better or worse? Companies are spending billions on AI. But is it actually making the economy better? And more importantly, will it make the economy better FOR YOU? Right now, the evidence is weird. Only 1 in 8 CEOs says AI is both increasing revenue & cutting costs. At the same time, 77% of CEOs say AI has been overhyped so far-but may actually be underhyped over the next decade. So what happens next? A productivity boom that creates new industries & better jobs? Or enormous investment, displaced workers, & technology that never delivers enough value to justify the hype? Daniel Di Martino, an economist & Fellow at the Manhattan Institute, studies economic growth, labor markets, & the policies that drive American competitiveness. Dr. Cecilia Dones is a Columbia lecturer & longtime data & AI executive who works with organizations trying to turn massive AI investments into actual business value. Luke Strathmann, our opener, runs the funniest (and only) Economics comedy show in NYC. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

events.name: Spatial Analytics w/ Python
events.description: Join PyData NYC on October 27th at 6:30 PM for an evening exploring geospatial data science with Python, featuring Brendan Collins, Founder & CTO at Makepath & creator of Xarray-Spatial! Discover how Python can transform spatial data into powerful insights, from terrain analysis & hydrology to scalable CPU- & GPU-accelerated computing. Please bring your  to follow along & sign up using your official government-issued name.  Pizza & drinks will be provided - Thank you, Makepath! Agenda xarray-spatial: In & Out of the Raster-verseSpeaker: Brendan Collins (Founder & CTO at Makepath)Spatial data comes in many shapes & sizes, but some of the most powerful spatial analysis techniques begin by viewing the world as a grid.Led by the library's creator & maintainer, this talk introduces Xarray-Spatial, an open-source Python library for scalable raster analysis with CPU & GPU acceleration.We'll learn how to enter the Raster-verse by bringing spatial data into Xarray, explore the Raster-verse using algorithms for terrain analysis, hydrology, proximity, & more, & escape the Raster-verse through techniques like zonal statistics & polygonization.Finally, we'll discuss contributing to the Raster-verse, sharing lessons from maintaining Xarray-Spatial & how AI-augmented development is transforming open-source contributions, code quality, & scientific software engineering.Whether you're a GIS practitioner, data scientist, or Python developer, you'll leave with practical ideas for working with spatial data & contributing to open source.  About the SpeakerBrendan Collins is the Founder & CTO of Makepath, where he helps early-stage startups & Fortune 500 engineering teams realize their product ambitions.A former employee of Anaconda, Brendan has spent the past decade applying PyData technologies, including NumPy, Xarray, & Numba, to engineering challenges across the public, private, & nonprofit sectors.When not writing in the third person, Brendan enjoys swimming, playing the banjo, & gardening.  NetworkingConnect with fellow data enthusiasts, Python developers, researchers, & community leaders. Build meaningful connections, exchange ideas, & explore opportunities for collaboration.

events.name: Vibecoding 101
events.description: A 4-week scaffolded, hands-on introduction to vibecoding for beginners.Vibecoding, or AI-assisted software development, is the practice of guiding coding agents to translate your ideas into working software - without writing code yourself. We see vibecoding as 4 different product skills in a trench coat. While they may not write code, effective vibecoders mobilize concepts & workflows across software engineering, design, quality assurance, & product management. This course is a scaffolded, hands-on introduction to the fundamental skills & concepts required for a sustainable vibecoding practice. Students will learn through a combination of short lectures, applied exercises, personalized feedback, & demos to peers. We begin by working with coding agents in a multiplayer environment designed for beginners. We will create interactive frontends, learn the basics of the terminal, build integrations with APIs, & create stateful, full-stack applications with a database & user authentication. By the end of the course, students will transition to state-of-the-art coding agents installed on their personal machines, which they will use to build & deploy a working prototype to the web. SyllabusSession 1: Coding agents & frontends We introduce the course & core concepts of vibecoding. We introduce a basic taxonomy of web architecture. Students practice creating basic interactive frontends. Session 2: CLIs, APIs, & the terminal We cover core backend & data concepts. We gently introduce the terminal. Students practice writing simple CLI programs, & integrating with an API. Session 3: Stateful full-stack applications We cover databases & user authentication; students build a full stack app. Session 4: Deployment & demos The final session covers deployment. Students demo their prototypes for the class. Learning OutcomesAcquire core vocabulary & mental models for software development. Prompt coding agents to create frontends, API integrations, & stateful applications. Be able to translate your ideas into working prototypes using AI. Practice presenting your product ideas to peers & colleagues. ResourcesThis new world of ours rewards being a dilettante with a vague mental map of vast territories.- Ted Underwood There is a new kind of coding I call vibecoding,' where you fully give in to the vibes, embrace exponentials, & forget that the code even exists. It's possible because the LLMs (e.g. Cursor Composer w Sonnet) are getting too good it's not really coding - I just see stuff, say stuff, run stuff, & copy paste stuff, & it mostly works.- Andrej Karpathy Slow is smooth, & smooth is fast.- Anonymous ScholarshipIndex scholarships are designed to benefit members of our community who do not have expendable cash to pay for the course, & those for whom the class price is not accessible. These need-based scholarships will go to the candidates who best demonstrate why they should be chosen for the free spot to our class based on the following criteria: Belong to groups that are traditionally underrepresented in the graphic design & creative industries Do not have jobs that would pay for these courses as professional development Cannot independently afford the class at list price Share our value of intentional community The number of selected applicants chosen is subject to the discretion of Index & the instructor, but every course will select at least one. Apply for a scholarship here. Applications close October 20th. Instructor Bio Bill Roberts is an independent technologist based in Brooklyn. Drawn to socially beneficial uses of technology, he has 10 years of software engineering experience on teams spanning healthcare, climate, politics, & education. He runs Legible Labs, a product studio that helps clients design & build AI applications. As a research engineer, he has coauthored papers in peer-reviewed journals & conferences that empirically evaluate the capabilities of AI in educational settings. Bill holds a BA in Computer Science & Sociology from Columbia University.   Refunds We get that things come up, but we rely on headcounts to make our programs viable. If you request a refund... More than 4 weeks before the program begins  100% refundMore than 2 weeks before the program begins  50% refundFewer than 2 weeks before the program begins  No refund Thanks for understanding & for supporting our ability to provide cool offerings through your purchase. Media Release Clause By attending this event, you consent to being photographed, filmed, or recorded, & grant Index Space permission to use this content for promotional or informational purposes.

events.name: Business Funding - An International Perspective
events.description: Every stage of growing a business is a funding decision, even when it doesn't feel like one. How you pay for the next market, the next hire, the next acquisition quietly shapes what the business is worth years later, & who you can sell it to. Across the Atlantic, the options multiply & the advice gets thinner. During the evening, hear from speakers across the corporate lifecycle, sharing their different funding, expansion & exit stories, so you leave with greater insight & awareness of the opportunities, & the pitfalls to avoid. Designed for international founders & business executives planning to grow in New York City, the discussion will cover the advantages, tradeoffs, & tactics involved in raising capital from VC & PE sources.  Speakers Dan Jaeck is a Principal at Crane VC, based between New York & London, where he partners with founders building transformational software companies.Before joining Crane, he spent four years at Eniac Ventures in NYC, investing in AI application-layer & infrastructure companies. Prior to Eniac, Dan began his career at Goldman Sachs in London on the Emerging Market Equities desk. Joel Goschalk is a Senior Director at Dundon Advisers, advising middle-market companies on recapitalizations, restructurings & credit. He started as a London insolvency practitioner, co-founded & scaled a UK litigation funding & private equity business (Cavendish IP Solutions), & has spent over a decade as COO of a family office, advising on fundraising rounds, fund formation across the UK, US & offshore, & cross-border expansion.  Co-host: The Transatlantic Innovation Hub, is New York's launch pad for Italian & European companies, to help them successfully enter & scale in the U.S. market. Located in the heart of Manhattan, TIH serves as a landing pad for innovation ecosystems, providing companies with both a physical presence in New York & a structured set of market access services to accelerate their U.S. expansion. The Knowledge Shop is the founder community in NYC. We are industry & stage agnostic, helping not just startups grow, but supporting the founders building them.  Founding Partner: Sabre Integrated has been providing commercial security systems in NYC since 2000.From access control & video surveillance to fully integrated security systems, they design, install & support your business every step of the way  Charity Partner: The St George's Society of New York, provides life-changing support to immigrants from Britain & the Commonwealth in New York. Established in 1770, we're the second-oldest charity in the city. We hold events year round - join us for Pancake day   Find even more Tech events at: www.foundereventsnyc.com

events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: AI & China
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In July, a Chinese lab you'd probably never heard of published Kimi K3: 2.8 trillion parameters, billed as the largest open model on earth, weights posted free on Hugging Face for anyone to download. It's one of four Chinese labs that spent the last year closing the gap with the American frontier, then giving the result away. Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi. Four of the five most-used open models in the world now come out of Beijing, & American developers are running them inside hospitals, law firms, & startups because they're the cheapest, fastest tools available. No API someone in Washington controls. No off switch. Just download & go. One camp says a model is just math. Open weights run on a consumer's machine, the code is right there to inspect, & cutting Americans off from the best tools on the planet is how you lose a technology race. The other camp says the giveaway is the strategy. China seeds the world's infrastructure with their standards, their defaults, their assumptions, & the dependency follows once switching costs become unbeatable. So: should Americans be allowed to build on Chinese open-weight models or is this the new Cold War's Monkey's Paw? Arguing for, Rob Li is Managing Partner of Amont Partners, a New York global equity firm that invests across the US & Asia. He has spent his career putting capital on both sides of the Pacific, from Yum China to Alibaba deals, & he thinks the country that walls itself off from the best tools available loses. Arguing against, Will McKelvey is a Principal at Lerer Hippeau, one of New York's oldest venture firms, where he backs early-stage founders & spends his days watching for the future of AI, especially in consumer. He got his start by way of a congressional office, & he thinks the cheapest model on the market is the one you pay for slowly. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones. In collaboration with COMMITTEE OF 100Committee of 100 (C100) is a nonprofit U.S. leadership organization of distinguished Chinese Americans dedicated to advancing the full participation of Chinese Americans in American society & fostering constructive U.S.-China relations. For more than 35 years, C100 has brought together leaders across business, government, academia, technology, media, the arts, & other fields to advance its dual mission. Learn more at committee100.org.

events.name: Spooky Civic AI Hackathon - Build Weekend
events.description: Demos are Sunday at Demo Day. RSVP for that separately: luma.com/3perce-pi2u Spooky Civic AI Hackathon: Build AI Tools for NYC Free. Open to everyone. No approval needed, just RSVP.Fri Oct 23 - Sat Oct 24, in person in NYC or on Zoom.Come solo & we'll help you find a team. Free food for in-person builders. Who can come? Anyone who wants to build something for New York City: engineers, product managers, designers, people who used to code, & people who never have. The best teams pair people who know a problem with people who can build the tech. Builders write the code & ship the tool. Problem-solvers (PMs, designers, policy & community folks) pick the problem, shape how people will use it, & lead the pitch. No team? No problem. Most people come solo. You can meet teammates at our Oct 14 & Oct 15 classes, or at Friday's kickoff. Pick a track The Existential Track: Climate & Sustainability. Heat, waste, food access, cleaner air. Urban Nightmares: Housing, Healthcare, Education & Justice. Tenant rights, benefits, school help, legal info in plain English. Ghost in the Machine: AI infrastructure & scaling. Build the parts under civic AI tools, like search, data, & agents that keep them running. Physical AI for Good: Build AI that moves, with robot arm kits on site. No robotics experience needed. You leave with a working prototype, a demo video, & a real project for your portfolio. Mentors will be on hand all weekend. Where: NYC venue announced soon. The Zoom link goes to everyone who RSVPs. Partners: Robot arm kits & on-site mentors from Viam. Food & builder API credits from Vonage. Costumes encouraged. In-person spots are limited, so RSVP now. Sponsorship inquiries: Partner with 3percentclub About Viam: Viam is a New York-based software platform for building, deploying, & managing robotics & AI in the physical world. Viam is supplying robot arm kits & on-site mentors for this hackathon. About Vonage: Vonage, part of Ericsson, builds communications APIs for voice, video, messaging, & verification that developers put into their apps. Vonage is providing food & builder API credits for this hackathon. About 3percentclub: 3percentclub is an NYC nonprofit that teaches free AI classes for underrepresented builders: engineers, career changers, product managers, designers, & people who have never coded. This event is open to everyone. Want to go deeper with AI? Apply to the free AI Architect Fellowship for weekly classes, mentorship, & a community to build with. The AI Collective is a global non-profit building the human layer for the AI era. We unite 1,000,000+ leaders, builders, & stakeholders across 300+ forums worldwide to democratize the frontier, build trust, & coordinate how society navigates the rapid acceleration of technological progress. All attendees & organizers at events affiliated with The AI Collective agree to our privacy policy & are subject to our code of conduct.

events.name: TransportationCamp 2026
events.description: Join us on Saturday, October 24, for TransportationCamp NYC 2026! TransportationCamp NYC will be held on Saturday, October 24 at NYU's Tandon School of Engineering in Downtown Brooklyn. Join us to discuss all things transportation & connect with professionals, students, & enthusiasts alike! TransportationCamp is an unconference - every session is planned, proposed, & led by attendees like you. It's the perfect opportunity to share your transportation passion with a diverse gathering of individuals from our multidisciplinary industry. TransportationCamp welcomes all attendees, whether you're a planner, software developer, engineer, student, transportation professional, community member, policymaker, or just excited about mobility! Register here to join us for a fun day of transportation learning & networking on October 24! Interested in sponsoring?We are seeking sponsorship from engineering firms, research centers, planning organizations, & more to make TCNYC26 extra special! To learn about sponsorship packages, contact TCampNYC@gmail.com. Put your organization's name in front of the people who are working on the latest & greatest at the intersection of transportation & technology. Student ScholarshipApplications are now open for our student scholarship! TransportationCamp NYC will award one $500 scholarship this year thanks to the support of VHB! All undergraduate students, as well as full-time master's degree students, are eligible to apply. The deadline for scholarship applications is Sunday, October 18, at 11:59pm ET! Presenting?Thinking about presenting at a session? Sessions may come in a variety of formats: informal discussions, birds-of-a-feather, lightning talks, presentations, & others. We welcome experts, but really you just need to care about transportation issues or be nerds about it like us. The important thing is that you bring your ideas & enthusiasm, & engage! All the breakout rooms are equipped with a projector or whiteboard. We will be handing out session idea cards throughout registration. If you have an idea for a session, feel free to write it down in advance & bring it with you to the event. First time at a TransportationCamp?How To TransportationCamp: Review the TransportationCamp 101 guide that explains all aspects of the event.Participation Encouraged: Sessions are formed as the day goes on, so be sure to come with topics for discussion. If you have an idea, feel free to share & add your thoughts.Rule of Two Feet: Never hesitate to leave a session if you suddenly find it's not for you, or if there's another session that you want to check out, too!Social mediaMake sure you're up to date by following us on LinkedIn & by subscribing to our email updates. And keep the conversation going! Tag your tweets, Instagram photos, & more with the official event hashtag: #TCNYC26

events.name: Climate Cafe w/ CUNY
events.description: Join CUNY at the Climate Imaginarium!Open to the public! Members of the CUNY community will be joining us for a gallery tour, followed by a meditation & climate cafe. Climate cafes are listening circles for your climate-linked emotions. Get help facing your climate anxiety & connect with impactful local organizers. Vegan snacks provided!  About the Climate ImaginariumThe Climate Imaginarium is a center for climate, community, & culture in New York City. Located on Governors Island, the Climate Imaginarium is activating a cultural destination at the heart of New York City's burgeoning green economy, where artists, scientists, advocates, & storytellers come together to reimagine & build toward a more resilient future.  Getting to the Climate ImaginariumFor the weekend ferry schedule to Governors Island, please check here. Ferries run every 15 minutes. Take the ferry that's most convenient for you from either Lower Manhattan (10 South Street), Brooklyn Bridge Park (Pier 6), or Red Hook/Atlantic Basin. Please arrive 15 minutes prior to your ferry departure time with your ticket ready to display. Ferry tickets must be purchased at the ferry terminal or online. Fares are $5 for a round trip ticket & free for adults over 65, children 12 & under, Climate Imaginarium summer volunteers, & others. All passengers ride free before 11am on weekends. Cars are not permitted. Governors Island is also accessible from any route via NYC Ferry by transferring at Wall Street/Pier 11. You can find the NYC Ferry schedule here. Tickets on NYC Ferry are $4.50 each way. Once you get to Governors Island, you will either get out at Soissons Landing (from Manhattan) or Yankee Pier (from Brooklyn). You can use this map of Governors Island to locate Colonels Row. The Climate Imaginarium is in Building 406A, in the middle of Colonels Row, & will have a visible sign outside the doorway. Our address is 406A Comfort Road.

events.name: GILD AI Forum: AI & Engineering Leaders Dinner
events.description: This GILD AI Forum brings together CTOs, VPs of Engineering, Heads of AI, & senior technical leaders for candid conversations about building, scaling, & implementing AI inside their companies. This isn't a conference. It's not a panel. It's a small, curated room of technical leaders sharing what's actually working, what's not, & the real challenges of shipping AI in the AI era. Each Forum opens with a Conversation Starter, a practitioner sharing what their team is building with AI, followed by open Q&A. From there, the room breaks into intimate discussions where everyone has a seat at the table. Every attendee brings their own experience. Every attendee contributes. No pitches. No performative networking. Just senior technical leaders being honest about the architectures they're choosing, the tradeoffs they're making, & what they wish they'd figured out sooner. TRENDING THEMES FOR THIS SESSION Conversations at the Forum are shaped by what technical leaders bring to the table. Themes likely to surface this evening include: From AI pilots to AI in production: breaking out of the proof-of-concept trap & scaling agents into real workflows Connecting AI to legacy systems: architectural patterns for integrating modern AI with 20-year-old stacks without breaking everything The AI tooling budget problem: balancing experimentation with unsustainable spend as engineers blow through AI tool budgets Engineers as curators, not creators: the shift from writing code to orchestrating AI agents, reusable components, & external services MCP, multi-agent systems, & the orchestration layer: what's working, what's overhyped, & what technical leaders are actually building Guardrails & governance for AI-generated code: who's accountable when the AI writes it, & what review processes actually hold up in production Presented in partnership with Tecla Tecla gives companies flexible access to vetted talent across the US & Latin America, developed for AI-native work & available from fractional engagements to dedicated nearshore pods. Learn more at www.tecla.io THE FORMAT Intentionally small & highly curated, 20 to 25 max. A seated round-table dinner, private & off the record under Chatham House Rules. AGENDA 6:00 - 6:30 PM  Cocktails & passed appetizers 6:30 - 7:00 PM  Dinner is served Find a seat & get comfortable. 6:45 - 6:50 PM  GILD & Partner Welcome A few words from the GILD team & our partners on what the night holds & how we'll spend it together. 6:50 - 7:00 PM  Conversation Starter A fellow engineering leader opens the discussion with a candid perspective on AI, with a brief Q&A. 7:00 - 8:00 PM  Table discussions 8:00 - 8:30 PM  Open mingling WHO THIS IS FOR Founders  CEOs  CTOs  VPs of Engineering  Heads of AI  Technical Leaders  Product Leaders This session is for leaders responsible for building, deploying, & maintaining AI systems in production. Chatham House Rules apply. Discussion stays private.

events.name: AI Founders Supper Club
events.description: Hi fellow founders  Angela & Hamza here from the AI Furnace. The AI Founders Supper Club is a private founders dinner club hosted by The AI Furnace (the largest community of AI startups in the world). Once a month, we host 15-20 early stage AI founders for a night of delicious food, discussions & connections with curated high quality founders in NYC. This is a referral based network, so feel free to apply here but the other way to get in is by being referred in by an existing founder member. What to expect: A 3-course meal, courtesy of our partners Meet dope founders building out of NYC Real conversations & place to vibe with other founders, solving similar problems ABOUT OUR HOSTS & SPONSORS The AI Furnace is NYC's largest & most active AI community. It was started by AI founders, Angela Mascarenas & Hamza Zaveri, who were based in NYC & London & started the org to support fellow AI founders & operators building in local cities outside of Cerebral Valley (San Francisco). It has since grown to a global community of 20,000 AI founders, operators & researchers & has since organized events in 4 countries & 7 cities including NYC, London, Paris, Dubai, Boston, DC, & Philly. Fidelity Private Shares brings certainty to startup founders with their cap table platform to help automate equity management operations & financings in a single collaborative hub. Leverage the scenario modeling tool & secure data room to prepare for the next round of funding. From inception to IPO, Fidelity has the expertise & robust support to help guide you. Connect with Charlie Stephens for more information. PwC's Emerging Company Solutions (ECS) practice is the leading provider of audit, tax, & IPO readiness services to companies backed by venture capital (VC) & private equity (PE) firms. More specifically, PwC's ECS practice has the greatest market share & is the #1 provider of audits of technology, software, & media company IPOs amongst the Big 4 accounting firms since 2017. Whether it be in connection with a Series A capital raise, a later-stage VC or PE firm investment, leading up to, during & subsequent to an IPO, PwC's ECS practice is uniquely positioned to be with you every step of the way, helping you achieve your business goals while minimizing risk. Niural is an AI-native, end-to-end HR & finance platform transforming global payroll, PEO, & compliance. Powered by EMMA, our intelligent AI coworker, Niural brings payroll, HR, & finance into a single, streamlined ecosystem. From automated payroll & HR workflows to global compliance across multiple jurisdictions-including support for both fiat & crypto payments-Niural helps companies scale with confidence. We make global operations smarter, faster, & more efficient. Ramp is an all-in-one financial operations platform designed to save businesses time & money. Combining corporate cards, expense management, bill payments, accounting automation, procurement, travel, treasury, & more, Ramp empowers finance teams to do their best work. More than 70,000 companies, from family-owned farms to space startups, have saved $10B & 27.5M hours with Ramp since its founding in 2019. Investors include Founders Fund, Thrive Capital, Khosla Ventures, Sequoia, Greylock, Stripe, Goldman Sachs, Coatue, & Redpoint, as well as over 100 angel investors who were founders or executives of leading companies.

events.name: For The Firsts Meetup
events.description: For The Firsts is a meetup club for those building without a blueprintExpect an evening of interesting conversation in an inviting space as you meet & mingle with other "firsts" - those who are the first in their family to choose their professional path with intention instead of inertia. This month, we'll be sitting down with Jeanelle Teves, the Chief Commercial Officer of Bugaboo, founder of Work Lunch, creator, mother, & author. Enjoy refreshing drinks, delicious bites, & the chance to connect with other professionals, creatives, students, & founders. Each of our meetups looks something like this: 6:00 - 6:30 PM: Arrival & Open Mixer 6:30 - 7:30 PM: Fireside chat with Jeanelle Teves 7:30 - 9:00 PM: Guided Mixer If you are approved, please try to arrive on time, as our events regularly hit capacity & we have many folks on the waitlist. Here's what to expect:Cringe-Free Conversation: This isn't a networking event. It's a purpose-led meetup where who you are will always be more important than what you do. The dress code is always 'come exactly as you are, meet exactly who you need'. Guided Moments of Connection: This experience is at the core of For The Firsts. We'll have a few rounds of guided connection meant to introduce you to others who share your story. Remember the first rule of For The Firsts: go deeper than your job title! Firsts, not Followers: Each meetup is curated to bring together the best possible group of professionals, creatives, & founders in NYC who are the architects of their own lives. Intention is in everything we do, & you'll find that in the people you meet. Remember, the best way to get to know someone is to get someone to know you. I want to encourage you to connect on who you are & your purpose for your work & life. Remember Rule #1: No job titles, go deeper. Tell us why, how & for whom you do what you do. Disclaimer:*By signing up for the event, you will also be subscribed to our weekly Substack 'First Things First' for additional updates & event announcements. *This event will be photographed, & For the Firsts reserves the right to use photos & video from the event for marketing & communications purposes. By attending the event, you consent to the use of your image for these purposes.

events.name: Six Math Essentials w/ Terence Tao
events.description: Book Launch & Conversation with Janna Levin Widely regarded as the world's greatest living mathematician, Fields Medalist Terence Tao approaches mathematics as a sublime art-a quiet, rigorous effort to map the hidden scaffolding of reality. To mark the publication of his first popular book, Six Math Essentials, join us for an evening with Tao in conversation with Pioneer Works Director of Sciences Janna Levin. Tracing the central pillars of his book-from algebra as abstraction & geometry beyond sight, to navigating uncertainty & the mathematics of change-they will reveal math not as obscure magic, but as a deeply creative, interconnected way of thinking. Often referred to as the Mozart of mathematics, Tao will also explore how AI is transforming his own practice, the frontier of research, & our collective future. Together, we will consider what becomes of human intuition & creativity when the tools of thought are no longer uniquely human-and whether the true beauty of math lies not in the answers we find, but in the human mind reaching for them. Tao will sign copies of Six Math Essentials following the conversation, with books available for purchase on site. (Unable to attend? Order a signed copy here.) Please note that seating is limited & will be available on a first-come, first-served basis.   About the speakersTerence Tao is an Australian-American professor of mathematics at UCLA whose work focuses primarily on harmonic analysis, partial differential equations, combinatorics, & analytic number theory. The recipient of a Fields Medal, a MacArthur Genius Grant, & a Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics, among many other accolades, he is one of the most decorated & prolific mathematicians working today. Tao is the author of several academic books including Solving Mathematical Problems: A Personal Perspective & Additive Combinatorics, as well as his first popular math book, Six Math Essentials. He lives in Los Angeles. Janna Levin is the Claire Tow Professor of physics & astronomy at Barnard College of Columbia University. A Guggenheim Fellow, she has contributed to our understanding of black holes, extra dimensions, & cosmology. She is the founding director of sciences at Pioneer Works & the founding editor-in-chief of the magazine Pioneer Works Broadcast. She often contributes to news, documentaries, & radio, including as the presenter of the NOVA feature Black Hole Apocalypse on PBS & as a contributor to CBS, CNN, BBC, & NBC. She has authored books on black holes & the universe-Black Hole Blues, How the Universe Got its Spots, & Black Hole Survival Guide-as well as a PEN award-winning novel, A Madman Dreams of Turing Machines. You can find her current writings in Higher Dimensions. This program is funded by the Simons Foundation International & administered by the Simons Foundation's Science, Society & Culture division.

events.name: Health2Tech
events.description: Health2Tech - a series of digital health events.Join us on October 22nd for an exclusive gathering that brings together the brightest minds in the digital health space. Hosted by Bailey Morgan & Alex Koshykov, this evening promises to be a confluence of innovation, inspiration, & invaluable networking.  Event Schedule: 5:30 PM - 6:00 Doors Open. Begin the evening with a warm welcome & a chance to settle in. 6:00 - 6:45: "Women's Health: Undervalued to Unavoidable" by Marissa Fayer & Bailey Morgan. 6:45 - 8:30 Networking. Connect, converse, & collaborate with peers driven by a common passion for advancing healthcare through technology.  About our Guest Speaker: Marissa Fayer has spent 25+ years operating at the intersection of technology & women's health. She's CEO of DeepLook Medical, an FDA-cleared AI diagnostics company focused on improving cancer detection for patients with dense breast tissue, & CEO/founder of HERhealthEQ, a nonprofit that's improved the health outcomes of 151,000+ women in 13 different countries by expanding access to medical devices & equipment. Marissa approaches women's health as infrastructure: when properly funded & built, it drives measurable returns across economies, workforces, & communities. Previously, Marissa held executive roles at Hologic, Olympus, Maquet Getinge, & has consulted for organizations including Pfizer, the National Institutes of Health (NIH), NuVasive, & Boehringer Ingelheim. She currently serves as an Investment Committee Member of GG Ventures, a 2026-2028 World Economic Forum (WEF) Technology Fellow, is an active founding member of Milken Institute's Women's Health Committee, & advisor to Welwaze Medical, Impact.51, & TechThrive Ventures. Marissa is the author of Undervalued to Unavoidable: Women's Health as Infrastructure. Marissa is a TEDx speaker (2019 TEDxLugano), has delivered keynotes at leading global healthcare conferences, & has been recognized as a Top 100 Women in Medtech & a Medtech Voice to Follow. Marissa can be found at www.marissafayer.com  Why Attend? Meet like-minded individuals who are actively shaping the health tech landscape. Share experiences, discuss challenges, & explore potential solutions with fellow founders. Learn from the journeys of other entrepreneurs, discover something new, seek advice, & perhaps find the mentor or partner you've been looking for.  Who Should Attend? Digital Health Founders at various stages of their startup journey. Healthcare Professionals who are passionate about health innovation. Investors looking to make impactful contributions to the digital health & medtech spaces.  Why This Event Is A Must? Hear from thought leaders & innovators in the digital health domain (at every event, we'll have a new set of speakers). Connect with peers, potential collaborators, & mentors. Participate in engaging Q&As & discussions that can spark new ideas & opportunities.  Venue Details: Great location in the heart of New York, equipped to foster conversations & connections. Venue details will be shared with registered attendees. Because of limited capacity, we won't be able to accommodate everyone, so please register whenever you are sure you can attend. Don't miss this chance to be part of a community that's driving the future of health tech. Reserve your spot now & join us in shaping the landscape of digital health for 2026 & beyond. Partners FINN Partners - more than an agency. Champions of change. FINN Partners is one of the fastest-growing global, independent marketing & communications agencies in the world, serving clients through a powerful combination of bold creativity, informed strategy, hands-on partnership, & highly specialized expertise. About the organizer Bailey Morgan, Based in Astoria, NYC, is a versatile healthtech leader who merges clinical expertise with business acumen to accelerate healthcare innovation & community impact. Having started her career as a medical speech language pathologist working within inpatient facilities throughout the boroughs of NYC, she saw firsthand how behind the healthcare tech ecosystem was compared to industries such as tech or finance. After leaving healthcare to move into the healthtech startup space, Bailey has since raised over $10M in capital, led several successful sales & marketing teams through go-to-market stages in both SaaS & CPG, & has closed over $2M in technology sales herself. She currently serves as Chief of Staff at Groth Pain & Spine, a pain management practice with 10+ locations & 40+ providers, where she leads the change management & technology integrations for the practices acquisitions. In addition to consulting with various healthcare technology companies, Bailey is a Director & the Treasurer for an NYC-based dementia-focused nonprofit that employs individuals living with dementia & supports families & caregivers. Alex Koshykov is a co-founder of BeKey & a digital health expert who constantly shares news, introduces promising technologies, & promotes secure software & hardware for the healthcare industry on his YouTube channel. Additionally to that, he is a co-founder of YODD, a medical device startup. Additional Information By signing up, your email will be automatically added to the Health2Tech newsletter with news & upcoming events - but don't worry, we won't flood your inbox! ;) Also, just a note that this event might be photographed or filmed. If we do capture some moments, Health2Tech may use the photos or videos for marketing & communication purposes. By registering, you're giving us the thumbs up for using your image for these reasons.

events.name: NAB Creator Connect
events.description: ASUS ProArt Creator Connect: NYCWhere the Future of Creative Workflows Live in New YorkOctober 21, 2026 | 6:00-9:00 PM | Pier59 Studios, New York City Join ASUS ProArt & Pier59 Studios in New York City for an evening bringing together professionals from across film, television, broadcast, production, post-production, VFX & the wider creative industries to explore the technology shaping the future of creative workflows. And we're doing it somewhere pretty special. ProArt Creator Connect: NYC will take place inside Studio C at Pier59 Studios, one of North America's most technically advanced virtual production environments & an incredible opportunity to experience the technology, scale & capabilities of a cutting-edge New York production studio first-hand. With the industry in New York for NAB Show New York, we're bringing together the people creating great work with the people building, specifying, buying & deploying the technology behind it. We'll explore how new technology, AI & increasingly powerful professional tools are changing production & creative workflows, with an ASUS ProArt keynote, an industry fireside conversation, hands-on demonstrations & plenty of opportunity to experience the latest technology in a real production environment. Just as importantly, this is an opportunity to step away from the show floor, grab a drink & spend an evening with other people working across the industry in one of New York's most impressive production spaces. What to expectExperience Pier59's Studio C virtual production environment & get hands-on with the latest ASUS ProArt technology & professional creative workflows. Throughout the evening, you'll be able to explore technology designed for demanding production, post-production & creative environments, hear from industry experts about where professional workflows are heading, & meet people working across film & television production, broadcast, post, VFX, virtual production, AI & content creation. We'll look at the increasingly important role of AI & high-performance computing in professional creative environments, alongside the displays, systems & technologies being used throughout modern production pipelines. There'll be drinks, demonstrations & plenty of time for conversation throughout the evening. Whether you're responsible for creating the content, building the workflow or making the technology decisions behind it, Creator Connect: NYC is designed to bring those worlds together. Who should attend?ProArt Creator Connect: NYC is for professionals working across film, television, broadcast, production, post-production, VFX, virtual production, photography, design, AI & content creation. That includes filmmakers, editors, colorists, VFX artists, DPs, producers & creators, but also the people responsible for the technology behind their work: technical directors, production & post-production leaders, studio teams, technology executives, IT professionals, systems integrators, resellers & those responsible for specifying & investing in creative technology. If you're in New York for NAB Show New York, work within the city's production & post community, or simply want to see where professional creative technology is heading next, come & join us. It's also a rare opportunity to spend an evening inside Pier59's Studio C & experience one of North America's most advanced virtual production environments. Space is limited. Registration is free, but advance registration is required. Presented by ASUS ProArt & hosted with Pier59 Studios. By registering for this event, you agree that your registration details may be shared with ASUS Computer International (ACI) & participating event partners for event administration & relevant follow-up communications. If you would prefer not to have your details shared with event partners, you can opt out at any time by contacting us.

events.name: Red Carpet Room Launch Party
events.description: If you show up with a backpack or your laptop you will be banned from the event. Please leave backpacks at home. RED CARPET ROOM Formerly Fun HouseHosted by Anwar EnterprisesSaturday, October 31, 2026 Exact address released to confirmed guests 24 hours before doors. About the Event Red Carpet Room is the next chapter of Fun House, rebuilt around a single idea: the people building brands should be building them together. This is a mixer for founders, creators, & investors from the Anwar Events community, gathered in one room with a shared reason to be there. Everyone in attendance is constructing something with their name attached to it. The night is designed so the person who can unblock you is standing a few feet away. We are doing it on Halloween on purpose. The city will be full of parties where nothing happens beyond the party itself. This one gives you a panel worth sitting through, a room worth working, & footage of yourself that you will actually use. Run of Show [7pm] - Doors, check-in, & open networking to start the night[8pm] - Panel: operators who built audiences, companies, & reputations from nothing   SPECIAL GUESTS BEING REVEALED NEXT WEEK [9pm] - Open mixer, with Red Carpet Show interviews running in the back room Who's Coming The typical guest is a founder raising or building, a creator monetizing an audience, or an investor looking for both. Expect crossover from fashion, music, media, tech, art & consumer brands, since that is who the Anwar Events community actually contains. Whether you are hiring, raising, pitching a collaboration, or looking for people who take their work as seriously as you do, you will be in the right room. The Red Carpet Show Throughout the night, Ilias will pull guests aside for on-camera interviews for The Red Carpet Show. There is one question at the center of every interview: how can he help you. Those conversations get cut into content that reaches an audience of 70,000 plus founders, investors, & creators. Sitting down costs you four minutes & can put your company in front of people you would never cold email. Dress Code Halloween night calls for more than a costume assembled at the last minute. Come dressed as the version of yourself the press would photograph, whether that means black tie, full character, or your own blend of both. Cameras run from the door onward, so arrive accordingly. Capacity & Entry Space is limited & the guest list is curated. A confirmed RSVP secures your place only until capacity fills, so arriving early is strongly recommended. Bring a valid ID for check-in at the door. About the Host Ilias Anwar is an entrepreneur, marketer, & community builder based in New York City. He has produced more than 600 events across NYC, LA, & San Francisco, cultivating a network of over 70,000 founders, investors, & creators. His work includes brand partnerships with Google, Red Bull, Andreessen Horowitz, & Universal Music Group, along with activations at NFL Super Bowl Weekend & New York Fashion Week. Today he runs Anwar Enterprises, a venture studio that launches & scales consumer & tech companies through distribution first. If you need to meet someone in this city, they have probably attended one of his events. Partners & Sponsors Creatorsarethenewstudios.comCanvas helps creators, founders, & brands turn ideas into media IP they own. AI agents handle the story, production plan, budget, & distribution, & your first IP is free. Happyboards.comHappyBoards makes chef-built charcuterie boards & grazing tables from locally sourced ingredients. It delivers same-day across 27+ Northeast cities, & HappyBoards is feeding the room tonight.Stay Connected Future Anwar Events drop to the community first. Get on the list at luma.com/iliasanwar & follow along on Instagram, X, & LinkedIn for everything we run next. Community Standards Red Carpet Room is inclusive of gender, sexuality, race, religion, & ability. Discrimination or harassment of any kind will not be tolerated on site. For urgent security concerns during the event, please contact venue staff directly. Disclaimers By attending this event, you agree to the following terms. Photography, Video, & Recording: This event will be photographed, filmed, live-streamed, & audio recorded. By entering the venue, you consent to being captured on camera & to the use of your name, image, voice, statements, & likeness by Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, The Red Carpet Show, & their affiliated partners & sponsors. Marketing & Promotional Use: Any material captured at this event may appear in promotional content, social media, websites, newsletters, press coverage, paid advertising, sponsor recap materials, & future marketing assets, worldwide & in perpetuity, without compensation. Guests waive any right to inspect or approve the finished material before publication. On-Camera Interviews: Participation in The Red Carpet Show is entirely voluntary. Sitting for an interview grants Anwar Enterprises the full right to edit, distribute, & monetize that footage across any platform, in any format, without further approval. Opting Out: If you do not wish to be photographed or filmed, please notify event staff upon arrival & avoid the designated filming areas. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to accommodate your request, though appearance in wide or crowd shots cannot be fully prevented. Guest Policy: This is a private, invitation-only event. RSVPs are non-transferable & entry is subject to ID verification. Organizers reserve the right to refuse entry at their discretion. Capacity & Access: This event has a strict capacity limit. A confirmed RSVP does not guarantee entry once capacity has been reached, so early arrival is strongly encouraged. Code of Conduct: All attendees are expected to conduct themselves professionally & respectfully. Organizers reserve the right to remove any guest whose behavior is disruptive or inappropriate, without refund or recourse. Liability: Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, & the venue are not responsible for loss, theft, or damage to personal property. Attendance is at your own risk. Data & Registration: Information submitted at registration may be shared with event sponsors & partners in accordance with their respective privacy policies. Guests may opt out of sponsor communications at any time. Changes & Cancellations: Event details including time, venue, panelists, & programming are subject to change. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to notify registered guests of any material changes.
