events.name: Ugly Talks: Failure Is Key To Success
events.description: Failure gets talked about like it is part of the journey. That is the lie. The real thing is messier. Missed bets. Wrong hires. Near-breakdowns. The week you stop sleeping & start doing math at 3:00 AM. Founders are expected to eat it quietly & keep moving. No language for what happened. No playbook for what to do next. Ugly Talk is a founder room for the part nobody posts. No fluff. No consultants. Just builders with scars, talking about the call that cost them.  Why you should be in this room.Hear what failure cost them. Then hear what they did next. Learn how experienced founders separate self-worth from outcomes when things go sideways. Spot the patterns behind repeat mistakes. And the early signals you should not ignore. Leave with a few concrete moves for the next hard week. Not inspiration. Meet other founders in the thick of it. The ones who are still building.  What's on the table.Dare to suck: how permission to fail unlocks real progress The moment things broke: missed opportunities, wrong turns, near-breakdowns, & what changed afterward Failure vs identity: separating self-worth from outcomes Treating setbacks as data: what to measure, what to ignore, & how to decide fast Rejection as redirection: how founders find the signal in the no Habits for staying focused & resilient when everything feels uncertain  Run of show6:00 - 6:30 PM: Reception (check-in & light drinks) 6:30 - 6:40 PM: Welcome remarks 6:40 - 6:50 PM: Keynote Speech by Ben McKean 6:50 - 7:30 PM: Panel Discussion 7:30 - 7:45 PM: Audience Q&A 7:45 - 8:00 PM: Mixer + snacks & drinks  Featured speakers.Ben McKean - Founder & Chief Executive Officer, Hungryroot Ben McKean is the Founder & CEO of Hungryroot, a personalized healthy eating assistant that uses AI to make meal planning, food shopping, & nutrition effortless & enjoyable. Prior to Hungryroot, Ben was a Vice President & General Manager at Groupon, overseeing their food & beverage business. Ben came to Groupon through the acquisition of Savored, which he founded in 2009. Savored was the nation's leading provider of yield management technology to the restaurant industry, used by over two thousand restaurants nationwide & nearly one million diners. Prior to Savored, Ben worked in Merrill Lynch's technology investment banking group. Ben is a graduate of Georgetown University & currently lives in North Carolina with his wife & kids. Stephen McKinney - Founder & CEO, Bizbe Stephen McKinney is a serial entrepreneur with over a decade of experience across tech, marketing, & logistics. He's the founder & CEO of Bizbe.com, an AI-native business brokerage & lower middle market M&A firm based in New York & Miami. A former contestant on ABC's Shark Tank, Steve previously founded & led Retty Logistics, a seven-figure last-mile delivery company acquired by DXP Logistics & Webster Logistics. Dmitry Koltunov - Founder & CEO, Arbor Dmitry Koltunov is a serial entrepreneur, technologist, educator, & storyteller. He is the founder & CEO of Arbor, an AI-powered content engine that helps enterprises scale their communications with video & beyond. Previously, he co-founded & served as CTO of ALICE, a hospitality technology company that grew into a global industry leader before being acquired by Expedia Group. Dmitry also leads the New York City chapter of the Startup Leadership Program, New York's oldest startup fellowship, whose 500+ alumni have collectively raised more than $1 billion in funding across every industry imaginable. He is passionate about helping founders navigate the challenges of building & scaling companies. Outside of technology, Dmitry is an award-winning songwriter & theater producer currently developing a new musical for Broadway. He holds degrees in Computer Science & Economics from the University of Pennsylvania & is a CFA charterholder. Gwendolyn von Rahn - Co-Founder & CEO, Sweetling Health Gwendolyn von Rahn is the Co-Founder & CEO of Sweetling Health, an postpartum intelligence platform built for at-risk & hard-to-reach populations. She's a second-time exited founder, an award-winning marketer with over a decade of experience building consumer brands for women, Gwen led creative & brand teams at Vogue, InStyle, & POPSUGAR before founding & scaling a mission-driven consumer brand into Nordstrom distribution that raised over $1M for melanoma research through the Melanoma Research Foundation. She holds a Cornell Johnson MBA & founded Sweetling from her own lived experience with the postpartum care gap.  Who's hosting it.Victoria Yampolsky - President, The Startup Station Victoria Yampolsky is the Founder & President of The Startup Station, a strategic CFO advisory firm & financial education platform for startups. She partners with founders on financial strategy, modeling, & fundraising, having supported over 150 companies across 15 industries in raising more than $50M in venture capital. Victoria is also an advocate for female founders & access to capital, & has taught finance to more than 20,000 entrepreneurs through programs including the Bank of America Institute for Women's Entrepreneurship at Cornell. She began her career at Deutsche Bank & Capgemini, & holds a BS in Computer Science from Cornell University & an MBA from Columbia Business School.  Who's getting in.Early-stage tech founders & operators navigating uncertainty, setbacks, or the emotional weight of building a company. Expected roles may include: Founders & co-founders (pre-seed to Series A) Operators (COO, Head of Ops, Chief of Staff) Product & Engineering leads building through ambiguity Growth & GTM leads working through missed targets & pivots Finance & strategy leaders supporting founder decision-making  Who's backing this.The Startup Station The Startup Station - is a CFO advisory & financial education platform for early-stage startups. We help early-stage founders build investor-ready financials & tell their funding story with confidence. In the past decade, we've helped 150+ founders raise over $50M & educated 20,000+ entrepreneurs worldwide. The Startup Station also runs Speed Pitch, an exclusive investor-founder matchmaking event series for early-stage startups where founders are matched with 3 investors by sector, stage, & check size. Mind Your Business Every attendee will receive a free copy of keynote speaker Ben McKean's Mind Your Business. Mind Your Business is a practical parable for people rethinking work as AI advances. Set over a four-day retreat, it follows six participants competing for funding to bring one vision to life. As they evaluate six competing proposals, they begin to confront deeper questions about what gives them energy, who they serve, & what they uniquely contribute. Those patterns form what the book calls their Soulcode-the way purpose, belonging, imagination, & courage shape how they work. Told with humor & warmth, the story turns familiar workplace tensions into practical lessons for contributing more deeply, seeing new possibilities, & acting with greater conviction. At its core, the book argues that the opportunity of the AI era isn't doing more work-it's knowing what work is worth doing. GREY Journal GREY Journal - Media partner spotlighting modern entrepreneurs (featured on Apple News + Google News).  About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough "aha!" moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons & insights. With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami, we've built a vibrant community of thousands of founders & industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape. Official Website: UglyTalk.com Important Notice for Ugly Talk AttendeesAdmission & Confirmation Attendance is by approval only. Approved guests will receive a confirmation email along with a calendar invite. Invitations are non-transferable. Additional event details will be shared as the event approaches. Code of Conduct By attending, you agree to: Maintain respect & professionalism, adhering to all venue rules, policies, & applicable laws. Refrain from harassment, discrimination, unwelcome sexual advances (verbal or physical), intimidation, or inappropriate photography/recording. Report any violations to the event hosts immediately. Violations may result in immediate removal from the event & exclusion from future invitations. Liability & Risk Participation is voluntary & at your own risk. The event organizers, hosts, sponsors, & venue are not liable for personal injury, lost or stolen belongings, or any other damages incurred during the event. Media Consent By attending, you grant the event organizers & affiliated entities the right to capture, use, & distribute photos, videos, & audio recordings of you for promotional, marketing, & other lawful purposes, including digital & print media, advertising, & social media. You waive any right to inspect or approve the final materials & release all claims related to their use. Communications By registering, you agree to receive marketing & promotional communications from Ugly Talk & its co-hosts, partners, & sponsors. You may unsubscribe at any time. Agreement If you do not agree to this Code of Conduct, please refrain from attending the event.  Join us to stay updated on upcoming Ugly Talk events! Join the newsletter  Follow us on IG  Official website

events.name: PMAI: Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Sales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. - Bring a computer. You're writing three things tonight.- Most founders can get meetings. The deals die after meeting one.- You'll leave with your buyer in one sentence, a cold email written to a real person, & five questions for your next call. About Farzad, the speaker Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. events.name: Transit Techies
events.description: The Center for Urban Science + Progress (CUSP) at NYU Tandon & Transit Techies welcome you to attend two presentations: Phil Cline on Swiftly & Joe Puccio on WalkNYC. Connect with NYU Tandon CUSP & Transit Techies NYC at this talk; attendees are welcome to bring their own food. The event will be held at 370 Jay Street, Brooklyn, NY in Room 1201. We hope to see you there! About the TalksSwiftly Phil Cline will share some of his work on assisting transit agencies with better drawing & dissemination of bus detours at Swiftly WalkNYC In May, Joe created WalkNYC, an app that tracks which blocks you've walked. He built it as a personal project while trying to walk every block in Manhattan. Since launch over 25,000 New Yorkers have started using WalkNYC to stay active & explore the city. About the SpeakersPhil ClineSoftware Engineer, Swiftly Phil Cline is a Brooklyn-based software engineer originally from Toronto who has worked in the transit industry for over 7 years & has a lot of experience with transit data standards like GTFS & GTFS-RT. Joe PuccioCreator, WalkNYC & Founder Coursicle Joe Puccio is a designer & programmer based in NYC. He is the founder of Coursicle, an app used by millions of college students to manage their class schedules & assignments. A central focus of Joe's work is running his companies ethically & building products that are fundamentally beneficial to people's lives. At Coursicle, all employees receive the same salary, & profits are split among employees at the end of each year. Joe graduated from UNC Chapel Hill in 2016 with degrees in Mathematics & Computer Science. He writes about design, technology, & other ideas at joepuccio.com. Vistor InformationPlease visit the NYU Tandon website for directions & a campus map. Advance registration through Luma is required for campus access at NYU for external guests. Attendees who are not current students, faculty, or staff at NYU, including alumni, are asked to register using a personal email address. About CUSP at NYU TandonThe Center for Urban Science + Progress (CUSP) at NYU Tandon is an interdisciplinary center dedicated to applying science, technology, engineering, math, & social sciences to serve urban communities worldwide. Founded as a partnership between NYU & the City of New York, CUSP leads research, educational, & entrepreneurial initiatives that advance the science of cities. By applying novel insights to urban issues, we develop data- & technology-driven approaches that drive positive impact. With an additional focus on training future leaders, CUSP offers interdisciplinary academic programs in applied urban science & informatics for graduate students & professionals. CUSP also engages with stakeholders across city agencies, start-ups, industry players, community-based organizations, & nonprofits to address urgent socioeconomic, environmental, & infrastructural challenges. The center's ultimate objective is to improve urban quality of life by using data to innovate & refine inclusive, equitable, & sustainable practices for cities everywhere. About Transit Techies NYCBringing together the technologists who love transit & the transit enthusiasts who hack! We'll have speakers present transit-related projects. Presenters may be household hackers, data scientists, researchers, product developers, or you! All presentations will be technical & awesome. Follow our calendar to stay up-to-date on our future events! Learn more on our website.

events.name: Future Of AI Infrastructure
events.description: Let's talk about what's coming in the world of AI infra. Anthony Erondu is a Principal Consultant focused on AI infrastructure, GPU compute & Physical AI. He partners with high growth companies across the space to build product & engineering teams, placing talent from VP level leaders through senior ICs across some of the most critical areas of the AI stack. Akaanksha Sinha is an award-winning trailblazer in AI, cybersecurity & governance architecture. Over a decade in the enterprise stack. She founded AKAVAM, a governance-through-architecture company for enterprise AI. Its platform, AEVO, combines infrastructure as code, policy as code & compliance as code into deterministic execution, turning organizational context into operating capability. Ex-IBM, Deloitte, CUNY Srinivas Venkatanarayanan is a Senior Systems Research Engineer in Nvidia, Working in Cosmos Search. He specializes in multimodal reasoning, search & Curation for Post-training Vision Language Action Models. He works in Autonomous Vehicle & Robotics domain. Joshua Ness is a Senior AI Advisor & Consultant based in New York City. He spent 6 years at Verizon 5G Labs where he advised on enterprise adoption of 5G & edge computing technologies for clients, including the NFL, Disney, & MasterCard. He currently advises PE-backed global technology firms on AI implemention & organizational structure, including tech infrastructure modernization & regulatory compliance. Joshua holds a Fulbright Specialist appointment through which he works with the government of the Philippines on national AI readiness programs. He holds certifications from AWS, IBM, & IEEE in applied AI & cloud infrastructure.

events.name: Future Forum - Science For Society
events.description: The 2026 FUTURE FORUM will convene leaders from diverse backgrounds including academia, museums, journalism, media, public engagement, government, industry, & scientific organizations from the United States & Germany to explore how science can more effectively serve society through communication, collaboration, & public engagement. Centered on the theme Science for Society, the meeting will examine how trust in science is built & sustained, how scientific discoveries & long-term research can be communicated more effectively to diverse audiences, & how institutions can demonstrate the societal value of science. A panel discussion will address the roles of museums, journalists, policymakers, & other non-traditional science communicators; strategies for strengthening public confidence in science & evidence-based decision-making; the importance of open & international scientific collaboration amid increasing geopolitical pressures; & approaches to fostering public engagement, scientific literacy, & global collaboration. Through interdisciplinary dialogue & transatlantic relationship-building, the 2026 FUTURE FORUM aims to develop new partnerships, identify best practices, & strengthen the role of science communication in advancing an informed, engaged, & resilient society. About the FUTURE FORUM The FUTURE FORUM brings together experts from Germany, the United States, & beyond to exchange perspectives on emerging issues in science, innovation, & society. Through focused expert dialogue & public engagement, the format creates space to examine shared challenges, identify new perspectives, & strengthen transatlantic exchange. Previous editions have explored themes including Science Diplomacy in an Era of Technological Disruption at the Science Diplomacy Hub at Johns Hopkins University, Washington, D.C. in 2025. Or Health. Tech. Diplomacy., which focused on global health at the Broad Institute of MIT & Harvard in 2025. In 2026, the FUTURE FORUM returns with Science for Society, bringing together transatlantic experts to explore questions around science communication, public trust, scientific literacy, public engagement, & collaboration across disciplines & borders.

events.name: Startup Pitch & Networking
events.description: Join our event in New York! We design Pitch & Networking nights to help founders sharpen their thinking through direct, candid feedback & to give strong investors access to serious teams. Our pitch night is complemented by a structured networking session before & after the pitch session.  What to expect: Startups pitch live & receive focused feedback from angels & VC partners Structured networking session before & after the pitches Entrepreneurs, startup founders, & operators are joining to network, exchange ideas, & build strong connections Active investors & venture scouts joining to discover the best startups early  Who you will meet at the event: Founders Investors, VC partners, Venture Scouts Marketers, Salespeople, Business Advisors Industry Disruptors AI Experts Entrepreneurs from Europe, Asia, & the United Kingdom  We Welcome New Investors: We invite investors to our event to expand their network, get acquainted with new startups, evaluate them, share feedback, & participate in discussions with early-stage & serial founders. We offer complimentary tickets to institutional investors, angels, & venture scouts with a proven track record. If you'd like to access our database of promising startups or provide mentorship support to our best startups, please fill out this short Investor Application Form, & our team will contact you.  Want to Pitch? A limited number of founders will have the opportunity to pitch their startup or business to a panel of investors & experts. 4-6 selected founders will pitch their startup, followed by a short Q&A where participants can ask questions & share feedback. Apply by filling out the Pitch Application Form & sending us your pitch deck. Spots are limited, & we select founders in advance. To maintain high-quality pitches, you are required to present with a pitch deck. We will share our pitching guide and, if you'd like, coach you so you're fully prepared for pitch night.  The best startups will be featured across our social media & included in our investor newsletter. Requirements for attendees: Dress code: smart casual. Bring good energy.  Join our event & secure your ticket today! About us: Startup Valley is a global event organizer hosting pitch nights in 25 cities since 2023. Since then, we have hosted 850 events for 40,000 attendees. Over these years, we connected countless outstanding early-stage startups to serious investors, & we are not planning to stop. We maintain strategic partnerships with VC funds in the US, Europe, & Asia to support our community. Do you have a question, a partnership proposal, or want to clarify something? Reach us at hello@startupvalley.club Agenda 18:00-18:30 - Registration: Guests register, receive badges, & event programs. This is an opportunity for casual networking, making first connections, & preparing for the event. 18:30-19:00 - Event Kickoff & Interactive Networking: Official welcome from the organizers with a brief overview of the event goals & schedule. Interactive networking session to connect with key contacts. 19:00-19:50 - Startup Pitch Session: Startups present their projects to investors & experts. Each team has 5 minutes to pitch, covering the project's core idea, business model, & target market. 19:50-21:00 - Chill & Networking: Participants enjoy casual conversations with investors, discuss collaboration opportunities, & exchange ideas over refreshments. FAQ Can I pitch? Yes! To pitch, please purchase a Pitch Ticket & fill out the Pitch Application Form. We will contact you to discuss & approve your pitch. The pitch duration is 5 minutes. You will also have some time to answer questions from the audience. How does the pitch go? Selected founders present on stage to the audience & the investors in the room. You get 5 minutes to pitch your idea, business model, target market, & investment ask, followed by a short Q&A. The best startups are featured across our social media channels & in the investor newsletter. Who will I meet? Founders, angel investors, VC partners, venture scouts, AI experts, engineers, operators, marketing & sales experts, & international entrepreneurs from across Europe, Asia, & the US. Do investors get free tickets? Yes! Please apply above or email hello@startupvalley.club, & we will issue a complimentary ticket for you & your team. Can I request a refund? Yes. Refunds are available if requested at least 1 day before the event start time. Please submit the refund request on the platform where you purchased your ticket, or email us at hello@startupvalley.club

events.name: An UNMUTED Book Club: The 100 Years War On Palestine
events.description: READING NOT REQUIRED - just be curious! Next up: Rashid Khalidi's The Hundred Years' War on Palestine, the 2020 book that argues the Israeli-Palestinian conflict isn't simply a tragic struggle between two peoples claiming the same land, but a century-long colonial campaign against Palestinians, backed first by Britain & later by the United States. Khalidi, a Palestinian-American historian at Columbia, tells the story through six turning points, beginning with the 1917 Balfour Declaration & moving through the creation of Israel, the wars that followed, & the failures of the peace process. Drawing on historical archives & his own family's experiences, he makes a provocative argument: that Palestinians have never been negotiating on equal terms, & that understanding the conflict as a dispute between two competing national movements obscures the enormous imbalance of power between them. It's a forceful challenge to conventional accounts of Israel's founding, Zionism, & America's role in the region, & one that raises uncomfortable questions about nationalism, colonialism, & self-determination. Show up even if you only got through a chunk. We'll talk about where Khalidi's account is most convincing, where it leaves out important context, whether Zionism is best understood as a colonial movement or a national liberation movement, & what his interpretation of the past means for the possibility of peace today. UNMUTED is a discussion forum for the politically curious. Accessible. Engaging. Social. Open-minded is the name of the game. Join your people.

events.name: The Deployment Room
events.description: The Builder Series: A 60,000+ member community redefining what networking looks like curating founders, investors into intentional rooms built for experiences people remember & relationships that last. It's a direct line to the most ambitious builders.Find us here: Instagram  LinkedIn  TikTok  Facebook  X : WhatsApp Broad Channel (Not a GC)This is the 3rd edition of our luncheon.This time, we're hosting it in an $8.5M townhouse, because we believe in high-class experiences, & incredible people. (Pictures Below)Every room has been bigger than the last. Our 2nd edition versus the 1st:Founder revenue: $90M+ a year, up from $18M+ in August.Money being raised: $197M+ across 19 founders, up from $95M+ across 14 in August.Capital already raised: $43M+, up from $35M+ in August.The investors at the table:We feature 6 investors from our network, & we always end up with more.1st edition: We expected 6. We brought 10.2nd edition: We expected 10. We brought 12.$2B+ combined AUM across both events.$1M average check, $100K minimum.$10M+ in live check capacity.Who this room is forTo get into this room, you should to have raised at least $1M or be doing $1M+ in ARR. Our last edition averaged $3.8M+ ARR per founder.Raised your first round, onto your second, or bootstrapped to $1M or 15M ARR? You're in the right place. If you're an exited founder, LP/GP, dealmaker or capital raiser, you belong in this room too.Every investor here is from our network. We're curating this room deliberately, matching founders to the investors most likely to be a fit, & making the introduction ourselves.The goal: getting founders funded by our investor network.The 6 Investors joining us from our network: (More will be joining)Francesca Poupel: F&G Capital Partners (Managing Partner): Backing founders from pre-seed to Series A in AI, fintech, & blockchain, writing $300K$500K checks & partnering closely with teams as they scale.Mahir Laul (Partner) representing Laul Global a family office & holding company operating four interconnected pillars: Education Engine, Real Assets, Future Ventures, & Acquisitions. One integrated system. One long-term vision.Laul Global is owned & operated by the Laul family. We started with a single student recruitment company. We built it into one of Canada's most diversified education holding groups. Today the portfolio spans institutions, edtech, real estate, & a tech venture studio, with reach across 20+ countries & no plans to slow down.Triet Leminh: Principal, LMT Partners: Lawyer, founder, & investor backing pre-seed to Series A founders building in enterprise & regulated industries. Writing $200K$300K checks.Andrew Antar (General Partner, AG Venture Capital): A generalist fund backing extraordinary founders, sector agnostic. Also a Venture Partner at Arcadian Capital, focused on late-stage secondaries & pre-IPO tech, & served as Crypto Policy Advisor to the NYC Office of the Mayor  advising on the city's crypto regulatory framework & organizing the NYC Crypto Summit at Gracie Mansion. He is also founder of Tune.FM, a tokenized music streaming platform & digital asset marketplace, & co-founded Clear Quantum, a stealth quantum AI startup.Gonzalo Quincot (Founder, Sinober): Sinober is a financial intelligence platform that combines public & private market intelligence with institutional-grade methodology, corporate finance & proprietary AI tools to sharpen investment & capital decisions for individuals & businesses. Invests in automation, robotics, data centers & applied AI.Shilpi Nayak: (Founder & General Partner, 434 VC): Invests in early-stage technical founders across AI, infrastructure, physical AI & emerging technology. She is also the founder of House of 434, a community bringing together founders, investors & industry leaders.Pranav Jajapur (Co-Founder, ZERON Ventures): ZERON is an early-stage venture fund with an execution platform behind it, backing real-world technology, AI, healthcare, deep tech & climate companies building in the physical world, inside biology. Pre-seed through Series A with core deployment at seed, writing $400K$500k checks. Preferred focus is institutionally-anchored AI: structural research relationships at academic institutions, spinouts, & founder-led research programs.Fund I in formation. Deploying Q1All 6 senior investors confirmed.Part of building rooms is making sure real capital is present. Six investors actively deploying writing capital will be joining. Our first confirmed:Why we do this: Putting active investors in the same room as exceptional founders, & keeps the room small enough to ensure everyone actually meets. We value intentional networking & community.If you're here to meet the best of the best, this is the room.What to expect for this:A Greek style lunch, courtesy of our teamConversations with fellow high-performing startup leadersAn experience designed to facilitate new meaningful connections conversations with ambitious peers solving similar problemsEvent to be hosted at a beautiful private Soho loftOur intent is to bring good, smart humans together, & active investors together to fun incredible founders. Community has been lost & we are rebuilding it.Our Venue: Some PhotosOur Greek Inspired Menu:About the mealA three-course Greek menu. Appetizers & dessert are shared & open to everyone; each will get one entre.The format is intentionally part standing, part seated so you can enjoy incredible food without being anchored to a single table or a single conversation.Why we do thisOur intent is simple: bring good, smart humans together, put active investors in the same room as incredible founders. Intentional community has been lost. We're rebuilding it.

events.name: The AI Era & What It Means To Be Human
events.description: The AI Era & What It Means to Be HumanAI is changing how we work, learn, create, & make decisions. But underneath the conversation about models, agents, & automation is a more fundamental question: what does it mean to be human in an age of increasingly capable machines? On October 23rd, The AI Collective is bringing together 100 people in NYC for an evening exploring the human side of the AI era. We'll move beyond the usual conversation about what AI can do & look instead at what its rise asks of us: how we learn, how we maintain agency, how we relate to one another, & which distinctly human capacities become more important as technology advances. The evening will combine conversation, small-group discussion, & experiential mindfulness/wellness exercises. This is not a technical AI event. We're creating a conversation about the human layer: the trust, awareness, connection, & shared understanding we'll need to build alongside the technology. Come curious. Expect to participate. Agenda6:00 PM: Arrival & Welcome6:30 PM: Opening Remarks + Experiential Mindfulness Exercise6:45 PM: Fireside Chat: AI & the Human Condition with Mohan Nair, author of "Unreachable: How to Not Lose Your Mind in an AI-Obsessed Era."7:15 PM: Conversation with Catherine & Manas followed by Breath-work & Meditation.7:45 PM: Small-Group Roundtables8:15 PM: Dessert & Networking Food & beverages provided. Space is limited to 75 participants. Co-hosted by The AI Collective & Manas Ram with support from JQ Consulting, whose work focuses on the science of human wellbeing, resilience, happiness, mindfulness, & the human condition. Please be advised: Unfortunately, space is very limited at these community events & we can not always accept everyone we would like to. If you are not accepted to this event, please keep applying! We appreciate your application tremendously & we are looking forward to seeing you at a future event very soon! The AI Collective is a global non-profit building the human layer for the AI era. We unite 200,000+ leaders, builders, & stakeholders across 100+ forums worldwide to democratize the frontier, build trust, & coordinate how society navigates the rapid acceleration of technological progress. All attendees & organizers at events affiliated with The AI Collective agree to our privacy policy & are subject to our code of conduct.

events.name: Prototyping In Public: Where Art & Science Get Tested On The Gallery Floor
events.description: What if a museum ran like a lab, with the experiment still in progress? Ann Neumann is Director of Galleries & Exhibitions at the MIT Museum. Her question for the evening: can a museum serve as infrastructure for public experimentation, a place where visitors take part in the work rather than just walk through it? If you build products, run pilots, or spend your days deciding what's ready to put in front of real people, this is a look at how one of the best-known science museums handles prototyping in public. In collaboration with the National Arts Club & its Art & Technology Committee, Ann will walk through the interactive projects she's shepherded at the MIT Museum. Each one works as a prototype for engaging the public with technologies like CRISPR, machine learning, & sensory neuroscience. Reserve your spot & arrive early. Space is limited. Founded in 1898, the National Arts Club is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit with a mission to stimulate, foster, & promote public interest in the arts & to educate the American people in the fine arts. Annually, the Club offers more than 150 free programs-both in-person & virtually-to the public, including exhibitions, theatrical & musical performances, lectures, & readings, attracting an audience of over 30,000 in-person visitors & thousands more online.

events.name: Borderless Office - Identity & Access In World Of Remote-First Growth
events.description: Join Antoine Jebara (Co-founder, JumpCloud) & Noah Landow (Founder & CEO, Macktez) for an informal conversation between an expert on scaling global technology companies & the evolution of identity & access management & the founder of a technology consulting firm. In an era defined by remote work & the rapid rise of agentic AI, the concepts of identity & security are shifting beneath our feet. As AI agents begin to act on our behalf, how do we maintain control, responsibility, & security? If an AI agent executes a transaction or accesses a database, who is truly holding the keys? Antoine brings a unique perspective from the front lines of this transition, from pioneering decentralized 2FA & password management at MYKI to driving global strategy & partner ecosystems at JumpCloud. Join us at the Macktez office, after work, over light snacks & sips, for an exploratory conversation on the challenges of scaling fast-growing global companies & how different security architectures impact our long-term safety in a cloud-first world. We will dive into the shifting landscape of encryption, the unique hurdles of managing remote-first organizations, & what it truly means to "identity" ourselves in the age of AI. Photography, audio, & video recording may occur at this event & by attending you consent to such recording media & its release, publication, exhibition, or reproduction. Event StructureWe ask that guests arrive between 7-7:30 pm to minimize disruption during the talk. 7 pm - Doors open, opportunity to mingle over snacks & sips with other attendees7:30 pm - Guests take their seats for the talk8:15 pm - Informal mixer resumes On AttendanceWe have a limited capacity. If your plans change, please update your registration so someone else can join. A bit about Macktez, & why we host this seriesMacktez is a technology consultancy collaborating with organizations going through dynamic change. Our goal is to form a lasting partnership between our team & our clients, so we can anticipate their technology challenges & help them navigate growth, disruption, & other evolving conditions. Each event in our Tte--Tech series is an opportunity to explore a specific cultural, scientific, historical, & personal issue. We fire at the synapses that connect each topic to other fields of interest & to our individual lives. And we do so in a comfortable environment to facilitate conversation that can be casual, surprising, & illuminating. To learn more, visit us at macktez.com.

events.name: SOSV Deep Tech Summit
events.description: Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. The producers of the Summit are SOSV's Ned Desmond, Ben Joffe, & Norm Amandi. SOSV's mission is to invest in deep tech companies that advance human & planetary health, & embedded in building an 800+ company portfolio with a remarkable array of companies applying AI in the physical world. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

events.name: Silicon Alley Hack | Build Cool Hardware
events.description: Everyone & their grandma is hosting a hackathon. This is the one where you build something physical. Silicon Alley Hack is a one-day, in-person sprint for builders who'd rather solder than ship a vibe-coded app. Microcontrollers. Sensors. Connected devices. Real hardware that runs in the real world & has to work when we plug it in on stage. Application-based. Teams of 4. Every team gets an STM32 development board & peripherals on arrival. Bring your laptop, your wits, & your soldering instincts.  The Problem StatementSoftware ate the world & then got bored. The interesting frontier moved back to atoms - robots that navigate a room, drones that deliver, sensors that make a physical space legible to a machine. All of it runs on constrained silicon, in real time, in places where the cloud is too slow, too far, or not there at all. So that's the terrain: edge intelligence. Machines that sense the world & act on it, on-device.  The Challenge ThemeThe sealed spec will live somewhere in here: Sense  decide  act, running on-device IoT, sensors, & connected devices Physical/digital interaction - things that move, respond, or react Anything that runs on hardware, not just in a browser Constraints you can count on: You'll be working on an STM32 development board & peripherals - get familiar before you show up It has to run live. Slides don't win. Working hardware wins. First team to solve it take the prizes. This is a race, not a showcase.  What to ExpectA live race-to-win challenge dropped at kickoff An STM32 dev kit + peripherals for every team, free 5 hours of focused build time Team formation on-site, or come with your crew Breakfast & lunch provided Exciting prizes for the winning A room full of NYC's hardware people - embedded engineers, drone builders, robotics founders, spatial-data folks  Schedule10:00 - 11:00 AM - Doors open. Breakfast, networking mixer, team formation. 11:00 - 11:30 AM - Partner intros, Root Access demo, challenge drop, rules & judging criteria. 11:30 AM - 4:30 PM - Build sprint. Lunch provided. Clock does not stop. 4:30 - 5:15 PM - Live hardware demos to the judges. 5:15 - 6:00 PM - Photos & Mixer.  PrizesA mix of cash, credits, & perks for the winning team. Sponsors are getting locked in - full breakdown announced before doors.  Who Should AttendEmbedded & firmware engineers Robotics, drone, & hardware builders EE / CE students & anyone who's ever blown up a dev board Founders building physical products Software engineers who want to get their hands on real silicon Anyone curious, ambitious, & hands-on  Sponsors[Sponsor TBD - reach out to somyag00@gmail.com to sponsor]  Hosts & PartnersSomya Gupta - The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Pulse NYC AI - A community, incubator, & venture fund built for founders, researchers, & technologists shaping the future of AI in New York City. ConnNext - A next-gen mobile app & community built for career growth.

events.name: ODSC AI NYC - AI for Work Summit
events.description: AI has changed. It's time for workflows to catch up.Join AI builders, business practitioners, product leaders, founders, and executives in Midtown Manhattan for ODSC AI NYC, a two-day, workshop-driven summit focused on putting AI to work. December 2-3, 2026Jay Conference Center Bryant Park, New York CityIn personLearn more at www.summit.ai. This is where technical implementation meets real business adoption. Through hands-on workshops, practical demonstrations, enterprise case studies, and leadership discussions, you'll explore how organizations are moving AI agents, copilots, and automation beyond experimentation and into reliable, scalable workflows. Why Attend?ODSC AI NYC is designed to help you: - Move AI agents and copilots from pilots into production- Build reliable evaluation, monitoring, and governance processes- Redesign workflows around AI-native ways of working- Understand the cost, latency, quality, and security trade-offs of AI systems- Learn from teams actively deploying AI across their organizations- Connect with practitioners and leaders facing the same challenges- Create a practical 90-day roadmap for what your team should build, test, scale, or retire

events.name: Deal Flow - NYC's First VC Hackathon
events.description: Event DescriptionNew York is getting its first VC hackathon, & you're building for the people who write the checks. Deal Flow is a one-day, in-person hackathon hosted by localhost:nyc & VCLab. You get 9 hours to build working products for the real problems VCs face every day. Partners from NYC's top funds judge live, & the best teams leave with intros to those funds. Problem StatementVenture capital runs on spreadsheets, gut feel & endless inbox triage. Firms move billions of dollars with tools that haven't changed in a decade. Your challenge is to build software that helps VCs find better companies, make faster decisions & support their founders after the check clears. The Challenge ThemeSourcing: finding breakout founders before everyone else does Diligence: market maps, competitive analysis & memo drafting Portfolio ops: helping funds support their companies at scale LP reporting: making fund updates less painful & more useful Deal pipeline & CRM workflows that VCs will actually use What to Expect9 hours of focused building, 9 AM to 6 PM Real VC problems, with investors in the room to test your ideas against Teams of 4 Time to meet founders, engineers & investors from across NYC Live demos to a panel of VC judges at the end of the day Food & drinks all day PrizesTo Be Announced. JudgesAbeera Saeed is the Ventures Principal at Plug & Play, investing in Enterprise & AI B2B SaaS companies from Pre-Seed to Series A. Michael Barone - Associate at Everywhere Ventures, a global pre-seed venture capital firm. D. J. Patel - VC | 3x exited founder. Garrett Higgins is a skilled operator with experience running Finance & GTM Operations at high growth companies & an angel investor. He loves helping founders win & drive growth. Radhika Khandelwal builds AI agents for a living as a product leader at Wand AI, & she's spent years in the VC world seeing what makes startups stick. She'll want to see both slick code & a real business. Bettina Sosa is co-founder & CEO of Yaven, building a local-first AI workforce for independent businesses. Who Should AttendPre-seed & seed founders Engineers Builders who have felt the pain of fundraising firsthand Anyone curious about how venture capital actually works from the inside You don't need VC experience or a finished idea. Just show up ready to build. SponsorsSeedLegals is your one-stop legal platform from idea to Series A & beyond. Incorporate your Delaware C Corp or convert your to a C Corp, raise with SAFEs, manage your cap table, give stock options to your team, do a priced round, all on one platform, for way less than paying lawyers, with an amazing team to help. Hostslocalhost:nyc: Making NYC the biggest startup ecosystem in the world. Tracy Huang: VC Lab & CEO of Interlink IQ Olivia Iarmak - Researcher | Meta Reality Labs. ConnNext is a next-gen mobile app & community built for career growth. Visionbrew helps people be 2 places at once with 3D AI avatars. Pulse NYC AI - A community, incubator, & venture fund built for founders, researchers, & technologists shaping the future of AI in New York City.

events.name: Double Diamond
events.description: Double Diamond, NYC's favorite live design podcast & event series, is BACK with another night of conversations about designing & building at the frontier. Our October event brings Alejandro Matamala Ortiz, Mina Fahmi, & Alex Leiphart to the stage to share what they're building & how they think about designing with intelligence. The LineupAlejandro Matamala Ortiz, Co-founder & Chief Innovation Officer at Runway Alejandro co-founded Runway to build new creative tools for the age of AI, & he leads the company's work on what's next, including Solaris, its research into interfaces that adapt & build themselves around what you're trying to do. Before Runway, he explored AI & creativity as a research resident at NYU. Mina Fahmi, Co-founder & CEO at Sandbar Mina is building Stream, Sandbar's private voice ring for capturing thoughts, dictating quietly, & talking through your ideas. He previously developed human-computer interfaces at the MIT Media Lab & at CTRL-labs (acquired by Meta). Alex Leiphart, Partner & Head of Product at Little Plains Alex helps lead Little Plains, the New York brand & product studio, where he heads up product. He's pioneering an intelligence-native approach to brand systems, rethinking how brands get built & run when agents are part of the team from day one. Audience & CurationEvery Double Diamond audience is intentionally curated. We're prioritizing product builders & design leaders who are actively building for & with intelligence. If you're designing products at the frontier of human<>intelligence interaction, or building with agents & emerging tools, you're likely a good fit. Recording & SharingWe'll have a professional production crew recording the night. Attendees will receive a link to the recording in the days after the event to share with their teams or on social. Agenda6:00 PM ~ 7:15 PM: Arrivals + Happy Hour + DJ 7:15 PM ~ 8:30 PM: Showtime (Alejandro, Mina, & Alex) 8:30 PM - Late: Open Hang + Drinks + DJ About Double DiamondThis event is hosted by Double Diamond, a live-in-NYC event & content series for product & design practitioners building with AI right now. We put people on stage to share recent work, & we pair that with a carefully selected room of peers. Double Diamond is presented by Basis, who are building at the frontier of applied intelligence right here in NYC. Follow us on Twitter, LinkedIn, & Luma to keep up with our events & conversations.

events.name: Plug & Play x PMAI: Pitching Masterclass III
events.description: IT IS BACK! CALLING ALL FOUNDERS! Hosted by Plug & Play NYC & Pioneering Minds AI Apply to pitch here:https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScOGgbEqUmtEHmKrhqpzynRzYX4Lk4EUC8qrYvSt6YZhXrGvg Pitching is one of the most important skills a founder develops, yet it's rarely practiced in a setting where you can iterate in real time. In this interactive workshop, founders will present their pitch, receive direct feedback, & immediately refine it live. This is a hands-on pitch masterclass where builders learn by doing, & by watching other founders sharpen their story. For founders, few people have a better perspective on how to communicate complex technology simply & convincingly. In this session, Anthony & Anna will work directly with founders in a live pitch lab, helping them sharpen their narrative & strengthen how they present their ideas. Come have a sales pitch, demo pitch, or even a VC pitch! Anthony RoseAnthony Rose is a pioneering technology entrepreneur best known as the co-creator & former CTO of the BBC iPlayer, one of the world's first large-scale streaming platforms that fundamentally changed how millions consume television. He has spent decades building technology at the intersection of consumer platforms, developer ecosystems, & emerging tech. events.name: Prototyping In Public: Where Art & Science Get Tested On The Gallery Floor
events.description: What if a museum ran like a lab, with the experiment still in progress? Ann Neumann is Director of Galleries & Exhibitions at the MIT Museum. Her question for the evening: can a museum serve as infrastructure for public experimentation, a place where visitors take part in the work rather than just walk through it? If you build products, run pilots, or spend your days deciding what's ready to put in front of real people, this is a look at how one of the best-known science museums handles prototyping in public. In collaboration with the National Arts Club & its Art & Technology Committee, Ann will walk through the interactive projects she's shepherded at the MIT Museum. Each one works as a prototype for engaging the public with technologies like CRISPR, machine learning, & sensory neuroscience. Reserve your spot & arrive early. Space is limited. Founded in 1898, the National Arts Club is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit with a mission to stimulate, foster, & promote public interest in the arts & to educate the American people in the fine arts. Annually, the Club offers more than 150 free programs-both in-person & virtually-to the public, including exhibitions, theatrical & musical performances, lectures, & readings, attracting an audience of over 30,000 in-person visitors & thousands more online.

events.name: GILD AI Forum: AI & Engineering Leaders Dinner
events.description: This GILD AI Forum brings together CTOs, VPs of Engineering, Heads of AI, & senior technical leaders for candid conversations about building, scaling, & implementing AI inside their companies. This isn't a conference. It's not a panel. It's a small, curated room of technical leaders sharing what's actually working, what's not, & the real challenges of shipping AI in the AI era. Each Forum opens with a Conversation Starter, a practitioner sharing what their team is building with AI, followed by open Q&A. From there, the room breaks into intimate discussions where everyone has a seat at the table. Every attendee brings their own experience. Every attendee contributes. No pitches. No performative networking. Just senior technical leaders being honest about the architectures they're choosing, the tradeoffs they're making, & what they wish they'd figured out sooner. TRENDING THEMES FOR THIS SESSION Conversations at the Forum are shaped by what technical leaders bring to the table. Themes likely to surface this evening include: From AI pilots to AI in production: breaking out of the proof-of-concept trap & scaling agents into real workflows Connecting AI to legacy systems: architectural patterns for integrating modern AI with 20-year-old stacks without breaking everything The AI tooling budget problem: balancing experimentation with unsustainable spend as engineers blow through AI tool budgets Engineers as curators, not creators: the shift from writing code to orchestrating AI agents, reusable components, & external services MCP, multi-agent systems, & the orchestration layer: what's working, what's overhyped, & what technical leaders are actually building Guardrails & governance for AI-generated code: who's accountable when the AI writes it, & what review processes actually hold up in production Presented in partnership with Tecla Tecla gives companies flexible access to vetted talent across the US & Latin America, developed for AI-native work & available from fractional engagements to dedicated nearshore pods. Learn more at www.tecla.io THE FORMAT Intentionally small & highly curated, 20 to 25 max. A seated round-table dinner, private & off the record under Chatham House Rules. AGENDA 6:00 - 6:30 PM  Cocktails & passed appetizers 6:30 - 7:00 PM  Dinner is served Find a seat & get comfortable. 6:45 - 6:50 PM  GILD & Partner Welcome A few words from the GILD team & our partners on what the night holds & how we'll spend it together. 6:50 - 7:00 PM  Conversation Starter A fellow engineering leader opens the discussion with a candid perspective on AI, with a brief Q&A. 7:00 - 8:00 PM  Table discussions 8:00 - 8:30 PM  Open mingling WHO THIS IS FOR Founders  CEOs  CTOs  VPs of Engineering  Heads of AI  Technical Leaders  Product Leaders This session is for leaders responsible for building, deploying, & maintaining AI systems in production. Chatham House Rules apply. Discussion stays private.

events.name: For The Firsts: October Meetup
events.description: For The Firsts is a meetup club for those building without a blueprintExpect an evening of interesting conversation in an inviting space as you meet & mingle with other "firsts" - those who are the first in their family to choose their professional path with intention instead of inertia. This month, we'll be sitting down with Jeanelle Teves, the Chief Commercial Officer of Bugaboo, founder of Work Lunch, creator, mother, & author. Enjoy refreshing drinks, delicious bites, & the chance to connect with other professionals, creatives, students, & founders. Each of our meetups looks something like this: 6:00 - 6:30 PM: Arrival & Open Mixer 6:30 - 7:30 PM: Fireside chat with Jeanelle Teves 7:30 - 9:00 PM: Guided Mixer If you are approved, please try to arrive on time, as our events regularly hit capacity & we have many folks on the waitlist. Here's what to expect:Cringe-Free Conversation: This isn't a networking event. It's a purpose-led meetup where who you are will always be more important than what you do. The dress code is always 'come exactly as you are, meet exactly who you need'. Guided Moments of Connection: This experience is at the core of For The Firsts. We'll have a few rounds of guided connection meant to introduce you to others who share your story. Remember the first rule of For The Firsts: go deeper than your job title! Firsts, not Followers: Each meetup is curated to bring together the best possible group of professionals, creatives, & founders in NYC who are the architects of their own lives. Intention is in everything we do, & you'll find that in the people you meet. Remember, the best way to get to know someone is to get someone to know you. I want to encourage you to connect on who you are & your purpose for your work & life. Remember Rule #1: No job titles, go deeper. events.description: Edition 5.0. Theme, year end capital. The monthly room where founders, investors & operators actually get matched. Capped & curated. Everyone leaves with at least one named introduction & the framing for the conversation. November is when allocators are deploying what is left of the year & family offices are planning the next one. This edition leans toward the capital side of the network. Who we are. Propel Earth has run 100+ events & built a network of 36,000+ founders, investors, operators, & service providers across six continents. We are not an events company. We are an outcomes company that happens to use rooms. You bring the intent. We deliver the outcome. This is not a business card room. We cap it at 40-50 people & we curate it. Tell us what you are building & who you need when you register, & before you walk in we hand you at least one match: a specific person, plus the framing for the conversation. Everyone leaves having met someone who matters to what they are working on. You do not need to apply to the cohort to attend. This room is open. Tickets Early Access - $20. events.name: Solution Smithing: How To Raise & Give A Million Dollars, with The Haven Fund
events.description: Join Anew & pop-up foundation The Haven Fund on October 20th for a brainstorming discussion on an urgent need: how to deploy resources efficiently & quickly towards the most pressing issues of our time. The Haven Fund, part of Anew's Fall 2025 cohort of Entrepreneurs in Residence, was born out of a desire to tackle an urgent problem - the immigration crackdown in NYC - by directing capital quickly to those organizations on the ground with the deepest knowledge of the issue. Since Lisa Cowan started this endeavor at the beginning of this year, it has distributed almost $1 million in funds to organizations throughout New York City, no strings attached. In an era of rolling, overlapping crises, we want to ask the audience & panelists, is this model replicable? If so, what would it take to create a template that anyone can use to tackle issues in their community & in different places? Join us as we together explore why this model was a success & how might The Haven Fund scale this model to address additional urgent issues. Panelists include: Iara Peng, Founder & CEO, JustFund, Emily Shechtman, Founder & Director, South Brooklyn Sanctuary, & Jennifer Ching, Executive Director, North Star Fund Anew is a gathering space & discovery center for social transformation located in NYC. We host interactive events & workshops, an accelerator program for nonprofits, & a retail lab featuring ethically-sourced coffee & gifts. The Haven Fund is a pop-up foundation that is raising $1 million in 1 year to support neighborhood-level immigration organizations in New York City. Lisa Cowan is the founder & Director of the Haven Fund. Formerly the Vice President of the Robert Sterling Clark Foundation, she is an organizer, weaver, writer & New Yorker.

events.name: An UNMUTED Book Club: The 100 Years War On Palestine
events.description: READING NOT REQUIRED - just be curious! Next up: Rashid Khalidi's The Hundred Years' War on Palestine, the 2020 book that argues the Israeli-Palestinian conflict isn't simply a tragic struggle between two peoples claiming the same land, but a century-long colonial campaign against Palestinians, backed first by Britain & later by the United States. Khalidi, a Palestinian-American historian at Columbia, tells the story through six turning points, beginning with the 1917 Balfour Declaration & moving through the creation of Israel, the wars that followed, & the failures of the peace process. Drawing on historical archives & his own family's experiences, he makes a provocative argument: that Palestinians have never been negotiating on equal terms, & that understanding the conflict as a dispute between two competing national movements obscures the enormous imbalance of power between them. It's a forceful challenge to conventional accounts of Israel's founding, Zionism, & America's role in the region, & one that raises uncomfortable questions about nationalism, colonialism, & self-determination. Show up even if you only got through a chunk. We'll talk about where Khalidi's account is most convincing, where it leaves out important context, whether Zionism is best understood as a colonial movement or a national liberation movement, & what his interpretation of the past means for the possibility of peace today. UNMUTED is a discussion forum for the politically curious. Accessible. Engaging. Social. Open-minded is the name of the game. Join your people.

events.name: The Human Edge: A Founders' Cacao Salon
events.description: The Human Edge: A Founders Salon for the Age of AIBreakfast  Cacao  Capital  Curated Connection AI is making it easier than ever to build. But trust, conviction, introductions, & the relationships that actually move companies forward are still deeply human. The Human Edge brings together an intimate group of founders, investors, & operators for a morning in Tribeca designed around useful insight & meaningful connection. The morning is structured so the right conversations have time to actually go somewhere. What you'll walk away withA current read on fundraising & what investors are paying attention to, fresh from San Francisco Tech Week A practical perspective on leading teams & building companies as AI changes how we work Three or four people you'll genuinely want to reconnect with A focused, energizing start to your day The morning9:45 AM  Doors openBreakfast & arrival 10:00 AM  Welcome 10:15 AM  Cacao openingA short guided ritual with Sasha Sakhar to arrive, settle in, & set an intention for the morning. 10:45 AM  What investors are seeing nowTanya Montman shares observations from San Francisco Tech Week: where capital is moving, what investors are asking founders, & how AI is changing the fundraising landscape. 11:00 AM  The human side of building with AIGeoff Scott on building companies, teams, & products where AI amplifies people rather than replaces human leadership. 11:15 AM  Open conversation & Q&A 11:30 AM  Curated connection roundsGuided small-group conversations matched around stage, interests, & goals so the conversation gets past the usual networking script. 11:50 AM  Closing + open networking 12:00 PM  Close In the room Tanya Montman  VC & fundraising advisor. After a decade at J.P. Morgan across leveraged finance & M&A, Tanya founded StartLinkVentures to connect founders with capital & advises companies across New York, Boston, & Silicon Valley.  Geoff Scott  CTO, founder, & advisor. Three companies started, four exits, four AI patents, & still coding. Board member at SIM New York Metro & creator of KindnessFlywheel.org, focused on human-centered leadership in the age of AI.  Sasha Sakhar  Founder of SUGARHAUS, an NYC experiential studio reimagining how people gather. For seven years, Sasha has facilitated cacao rituals, connection experiences, & curated gatherings for founders, teams, & creatives. Why cacao?Ceremonial cacao creates a simple transition from doing to being present. Its naturally occurring theobromine offers a gentler, steadier lift than coffee, while the ritual gives us something rare in founder culture: a moment to arrive before the titles, pitches, & ideas begin. You don't need to know anything about cacao. Just come curious. Who it's forEarly-stage founders with a product in market, particularly those preparing for or currently raising, alongside selected operators, angels, investors, & ecosystem builders. An intimate group. Curated guest list.  Fabrik NYC  12-16 Vestry St, 4th Floor  Tribeca Tuesday, October 20  Doors 9:45 AM  Program 10:00 AM-12:00 PM $35  breakfast + ceremonial cacao included Phones away during the facilitated portion so the room gets everyone's full attention

events.name: Business Funding - An International Perspective
events.description: Every stage of growing a business is a funding decision, even when it doesn't feel like one. How you pay for the next market, the next hire, the next acquisition quietly shapes what the business is worth years later, & who you can sell it to. Across the Atlantic, the options multiply & the advice gets thinner. During the evening, hear from speakers across the corporate lifecycle, sharing their different funding, expansion & exit stories, so you leave with greater insight & awareness of the opportunities, & the pitfalls to avoid. Designed for international founders & business executives planning to grow in New York City, the discussion will cover the advantages, tradeoffs, & tactics involved in raising capital from VC & PE sources.  Speakers Dan Jaeck is a Principal at Crane VC, based between New York & London, where he partners with founders building transformational software companies.Before joining Crane, he spent four years at Eniac Ventures in NYC, investing in AI application-layer & infrastructure companies. Prior to Eniac, Dan began his career at Goldman Sachs in London on the Emerging Market Equities desk. Joel Goschalk is a Senior Director at Dundon Advisers, advising middle-market companies on recapitalizations, restructurings & credit. He started as a London insolvency practitioner, co-founded & scaled a UK litigation funding & private equity business (Cavendish IP Solutions), & has spent over a decade as COO of a family office, advising on fundraising rounds, fund formation across the UK, US & offshore, & cross-border expansion.  Co-host: The Transatlantic Innovation Hub, is New York's launch pad for Italian & European companies, to help them successfully enter & scale in the U.S. market. Located in the heart of Manhattan, TIH serves as a landing pad for innovation ecosystems, providing companies with both a physical presence in New York & a structured set of market access services to accelerate their U.S. expansion. The Knowledge Shop is the founder community in NYC. We are industry & stage agnostic, helping not just startups grow, but supporting the founders building them.  Founding Partner: Sabre Integrated has been providing commercial security systems in NYC since 2000.From access control & video surveillance to fully integrated security systems, they design, install & support your business every step of the way  Charity Partner: The St George's Society of New York, provides life-changing support to immigrants from Britain & the Commonwealth in New York. Established in 1770, we're the second-oldest charity in the city. We hold events year round - join us for Pancake day   Find even more Tech events at: www.foundereventsnyc.com

events.name: Deal Flow - NYC's First VC Hackathon
events.description: Event DescriptionNew York is getting its first VC hackathon, & you're building for the people who write the checks. Deal Flow is a one-day, in-person hackathon hosted by localhost:nyc & VCLab. You get 9 hours to build working products for the real problems VCs face every day. Partners from NYC's top funds judge live, & the best teams leave with intros to those funds. Problem StatementVenture capital runs on spreadsheets, gut feel & endless inbox triage. Firms move billions of dollars with tools that haven't changed in a decade. Your challenge is to build software that helps VCs find better companies, make faster decisions & support their founders after the check clears. The Challenge ThemeSourcing: finding breakout founders before everyone else does Diligence: market maps, competitive analysis & memo drafting Portfolio ops: helping funds support their companies at scale LP reporting: making fund updates less painful & more useful Deal pipeline & CRM workflows that VCs will actually use What to Expect9 hours of focused building, 9 AM to 6 PM Real VC problems, with investors in the room to test your ideas against Teams of 4 Time to meet founders, engineers & investors from across NYC Live demos to a panel of VC judges at the end of the day Food & drinks all day PrizesTo Be Announced. JudgesAbeera Saeed is the Ventures Principal at Plug & Play, investing in Enterprise & AI B2B SaaS companies from Pre-Seed to Series A. Michael Barone - Associate at Everywhere Ventures, a global pre-seed venture capital firm. D. J. Patel - VC | 3x exited founder. Garrett Higgins is a skilled operator with experience running Finance & GTM Operations at high growth companies & an angel investor. He loves helping founders win & drive growth. Radhika Khandelwal builds AI agents for a living as a product leader at Wand AI, & she's spent years in the VC world seeing what makes startups stick. She'll want to see both slick code & a real business. Bettina Sosa is co-founder & CEO of Yaven, building a local-first AI workforce for independent businesses. Who Should AttendPre-seed & seed founders Engineers Builders who have felt the pain of fundraising firsthand Anyone curious about how venture capital actually works from the inside You don't need VC experience or a finished idea. Just show up ready to build. SponsorsSeedLegals is your one-stop legal platform from idea to Series A & beyond. Incorporate your Delaware C Corp or convert your to a C Corp, raise with SAFEs, manage your cap table, give stock options to your team, do a priced round, all on one platform, for way less than paying lawyers, with an amazing team to help. Hostslocalhost:nyc: Making NYC the biggest startup ecosystem in the world. Tracy Huang: VC Lab & CEO of Interlink IQ Olivia Iarmak - Researcher | Meta Reality Labs. ConnNext is a next-gen mobile app & community built for career growth. Visionbrew helps people be 2 places at once with 3D AI avatars. Pulse NYC AI - A community, incubator, & venture fund built for founders, researchers, & technologists shaping the future of AI in New York City.

events.name: PMAI: Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Sales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. - Bring a computer. You're writing three things tonight.- Most founders can get meetings. The deals die after meeting one.- You'll leave with your buyer in one sentence, a cold email written to a real person, & five questions for your next call. About Farzad, the speaker Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding & generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.
