events.description: Join Antoine Jebara (Co-founder, JumpCloud) & Noah Landow (Founder & CEO, Macktez) for an informal conversation between an expert on scaling global technology companies & the evolution of identity & access management & the founder of a technology consulting firm. In an era defined by remote work & the rapid rise of agentic AI, the concepts of identity & security are shifting beneath our feet. As AI agents begin to act on our behalf, how do we maintain control, responsibility, & security? If an AI agent executes a transaction or accesses a database, who is truly holding the keys? Antoine brings a unique perspective from the front lines of this transition, from pioneering decentralized 2FA & password management at MYKI to driving global strategy & partner ecosystems at JumpCloud. Join us at the Macktez office, after work, over light snacks & sips, for an exploratory conversation on the challenges of scaling fast-growing global companies & how different security architectures impact our long-term safety in a cloud-first world. We will dive into the shifting landscape of encryption, the unique hurdles of managing remote-first organizations, & what it truly means to "identity" ourselves in the age of AI. Photography, audio, & video recording may occur at this event & by attending you consent to such recording media & its release, publication, exhibition, or reproduction. Event StructureWe ask that guests arrive between 7-7:30 pm to minimize disruption during the talk. 7 pm - Doors open, opportunity to mingle over snacks & sips with other attendees7:30 pm - Guests take their seats for the talk8:15 pm - Informal mixer resumes On AttendanceWe have a limited capacity. events.name: Vibecoding 101
events.description: A 4-week scaffolded, hands-on introduction to vibecoding for beginners.Vibecoding, or AI-assisted software development, is the practice of guiding coding agents to translate your ideas into working software - without writing code yourself. We see vibecoding as 4 different product skills in a trench coat. While they may not write code, effective vibecoders mobilize concepts & workflows across software engineering, design, quality assurance, & product management. This course is a scaffolded, hands-on introduction to the fundamental skills & concepts required for a sustainable vibecoding practice. Students will learn through a combination of short lectures, applied exercises, personalized feedback, & demos to peers. We begin by working with coding agents in a multiplayer environment designed for beginners. We will create interactive frontends, learn the basics of the terminal, build integrations with APIs, & create stateful, full-stack applications with a database & user authentication. By the end of the course, students will transition to state-of-the-art coding agents installed on their personal machines, which they will use to build & deploy a working prototype to the web. SyllabusSession 1: Coding agents & frontends We introduce the course & core concepts of vibecoding. We introduce a basic taxonomy of web architecture. Students practice creating basic interactive frontends. Session 2: CLIs, APIs, & the terminal We cover core backend & data concepts. We gently introduce the terminal. Students practice writing simple CLI programs, & integrating with an API. Session 3: Stateful full-stack applications We cover databases & user authentication; students build a full stack app. Session 4: Deployment & demos The final session covers deployment. events.name: The Age Of AI  - Live Recording Of The Builders
events.description: Bestselling biographer Walter Isaacson joins us for a live recording of the first episode of his brand-new podcast, The Builders, with Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of Microsoft AI & one of the most influential thinkers & leaders working in artificial intelligence today. AI is reshaping our world at breathtaking speed. But behind the technology, real human beings are making choices about what our future will look like, how we'll work & live, & whose vision will shape what comes next. And as AI grows more powerful, so does the unease surrounding it. Will it usher in an era of extraordinary human possibility - or are we building something we may ultimately struggle to control? On The Builders, Walter Isaacson talks to the entrepreneurs, scientists & technologists building AI & other technologies that are rapidly reshaping our world to get inside the thinking of some of the most consequential figures of our time. Throughout his career, Isaacson has been fascinated by the people who change the world - from Leonardo da Vinci & Albert Einstein to Steve Jobs, Jennifer Doudna & Elon Musk. With The Builders, he turns his attention to the entrepreneurs, scientists & technologists building AI & the other technologies transforming our lives. For this special live recording, Isaacson sits down with Suleyman to go inside the ideas, ambitions & decisions driving the AI revolution. From fears about jobs & misinformation to the existential question of whether superintelligent machines could one day threaten humanity itself, the stakes can feel almost impossibly high. What does it mean to build technology with the power to reshape society? Who gets to decide where it takes us? Hear two singular thinkers explore the promise, power & profound questions of the AI age & the question at the heart of The Builders: whose imagination do we want to live in?

events.name: Red Carpet Room Launch Party
events.description: If you show up with a backpack or your laptop you will be banned from the event. Please leave backpacks at home. RED CARPET ROOM Formerly Fun HouseHosted by Anwar EnterprisesSaturday, October 31, 2026 Exact address released to confirmed guests 24 hours before doors. About the Event Red Carpet Room is the next chapter of Fun House, rebuilt around a single idea: the people building brands should be building them together. This is a mixer for founders, creators, & investors from the Anwar Events community, gathered in one room with a shared reason to be there. Everyone in attendance is constructing something with their name attached to it. The night is designed so the person who can unblock you is standing a few feet away. We are doing it on Halloween on purpose. The city will be full of parties where nothing happens beyond the party itself. This one gives you a panel worth sitting through, a room worth working, & footage of yourself that you will actually use. Run of Show [7pm] - Doors, check-in, & open networking to start the night[8pm] - Panel: operators who built audiences, companies, & reputations from nothing   SPECIAL GUESTS BEING REVEALED NEXT WEEK [9pm] - Open mixer, with Red Carpet Show interviews running in the back room Who's Coming The typical guest is a founder raising or building, a creator monetizing an audience, or an investor looking for both. Expect crossover from fashion, music, media, tech, art & consumer brands, since that is who the Anwar Events community actually contains. Whether you are hiring, raising, pitching a collaboration, or looking for people who take their work as seriously as you do, you will be in the right room. The Red Carpet Show Throughout the night, Ilias will pull guests aside for on-camera interviews for The Red Carpet Show. There is one question at the center of every interview: how can he help you. events.name: [Legal Engineers] What Do Clients Want - Law Firm AI Governance
events.description: What Do Clients Want? Law Firm AI Governance Clients are writing AI rules for their law firms: outside counsel guidelines that ban public AI tools, insurance carriers that require approval for each AI use or reserve the right to audit it, procurement questionnaires that ask how AI use is controlled. What does it take to meet those rules, & to prove you did? We will bring real, published client AI requirements. Pick one & build an approach to it: the policy, tools, workflow or checks a firm would need, & how it would show the client it complied. Or show a governance tool you use or have tried, from approved-tool lists & logging to governance platforms & things you built. Laptops open; no coding required; demos encouraged. ICME Labs will show how PreFlight lets firms prove to clients that their AI followed the rules, without disclosing client data. We finish with the group's map of what clients are asking for, the approaches that work, & the gaps nobody has solved yet. Our first session brought 47 legal engineers to Falcon Rappaport & Berkman to test which AI tools invent case law. This one turns to the rules clients are writing for the firms that use AI. Date: Wednesday, October 14, 4:00pm - 5:30pm Location: Meeting Room A, 40 Wall St, 28th Floor, New York. Legal Engineers NYC is a hands-on group for people who turn law, policy, & practice into the workflows, agents, evals, & controls that run legal work. We meet weekly on Thursdays in Manhattan, laptops open, & build something each time. Any platform counts, & no coding required. Legal Engineers NYC is organized by ICME Labs & led by cofounder Houman Shadab. Contact houman@icme.io to host or sponsor a session.

events.name: Faith At Work - Christians Working In Big Tech
events.description: Our daily work can be a calling only if it is re-conceived as God's assignment to serve others.  Tim Keller, Every Good Endeavor: Connecting Your Work to God's Work So many of us fool ourselves, believing our work is all about us: What can I accomplish? What do I get from it? Will it give me the money & life that I crave? We're convinced there's a better, different path Christians are meant to consider in how you can show up at work with a sacrificial posture in the tech space. On October 12th, FaithTech NYC is putting a panel together of Christians working in Big Tech companies who've had to work it out on the job, under deadline, with serious consequences. During out time together, we'll unpack: How they make tough decisions based on what the gospel compels us to consider. How they lead & navigate layoffs when they're the one delivering the news. How they talk about Jesus with their co-workers & how you can too. How they think about serving their team in the midst of a work culture obsessed with performance & output. Why their faith has made them better at their job. We'll make some room for your questions at the end. Our hope is that you come away encouraged & inspired to show up different at work the next day. Light food will be provided (donations are appreciated). See you there!

events.name: Brooklyn Navy Yard Annual Open House
events.description: Explore cool spots, meet makers, & dive into history at the Brooklyn Navy Yard Annual Open House! The Brooklyn Navy Yard's Annual Open House Discover the Yard's 300-acre innovative campus during our Annual Open House, part of Open House New York Weekend. Step inside the studios of businesses in fashion, design, & technology for exclusive behind-the-scenes access & immersive activations. This day celebrates our campus of makers & offers artists, designers, entrepreneurs, & neighbors alike the chance to connect with peers, explore our campus & the businesses who thrive here, & experience the innovation at the Yard up close. This year, we've created two unqiue tracks to guide you through our campus: Creative Currents- Creativity flows through the Brooklyn Navy Yard; home to hundreds of artists, ranging from painters to photographers to jewelers. They'll be opening their studios to the public, inviting audiences in for a rare opportunity to view their work, learn about their processes, inspirations, & their journeys here at the Yard. BNY Past, Present, & Future - From our start in 1801 as a premiere ship building facility, we've always been on the cutting edge of manufacturing & technology, right here in New York City. On our campus, rich history meets an innovative future, as we look ahead towards what's next in the fields of space tech, green energy, robotics, & more. Come tour our waterfront campus & take in centuries of legacy, while gaining access to the labs & studios where the tech of the future is being made.   Also Featuring... Arnsenal's Tequila & Whisky Tasting Food Trucks Live Art Demos   BNYDC RULES, PROTOCOLS & ACKNOWLEDGEMENT  Check-In Procedure All visitors must check-in at Building 77. Visitors arriving through other entry points will be redirected to enter through official entry locations.All visitors must register for the event. No one will be admitted without an official RSVP. It is highly recommended that you RSVP in advance although day of registration is permitted.A valid photo ID is required for entry. Visitors under 18 must be accompanied by an adult & do not need a photo ID.Visitors who fail to register or do not present a valid photo ID will be denied entry.Expect an estimated 5-minute check-in & security screening process.Security Protocols All bags will be checked at the entrance for prohibited items.Prohibited items include but are not limited to alcohol; weapons, noise-making devices; laser pointers; fireworks; professional camera equipment; large political signs, banners, or flags; & other materials that may cause harm, damage, or disruption.Bags must not exceed the size of a standard school backpack (Approximately 18 x 14 x 6)Large bags, including roller bags, will not be permitted. Campus Rules for Event All visitors must stay in approved areas. Visitors should not enter closed or restricted spaces during the event. This includes active construction areas.If buildings & businesses are open, please be respectful while in their spaces & remain mindful that these are working studios & manufacturing centers.Participating businesses may choose to close their spaces at their discretion, including if they determine that visitors are being disruptive.The Brooklyn Navy Yard is an active manufacturing & industrial campus. Furthermore, you release the Brooklyn Navy Yard Development Corporation, its officers, employees, & agents, from any liability in connection with such photography or videography & the use thereof, & waive any claims you may have for payment in connection with such materials & the use thereof.  Newsletter Acknowledgement & Permission By signing up for this event, you are agreeing to be added to the free Brooklyn Navy Yard public newsletter list. Newsletters are sent 1 - 2 times each month & list public programs, events, & exhibitions at the Yard. You may unsubscribe at any time.

events.name: Hack For Impact - AI Workflow Hackathon
events.description: Pioneering Minds AI: Hack for ImpactAn AI Workflow HackathonDont just use AI. Redesign how work gets done.AI is changing how we research, learn, build products, analyze contracts, manage money, & make decisions. But adding a chatbot to an existing process is not the same as building an AI-native workflow.The real opportunity is to rethink the workflow itself:What should humans still do?What should AI handle?What can be automated entirely?And where does human judgment become even more important?This is a one-day hackathon where participants redesign real-world workflows using AI.Teams will choose a problem from one of four tracks, identify a broken or inefficient workflow, & build an AI-native product, agent, or system that makes it dramatically better.You do not need to arrive with a startup idea.Come with curiosity. Find a problem. Build something.The winning teams can also secure their spot at our upcoming Pitching Masterclass, where they can sharpen their story, product positioning, & pitch.The ChallengeTeams will identify an existing workflow & redesign it for the age of AI.Your project should answer three questions:What is broken, slow, repetitive, or unnecessarily difficult today?What should AI do differently?What does the new workflow look like when AI is built into it from the beginning?Projects can take the form of an AI agent, internal tool, workflow automation, consumer product, enterprise application, or prototype.Hackathon TracksParticipants may choose one of four tracks.Critical Thinking & LearningAI can produce answers in seconds. But getting an answer is not the same as understanding something. As AI becomes capable of performing more cognitive tasks, skills such as critical thinking, judgment, curiosity, problem decomposition, & learning how to learn may become even more important. Build a product or workflow that uses AI to help people think better rather than simply think less.AI for Product Management WorkflowsProduct managers spend enormous amounts of time gathering information, coordinating teams, analyzing feedback, writing documents, prioritizing ideas, & turning ambiguity into decisions.Many of these workflows were designed before AI existed. Redesign them.Legal Tech WorkflowsLegal work is full of complex, document-heavy processes where accuracy, judgment, & context matter.AI creates an opportunity to fundamentally rethink how legal professionals research, review, draft, analyze, & manage information.They must also consider accuracy, explainability, accountability, & human review.Fintech & Insurtech WorkflowsFinancial services & insurance involve some of the most complex workflows in business: underwriting, compliance, risk assessment, fraud detection, claims, financial analysis, & customer onboarding.Many still involve fragmented systems, repetitive manual review, & enormous amounts of unstructured data.What You'll BuildTeams will have one day to identify a problem, design a solution, build a prototype, & present it to our judges.Your prototype does not need to be production-ready.We care about:The quality of the problemHow thoughtfully you redesign the workflowHow meaningfully AI improves the processThe usability of your prototypeWhether someone would actually use itAll backgrounds are welcome.You do not need to be an engineer to participate.Product managers, designers, lawyers, finance professionals, founders, students, operators, & domain experts are strongly encouraged to join.Coaching & mentorship will be available onsite.What We'll ExploreAI agents & workflow automationHuman + events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: AI & China
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In July, a Chinese lab you'd probably never heard of published Kimi K3: 2.8 trillion parameters, billed as the largest open model on earth, weights posted free on Hugging Face for anyone to download. It's one of four Chinese labs that spent the last year closing the gap with the American frontier, then giving the result away. Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi. Four of the five most-used open models in the world now come out of Beijing, & American developers are running them inside hospitals, law firms, & startups because they're the cheapest, fastest tools available. No API someone in Washington controls. No off switch. Just download & go. One camp says a model is just math. Open weights run on a consumer's machine, the code is right there to inspect, & cutting Americans off from the best tools on the planet is how you lose a technology race. The other camp says the giveaway is the strategy. China seeds the world's infrastructure with their standards, their defaults, their assumptions, & the dependency follows once switching costs become unbeatable. So: should Americans be allowed to build on Chinese open-weight models or is this the new Cold War's Monkey's Paw? Arguing for, Rob Li is Managing Partner of Amont Partners, a New York global equity firm that invests across the US & Asia. He has spent his career putting capital on both sides of the Pacific, from Yum China to Alibaba deals, & he thinks the country that walls itself off from the best tools available loses. Arguing against, Will McKelvey is a Principal at Lerer Hippeau, one of New York's oldest venture firms, where he backs early-stage founders & spends his days watching for the future of AI, especially in consumer. He got his start by way of a congressional office, & he thinks the cheapest model on the market is the one you pay for slowly. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones. In collaboration with COMMITTEE OF 100Committee of 100 (C100) is a nonprofit U.S. leadership organization of distinguished Chinese Americans dedicated to advancing the full participation of Chinese Americans in American society & fostering constructive U.S.-China relations. For more than 35 years, C100 has brought together leaders across business, government, academia, technology, media, the arts, & other fields to advance its dual mission. Learn more at committee100.org.

events.name: An Unmuted Debate - Peptides vs The People
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In partnership with Pepper NYC & the Peptide Club of NYC A peptide to heal your tendon. An injection to rebuild your knee. Exosomes to make your body younger. Regenerative medicine is moving fast, & consumers increasingly don't want to wait ten years for the clinical trials to catch up (the AIDS crisis..). Some of these treatments have real science behind them. Others have promising early evidence. And some are being sold for thousands of dollars long before anyone can say with confidence that they actually work. But maybe that's the point. We let adults make risky decisions everywhere else. If a patient understands the evidence is uncertain, why shouldn't they be allowed to spend their own money trying something experimental? The alternative is the basic bargain medicine has relied on for decades: prove it works before you sell it. Because when the person explaining the risks is also making money from the treatment, "informed consent" can start looking a lot like a sales pitch. So: should experimental regenerative therapies be sold to consumers, or should medicine have to prove they work first? Arguing for, Julius Ritter is the founder of the California Peptide Club & CEO of Transcendence, a longevity company working with peptide, exosome, & regenerative therapies. He's part of a growing movement that thinks patients & physicians should have much more freedom to experiment at the frontier of medicine. Arguing against, Dr. Tiana Woolridge is a primary sports medicine physician at Hospital for Special Surgery, double board certified in pediatrics & sports medicine. She's trained in regenerative treatments like PRP herself, which is exactly why she thinks there's a difference between promising medicine & selling something before the evidence is there. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

events.name: Propel Demo Day  Innovation In Public Cohort Showcase
events.description: Ten companies. Twelve minutes each. An investor room in New York. Who we are. Propel Earth has run 100+ events & built a network of 36,000+ founders, investors, operators, & service providers across six continents. We are not an events company. We are an outcomes company that happens to use rooms. You bring the intent. We deliver the outcome. Demo Night NYC is the biggest room we have ever run, 26,666 people on the guest list & 35+ investors in the room. This is that format, built for the companies coming out of our cohort & the investors who back them. Every attendee tells us at registration what they are building & who they need to meet. Before doors open we hand you at least one named introduction plus the framing for the conversation. Founders leave with investor conversations, investors leave with deal flow they did not have to source. The night 6:00 Doors, drinks, & your matches are waiting7:00 Ten companies, twelve minutes each, pitch & questions8:15 Room favourite, voted live8:30 Open floor with the investors in the room9:00 Close Tickets General admission, free. Open to founders, investors, operators & anyone building.Present Your Company, 250 dollars. Ten slots only. Stage time in front of an investor room, professional video of your pitch, & your company in the post event send.Title Sponsor, 5,000 dollars. One per Demo Day. Naming rights, logo on all promotion & the photo backdrop, a brand moment from the stage, & the full registrant list within 48 hours.Free for Propel Private Network members. What Propel actually does for you 1  Innovation in Public, our GTM accelerator. For founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go to market: content, distribution, & more sales. Four weeks, twice a week, building in public, closing with a public showcase at Propel Demo Day in front of an investor room. Applications for the next cohort are open at this link. 2  The Propel Private Network. Stop networking. Start getting matched. Every month we personally hand you three introductions chosen for what you need right now - someone who can pay you, hire you, or move your company forward. It works both ways: you go into the pool too. Founding rate $200/mo, first 25 members, locked for life  Claim a founding membership 3  Propel Community Coworking x Wayo Club. Come Wednesday night, then come back Thursday & build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, founded by Jason Malefakis. Wayo is a curated community workspace network where members work from premium venues alongside thoughtfully selected founders, operators, & consultants they can collaborate with, refer, hire, or do business with. Attendees typically report being 1.5 to 2x more productive than working from home or a cafe, & leave with 2 to 3 meaningful connections. Lunch is included. Register with us  Propel Community Coworking 1.0  Get a Wayo Community Workday membership  Join the Wayo Anytime waitlist 4  Featured Founder. Build your founder or service-provider profile on Propel & we will give you one additional intro on us  propel.earth/featured-founders 5  Providers already in the room. This is not theoretical. Moshe Cohen, CPA of Cohen & Co runs tax strategy, bookkeeping & fractional CFO work for Propel founders & takes bookings through us. Thirty minute paid session, 120 dollars  Book Moshe. Stephen Michael Consulting, a 45 minute strategy call for funded founders raising, investors deploying, & enterprises entering the startup ecosystem, 150 dollars  Book a strategy call. If you provide a service & want a table at the next one, that is what the provider ticket is. On camera: Nik Michael, host of the Pivot Point podcast, is shooting photography, video, & follow up interviews with select attendees. Nik is a licensed clinician with more than thirty years in counseling & decades in business, education, & investing, & his show explores the moments where transformation begins. Watch the show on YouTube  Listen on Spotify or Apple Podcasts  More at counselingtherapy.com/pivotpoint. Want to be featured, reach out to him directly. Newsletter  propelearth.beehiiv.com  Propel Earth  propel.earth  Questions, text Stephen at 516 307 6380. About The WilsonThe Wilson NYC is a popular American comfort-food restaurant & bar located in NoMad/Chelsea. While the restaurant does not hold traditional culinary stars (like Michelin), it acts as a highly-rated, frequent event space for awards shows & local hospitality honors due to its event duplex & outdoor patio. The Wilson has also been celebrated for supporting its employees through the One Fair Wage What Propel does, & what it has produced Nine ways we connect this network. Every one of these is a room we have already run. Founders & Investors. We put founders in rooms with the people who write checks. Demo Night NYC ran in front of 35+ investors. Founders x Investors Night at PhD Lounge, the Funders x Founders High Line Walk, the Harvard Club Investment Dinner, & the NYTW Pitch Competition with 800+ registrations. Every monthly mixer does the same thing at a smaller scale, which is why we cap the room & match you before you arrive. Founders & Service Providers. You tell us what you need & we match you to someone vetted who does it. Legal, tax, engineering, design, growth, operations. Our Founders Meet Providers rooms exist for exactly this, & the Propel Marketplace runs it year round. Featured provider this month is Moshe Cohen, CPA, offering a 30 minute startup tax & finance session for $120. Book a session or browse the marketplace Work with Stephen directly. A 45 minute strategy call for funded founders raising, investors deploying, & enterprises trying to get into the startup ecosystem. Book a strategy call, browse the marketplace50 Hiring & Talent. Our Tech Job Fair & Developer Job Fair each brought over 150 engineers & operators into the room. That now runs continuously on Propel Earth Jobs, where employers, candidates, & referrers all work in one place. Post a role or find one Product Launches. We launch products to the whole network. The ConnNext App Launch Party pulled 475 registrations, the largest event we have ever run. BECOMEFAMOUS.AI pulled 222. If you are launching something & you need a room, reply to this & we will build it. Capital & Family Office. The capital side of the network. events.name: Urban Future Summit - 10 Years Of Impact
events.description: The 2026 Urban Future Summit is supported by New York Community Trust, New York State Energy Research & Development Authority, MUFG Bank, & NYU Tandon School of Engineering - this year is extra special as we're celebrating 10 years of supporting climate innovation & the entrepreneurs who have shaped it. 2 PRIZE TRACKS. 8 FINALISTS. HEAR THEM PITCH ON 10/22.Read the full press release  Climate Adaptation Prize: focused on solutions that help communities & ecosystems adapt to & build resilience against the impacts of climate change. Airbuild: Autonomous biological nutrient recovery systems that convert wastewater nutrients into carbon-sequestering biochar fertilizer, helping municipalities meet EPA compliance & cut costs while creating new revenue for farmers. Class 3 Technologies: Engineering-grade, building-level climate risk assessments powered by Iris, a proprietary simulation engine, helping large property owners quantify physical vulnerability & evaluate resilience strategies across their portfolios, while extending that same risk intelligence to underserved communities. Rarefied: A sunlight-driven propulsion mechanism enabling persistent flight in near-space, building a new atmospheric data layer to improve weather forecasting, disaster resilience, & climate risk modeling - data especially valuable in equatorial & developing regions, where sparse observations weaken storm & drought forecasts. Supercool Earth: An end-to-end precipitation enhancement platform that uses biology to increase rain & snowfall on demand for ski resorts, water utilities, hydropower operators, & agriculture, giving water-scarce communities a tool to stabilize supply before rationing or crop failure set in. Climate Mitigation Prize: focused on solutions that reduce greenhouse gas emissions & mitigate the impacts of climate change. Arcticar: An intelligent, clean energy platform for the cold chain, replacing diesel-powered trailer refrigeration with lower-cost electric units & integrated battery storage, eliminating the emissions & noise pollution reefers create. Emulate Cities: AI infrastructure that helps local governments automate permit review, cutting permitting timelines from weeks to minutes to accelerate deployment of housing, clean energy, & climate-resilient infrastructure. Every Electric: Operator of New York City's largest plug-in powerbank network, giving households access to affordable backup power while strengthening grid reliability for all New Yorkers. Ultropia: An ultrasonic mechanical water extraction platform that removes moisture from materials, targeting the energy-intensive gas dryers used across the industrial laundry industry. For more than a decade, the Urban Future Prize Competition has identified & accelerated the founders building the technologies, infrastructure, & systems that cities need to thrive in a changing world. What begins as an early-stage idea has repeatedly become a market-shaping company: 23 startups supported, more than $1 million awarded in non-dilutive funding, & over $515 million in follow-on capital raised - a remarkable 515x return on prize dollars deployed. At this year's Urban Future Summit, attendees will actively participate in the next chapter of that story. The Summit will culminate with presentations from the 2026 Urban Future Prize Competition finalists - founders tackling some of the most urgent challenges we're facing today, from climate resilience & emissions reduction to mobility, energy, & the circular economy. These entrepreneurs are not only competing for funding; they are competing for the opportunity to join ACRE, New York's longest-running climatetech incubator, where breakthrough ideas are transformed into scalable businesses. This year marks an important milestone for the Urban Future Prize Competition. For the first time, four awardees will be selected across the Climate Adaptation & Climate Mitigation prize tracks. Two winners get access to $50k & two runner-up teams in each track will also receive $10k in non-dilutive funding & admission into the ACRE Incubator. By expanding support to a broader cohort of entrepreneurs, we're investing in a larger pipeline of innovators at a moment when climate resilience & decarbonization must advance together.

events.name: The Deployment Room: 6 Active Funds, Funding Founders (Seed to Series A+)
events.description: The Builder Series: A 60,000+ member community redefining what networking looks like curating founders, investors into intentional rooms built for experiences people remember & relationships that last. It's a direct line to the most ambitious builders. Find us here: Instagram  LinkedIn  TikTok  Facebook  X : WhatsApp Broad Channel (Not a GC) August was our pilot. Here's how it performed. Our intent 20 founders, 6 investors. The real turnout: 30 guests: 20 founders, 10 capital allocators $70M+ raised collectively by the founders present $3.5M average raised per founder $2.3B+ combined AUM across the investors $1M average check, $100K minimum $10M+ in live check capacity This is today objective: Every founder in the room is doing $1M+ in ARR or has raised a round of $1M or more. Raised your 1st round, onto your 2nd, or bootstrapped to $1M ARR? You're in the right place. Every investor here is from our network. We're curating this room deliberately, matching founders to the investors most likely to be a fit, & making the introduction ourselves. The goal here: Getting founders funded by our investor network. The 6 Investors joining us from our network: (More will be joining) Francesca Poupel: F&G Capital Partners (Managing Partner): Backing founders from pre-seed to Series A in AI, fintech, & blockchain, writing $300K-$500K checks & partnering closely with teams as they scale. Mahir Laul (Partner) representing Laul Global a family office & holding company operating four interconnected pillars: Education Engine, Real Assets, Future Ventures, & Acquisitions. One integrated system. One long-term vision. Laul Global is owned & operated by the Laul family. We started with a single student recruitment company. We built it into one of Canada's most diversified education holding groups. Today the portfolio spans institutions, edtech, real estate, & a tech venture studio, with reach across 20+ countries & no plans to slow down.  Triet Leminh: Principal, LMT Partners: Lawyer, founder, & investor backing pre-seed to Series A founders building in enterprise & regulated industries. Writing $200K-$300K checks.  Andrew Antar (General Partner, AG Venture Capital): A generalist fund backing extraordinary founders, sector agnostic. Also a Venture Partner at Arcadian Capital, focused on late-stage secondaries & pre-IPO tech, & served as Crypto Policy Advisor to the NYC Office of the Mayor - advising on the city's crypto regulatory framework & organizing the NYC Crypto Summit at Gracie Mansion. He is also founder of Tune.FM, a tokenized music streaming platform & digital asset marketplace, & co-founded Clear Quantum, a stealth quantum AI startup. Gonzalo Quincot (Founder, Sinober): Sinober is a financial intelligence platform that combines public & private market intelligence with institutional-grade methodology, corporate finance & proprietary AI tools to sharpen investment & capital decisions for individuals & businesses. Invests in automation, robotics, data centers & applied AI.  Shilpi Nayak: (Founder & General Partner, 434 VC): Invests in early-stage technical founders across AI, infrastructure, physical AI & emerging technology. She is also the founder of House of 434, a community bringing together founders, investors & industry leaders.  Pranav Jajapur (Co-Founder, ZERON Ventures): ZERON is an early-stage venture fund with an execution platform behind it, backing real-world technology, AI, healthcare, deep tech & climate companies building in the physical world, inside biology. Pre-seed through Series A with core deployment at seed, writing $400K-$500k checks. Preferred focus is institutionally-anchored AI: structural research relationships at academic institutions, spinouts, & founder-led research programs. Fund I in formation. Deploying Q1  All 6 senior investors confirmed. Part of building rooms is making sure real capital is present. Six investors actively deploying writing capital will be joining. Our first confirmed: Why we do this: Putting active investors in the same room as exceptional founders, & keeps the room small enough to ensure everyone actually meets. We value intentional networking & community. If you're here to meet the best of the best, this is the room. Our Sponsor: Composition WealthYour seat at the table is waiting. Your life is shaped by new beginnings, major decisions, & milestones. That's why when it comes to developing the strategies to achieve your financial goals, we make sure you have a seat at the table & are empowered with the knowledge & tools to shape your own future. At Composition Wealth, our goal is to empower you to reach YOUR goals. Chris Guarino, CFPBook some time: Calendly link What to expect for this: A Greek style lunch, courtesy of our team Conversations with fellow high-performing startup leaders An experience designed to facilitate new meaningful connections conversations with ambitious peers solving similar problems Event to be hosted at a beautiful private Soho loft Our intent is to bring good, smart humans together, & active investors together to fun incredible founders. Community has been lost & we are rebuilding it. Our Greek Inspired Menu: About the meal A three-course Greek menu. Appetizers & dessert are shared & open to everyone; each will get one entre. The format is intentionally part standing, part seated so you can enjoy incredible food without being anchored to a single table or a single conversation. Why we do this Our intent is simple: bring good, smart humans together, put active investors in the same room as incredible founders. Intentional community has been lost. We're rebuilding it.

events.name: The Rise Circle - Innovation, Access & Impact
events.description: The right connection can change the trajectory of an idea, a business, or a career.The Rise Circle: Innovation, Access & Impact Panel & Mixer brings together founders, investors, STEM & healthcare professionals, corporate leaders, & ecosystem builders for an experience designed to turn introductions into meaningful opportunities.Through a short panel conversation, attendee spotlights, & intentional networking, well explore how innovation, access, investment, & strategic relationships can help ideas move forward & create measurable impact.But this isnt a mixer where you grab a name tag, collect a few business cards, & go home.Attendees will have opportunities to share what theyre building, what theyre looking for, & where they can be a resource to others. Come ready to meet potential collaborators, investors, advisors, partners, & professionals who can help open the next door.HostFiserv iHub,  RUTGERS NewarkFeatured SpeakersGadareth Higgs, PhD | Healthcare & Life Sciences Investor + AdvisorWith more than 15 years of experience across bioinformatics, consulting, & healthcare, Gadareth works with startups navigating growth, investment, & commercialization. Through Higgs Insights, he has helped startup clients increase investor interest, raise between $200K & $7M, & secure significant investor commitments. His experience also includes precision oncology, biotechnology, ConcertAI, & McKinsey.Gary Burnett | Healthcare + Transformation ExecutiveGary works at the intersection of healthcare innovation, organizational transformation, talent strategy, & community impact. His work focuses on building cross-sector partnerships & creating strategies that improve organizational performance while expanding access & outcomes for diverse communities.Whether youre raising capital, building a company, advancing an idea, looking for strategic partners, or simply trying to find the right people to help you move forward, The Rise Circle is designed to help make the room smaller & the connections stronger.Come ready to share. Come ready to connect. Come ready to find your next opportunity.Disclaimer: By attending The Rise Circle, you consent to being photographed and/or recorded during the event. These photos & videos may be used by The Rise Circle for promotional, marketing, & educational purposes, including future events, social media, websites, & other communications.Interested in sponsoring or exhibiting? Connect with us: info@therisecircleglobal.comLearn more about UsWhy Rise Circle?Two Founders. One Encounter. Boundless Possibilities.We connected last year, survived an accelerator together (it didn't kill us, so I guess we are stronger). Several train rides (to NYC) & car rides (to Philly) later, we were more exposed to the founder ecosystem, absolutely loved the experience, but something was still missing...We are curating conversations & experiences that our ecosystem needs. And we are excited to do it right here in New Jersey.Our MissionOur mission is to create an ecosystem that facilitates strategic partnerships, with a special focus on highlighting underrepresented founders, leaders, & innovators in the STEM & Healthcare spaces; alongside the organizations, corporations, venture firms, & ecosystem partners that invest in & champion their success.HostsIdongesit Obeya | Founder, Altruistic ScribeIdongesit Obeya, RN, BSN, MSN, CCM, is a distinguished healthcare leader, professor, & advocate whose work is rooted in advancing equity, innovation, & human-centered care. As the Founder & CEO of Altruistic Scribe, she is committed to transforming health outcomes through culturally responsive education, strategic advocacy, & solutions that bridge gaps in care for underserved communities.With more than 16 years of experience across diverse healthcare settings, Idongesit brings deep expertise in nursing, case management, patient education, & public health engagement. She is widely recognized for her ability to connect clinical insight with compassionate leadership, creating meaningful impact for both individuals & communities.A passionate champion for progress at the intersection of healthcare, STEM, & innovation, Idongesit believes that the future of care must be both technologically forward & deeply humaneAdaeze Iloeje-Udeogalanya | Founder, African Women in STEMAdaeze Iloeje-Udeogalanya is a leadership & AI strategist, TEDx speaker, & the founder of African Women in STEM, a global career & leadership ecosystem advancing access & opportunities for women in STEM fields.With over 20 years of experience as an engineer, strategist, & executive in the energy sector, Adaeze has led large-scale initiatives totaling more than $500 million. Today, she works at the intersection of leadership & emerging technology, advising organizations & professionals on how AI is reshaping authority, decision-making, & visibility.Through African Women in STEM, she partners with organizations, institutions, & companies to deliver events, programming, mentorship, & initiatives that strengthen talent pipelines & expand professional opportunities. Her TEDx talk, viewed over 100,000 times, reframes cultural identity as a strategic advantage in the future of work.

events.name: Innovation in Public Mixer 5.0  Year End Capital
events.description: Edition 5.0. Theme, year end capital. The monthly room where founders, investors & operators actually get matched. Capped & curated. Everyone leaves with at least one named introduction & the framing for the conversation. November is when allocators are deploying what is left of the year & family offices are planning the next one. This edition leans toward the capital side of the network. Who we are. Propel Earth has run 100+ events & built a network of 36,000+ founders, investors, operators, & service providers across six continents. We are not an events company. We are an outcomes company that happens to use rooms. You bring the intent. We deliver the outcome. This is not a business card room. We cap it at 40-50 people & we curate it. Tell us what you are building & who you need when you register, & before you walk in we hand you at least one match: a specific person, plus the framing for the conversation. Everyone leaves having met someone who matters to what they are working on. You do not need to apply to the cohort to attend. This room is open. Tickets Early Access - $20. Limited, nearly gone.General Admission - $40.Free for Propel Private Network members. Dinner is highly encouraged - the kitchen at The Wilson is excellent. Come hungry & stay late. What Propel actually does for you 1  Innovation in Public - our GTM accelerator. For founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go-to-market: content, distribution, & more sales. Four weeks, twice a week, building in public, closing with a public showcase in front of the room. Applications open for the August cohort  Apply here 2  The Propel Private Network. Stop networking. Start getting matched. Every month we personally hand you three introductions chosen for what you need right now - someone who can pay you, hire you, or move your company forward. It works both ways: you go into the pool too. Founding rate $200/mo, first 25 members, locked for life  Claim a founding membership 3  Propel Community Coworking x Wayo Club. Come Wednesday night, then come back Thursday & build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, founded by Jason Malefakis. Wayo is a curated community workspace network where members work from premium venues alongside thoughtfully selected founders, operators, & consultants they can collaborate with, refer, hire, or do business with. Attendees typically report being 1.5 to 2x more productive than working from home or a cafe, & leave with 2 to 3 meaningful connections. Lunch is included. Register with us  Propel Community Coworking 1.0  Get a Wayo Community Workday membership  Join the Wayo Anytime waitlist 4  Featured Founder. Build your founder or service-provider profile on Propel & we will give you one additional intro on us  propel.earth/featured-founders On camera: Nik Michael of the Pivot Point podcast is shooting photography, video, & follow-up interviews with select attendees. Want to be featured, reach out to him directly. Newsletter  propelearth.beehiiv.com  Propel Earth  propel.earth  Questions, text Stephen at 516 307 6380. About The WilsonThe Wilson NYC is a popular American comfort-food restaurant & bar located in NoMad/Chelsea. While the restaurant does not hold traditional culinary stars (like Michelin), it acts as a highly-rated, frequent event space for awards shows & local hospitality honors due to its event duplex & outdoor patio. The Wilson has also been celebrated for supporting its employees through the One Fair Wage What Propel does, & what it has produced Nine ways we connect this network. Every one of these is a room we have already run. Founders & Investors. We put founders in rooms with the people who write checks. Demo Night NYC ran in front of 35+ investors. Founders x Investors Night at PhD Lounge, the Funders x Founders High Line Walk, the Harvard Club Investment Dinner, & the NYTW Pitch Competition with 800+ registrations. Every monthly mixer does the same thing at a smaller scale, which is why we cap the room & match you before you arrive. Founders & Service Providers. You tell us what you need & we match you to someone vetted who does it. Legal, tax, engineering, design, growth, operations. Our Founders Meet Providers rooms exist for exactly this, & the Propel Marketplace runs it year round. Featured provider this month is Moshe Cohen, CPA, offering a 30 minute startup tax & finance session for $120. Book a session or browse the marketplace Hiring & Talent. Our Tech Job Fair & Developer Job Fair each brought over 150 engineers & operators into the room. That now runs continuously on Propel Earth Jobs, where employers, candidates, & referrers all work in one place. Post a role or find one Product Launches. We launch products to the whole network. The ConnNext App Launch Party pulled 475 registrations, the largest event we have ever run. BECOMEFAMOUS.AI pulled 222. If you are launching something & you need a room, reply to this & we will build it. Capital & Family Office. The capital side of the network. Our Private Markets Discussion Panel drew 280 registrations & Family Office Crypto with Forum Pay brought allocators into the room. These are smaller rooms with higher stakes. See the next one Masterclasses & Info Sessions. Free, online, & taught by specialists who actually do the work. Our Social Impact Cohort Info Session drew 297 registrations. TRIIBE TALK on branding drew 157. Tax, legal, fundraising, & go to market, taught by operators. See the calendar The GTM Accelerator. Four weeks for founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go to market help: content, distribution, & more sales. You get a dedicated BDR, a custom digital asset kit, & a public showcase in front of the room. Our last cohort presented at Demo Day to 35+ investors. August applications are open & you can see how we represented the last cohort The Social Rooms. Not everything is a pitch. Foundersgiving Party & Pitch Roast drew 381 people. LABYRINTH at Hotel Chelsea drew 309. Above Fridays Rooftop Networking, Holiday Chemistry Night, & Bowling & Business. These are the rooms where relationships actually form, & they are the reason the other eight verticals work. Community Coworking. Come to the mixer on Wednesday, then come back Thursday & actually build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, coffee & lunch included. Register here The Private Network, the thread through all of it. Every vertical above runs on the same engine. You tell us what you need, we find the person, we make the introduction in writing. Members receive three curated introductions every month plus free entry to every mixer & select special events. $200 per month, & the first 25 founding members lock that rate for life. Join here Want to sponsor a room? One sponsor per event so it never feels crowded. Email stephen@propel.earth Media ConsentPhotography & Video Acknowledgement. events.name: SOSV Deep Tech Summit
events.description: Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. events.name: Spatial Analytics w/ Python
events.description: Join PyData NYC on October 27th at 6:30 PM for an evening exploring geospatial data science with Python, featuring Brendan Collins, Founder & CTO at Makepath & creator of Xarray-Spatial! Discover how Python can transform spatial data into powerful insights, from terrain analysis & hydrology to scalable CPU- & GPU-accelerated computing. Please bring your  to follow along & sign up using your official government-issued name.  Pizza & drinks will be provided - Thank you, Makepath! Agenda xarray-spatial: In & Out of the Raster-verseSpeaker: Brendan Collins (Founder & CTO at Makepath)Spatial data comes in many shapes & sizes, but some of the most powerful spatial analysis techniques begin by viewing the world as a grid.Led by the library's creator & maintainer, this talk introduces Xarray-Spatial, an open-source Python library for scalable raster analysis with CPU & GPU acceleration.We'll learn how to enter the Raster-verse by bringing spatial data into Xarray, explore the Raster-verse using algorithms for terrain analysis, hydrology, proximity, & more, & escape the Raster-verse through techniques like zonal statistics & polygonization.Finally, we'll discuss contributing to the Raster-verse, sharing lessons from maintaining Xarray-Spatial & how AI-augmented development is transforming open-source contributions, code quality, & scientific software engineering.Whether you're a GIS practitioner, data scientist, or Python developer, you'll leave with practical ideas for working with spatial data & contributing to open source.  About the SpeakerBrendan Collins is the Founder & CTO of Makepath, where he helps early-stage startups & Fortune 500 engineering teams realize their product ambitions.A former employee of Anaconda, Brendan has spent the past decade applying PyData technologies, including NumPy, Xarray, & Numba, to engineering challenges across the public, private, & nonprofit sectors.When not writing in the third person, Brendan enjoys swimming, playing the banjo, & gardening.  NetworkingConnect with fellow data enthusiasts, Python developers, researchers, & community leaders. Build meaningful connections, exchange ideas, & explore opportunities for collaboration.

events.name: Wind-Win Startup Showdown
events.description: Step into the Future of Ocean Renewables:  An Electrifying Evening with the 2026 Offshore Wind Innovation Hub Innovator Cohort!The 4th annual Wind-Win Startup Showdown offers a pitch experience like no other, spotlighting cutting-edge technology breakthroughs to transform the future of ocean renewables. This is a special year for us: the program set a record high: 118 applications & the strongest competition reviewers have seen to date. In 2026, we also drew in a more diverse cohort than ever before by broadening this year's technology scope  a 123% increase in application numbers compared to last year's, reflecting the parallel growth in industry demand for novel solutions needed in the market.Presented by the Offshore Wind Innovation Hub, this networking & pitch event brings together stakeholders across the climate landscapeinvestors, founders, academia, industry, & thought leadersfor an evening of connection, collaboration, & celebration.Come see it for yourself! Join us to engage with leading innovators tackling climates most complex challenges with bold, next-generation solutions.Refreshments & light hors d'oeuvres will be provided.AgendaDoors OpenKeynote + Welcome RemarksAlso on stage:  Tone Sndergaard, Director, Offshore Wind Innovation Hub at NYU Tandon Urban Future LabInnovator Lightning Pitches by the 2026 CohortEach of our Offshore Wind Innovation Hub partners has sent their most experienced innovation experts to provide feedback for each of the selected cohort companies.Sam Jung, SVP, Green Economy, New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYC EDC)Lyndie Hice-Dunton, Executive Director, National Offshore Wind Research & Development Consortium (NOWRDC)Robert Fenton, Head of Americas Generation Procurement, rstedStephan Kremers, Senior Technical Project Manager, VestasFireside Chat on Dual-Use Technology AdaptationNetworking & RefreshmentsMeet our 2026 FinalistsBlue Ocean Transfers Group (BOT) (New York, US) - Multipurpose, hybrid electric support vessel enabling maritime decarbonization.Bubble Robotics (California, US) - Resident fleet of autonomous underwater robots monitoring offshore infrastructure.Clema (New York, US) - Thermoelectric cooling vest for workers in extreme heat.Fleet Robotics (Massachusetts, US) - Data insights powered by submersible, autonomous cleaning & inspection robots.Hefring Marine (Iceland) - Intelligence platform combining onboard hardware with software to optimize marine operations.HiFIT USA (New York, US) - Impact treatment welding to enable life extension & lighter structures.NeuralX (California, US) - Underwater video & computer vision for fisheries monitoring & ecological data.Sail GTX (New York, US) - Platform for smarter customs workflows for offshore wind components.TMA The Hazardous Goods Companion (Germany) - RFID & AIoT inventory visibility & predictive inventory management solution.Tree Composites (The Netherlands) - Composite joints for offshore support structure to realise material & manufacturing optimization.Vital Ocean (Oregon, US) - Intelligence platform combining ocean data, marine environment, & decision interface.Stay tuned in the next few weeks on our website & LinkedIn for updates on our selected cohort!Innovation in FocusOur 2026 cohort takes the stage to pitch ocean & maritimes most promising technologies. This year's lineup features innovations spanning ports, O&M, environmental monitoring & coexistence, workforce development, installation, construction, & commissioning, maritime applications, among others. The scope doesn't just stop there. The majority of this year's solutions are dual-use, carrying relevance across adjacent industries & global markets, a reflection of just how far the blue economy reaches.Marking the official launch of the 2026 Innovator program, this event offers a unique chance to connect directly with the founders behind these ready-to-scale solutions. Explore their real-world impact, uncover new business opportunities, & spark the kind of strategic partnerships that move ideas forward.The Offshore Wind Innovation Hub Innovator ProgramA world-class program open to global offshore wind innovators. Building on three successful cohorts, this eight-month intensive program provides unparalleled support for innovators looking to develop novel technology & advance commercialization in New York & beyond.The Offshore Wind Innovation Hub is an initiative led by Urban Future Lab at NYU Tandon School of Engineering & the National Offshore Wind R&D Consortium (NOWRDC) in collaboration with the New York State Research & Development Authority (NYSERDA) & New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYC EDC).The Innovator program is also supported by industry partners Equinor, rsted, & Vestas.

events.name: AI & Future Of Education
events.description: AI & the Future of Education Artificial intelligence has caused seismic disruption in the field of education in just a few years. Students, educators, & parents are confused about how to navigate this game-changing technology. How should schools from K-12 to colleges & universities approach learning in this new era, & how can they prepare students for success in a transformed workplace? A panel of experts weighs in on the salient issues, the points of tension, & possible paths forward.   Featuring Steven Jackson, professor of information science & science & technology studies & vice provost for academic innovation at Cornell University; Aankit Patel, university dean for technology & computer & information sciences, The City University of New York; & Natasha Singer, a technology reporter for the business section of The New York Times, whose new book is Coding Kids: Big Tech's Battle to Remake Public Schools. Luke Waltzer, director of the Teaching & Learning Center at the CUNY Graduate Center, moderates.   Presented with the Teaching & Learning Center, CUNY AI Lab, GC Digital Initiatives, the American Social History Project/Center for Media & Learning, & the Mina Rees Library.

events.name: Founder Pitch Clinic
events.description: Join us in NYC for an in-person, hands-on pitch clinic designed to help founders become more confident on stage & sharpen the way they pitch to investors. Whether you're preparing for a fundraising round, an investor meeting, or your next demo day, this session will give you practical tools to communicate your story with greater confidence, clarity, & impact. The clinic features two focused, 30-minute workshops covering both sides of a great pitch: how you show up & what you say. Don't Calm Down30-minute interactive workshop with Dave Wolovsky (Coach & StartX mentor) Building a company, raising capital, & leading at a high level all require founders to manage stress under pressure. But performing at your best doesn't necessarily mean trying to calm yourself down. In this interactive session, Cognitive Performance Coach Dave Wolovsky will show you how to compose yourself when pitching & presenting. Through practical exercises, you'll learn techniques to pitch with greater presence, work with pressure rather than against it, & operate more effectively in high-stakes moments. About Dave WolovskyDave is a Cognitive Performance Coach with an MS in Neuroscience & Education from Columbia University. He coaches founders to maintain focus in high-pressure moments & establish better habits for managing their daily energy. Learn more at effortwise.com/founders. He also serves as a mentor in the StartX accelerator program. The Art of Pitching to Attract Investors30-minute workshop with Anthony Rose What makes investors lean in? Anthony will break down the art of delivering a compelling founder pitch-from communicating your vision & opportunity to presenting your business in a way that resonates with potential investors. Expect practical insights from someone who has worked with thousands of startups navigating fundraising & investment. About Anthony RoseAnthony is the founder & CEO of SeedLegals, the legaltech platform that helps startups get investment-ready, run funding rounds, & handle their legal needs, used by more than 50,000 startups. Before SeedLegals, Anthony's career spanned 3D graphics, P2P music, internet video, & social TV, including leading BBC iPlayer. Wired Magazine's 2009 cover story called him The Man Who Saved the BBC. Come ready to learn, practice, & leave with techniques you can put to work in your very next pitch.

events.name: Startup Pitch & Networking
events.description: Join our event in New York! We design Pitch & Networking nights to help founders sharpen their thinking through direct, candid feedback & to give strong investors access to serious teams. Our pitch night is complemented by a structured networking session before & after the pitch session.  What to expect: Startups pitch live & receive focused feedback from angels & VC partners Structured networking session before & after the pitches Entrepreneurs, startup founders, & operators are joining to network, exchange ideas, & build strong connections Active investors & venture scouts joining to discover the best startups early  Who you will meet at the event: Founders Investors, VC partners, Venture Scouts Marketers, Salespeople, Business Advisors Industry Disruptors AI Experts Entrepreneurs from Europe, Asia, & the United Kingdom  We Welcome New Investors: We invite investors to our event to expand their network, get acquainted with new startups, evaluate them, share feedback, & participate in discussions with early-stage & serial founders. We offer complimentary tickets to institutional investors, angels, & venture scouts with a proven track record. If you'd like to access our database of promising startups or provide mentorship support to our best startups, please fill out this short Investor Application Form, & our team will contact you.  Want to Pitch? A limited number of founders will have the opportunity to pitch their startup or business to a panel of investors & experts. 4-6 selected founders will pitch their startup, followed by a short Q&A where participants can ask questions & share feedback. Apply by filling out the Pitch Application Form & sending us your pitch deck. Spots are limited, & we select founders in advance. To maintain high-quality pitches, you are required to present with a pitch deck. We will share our pitching guide and, if you'd like, coach you so you're fully prepared for pitch night.  The best startups will be featured across our social media & included in our investor newsletter. Requirements for attendees: Dress code: smart casual. Bring good energy.  Join our event & secure your ticket today! About us: Startup Valley is a global event organizer hosting pitch nights in 25 cities since 2023. Since then, we have hosted 850 events for 40,000 attendees. Over these years, we connected countless outstanding early-stage startups to serious investors, & we are not planning to stop. We maintain strategic partnerships with VC funds in the US, Europe, & Asia to support our community. Do you have a question, a partnership proposal, or want to clarify something? Reach us at hello@startupvalley.club Agenda 18:00-18:30 - Registration: Guests register, receive badges, & event programs. This is an opportunity for casual networking, making first connections, & preparing for the event. 18:30-19:00 - Event Kickoff & Interactive Networking: Official welcome from the organizers with a brief overview of the event goals & schedule. Interactive networking session to connect with key contacts. 19:00-19:50 - Startup Pitch Session: Startups present their projects to investors & experts. Each team has 5 minutes to pitch, covering the project's core idea, business model, & target market. 19:50-21:00 - Chill & Networking: Participants enjoy casual conversations with investors, discuss collaboration opportunities, & exchange ideas over refreshments. FAQ Can I pitch? Yes! To pitch, please purchase a Pitch Ticket & fill out the Pitch Application Form. We will contact you to discuss & approve your pitch. The pitch duration is 5 minutes. You will also have some time to answer questions from the audience. How does the pitch go? Selected founders present on stage to the audience & the investors in the room. You get 5 minutes to pitch your idea, business model, target market, & investment ask, followed by a short Q&A. The best startups are featured across our social media channels & in the investor newsletter. Who will I meet? Founders, angel investors, VC partners, venture scouts, AI experts, engineers, operators, marketing & sales experts, & international entrepreneurs from across Europe, Asia, & the US. Do investors get free tickets? Yes! Please apply above or email hello@startupvalley.club, & we will issue a complimentary ticket for you & your team. Can I request a refund? Yes. Refunds are available if requested at least 1 day before the event start time. Please submit the refund request on the platform where you purchased your ticket, or email us at hello@startupvalley.club

events.name: AI/ML Lecture & Mixer
events.description: A monthly ML research colloquium by the New York Machine Learning Research Guild - this session in collaboration with our partner, CUNY Tech Prep. Speaker: Zayne Sprague  PhD Researcher, Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences, NYU & GoogleTopic: From Chain of Thought to Agent Swarms: A Brief Story on Reasoning in LLMs Giving language models more time to think has produced substantial gains, but in targeted domains, & the benefits appear to remain uneven across tasks. This talk explores how models can use additional computation at inference time effectively, reviewing the progression from prompt based methods to multi-agent systems. We will begin with chain-of-thought prompting, asking a model to think before giving a final answer, presenting our work showing that chain-of-thought prompting has its strongest benefits concentrated in mathematics & symbolic reasoning. These domains also share a practical advantage: answers can often be checked automatically, providing feedback that can be used to train models through reinforcement learning. This leads us to SkillFactory, where we use a model's own successful & unsuccessful attempts to construct training examples that demonstrate checking answers & retrying. Combining supervised finetuning on these examples with reinforcement learning helps models develop these behaviors & generalize to harder problems. Finally, we will discuss recent work on agent swarms, exploring how reasoning can scale in parallel & what role verification can play in making that additional computation useful. This session is a close-quarters look at that work, with plenty of room to push back & dig in. # Who this is forNY-MLR colloquia are small by design. The room is capped, & we keep it that way so the discussion stays substantive & everyone in it can contribute. We'd love to see you if you're:- A practitioner working seriously on ML, in industry or in a lab- A researcher or graduate student in ML, NLP, or an adjacent field- A highly motivated student or self-directed learner of any age or background, with real depth of interest # Schedule5:00 - 5:30 PM - Doors open, arrivals, mingling5:30 - 6:30 PM - Speaker Lecture6:30 - 7:00 PM - Moderated Q&A7:00 - 8:00 PM - After hours, mingling, wind-down8:00 PM - Lights out Venue: Amazon JFK27 ("Hank")  12 W 39th St, New York, NY 10018

events.name: Borderless Office - Identity & Access In World Of Remote-First Growth
events.description: Join Antoine Jebara (Co-founder, JumpCloud) & Noah Landow (Founder & CEO, Macktez) for an informal conversation between an expert on scaling global technology companies & the evolution of identity & access management & the founder of a technology consulting firm. In an era defined by remote work & the rapid rise of agentic AI, the concepts of identity & security are shifting beneath our feet. As AI agents begin to act on our behalf, how do we maintain control, responsibility, & security? If an AI agent executes a transaction or accesses a database, who is truly holding the keys? Antoine brings a unique perspective from the front lines of this transition, from pioneering decentralized 2FA & password management at MYKI to driving global strategy & partner ecosystems at JumpCloud. Join us at the Macktez office, after work, over light snacks & sips, for an exploratory conversation on the challenges of scaling fast-growing global companies & how different security architectures impact our long-term safety in a cloud-first world. We will dive into the shifting landscape of encryption, the unique hurdles of managing remote-first organizations, & what it truly means to "identity" ourselves in the age of AI. Photography, audio, & video recording may occur at this event & by attending you consent to such recording media & its release, publication, exhibition, or reproduction. Event StructureWe ask that guests arrive between 7-7:30 pm to minimize disruption during the talk. 7 pm - Doors open, opportunity to mingle over snacks & sips with other attendees7:30 pm - Guests take their seats for the talk8:15 pm - Informal mixer resumes On AttendanceWe have a limited capacity. If your plans change, please update your registration so someone else can join. A bit about Macktez, & why we host this seriesMacktez is a technology consultancy collaborating with organizations going through dynamic change. Our goal is to form a lasting partnership between our team & our clients, so we can anticipate their technology challenges & help them navigate growth, disruption, & other evolving conditions. Each event in our Tte--Tech series is an opportunity to explore a specific cultural, scientific, historical, & personal issue. We fire at the synapses that connect each topic to other fields of interest & to our individual lives. And we do so in a comfortable environment to facilitate conversation that can be casual, surprising, & illuminating. To learn more, visit us at macktez.com.

events.name: PMAI: Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Sales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. events.description: Agentic Security NYC is a practitioner-only gathering for security engineers & leaders actually running AI agents in production not a conference, not a panel, & not a place to pitch a product. We ran the first one in August. This one lands during BSidesNYC week. The format: a small room, real conversation, no slides. We pose a handful of hard questions & let practitioners argue them out: what actually broke, who in your org has the authority to say no to an agent going to production, whether you could actually prove what an agent did last week if you had to, where your own line on autonomy really sits. Rules of the room: Chatham House - share the ideas afterward, not who said what No vendor pitches, from us or anyone else Practitioners only If you're building or defending AI agents in production: security engineering, AppSec, ProdSec, InfraSec, AI governance & this is genuinely on your mind, request an invite. Space is limited.

events.name: AI & The Culture IRL - Create Once, Publish Everywhere
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back - In Person at Salesforce We're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City & sponsored by Boldforce. This Month We Present...Create Once. Publish Everywhere.Learn how top creators turn one idea into newsletters, videos, podcasts, social posts, presentations, & more using AI-powered content systems. Creating the idea is only half the work. Then comes the newsletter. The social posts. The video. The presentation. The podcast. The clips. And somehow, every platform wants something different. What if you didn't have to start from scratch every single time? At this month's AI & The Culture meetup, we're exploring how creators, entrepreneurs, educators, filmmakers, & small teams are using AI-powered content systems to turn one strong idea into an entire ecosystem of content. We'll look beyond simply asking AI to write me a post & dig into how you can build repeatable workflows that help you create, adapt, & distribute your ideas across formats-without losing your voice in the process. Together we'll explore:  How to turn one core idea into multiple pieces of content  AI workflows for newsletters, social posts, video, podcasts, presentations, & more  How to adapt an idea for different platforms instead of simply copying & pasting  Ways to build repeatable content systems that save time & creative energy  How to keep your voice, perspective, & cultural context consistent across AI-assisted content  Practical strategies for spending less time feeding the content machine & more time developing ideas worth sharing The goal isn't to create more content just for the sake of creating more content. It's to make your best ideas work harder for you. Expect a welcoming room filled with creators, technologists, educators, founders, artists, & curious minds ready to learn how AI can support a smarter, more sustainable creative process. Who Should Attend?  Creators & content makers  Filmmakers, writers, artists, & storytellers  Educators & community builders  Entrepreneurs, founders, & solopreneurs  Marketers, strategists, & social media professionals  Podcasters & video creators  Anyone with ideas they want to share more consistently Whether you're building a personal brand, growing a business, educating an audience, promoting your creative work, or simply tired of reinventing the wheel every time you post-this conversation is for you. Come Ready to Build This won't be a sit-back-and-scroll kind of evening. Bring your laptop, something to write with, & a mindset ready to learn, experiment, & share. We'll be exploring ideas, tools, & workflows you can start applying to your own creative process.  Bring your laptop  Bring a notebook or something to take notes with  Bring your curiosity & questions Come ready to learn. Come ready to contribute. Come ready to build. About AI & The Culture AI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, & culture. Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams & King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, & culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, & community. We're building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI. This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture - grounded in community, focused on real-world use, & centered on learning together in the room. Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Let's build - together.  About Your Hosts Shirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, & co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, & creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, & real-world execution. About King Willonius King Willonius is a creative technologist & cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, & creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, & community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable & useful - especially for creatives & innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm.  Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio) #AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: Sobremesa - Private Dinner For Latin American Founders

We skipped straight to it. This is not a mixer & it is not a pitch night. There is no panel & no deck. Just founders who are building between Latin America & the United States, at one table, talking about the parts they don't put on LinkedIn. The guest list is the product, so it is built by hand. This dinner is the smaller, quieter room the night after - same community, twenty seats instead of a hundred. Co-hosted by Christopher Martnez (Ziora Copilot) & Sharon Rao, MD. Nuestra gente, nuestra mesa.
