DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In partnership with Pepper NYC & the Peptide Club of NYC A peptide to heal your tendon. An injection to rebuild your knee. Exosomes to make your body younger. Regenerative medicine is moving fast, & consumers increasingly don't want to wait ten years for the clinical trials to catch up (the AIDS crisis..). Some of these treatments have real science behind them. Others have promising early evidence. And some are being sold for thousands of dollars long before anyone can say with confidence that they actually work. But maybe that's the point. We let adults make risky decisions everywhere else. If a patient understands the evidence is uncertain, why shouldn't they be allowed to spend their own money trying something experimental? The alternative is the basic bargain medicine has relied on for decades: prove it works before you sell it. Because when the person explaining the risks is also making money from the treatment, "informed consent" can start looking a lot like a sales pitch. So: should experimental regenerative therapies be sold to consumers, or should medicine have to prove they work first? Arguing for, Julius Ritter is the founder of the California Peptide Club & is building infrastructure for the peptide space, from education to real-world outcome data. He argues that the answer to uncertain evidence is more transparency & better data, not keeping adults from making their own choices Arguing against, Dr. Tiana Woolridge is a primary sports medicine physician at Hospital for Special Surgery, double board certified in pediatrics & sports medicine. She's trained in regenerative treatments like PRP herself, which is exactly why she thinks there's a difference between promising medicine & selling something before the evidence is there. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

events.name: Urban Future Summit - 10 Years Of Impact
events.description: The 2026 Urban Future Summit is supported by New York Community Trust, New York State Energy Research & Development Authority, MUFG Bank, & NYU Tandon School of Engineering - this year is extra special as we're celebrating 10 years of supporting climate innovation & the entrepreneurs who have shaped it. 2 PRIZE TRACKS. 8 FINALISTS. HEAR THEM PITCH ON 10/22.Read the full press release  Climate Adaptation Prize: focused on solutions that help communities & ecosystems adapt to & build resilience against the impacts of climate change. Airbuild: Autonomous biological nutrient recovery systems that convert wastewater nutrients into carbon-sequestering biochar fertilizer, helping municipalities meet EPA compliance & cut costs while creating new revenue for farmers. Class 3 Technologies: Engineering-grade, building-level climate risk assessments powered by Iris, a proprietary simulation engine, helping large property owners quantify physical vulnerability & evaluate resilience strategies across their portfolios, while extending that same risk intelligence to underserved communities. Rarefied: A sunlight-driven propulsion mechanism enabling persistent flight in near-space, building a new atmospheric data layer to improve weather forecasting, disaster resilience, & climate risk modeling - data especially valuable in equatorial & developing regions, where sparse observations weaken storm & drought forecasts. Supercool Earth: An end-to-end precipitation enhancement platform that uses biology to increase rain & snowfall on demand for ski resorts, water utilities, hydropower operators, & agriculture, giving water-scarce communities a tool to stabilize supply before rationing or crop failure set in. Climate Mitigation Prize: focused on solutions that reduce greenhouse gas emissions & mitigate the impacts of climate change. Arcticar: An intelligent, clean energy platform for the cold chain, replacing diesel-powered trailer refrigeration with lower-cost electric units & integrated battery storage, eliminating the emissions & noise pollution reefers create. Emulate Cities: AI infrastructure that helps local governments automate permit review, cutting permitting timelines from weeks to minutes to accelerate deployment of housing, clean energy, & climate-resilient infrastructure. Every Electric: Operator of New York City's largest plug-in powerbank network, giving households access to affordable backup power while strengthening grid reliability for all New Yorkers. Ultropia: An ultrasonic mechanical water extraction platform that removes moisture from materials, targeting the energy-intensive gas dryers used across the industrial laundry industry. For more than a decade, the Urban Future Prize Competition has identified & accelerated the founders building the technologies, infrastructure, & systems that cities need to thrive in a changing world. What begins as an early-stage idea has repeatedly become a market-shaping company: 23 startups supported, more than $1 million awarded in non-dilutive funding, & over $515 million in follow-on capital raised - a remarkable 515x return on prize dollars deployed. At this year's Urban Future Summit, attendees will actively participate in the next chapter of that story. The Summit will culminate with presentations from the 2026 Urban Future Prize Competition finalists - founders tackling some of the most urgent challenges we're facing today, from climate resilience & emissions reduction to mobility, energy, & the circular economy. These entrepreneurs are not only competing for funding; they are competing for the opportunity to join ACRE, New York's longest-running climatetech incubator, where breakthrough ideas are transformed into scalable businesses. This year marks an important milestone for the Urban Future Prize Competition. For the first time, four awardees will be selected across the Climate Adaptation & Climate Mitigation prize tracks. Two winners get access to $50k & two runner-up teams in each track will also receive $10k in non-dilutive funding & admission into the ACRE Incubator. By expanding support to a broader cohort of entrepreneurs, we're investing in a larger pipeline of innovators at a moment when climate resilience & decarbonization must advance together.

events.name: PMAI: Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Sales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. - Bring a computer. You're writing three things tonight.- Most founders can get meetings. The deals die after meeting one.- You'll leave with your buyer in one sentence, a cold email written to a real person, & five questions for your next call. About Farzad, the speaker Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding & generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: The AI-ndustrial Revolution?
events.description: Companies are spending billions on AI. But is it actually making the economy better? Right now, the evidence is weird. Only 1 in 8 CEOs says AI is both increasing revenue & cutting costs. At the same time, 77% of CEOs say AI has been overhyped so far-but may actually be underhyped over the next decade. So what happens next? A productivity boom that creates new industries & better jobs? Or enormous investment, displaced workers, & technology that never delivers enough value to justify the hype? Daniel Di Martino, an economist & Fellow at the Manhattan Institute, studies economic growth, labor markets, & the policies that drive American competitiveness. Dr. Cecilia Dones is a Columbia lecturer & longtime data & AI executive who works with organizations trying to turn massive AI investments into actual business value. Will AI be a net benefit to the American economy? Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

events.name: Agentic AI In The Wild: Open Source Agents In Production
events.description: AI & Open Source Builders Meetup, New York City AI agents are moving into production, & more & more of them are built on open source. The question is no longer whether to use them, but what it takes to make them reliable once the demo is over. This meetup brings together builders, maintainers, & practitioners integrating AI agents into real codebases, CI/CD pipelines, internal developer platforms, cloud native infrastructure, & observability stacks. The evening focuses on the conversations that rarely fit into conference talks: what breaks at scale, how open source tools & standards shape agentic systems, where failure modes hide, & how teams build systems they can trust. Under the theme Open Source in Production, we will explore agentic code review, agent loops in CI/CD, developer platforms, eBPF-powered observability & security, & the role open source communities play in how production AI gets built. No vendor pitches. Just practical lessons from systems running in production. Agenda 5:00 PM Doors Open, Drinks & Networking5:30 PM Welcome & Opening Remarks5:40 PM [Speaker TBD], Qodo Dev Community6:05 PM Break, Food & Networking6:25 PM Panel: Agentic AI in the Wild7:15 PM Ryan Hamilton, Senior Developer & Community Lead, CircleCI AI Lab7:40 PM Closing Remarks7:45 PM Networking until 8:00 PM Speakers & Sessions [Speaker TBD], Qodo[Talk title TBD][Talk abstract TBD] Ryan Hamilton, Senior Developer & Community Lead, CircleCI AI LabOne Take: Engineering Agent Loops That Ship 100% Green PRs on the First PushMost teams optimizing AI-assisted development are focused on the wrong variable: prompting harder, adding rework, dumping larger failure logs into context. The real question isn't how to fix red PRs faster. It's how to stop producing them.Ryan shares findings from three connected Loop Lab experiments, each using the same controlled Snake game benchmark to isolate one variable at a time. Each one reveals something unexpected about where the real leverage lives in an agent loop, & what it means for cutting the cost of agentic development.Together, these experiments map a clear path from "rework is inevitable" to "rework is reserved for the unknowable." The result is a practical harness design that bakes a low Merge Efficiency Ratio (MER, the number of validation cycles it takes to get a change onto main) in from the start, & a new way to think about where validation belongs in the agent loop. Panel: Agentic AI in the WildWhat does it take to move AI agents from proof of concept into systems that operate reliably, & what role does open source play?Practitioners from across the stack will discuss context management, governance, open standards, observability, security, & what changes when agentic systems scale.Expect concrete lessons, not talking points. ModeratorDana Fine, Open Source & Developer Relations Manager, QodoDana leads open source programs & community initiatives at Qodo. She runs the GitHub User Group, CNCF local & GenAI communities, & the Bond AI meetup series. PanelistsBaruch Sadogursky, PortBaruch is a longtime developer advocate & a well-known speaker at developer conferences around the world. He co-authored Liquid Software & DevOps Tools for Java Developers, & focuses on developer productivity, DevOps, & how AI is changing the way software gets built & shipped. [Speaker TBD], Claude Community[Bio TBD] [Speaker TBD], NVIDIA[Bio TBD] Community PartnersAWS User Group NYC, CNCF NYC, Frontend NYC, WeMakeDevs, Bond AI, Qodo Dev Community Join the CommunityQodo Dev Community on Discord: [Discord invite link]Follow us on Meetup: [Meetup group link]

events.description: We're bringing together builders & long-time contributors from the Numerai & decentralized AI ecosystems for a mix of talks, a workshop, & a special community panel. Featured speakers: Jason - Co-Founder & CEO, CrowdCent Nick - Co-Founder & CEO, Allora Labs Matteo - Co-Founder & CEO, Orion Finance The Numerai "Out of Sample" Special Panel  A discussion & AMA-style panel with guests featured on the Out of Sample interview series. All three are current or former members of the Numerai Council of Elders, with the panel moderated by another member of the Council. Tim (aka jefferythewind) (see episode 2) ShatteredX (see episode 3) Jason (see episode 4) More speakers & session details coming soon. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/ Important Note  This is an in-person-only event; there will be no livestream. For security reasons, we must provide a guest list to the security team at least 24 hours before the event. Your full name will be shared only with the security team. About Decentralized AI Days  Decentralized AI Days are community-driven events exploring how open, decentralized AI & Web3 can work together in practice. We bring together engineers, researchers, & builders for a day of technical talks, hands-on workshops, & honest conversation - no hype, no sales pitches, & no pay-to-play. The ecosystem we care about includes projects such as Numerai & CrowdCent. The door is open to anyone building with or curious about decentralized AI. Come for the substance, stay for the community. Call for Presentations  Interested in sharing your experience with our community? Please contact me (Joe) directly via X, or on LinkedIn. I'll get back to you as soon as possible. Everyone is welcome to apply, as long as your talk or workshop topic is relevant. Agenda  More details will be announced soon! Expect a program of tech talks & workshops, followed by a relaxed evening mixer. What to Expect   Connect with a friendly community of AI & Web3 builders, researchers, & curious minds.  Enjoy zero-hype technical talks focused on real problems & practical insights.  Take part in hands-on workshops where you can learn by building.  Watch live demos of decentralized AI & related projects.  Meet the organizers & share your questions & feedback directly.  Explore community resources & connect over food. Who Should Attend)  Decentralized AI Days are for everyone curious about where AI & decentralized systems meet: AI/ML engineers, Web3 developers, researchers, students, & builders at any experience level. Sexually explicit language or imagery is inappropriate for any part of the event, including talks, workshops, social activities, or online platforms. Participants who violate these rules may be warned or expelled from the event at the discretion of the organizers. Past Events  Materials from past Decentralized AI Days live in the community meetups repository. We have also hosted similar events under a different name (Numerai Community Meetup) from 2022 to 2024: London (July 2022) New York (September 2022) Tokyo (April 2023) Prague (July 2023) Toronto (October 2023) San Francisco (January 2024) Frankfurt (April 2024) Tokyo (July 2024) Bangkok (November 2024) Finally, here's one meme to sum up the vibe.

events.description: In the 1980s, Renaissance Technologies pioneered a new way to beat the markets: computing power, statistics, and signal processing. Today that approach anchors a $1.2 trillion asset class, but one built almost entirely on short-horizon trades.The holy grail has always been the opposite: long-horizon investing, fully automated. events.name: AI & Future Of Education
events.description: AI & the Future of Education Artificial intelligence has caused seismic disruption in the field of education in just a few years. Students, educators, & parents are confused about how to navigate this game-changing technology. How should schools from K-12 to colleges & universities approach learning in this new era, & how can they prepare students for success in a transformed workplace? A panel of experts weighs in on the salient issues, the points of tension, & possible paths forward.   Featuring Steven Jackson, professor of information science & science & technology studies & vice provost for academic innovation at Cornell University; Aankit Patel, university dean for technology & computer & information sciences, The City University of New York; & Natasha Singer, a technology reporter for the business section of The New York Times, whose new book is Coding Kids: Big Tech's Battle to Remake Public Schools. Luke Waltzer, director of the Teaching & Learning Center at the CUNY Graduate Center, moderates.   Presented with the Teaching & Learning Center, CUNY AI Lab, GC Digital Initiatives, the American Social History Project/Center for Media & Learning, & the Mina Rees Library.

events.name: Ugly Talk: Building Fandoms In 2027
events.description: A customer buys once. A fan brings people with them. Getting there takes months of showing up. Listening. Keeping promises. Giving people a reason to care when you are no longer in their feed. This Ugly Talk gets into the work behind real fandom. The creator calls that went nowhere. The community plays that looked dead for months. The moment loyal customers pushed back & the brand had to answer. No follower-count victory laps. Just the decisions, mistakes, & proof behind communities that stick.  Why you should be in this room.Hear how consumer brands turn one-time buyers into people who recruit other buyers. Learn which signals reveal loyalty before revenue catches up. See how brands build with creators from the first idea through launch. Learn what to keep doing when the community looks quiet. Hear how leaders respond when their biggest supporters become their loudest critics.  What's on the table.Building superfans at scale: What makes customers care enough to bring other people in. Creators & co-creation: How brands share the build instead of buying a post at the end. Measuring fandom: The numbers that matter after likes & reach stop telling the truth. The slow build: What to do when months of work look like nothing is happening. When fandom turns: What community pushback reveals about the trust you built. Managing a crisis: How to respond fast, own the miss, & keep trust intact.  Who's hosting it. Rob Fajardo - Founder, LeaveNormalBehind Rob Fajardo is an entrepreneur, operator, & cultural architect whose work centers on a simple question: what does winning look like? Early in his career, Rob helped drive the fidget spinner phenomenon by building & activating an influencer network across Instagram & Facebook, reaching over 150 million people. Since then, he has worked with brands including DoorDash, Lowe's, FedEx, Converse, Red Bull, & Wyndham Resort Group, & has been featured in Forbes, Entrepreneur, Thrive Global, & BuzzFeed. Rob is the founder of Leave Normal Behind, a global network of purpose-driven leaders, creators, & investors built around meaningful connection, personal growth, & human flourishing. Over the past decade, he has brought together people across industries & generations through designed gatherings & strategic collaborations. He also serves as Head of Operations for the School of Content at The School of Hard Knocks, one of the world's largest business media platforms with 26M+ followers, where he coaches business owners generating six to nine figures on go-to-market. In addition, he is a Strategic Advisor to The AI Collective, the world's largest AI community, with 70,000+ members across 25+ global chapters.  Who's getting in.CPG & consumer-brand founders building a customer base that sticks. Brand & community leaders responsible for loyalty & retention. Creators building their own audience or working with consumer brands. Marketers who care about advocacy, repeat purchases, & long-term growth.  About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough "aha!" moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons & insights. With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami, we've built a vibrant community of thousands of founders & industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape. Official Website: UglyTalk.com Important Notice for Ugly Talk AttendeesAdmission & Confirmation Attendance is by approval only. Approved guests will receive a confirmation email along with a calendar invite. Invitations are non-transferable. Additional event details will be shared as the event approaches. Code of Conduct By attending, you agree to: Maintain respect & professionalism, adhering to all venue rules, policies, & applicable laws. Refrain from harassment, discrimination, unwelcome sexual advances (verbal or physical), intimidation, or inappropriate photography/recording. Report any violations to the event hosts immediately. Violations may result in immediate removal from the event & exclusion from future invitations. Liability & Risk Participation is voluntary & at your own risk. You waive any right to inspect or approve the final materials & release all claims related to their use. Communications By registering, you agree to receive marketing & promotional communications from Ugly Talk & its co-hosts, partners, & sponsors. events.name: Transit Techies #39
events.description: The Center for Urban Science + Progress (CUSP) at NYU Tandon & Transit Techies welcome you to attend two presentations: Phil Cline on Swiftly & Joe Puccio on WalkNYC. Connect with NYU Tandon CUSP & Transit Techies NYC at this talk; attendees are welcome to bring their own food. The event will be held at 370 Jay Street, Brooklyn, NY in Room 1201. We hope to see you there! About the TalksSwiftly Phil Cline will share some of his work on assisting transit agencies with better drawing & dissemination of bus detours at Swiftly WalkNYC In May, Joe created WalkNYC, an app that tracks which blocks you've walked. He built it as a personal project while trying to walk every block in Manhattan. Since launch over 25,000 New Yorkers have started using WalkNYC to stay active & explore the city. About the SpeakersPhil ClineSoftware Engineer, Swiftly Phil Cline is a Brooklyn-based software engineer originally from Toronto who has worked in the transit industry for over 7 years & has a lot of experience with transit data standards like GTFS & GTFS-RT. Joe PuccioCreator, WalkNYC & Founder Coursicle Joe Puccio is a designer & programmer based in NYC. He is the founder of Coursicle, an app used by millions of college students to manage their class schedules & assignments. A central focus of Joe's work is running his companies ethically & building products that are fundamentally beneficial to people's lives. At Coursicle, all employees receive the same salary, & profits are split among employees at the end of each year. Joe graduated from UNC Chapel Hill in 2016 with degrees in Mathematics & Computer Science. He writes about design, technology, & other ideas at joepuccio.com. Vistor InformationPlease visit the NYU Tandon website for directions & a campus map. Advance registration through Luma is required for campus access at NYU for external guests. Attendees who are not current students, faculty, or staff at NYU, including alumni, are asked to register using a personal email address. About CUSP at NYU TandonThe Center for Urban Science + Progress (CUSP) at NYU Tandon is an interdisciplinary center dedicated to applying science, technology, engineering, math, & social sciences to serve urban communities worldwide. Founded as a partnership between NYU & the City of New York, CUSP leads research, educational, & entrepreneurial initiatives that advance the science of cities. By applying novel insights to urban issues, we develop data- & technology-driven approaches that drive positive impact. With an additional focus on training future leaders, CUSP offers interdisciplinary academic programs in applied urban science & informatics for graduate students & professionals. CUSP also engages with stakeholders across city agencies, start-ups, industry players, community-based organizations, & nonprofits to address urgent socioeconomic, environmental, & infrastructural challenges. The center's ultimate objective is to improve urban quality of life by using data to innovate & refine inclusive, equitable, & sustainable practices for cities everywhere. About Transit Techies NYCBringing together the technologists who love transit & the transit enthusiasts who hack! We'll have speakers present transit-related projects. Presenters may be household hackers, data scientists, researchers, product developers, or you! All presentations will be technical & awesome. Follow our calendar to stay up-to-date on our future events! Learn more on our website.

events.name: Dating The Dead - What Makes A Connection Real?
events.description: Dating Lab NYC presents:Dating the Dead: What Makes a Connection Real?Dating Lab NYC is a monthly interactive discussion series exploring the psychology, culture, & technology shaping modern connection. Each gathering combines a research-informed presentation, open conversation, an anonymous audience survey, & time to connect with other curious New Yorkers. This month, we'll explore connection on & off the dating apps: what makes it feel real, & how technology shapes what we seek from one another. The conversation is inspired by For Human Use, a novel by Sarah G. Pierce, who will join us as a special guest speaker. Sarah will share the inspiration behind her book & how she explored questions of dating & connection through her story, bringing her perspective into our discussion. We'll wrap up with a book giveaway & author signing, alongside time to meet & connect with fellow attendees. No need to read the book in advance. Come curious. Presented & facilitated by Becky BergBecky is a behavioral researcher with a master's degree in clinical psychology from Columbia University. events.name: Six Math Essentials w/ Terence Tao
events.description: Book Launch & Conversation with Janna Levin Widely regarded as the world's greatest living mathematician, Fields Medalist Terence Tao approaches mathematics as a sublime art-a quiet, rigorous effort to map the hidden scaffolding of reality. To mark the publication of his first popular book, Six Math Essentials, join us for an evening with Tao in conversation with Pioneer Works Director of Sciences Janna Levin. Tracing the central pillars of his book-from algebra as abstraction & geometry beyond sight, to navigating uncertainty & the mathematics of change-they will reveal math not as obscure magic, but as a deeply creative, interconnected way of thinking. Often referred to as the Mozart of mathematics, Tao will also explore how AI is transforming his own practice, the frontier of research, & our collective future. Together, we will consider what becomes of human intuition & creativity when the tools of thought are no longer uniquely human-and whether the true beauty of math lies not in the answers we find, but in the human mind reaching for them. Tao will sign copies of Six Math Essentials following the conversation, with books available for purchase on site. (Unable to attend? Order a signed copy here.) Please note that seating is limited & will be available on a first-come, first-served basis.   About the speakersTerence Tao is an Australian-American professor of mathematics at UCLA whose work focuses primarily on harmonic analysis, partial differential equations, combinatorics, & analytic number theory. The recipient of a Fields Medal, a MacArthur Genius Grant, & a Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics, among many other accolades, he is one of the most decorated & prolific mathematicians working today. Tao is the author of several academic books including Solving Mathematical Problems: A Personal Perspective & Additive Combinatorics, as well as his first popular math book, Six Math Essentials. He lives in Los Angeles. Janna Levin is the Claire Tow Professor of physics & astronomy at Barnard College of Columbia University. A Guggenheim Fellow, she has contributed to our understanding of black holes, extra dimensions, & cosmology. She is the founding director of sciences at Pioneer Works & the founding editor-in-chief of the magazine Pioneer Works Broadcast. She often contributes to news, documentaries, & radio, including as the presenter of the NOVA feature Black Hole Apocalypse on PBS & as a contributor to CBS, CNN, BBC, & NBC. She has authored books on black holes & the universe-Black Hole Blues, How the Universe Got its Spots, & Black Hole Survival Guide-as well as a PEN award-winning novel, A Madman Dreams of Turing Machines. You can find her current writings in Higher Dimensions. This program is funded by the Simons Foundation International & administered by the Simons Foundation's Science, Society & Culture division.

events.name: Creative Showcase Vol. 7
events.description: A chance for creatives to show off what they've been working on or be inspired by others in a series of quickfire 20-slide presentations.This is an opportunity to share a creative project that you have been working on with the Index Community in the form of a Pecha Kucha-a rapid presentation style where each person presents 20 slides, for 20 seconds each. This fast pace encourages storytellers to be concise, creative, & to the point-perfect for keeping the audience's attention. Whether you are presenting or just attending, this is an open forum, a space to gather & share, a place to mingle with other NYC creatives. Come be inspired or present what you've been working on. Interested in sharing your work? Applications for this event are now closed, but we hope you'll come see our amazing presenters & submit your project for consideration next time! Clipart Studio by Sami Smith Clipart Studio is a website where visitors can take magazines from the Internet Archive & make collages from them by "cutting" them out & arranging the pieces, or uploading their own materials to work with. There's also a gallery where you can see the thousands of wonderful user-submitted collages made with the program. Palestine Skating Game A videogame in development that centers Arabic electronic music, graffiti, & Splatoon-style paint shooting. The game team employs coders in Gaza & the West Bank. Brooklyn Design Archive by Gerardo Torres Davila Acultural project advancing the understanding of important pieces from the fields of furniture & industrial design. Ball-Jointed Doll Making by Tatyana Deslandes Mustakos Tatyana delves into both the theoretical & technical sides of her doll making practice & how it's evolved over the years. Urban Fossil by Suyeon Kim Urban Fossil is an immersive exhibition that transforms street debris into a typographic system & visceral data visualization. It translates ephemeral waste into a functional alphabet across an interactive website, a printed zine, & a gallery installation. Katie Ehrlich is a Brooklyn-based graphic designer, photographer, & founder of StudioKat. Her clients have ranged from brands like Google, American Express, & TikTok to publications for Stanford, the Smithsonian, & Cultured Magazine. Her work has been recognized by Communication Arts, Black + White Photography, & the CASE Awards.   Refunds We get that things come up, but we rely on headcounts to make our programs viable. events.name: Brooklyn Navy Yard Annual Open House
events.description: Explore cool spots, meet makers, & dive into history at the Brooklyn Navy Yard Annual Open House! The Brooklyn Navy Yard's Annual Open House Discover the Yard's 300-acre innovative campus during our Annual Open House, part of Open House New York Weekend. Step inside the studios of businesses in fashion, design, & technology for exclusive behind-the-scenes access & immersive activations. This day celebrates our campus of makers & offers artists, designers, entrepreneurs, & neighbors alike the chance to connect with peers, explore our campus & the businesses who thrive here, & experience the innovation at the Yard up close. This year, we've created two unqiue tracks to guide you through our campus: Creative Currents- Creativity flows through the Brooklyn Navy Yard; home to hundreds of artists, ranging from painters to photographers to jewelers. They'll be opening their studios to the public, inviting audiences in for a rare opportunity to view their work, learn about their processes, inspirations, & their journeys here at the Yard. BNY Past, Present, & Future - From our start in 1801 as a premiere ship building facility, we've always been on the cutting edge of manufacturing & technology, right here in New York City. On our campus, rich history meets an innovative future, as we look ahead towards what's next in the fields of space tech, green energy, robotics, & more. Come tour our waterfront campus & take in centuries of legacy, while gaining access to the labs & studios where the tech of the future is being made.   Also Featuring... Arnsenal's Tequila & Whisky Tasting Food Trucks Live Art Demos   BNYDC RULES, PROTOCOLS & ACKNOWLEDGEMENT  Check-In Procedure All visitors must check-in at Building 77. Visitors arriving through other entry points will be redirected to enter through official entry locations.All visitors must register for the event. No one will be admitted without an official RSVP. It is highly recommended that you RSVP in advance although day of registration is permitted.A valid photo ID is required for entry. Visitors under 18 must be accompanied by an adult & do not need a photo ID.Visitors who fail to register or do not present a valid photo ID will be denied entry.Expect an estimated 5-minute check-in & security screening process.Security Protocols All bags will be checked at the entrance for prohibited items.Prohibited items include but are not limited to alcohol; weapons, noise-making devices; laser pointers; fireworks; professional camera equipment; large political signs, banners, or flags; & other materials that may cause harm, damage, or disruption.Bags must not exceed the size of a standard school backpack (Approximately 18 x 14 x 6)Large bags, including roller bags, will not be permitted. Campus Rules for Event All visitors must stay in approved areas. Visitors should not enter closed or restricted spaces during the event. For this hackathon, Google DeepMind will support builders with access to its latest AI capabilities & technical resources.

events.name: Code & Coffee Hackathon
events.description: Everyone's a builder here: coders, PMs, designers, & the just-curious.Get ready to build something real for Newark! We're taking over Rutgers iHub for a full-day hackathon focused on solving problems that actually matter to the people who call this city home, from water safety to food access to just making city government easier to navigate.Theme:Description:This hackathon challenges participants to pick a real issue facing Newark & build something that actually helps: a tool, an assistant, a dashboard, whatever gets the job done. Teams can dig into problem areas like environmental & water justice, food access, cost of living, or civic transparency, or bring their own idea if they see a sharper angle. Expect AI to play a role in your build, but what we're really looking for is a solution that works. Judging will weigh usefulness & execution as heavily as technical approach.Technical Scope:Participants can use any technical stack they prefer (code-based, no-code, or a mix)Projects must be built from scratch during the hackathon, no prebuilt solutionsTeams are free to choose one of our suggested problem areas or pitch their own. We'll share a few starting points at kickoff, but the direction is yoursJudging Criteria:Relevance & Impact: Does this solve a real, specific problem for Newark residents, & could someone actually use it?Execution: How complete & functional is the prototype, given the short build window?Thoughtful AI Use: How & why did you use AI? A simple, well-executed approach counts; bonus points for teams who push further with multi-step reasoning or tool use where it genuinely fits the problem.Usability & Creativity: Would a non-technical resident actually get it? events.name: The Deployment Room
events.description: The Builder Series: A 60,000+ member community redefining what networking looks like curating founders, investors into intentional rooms built for experiences people remember & relationships that last. It's a direct line to the most ambitious builders.Find us here: Instagram  LinkedIn  TikTok  Facebook  X : WhatsApp Broad Channel (Not a GC)This is the 3rd edition of our luncheon.This time, we're hosting it in an $8.5M townhouse, because we believe in high-class experiences, & incredible people. (Pictures Below)Every room has been bigger than the last. Our 2nd edition versus the 1st:Founder revenue: $90M+ a year, up from $18M+ in August.Money being raised: $197M+ across 19 founders, up from $95M+ across 14 in August.Capital already raised: $43M+, up from $35M+ in August.The investors at the table:We feature 6 investors from our network, & we always end up with more.1st edition: We expected 6. We brought 10.2nd edition: We expected 10. We brought 12.$2B+ combined AUM across both events.$1M average check, $100K minimum.$10M+ in live check capacity.Who this room is forTo get into this room, you should to have raised at least $1M or be doing $1M+ in ARR. Our last edition averaged $3.8M+ ARR per founder.Raised your first round, onto your second, or bootstrapped to $1M or 15M ARR? You're in the right place. If you're an exited founder, LP/GP, dealmaker or capital raiser, you belong in this room too.Every investor here is from our network. We're curating this room deliberately, matching founders to the investors most likely to be a fit, & making the introduction ourselves.The goal: getting founders funded by our investor network.The 6 Investors joining us from our network: (More will be joining)Francesca Poupel: F&G Capital Partners (Managing Partner): Backing founders from pre-seed to Series A in AI, fintech, & blockchain, writing $300K$500K checks & partnering closely with teams as they scale.Mahir Laul (Partner) representing Laul Global a family office & holding company operating four interconnected pillars: Education Engine, Real Assets, Future Ventures, & Acquisitions. One integrated system. One long-term vision.Laul Global is owned & operated by the Laul family. We started with a single student recruitment company. We built it into one of Canada's most diversified education holding groups. Today the portfolio spans institutions, edtech, real estate, & a tech venture studio, with reach across 20+ countries & no plans to slow down.Triet Leminh: Principal, LMT Partners: Lawyer, founder, & investor backing pre-seed to Series A founders building in enterprise & regulated industries. Writing $200K$300K checks.Andrew Antar (General Partner, AG Venture Capital): A generalist fund backing extraordinary founders, sector agnostic. Also a Venture Partner at Arcadian Capital, focused on late-stage secondaries & pre-IPO tech, & served as Crypto Policy Advisor to the NYC Office of the Mayor  advising on the city's crypto regulatory framework & organizing the NYC Crypto Summit at Gracie Mansion. He is also founder of Tune.FM, a tokenized music streaming platform & digital asset marketplace, & co-founded Clear Quantum, a stealth quantum AI startup.Gonzalo Quincot (Founder, Sinober): Sinober is a financial intelligence platform that combines public & private market intelligence with institutional-grade methodology, corporate finance & proprietary AI tools to sharpen investment & capital decisions for individuals & businesses. Invests in automation, robotics, data centers & applied AI.Shilpi Nayak: (Founder & General Partner, 434 VC): Invests in early-stage technical founders across AI, infrastructure, physical AI & emerging technology. She is also the founder of House of 434, a community bringing together founders, investors & industry leaders.Pranav Jajapur (Co-Founder, ZERON Ventures): ZERON is an early-stage venture fund with an execution platform behind it, backing real-world technology, AI, healthcare, deep tech & climate companies building in the physical world, inside biology. Pre-seed through Series A with core deployment at seed, writing $400K$500k checks. Preferred focus is institutionally-anchored AI: structural research relationships at academic institutions, spinouts, & founder-led research programs.Fund I in formation. Deploying Q1All 6 senior investors confirmed.Part of building rooms is making sure real capital is present. Six investors actively deploying writing capital will be joining. Our first confirmed:Why we do this: Putting active investors in the same room as exceptional founders, & keeps the room small enough to ensure everyone actually meets. We value intentional networking & community.If you're here to meet the best of the best, this is the room.What to expect for this:A Greek style lunch, courtesy of our teamConversations with fellow high-performing startup leadersAn experience designed to facilitate new meaningful connections conversations with ambitious peers solving similar problemsEvent to be hosted at a beautiful private Soho loftOur intent is to bring good, smart humans together, & active investors together to fun incredible founders. events.name: Vibecoding 101
events.description: A 4-week scaffolded, hands-on introduction to vibecoding for beginners.Vibecoding, or AI-assisted software development, is the practice of guiding coding agents to translate your ideas into working software - without writing code yourself. We see vibecoding as 4 different product skills in a trench coat. While they may not write code, effective vibecoders mobilize concepts & workflows across software engineering, design, quality assurance, & product management. This course is a scaffolded, hands-on introduction to the fundamental skills & concepts required for a sustainable vibecoding practice. Students will learn through a combination of short lectures, applied exercises, personalized feedback, & demos to peers. We begin by working with coding agents in a multiplayer environment designed for beginners. We will create interactive frontends, learn the basics of the terminal, build integrations with APIs, & create stateful, full-stack applications with a database & user authentication. By the end of the course, students will transition to state-of-the-art coding agents installed on their personal machines, which they will use to build & deploy a working prototype to the web. SyllabusSession 1: Coding agents & frontends We introduce the course & core concepts of vibecoding. We introduce a basic taxonomy of web architecture. Students practice creating basic interactive frontends. Session 2: CLIs, APIs, & the terminal We cover core backend & data concepts. We gently introduce the terminal. Students practice writing simple CLI programs, & integrating with an API. Session 3: Stateful full-stack applications We cover databases & user authentication; students build a full stack app. Session 4: Deployment & demos The final session covers deployment. Students demo their prototypes for the class. Learning OutcomesAcquire core vocabulary & mental models for software development. Prompt coding agents to create frontends, API integrations, & stateful applications. Be able to translate your ideas into working prototypes using AI. Practice presenting your product ideas to peers & colleagues. ResourcesThis new world of ours rewards being a dilettante with a vague mental map of vast territories.- Ted Underwood There is a new kind of coding I call vibecoding,' where you fully give in to the vibes, embrace exponentials, & forget that the code even exists. It's possible because the LLMs (e.g. Cursor Composer w Sonnet) are getting too good it's not really coding - I just see stuff, say stuff, run stuff, & copy paste stuff, & it mostly works.- Andrej Karpathy Slow is smooth, & smooth is fast.- Anonymous ScholarshipIndex scholarships are designed to benefit members of our community who do not have expendable cash to pay for the course, & those for whom the class price is not accessible. These need-based scholarships will go to the candidates who best demonstrate why they should be chosen for the free spot to our class based on the following criteria: Belong to groups that are traditionally underrepresented in the graphic design & creative industries Do not have jobs that would pay for these courses as professional development Cannot independently afford the class at list price Share our value of intentional community The number of selected applicants chosen is subject to the discretion of Index & the instructor, but every course will select at least one. Apply for a scholarship here. Applications close October 20th. Instructor Bio Bill Roberts is an independent technologist based in Brooklyn. Drawn to socially beneficial uses of technology, he has 10 years of software engineering experience on teams spanning healthcare, climate, politics, & education. He runs Legible Labs, a product studio that helps clients design & build AI applications. As a research engineer, he has coauthored papers in peer-reviewed journals & conferences that empirically evaluate the capabilities of AI in educational settings. Bill holds a BA in Computer Science & Sociology from Columbia University.   Refunds We get that things come up, but we rely on headcounts to make our programs viable. If you request a refund... More than 4 weeks before the program begins  100% refundMore than 2 weeks before the program begins  50% refundFewer than 2 weeks before the program begins  No refund Thanks for understanding & for supporting our ability to provide cool offerings through your purchase. Media Release Clause By attending this event, you consent to being photographed, filmed, or recorded, & grant Index Space permission to use this content for promotional or informational purposes.

events.description: What does it mean for a machine to be intelligent, & can we define it mathematically? Join 90/30 for a reading group on Shane Legg's Machine Super Intelligence. This 2008 PhD thesis explores universal artificial intelligence, the theoretical agent AIXI, & the limits of building machines that learn & act across unfamiliar environments. We'll discuss: How can we measure intelligence beyond performance on a single task? What does AIXI tell us about an ideal intelligent agent? What changes when we move from theoretical intelligence to systems with limited compute? How useful are these ideas for understanding today's AI? This is a long read, so come with a section, question, or argument you want to unpack. You don't need to understand every proof to join the conversation. We are only mandating chapter 1 & 4 while 2 is suggested.

events.name: AI for operators
events.description: AI for Forward-thinking OperatorsA 2-hour hands-on workshop for execs, VPs, operators, fractional leaders, and founders.You're further along in your career than you are in AI - and you're tired of nodding along while colleagues and vendors pitch magic and your team runs experiments you can't evaluate.This isn't a talk. It's a working session. Bring your laptop. In two hours you'll set up Claude Code, Muse, or Hark - connect them to the tools and services you actually live in, and produce something real. Something that'll solve an actual problem you tackle, or something that'll help your work.Past execs have left with having created things like:dynamic competitive research and action toolsomething that runs analysis on their products and sales and automatically finds room for offloading inventory, dynamic promos, and actionable customer segmentshelps them hold their vendors and teams accountable automatically using briefs, followups, real-time measurementcloses their monthly books accuratelyautomates sales research and outreach relevant to them, not boilerplateautomates HR paperwork relevant to them, not boilerplateSmall by design: 3-5 seats, hands-on help throughout. We build alongside you and troubleshoot in real time, so you walk out ready to run this inside your company, immediately.About the host: Deepak DevjaniSomewhere along the way I started training my own team on AI, just so we could ship faster. And the coaching thing kind of fell in my lap. Turns out I love it.Then execs started coming to me. They wanted the same thing for themselves. Then other founders. For the last couple years I've been training execs and their C-suite teams, and honestly the change is night and day. They have more time. They get way more done.One thing I learned fast: for this to actually work, it has to be as close to personal and private as possible  essentially 1:1. That's the whole reason this class is small. You can literally know nothing walking in and you'll be OK; that's by design. And what you leave with isn't just a tool you built  it's the confidence to walk into work and actually use this.So that's what Reliable Bits is now. We still go into companies and implement AI for real. But a big part of what we do is coach the people doing the actual work. Operators, execs, VPs.

events.name: Borderless Office - Identity & Access In World Of Remote-First Growth
events.description: Join Antoine Jebara (Co-founder, JumpCloud) & Noah Landow (Founder & CEO, Macktez) for an informal conversation between an expert on scaling global technology companies & the evolution of identity & access management & the founder of a technology consulting firm. In an era defined by remote work & the rapid rise of agentic AI, the concepts of identity & security are shifting beneath our feet. As AI agents begin to act on our behalf, how do we maintain control, responsibility, & security? If an AI agent executes a transaction or accesses a database, who is truly holding the keys? Antoine brings a unique perspective from the front lines of this transition, from pioneering decentralized 2FA & password management at MYKI to driving global strategy & partner ecosystems at JumpCloud. Join us at the Macktez office, after work, over light snacks & sips, for an exploratory conversation on the challenges of scaling fast-growing global companies & how different security architectures impact our long-term safety in a cloud-first world. We will dive into the shifting landscape of encryption, the unique hurdles of managing remote-first organizations, & what it truly means to "identity" ourselves in the age of AI. Photography, audio, & video recording may occur at this event & by attending you consent to such recording media & its release, publication, exhibition, or reproduction. Event StructureWe ask that guests arrive between 7-7:30 pm to minimize disruption during the talk. 7 pm - Doors open, opportunity to mingle over snacks & sips with other attendees7:30 pm - Guests take their seats for the talk8:15 pm - Informal mixer resumes On AttendanceWe have a limited capacity. If your plans change, please update your registration so someone else can join. A bit about Macktez, & why we host this seriesMacktez is a technology consultancy collaborating with organizations going through dynamic change. Our goal is to form a lasting partnership between our team & our clients, so we can anticipate their technology challenges & help them navigate growth, disruption, & other evolving conditions. Each event in our Tte--Tech series is an opportunity to explore a specific cultural, scientific, historical, & personal issue. We fire at the synapses that connect each topic to other fields of interest & to our individual lives. And we do so in a comfortable environment to facilitate conversation that can be casual, surprising, & illuminating. To learn more, visit us at macktez.com.

events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Create Once. Publish Everywhere.
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back - In Person at Salesforce We're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City & sponsored by Boldforce. This Month We Present...Create Once. Publish Everywhere.Learn how top creators turn one idea into newsletters, videos, podcasts, social posts, presentations, & more using AI-powered content systems. Creating the idea is only half the work. Then comes the newsletter. The social posts. The video. The presentation. The podcast. The clips. And somehow, every platform wants something different. What if you didn't have to start from scratch every single time? At this month's AI & The Culture meetup, we're exploring how creators, entrepreneurs, educators, filmmakers, & small teams are using AI-powered content systems to turn one strong idea into an entire ecosystem of content. We'll look beyond simply asking AI to write me a post & dig into how you can build repeatable workflows that help you create, adapt, & distribute your ideas across formats-without losing your voice in the process. Together we'll explore:  How to turn one core idea into multiple pieces of content  AI workflows for newsletters, social posts, video, podcasts, presentations, & more  How to adapt an idea for different platforms instead of simply copying & pasting  Ways to build repeatable content systems that save time & creative energy  How to keep your voice, perspective, & cultural context consistent across AI-assisted content  Practical strategies for spending less time feeding the content machine & more time developing ideas worth sharing The goal isn't to create more content just for the sake of creating more content. It's to make your best ideas work harder for you. Expect a welcoming room filled with creators, technologists, educators, founders, artists, & curious minds ready to learn how AI can support a smarter, more sustainable creative process. Who Should Attend?  Creators & content makers  Filmmakers, writers, artists, & storytellers  Educators & community builders  Entrepreneurs, founders, & solopreneurs  Marketers, strategists, & social media professionals  Podcasters & video creators  Anyone with ideas they want to share more consistently Whether you're building a personal brand, growing a business, educating an audience, promoting your creative work, or simply tired of reinventing the wheel every time you post-this conversation is for you. Come Ready to Build This won't be a sit-back-and-scroll kind of evening. Bring your laptop, something to write with, & a mindset ready to learn, experiment, & share. We'll be exploring ideas, tools, & workflows you can start applying to your own creative process.  Bring your laptop  Bring a notebook or something to take notes with  Bring your curiosity & questions Come ready to learn. Come ready to contribute. Come ready to build. About AI & The Culture AI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, & culture. Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams & King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, & culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, & community. We're building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI. This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture - grounded in community, focused on real-world use, & centered on learning together in the room. Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Let's build - together.  About Your Hosts Shirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, & co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, & creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, & real-world execution. About King Willonius King Willonius is a creative technologist & cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, & creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, & community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable & useful - especially for creatives & innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm.  Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio) #AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: Deal Flow: NYC's First VC Hackathon
events.description: Event DescriptionNew York is getting its first VC hackathon, & you're building for the people who write the checks. Deal Flow is a one-day, in-person hackathon hosted by localhost:nyc & VCLab. You get 9 hours to build working products for the real problems VCs face every day. Partners from NYC's top funds judge live, & the best teams leave with intros to those funds. Problem StatementVenture capital runs on spreadsheets, gut feel & endless inbox triage. Firms move billions of dollars with tools that haven't changed in a decade. Your challenge is to build software that helps VCs find better companies, make faster decisions & support their founders after the check clears. The Challenge ThemeSourcing: finding breakout founders before everyone else does Diligence: market maps, competitive analysis & memo drafting Portfolio ops: helping funds support their companies at scale LP reporting: making fund updates less painful & more useful Deal pipeline & CRM workflows that VCs will actually use What to Expect9 hours of focused building, 9 AM to 6 PM Real VC problems, with investors in the room to test your ideas against Teams of 4 Time to meet founders, engineers & investors from across NYC Live demos to a panel of VC judges at the end of the day Food & drinks all day PrizesWinners get intros to the funds in the room + other prizes to be announced. JudgesAbeera Saeed is the Ventures Principal at Plug & Play, investing in Enterprise & AI B2B SaaS companies from Pre-Seed to Series A. Michael Barone - Investment Analyst at Everywhere Ventures, a global pre-seed venture capital firm. D. J. Patel - VC | 3x exited founder. Radhika Khandelwal builds AI agents for a living as a product leader at Wand AI, & she's spent years in the VC world seeing what makes startups stick. She'll want to see both slick code & a real business. Who Should AttendPre-seed & seed founders Engineers Builders who have felt the pain of fundraising firsthand Anyone curious about how venture capital actually works from the inside You don't need VC experience or a finished idea. Just show up ready to build. Sponsors[Sponsor TBD. Want to back NYC's first VC hackathon? Email somyag00@gmail.com] HostsSomya Gupta: The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Tracy Huang: VC Lab & CEO of Interlink IQ

events.name: Creativity Is Dead, Long Live Creativity - Gen AI & Meaning Of Art
events.description: The concept of creativity has a surprisingly short history. While ancient philosophers expounded on imagination & free will, theorizations of creativity as a distinct trait only date to the past hundred years. GenAI suggests that creativity is not unique to humans or even conscious organisms, but is reducible to mere calculation & programming. Has creativity finally been revealed as a sham? This week's interactive community conversation explores thought experiments that embody the philosophical issues raised by genAI tools; how scholars & artists have framed the relationship between creativity & technology; was creativity always a myth, & if so, is this a problem? OUR FACILITATOREmma Stamm is the Co-Founder & Executive Director of The Lenox Institute for Advanced Study. She holds a PhD in Interdisciplinary Studies from Virginia Tech, & her work bridges critical theory & STS. WHO'S IT FOR?Idea people. Founders. Builders. Creatives. Researchers. The Curious. And their Supporters --------------FORMATOur format explores ideas together through our diverse backgrounds, while building relationships & community through the process. We want you to talk to each other, instead of just being talked at. 5:30PM - Settle in, grab a drink & some food at the bar, & meet some new people before we start our event. 6:00PM - Our conversation begins with our facilitator presenting the knowledge & context for the conversation along the way. The conversation between attendees will explore from surface level understandings, to deep implications & future iterations. 7:30PM - Meet & connect with new people, catch up with people you haven't seen in a while, discover all the different ways you overlap. And then just hang out, grab a drink, play some pool or ping pong! Or stay for the band afterwards! Our desire is to be the antithesis of NYC's corporate panel & transactional networking culture. We aim to create a vibrant idea & build space in NYC that focuses on the passion & values beyond the money & the hustle.  ------------------ABOUT COHORTCohort is a space & home for ideas, & the people who think about them, create new ones, & build things from them. Many of us are founders, builders, artists, researchers, & their supporters here in NYC. Our goal is to turn the city into a campus after college. We hold idea & discussion events, coworking events for support & accountability for those building & creating things, & pure social events to build genuine relationships & community. Subscribe, browse our calendar, & join us for our next events!  Photography Notice We may take photos & video at our events to share on social media & our website. We use it to spread the word & help more people find this community. By attending, you're giving us permission to use those photos & videos in anything related to Cohort's promotion & outreach. If you'd rather not be photographed, just let us know when you arrive & we'll make sure you're not included. More from Cohort Monday Oct 19 Wednesday Oct 14 Dating the Dead Oct 15 Halloween crawl Oct 31 Calendar

events.name: An Unmuted Debate - Peptides vs The People
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In partnership with Pepper NYC & the Peptide Club of NYC A peptide to heal your tendon. An injection to rebuild your knee. Exosomes to make your body younger. Regenerative medicine is moving fast, & consumers increasingly don't want to wait ten years for the clinical trials to catch up (the AIDS crisis..). Some of these treatments have real science behind them. Others have promising early evidence. And some are being sold for thousands of dollars long before anyone can say with confidence that they actually work. But maybe that's the point. We let adults make risky decisions everywhere else. If a patient understands the evidence is uncertain, why shouldn't they be allowed to spend their own money trying something experimental? The alternative is the basic bargain medicine has relied on for decades: prove it works before you sell it. Because when the person explaining the risks is also making money from the treatment, "informed consent" can start looking a lot like a sales pitch. So: should experimental regenerative therapies be sold to consumers, or should medicine have to prove they work first? Arguing for, Julius Ritter is the founder of the California Peptide Club & CEO of Transcendence, a longevity company working with peptide, exosome, & regenerative therapies. He's part of a growing movement that thinks patients & physicians should have much more freedom to experiment at the frontier of medicine. Arguing against, Dr. Tiana Woolridge is a primary sports medicine physician at Hospital for Special Surgery, double board certified in pediatrics & sports medicine. She's trained in regenerative treatments like PRP herself, which is exactly why she thinks there's a difference between promising medicine & selling something before the evidence is there. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Build Your Creative Operating System
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back - In Person at Salesforce We're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City & sponsored by Boldforce. This Month We Present...Build Your Creative Operating SystemBuild a personalized AI workflow that supports your entire creative process-from capturing ideas to publishing finished work-so you're never starting from scratch. Most of us don't have an idea problem. We have a system problem. Ideas live in our Notes app. Research is scattered across browser tabs. Drafts are hiding in Google Docs. Inspiration gets screenshotted & forgotten. And every new project somehow feels like we're starting all over again. What if your creative process actually remembered how you work? At this month's AI & The Culture meetup, we're exploring how to build your own Creative Operating System-a personalized workflow that uses AI to help you capture ideas, organize knowledge, research, create, refine, & publish your work. Instead of collecting more AI tools, we'll focus on connecting the ones that actually support your process. Together we'll explore:  How to map your creative process from idea to finished work  Ways to capture & organize ideas so they don't disappear into the digital abyss  How AI can help you research, brainstorm, draft, edit, & refine your work  Building a personal knowledge base that makes past ideas & research useful again  How to connect AI tools into repeatable workflows instead of using them one at a time  Where automation can save time-and where your human judgment should stay firmly in the driver's seat  How to create a system that gets smarter & more useful the more you use it The goal isn't to automate your creativity. It's to build the infrastructure around your creativity so you have more time & energy for the work only you can do. Expect a welcoming room filled with creators, technologists, educators, founders, artists, & curious minds ready to rethink how we organize & support our creative lives. Who Should Attend?  Creators & content makers  Filmmakers, writers, artists, & storytellers  Educators & community builders  Entrepreneurs, founders, & solopreneurs  Marketers, strategists, & creative professionals  Technologists & AI enthusiasts  Anyone with too many ideas, too many tabs, & not enough systems  Whether your creative process is already organized or currently held together by screenshots, open tabs, & vibes, you're welcome here. Come Ready to Build This won't be a sit-back-and-scroll kind of evening. Bring your laptop, something to write with, & a mindset ready to learn, experiment, & share. We'll be exploring ideas, tools, & workflows you can begin applying to your own creative process.  Bring your laptop  Bring a notebook or something to take notes with  Bring your curiosity & questions Come ready to learn. Come ready to contribute. Come ready to build. About AI & The Culture AI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, & culture. Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams & King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, & culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, & community. We're building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI. This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture - grounded in community, focused on real-world use, & centered on learning together in the room. Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Let's build - together.  About Your Hosts Shirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, & co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, & creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, & real-world execution. About King Willonius King Willonius is a creative technologist & cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, & creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, & community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable & useful - especially for creatives & innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm.  Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio) #AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: Sobremesa - Private Dinner For Latin American Founders
events.description: Twenty Latin American founders. One table. No stage, no badges, no programme. Sobremesa is the part of the meal nobody schedules - when the plates are cleared & the real conversation starts. That's the whole event. We skipped straight to it. This is not a mixer & it is not a pitch night. There is no panel & no deck. Just founders who are building between Latin America & the United States, at one table, talking about the parts they don't put on LinkedIn. The guest list is the product, so it is built by hand. Every application is reviewed. Who's at the tableFounders who have raised Seed or beyond, based in New York or operating here. Cross-sector by design - fintech next to healthtech next to logistics, because the useful conversations happen between people solving different problems with the same constraints. Our host sponsorDinner is covered by a sponsor who works with founders like the ones at this table. They'll say a few words at the start & then eat with everyone else. We pick partners whose work actually applies to this room - immigration, payroll, hiring across borders - so the conversation stays useful in both directions. Why October 16It closes a week. The night before, Ugly Talk NYC brings Latino founders on stage to tell the version they leave out of the pitch. This dinner is the smaller, quieter room the night after - same community, twenty seats instead of a hundred. Co-hosted by Christopher Martnez (Ziora Copilot) & Sharon Rao, MD. Nuestra gente, nuestra mesa.

events.name: Faith At Work - Christians Working In Big Tech
events.description: Our daily work can be a calling only if it is re-conceived as God's assignment to serve others.  Tim Keller, Every Good Endeavor: Connecting Your Work to God's Work So many of us fool ourselves, believing our work is all about us: What can I accomplish? What do I get from it? Will it give me the money & life that I crave? We're convinced there's a better, different path Christians are meant to consider in how you can show up at work with a sacrificial posture in the tech space. On October 12th, FaithTech NYC is putting a panel together of Christians working in Big Tech companies who've had to work it out on the job, under deadline, with serious consequences. During out time together, we'll unpack: How they make tough decisions based on what the gospel compels us to consider. How they lead & navigate layoffs when they're the one delivering the news. How they talk about Jesus with their co-workers & how you can too. How they think about serving their team in the midst of a work culture obsessed with performance & output. Why their faith has made them better at their job. We'll make some room for your questions at the end. Our hope is that you come away encouraged & inspired to show up different at work the next day. Light food will be provided (donations are appreciated). See you there!

events.name: Startup Pitch & Networking
events.description: Join our event in New York! We design Pitch & Networking nights to help founders sharpen their thinking through direct, candid feedback & to give strong investors access to serious teams. Our pitch night is complemented by a structured networking session before & after the pitch session.  What to expect: Startups pitch live & receive focused feedback from angels & VC partners Structured networking session before & after the pitches Entrepreneurs, startup founders, & operators are joining to network, exchange ideas, & build strong connections Active investors & venture scouts joining to discover the best startups early  Who you will meet at the event: Founders Investors, VC partners, Venture Scouts Marketers, Salespeople, Business Advisors Industry Disruptors AI Experts Entrepreneurs from Europe, Asia, & the United Kingdom  We Welcome New Investors: We invite investors to our event to expand their network, get acquainted with new startups, evaluate them, share feedback, & participate in discussions with early-stage & serial founders. We offer complimentary tickets to institutional investors, angels, & venture scouts with a proven track record. If you'd like to access our database of promising startups or provide mentorship support to our best startups, please fill out this short Investor Application Form, & our team will contact you.  Want to Pitch? A limited number of founders will have the opportunity to pitch their startup or business to a panel of investors & experts. 4-6 selected founders will pitch their startup, followed by a short Q&A where participants can ask questions & share feedback. Apply by filling out the Pitch Application Form & sending us your pitch deck. Spots are limited, & we select founders in advance. To maintain high-quality pitches, you are required to present with a pitch deck. We will share our pitching guide and, if you'd like, coach you so you're fully prepared for pitch night.  The best startups will be featured across our social media & included in our investor newsletter. Requirements for attendees: Dress code: smart casual. Bring good energy.  Join our event & secure your ticket today! About us: Startup Valley is a global event organizer hosting pitch nights in 25 cities since 2023. Since then, we have hosted 850 events for 40,000 attendees. Over these years, we connected countless outstanding early-stage startups to serious investors, & we are not planning to stop. We maintain strategic partnerships with VC funds in the US, Europe, & Asia to support our community. Do you have a question, a partnership proposal, or want to clarify something? Reach us at hello@startupvalley.club Agenda 18:00-18:30 - Registration: Guests register, receive badges, & event programs. This is an opportunity for casual networking, making first connections, & preparing for the event. 18:30-19:00 - Event Kickoff & Interactive Networking: Official welcome from the organizers with a brief overview of the event goals & schedule. Interactive networking session to connect with key contacts. 19:00-19:50 - Startup Pitch Session: Startups present their projects to investors & experts. Each team has 5 minutes to pitch, covering the project's core idea, business model, & target market. 19:50-21:00 - Chill & Networking: Participants enjoy casual conversations with investors, discuss collaboration opportunities, & exchange ideas over refreshments. FAQ Can I pitch? Yes! To pitch, please purchase a Pitch Ticket & fill out the Pitch Application Form. We will contact you to discuss & approve your pitch. The pitch duration is 5 minutes. You will also have some time to answer questions from the audience. How does the pitch go? Selected founders present on stage to the audience & the investors in the room. You get 5 minutes to pitch your idea, business model, target market, & investment ask, followed by a short Q&A. The best startups are featured across our social media channels & in the investor newsletter. Who will I meet? Founders, angel investors, VC partners, venture scouts, AI experts, engineers, operators, marketing & sales experts, & international entrepreneurs from across Europe, Asia, & the US. Do investors get free tickets? Yes! Please apply above or email hello@startupvalley.club, & we will issue a complimentary ticket for you & your team. Can I request a refund? Yes. Refunds are available if requested at least 1 day before the event start time. Please submit the refund request on the platform where you purchased your ticket, or email us at hello@startupvalley.club
