events.name: SOSV Deep Tech Summit
events.description: Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. The producers of the Summit are SOSV's Ned Desmond, Ben Joffe, & Norm Amandi. SOSV's mission is to invest in deep tech companies that advance human & planetary health, & embedded in building an 800+ company portfolio with a remarkable array of companies applying AI in the physical world. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

events.name: Deal Flow: NYC's First VC Hackathon
events.description: Event DescriptionNew York is getting its first VC hackathon, & you're building for the people who write the checks. Deal Flow is a one-day, in-person hackathon hosted by localhost:nyc & VCLab. You get 9 hours to build working products for the real problems VCs face every day. Partners from NYC's top funds judge live, & the best teams leave with intros to those funds. Problem StatementVenture capital runs on spreadsheets, gut feel & endless inbox triage. Firms move billions of dollars with tools that haven't changed in a decade. Your challenge is to build software that helps VCs find better companies, make faster decisions & support their founders after the check clears. The Challenge ThemeSourcing: finding breakout founders before everyone else does Diligence: market maps, competitive analysis & memo drafting Portfolio ops: helping funds support their companies at scale LP reporting: making fund updates less painful & more useful Deal pipeline & CRM workflows that VCs will actually use What to Expect9 hours of focused building, 9 AM to 6 PM Real VC problems, with investors in the room to test your ideas against Teams of 4 Time to meet founders, engineers & investors from across NYC Live demos to a panel of VC judges at the end of the day Food & drinks all day PrizesWinners get intros to the funds in the room + other prizes to be announced. JudgesAbeera Saeed is the Ventures Principal at Plug & Play, investing in Enterprise & AI B2B SaaS companies from Pre-Seed to Series A. Michael Barone - Investment Analyst at Everywhere Ventures, a global pre-seed venture capital firm. D. J. Patel - VC | 3x exited founder. Radhika Khandelwal builds AI agents for a living as a product leader at Wand AI, & she's spent years in the VC world seeing what makes startups stick. She'll want to see both slick code & a real business. Who Should AttendPre-seed & seed founders Engineers Builders who have felt the pain of fundraising firsthand Anyone curious about how venture capital actually works from the inside You don't need VC experience or a finished idea. Just show up ready to build. Sponsors[Sponsor TBD. Want to back NYC's first VC hackathon? Email somyag00@gmail.com] HostsSomya Gupta: The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Tracy Huang: VC Lab & CEO of Interlink IQ

events.name: Robot Hackathon - Code That Moves
events.description: Build physical AI applications with real robot arms @ Viam! About the Event We're excited to host a two-day, hands-on hackathon for curious, ambitious builders who want to go deep on physical AI. You'll get a real robot arm & support from Viam experts throughout. No prior robotics experience is required, just an interest in physical AI & some software experience. See what engineers built at the last hackathon here. Space is limited! Apply through this page. Applicants will be accepted on a rolling basis. What You'll Build Working in a team of 2-3, you'll build an end-to-end robotics application using Viam & a real robot arm. Each team will have access to: UFactory xArm or Universal Robots arm with a two-finger gripper attachment (feel free to also bring your own SO-101) Linux compute machine RealSense D435 or Orbbec Astra 2 camera (fixed to arm) Webcams A free Viam account We'll provide a variety of objects for your robot to manipulate. You are encouraged to bring anything required for the project you have in mind. Please bring your own laptop. In your application, please summarize what project you have in mind. Ideas from past events: training a VLA, playing chess, mixing a cocktail, quality inspection, drawing a picture, puzzle insertion, manipulating a robot arm using computer vision & hand gestures. Prizes We'll award prizes to a total of three teams. Each member of a winning team will take home SO-101 pre-assembled robot kits, including: a leader arm, a follower arm, & a camera + Viam credits. Gold: SO-101 arm + $5,000 in Viam credits Silver: SO-101 arm+ $2,500 in Viam credits Bronze: SO-101 arm + $1,000 in Viam credits Please bring your own laptop. We recommend taking our free online course Viam 101 (est time: 45-90mins) ahead of time. Even if you only go through the first lessons, it will help you get the hang of things quickly. Schedule Friday, October 169:00 AM: Check-in & breakfast9:30 AM: Kickoff: Welcome & crash course on building with Viam10:00 AM: Teams & hardware10:30 AM: Hacking begins1:00 PM: Lunch6:00 PM: Dinner9:00 PM: Hard close: Robots power down, doors close (no overnight hacking) Saturday, October 179:00 AM: Doors open, breakfast9:30 AM: Hacking resumes12:30 PM: Lunch3:30 PM: Demos & drinks5:00 PM: Awards6:00 PM: Event concludes What Skills You Need No robotics experience required, but you should be comfortable with: Coding: Python, Go, TypeScript/JavaScript, or C++ Linux: Using SSH & running basic terminal commands JSON: Reading & editing configuration files Git: Basic workflows so your team can build together Bonus: knowing how to plug in a pre-trained vision model (like YOLO or OpenCV) to help the robot see & identify objects (not required) Before the Event We recommend taking our free online course Viam 101 (est time: 45-90mins) ahead of time. Even the first few lessons will help you get the hang of things quickly. How to Join Space is limited! Apply through this page. Applicants will be accepted on a rolling basis. We'll select a curated group of ambitious software developers & send official confirmations to accepted participants. Attendees must be approved in advance to participate. Presented By Viam - The robotics software platform we'll use to configure, control, & deploy models to your robot. Viam makes it easy to get a robot up & running quickly.

events.name: AI Engineer Kids Day
events.description: Welcome to our very first AI Engineer Kids Day in New York City. We're thrilled to have you here! This special event brings together curious young minds & their families for a fun, hands-on introduction to artificial intelligence, coding, & technology. We're especially excited to welcome Cassandra Chin, an outstanding computer science graduate & author, who has led engaging workshops at conferences around the world. Cassandra will guide participants through interactive sessions designed to spark creativity, build confidence, & make complex ideas accessible & fun. These workshops are recommended for kids aged 9 to 15, & parents are encouraged to join. Whether you're completely new to AI or already curious about how things work behind the scenes, this is a chance to learn, explore, & create - together! Agenda 12:30 PM - Doors open & registration - Arrive, check in, & get settled. 1:00 PM -  AI Workshop 3:00 PM - Workshop concludes, parents arrive for pickup 3:30 PM - Event ends Workshops Learn AI by Making Games with Phippy!Taught by Cassandra Chin What if you could dream up a game & bring it to life with AI? In this hands-on workshop, kids will team up with an AI coding assistant to create their own playable 2D games using the open source Godot game engine & colorful Phippy & Friends characters. From treasure hunts to tricky mazes, they'll choose the adventure & help shape the rules. As they build, play, & improve their games, kids will practice giving AI clear instructions, checking its work, & solving problems when things don't go as planned. Along the way, they'll discover that AI can help write the code, but they're the game designers in charge! No previous coding or game-making experience is needed, just curiosity & a willingness to experiment, explore, & play! Bio: Cassandra Chin is a keynote speaker, author, podcast host, & computer science student. She has led technology workshops for kids at international conferences since age 13 & is passionate about expanding access to tech education for women, minorities, & underserved communities. What to know before you come:Please bring your own laptop so you can fully participate in the hands-on activities. Space is limited, so if you're unable to attend, please cancel your registration to allow another child to join. We will be taking photos & videos during the event, which will be shared online & featured at the keynote of the AI Engineer World Fair conference that week. Please let us know if you agree to be included in the registration process. Parents or guardians will need to be present to sign their child in at the beginning & sign them out at the end of the event & they welcome to stay & assist your child. No lunch provided, please bring your snack & water Call for Volunteers We're looking for volunteers to support kids during the hands-on workshops. Parents & those with some technical background are invited to help guide & inspire kids as they build & explore. Please register at Open Google Form We can't wait to build with you!

events.name: Borderless Office - Identity & Access In World Of Remote-First Growth
events.description: Join Antoine Jebara (Co-founder, JumpCloud) & Noah Landow (Founder & CEO, Macktez) for an informal conversation between an expert on scaling global technology companies & the evolution of identity & access management & the founder of a technology consulting firm. In an era defined by remote work & the rapid rise of agentic AI, the concepts of identity & security are shifting beneath our feet. As AI agents begin to act on our behalf, how do we maintain control, responsibility, & security? If an AI agent executes a transaction or accesses a database, who is truly holding the keys? Antoine brings a unique perspective from the front lines of this transition, from pioneering decentralized 2FA & password management at MYKI to driving global strategy & partner ecosystems at JumpCloud. Join us at the Macktez office, after work, over light snacks & sips, for an exploratory conversation on the challenges of scaling fast-growing global companies & how different security architectures impact our long-term safety in a cloud-first world. We will dive into the shifting landscape of encryption, the unique hurdles of managing remote-first organizations, & what it truly means to "identity" ourselves in the age of AI. Photography, audio, & video recording may occur at this event & by attending you consent to such recording media & its release, publication, exhibition, or reproduction. Event StructureWe ask that guests arrive between 7-7:30 pm to minimize disruption during the talk. 7 pm - Doors open, opportunity to mingle over snacks & sips with other attendees7:30 pm - Guests take their seats for the talk8:15 pm - Informal mixer resumes On AttendanceWe have a limited capacity. If your plans change, please update your registration so someone else can join. A bit about Macktez, & why we host this seriesMacktez is a technology consultancy collaborating with organizations going through dynamic change. Our goal is to form a lasting partnership between our team & our clients, so we can anticipate their technology challenges & help them navigate growth, disruption, & other evolving conditions. Each event in our Tte--Tech series is an opportunity to explore a specific cultural, scientific, historical, & personal issue. We fire at the synapses that connect each topic to other fields of interest & to our individual lives. And we do so in a comfortable environment to facilitate conversation that can be casual, surprising, & illuminating. To learn more, visit us at macktez.com.

events.name: AI/ML Lecture & Mixer
events.description: A monthly ML research colloquium by the New York Machine Learning Research Guild - this session in collaboration with our partner, CUNY Tech Prep. Speaker: Zayne Sprague  PhD Researcher, Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences, NYU & GoogleTopic: From Chain of Thought to Agent Swarms: A Brief Story on Reasoning in LLMs Giving language models more time to think has produced substantial gains, but in targeted domains, & the benefits appear to remain uneven across tasks. This talk explores how models can use additional computation at inference time effectively, reviewing the progression from prompt based methods to multi-agent systems. We will begin with chain-of-thought prompting, asking a model to think before giving a final answer, presenting our work showing that chain-of-thought prompting has its strongest benefits concentrated in mathematics & symbolic reasoning. These domains also share a practical advantage: answers can often be checked automatically, providing feedback that can be used to train models through reinforcement learning. This leads us to SkillFactory, where we use a model's own successful & unsuccessful attempts to construct training examples that demonstrate checking answers & retrying. Combining supervised finetuning on these examples with reinforcement learning helps models develop these behaviors & generalize to harder problems. Finally, we will discuss recent work on agent swarms, exploring how reasoning can scale in parallel & what role verification can play in making that additional computation useful. This session is a close-quarters look at that work, with plenty of room to push back & dig in. # Who this is forNY-MLR colloquia are small by design. The room is capped, & we keep it that way so the discussion stays substantive & everyone in it can contribute. We'd love to see you if you're:- A practitioner working seriously on ML, in industry or in a lab- A researcher or graduate student in ML, NLP, or an adjacent field- A highly motivated student or self-directed learner of any age or background, with real depth of interest # Schedule5:00 - 5:30 PM - Doors open, arrivals, mingling5:30 - 6:30 PM - Speaker Lecture6:30 - 7:00 PM - Moderated Q&A7:00 - 8:00 PM - After hours, mingling, wind-down8:00 PM - Lights out Venue: Amazon JFK27 ("Hank")  12 W 39th St, New York, NY 10018

There's also a gallery where you can see the thousands of wonderful user-submitted collages made with the program. Palestine Skating Game A videogame in development that centers Arabic electronic music, graffiti, & Splatoon-style paint shooting. events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: AI & China
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In July, a Chinese lab you'd probably never heard of published Kimi K3: 2.8 trillion parameters, billed as the largest open model on earth, weights posted free on Hugging Face for anyone to download. It's one of four Chinese labs that spent the last year closing the gap with the American frontier, then giving the result away. Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi. Four of the five most-used open models in the world now come out of Beijing, & American developers are running them inside hospitals, law firms, & startups because they're the cheapest, fastest tools available. No API someone in Washington controls. No off switch. Just download & go. One camp says a model is just math. Open weights run on a consumer's machine, the code is right there to inspect, & cutting Americans off from the best tools on the planet is how you lose a technology race. The other camp says the giveaway is the strategy. China seeds the world's infrastructure with their standards, their defaults, their assumptions, & the dependency follows once switching costs become unbeatable. So: should Americans be allowed to build on Chinese open-weight models or is this the new Cold War's Monkey's Paw? Arguing for, Rob Li is Managing Partner of Amont Partners, a New York global equity firm that invests across the US & Asia. He has spent his career putting capital on both sides of the Pacific, from Yum China to Alibaba deals, & he thinks the country that walls itself off from the best tools available loses. Arguing against, Will McKelvey is a Principal at Lerer Hippeau, one of New York's oldest venture firms, where he backs early-stage founders & spends his days watching for the future of AI, especially in consumer. He got his start by way of a congressional office, & he thinks the cheapest model on the market is the one you pay for slowly. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones. In collaboration with COMMITTEE OF 100Committee of 100 (C100) is a nonprofit U.S. leadership organization of distinguished Chinese Americans dedicated to advancing the full participation of Chinese Americans in American society & fostering constructive U.S.-China relations. For more than 35 years, C100 has brought together leaders across business, government, academia, technology, media, the arts, & other fields to advance its dual mission. Learn more at committee100.org.

events.name: Post Human Investment Summit
events.description: In the 1980s, Renaissance Technologies pioneered a new way to beat the markets: computing power, statistics, and signal processing. Today that approach anchors a $1.2 trillion asset class, but one built almost entirely on short-horizon trades.The holy grail has always been the opposite: long-horizon investing, fully automated. An agentic Warren Buffett. With the tools we had, it felt out of reach. Agentic reasoning systems may finally change that. A new wave of frontier researchers, 6 newly launched fully agentic funds, and tiger teams inside established funds are setting out to build it.Join us for a one day summit alongside many of the early leaders in this space, to share ideas, challenge assumptions, and brainstorm the various paths ahead for this burgeoning space. The event will be a tightly curated group of researchers, builders, investment professionals, and LPs. Please apply below to be included.Hosted by Pillar VCPillar VC is a Boston-based seed-stage venture capital firm. We invest in engineers, researchers, and scientists building solutions to the worlds greatest challenges, including Circle, Abridge, Algorand, PillPack, Jellyfish, Neural Magic, Hometap, Asimov, and PathAI, and others.

events.name: How To Raise Your First Priced Round
events.description: 4 part workshop hosted by Healing Healthtech on "How to Raise Your First Priced Round." Raising your first priced round is a completely different undertaking than stacking safe notes. I want to help you skip the avoidable mistakes.  The diligence is deeper, the relevant terms are completely different, & the stakes for getting it wrong are much higher as priced round investors will almost always take board seats & protective provisions.  I've taught founders how to navigate a priced round for years & on October 27th in NYC will be conducting a public bootcamp / workshop with the highest impact aspects. Location will be the beautiful Gunderson Dettmer NYC offices above Flatiron. Generously sponsored by Jose Rivera & Tonna Obaze of Gunderson Dettmer, Kelly Caviglia of Mercury, & Paul Brezovsky III of Qapita. Session 1: Taught by Ramesh Karra & Paul Brezovsky III's team at Qapita will focus on Data Room. What goes in, what doesn't, what investors are looking for, & how not get get tripped up. Session 2: Taught by Jose Rivera of Gunderson Dettmer will focus on the term sheet negotiation. What terms matter & which don't. How to affect outcomes that are durable & beneficial for your business. Session 3: Taught by me will focused on how to find, pitch, & close priced round investors. Session 4: Will be a panel discussion & fireside chat with 3 partners at NYC VC firms. I've purposely chosen folks who represent software & hardware investors as well as funds that operate outside of healthcare. Mat Kaliski of Acronym Venture CapitalBrian Laung Aoaeh, CFA of REFASHIOND Ventures: The Industrial Transformation FundOwen Willis of Opal Ventures & Primary Venture Partners

events.name: Tech Table Talk: At The Intersection Of Tech, Media & AI
events.description: Tech Table Talk is an intimate dinner bringing together women shaping what's next across technology, media, commerce, & AI. Hosted by People Culture & Belonging & Black Affinity Group in partnership with Baddies in Tech, the evening is designed to create space for meaningful connection, candid conversation, & thoughtful exchange around how women are influencing the future of these rapidly evolving industries. What to ExpectArrival & ConnectionEase into the evening with drinks, light bites, & time to connect with fellow guests before dinner begins. Dinner & Tech Table TalkOver dinner, guests will have the opportunity to connect more deeply with one another through thoughtful conversation & curated table prompts. The conversation will invite guests to share what they're building, exploring, questioning, & imagining for the future of technology, media, commerce, & AI. Dessert & Fireside ConversationTo close the evening, Randi Gray, Head of IT at MERIT Beauty, will join Allie Joy Tsahey, CEO of Baddies in Tech, for an intimate fireside conversation exploring the intersection of technology, AI, media, & commerce. Together, they'll unpack how emerging technology is reshaping the way people discover, consume, create, shop, & engage with content & products, & what that evolution means for the women helping shape what comes next. What You'll meaningful connection to the Baddies in Tech & People communities A new question, idea, or perspective to carry with you beyond the evening Attendance is complimentary & curated. Because this form expresses your interest in attending & does not guarantee an invitation. events.name: SOSV Deep Tech Summit
events.description: SOSV DEEP TECH SUMMIT Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. The producers of the Summit are SOSV's Ned Desmond, Ben Joffe, & Norm Amandi. More DetailsSOSV's mission is to invest in deep tech companies that advance human & planetary health, & embedded in building an 800+ company portfolio with a remarkable array of companies applying AI in the physical world. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

events.name: Latinos x AI Hackathon
events.description: Latinos x AI Hackathon - NYCSaturday, October 10  10:00 AM - 6:00 PM  New York City Nuestra gente. Nuestros problemas. Nuestro cdigo. For Hispanic Heritage Month, 150 builders are spending one Saturday in New York building AI for the problems our communities actually live with. Not a demo day. Not a panel. Eight hours, three tracks, working software by 5pm. Applications are reviewed. Attendance is free. The Three TracksPick one when you apply. Build for it all day. 01  Immigration - Papers & Process Status, documents, deadlines, & the systems that decide who belongs. Think intake triage for legal aid clinics, plain-language explainers for immigration forms, interpreter tooling, case-status tracking, know-your-rights assistants. 02  Healthcare - Care Without Barriers Language, coverage, & access for patients the system was not built for. Think interpretation at the point of care, insurance navigation, discharge instructions people can actually read, community health worker tooling, prescription & benefits literacy. 03  Finance - Banking the Unbanked Credit, remittances, & building wealth without a financial history. Think remittance transparency, credit-building for thin-file borrowers, small business bookkeeping for cash operations, benefits & tax navigation, fraud protection for first-generation account holders. Prizes$4,500 total - $1,500 per track. Every track winner also gets [sponsor perks once confirmed]. ScheduleSchedule 10:00 AM - Doors, breakfast, team formation10:45 AM - Opening remarks & track briefings11:15 AM - Building starts1:00 PM - Lunch3:00 PM - Mentor office hours & mid-day checkpoint4:45 PM - Submissions close5:00 PM - Demos on stage5:45 PM - Judging & awards6:00 PM - Close Who Should ApplyEngineers, data scientists, & designers who want to ship something real in a day Product people & founders who can shape a problem & pitch it Clinicians, immigration attorneys, paralegals, social workers, & financial counselors - the people who know the problem from the inside. You do not need to code to be valuable here. Teams with a domain expert consistently win. Students & career switchers You can apply solo or with a team of up to four. Solo applicants will be matched at 10:00 AM. What to BringLaptop & charger A problem you have seen up close ID for building security We provide breakfast, lunch, coffee, wifi, power, mentors, & the room. RulesBuild during the event. Prior research & planning are fine; prior code is not. Teams of one to four. Every submission needs a public repo, a two-minute demo video, & a short written description. You keep everything you build. No IP claims from organizers or sponsors. Be decent to each other. Harassment of any kind means you leave. Mentors & Judges[ADD once confirmed: names, titles, organizations.] Partners & Sponsors[ADD once confirmed: logos & names.] Interested in sponsoring or partnering? Write to chris@ziora-copilot.com or book 30 minutes. Sponsorship closes October 1. FAQIs it free? Yes. Applications are reviewed because space is limited to 150. Where is it? New York City. The exact address is shared with approved attendees. Do I have to be Latino to attend? No. The event is built by & for the Latino community in New York, & everyone who wants to build for these problems is welcome. Do I need a team? No. Come solo & we will match you at the start. What language is the event in? English, with Spanish spoken throughout. Apply & demo in whichever you prefer. Can I keep working on my project afterward? Please do. That is the point. A note on selection: This edition is built for & centered on the Latino community in New York. Applications from Latino & Hispanic builders will be prioritized. Allies are welcome to apply & will be considered as space allows. Questions: chris@ziora-copilot.com Hosted by Christopher Martinez

events.name: Ugly Talk: Your First $100K Deal
events.description: Your first six-figure deal can expose every weak spot in your sales process. You chased the wrong buyer. Priced from fear. Followed up too late. Let one internal champion carry the whole deal. Then the contract lands. You celebrate. The next question hurts more: can you do it again? This Ugly Talk gets into the hard calls behind closing a major customer. You will hear what founders got wrong. events.description: ATLAS Innovation Exchange @ NY Tech Meetup   NY Tech Alliance is excited to welcome back our friends from ATLAS in Rome, Italy for another special international edition of the NY Tech Meetup. We're bringing together the NYC tech community & a new group of standout Italian founders building ambitious companies & technologies for the future. It's an opportunity to connect two dynamic tech ecosystems, meet founders you may not otherwise encounter in New York, & build new relationships across the Atlantic. Whether you're a founder, investor, technologist, operator, or simply curious about what's emerging next, come meet the people building it. Come for the demos. It is the world's largest meetup group of its kind with over 50,000 members who have a common interest in learning from & helping one another. At each event, entrepreneurs, founders, CEOs, & their teams demo cutting edge & transformative tech, answer questions from attendees & network with all in a welcoming & fun-filled space. Since its creation, over 1,200 companies have participated & have been a driving force of innovation & job creation in NYC & the greater NY area. About ATLAS ATLAS is a leading Italian ecosystem supporting the internationalization of startups. Based in Rome & part of Confindustria's innovation network, ATLAS helps founders expand into the U.S. & global markets through education, tools, & strategic support.  Learn more: www.assoatlas.org

events.name: Hack For Impact - AI Workflow Hackathon
events.description: Pioneering Minds AI: Hack for ImpactAn AI Workflow HackathonDont just use AI. Redesign how work gets done.AI is changing how we research, learn, build products, analyze contracts, manage money, & make decisions. But adding a chatbot to an existing process is not the same as building an AI-native workflow.The real opportunity is to rethink the workflow itself:What should humans still do?What should AI handle?What can be automated entirely?And where does human judgment become even more important?This is a one-day hackathon where participants redesign real-world workflows using AI.Teams will choose a problem from one of four tracks, identify a broken or inefficient workflow, & build an AI-native product, agent, or system that makes it dramatically better.You do not need to arrive with a startup idea.Come with curiosity. Find a problem. Build something.The winning teams can also secure their spot at our upcoming Pitching Masterclass, where they can sharpen their story, product positioning, & pitch.The ChallengeTeams will identify an existing workflow & redesign it for the age of AI.Your project should answer three questions:What is broken, slow, repetitive, or unnecessarily difficult today?What should AI do differently?What does the new workflow look like when AI is built into it from the beginning?Projects can take the form of an AI agent, internal tool, workflow automation, consumer product, enterprise application, or prototype.Hackathon TracksParticipants may choose one of four tracks.Critical Thinking & LearningAI can produce answers in seconds. But getting an answer is not the same as understanding something. As AI becomes capable of performing more cognitive tasks, skills such as critical thinking, judgment, curiosity, problem decomposition, & learning how to learn may become even more important. Build a product or workflow that uses AI to help people think better rather than simply think less.AI for Product Management WorkflowsProduct managers spend enormous amounts of time gathering information, coordinating teams, analyzing feedback, writing documents, prioritizing ideas, & turning ambiguity into decisions.Many of these workflows were designed before AI existed. Redesign them.Legal Tech WorkflowsLegal work is full of complex, document-heavy processes where accuracy, judgment, & context matter.AI creates an opportunity to fundamentally rethink how legal professionals research, review, draft, analyze, & manage information.They must also consider accuracy, explainability, accountability, & human review.Fintech & Insurtech WorkflowsFinancial services & insurance involve some of the most complex workflows in business: underwriting, compliance, risk assessment, fraud detection, claims, financial analysis, & customer onboarding.Many still involve fragmented systems, repetitive manual review, & enormous amounts of unstructured data.What You'll BuildTeams will have one day to identify a problem, design a solution, build a prototype, & present it to our judges.Your prototype does not need to be production-ready.We care about:The quality of the problemHow thoughtfully you redesign the workflowHow meaningfully AI improves the processThe usability of your prototypeWhether someone would actually use itAll backgrounds are welcome.You do not need to be an engineer to participate.Product managers, designers, lawyers, finance professionals, founders, students, operators, & domain experts are strongly encouraged to join.Coaching & mentorship will be available onsite.What We'll ExploreAI agents & workflow automationHuman + AI collaborationProduct design in the age of AICritical thinking & human judgmentLegal AIFintech & insurtechRapid prototypingStartup product strategyVenture-style pitchingSchedule09:00  09:30 Check-in events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Personal AI Agents, Muse, Instinct & Fight For Your Inbox
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quick research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data.  45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Personal AI agents - Muse, Instinct, & the fight for your inbox Meta's new agent Muse hit #1 on the App Store within 10 days of launch, passing ChatGPT - while a much smaller startup, Instinct, is quietly building a following by working entirely through text message, no app required. Both agents now book things, send emails, & make purchases on your behalf, & both have already run into real trust & privacy controversies. We're decoding: Are personal AI agents actually ready to be trusted with your accounts & money? Supporting questions: What's the real difference between "an agent that acts for you" & "a chatbot that answers you" - & does that difference justify the privacy trade-off? Does Meta's distribution advantage make Muse the inevitable winner, or does Instinct's leaner, invite-only approach have a real shot? What if Google, Apple & others launch personal AI Agents like Muse? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like.

events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Build Your Creative Operating System
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back - In Person at Salesforce We're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City & sponsored by Boldforce. This Month We Present...Build Your Creative Operating SystemBuild a personalized AI workflow that supports your entire creative process-from capturing ideas to publishing finished work-so you're never starting from scratch. Most of us don't have an idea problem. We have a system problem. Ideas live in our Notes app. Research is scattered across browser tabs. Drafts are hiding in Google Docs. Inspiration gets screenshotted & forgotten. And every new project somehow feels like we're starting all over again. What if your creative process actually remembered how you work? At this month's AI & The Culture meetup, we're exploring how to build your own Creative Operating System-a personalized workflow that uses AI to help you capture ideas, organize knowledge, research, create, refine, & publish your work. Instead of collecting more AI tools, we'll focus on connecting the ones that actually support your process. Together we'll explore:  How to map your creative process from idea to finished work  Ways to capture & organize ideas so they don't disappear into the digital abyss  How AI can help you research, brainstorm, draft, edit, & refine your work  Building a personal knowledge base that makes past ideas & research useful again  How to connect AI tools into repeatable workflows instead of using them one at a time  Where automation can save time-and where your human judgment should stay firmly in the driver's seat  How to create a system that gets smarter & more useful the more you use it The goal isn't to automate your creativity. It's to build the infrastructure around your creativity so you have more time & energy for the work only you can do. Expect a welcoming room filled with creators, technologists, educators, founders, artists, & curious minds ready to rethink how we organize & support our creative lives. Who Should Attend?  Creators & content makers  Filmmakers, writers, artists, & storytellers  Educators & community builders  Entrepreneurs, founders, & solopreneurs  Marketers, strategists, & creative professionals  Technologists & AI enthusiasts  Anyone with too many ideas, too many tabs, & not enough systems  Whether your creative process is already organized or currently held together by screenshots, open tabs, & vibes, you're welcome here. Come Ready to Build This won't be a sit-back-and-scroll kind of evening. Bring your laptop, something to write with, & a mindset ready to learn, experiment, & share. We'll be exploring ideas, tools, & workflows you can begin applying to your own creative process.  Bring your laptop  Bring a notebook or something to take notes with  Bring your curiosity & questions Come ready to learn. Come ready to contribute. Come ready to build. About AI & The Culture AI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, & culture. Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams & King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, & culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, & community. We're building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI. This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture - grounded in community, focused on real-world use, & centered on learning together in the room. Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Let's build - together.  About Your Hosts Shirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, & co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, & creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, & real-world execution. About King Willonius King Willonius is a creative technologist & cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, & creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, & community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable & useful - especially for creatives & innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm.  Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio) #AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: Decentralized AI Day
events.description: We're bringing together builders & long-time contributors from the Numerai & decentralized AI ecosystems for a mix of talks, a workshop, & a special community panel. Featured speakers: Jason - Co-Founder & CEO, CrowdCent Nick - Co-Founder & CEO, Allora Labs Matteo - Co-Founder & CEO, Orion Finance The Numerai "Out of Sample" Special Panel  A discussion & AMA-style panel with guests featured on the Out of Sample interview series. All three are current or former members of the Numerai Council of Elders, with the panel moderated by another member of the Council. Tim (aka jefferythewind) (see episode 2) ShatteredX (see episode 3) Jason (see episode 4) More speakers & session details coming soon. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/ Important Note  This is an in-person-only event; there will be no livestream. For security reasons, we must provide a guest list to the security team at least 24 hours before the event. You must provide your  FULL NAME  when registering for this event. If you prefer not to display your full name publicly, please provide it in the final registration question instead. Your full name will be shared only with the security team. About Decentralized AI Days  Decentralized AI Days are community-driven events exploring how open, decentralized AI & Web3 can work together in practice. We bring together engineers, researchers, & builders for a day of technical talks, hands-on workshops, & honest conversation - no hype, no sales pitches, & no pay-to-play. The ecosystem we care about includes projects such as Numerai & CrowdCent. The door is open to anyone building with or curious about decentralized AI. Come for the substance, stay for the community. Call for Presentations  Interested in sharing your experience with our community? Please contact me (Joe) directly via X, or on LinkedIn. I'll get back to you as soon as possible. Everyone is welcome to apply, as long as your talk or workshop topic is relevant. Agenda  More details will be announced soon! Expect a program of tech talks & workshops, followed by a relaxed evening mixer. What to Expect   Connect with a friendly community of AI & Web3 builders, researchers, & curious minds.  Enjoy zero-hype technical talks focused on real problems & practical insights.  Take part in hands-on workshops where you can learn by building.  Watch live demos of decentralized AI & related projects.  Meet the organizers & share your questions & feedback directly.  Explore community resources & connect over food. Who Should Attend)  Decentralized AI Days are for everyone curious about where AI & decentralized systems meet: AI/ML engineers, Web3 developers, researchers, students, & builders at any experience level. If you are new to the space, you are welcome; if you have been building for years, you will find your people here. Come ready to learn, share, & connect. The Venue  Register to see the address. Here are some photos of the venue: Main Room Sponsors  DeAI Day is a community event series sponsored by Numerai & the Numerai Council of Elders. Complimentary refreshments will be provided throughout the day. Come early & grab some cool swags! Code of Conduct  All attendees, speakers, sponsors, & volunteers must agree to the following Code of Conduct. Event organizers will enforce these guidelines throughout the event. We expect full cooperation from everyone to help ensure a welcoming & safe environment for all participants. Our event is committed to providing an inclusive & harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of gender, gender identity or expression, age, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance, body size, race, ethnicity, religion (or lack thereof), or technology preferences. Harassment in any form will not be tolerated. Sexually explicit language or imagery is inappropriate for any part of the event, including talks, workshops, social activities, or online platforms. Participants who violate these rules may be warned or expelled from the event at the discretion of the organizers. Past Events  Materials from past Decentralized AI Days live in the community meetups repository. We have also hosted similar events under a different name (Numerai Community Meetup) from 2022 to 2024: London (July 2022) New York (September 2022) Tokyo (April 2023) Prague (July 2023) Toronto (October 2023) San Francisco (January 2024) Frankfurt (April 2024) Tokyo (July 2024) Bangkok (November 2024) Finally, here's one meme to sum up the vibe.

events.name: Six Math Essentials w/ Terence Tao
events.description: Book Launch & Conversation with Janna Levin Widely regarded as the world's greatest living mathematician, Fields Medalist Terence Tao approaches mathematics as a sublime art-a quiet, rigorous effort to map the hidden scaffolding of reality. To mark the publication of his first popular book, Six Math Essentials, join us for an evening with Tao in conversation with Pioneer Works Director of Sciences Janna Levin. Tracing the central pillars of his book-from algebra as abstraction & geometry beyond sight, to navigating uncertainty & the mathematics of change-they will reveal math not as obscure magic, but as a deeply creative, interconnected way of thinking. Often referred to as the Mozart of mathematics, Tao will also explore how AI is transforming his own practice, the frontier of research, & our collective future. Together, we will consider what becomes of human intuition & creativity when the tools of thought are no longer uniquely human-and whether the true beauty of math lies not in the answers we find, but in the human mind reaching for them. Tao will sign copies of Six Math Essentials following the conversation, with books available for purchase on site. (Unable to attend? Order a signed copy here.) Please note that seating is limited & will be available on a first-come, first-served basis.   About the speakersTerence Tao is an Australian-American professor of mathematics at UCLA whose work focuses primarily on harmonic analysis, partial differential equations, combinatorics, & analytic number theory. The recipient of a Fields Medal, a MacArthur Genius Grant, & a Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics, among many other accolades, he is one of the most decorated & prolific mathematicians working today. Tao is the author of several academic books including Solving Mathematical Problems: A Personal Perspective & Additive Combinatorics, as well as his first popular math book, Six Math Essentials. He lives in Los Angeles. Janna Levin is the Claire Tow Professor of physics & astronomy at Barnard College of Columbia University. A Guggenheim Fellow, she has contributed to our understanding of black holes, extra dimensions, & cosmology. She is the founding director of sciences at Pioneer Works & the founding editor-in-chief of the magazine Pioneer Works Broadcast. She often contributes to news, documentaries, & radio, including as the presenter of the NOVA feature Black Hole Apocalypse on PBS & as a contributor to CBS, CNN, BBC, & NBC. She has authored books on black holes & the universe-Black Hole Blues, How the Universe Got its Spots, & Black Hole Survival Guide-as well as a PEN award-winning novel, A Madman Dreams of Turing Machines. You can find her current writings in Higher Dimensions. This program is funded by the Simons Foundation International & administered by the Simons Foundation's Science, Society & Culture division.

events.name: AI Fraud & Death Of Resume - Restoring Algorithmic Trust
events.description: Conquer the AI job market battleground with elite CISO Dr. Rachel Levitch. Learn to restore algorithmic trust & secure your pipeline!  The 2026 job market is facing an unprecedented security & operational crisis. The recruitment landscape has evolved from a standard talent search into a high-stakes battleground of synthetic data. Candidates are deploying advanced, hyper-automated AI agents to mass-apply to hundreds of open roles instantly, reverse-engineer corporate Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS), auto-generate perfect skill matches, & deploy deepfake technology to bypass initial technical screenings. HR departments & engineering teams are drowning in a sea of algorithmic noise. As talent pipelines become flooded with AI-polished fraud, a staggering percentage of enterprise managers report that total trust in the inbound pipeline has completely eroded. In this high-stakes security & talent briefing, Dr. Rachel Levitch-seasoned Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) & founder of the Cognitive Institute-shifts the conversation from simple recruitment metrics to hard-line Systems Security & Information Integrity. We will move beyond the traditional interview structure to explore the mechanics of modern algorithmic fraud, the vulnerabilities of automated screening systems, & the implementation of secure identity & skill verification frameworks. This session provides human resource executives, tech founders, & venture capitalists with the exact tactical roadmap required to bypass synthetic candidate noise, protect personal data privacy, & restore institutional trust in a market-led crisis. Key Takeaways for Attendees: The AI Vulnerability Audit: A live technical breakdown of how 2026 AI-auto-apply bots actively breach, manipulate, & exploit corporate ATS filters.Detecting the Synthetic Candidate: Concrete, practical strategies for talent acquisition teams to identify AI-forged certifications, deepfake video setups, & automated resume stuffing.Rebuilding the Trust Chain: Transitioning your organization toward zero-trust recruitment frameworks, secure identity verification, & authentic human-sustainability metrics. Purchase Tickets At URL Below or See All Events here: https://www.eventbrite.com/o/121452823948

events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Create Once. Publish Everywhere.
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back - In Person at Salesforce We're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City & sponsored by Boldforce. This Month We Present...Create Once. Publish Everywhere.Learn how top creators turn one idea into newsletters, videos, podcasts, social posts, presentations, & more using AI-powered content systems. Creating the idea is only half the work. Then comes the newsletter. The social posts. The video. The presentation. The podcast. The clips. And somehow, every platform wants something different. What if you didn't have to start from scratch every single time? At this month's AI & The Culture meetup, we're exploring how creators, entrepreneurs, educators, filmmakers, & small teams are using AI-powered content systems to turn one strong idea into an entire ecosystem of content. We'll look beyond simply asking AI to write me a post & dig into how you can build repeatable workflows that help you create, adapt, & distribute your ideas across formats-without losing your voice in the process. Together we'll explore:  How to turn one core idea into multiple pieces of content  AI workflows for newsletters, social posts, video, podcasts, presentations, & more  How to adapt an idea for different platforms instead of simply copying & pasting  Ways to build repeatable content systems that save time & creative energy  How to keep your voice, perspective, & cultural context consistent across AI-assisted content  Practical strategies for spending less time feeding the content machine & more time developing ideas worth sharing The goal isn't to create more content just for the sake of creating more content. It's to make your best ideas work harder for you. Expect a welcoming room filled with creators, technologists, educators, founders, artists, & curious minds ready to learn how AI can support a smarter, more sustainable creative process. Who Should Attend?  Creators & content makers  Filmmakers, writers, artists, & storytellers  Educators & community builders  Entrepreneurs, founders, & solopreneurs  Marketers, strategists, & social media professionals  Podcasters & video creators  Anyone with ideas they want to share more consistently Whether you're building a personal brand, growing a business, educating an audience, promoting your creative work, or simply tired of reinventing the wheel every time you post-this conversation is for you. Come Ready to Build This won't be a sit-back-and-scroll kind of evening. Bring your laptop, something to write with, & a mindset ready to learn, experiment, & share. We'll be exploring ideas, tools, & workflows you can start applying to your own creative process.  Bring your laptop  Bring a notebook or something to take notes with  Bring your curiosity & questions Come ready to learn. Come ready to contribute. Come ready to build. About AI & The Culture AI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, & culture. Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams & King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, & culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, & community. We're building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI. This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture - grounded in community, focused on real-world use, & centered on learning together in the room. Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Let's build - together.  About Your Hosts Shirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, & co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, & creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, & real-world execution. About King Willonius King Willonius is a creative technologist & cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, & creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, & community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable & useful - especially for creatives & innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm.  Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio) #AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: An Unmuted Debate - Peptides vs The People
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In partnership with Pepper NYC & the Peptide Club of NYC A peptide to heal your tendon. An injection to rebuild your knee. Exosomes to make your body younger. Regenerative medicine is moving fast, & consumers increasingly don't want to wait ten years for the clinical trials to catch up (the AIDS crisis..). Some of these treatments have real science behind them. Others have promising early evidence. And some are being sold for thousands of dollars long before anyone can say with confidence that they actually work. But maybe that's the point. We let adults make risky decisions everywhere else. If a patient understands the evidence is uncertain, why shouldn't they be allowed to spend their own money trying something experimental? The alternative is the basic bargain medicine has relied on for decades: prove it works before you sell it. Because when the person explaining the risks is also making money from the treatment, "informed consent" can start looking a lot like a sales pitch. So: should experimental regenerative therapies be sold to consumers, or should medicine have to prove they work first? Arguing for, Julius Ritter is the founder of the California Peptide Club & CEO of Transcendence, a longevity company working with peptide, exosome, & regenerative therapies. He's part of a growing movement that thinks patients & physicians should have much more freedom to experiment at the frontier of medicine. Arguing against, Dr. Tiana Woolridge is a primary sports medicine physician at Hospital for Special Surgery, double board certified in pediatrics & sports medicine. She's trained in regenerative treatments like PRP herself, which is exactly why she thinks there's a difference between promising medicine & selling something before the evidence is there. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

This day celebrates our campus of makers & offers artists, designers, entrepreneurs, & neighbors alike the chance to connect with peers, explore our campus & the businesses who thrive here, & experience the innovation at the Yard up close. This year, we've created two unqiue tracks to guide you through our campus: Creative Currents- Creativity flows through the Brooklyn Navy Yard; home to hundreds of artists, ranging from painters to photographers to jewelers. They'll be opening their studios to the public, inviting audiences in for a rare opportunity to view their work, learn about their processes, inspirations, & their journeys here at the Yard. BNY Past, Present, & Future - From our start in 1801 as a premiere ship building facility, we've always been on the cutting edge of manufacturing & technology, right here in New York City. On our campus, rich history meets an innovative future, as we look ahead towards what's next in the fields of space tech, green energy, robotics, & more. Come tour our waterfront campus & take in centuries of legacy, while gaining access to the labs & studios where the tech of the future is being made.   Also Featuring... Arnsenal's Tequila & Whisky Tasting Food Trucks Live Art Demos   BNYDC RULES, PROTOCOLS & ACKNOWLEDGEMENT  Check-In Procedure All visitors must check-in at Building 77. Visitors arriving through other entry points will be redirected to enter through official entry locations.All visitors must register for the event. No one will be admitted without an official RSVP. It is highly recommended that you RSVP in advance although day of registration is permitted.A valid photo ID is required for entry. Visitors under 18 must be accompanied by an adult & do not need a photo ID.Visitors who fail to register or do not present a valid photo ID will be denied entry.Expect an estimated 5-minute check-in & security screening process.Security Protocols All bags will be checked at the entrance for prohibited items.Prohibited items include but are not limited to alcohol; weapons, noise-making devices; laser pointers; fireworks; professional camera equipment; large political signs, banners, or flags; & other materials that may cause harm, damage, or disruption.Bags must not exceed the size of a standard school backpack (Approximately 18 x 14 x 6)Large bags, including roller bags, will not be permitted. Campus Rules for Event All visitors must stay in approved areas. Visitors should not enter closed or restricted spaces during the event. This includes active construction areas.If buildings & businesses are open, please be respectful while in their spaces & remain mindful that these are working studios & manufacturing centers.Participating businesses may choose to close their spaces at their discretion, including if they determine that visitors are being disruptive.The Brooklyn Navy Yard is an active manufacturing & industrial campus. Visitors are expected to walk on sidewalks where possible & to be mindful of road traffic.To ensure proper pedestrian movement, do not congregate in ways that block entrances, exits, roadways, or parking lots during your visit.Visitors are prohibited from causing damage to Brooklyn Navy Yard property or causing disruptions to other visitors, business owners or workers, & volunteers & staff working at the event. Photo Acknowledgement & Permissions By registering for the event, you understand that photography and/or video may be taken at the event for marketing or promotional purposes & you consent to being filmed or photographed for such use. Furthermore, you release the Brooklyn Navy Yard Development Corporation, its officers, employees, & agents, from any liability in connection with such photography or videography & the use thereof, & waive any claims you may have for payment in connection with such materials & the use thereof.  Newsletter Acknowledgement & Permission By signing up for this event, you are agreeing to be added to the free Brooklyn Navy Yard public newsletter list. Newsletters are sent 1 - 2 times each month & list public programs, events, & exhibitions at the Yard. You may unsubscribe at any time.

events.description: The Shortlist NYC - October Founder Showcase (#10)The Shortlist is back for our monthly Founder Showcase & the room keeps getting better. This is a monthly curated, application-only evening connecting early-stage founders with exceptional operators across New York. No panels. No pitches to VCs. Just six founders building breakout companies, a room full of people who've built things themselves, & the kind of candid conversation you don't get at most events. Each founder will share what they're building, why it matters, & the specific roles they're actively hiring for right now - followed by a mixer. What to expect: Founders presenting at the seed through Series B stage. Operators, builders, & executives who've seen what good looks like. An intentionally small room designed for real connection. Who this is for: Exceptional operators - whether you're actively exploring your next role, casually curious, or simply want to stay close to what's being built in NYC right now. Founders will be announced in the days leading up to the event.  Attendance is intentionally limited. Apply to be considered. More information on The Shortlist can be found here. Founded by Andrew Yeung & Ivor Straford.

events.name: Speaking For The Invisible City
events.description: Welcome Kevin Slavin to the Civic Hall stage to present Speaking for the Invisible City! Kevin Slavin makes invisible systems playable, legible, & lately, accountable. This is a thin but discernible through-line in a career across art, design, science, game development, & biotech. Trained in sculpture at Cooper Union under Hans Haacke, Kevin co-founded Area/Code Entertainment, whose pioneering work in location-based games led to acquisition by Zynga. He was recruited to the MIT Media Lab as faculty, where his work on urban metagenomics was exhibited in the context of the Venice Architecture Biennale & at the Storefront for Art & Architecture. His 2011 TED talk on how algorithms shape the world became a frequent reference in understanding the ways that systems change our world, & our experience of the world. Kevin was the founding Chief Science & Technology Officer of The Shed at Hudson Yards, & a co-founding editor of the MIT Press Journal of Design & Science. He spent years in biosecurity between commercial real estate, public health & the intelligence community, & is now co-founder of Fairfield Bio, building a global marketplace for non-human genomic data. He served eight years on the board of Cooper Union, including four years as Vice-Chair. Kevin lives in the Bronx with his wife, daughter, & 14 trees.

This is a thin but discernible through-line in a career across art, design, science, game development, & biotech. Trained in sculpture at Cooper Union under Hans Haacke, Kevin co-founded Area/Code Entertainment, whose pioneering work in location-based games led to acquisition by Zynga. He was recruited to the MIT Media Lab as faculty, where his work on urban metagenomics was exhibited in the context of the Venice Architecture Biennale & at the Storefront for Art & Architecture. His 2011 TED talk on how algorithms shape the world became a frequent reference in understanding the ways that systems change our world, & our experience of the world. Kevin was the founding Chief Science & Technology Officer of The Shed at Hudson Yards, & a co-founding editor of the MIT Press Journal of Design & Science. He spent years in biosecurity between commercial real estate, public health & the intelligence community, & is now co-founder of Fairfield Bio, building a global marketplace for non-human genomic data. He served eight years on the board of Cooper Union, including four years as Vice-Chair. Kevin lives in the Bronx with his wife, daughter, & 14 trees.

events.name: AI for operators
events.description: AI for Forward-thinking OperatorsA 2-hour hands-on workshop for execs, VPs, operators, fractional leaders, and founders.You're further along in your career than you are in AI - and you're tired of nodding along while colleagues and vendors pitch magic and your team runs experiments you can't evaluate.This isn't a talk. It's a working session. Bring your laptop. In two hours you'll set up Claude Code, Muse, or Hark - connect them to the tools and services you actually live in, and produce something real. Something that'll solve an actual problem you tackle, or something that'll help your work.Past execs have left with having created things like:dynamic competitive research and action toolsomething that runs analysis on their products and sales and automatically finds room for offloading inventory, dynamic promos, and actionable customer segmentshelps them hold their vendors and teams accountable automatically using briefs, followups, real-time measurementcloses their monthly books accuratelyautomates sales research and outreach relevant to them, not boilerplateautomates HR paperwork relevant to them, not boilerplateSmall by design: 3-5 seats, hands-on help throughout. We build alongside you and troubleshoot in real time, so you walk out ready to run this inside your company, immediately.About the host: Deepak DevjaniSomewhere along the way I started training my own team on AI, just so we could ship faster. And the coaching thing kind of fell in my lap. Turns out I love it.Then execs started coming to me. They wanted the same thing for themselves. Then other founders. For the last couple years I've been training execs and their C-suite teams, and honestly the change is night and day. They have more time. They get way more done.One thing I learned fast: for this to actually work, it has to be as close to personal and private as possible  essentially 1:1. That's the whole reason this class is small. You can literally know nothing walking in and you'll be OK; that's by design. And what you leave with isn't just a tool you built  it's the confidence to walk into work and actually use this.So that's what Reliable Bits is now. We still go into companies and implement AI for real. But a big part of what we do is coach the people doing the actual work. Operators, execs, VPs.

events.description: Tech Empowerment Days (TEDs) are free, one-day events hosted by The Knowledge House that aim to empower young professionals & career changers interested in exploring technology careers.This fall, TKH is bringing a Newark Tech Empowerment Day back to the community, & would be grateful for the opportunity to have the event included as part of Newark Tech Week.In workshops throughout the day, participants will learn about tech career pathways, develop critical digital literacy & AI skills for the workplace, get a hands-on intro to coding & emerging technologies like GenAI, & network with community members & tech industry professionals.Attendees will also have the opportunity to attend an overview & Q&A session for the 2027 Innovation Fellowship, a free job training program that prepares participants for tech-enabled roles across sectors, & will be invited to apply.The mission of the Knowledge House (TKH) is to empower & sustain a talent pipeline of technologists & digital leaders who will uplift their communities. events.name: Urban Future Summit - 10 Years Of Impact
events.description: The 2026 Urban Future Summit is supported by New York Community Trust, New York State Energy Research & Development Authority, MUFG Bank, & NYU Tandon School of Engineering - this year is extra special as we're celebrating 10 years of supporting climate innovation & the entrepreneurs who have shaped it. 2 PRIZE TRACKS. 8 FINALISTS. HEAR THEM PITCH ON 10/22.Read the full press release  Climate Adaptation Prize: focused on solutions that help communities & ecosystems adapt to & build resilience against the impacts of climate change. Airbuild: Autonomous biological nutrient recovery systems that convert wastewater nutrients into carbon-sequestering biochar fertilizer, helping municipalities meet EPA compliance & cut costs while creating new revenue for farmers. Class 3 Technologies: Engineering-grade, building-level climate risk assessments powered by Iris, a proprietary simulation engine, helping large property owners quantify physical vulnerability & evaluate resilience strategies across their portfolios, while extending that same risk intelligence to underserved communities. Rarefied: A sunlight-driven propulsion mechanism enabling persistent flight in near-space, building a new atmospheric data layer to improve weather forecasting, disaster resilience, & climate risk modeling - data especially valuable in equatorial & developing regions, where sparse observations weaken storm & drought forecasts. Supercool Earth: An end-to-end precipitation enhancement platform that uses biology to increase rain & snowfall on demand for ski resorts, water utilities, hydropower operators, & agriculture, giving water-scarce communities a tool to stabilize supply before rationing or crop failure set in. Climate Mitigation Prize: focused on solutions that reduce greenhouse gas emissions & mitigate the impacts of climate change. Arcticar: An intelligent, clean energy platform for the cold chain, replacing diesel-powered trailer refrigeration with lower-cost electric units & integrated battery storage, eliminating the emissions & noise pollution reefers create. Emulate Cities: AI infrastructure that helps local governments automate permit review, cutting permitting timelines from weeks to minutes to accelerate deployment of housing, clean energy, & climate-resilient infrastructure. Every Electric: Operator of New York City's largest plug-in powerbank network, giving households access to affordable backup power while strengthening grid reliability for all New Yorkers. Ultropia: An ultrasonic mechanical water extraction platform that removes moisture from materials, targeting the energy-intensive gas dryers used across the industrial laundry industry. For more than a decade, the Urban Future Prize Competition has identified & accelerated the founders building the technologies, infrastructure, & systems that cities need to thrive in a changing world. What begins as an early-stage idea has repeatedly become a market-shaping company: 23 startups supported, more than $1 million awarded in non-dilutive funding, & over $515 million in follow-on capital raised - a remarkable 515x return on prize dollars deployed. At this year's Urban Future Summit, attendees will actively participate in the next chapter of that story. The Summit will culminate with presentations from the 2026 Urban Future Prize Competition finalists - founders tackling some of the most urgent challenges we're facing today, from climate resilience & emissions reduction to mobility, energy, & the circular economy. These entrepreneurs are not only competing for funding; they are competing for the opportunity to join ACRE, New York's longest-running climatetech incubator, where breakthrough ideas are transformed into scalable businesses. This year marks an important milestone for the Urban Future Prize Competition. For the first time, four awardees will be selected across the Climate Adaptation & Climate Mitigation prize tracks. Two winners get access to $50k & two runner-up teams in each track will also receive $10k in non-dilutive funding & admission into the ACRE Incubator. By expanding support to a broader cohort of entrepreneurs, we're investing in a larger pipeline of innovators at a moment when climate resilience & decarbonization must advance together.

events.name: Legal Engineers NYC: What Do Clients Want? Law Firm AI Governance
events.description: What Do Clients Want? Law Firm AI Governance Clients are writing AI rules for their law firms: outside counsel guidelines that ban public AI tools, insurance carriers that require approval for each AI use or reserve the right to audit it, procurement questionnaires that ask how AI use is controlled. What does it take to meet those rules, & to prove you did? We will bring real, published client AI requirements. Pick one & build an approach to it: the policy, tools, workflow or checks a firm would need, & how it would show the client it complied. Or show a governance tool you use or have tried, from approved-tool lists & logging to governance platforms & things you built. Laptops open; no coding required; demos encouraged. ICME Labs will show how PreFlight lets firms prove to clients that their AI followed the rules, without disclosing client data. We finish with the group's map of what clients are asking for, the approaches that work, & the gaps nobody has solved yet. Our first session brought 47 legal engineers to Falcon Rappaport & Berkman to test which AI tools invent case law. This one turns to the rules clients are writing for the firms that use AI. Date: Wednesday, October 14, 4:00pm - 5:30pm Location: Meeting Room A, 40 Wall St, 28th Floor, New York. Legal Engineers NYC is a hands-on group for people who turn law, policy, & practice into the workflows, agents, evals, & controls that run legal work. We meet weekly on Thursdays in Manhattan, laptops open, & build something each time. Any platform counts, & no coding required. Legal Engineers NYC is organized by ICME Labs & led by cofounder Houman Shadab. Contact houman@icme.io to host or sponsor a session.
