events.name: SOSV Deep Tech Summit
events.description: Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. The producers of the Summit are SOSV's Ned Desmond, Ben Joffe, & Norm Amandi. SOSV's mission is to invest in deep tech companies that advance human & planetary health, & embedded in building an 800+ company portfolio with a remarkable array of companies applying AI in the physical world. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Reality Of Data Centers In Space
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a small, curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for.Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data. No talking, just thinking. 45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: The Reality of Data Centers in SpaceStarcloud just raised $250M to build satellites that run AI workloads in orbit, joining Google's "Project Suncatcher" & a SpaceX effort in a race to solve AI's power problem by moving compute off the planet entirely. The pitch is compelling - unlimited solar power, no water usage - but basic questions about heat dissipation, launch costs, & maintenance remain mostly unanswered. We're decoding: Is space-based computing a real solution to AI's real estate & energy issues? Supporting questions: What would actually have to be true for orbital data centers to beat a terrestrial one on cost? Who's positioned to win this race - the well-funded startups (Starcloud), or the hyperscalers who already have the capital & infrastructure (Google, SpaceX)? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like.

events.name: Real-Time Video Agents Hack
events.description: The VAST Builders Challenge is a three-city technical event series bringing together founders & engineers across New York, London, & San Francisco to build production-ready AI systems. Spend the day building agents to unlock the value of video. Because video is hard to search & analyze,  most of it stays in storage, unwatched & underused. Experiment with the latest AI infrastructure, collaborate with other ambitious builders, & turn your ideas into shippable prototypes - with access to expert guidance, compute, & the tools you need to ship. Hosted with VAST Data in collaboration with NVIDIA, SpaceXAI, CoreWeave & Weights & Biases. Note: Registration closes on Oct 6th. Prizes1st place: NVIDIA DGX Spark HuggingFace Microduck Cursor Credits Cash Gift Cards The Builders StackYou don't have to worry about starting from scratch, we've set it up for you: Video understanding: reason over a video clip with NVIDIA Cosmos. Semantic search: find moments across hours of footage using natural language. Object detection: real-time detection & tracking across frames with YOLO. General-purpose LLMs: models from Weights & Biases to power your application logic (e.g. video agents). The VAST AI OS orchestrates the video ingestion & data layer, models are served on CoreWeave GPUs, & builders ship with Cursor. Build your own video agent or something no one's thought of. We'll share the videos to get you started on building video agents. JudgesDiego Garzon - Senior Solution Architect for AI/AV Simulation @ Nvidia Ravi Garg - Solutions Architect @ Nvidia Ram B. - Sr. Developer Advocate @ VAST Data Brian Verkley - Director, AI Data Platform @ VAST Data Prashanth Nalubandhu - Staff AI Solutions Architect @ CoreWeave Brandon Kates - Founding FDE @ CoreWeave Vera A - Senior Solutions Architect @ Weights & Biases Who should attendDevelopers, ML/AI engineers, agent builders, & data engineers, from startups to enterprise teams working with video or multimodal AI. While individuals are welcome, we encourage teams of up to four members & will prioritize team applications. You can form a team on the day of the event or arrive with one already assembled. Applications are required. Space is limited. Registration closes one week prior to the event. *Register with Personal Email*We'll use this for event comms & to credit your Cursor account. Sign up for Cursor with this same personal email if you don't have an account. Agenda8:30am Doors Open + Breakfast9:00am Opening Keynotes9:30am Build Begins12:30pm Lunch4:30pm Demos6:30pm Closing & Awards Note: This event will be photographed & filmed. By attending, you consent to appearing in photos & videos that may be used for social media & promotional materials. SponsorsVAST Data: A unified AI data platform that provides the foundation for managing, processing, & activating data for AI workloads CoreWeave: AI cloud infrastructure that delivers high-performance GPU compute for training, fine-tuning, & inference workloads. SpaceXAI: AI-assisted software development tools that help developers move from idea to implementation faster NVIDIA: Accelerated computing & AI software that enables developers to build & deploy advanced AI applications Weights & Biases (A CoreWeave company): AI developer tools for experiment tracking, model evaluation, & collaborative ML development

events.name: 90/30 NYC: Machine Super Intelligence
events.description: What does it mean for a machine to be intelligent, & can we define it mathematically? Join 90/30 for a reading group on Shane Legg's Machine Super Intelligence. This 2008 PhD thesis explores universal artificial intelligence, the theoretical agent AIXI, & the limits of building machines that learn & act across unfamiliar environments. We'll discuss: How can we measure intelligence beyond performance on a single task? What does AIXI tell us about an ideal intelligent agent? What changes when we move from theoretical intelligence to systems with limited compute? How useful are these ideas for understanding today's AI? This is a long read, so come with a section, question, or argument you want to unpack. You don't need to understand every proof to join the conversation. We are only mandating chapter 1 & 4 while 2 is suggested.

events.name: Agentic AI In The Wild: Open Source Agents In Production
events.description: AI & Open Source Builders Meetup, New York City AI agents are moving into production, & more & more of them are built on open source. The question is no longer whether to use them, but what it takes to make them reliable once the demo is over. This meetup brings together builders, maintainers, & practitioners integrating AI agents into real codebases, CI/CD pipelines, internal developer platforms, cloud native infrastructure, & observability stacks. The evening focuses on the conversations that rarely fit into conference talks: what breaks at scale, how open source tools & standards shape agentic systems, where failure modes hide, & how teams build systems they can trust. Under the theme Open Source in Production, we will explore agentic code review, agent loops in CI/CD, developer platforms, eBPF-powered observability & security, & the role open source communities play in how production AI gets built. No vendor pitches. Just practical lessons from systems running in production. Agenda 5:00 PM Doors Open, Drinks & Networking5:30 PM Welcome & Opening Remarks5:40 PM [Speaker TBD], Qodo Dev Community6:05 PM Break, Food & Networking6:25 PM Panel: Agentic AI in the Wild7:15 PM Ryan Hamilton, Senior Developer & Community Lead, CircleCI AI Lab7:40 PM Closing Remarks7:45 PM Networking until 8:00 PM Speakers & Sessions [Speaker TBD], Qodo[Talk title TBD][Talk abstract TBD] Ryan Hamilton, Senior Developer & Community Lead, CircleCI AI LabOne Take: Engineering Agent Loops That Ship 100% Green PRs on the First PushMost teams optimizing AI-assisted development are focused on the wrong variable: prompting harder, adding rework, dumping larger failure logs into context. The real question isn't how to fix red PRs faster. It's how to stop producing them.Ryan shares findings from three connected Loop Lab experiments, each using the same controlled Snake game benchmark to isolate one variable at a time. Each one reveals something unexpected about where the real leverage lives in an agent loop, & what it means for cutting the cost of agentic development.Together, these experiments map a clear path from "rework is inevitable" to "rework is reserved for the unknowable." The result is a practical harness design that bakes a low Merge Efficiency Ratio (MER, the number of validation cycles it takes to get a change onto main) in from the start, & a new way to think about where validation belongs in the agent loop. Panel: Agentic AI in the WildWhat does it take to move AI agents from proof of concept into systems that operate reliably, & what role does open source play?Practitioners from across the stack will discuss context management, governance, open standards, observability, security, & what changes when agentic systems scale.Expect concrete lessons, not talking points. ModeratorDana Fine, Open Source & Developer Relations Manager, QodoDana leads open source programs & community initiatives at Qodo. She runs the GitHub User Group, CNCF local & GenAI communities, & the Bond AI meetup series. PanelistsBaruch Sadogursky, PortBaruch is a longtime developer advocate & a well-known speaker at developer conferences around the world. He co-authored Liquid Software & DevOps Tools for Java Developers, & focuses on developer productivity, DevOps, & how AI is changing the way software gets built & shipped. [Speaker TBD], Claude Community[Bio TBD] [Speaker TBD], NVIDIA[Bio TBD] Community PartnersAWS User Group NYC, CNCF NYC, Frontend NYC, WeMakeDevs, Bond AI, Qodo Dev Community Join the CommunityQodo Dev Community on Discord: [Discord invite link]Follow us on Meetup: [Meetup group link]

events.name: Faith At Work - Christians Working In Big Tech
events.description: Our daily work can be a calling only if it is re-conceived as God's assignment to serve others.  Tim Keller, Every Good Endeavor: Connecting Your Work to God's Work So many of us fool ourselves, believing our work is all about us: What can I accomplish? What do I get from it? Will it give me the money & life that I crave? We're convinced there's a better, different path Christians are meant to consider in how you can show up at work with a sacrificial posture in the tech space. On October 12th, FaithTech NYC is putting a panel together of Christians working in Big Tech companies who've had to work it out on the job, under deadline, with serious consequences. During out time together, we'll unpack: How they make tough decisions based on what the gospel compels us to consider. How they lead & navigate layoffs when they're the one delivering the news. How they talk about Jesus with their co-workers & how you can too. How they think about serving their team in the midst of a work culture obsessed with performance & output. Why their faith has made them better at their job. We'll make some room for your questions at the end. Our hope is that you come away encouraged & inspired to show up different at work the next day. Light food will be provided (donations are appreciated). See you there!

events.name: Founder Pitch Clinic
events.description: Join us in NYC for an in-person, hands-on pitch clinic designed to help founders become more confident on stage & sharpen the way they pitch to investors. Whether you're preparing for a fundraising round, an investor meeting, or your next demo day, this session will give you practical tools to communicate your story with greater confidence, clarity, & impact. The clinic features two focused, 30-minute workshops covering both sides of a great pitch: how you show up & what you say. Don't Calm Down30-minute interactive workshop with Dave Wolovsky (Coach & StartX mentor) Building a company, raising capital, & leading at a high level all require founders to manage stress under pressure. But performing at your best doesn't necessarily mean trying to calm yourself down. In this interactive session, Cognitive Performance Coach Dave Wolovsky will show you how to compose yourself when pitching & presenting. Through practical exercises, you'll learn techniques to pitch with greater presence, work with pressure rather than against it, & operate more effectively in high-stakes moments. About Dave WolovskyDave is a Cognitive Performance Coach with an MS in Neuroscience & Education from Columbia University. He coaches founders to maintain focus in high-pressure moments & establish better habits for managing their daily energy. Learn more at effortwise.com/founders. He also serves as a mentor in the StartX accelerator program. The Art of Pitching to Attract Investors30-minute workshop with Anthony Rose What makes investors lean in? Anthony will break down the art of delivering a compelling founder pitch-from communicating your vision & opportunity to presenting your business in a way that resonates with potential investors. Expect practical insights from someone who has worked with thousands of startups navigating fundraising & investment. About Anthony RoseAnthony is the founder & CEO of SeedLegals, the legaltech platform that helps startups get investment-ready, run funding rounds, & handle their legal needs, used by more than 50,000 startups. Before SeedLegals, Anthony's career spanned 3D graphics, P2P music, internet video, & social TV, including leading BBC iPlayer. Wired Magazine's 2009 cover story called him The Man Who Saved the BBC. Come ready to learn, practice, & leave with techniques you can put to work in your very next pitch.

events.name: Red Carpet Room Launch Party
events.description: If you show up with a backpack or your laptop you will be banned from the event. Please leave backpacks at home. RED CARPET ROOM Formerly Fun HouseHosted by Anwar EnterprisesSaturday, October 31, 2026 Exact address released to confirmed guests 24 hours before doors. About the Event Red Carpet Room is the next chapter of Fun House, rebuilt around a single idea: the people building brands should be building them together. This is a mixer for founders, creators, & investors from the Anwar Events community, gathered in one room with a shared reason to be there. Everyone in attendance is constructing something with their name attached to it. The night is designed so the person who can unblock you is standing a few feet away. We are doing it on Halloween on purpose. The city will be full of parties where nothing happens beyond the party itself. This one gives you a panel worth sitting through, a room worth working, & footage of yourself that you will actually use. Run of Show [7pm] - Doors, check-in, & open networking to start the night[8pm] - Panel: operators who built audiences, companies, & reputations from nothing   SPECIAL GUESTS BEING REVEALED NEXT WEEK [9pm] - Open mixer, with Red Carpet Show interviews running in the back room Who's Coming The typical guest is a founder raising or building, a creator monetizing an audience, or an investor looking for both. Expect crossover from fashion, music, media, tech, art & consumer brands, since that is who the Anwar Events community actually contains. Whether you are hiring, raising, pitching a collaboration, or looking for people who take their work as seriously as you do, you will be in the right room. The Red Carpet Show Throughout the night, Ilias will pull guests aside for on-camera interviews for The Red Carpet Show. There is one question at the center of every interview: how can he help you. Those conversations get cut into content that reaches an audience of 70,000 plus founders, investors, & creators. Sitting down costs you four minutes & can put your company in front of people you would never cold email. Dress Code Halloween night calls for more than a costume assembled at the last minute. Come dressed as the version of yourself the press would photograph, whether that means black tie, full character, or your own blend of both. Cameras run from the door onward, so arrive accordingly. Capacity & Entry Space is limited & the guest list is curated. A confirmed RSVP secures your place only until capacity fills, so arriving early is strongly recommended. events.name: Dating The Dead - What Makes A Connection Real?
events.description: Dating Lab NYC presents:Dating the Dead: What Makes a Connection Real?Dating Lab NYC is a monthly interactive discussion series exploring the psychology, culture, & technology shaping modern connection. Each gathering combines a research-informed presentation, open conversation, an anonymous audience survey, & time to connect with other curious New Yorkers. This month, we'll explore connection on & off the dating apps: what makes it feel real, & how technology shapes what we seek from one another. The conversation is inspired by For Human Use, a novel by Sarah G. Pierce, who will join us as a special guest speaker. Sarah will share the inspiration behind her book & how she explored questions of dating & connection through her story, bringing her perspective into our discussion. We'll wrap up with a book giveaway & author signing, alongside time to meet & connect with fellow attendees. No need to read the book in advance. Come curious. Presented & facilitated by Becky BergBecky is a behavioral researcher with a master's degree in clinical psychology from Columbia University. She has studied romantic relationships at Columbia's Couples Lab & NYU's Love Smarter Lab & now conducts independent research on dating-app users & how technology facilitates modern connection. Schedule6:30 PM - Drinks, food, introductions, & anonymous audience survey7:00 PM - Presentation & interactive discussion with special guest Sarah G. Pierce8:00 PM - The Room Report, book giveaway, author signing, & networking until 8:30 PM In partnership with CohortCohort is a community of builders, creatives, & founders who show up for one another through genuine accountability, meaningful support, & honest feedback. Its goal is to foster a culture of building & developing ideas in New York City.  Photography NoticePhotos & videos may be taken during the event & shared on social media or our websites. If you prefer not to be photographed, please let us know when you arrive, & we'll keep you out of frame.

events.name: AI & Future Of Education
events.description: AI & the Future of Education Artificial intelligence has caused seismic disruption in the field of education in just a few years. Students, educators, & parents are confused about how to navigate this game-changing technology. How should schools from K-12 to colleges & universities approach learning in this new era, & how can they prepare students for success in a transformed workplace? A panel of experts weighs in on the salient issues, the points of tension, & possible paths forward.   Featuring Steven Jackson, professor of information science & science & technology studies & vice provost for academic innovation at Cornell University; Aankit Patel, university dean for technology & computer & information sciences, The City University of New York; & Natasha Singer, a technology reporter for the business section of The New York Times, whose new book is Coding Kids: Big Tech's Battle to Remake Public Schools. Luke Waltzer, director of the Teaching & Learning Center at the CUNY Graduate Center, moderates.   Presented with the Teaching & Learning Center, CUNY AI Lab, GC Digital Initiatives, the American Social History Project/Center for Media & Learning, & the Mina Rees Library.

events.name: Ugly Talks: Failure Is Key To Success
events.description: Failure gets talked about like it is part of the journey. That is the lie. The real thing is messier. Missed bets. Wrong hires. Near-breakdowns. The week you stop sleeping & start doing math at 3:00 AM. Founders are expected to eat it quietly & keep moving. No language for what happened. No playbook for what to do next. Ugly Talk is a founder room for the part nobody posts. No fluff. No consultants. Just builders with scars, talking about the call that cost them.  Why you should be in this room.Hear what failure cost them. Then hear what they did next. Learn how experienced founders separate self-worth from outcomes when things go sideways. Spot the patterns behind repeat mistakes. And the early signals you should not ignore. Leave with a few concrete moves for the next hard week. Not inspiration. Meet other founders in the thick of it. The ones who are still building.  What's on the table.Dare to suck: how permission to fail unlocks real progress The moment things broke: missed opportunities, wrong turns, near-breakdowns, & what changed afterward Failure vs identity: separating self-worth from outcomes Treating setbacks as data: what to measure, what to ignore, & how to decide fast Rejection as redirection: how founders find the signal in the no Habits for staying focused & resilient when everything feels uncertain  Run of show6:00 - 6:30 PM: Reception (check-in & light drinks) 6:30 - 6:40 PM: Welcome remarks 6:40 - 6:50 PM: Keynote Speech by Ben McKean 6:50 - 7:30 PM: Panel Discussion 7:30 - 7:45 PM: Audience Q&A 7:45 - 8:00 PM: Mixer + snacks & drinks  Featured speakers.Ben McKean - Founder & Chief Executive Officer, Hungryroot Ben McKean is the Founder & CEO of Hungryroot, a personalized healthy eating assistant that uses AI to make meal planning, food shopping, & nutrition effortless & enjoyable. Prior to Hungryroot, Ben was a Vice President & General Manager at Groupon, overseeing their food & beverage business. Ben came to Groupon through the acquisition of Savored, which he founded in 2009. Savored was the nation's leading provider of yield management technology to the restaurant industry, used by over two thousand restaurants nationwide & nearly one million diners. Prior to Savored, Ben worked in Merrill Lynch's technology investment banking group. Ben is a graduate of Georgetown University & currently lives in North Carolina with his wife & kids. Stephen McKinney - Founder & CEO, Bizbe Stephen McKinney is a serial entrepreneur with over a decade of experience across tech, marketing, & logistics. He's the founder & CEO of Bizbe.com, an AI-native business brokerage & lower middle market M&A firm based in New York & Miami. A former contestant on ABC's Shark Tank, Steve previously founded & led Retty Logistics, a seven-figure last-mile delivery company acquired by DXP Logistics & Webster Logistics. Dmitry Koltunov - Founder & CEO, Arbor Dmitry Koltunov is a serial entrepreneur, technologist, educator, & storyteller. He is the founder & CEO of Arbor, an AI-powered content engine that helps enterprises scale their communications with video & beyond. Previously, he co-founded & served as CTO of ALICE, a hospitality technology company that grew into a global industry leader before being acquired by Expedia Group. Dmitry also leads the New York City chapter of the Startup Leadership Program, New York's oldest startup fellowship, whose 500+ alumni have collectively raised more than $1 billion in funding across every industry imaginable. He is passionate about helping founders navigate the challenges of building & scaling companies. Outside of technology, Dmitry is an award-winning songwriter & theater producer currently developing a new musical for Broadway. He holds degrees in Computer Science & Economics from the University of Pennsylvania & is a CFA charterholder. Gwendolyn von Rahn - Co-Founder & CEO, Sweetling Health Gwendolyn von Rahn is the Co-Founder & CEO of Sweetling Health, an postpartum intelligence platform built for at-risk & hard-to-reach populations. She's a second-time exited founder, an award-winning marketer with over a decade of experience building consumer brands for women, Gwen led creative & brand teams at Vogue, InStyle, & POPSUGAR before founding & scaling a mission-driven consumer brand into Nordstrom distribution that raised over $1M for melanoma research through the Melanoma Research Foundation. She holds a Cornell Johnson MBA & founded Sweetling from her own lived experience with the postpartum care gap.  Who's hosting it.Victoria Yampolsky - President, The Startup Station Victoria Yampolsky is the Founder & President of The Startup Station, a strategic CFO advisory firm & financial education platform for startups. She partners with founders on financial strategy, modeling, & fundraising, having supported over 150 companies across 15 industries in raising more than $50M in venture capital. Victoria is also an advocate for female founders & access to capital, & has taught finance to more than 20,000 entrepreneurs through programs including the Bank of America Institute for Women's Entrepreneurship at Cornell. She began her career at Deutsche Bank & Capgemini, & holds a BS in Computer Science from Cornell University & an MBA from Columbia Business School.  Who's getting in.Early-stage tech founders & operators navigating uncertainty, setbacks, or the emotional weight of building a company. Expected roles may include: Founders & co-founders (pre-seed to Series A) Operators (COO, Head of Ops, Chief of Staff) Product & Engineering leads building through ambiguity Growth & GTM leads working through missed targets & pivots Finance & strategy leaders supporting founder decision-making  Who's backing this.The Startup Station The Startup Station - is a CFO advisory & financial education platform for early-stage startups. We help early-stage founders build investor-ready financials & tell their funding story with confidence. In the past decade, we've helped 150+ founders raise over $50M & educated 20,000+ entrepreneurs worldwide. The Startup Station also runs Speed Pitch, an exclusive investor-founder matchmaking event series for early-stage startups where founders are matched with 3 investors by sector, stage, & check size. Mind Your Business Every attendee will receive a free copy of keynote speaker Ben McKean's Mind Your Business. Mind Your Business is a practical parable for people rethinking work as AI advances. Set over a four-day retreat, it follows six participants competing for funding to bring one vision to life. As they evaluate six competing proposals, they begin to confront deeper questions about what gives them energy, who they serve, & what they uniquely contribute. Those patterns form what the book calls their Soulcode-the way purpose, belonging, imagination, & courage shape how they work. Told with humor & warmth, the story turns familiar workplace tensions into practical lessons for contributing more deeply, seeing new possibilities, & acting with greater conviction. At its core, the book argues that the opportunity of the AI era isn't doing more work-it's knowing what work is worth doing. GREY Journal GREY Journal - Media partner spotlighting modern entrepreneurs (featured on Apple News + Google News).  About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough "aha!" moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons & insights. With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami, we've built a vibrant community of thousands of founders & industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape. Official Website: UglyTalk.com Important Notice for Ugly Talk AttendeesAdmission & Confirmation Attendance is by approval only. Approved guests will receive a confirmation email along with a calendar invite. Invitations are non-transferable. Additional event details will be shared as the event approaches. Code of Conduct By attending, you agree to: Maintain respect & professionalism, adhering to all venue rules, policies, & applicable laws. Refrain from harassment, discrimination, unwelcome sexual advances (verbal or physical), intimidation, or inappropriate photography/recording. Report any violations to the event hosts immediately. Violations may result in immediate removal from the event & exclusion from future invitations. Liability & Risk Participation is voluntary & at your own risk. The event organizers, hosts, sponsors, & venue are not liable for personal injury, lost or stolen belongings, or any other damages incurred during the event. Media Consent By attending, you grant the event organizers & affiliated entities the right to capture, use, & distribute photos, videos, & audio recordings of you for promotional, marketing, & other lawful purposes, including digital & print media, advertising, & social media. You waive any right to inspect or approve the final materials & release all claims related to their use. Communications By registering, you agree to receive marketing & promotional communications from Ugly Talk & its co-hosts, partners, & sponsors. You may unsubscribe at any time. Agreement If you do not agree to this Code of Conduct, please refrain from attending the event.  Join us to stay updated on upcoming Ugly Talk events! Join the newsletter  Follow us on IG  Official website

events.name: An Unmuted Debate - Peptides vs The People
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In partnership with Pepper NYC & the Peptide Club of NYC A peptide to heal your tendon. An injection to rebuild your knee. Exosomes to make your body younger. Regenerative medicine is moving fast, & consumers increasingly don't want to wait ten years for the clinical trials to catch up (the AIDS crisis..). Some of these treatments have real science behind them. Others have promising early evidence. And some are being sold for thousands of dollars long before anyone can say with confidence that they actually work. But maybe that's the point. We let adults make risky decisions everywhere else. If a patient understands the evidence is uncertain, why shouldn't they be allowed to spend their own money trying something experimental? The alternative is the basic bargain medicine has relied on for decades: prove it works before you sell it. Because when the person explaining the risks is also making money from the treatment, "informed consent" can start looking a lot like a sales pitch. So: should experimental regenerative therapies be sold to consumers, or should medicine have to prove they work first? Arguing for, Julius Ritter is the founder of the California Peptide Club & CEO of Transcendence, a longevity company working with peptide, exosome, & regenerative therapies. He's part of a growing movement that thinks patients & physicians should have much more freedom to experiment at the frontier of medicine. Arguing against, Dr. Tiana Woolridge is a primary sports medicine physician at Hospital for Special Surgery, double board certified in pediatrics & sports medicine. She's trained in regenerative treatments like PRP herself, which is exactly why she thinks there's a difference between promising medicine & selling something before the evidence is there. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In partnership with Pepper NYC & the Peptide Club of NYC A peptide to heal your tendon. An injection to rebuild your knee. Exosomes to make your body younger. Regenerative medicine is moving fast, & consumers increasingly don't want to wait ten years for the clinical trials to catch up (the AIDS crisis..). Some of these treatments have real science behind them. Others have promising early evidence. And some are being sold for thousands of dollars long before anyone can say with confidence that they actually work. But maybe that's the point. We let adults make risky decisions everywhere else. If a patient understands the evidence is uncertain, why shouldn't they be allowed to spend their own money trying something experimental? The alternative is the basic bargain medicine has relied on for decades: prove it works before you sell it. Because when the person explaining the risks is also making money from the treatment, "informed consent" can start looking a lot like a sales pitch. So: should experimental regenerative therapies be sold to consumers, or should medicine have to prove they work first? Arguing for, Julius Ritter is the founder of the California Peptide Club & CEO of Transcendence, a longevity company working with peptide, exosome, & regenerative therapies. He's part of a growing movement that thinks patients & physicians should have much more freedom to experiment at the frontier of medicine. Arguing against, Dr. Tiana Woolridge is a primary sports medicine physician at Hospital for Special Surgery, double board certified in pediatrics & sports medicine. She's trained in regenerative treatments like PRP herself, which is exactly why she thinks there's a difference between promising medicine & selling something before the evidence is there. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Build Your Creative Operating System
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back - In Person at Salesforce We're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City & sponsored by Boldforce. This Month We Present...Build Your Creative Operating SystemBuild a personalized AI workflow that supports your entire creative process-from capturing ideas to publishing finished work-so you're never starting from scratch. Most of us don't have an idea problem. We have a system problem. Ideas live in our Notes app. Research is scattered across browser tabs. Drafts are hiding in Google Docs. Inspiration gets screenshotted & forgotten. And every new project somehow feels like we're starting all over again. What if your creative process actually remembered how you work? At this month's AI & The Culture meetup, we're exploring how to build your own Creative Operating System-a personalized workflow that uses AI to help you capture ideas, organize knowledge, research, create, refine, & publish your work. Instead of collecting more AI tools, we'll focus on connecting the ones that actually support your process. Together we'll explore:  How to map your creative process from idea to finished work  Ways to capture & organize ideas so they don't disappear into the digital abyss  How AI can help you research, brainstorm, draft, edit, & refine your work  Building a personal knowledge base that makes past ideas & research useful again  How to connect AI tools into repeatable workflows instead of using them one at a time  Where automation can save time-and where your human judgment should stay firmly in the driver's seat  How to create a system that gets smarter & more useful the more you use it The goal isn't to automate your creativity. It's to build the infrastructure around your creativity so you have more time & energy for the work only you can do. Expect a welcoming room filled with creators, technologists, educators, founders, artists, & curious minds ready to rethink how we organize & support our creative lives. Who Should Attend?  Creators & content makers  Filmmakers, writers, artists, & storytellers  Educators & community builders  Entrepreneurs, founders, & solopreneurs  Marketers, strategists, & creative professionals  Technologists & AI enthusiasts  Anyone with too many ideas, too many tabs, & not enough systems  Whether your creative process is already organized or currently held together by screenshots, open tabs, & vibes, you're welcome here. Come Ready to Build This won't be a sit-back-and-scroll kind of evening. Bring your laptop, something to write with, & a mindset ready to learn, experiment, & share. We'll be exploring ideas, tools, & workflows you can begin applying to your own creative process.  Bring your laptop  Bring a notebook or something to take notes with  Bring your curiosity & questions Come ready to learn. Come ready to contribute. Come ready to build. About AI & The Culture AI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, & culture. Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams & King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, & culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, & community. We're building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI. This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture - grounded in community, focused on real-world use, & centered on learning together in the room. Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Let's build - together.  About Your Hosts Shirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, & co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, & creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, & real-world execution. About King Willonius King Willonius is a creative technologist & cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, & creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, & community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable & useful - especially for creatives & innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm.  Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio) #AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: 90/30 NYC: Machine Super Intelligence
events.description: What does it mean for a machine to be intelligent, & can we define it mathematically? Join 90/30 for a reading group on Shane Legg's Machine Super Intelligence. This 2008 PhD thesis explores universal artificial intelligence, the theoretical agent AIXI, & the limits of building machines that learn & act across unfamiliar environments. We'll discuss: How can we measure intelligence beyond performance on a single task? What does AIXI tell us about an ideal intelligent agent? What changes when we move from theoretical intelligence to systems with limited compute? How useful are these ideas for understanding today's AI? This is a long read, so come with a section, question, or argument you want to unpack. You don't need to understand every proof to join the conversation. We are only mandating chapter 1 & 4 while 2 is suggested.

events.name: Ugly Talk: Building Fandoms In 2027
events.description: A customer buys once. A fan brings people with them. Getting there takes months of showing up. Listening. Keeping promises. Giving people a reason to care when you are no longer in their feed. This Ugly Talk gets into the work behind real fandom. The creator calls that went nowhere. The community plays that looked dead for months. The moment loyal customers pushed back & the brand had to answer. No follower-count victory laps. Just the decisions, mistakes, & proof behind communities that stick.  Why you should be in this room.Hear how consumer brands turn one-time buyers into people who recruit other buyers. Learn which signals reveal loyalty before revenue catches up. See how brands build with creators from the first idea through launch. Learn what to keep doing when the community looks quiet. Hear how leaders respond when their biggest supporters become their loudest critics.  What's on the table.Building superfans at scale: What makes customers care enough to bring other people in. Creators & co-creation: How brands share the build instead of buying a post at the end. Measuring fandom: The numbers that matter after likes & reach stop telling the truth. The slow build: What to do when months of work look like nothing is happening. When fandom turns: What community pushback reveals about the trust you built. Managing a crisis: How to respond fast, own the miss, & keep trust intact.  Who's hosting it. Rob Fajardo - Founder, LeaveNormalBehind Rob Fajardo is an entrepreneur, operator, & cultural architect whose work centers on a simple question: what does winning look like? Early in his career, Rob helped drive the fidget spinner phenomenon by building & activating an influencer network across Instagram & Facebook, reaching over 150 million people. Since then, he has worked with brands including DoorDash, Lowe's, FedEx, Converse, Red Bull, & Wyndham Resort Group, & has been featured in Forbes, Entrepreneur, Thrive Global, & BuzzFeed. Rob is the founder of Leave Normal Behind, a global network of purpose-driven leaders, creators, & investors built around meaningful connection, personal growth, & human flourishing. Over the past decade, he has brought together people across industries & generations through designed gatherings & strategic collaborations. He also serves as Head of Operations for the School of Content at The School of Hard Knocks, one of the world's largest business media platforms with 26M+ followers, where he coaches business owners generating six to nine figures on go-to-market. In addition, he is a Strategic Advisor to The AI Collective, the world's largest AI community, with 70,000+ members across 25+ global chapters.  Who's getting in.CPG & consumer-brand founders building a customer base that sticks. Brand & community leaders responsible for loyalty & retention. Creators building their own audience or working with consumer brands. Marketers who care about advocacy, repeat purchases, & long-term growth.  About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough "aha!" moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons & insights. With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami, we've built a vibrant community of thousands of founders & industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape. Official Website: UglyTalk.com Important Notice for Ugly Talk AttendeesAdmission & Confirmation Attendance is by approval only. The event organizers, hosts, sponsors, & venue are not liable for personal injury, lost or stolen belongings, or any other damages incurred during the event. Media Consent By attending, you grant the event organizers & affiliated entities the right to capture, use, & distribute photos, videos, & audio recordings of you for promotional, marketing, & other lawful purposes, including digital & print media, advertising, & social media. You waive any right to inspect or approve the final materials & release all claims related to their use. Communications By registering, you agree to receive marketing & promotional communications from Ugly Talk & its co-hosts, partners, & sponsors. events.name: AI For Small Business - Work Smarter Every Day
events.description: Stop wondering how AI fits into your business-learn what to use, when to use it, & how to use it safely. AI can do more than generate content. Used well, it gives you back time on the work already sitting on your desk-customer emails, research, marketing, & everyday planning. This hands-on workshop shows you exactly how, using the three tools that matter most: ChatGPT, Gemini, & Claude. No coding. No technical background. No prior AI experience. Just practical examples you can put to work immediately. Who this is for This workshop is designed for people who run the day-to-day of a business, including: Small business owners Entrepreneurs Office managers Solo professionals Business operators Non-technical professionals What you'll walk away with A clear sense of which AI tool fits which task-and when to reach for each one Practical, repeatable ways to save time on writing, research, & marketing Confidence to use AI safely & intentionally, not just enthusiastically  Free attendee gifts Every attendee receives two ready-to-use resources: Company AI Policy - a customizable internal policy to help your team set clear, practical guidelines for AI use. Ideal IT Ecosystem Outline for Small Business in 2026 - a straightforward overview of how your AI, IT, cybersecurity, productivity, & technology systems fit together. Agenda 6:00-6:20 PM - Welcome + Foundations. A quick look at what an ideal small-business technology ecosystem looks like in 2026, where AI fits, & what a strong AI policy includes. 6:20-6:35 PM - ChatGPT. Practical ways to use it in your everyday work. 6:35-7:00 PM - Gemini. Applying it to research, content, & marketing tasks. 7:00-7:25 PM - Claude. Using it for writing & customer-facing communication. 7:25-7:30 PM - Q&A. 7:30-8:00 PM - Hands-On Practice + Conversation. Try the tools, ask questions, & explore how they fit your business. Why attend Small improvements add up. A few minutes saved on a marketing email, an hour saved on research, a faster path from idea to marketing content, a stronger first draft for a customer reply-repeated every day, these shifts change how much you get done. Come see what AI can do with your real, everyday work. Looking to build with AI? That's our separate Lovable build workshop. This session is the practical, tool-focused companion-perfect on its own or before you dive into building. Event details  Thursday, October 8, 2026  6:00-8:00 PM ET  Greater Nexus, 89-14 Parsons Blvd, Jamaica, NY 11432  $4.99 Space is limited. Bring your laptop & a few real business tasks you'd like to make easier. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/ Pulse NYC is the community-led platform behind AI Week New York & the Brooklyn Tech Expo - connecting 100,000+ founders, engineers, & tech leaders across NYC through citywide events, programming, & our weekly newsletter. https://pulse.nyc AI should be accessible to every business here, not just big tech companies. Queens AI brings practical, plain-English AI to business owners & executives who are aiming to leverage AI to its fullest potential so their businesses can continue to thrive & grow. For more information, please visit the Queens AI website.

(Pictures Below)Every room has been bigger than the last. Our 2nd edition versus the 1st:Founder revenue: $90M+ a year, up from $18M+ in August.Money being raised: $197M+ across 19 founders, up from $95M+ across 14 in August.Capital already raised: $43M+, up from $35M+ in August.The investors at the table:We feature 6 investors from our network, & we always end up with more.1st edition: We expected 6. We brought 10.2nd edition: We expected 10. We brought 12.$2B+ combined AUM across both events.$1M average check, $100K minimum.$10M+ in live check capacity.Who this room is forTo get into this room, you should to have raised at least $1M or be doing $1M+ in ARR. Our last edition averaged $3.8M+ ARR per founder.Raised your first round, onto your second, or bootstrapped to $1M or 15M ARR? You're in the right place. If you're an exited founder, LP/GP, dealmaker or capital raiser, you belong in this room too.Every investor here is from our network. We're curating this room deliberately, matching founders to the investors most likely to be a fit, & making the introduction ourselves.The goal: getting founders funded by our investor network.The 6 Investors joining us from our network: (More will be joining)Francesca Poupel: F&G Capital Partners (Managing Partner): Backing founders from pre-seed to Series A in AI, fintech, & blockchain, writing $300K$500K checks & partnering closely with teams as they scale.Mahir Laul (Partner) representing Laul Global a family office & holding company operating four interconnected pillars: Education Engine, Real Assets, Future Ventures, & Acquisitions. We built it into one of Canada's most diversified education holding groups. Writing $200K$300K checks.Andrew Antar (General Partner, AG Venture Capital): A generalist fund backing extraordinary founders, sector agnostic. He is also founder of Tune.FM, a tokenized music streaming platform & digital asset marketplace, & co-founded Clear Quantum, a stealth quantum AI startup.Gonzalo Quincot (Founder, Sinober): Sinober is a financial intelligence platform that combines public & private market intelligence with institutional-grade methodology, corporate finance & proprietary AI tools to sharpen investment & capital decisions for individuals & businesses. Invests in automation, robotics, data centers & applied AI.Shilpi Nayak: (Founder & General Partner, 434 VC): Invests in early-stage technical founders across AI, infrastructure, physical AI & emerging technology. She is also the founder of House of 434, a community bringing together founders, investors & industry leaders.Pranav Jajapur (Co-Founder, ZERON Ventures): ZERON is an early-stage venture fund with an execution platform behind it, backing real-world technology, AI, healthcare, deep tech & climate companies building in the physical world, inside biology. Pre-seed through Series A with core deployment at seed, writing $400K$500k checks. Preferred focus is institutionally-anchored AI: structural research relationships at academic institutions, spinouts, & founder-led research programs.Fund I in formation. Deploying Q1All 6 senior investors confirmed.Part of building rooms is making sure real capital is present. Six investors actively deploying writing capital will be joining. Community has been lost & we are rebuilding it.Our Venue: Some PhotosOur Greek Inspired Menu:About the mealA three-course Greek menu. Appetizers & dessert are shared & open to everyone; each will get one entre.The format is intentionally part standing, part seated so you can enjoy incredible food without being anchored to a single table or a single conversation.Why we do thisOur intent is simple: bring good, smart humans together, put active investors in the same room as incredible founders. events.name: Deal Flow: NYC's First VC Hackathon
events.description: Event DescriptionNew York is getting its first VC hackathon, & you're building for the people who write the checks. Deal Flow is a one-day, in-person hackathon hosted by localhost:nyc & VCLab. You get 9 hours to build working products for the real problems VCs face every day. Partners from NYC's top funds judge live, & the best teams leave with intros to those funds. Problem StatementVenture capital runs on spreadsheets, gut feel & endless inbox triage. Firms move billions of dollars with tools that haven't changed in a decade. Your challenge is to build software that helps VCs find better companies, make faster decisions & support their founders after the check clears. The Challenge ThemeSourcing: finding breakout founders before everyone else does Diligence: market maps, competitive analysis & memo drafting Portfolio ops: helping funds support their companies at scale LP reporting: making fund updates less painful & more useful Deal pipeline & CRM workflows that VCs will actually use What to Expect9 hours of focused building, 9 AM to 6 PM Real VC problems, with investors in the room to test your ideas against Teams of 4 Time to meet founders, engineers & investors from across NYC Live demos to a panel of VC judges at the end of the day Food & drinks all day PrizesWinners get intros to the funds in the room + other prizes to be announced. JudgesAbeera Saeed is the Ventures Principal at Plug & Play, investing in Enterprise & AI B2B SaaS companies from Pre-Seed to Series A. Michael Barone - Investment Analyst at Everywhere Ventures, a global pre-seed venture capital firm. D. J. Patel - VC | 3x exited founder. Radhika Khandelwal builds AI agents for a living as a product leader at Wand AI, & she's spent years in the VC world seeing what makes startups stick. She'll want to see both slick code & a real business. Who Should AttendPre-seed & seed founders Engineers Builders who have felt the pain of fundraising firsthand Anyone curious about how venture capital actually works from the inside You don't need VC experience or a finished idea. Just show up ready to build. Sponsors[Sponsor TBD. Want to back NYC's first VC hackathon? Email somyag00@gmail.com] HostsSomya Gupta: The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Tracy Huang: VC Lab & CEO of Interlink IQ

events.name: Creativity Is Dead, Long Live Creativity - Gen AI & Meaning Of Art
events.description: The concept of creativity has a surprisingly short history. While ancient philosophers expounded on imagination & free will, theorizations of creativity as a distinct trait only date to the past hundred years. GenAI suggests that creativity is not unique to humans or even conscious organisms, but is reducible to mere calculation & programming. Has creativity finally been revealed as a sham? This week's interactive community conversation explores thought experiments that embody the philosophical issues raised by genAI tools; how scholars & artists have framed the relationship between creativity & technology; was creativity always a myth, & if so, is this a problem? OUR FACILITATOREmma Stamm is the Co-Founder & Executive Director of The Lenox Institute for Advanced Study. She holds a PhD in Interdisciplinary Studies from Virginia Tech, & her work bridges critical theory & STS. WHO'S IT FOR?Idea people. Founders. Builders. Creatives. Researchers. The Curious. events.name: Six Math Essentials w/ Terence Tao
events.description: Book Launch & Conversation with Janna Levin Widely regarded as the world's greatest living mathematician, Fields Medalist Terence Tao approaches mathematics as a sublime art-a quiet, rigorous effort to map the hidden scaffolding of reality. To mark the publication of his first popular book, Six Math Essentials, join us for an evening with Tao in conversation with Pioneer Works Director of Sciences Janna Levin. Tracing the central pillars of his book-from algebra as abstraction & geometry beyond sight, to navigating uncertainty & the mathematics of change-they will reveal math not as obscure magic, but as a deeply creative, interconnected way of thinking. Often referred to as the Mozart of mathematics, Tao will also explore how AI is transforming his own practice, the frontier of research, & our collective future. Together, we will consider what becomes of human intuition & creativity when the tools of thought are no longer uniquely human-and whether the true beauty of math lies not in the answers we find, but in the human mind reaching for them. Tao will sign copies of Six Math Essentials following the conversation, with books available for purchase on site. (Unable to attend? Order a signed copy here.) Please note that seating is limited & will be available on a first-come, first-served basis.   About the speakersTerence Tao is an Australian-American professor of mathematics at UCLA whose work focuses primarily on harmonic analysis, partial differential equations, combinatorics, & analytic number theory. The recipient of a Fields Medal, a MacArthur Genius Grant, & a Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics, among many other accolades, he is one of the most decorated & prolific mathematicians working today. Tao is the author of several academic books including Solving Mathematical Problems: A Personal Perspective & Additive Combinatorics, as well as his first popular math book, Six Math Essentials. He lives in Los Angeles. Janna Levin is the Claire Tow Professor of physics & astronomy at Barnard College of Columbia University. A Guggenheim Fellow, she has contributed to our understanding of black holes, extra dimensions, & cosmology. She is the founding director of sciences at Pioneer Works & the founding editor-in-chief of the magazine Pioneer Works Broadcast. She often contributes to news, documentaries, & radio, including as the presenter of the NOVA feature Black Hole Apocalypse on PBS & as a contributor to CBS, CNN, BBC, & NBC. She has authored books on black holes & the universe-Black Hole Blues, How the Universe Got its Spots, & Black Hole Survival Guide-as well as a PEN award-winning novel, A Madman Dreams of Turing Machines. You can find her current writings in Higher Dimensions. This program is funded by the Simons Foundation International & administered by the Simons Foundation's Science, Society & Culture division.

Book Launch & Conversation with Janna Levin Widely regarded as the world's greatest living mathematician, Fields Medalist Terence Tao approaches mathematics as a sublime art-a quiet, rigorous effort to map the hidden scaffolding of reality. To mark the publication of his first popular book, Six Math Essentials, join us for an evening with Tao in conversation with Pioneer Works Director of Sciences Janna Levin. Tracing the central pillars of his book-from algebra as abstraction & geometry beyond sight, to navigating uncertainty & the mathematics of change-they will reveal math not as obscure magic, but as a deeply creative, interconnected way of thinking. Often referred to as the Mozart of mathematics, Tao will also explore how AI is transforming his own practice, the frontier of research, & our collective future. Together, we will consider what becomes of human intuition & creativity when the tools of thought are no longer uniquely human-and whether the true beauty of math lies not in the answers we find, but in the human mind reaching for them. Tao will sign copies of Six Math Essentials following the conversation, with books available for purchase on site. (Unable to attend? Order a signed copy here.) Please note that seating is limited & will be available on a first-come, first-served basis.   About the speakersTerence Tao is an Australian-American professor of mathematics at UCLA whose work focuses primarily on harmonic analysis, partial differential equations, combinatorics, & analytic number theory. The recipient of a Fields Medal, a MacArthur Genius Grant, & a Breakthrough Prize in Mathematics, among many other accolades, he is one of the most decorated & prolific mathematicians working today. Tao is the author of several academic books including Solving Mathematical Problems: A Personal Perspective & Additive Combinatorics, as well as his first popular math book, Six Math Essentials. He lives in Los Angeles. Janna Levin is the Claire Tow Professor of physics & astronomy at Barnard College of Columbia University. A Guggenheim Fellow, she has contributed to our understanding of black holes, extra dimensions, & cosmology. She is the founding director of sciences at Pioneer Works & the founding editor-in-chief of the magazine Pioneer Works Broadcast. She often contributes to news, documentaries, & radio, including as the presenter of the NOVA feature Black Hole Apocalypse on PBS & as a contributor to CBS, CNN, BBC, & NBC. She has authored books on black holes & the universe-Black Hole Blues, How the Universe Got its Spots, & Black Hole Survival Guide-as well as a PEN award-winning novel, A Madman Dreams of Turing Machines. You can find her current writings in Higher Dimensions. This program is funded by the Simons Foundation International & administered by the Simons Foundation's Science, Society & Culture division.

events.name: AI & The Culture IRL | Plan Your Best Year With AI
events.description: AI & The Culture Is Back  In Person at SalesforceWe're back for another edition of AI & The Culture IRL in partnership with Salesforce. This is yet another incredible in-person gathering, hosted at the Salesforce offices in New York City and sponsored by Boldforce.This Month We Present...Plan Your Best Year With AIJoin the community for an interactive planning session to reflect on the past year, identify your biggest opportunities, and build an AI-powered roadmap for the year ahead.Before we rush into a new year with another list of goals, lets get clear about what were actually building.What worked this year? What didnt? What deserves more of your energy? And where could AI help you turn those intentions into action?For our final AI & The Culture meetup of the year, were bringing the community together for an interactive planning and reflection session designed to help you look back, think forward, and build a roadmap for what comes next.This isnt about asking AI to magically plan your life. Its about using these tools as thought partnersto help you reflect, uncover patterns, explore possibilities, make decisions, and turn big ambitions into actionable next steps.Together well explore: How to use AI to reflect on your wins, lessons, challenges, and unfinished business from the past year Prompts that help you identify opportunities you might be overlooking How to turn big goals into realistic projects, milestones, and next steps Ways to use AI as a strategic thought partner for your creative work, career, business, or personal projects How to identify where AI and automation can give you back time in the year ahead Building a personalized AI-powered roadmap you can actually use after you leave the roomAnd because this is AI & The Culture, were making space for something AI cant replace: community.Youll have an opportunity to reflect alongside other creatives, founders, educators, artists, technologists, and curious mindsto exchange ideas, share what youre building, and potentially meet the people who can help you move it forward.The goal isnt to leave with 47 resolutions.Its to leave with clarity, priorities, and a plan.Who Should Attend? Creators and content makers Filmmakers, writers, artists, and storytellers Educators and community builders Entrepreneurs, founders, and solopreneurs Marketers, strategists, and creative professionals Technologists and AI enthusiasts Anyone ready to be more intentional about what theyre building nextWhether you already have your next year mapped out or youre still staring at a blank page wondering where to begin, youre welcome here.Come Ready to BuildThis one is especially hands-on, so come prepared to participate. Bring your laptop Bring a notebook or something to write with Bring a few goals, ideas, or questions youve been thinking about for the year ahead Bring your curiosity and a willingness to shareWell be working through reflection exercises, AI prompts, and planning activities togetherso you can leave with the beginnings of a roadmap, not just another page of notes.Come ready to reflect. Come ready to plan. Come ready to build.About AI & The CultureAI & The Culture is a growing movement exploring the intersection of artificial intelligence, creativity, and culture.Founded by Shirley Vernae Williams and King Willonius, we connect creatives of color, innovators, and culturally rooted creators through events, education, storytelling, and community.Were building spaces where the people shaping culture can also help shape the future of AI.This gathering represents the next chapter of AI & The Culture  grounded in community, focused on real-world use, and centered on learning together in the room.Pull up with curiosity. Let's have the important conversations.Lets build  together. About Your HostsShirley Williams-Toney is an award-winning storyteller, AI technologist, and co-founder of AI & The Culture. Her work sits at the intersection of culture, technology, and creative systems, with a focus on helping people use AI tools in ways that support clarity, productivity, and real-world execution.About King WilloniusKing Willonius is a creative technologist and cultural strategist exploring how emerging tools can support storytelling, workflow, and creative expression. Through demos, experimentation, and community-based learning, Will focuses on making AI feel approachable and useful  especially for creatives and innovators who want practical applications without technical overwhelm. Follow us on Instagram @the.culture.ai Join our WhatsApp community (link in bio)#AIAndTheCulture #BeginnerFriendlyAI #SlackAI #POCInTech #TechMeetsCulture #InclusiveInnovation #CreativeTechnology #FutureIsColorful

events.name: Legal Engineers NYC: What Do Clients Want? Law Firm AI Governance
events.description: What Do Clients Want? Law Firm AI Governance Clients are writing AI rules for their law firms: outside counsel guidelines that ban public AI tools, insurance carriers that require approval for each AI use or reserve the right to audit it, procurement questionnaires that ask how AI use is controlled. What does it take to meet those rules, & to prove you did? We will bring real, published client AI requirements. Pick one & build an approach to it: the policy, tools, workflow or checks a firm would need, & how it would show the client it complied. Or show a governance tool you use or have tried, from approved-tool lists & logging to governance platforms & things you built. Laptops open; no coding required; demos encouraged. ICME Labs will show how PreFlight lets firms prove to clients that their AI followed the rules, without disclosing client data. We finish with the group's map of what clients are asking for, the approaches that work, & the gaps nobody has solved yet. Our first session brought 47 legal engineers to Falcon Rappaport & Berkman to test which AI tools invent case law. This one turns to the rules clients are writing for the firms that use AI. Date: Wednesday, October 14, 4:00pm - 5:30pm Location: Meeting Room A, 40 Wall St, 28th Floor, New York. Legal Engineers NYC is a hands-on group for people who turn law, policy, & practice into the workflows, agents, evals, & controls that run legal work. We meet weekly on Thursdays in Manhattan, laptops open, & build something each time. Any platform counts, & no coding required. Legal Engineers NYC is organized by ICME Labs & led by cofounder Houman Shadab. Contact houman@icme.io to host or sponsor a session.

events.name: Columbia Starup Lab - Get Hired Hack
events.description: Event DescriptionSkip the resume pile. Get Hired Hack is a one-day, in-person hackathon at Columbia Startup Lab where NYC's fastest-growing startups bring real problems from their roadmaps, & you show them what working with you looks like. Founders who are hiring will be in the room, watching you build. Ship something great & your demo becomes your first commit. Problem StatementStartups don't hire resumes. They hire people who ship. But hiring still runs on LeetCode, keyword filters & 45-minute calls that tell a founder almost nothing about how you work. At Get Hired Hack, each hiring startup brings one real, scoped problem it would actually assign a new engineer. Pick a track, build against it, & demo it to the founder who wrote it. Founders get the best hiring signal there is: real work on their real problem. You get a shot at a role on proof of work, not pedigree. The Challenge Tracks Each track is a real problem from a hiring startup: TBD Expect problems across: AI agents & LLM-powered features Full-stack product work Infra, devtools & data pipelines Growth & internal tooling What to ExpectFounders who are hiring pitch their problem at kickoff [~6] hours of focused building on real startup problems Teams of 4 Demos to the founder whose problem you picked Lunch, coffee & a room full of people building NYC's next great companies PrizesEvery track winner gets a fast-tracked final-round interview with that startup's founder JudgesTBD Who Should AttendEngineers with real shipping experience (full stack, backend, AI/ML, infra) Senior engineers curious about joining an early-stage startup Builders who'd rather show their work than talk about it Engineers who want to be a startup's first or fifth hire, not its five-hundredth You don't need to be actively job hunting. Come build, meet founders & see what's out there. SponsorsTBD HostsSomya Gupta: The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Columbia Startup Lab: Columbia's home for alumni founders, a coworking space & community in SoHo.

Begin the evening with a warm welcome & a chance to settle in. 6:00 - 6:45: "Women's Health: Undervalued to Unavoidable" by Marissa Fayer & Bailey Morgan. 6:45 - 8:30 Networking. Connect, converse, & collaborate with peers driven by a common passion for advancing healthcare through technology.  About our Guest Speaker: Marissa Fayer has spent 25+ years operating at the intersection of technology & women's health. She's CEO of DeepLook Medical, an FDA-cleared AI diagnostics company focused on improving cancer detection for patients with dense breast tissue, & CEO/founder of HERhealthEQ, a nonprofit that's improved the health outcomes of 151,000+ women in 13 different countries by expanding access to medical devices & equipment. Marissa approaches women's health as infrastructure: when properly funded & built, it drives measurable returns across economies, workforces, & communities. Previously, Marissa held executive roles at Hologic, Olympus, Maquet Getinge, & has consulted for organizations including Pfizer, the National Institutes of Health (NIH), NuVasive, & Boehringer Ingelheim. She currently serves as an Investment Committee Member of GG Ventures, a 2026-2028 World Economic Forum (WEF) Technology Fellow, is an active founding member of Milken Institute's Women's Health Committee, & advisor to Welwaze Medical, Impact.51, & TechThrive Ventures. Marissa is the author of Undervalued to Unavoidable: Women's Health as Infrastructure. Marissa is a TEDx speaker (2019 TEDxLugano), has delivered keynotes at leading global healthcare conferences, & has been recognized as a Top 100 Women in Medtech & a Medtech Voice to Follow. Venue details will be shared with registered attendees. Because of limited capacity, we won't be able to accommodate everyone, so please register whenever you are sure you can attend. Don't miss this chance to be part of a community that's driving the future of health tech. Reserve your spot now & join us in shaping the landscape of digital health for 2026 & beyond. Partners FINN Partners - more than an agency. Champions of change. FINN Partners is one of the fastest-growing global, independent marketing & communications agencies in the world, serving clients through a powerful combination of bold creativity, informed strategy, hands-on partnership, & highly specialized expertise. About the organizer Bailey Morgan, Based in Astoria, NYC, is a versatile healthtech leader who merges clinical expertise with business acumen to accelerate healthcare innovation & community impact. Having started her career as a medical speech language pathologist working within inpatient facilities throughout the boroughs of NYC, she saw firsthand how behind the healthcare tech ecosystem was compared to industries such as tech or finance. After leaving healthcare to move into the healthtech startup space, Bailey has since raised over $10M in capital, led several successful sales & marketing teams through go-to-market stages in both SaaS & CPG, & has closed over $2M in technology sales herself. If we do capture some moments, Health2Tech may use the photos or videos for marketing & communication purposes. By registering, you're giving us the thumbs up for using your image for these reasons.

events.name: [AI Briefing] Private Equity - What Owners & Buyers Pay For
events.description: The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise.  This month's source: The PE AI Adoption Benchmark: From scaling to systematizing (Accordion with Wakefield Research - May 2026) Somebody's going to ask what your AI spend returned. If your company has a board or an eventual buyer, that question is already scheduled. Private equity gets asked first, so that's where this month's data comes from. Accordion surveyed 150 technology & AI operating partners at PE sponsors about the finance functions inside their portfolios. 41% are scaling AI across multiple companies with no operational playbook, & only 29% describe their firm as systematizing or leading. 75% of those companies arrived at acquisition unprepared or only partially ready for any of it. 86% of these operating partners expect buyers to pay a premium for AI-enabled finance capability within two years, & 44% say buyers are already asking in diligence without paying for it yet. Conviction is running ahead of price. The deployment that worked & left no evidence behind it is the one that costs you at exit. 67% of firms measure hours recovered. 29% put AI impact in front of a board.  The Mission: Building the evidence a board or a buyer will accept We'll work the measurement problem directly: which AI metrics connect to EBITDA, & how a company gets there without starting over. We'll examine why only 14% of portfolio finance functions have crossed from back-office automation into real decision intelligence, & what the rest are paying for instead.  The Format: The benchmark, fast: Five findings & the numbers under them, including the ones that don't hold up. Translating it out of PE: Sponsors run this test on a clock, so the pressure shows up there first. We'll take what it exposes & apply it to companies with other kinds of owners. Cross-pollinated debate: Operators compare what agentic finance already does in production (58% report automated covenant monitoring, 44% report AI-drafted board packages) against what their own governance can defend today.  Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: Leave with the measures a buyer or board will scrutinize, & an honest read on which ones you could produce this quarter. Founders & Builders: See what sponsors & portfolio CFOs are buying, & where the 47% assembling AI tools case-by-case stall out before anything compounds. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Compare notes on the constraint everything else runs into. Poor data infrastructure ranked first among all barriers by a wide margin, ahead of talent, legacy systems, change management, & budget. Most of it arrives at close & gets fixed while the books are closing.  The Prep: This is a working session, not a lecture. Read the report here. Bring your perspective.

events.name: Sobremesa - Private Dinner For Latin American Founders

This dinner is the smaller, quieter room the night after - same community, twenty seats instead of a hundred. Co-hosted by Christopher Martnez (Ziora Copilot) & Sharon Rao, MD. Nuestra gente, nuestra mesa.
