We're curating this room deliberately, matching founders to the investors most likely to be a fit, & making the introduction ourselves. The goal here: Getting founders funded by our investor network. The 6 Investors joining us from our network: (More will be joining) Francesca Poupel: F&G Capital Partners (Managing Partner): Backing founders from pre-seed to Series A in AI, fintech, & blockchain, writing $300K-$500K checks & partnering closely with teams as they scale. Mahir Laul (Partner) representing Laul Global a family office & holding company operating four interconnected pillars: Education Engine, Real Assets, Future Ventures, & Acquisitions. One integrated system. One long-term vision. Laul Global is owned & operated by the Laul family. We started with a single student recruitment company. We built it into one of Canada's most diversified education holding groups. Today the portfolio spans institutions, edtech, real estate, & a tech venture studio, with reach across 20+ countries & no plans to slow down.  Triet Leminh: Principal, LMT Partners: Lawyer, founder, & investor backing pre-seed to Series A founders building in enterprise & regulated industries. Writing $200K-$300K checks.  Andrew Antar (General Partner, AG Venture Capital): A generalist fund backing extraordinary founders, sector agnostic. Also a Venture Partner at Arcadian Capital, focused on late-stage secondaries & pre-IPO tech, & served as Crypto Policy Advisor to the NYC Office of the Mayor - advising on the city's crypto regulatory framework & organizing the NYC Crypto Summit at Gracie Mansion. He is also founder of Tune.FM, a tokenized music streaming platform & digital asset marketplace, & co-founded Clear Quantum, a stealth quantum AI startup. Gonzalo Quincot (Founder, Sinober): Sinober is a financial intelligence platform that combines public & private market intelligence with institutional-grade methodology, corporate finance & proprietary AI tools to sharpen investment & capital decisions for individuals & businesses. Invests in automation, robotics, data centers & applied AI.  Shilpi Nayak: (Founder & General Partner, 434 VC): Invests in early-stage technical founders across AI, infrastructure, physical AI & emerging technology. She is also the founder of House of 434, a community bringing together founders, investors & industry leaders.  Pranav Jajapur (Co-Founder, ZERON Ventures): ZERON is an early-stage venture fund with an execution platform behind it, backing real-world technology, AI, healthcare, deep tech & climate companies building in the physical world, inside biology. Pre-seed through Series A with core deployment at seed, writing $400K-$500k checks. Preferred focus is institutionally-anchored AI: structural research relationships at academic institutions, spinouts, & founder-led research programs. Fund I in formation. Deploying Q1  All 6 senior investors confirmed. Part of building rooms is making sure real capital is present. Six investors actively deploying writing capital will be joining. Our first confirmed: Why we do this: Putting active investors in the same room as exceptional founders, & keeps the room small enough to ensure everyone actually meets. We value intentional networking & community. If you're here to meet the best of the best, this is the room. Our Sponsor: Composition WealthYour seat at the table is waiting. Your life is shaped by new beginnings, major decisions, & milestones. That's why when it comes to developing the strategies to achieve your financial goals, we make sure you have a seat at the table & are empowered with the knowledge & tools to shape your own future. At Composition Wealth, our goal is to empower you to reach YOUR goals. Chris Guarino, CFPBook some time: Calendly link What to expect for this: A Greek style lunch, courtesy of our team Conversations with fellow high-performing startup leaders An experience designed to facilitate new meaningful connections conversations with ambitious peers solving similar problems Event to be hosted at a beautiful private Soho loft Our intent is to bring good, smart humans together, & active investors together to fun incredible founders. Community has been lost & we are rebuilding it. Our Greek Inspired Menu: About the meal A three-course Greek menu. Appetizers & dessert are shared & open to everyone; each will get one entre. The format is intentionally part standing, part seated so you can enjoy incredible food without being anchored to a single table or a single conversation. Why we do this Our intent is simple: bring good, smart humans together, put active investors in the same room as incredible founders. Intentional community has been lost. We're rebuilding it.

Deals in the room - one matched meeting at a time.

events.name: PMAI: Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Sales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. We'll cover how to identify & reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach & customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, & build the foundation for your first 100, & eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, & only scale the sales function when the business is ready. Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: Networking Who should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether you're preparing to launch, looking for your first 10-100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, you'll learn how to take ownership of sales & get closer to what customers actually want. It's especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, & generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets. - Bring a computer. You're writing three things tonight.- Most founders can get meetings. The deals die after meeting one.- You'll leave with your buyer in one sentence, a cold email written to a real person, & five questions for your next call. About Farzad, the speaker Farzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, & an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth & sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs & Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, & Blackstone. He has helped build & scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, & customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, & consumer brands. He has served as a fractional COO & CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) & Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding & generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the company's $140 million Series C. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: Supabase x Grafana & Friends

events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: The AI-ndustrial Revolution?
events.description: Companies are spending billions on AI. But is it actually making the economy better? Right now, the evidence is weird. Only 1 in 8 CEOs says AI is both increasing revenue & cutting costs. At the same time, 77% of CEOs say AI has been overhyped so far-but may actually be underhyped over the next decade. So what happens next? A productivity boom that creates new industries & better jobs? Or enormous investment, displaced workers, & technology that never delivers enough value to justify the hype? Daniel Di Martino, an economist & Fellow at the Manhattan Institute, studies economic growth, labor markets, & the policies that drive American competitiveness. Dr. Cecilia Dones is a Columbia lecturer & longtime data & AI executive who works with organizations trying to turn massive AI investments into actual business value. Will AI be a net benefit to the American economy? Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

Or enormous investment, displaced workers, & technology that never delivers enough value to justify the hype? Daniel Di Martino, an economist & Fellow at the Manhattan Institute, studies economic growth, labor markets, & the policies that drive American competitiveness. Dr. Cecilia Dones is a Columbia lecturer & longtime data & AI executive who works with organizations trying to turn massive AI investments into actual business value. Will AI be a net benefit to the American economy? Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

events.name: Ugly Talks: Failure Is Key To Success
events.description: Failure gets talked about like it is part of the journey. That is the lie. The real thing is messier. Missed bets. Wrong hires. Near-breakdowns. The week you stop sleeping & start doing math at 3:00 AM. Founders are expected to eat it quietly & keep moving. No language for what happened. No playbook for what to do next. Ugly Talk is a founder room for the part nobody posts. No fluff. No consultants. Just builders with scars, talking about the call that cost them.  Why you should be in this room.Hear what failure cost them. Then hear what they did next. Learn how experienced founders separate self-worth from outcomes when things go sideways. Spot the patterns behind repeat mistakes. And the early signals you should not ignore. Leave with a few concrete moves for the next hard week. Not inspiration. Meet other founders in the thick of it. The ones who are still building.  What's on the table.Dare to suck: how permission to fail unlocks real progress The moment things broke: missed opportunities, wrong turns, near-breakdowns, & what changed afterward Failure vs identity: separating self-worth from outcomes Treating setbacks as data: what to measure, what to ignore, & how to decide fast Rejection as redirection: how founders find the signal in the no Habits for staying focused & resilient when everything feels uncertain  Run of show6:00 - 6:30 PM: Reception (check-in & light drinks) 6:30 - 6:40 PM: Welcome remarks 6:40 - 6:50 PM: Keynote Speech by Ben McKean 6:50 - 7:30 PM: Panel Discussion 7:30 - 7:45 PM: Audience Q&A 7:45 - 8:00 PM: Mixer + snacks & drinks  Featured speakers.Ben McKean - Founder & Chief Executive Officer, Hungryroot Ben McKean is the Founder & CEO of Hungryroot, a personalized healthy eating assistant that uses AI to make meal planning, food shopping, & nutrition effortless & enjoyable. Prior to Hungryroot, Ben was a Vice President & General Manager at Groupon, overseeing their food & beverage business. Ben came to Groupon through the acquisition of Savored, which he founded in 2009. Savored was the nation's leading provider of yield management technology to the restaurant industry, used by over two thousand restaurants nationwide & nearly one million diners. Prior to Savored, Ben worked in Merrill Lynch's technology investment banking group. Ben is a graduate of Georgetown University & currently lives in North Carolina with his wife & kids. Stephen McKinney - Founder & CEO, Bizbe Stephen McKinney is a serial entrepreneur with over a decade of experience across tech, marketing, & logistics. He's the founder & CEO of Bizbe.com, an AI-native business brokerage & lower middle market M&A firm based in New York & Miami. A former contestant on ABC's Shark Tank, Steve previously founded & led Retty Logistics, a seven-figure last-mile delivery company acquired by DXP Logistics & Webster Logistics. Dmitry Koltunov - Founder & CEO, Arbor Dmitry Koltunov is a serial entrepreneur, technologist, educator, & storyteller. events.name: The Quantified Self - What AI Can Actually Tell US About Our Data
events.description: This year, ChatGPT started connecting to people's medical records & Apple Health data, & a glucose sensor no longer needs a prescription. Gary Wolf (Co-founder, Quantified Self; longtime WIRED writer & editor) has studied how people make sense of their own data for 20 years. Hear what AI now makes possible for users, & how founders can build answers people trust. This year, OpenAI started letting people connect their medical records & Apple Health data to ChatGPT.  Since 2024, Americans can buy a continuous glucose monitor without a prescription. For most of the Quantified Self movement's history, answering a question with your own data meant manual logs & spreadsheets. Today a sensor collects the data & an AI model analyzes it on demand. That leaves every founder building in this space with one hard question: when an AI's answer changes what someone eats or takes, how do they know it's right? Gary Wolf has spent nearly 20 years watching people try to answer questions with their own data.  He co-founded Quantified Self with Kevin Kelly, joined the WIRED editorial team in 1994, became the first executive producer of Wired Digital, & launched Wired News. His New York Times Magazine cover story on self-tracking brought the practice to a mainstream audience, & his TED talk on the subject has been watched more than a million times. His current work is about AI & personal data. He's researching a cryptographic protocol to prove where sensor data came from at the moment it's recorded, & writing essays on how people talk to AI chatbots.  His new book, The Quantified Self: Learning to Observe, lays out a method anyone can use to test a question against their own data. On Thursday, October 15, Gary joins Startup Grind to talk about what AI changes for people using their own data, & what that means for the founders building those products. WHAT YOU'LL LEARN What AI changed for self-trackers: The analysis Quantified Self members once did by hand, & what a user can now do in one conversation with a model.When to trust a model's answer: How to tell when an AI reading of your sleep or blood sugar holds up, & what a user needs before acting on it.Proving where data came from: Gary's research on verifying sensor data at the moment it's recorded, & what it means for products that make health claims.Building around the user's question: The question, observe, reason, discover method from his new book, & how to design a product around what a user is actually asking. WHO SHOULD ATTEND AI health & wellness founders: Your model tells people what their data means, & they're going to act on it.Wearable & sensor founders: You collect the data, & your users can now hand it to an AI to interpret.AI product builders in any category: You're shipping personalized advice & want to hear from someone who has studied how people make sense of their own numbers for nearly 2 decades.Founders who track themselves: You've already asked a chatbot about your sleep data & want to know how far to trust the answer.Tickets for this event include food & drinks, as well as time with Gary after the chat to ask about your own product.  BONUS: you'll have an opportunity to purchase Gary's new book & get your copy signed by the author, himself! You'll also meet dozens of other high-performing entrepreneurs who are creating their next big thing. Seriously, it's some of the best founder networking in the city. Getting a ticket guarantees admission. No waitlisting. AGENDA 6:00 PM: Networking, Food & Drinks7:00 PM: Fireside Chat with Gary Wolf8:00 PM: Meet the Speaker + Book SigningAnd don't miss our other monthly tech events. They are great opportunities for builders, founders, & operators to network with each other to share best practices & find new resources to grow your startup the right way. See our full event lineup here.

events.description: Join CUNY at the Climate Imaginarium!Open to the public! Members of the CUNY community will be joining us for a gallery tour, followed by a meditation & climate cafe. Climate cafes are listening circles for your climate-linked emotions. Get help facing your climate anxiety & connect with impactful local organizers. Vegan snacks provided!  About the Climate ImaginariumThe Climate Imaginarium is a center for climate, community, & culture in New York City. Located on Governors Island, the Climate Imaginarium is activating a cultural destination at the heart of New York City's burgeoning green economy, where artists, scientists, advocates, & storytellers come together to reimagine & build toward a more resilient future.  Getting to the Climate ImaginariumFor the weekend ferry schedule to Governors Island, please check here. Ferries run every 15 minutes. Take the ferry that's most convenient for you from either Lower Manhattan (10 South Street), Brooklyn Bridge Park (Pier 6), or Red Hook/Atlantic Basin. Please arrive 15 minutes prior to your ferry departure time with your ticket ready to display. Ferry tickets must be purchased at the ferry terminal or online. Fares are $5 for a round trip ticket & free for adults over 65, children 12 & under, Climate Imaginarium summer volunteers, & others. All passengers ride free before 11am on weekends. Cars are not permitted. Governors Island is also accessible from any route via NYC Ferry by transferring at Wall Street/Pier 11. You can find the NYC Ferry schedule here. Tickets on NYC Ferry are $4.50 each way. Once you get to Governors Island, you will either get out at Soissons Landing (from Manhattan) or Yankee Pier (from Brooklyn). You can use this map of Governors Island to locate Colonels Row. The Climate Imaginarium is in Building 406A, in the middle of Colonels Row, & will have a visible sign outside the doorway. Our address is 406A Comfort Road.

events.name: AI Fraud & Death Of Resume - Restoring Algorithmic Trust
events.description: Conquer the AI job market battleground with elite CISO Dr. Rachel Levitch. Learn to restore algorithmic trust & secure your pipeline!  The 2026 job market is facing an unprecedented security & operational crisis. The recruitment landscape has evolved from a standard talent search into a high-stakes battleground of synthetic data. Candidates are deploying advanced, hyper-automated AI agents to mass-apply to hundreds of open roles instantly, reverse-engineer corporate Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS), auto-generate perfect skill matches, & deploy deepfake technology to bypass initial technical screenings. HR departments & engineering teams are drowning in a sea of algorithmic noise. As talent pipelines become flooded with AI-polished fraud, a staggering percentage of enterprise managers report that total trust in the inbound pipeline has completely eroded. In this high-stakes security & talent briefing, Dr. Rachel Levitch-seasoned Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) & founder of the Cognitive Institute-shifts the conversation from simple recruitment metrics to hard-line Systems Security & Information Integrity. We will move beyond the traditional interview structure to explore the mechanics of modern algorithmic fraud, the vulnerabilities of automated screening systems, & the implementation of secure identity & skill verification frameworks. This session provides human resource executives, tech founders, & venture capitalists with the exact tactical roadmap required to bypass synthetic candidate noise, protect personal data privacy, & restore institutional trust in a market-led crisis. Key Takeaways for Attendees: The AI Vulnerability Audit: A live technical breakdown of how 2026 AI-auto-apply bots actively breach, manipulate, & exploit corporate ATS filters.Detecting the Synthetic Candidate: Concrete, practical strategies for talent acquisition teams to identify AI-forged certifications, deepfake video setups, & automated resume stuffing.Rebuilding the Trust Chain: Transitioning your organization toward zero-trust recruitment frameworks, secure identity verification, & authentic human-sustainability metrics. Purchase Tickets At URL Below or See All Events here: https://www.eventbrite.com/o/121452823948

events.name: The Age Of AI  - Live Recording Of The Builders
events.description: Bestselling biographer Walter Isaacson joins us for a live recording of the first episode of his brand-new podcast, The Builders, with Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of Microsoft AI & one of the most influential thinkers & leaders working in artificial intelligence today. AI is reshaping our world at breathtaking speed. But behind the technology, real human beings are making choices about what our future will look like, how we'll work & live, & whose vision will shape what comes next. And as AI grows more powerful, so does the unease surrounding it. Will it usher in an era of extraordinary human possibility - or are we building something we may ultimately struggle to control? On The Builders, Walter Isaacson talks to the entrepreneurs, scientists & technologists building AI & other technologies that are rapidly reshaping our world to get inside the thinking of some of the most consequential figures of our time. Throughout his career, Isaacson has been fascinated by the people who change the world - from Leonardo da Vinci & Albert Einstein to Steve Jobs, Jennifer Doudna & Elon Musk. With The Builders, he turns his attention to the entrepreneurs, scientists & technologists building AI & the other technologies transforming our lives. For this special live recording, Isaacson sits down with Suleyman to go inside the ideas, ambitions & decisions driving the AI revolution. From fears about jobs & misinformation to the existential question of whether superintelligent machines could one day threaten humanity itself, the stakes can feel almost impossibly high. What does it mean to build technology with the power to reshape society? Who gets to decide where it takes us? Hear two singular thinkers explore the promise, power & profound questions of the AI age & the question at the heart of The Builders: whose imagination do we want to live in?

events.name: Code & Coffee Hackathon
events.description: Everyone's a builder here: coders, PMs, designers, & the just-curious.Get ready to build something real for Newark! We're taking over Rutgers iHub for a full-day hackathon focused on solving problems that actually matter to the people who call this city home, from water safety to food access to just making city government easier to navigate.Theme:Description:This hackathon challenges participants to pick a real issue facing Newark & build something that actually helps: a tool, an assistant, a dashboard, whatever gets the job done. Teams can dig into problem areas like environmental & water justice, food access, cost of living, or civic transparency, or bring their own idea if they see a sharper angle. Expect AI to play a role in your build, but what we're really looking for is a solution that works. Judging will weigh usefulness & execution as heavily as technical approach.Technical Scope:Participants can use any technical stack they prefer (code-based, no-code, or a mix)Projects must be built from scratch during the hackathon, no prebuilt solutionsTeams are free to choose one of our suggested problem areas or pitch their own. We'll share a few starting points at kickoff, but the direction is yoursJudging Criteria:Relevance & Impact: Does this solve a real, specific problem for Newark residents, & could someone actually use it?Execution: How complete & functional is the prototype, given the short build window?Thoughtful AI Use: How & why did you use AI? A simple, well-executed approach counts; bonus points for teams who push further with multi-step reasoning or tool use where it genuinely fits the problem.Usability & Creativity: Would a non-technical resident actually get it? Does the approach show real originality?Pitch & Clarity: Can you clearly explain the problem, the solution, & who it's for in your demo?Agenda:10:00  10:30 AM | Check-in & NetworkingRegistration, coffee/light breakfast, casual networking10:30  11:00 AM | Welcome & Opening RemarksTheme & judging criteria overview11:00  11:30 AM | Team Formation & Idea PitchesParticipants pitch project ideas, team matchmaking session11:30 AM  4:00 PM | Hacking SessionTeams build prototypes, mentors available for tech & business guidance, lunch break at 1:00 PM4:00  5:00 PM | Project Demos & Pitches35 minute demos from each team, judged by partners & industry reps5:00  5:30 PM | Awards & Closing RemarksWinners announced, closing remarks5:30  6:00 PM | Networking & Wrap-UpInformal mingling with participants, judges, & partners

events.name: Plug & Play x PMAI: Pitching Masterclass III
events.description: IT IS BACK! CALLING ALL FOUNDERS! Hosted by Plug & Play NYC & Pioneering Minds AI Apply to pitch here:https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScOGgbEqUmtEHmKrhqpzynRzYX4Lk4EUC8qrYvSt6YZhXrGvg Pitching is one of the most important skills a founder develops, yet it's rarely practiced in a setting where you can iterate in real time. In this interactive workshop, founders will present their pitch, receive direct feedback, & immediately refine it live. This is a hands-on pitch masterclass where builders learn by doing, & by watching other founders sharpen their story. For founders, few people have a better perspective on how to communicate complex technology simply & convincingly. In this session, Anthony & Anna will work directly with founders in a live pitch lab, helping them sharpen their narrative & strengthen how they present their ideas. Come have a sales pitch, demo pitch, or even a VC pitch! Anthony RoseAnthony Rose is a pioneering technology entrepreneur best known as the co-creator & former CTO of the BBC iPlayer, one of the world's first large-scale streaming platforms that fundamentally changed how millions consume television. He has spent decades building technology at the intersection of consumer platforms, developer ecosystems, & emerging tech. His experience spans founding companies, leading engineering teams, & scaling global products. Nate HinmanNate Hinman is Senior Director at Plug & Play Tech Center. He works closely with startups, corporate partners, & investors to identify promising companies, accelerate growth, & create opportunities for founders to connect with some of the world's leading organizations. With extensive experience across Plug & Play's enterprise technology & AI ecosystem, Nate has seen hundreds of startups present, position, & refine their businesses. At this Pitch Masterclass, he will share an investor & accelerator perspective on what makes a pitch stand out, common mistakes founders make, & how to communicate a startup's story with greater clarity & impact. Workshop Format: Live Pitch Master Class 4-5 selected founders will pitch their startup & iterate live with Anthony. Each founder will go through the following format:  5-minute pitch 5 minutes of feedback 2-minute revised pitch incorporating feedback Watching this process unfold live helps everyone in the room see how small narrative adjustments can dramatically improve clarity, persuasion, & impact. Agenda:6:00 p.m. - Doors open6:25 p.m. - Pitches begin & live workshop7:30 p.m. - Networking session Who Should Attend This event is designed for:  AI founders preparing to raise funding Builders refining how they communicate their product Early-stage startups preparing for demo days or investor meetings Anyone interested in how strong startup narratives are built Apply to Pitch We will select 4-5 founders from the community to present during the session. If you would like to pitch your startup & receive live feedback, apply at this link! Selected founders will be notified ahead of the event. About Plug & PlayPlug & Play is the leading innovation platform, connecting startups, corporations, venture capital firms, universities, & government agencies. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, we're present in 60+ locations across 25+ industries. We offer corporate innovation programs, helping our partners in every stage of their innovation journey, from education to execution. We also run startup acceleration programs & have built an in-house VC where we've invested in hundreds of successful companies including Dropbox, Guardant Health, Honey, Lending Club, N26, PayPal, & Rappi. For more information, visit Plug & Play. About SeedLegalsSeedLegals is your full-stack legal platform from incorporation to Series A & beyond. Whether you're just starting out or gearing up for your next raise, SeedLegals is built to help founders move faster & smarter. Our tools make it simple to create & sign essential legal docs, close funding rounds, & reward your team - without burning time or cash on admin. There are over 50,000 startups on SeedLegals. If you're looking to incorporate, convert your to a C Corp, do a SAFE or a priced round, or manage your cap table, head over to SeedLegals, we're here to help you get there faster. About PRIMARYWelcome to PRIMARY, where 50,000 square feet of thoughtfully designed private & community spaces redefine coworking in downtown NYC. As the largest coworking space in FiDi, we combine premium private offices, shared workspaces, & an exclusive Lounge with top-tier amenities & exceptional service, creating the ultimate environment for your business to thrive. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: Agentic Security - BSides NYC Week
events.description: Agentic Security NYC is a practitioner-only gathering for security engineers & leaders actually running AI agents in production not a conference, not a panel, & not a place to pitch a product. We ran the first one in August. This one lands during BSidesNYC week. The format: a small room, real conversation, no slides. We pose a handful of hard questions & let practitioners argue them out: what actually broke, who in your org has the authority to say no to an agent going to production, whether you could actually prove what an agent did last week if you had to, where your own line on autonomy really sits. Rules of the room: Chatham House - share the ideas afterward, not who said what No vendor pitches, from us or anyone else Practitioners only If you're building or defending AI agents in production: security engineering, AppSec, ProdSec, InfraSec, AI governance & this is genuinely on your mind, request an invite. Space is limited.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Reality Of Data Centers In Space
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a small, curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for.Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data. No talking, just thinking. 45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: The Reality of Data Centers in SpaceStarcloud just raised $250M to build satellites that run AI workloads in orbit, joining Google's "Project Suncatcher" & a SpaceX effort in a race to solve AI's power problem by moving compute off the planet entirely. The pitch is compelling - unlimited solar power, no water usage - but basic questions about heat dissipation, launch costs, & maintenance remain mostly unanswered. We're decoding: Is space-based computing a real solution to AI's real estate & energy issues? Supporting questions: What would actually have to be true for orbital data centers to beat a terrestrial one on cost? Who's positioned to win this race - the well-funded startups (Starcloud), or the hyperscalers who already have the capital & infrastructure (Google, SpaceX)? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like.

events.name: AI Founders Supper Club
events.description: Hi fellow founders  Angela & Hamza here from the AI Furnace. The AI Founders Supper Club is a private founders dinner club hosted by The AI Furnace (the largest community of AI startups in the world). Once a month, we host 15-20 early stage AI founders for a night of delicious food, discussions & connections with curated high quality founders in NYC. This is a referral based network, so feel free to apply here but the other way to get in is by being referred in by an existing founder member. What to expect: A 3-course meal, courtesy of our partners Meet dope founders building out of NYC Real conversations & place to vibe with other founders, solving similar problems ABOUT OUR HOSTS & SPONSORS The AI Furnace is NYC's largest & most active AI community. It was started by AI founders, Angela Mascarenas & Hamza Zaveri, who were based in NYC & London & started the org to support fellow AI founders & operators building in local cities outside of Cerebral Valley (San Francisco). It has since grown to a global community of 20,000 AI founders, operators & researchers & has since organized events in 4 countries & 7 cities including NYC, London, Paris, Dubai, Boston, DC, & Philly. Fidelity Private Shares brings certainty to startup founders with their cap table platform to help automate equity management operations & financings in a single collaborative hub. Leverage the scenario modeling tool & secure data room to prepare for the next round of funding. From inception to IPO, Fidelity has the expertise & robust support to help guide you. Connect with Charlie Stephens for more information. PwC's Emerging Company Solutions (ECS) practice is the leading provider of audit, tax, & IPO readiness services to companies backed by venture capital (VC) & private equity (PE) firms. More specifically, PwC's ECS practice has the greatest market share & is the #1 provider of audits of technology, software, & media company IPOs amongst the Big 4 accounting firms since 2017. Whether it be in connection with a Series A capital raise, a later-stage VC or PE firm investment, leading up to, during & subsequent to an IPO, PwC's ECS practice is uniquely positioned to be with you every step of the way, helping you achieve your business goals while minimizing risk. Niural is an AI-native, end-to-end HR & finance platform transforming global payroll, PEO, & compliance. Powered by EMMA, our intelligent AI coworker, Niural brings payroll, HR, & finance into a single, streamlined ecosystem. From automated payroll & HR workflows to global compliance across multiple jurisdictions-including support for both fiat & crypto payments-Niural helps companies scale with confidence. We make global operations smarter, faster, & more efficient. Ramp is an all-in-one financial operations platform designed to save businesses time & money. Combining corporate cards, expense management, bill payments, accounting automation, procurement, travel, treasury, & more, Ramp empowers finance teams to do their best work. More than 70,000 companies, from family-owned farms to space startups, have saved $10B & 27.5M hours with Ramp since its founding in 2019. Investors include Founders Fund, Thrive Capital, Khosla Ventures, Sequoia, Greylock, Stripe, Goldman Sachs, Coatue, & Redpoint, as well as over 100 angel investors who were founders or executives of leading companies.

events.name: Peptide Freedom vs Proof First
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In partnership with Pepper NYC & the Peptide Club of NYC A peptide to heal your tendon. An injection to rebuild your knee. Exosomes to make your body younger. Regenerative medicine is moving fast, & consumers increasingly don't want to wait ten years for the clinical trials to catch up (the AIDS crisis..). Some of these treatments have real science behind them. Others have promising early evidence. And some are being sold for thousands of dollars long before anyone can say with confidence that they actually work. But maybe that's the point. We let adults make risky decisions everywhere else. If a patient understands the evidence is uncertain, why shouldn't they be allowed to spend their own money trying something experimental? The alternative is the basic bargain medicine has relied on for decades: prove it works before you sell it. Because when the person explaining the risks is also making money from the treatment, "informed consent" can start looking a lot like a sales pitch. So: should experimental regenerative therapies be sold to consumers, or should medicine have to prove they work first? Arguing for, Julius Ritter is the founder of the California Peptide Club & is building infrastructure for the peptide space, from education to real-world outcome data. He argues that the answer to uncertain evidence is more transparency & better data, not keeping adults from making their own choices Arguing against, Dr. Tiana Woolridge is a primary sports medicine physician at Hospital for Special Surgery, double board certified in pediatrics & sports medicine. She's trained in regenerative treatments like PRP herself, which is exactly why she thinks there's a difference between promising medicine & selling something before the evidence is there. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

events.name: AI Engineer Kids Day
events.description: Welcome to our very first AI Engineer Kids Day in New York City. We're thrilled to have you here! This special event brings together curious young minds & their families for a fun, hands-on introduction to artificial intelligence, coding, & technology. We're especially excited to welcome Cassandra Chin, an outstanding computer science graduate & author, who has led engaging workshops at conferences around the world. Cassandra will guide participants through interactive sessions designed to spark creativity, build confidence, & make complex ideas accessible & fun. These workshops are recommended for kids aged 9 to 15, & parents are encouraged to join. Whether you're completely new to AI or already curious about how things work behind the scenes, this is a chance to learn, explore, & create - together! Agenda 12:30 PM - Doors open & registration - Arrive, check in, & get settled. 1:00 PM -  AI Workshop 3:00 PM - Workshop concludes, parents arrive for pickup 3:30 PM - Event ends Workshops Learn AI by Making Games with Phippy!Taught by Cassandra Chin What if you could dream up a game & bring it to life with AI? In this hands-on workshop, kids will team up with an AI coding assistant to create their own playable 2D games using the open source Godot game engine & colorful Phippy & Friends characters. From treasure hunts to tricky mazes, they'll choose the adventure & help shape the rules. As they build, play, & improve their games, kids will practice giving AI clear instructions, checking its work, & solving problems when things don't go as planned. Along the way, they'll discover that AI can help write the code, but they're the game designers in charge! No previous coding or game-making experience is needed, just curiosity & a willingness to experiment, explore, & play! Bio: Cassandra Chin is a keynote speaker, author, podcast host, & computer science student. She has led technology workshops for kids at international conferences since age 13 & is passionate about expanding access to tech education for women, minorities, & underserved communities. What to know before you come:Please bring your own laptop so you can fully participate in the hands-on activities. Space is limited, so if you're unable to attend, please cancel your registration to allow another child to join. We will be taking photos & videos during the event, which will be shared online & featured at the keynote of the AI Engineer World Fair conference that week. Please let us know if you agree to be included in the registration process. Parents or guardians will need to be present to sign their child in at the beginning & sign them out at the end of the event & they welcome to stay & assist your child. No lunch provided, please bring your snack & water Call for Volunteers We're looking for volunteers to support kids during the hands-on workshops. Parents & those with some technical background are invited to help guide & inspire kids as they build & explore. Please register at Open Google Form We can't wait to build with you!

events.name: AI-ndustrial Revolution?
events.description: Companies are spending billions on AI. But is it actually making the economy better? Right now, the evidence is weird. Only 1 in 8 CEOs says AI is both increasing revenue & cutting costs. At the same time, 77% of CEOs say AI has been overhyped so far-but may actually be underhyped over the next decade. So what happens next? A productivity boom that creates new industries & better jobs? Or enormous investment, displaced workers, & technology that never delivers enough value to justify the hype? Daniel Di Martino, an economist & Fellow at the Manhattan Institute, studies economic growth, labor markets, & the policies that drive American competitiveness. Dr. Cecilia Dones is a Columbia lecturer & longtime data & AI executive who works with organizations trying to turn massive AI investments into actual business value. Will AI be a net benefit to the American economy? Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

Hear about what it's like to build & operate at the AI frontier. Whether you're aiming for a top startup after graduation or simply want to learn how the best operators think & work, this is a rare chance to hear it firsthand. Come ready with questions! Meet the speakers: Johnathan Bridges, Founding Marketing @ AntimetalJohnathan recently joined Antimetal as a founding marketer after nearly two years of working in Growth at Tennr. A Stanford grad (and former Class President), he'll talk about choosing a startup, taking on early leadership, & building a brand from zero.About Antimetal: Antimetal is building an autonomous AI system for managing software in production that diagnoses & fixes infrastructure issues so engineering teams can focus on building. Brian Zhou, Engineer @ CognitionBrian graduated from Princeton in May with a degree in Computer Science & now builds AI tools for federal customers at Cognition. His work spans product, ML infrastructure, & forward-deployed engineering. Previously, he wrote Starlink's wifi telemetry system at SpaceX as a founding member of the Aviation team.About Cognition: Cognition is the company behind Devin, the first fully autonomous AI software engineer, & one of the fastest-growing companies in AI coding. Ella Colby, MTS @ RogoElla joined Rogo as a Member of the Technical Staff after graduating from Princeton in May with a degree in Computer Science. Before Rogo, she conducted ML research in Professor Elad Hazan's Google Deepmind research group on AI alignment, spectral transformers, & PDEs, & she completed a software engineering internship at Bloomberg.About Rogo: Rogo is the AI operating system for finance. With a suite of agents purpose-built for Wall Street, it's trained to understand how bankers & investors actually work: from sourcing, diligence & modeling, to turning analysis into deliverables. Its model-agnostic architecture runs the best model for each task, so a firm's intelligence compounds over time. Matt Garcia, Business Operations & Strategy Lead @ TennrMatt works on Business Operations & Strategy at Tennr, contributing across revenue strategy, process optimization, special projects, & more. Matt joined Tennr after 2.5 years at McKinsey. events.description: We can do something about it, actually!Frontier AI companies are relying on the inevitability narrative to push every sector to adopt their techuse their products, or get left behind. events.name: SOSV Deep Tech Summit
events.description: Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. The producers of the Summit are SOSV's Ned Desmond, Ben Joffe, & Norm Amandi. SOSV's mission is to invest in deep tech companies that advance human & planetary health, & embedded in building an 800+ company portfolio with a remarkable array of companies applying AI in the physical world. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

events.name: Propel Demo Day  Innovation In Public Cohort Showcase
events.description: Ten companies. Twelve minutes each. An investor room in New York. Who we are. Propel Earth has run 100+ events & built a network of 36,000+ founders, investors, operators, & service providers across six continents. We are not an events company. We are an outcomes company that happens to use rooms. You bring the intent. We deliver the outcome. Demo Night NYC is the biggest room we have ever run, 26,666 people on the guest list & 35+ investors in the room. This is that format, built for the companies coming out of our cohort & the investors who back them. Every attendee tells us at registration what they are building & who they need to meet. Before doors open we hand you at least one named introduction plus the framing for the conversation. Founders leave with investor conversations, investors leave with deal flow they did not have to source. The night 6:00 Doors, drinks, & your matches are waiting7:00 Ten companies, twelve minutes each, pitch & questions8:15 Room favourite, voted live8:30 Open floor with the investors in the room9:00 Close Tickets General admission, free. Open to founders, investors, operators & anyone building.Present Your Company, 250 dollars. Ten slots only. Stage time in front of an investor room, professional video of your pitch, & your company in the post event send.Title Sponsor, 5,000 dollars. One per Demo Day. Naming rights, logo on all promotion & the photo backdrop, a brand moment from the stage, & the full registrant list within 48 hours.Free for Propel Private Network members. What Propel actually does for you 1  Innovation in Public, our GTM accelerator. For founders who already have a product ready to sell & need go to market: content, distribution, & more sales. Four weeks, twice a week, building in public, closing with a public showcase at Propel Demo Day in front of an investor room. Applications for the next cohort are open at this link. 2  The Propel Private Network. Stop networking. Start getting matched. Every month we personally hand you three introductions chosen for what you need right now - someone who can pay you, hire you, or move your company forward. It works both ways: you go into the pool too. Founding rate $200/mo, first 25 members, locked for life  Claim a founding membership 3  Propel Community Coworking x Wayo Club. Come Wednesday night, then come back Thursday & build. Full workdays at The Wilson with our partner Wayo Club, founded by Jason Malefakis. Wayo is a curated community workspace network where members work from premium venues alongside thoughtfully selected founders, operators, & consultants they can collaborate with, refer, hire, or do business with. Attendees typically report being 1.5 to 2x more productive than working from home or a cafe, & leave with 2 to 3 meaningful connections. Lunch is included. events.name: Silicon Alley Hack | Build Cool Hardware
events.description: Everyone & their grandma is hosting a hackathon. This is the one where you build something physical. Silicon Alley Hack is a one-day, in-person sprint for builders who'd rather solder than ship a vibe-coded app. Microcontrollers. Sensors. Connected devices. Real hardware that runs in the real world & has to work when we plug it in on stage. Application-based. Teams of 4. Every team gets an STM32 development board & peripherals on arrival. Bring your laptop, your wits, & your soldering instincts.  The Problem StatementSoftware ate the world & then got bored. The interesting frontier moved back to atoms - robots that navigate a room, drones that deliver, sensors that make a physical space legible to a machine. All of it runs on constrained silicon, in real time, in places where the cloud is too slow, too far, or not there at all. So that's the terrain: edge intelligence. Machines that sense the world & act on it, on-device.  The Challenge ThemeThe sealed spec will live somewhere in here: Sense  decide  act, running on-device IoT, sensors, & connected devices Physical/digital interaction - things that move, respond, or react Anything that runs on hardware, not just in a browser Constraints you can count on: You'll be working on an STM32 development board & peripherals - get familiar before you show up It has to run live. Slides don't win. Working hardware wins. First team to solve it take the prizes. This is a race, not a showcase.  What to ExpectA live race-to-win challenge dropped at kickoff An STM32 dev kit + peripherals for every team, free 5 hours of focused build time Team formation on-site, or come with your crew Breakfast & lunch provided Exciting prizes for the winning A room full of NYC's hardware people - embedded engineers, drone builders, robotics founders, spatial-data folks  Schedule10:00 - 11:00 AM - Doors open. Breakfast, networking mixer, team formation. 11:00 - 11:30 AM - Partner intros, Root Access demo, challenge drop, rules & judging criteria. 11:30 AM - 4:30 PM - Build sprint. Lunch provided. Clock does not stop. 4:30 - 5:15 PM - Live hardware demos to the judges. 5:15 - 6:00 PM - Photos & Mixer.  PrizesA mix of cash, credits, & perks for the winning team. Sponsors are getting locked in - full breakdown announced before doors.  Who Should AttendEmbedded & firmware engineers Robotics, drone, & hardware builders EE / CE students & anyone who's ever blown up a dev board Founders building physical products Software engineers who want to get their hands on real silicon Anyone curious, ambitious, & hands-on  Sponsors[Sponsor TBD - reach out to somyag00@gmail.com to sponsor]  Hosts & PartnersSomya Gupta - The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Pulse NYC AI - A community, incubator, & venture fund built for founders, researchers, & technologists shaping the future of AI in New York City. ConnNext - A next-gen mobile app & community built for career growth.

events.name: How To Raise Your First Priced Round
events.description: 4 part workshop hosted by Healing Healthtech on "How to Raise Your First Priced Round." Raising your first priced round is a completely different undertaking than stacking safe notes. I want to help you skip the avoidable mistakes.  The diligence is deeper, the relevant terms are completely different, & the stakes for getting it wrong are much higher as priced round investors will almost always take board seats & protective provisions.  I've taught founders how to navigate a priced round for years & on October 27th in NYC will be conducting a public bootcamp / workshop with the highest impact aspects. Location will be the beautiful Gunderson Dettmer NYC offices above Flatiron. Generously sponsored by Jose Rivera & Tonna Obaze of Gunderson Dettmer, Kelly Caviglia of Mercury, & Paul Brezovsky III of Qapita. Session 1: Taught by Ramesh Karra & Paul Brezovsky III's team at Qapita will focus on Data Room. What goes in, what doesn't, what investors are looking for, & how not get get tripped up. Session 2: Taught by Jose Rivera of Gunderson Dettmer will focus on the term sheet negotiation. What terms matter & which don't. How to affect outcomes that are durable & beneficial for your business. Session 3: Taught by me will focused on how to find, pitch, & close priced round investors. Session 4: Will be a panel discussion & fireside chat with 3 partners at NYC VC firms. I've purposely chosen folks who represent software & hardware investors as well as funds that operate outside of healthcare. Mat Kaliski of Acronym Venture CapitalBrian Laung Aoaeh, CFA of REFASHIOND Ventures: The Industrial Transformation FundOwen Willis of Opal Ventures & Primary Venture Partners

events.name: Faith At Work - Christians Working In Big Tech
events.description: Our daily work can be a calling only if it is re-conceived as God's assignment to serve others.  Tim Keller, Every Good Endeavor: Connecting Your Work to God's Work So many of us fool ourselves, believing our work is all about us: What can I accomplish? What do I get from it? Will it give me the money & life that I crave? We're convinced there's a better, different path Christians are meant to consider in how you can show up at work with a sacrificial posture in the tech space. On October 12th, FaithTech NYC is putting a panel together of Christians working in Big Tech companies who've had to work it out on the job, under deadline, with serious consequences. During out time together, we'll unpack: How they make tough decisions based on what the gospel compels us to consider. How they lead & navigate layoffs when they're the one delivering the news. How they talk about Jesus with their co-workers & how you can too. How they think about serving their team in the midst of a work culture obsessed with performance & output. Why their faith has made them better at their job. We'll make some room for your questions at the end. Our hope is that you come away encouraged & inspired to show up different at work the next day. Light food will be provided (donations are appreciated). See you there!

events.name: Future Forum - Science For Society
events.description: The 2026 FUTURE FORUM will convene leaders from diverse backgrounds including academia, museums, journalism, media, public engagement, government, industry, & scientific organizations from the United States & Germany to explore how science can more effectively serve society through communication, collaboration, & public engagement. Centered on the theme Science for Society, the meeting will examine how trust in science is built & sustained, how scientific discoveries & long-term research can be communicated more effectively to diverse audiences, & how institutions can demonstrate the societal value of science. A panel discussion will address the roles of museums, journalists, policymakers, & other non-traditional science communicators; strategies for strengthening public confidence in science & evidence-based decision-making; the importance of open & international scientific collaboration amid increasing geopolitical pressures; & approaches to fostering public engagement, scientific literacy, & global collaboration. Through interdisciplinary dialogue & transatlantic relationship-building, the 2026 FUTURE FORUM aims to develop new partnerships, identify best practices, & strengthen the role of science communication in advancing an informed, engaged, & resilient society. About the FUTURE FORUM The FUTURE FORUM brings together experts from Germany, the United States, & beyond to exchange perspectives on emerging issues in science, innovation, & society. Through focused expert dialogue & public engagement, the format creates space to examine shared challenges, identify new perspectives, & strengthen transatlantic exchange. Previous editions have explored themes including Science Diplomacy in an Era of Technological Disruption at the Science Diplomacy Hub at Johns Hopkins University, Washington, D.C. in 2025. Or Health. Tech. Diplomacy., which focused on global health at the Broad Institute of MIT & Harvard in 2025. In 2026, the FUTURE FORUM returns with Science for Society, bringing together transatlantic experts to explore questions around science communication, public trust, scientific literacy, public engagement, & collaboration across disciplines & borders.

events.name: Agentic AI In The Wild: Open Source Agents In Production
events.description: AI & Open Source Builders Meetup, New York City AI agents are moving into production, & more & more of them are built on open source. The question is no longer whether to use them, but what it takes to make them reliable once the demo is over. This meetup brings together builders, maintainers, & practitioners integrating AI agents into real codebases, CI/CD pipelines, internal developer platforms, cloud native infrastructure, & observability stacks. The evening focuses on the conversations that rarely fit into conference talks: what breaks at scale, how open source tools & standards shape agentic systems, where failure modes hide, & how teams build systems they can trust. Under the theme Open Source in Production, we will explore agentic code review, agent loops in CI/CD, developer platforms, eBPF-powered observability & security, & the role open source communities play in how production AI gets built. No vendor pitches. Just practical lessons from systems running in production. Agenda 5:00 PM Doors Open, Drinks & Networking5:30 PM Welcome & Opening Remarks5:40 PM [Speaker TBD], Qodo Dev Community6:05 PM Break, Food & Networking6:25 PM Panel: Agentic AI in the Wild7:15 PM Ryan Hamilton, Senior Developer & Community Lead, CircleCI AI Lab7:40 PM Closing Remarks7:45 PM Networking until 8:00 PM Speakers & Sessions [Speaker TBD], Qodo[Talk title TBD][Talk abstract TBD] Ryan Hamilton, Senior Developer & Community Lead, CircleCI AI LabOne Take: Engineering Agent Loops That Ship 100% Green PRs on the First PushMost teams optimizing AI-assisted development are focused on the wrong variable: prompting harder, adding rework, dumping larger failure logs into context. The real question isn't how to fix red PRs faster. It's how to stop producing them.Ryan shares findings from three connected Loop Lab experiments, each using the same controlled Snake game benchmark to isolate one variable at a time. Each one reveals something unexpected about where the real leverage lives in an agent loop, & what it means for cutting the cost of agentic development.Together, these experiments map a clear path from "rework is inevitable" to "rework is reserved for the unknowable." The result is a practical harness design that bakes a low Merge Efficiency Ratio (MER, the number of validation cycles it takes to get a change onto main) in from the start, & a new way to think about where validation belongs in the agent loop. Panel: Agentic AI in the WildWhat does it take to move AI agents from proof of concept into systems that operate reliably, & what role does open source play?Practitioners from across the stack will discuss context management, governance, open standards, observability, security, & what changes when agentic systems scale.Expect concrete lessons, not talking points. ModeratorDana Fine, Open Source & Developer Relations Manager, QodoDana leads open source programs & community initiatives at Qodo. She runs the GitHub User Group, CNCF local & GenAI communities, & the Bond AI meetup series. PanelistsBaruch Sadogursky, PortBaruch is a longtime developer advocate & a well-known speaker at developer conferences around the world. He co-authored Liquid Software & DevOps Tools for Java Developers, & focuses on developer productivity, DevOps, & how AI is changing the way software gets built & shipped. [Speaker TBD], Claude Community[Bio TBD] [Speaker TBD], NVIDIA[Bio TBD] Community PartnersAWS User Group NYC, CNCF NYC, Frontend NYC, WeMakeDevs, Bond AI, Qodo Dev Community Join the CommunityQodo Dev Community on Discord: [Discord invite link]Follow us on Meetup: [Meetup group link]

events.name: The AI Founder Playbook, Rewritten
events.description: Invitation only  15 seats  Approval required For leaders of Series A+ startups building proprietary AI models, with a select number of seats reserved for investors. This is a roundtable, not a panel: everyone at the table is welcome to bring opinions. Some of the investors in the room: Merck Global Health Innovation Fund (GHI Fund) Presidio Ventures (Sumitomo Corporation) Morgan Stanley Ventures Lab Description: When AI compresses engineering cycles from months to days, the scarcest thing in a startup is no longer the ability to build. It's knowing what to build, for whom, & how to win when everyone can ship. That shift rewrites the founder's job. Moats move from code to data, distribution, & judgment. Team shapes change. Capital efficiency changes what "venture scale" even means. The playbooks most of us learned are quietly going out of date, & the new ones are being written right now, by the people in rooms like this one. The evening: Dinner & conversation with a curated table of ~15 founders, operators, & investors. Exceptional wines, thoughtfully curated cuisine, & original artwork. Guests will experience a thoughtfully curated progression of refined dishes, premium selections, & seasonal ingredients, accompanied by Cava Brut & Ros, Petit Chablis, & Malbec. The evening concludes with an exclusive dessert pairing & the Signature Cocktail, a bespoke finale to the experience. What we'll get into: What's newly easy, what's suddenly hard, & what that does to the first 18 months of a company Where defensibility actually lives when software is cheap How team composition & hiring change when one builder does the work of five What the next generation of founder playbooks will look like House rules:Off the record. No slides, no pitches, no recording. Come with a point of view.

events.name: Tech Meetup: International Edition
events.description: ATLAS Innovation Exchange @ NY Tech Meetup  x NY Tech Alliance is excited to welcome the 3rd Annual ATLAS Next Program, a special Startup Showcase organized in partnership with ATLAS & its local Landing Pad, the Transatlantic Innovation Hub. Get ready to connect with the next wave of Italian innovation! We're bringing together the NYC Tech Community & a new, selected group of Italian founders building ambitious projects for the future. This year's event highlights the active role of Transatlantic Innovation Hub, a thriving operational center located right here in New York, dedicated to scaling Italian & European startups. Why Attend? Mingle with innovators: network with founders, tech leaders, & ecosystem builders. Discover ground-breaking technologies: get early access to disruptive European & transatlantic solutions. Invest in tomorrow's leaders: evaluate high-potential projects & back the startups you like best. Enjoy Italian focaccia & piadina from PIADI, paired with Mionetto Prosecco. Salute!  Whether you're a founder, investor, technologist, operator, or simply curious about what's emerging next, come meet the people building it! Agenda 6:00 PM - Doors Open & Networking with Italian Aperitivo6:30 PM - Welcome & Startup Demos8:00 PM - Community Ask/Offer8:15 PM - After Party & Networking Demo Lineup AstraTab - A revenue management & premium-access platform for the world's most in-demand venues. Astradyne - High-power satellite platforms designed for orbital computing. Dear.io - An AI-powered personal reflection platform that applies dialogical science to support meaningful interactions & individual well-being. ForLead - A sales intelligence platform that helps companies identify the right prospects at the moment they are most ready to buy. IdolMatch - A platform connecting athletes & brands to create new opportunities for sponsorships, marketing, & monetization. Jyamma GAMES - Crafting fun, culturally-rich gaming experiences that bring Italian folklore literature to life. Math Biology - A non-invasive technology platform supporting prevention, performance, & lifelong well-being. Nadit - A matching platform that connects students with the right academic programs & universities with the right prospective students. Prometheus Plasma Systems - Advanced plasma technologies designed to help turn nuclear fusion into a commercially viable energy source. SKNR - AI-powered skin & scalp pre-screening from a single photo, connecting users with a dermatologist, clinic, or pharmacy the same day. TeamKeys - An AI-native basketball intelligence platform that transforms performance data into actionable insights for scouting, recruitment, & match analysis. Seats are limited - register now to secure your spot! About the NY Tech Meetup The NY Tech Meetup (NYTM) is a signature event of theNY Tech Alliance that has been a monthly staple for the NYC tech ecosystem since 2004. It is the world's largest meetup group of its kind with over 50,000 members who have a common interest in learning from & helping one another. At each event, entrepreneurs, founders, CEOs, & their teams demo cutting edge & transformative tech, answer questions from attendees & network with all in a welcoming & fun-filled space. Since its creation, over 1,200 companies have participated & have been a driving force of innovation & job creation in NYC & the greater NY area. About ATLAS & Transatlantic Innovation Hub ATLAS & its US Hub form a flagship ecosystem dedicated to internationalizing European startups. Headquartered in Rome & rooted in New York City, at 417 5th Ave, the organization delivers hands-on strategic support, market access, & tailored education to help founders establish & grow their presence in the US market.

events.name: Transit Techies #39
events.description: The Center for Urban Science + Progress (CUSP) at NYU Tandon & Transit Techies welcome you to attend two presentations: Phil Cline on Swiftly & Joe Puccio on WalkNYC. Connect with NYU Tandon CUSP & Transit Techies NYC at this talk; attendees are welcome to bring their own food. The event will be held at 370 Jay Street, Brooklyn, NY in Room 1201. We hope to see you there! About the TalksSwiftly Phil Cline will share some of his work on assisting transit agencies with better drawing & dissemination of bus detours at Swiftly WalkNYC In May, Joe created WalkNYC, an app that tracks which blocks you've walked. He built it as a personal project while trying to walk every block in Manhattan. Since launch over 25,000 New Yorkers have started using WalkNYC to stay active & explore the city. About the SpeakersPhil ClineSoftware Engineer, Swiftly Phil Cline is a Brooklyn-based software engineer originally from Toronto who has worked in the transit industry for over 7 years & has a lot of experience with transit data standards like GTFS & GTFS-RT. Joe PuccioCreator, WalkNYC & Founder Coursicle Joe Puccio is a designer & programmer based in NYC. He is the founder of Coursicle, an app used by millions of college students to manage their class schedules & assignments. A central focus of Joe's work is running his companies ethically & building products that are fundamentally beneficial to people's lives. At Coursicle, all employees receive the same salary, & profits are split among employees at the end of each year. Joe graduated from UNC Chapel Hill in 2016 with degrees in Mathematics & Computer Science. He writes about design, technology, & other ideas at joepuccio.com. Vistor InformationPlease visit the NYU Tandon website for directions & a campus map. Advance registration through Luma is required for campus access at NYU for external guests. Attendees who are not current students, faculty, or staff at NYU, including alumni, are asked to register using a personal email address. About CUSP at NYU TandonThe Center for Urban Science + Progress (CUSP) at NYU Tandon is an interdisciplinary center dedicated to applying science, technology, engineering, math, & social sciences to serve urban communities worldwide. Founded as a partnership between NYU & the City of New York, CUSP leads research, educational, & entrepreneurial initiatives that advance the science of cities. By applying novel insights to urban issues, we develop data- & technology-driven approaches that drive positive impact. With an additional focus on training future leaders, CUSP offers interdisciplinary academic programs in applied urban science & informatics for graduate students & professionals. CUSP also engages with stakeholders across city agencies, start-ups, industry players, community-based organizations, & nonprofits to address urgent socioeconomic, environmental, & infrastructural challenges. The center's ultimate objective is to improve urban quality of life by using data to innovate & refine inclusive, equitable, & sustainable practices for cities everywhere. About Transit Techies NYCBringing together the technologists who love transit & the transit enthusiasts who hack! We'll have speakers present transit-related projects. Presenters may be household hackers, data scientists, researchers, product developers, or you! All presentations will be technical & awesome. Follow our calendar to stay up-to-date on our future events! Learn more on our website.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Personal AI Agents, Muse, Instinct & Fight For Your Inbox
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quick research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data.  45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Personal AI agents - Muse, Instinct, & the fight for your inbox Meta's new agent Muse hit #1 on the App Store within 10 days of launch, passing ChatGPT - while a much smaller startup, Instinct, is quietly building a following by working entirely through text message, no app required. Both agents now book things, send emails, & make purchases on your behalf, & both have already run into real trust & privacy controversies. We're decoding: Are personal AI agents actually ready to be trusted with your accounts & money? Supporting questions: What's the real difference between "an agent that acts for you" & "a chatbot that answers you" - & does that difference justify the privacy trade-off? Does Meta's distribution advantage make Muse the inevitable winner, or does Instinct's leaner, invite-only approach have a real shot? What if Google, Apple & others launch personal AI Agents like Muse? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like.

events.description: Latinos x AI Hackathon - NYCSaturday, October 10  10:00 AM - 6:00 PM  New York City Nuestra gente. Nuestros problemas. Nuestro cdigo. For Hispanic Heritage Month, 150 builders are spending one Saturday in New York building AI for the problems our communities actually live with. Not a demo day. Not a panel. Eight hours, three tracks, working software by 5pm. Applications are reviewed. Attendance is free. The Three TracksPick one when you apply. Build for it all day. 01  Immigration - Papers & Process Status, documents, deadlines, & the systems that decide who belongs. Think intake triage for legal aid clinics, plain-language explainers for immigration forms, interpreter tooling, case-status tracking, know-your-rights assistants. 02  Healthcare - Care Without Barriers Language, coverage, & access for patients the system was not built for. Think interpretation at the point of care, insurance navigation, discharge instructions people can actually read, community health worker tooling, prescription & benefits literacy. 03  Finance - Banking the Unbanked Credit, remittances, & building wealth without a financial history. Think remittance transparency, credit-building for thin-file borrowers, small business bookkeeping for cash operations, benefits & tax navigation, fraud protection for first-generation account holders. Prizes$4,500 total - $1,500 per track. Every track winner also gets [sponsor perks once confirmed]. ScheduleSchedule 10:00 AM - Doors, breakfast, team formation10:45 AM - Opening remarks & track briefings11:15 AM - Building starts1:00 PM - Lunch3:00 PM - Mentor office hours & mid-day checkpoint4:45 PM - Submissions close5:00 PM - Demos on stage5:45 PM - Judging & awards6:00 PM - Close Who Should ApplyEngineers, data scientists, & designers who want to ship something real in a day Product people & founders who can shape a problem & pitch it Clinicians, immigration attorneys, paralegals, social workers, & financial counselors - the people who know the problem from the inside. You do not need to code to be valuable here. Teams with a domain expert consistently win. Students & career switchers You can apply solo or with a team of up to four. Solo applicants will be matched at 10:00 AM. What to BringLaptop & charger A problem you have seen up close ID for building security We provide breakfast, lunch, coffee, wifi, power, mentors, & the room. RulesBuild during the event. Prior research & planning are fine; prior code is not. Teams of one to four. Every submission needs a public repo, a two-minute demo video, & a short written description. You keep everything you build. No IP claims from organizers or sponsors. Be decent to each other. Harassment of any kind means you leave. Mentors & Judges[ADD once confirmed: names, titles, organizations.] Partners & Sponsors[ADD once confirmed: logos & names.] Interested in sponsoring or partnering?
