events.name: Sovereign AI At Application Layer - Enterprise, Finance & Data
events.description: An AI Alliance Meetup, co-hosted with Neo4j & IBM | October 7, 2026 | IBM One Madison Avenue, New York Every enterprise now has the same problem in a different form. The data that would make a model useful is the data you are not allowed to move. It sits inside one firm, under one regulator, in a schema few have mapped. The interesting work in AI has quietly shifted from training bigger models alone to developing systems to utilize the data enterprises have. This afternoon is about how that is actually built. Potential topic areas: Context. Structuring the data inside a firm so a model may reason. Federation. Connecting institutions to train & evaluate to move an industry forward. Privacy. The architecture that makes cross-institution work permissible. Regulation. Why banks are now being asked to do this. events.name: An Unmuted Debate - Money In Politics
events.description: IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THOUGHT GALLERY (thoughtgallery.org) DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 Money in Politics, baby! Everyone agrees money runs American politics. The disagreement is whether that's a feature or a disease. In 2010, Citizens United v. FEC held that the government can't ban corporations, unions, or nonprofits from spending money on political speech. The First Amendment, the Court said, doesn't get weaker because the speaker is an organization rather than a person. Fifteen years later, it remains one of the most loved & most loathed decisions in modern constitutional law. For its defenders, the case is a straightforward win for free speech. Political speech is the most protected speech there is, & spending money to spread a message is part of how speech actually reaches people. Let the government decide who's allowed to spend on politics, the argument goes, & you've handed incumbents a tool to silence their critics. The answer to speech you dislike is more speech, not a federal permission slip. For its critics, the case broke American democracy. It opened the floodgates to super PACs & unlimited outside money, & turned elections into auctions where a few hundred families & corporations drown out everyone else. When a sliver of the wealthiest Americans funds the campaigns, candidates listen to them, not to you. That isn't free speech, the argument goes. It's legalized corruption wearing the First Amendment as a costume. One question every voter feels in a democracy that increasingly answers to its donors. Ilya Shapiro is a senior fellow & director of constitutional studies at the Manhattan Institute & has filed more than 500 Supreme Court amicus briefs over his career. The author of Lawless: The Miseducation of America's Elites & Supreme Disorder, he's one of the country's most prominent free-speech-first voices on constitutional law. If you want the case that Citizens United got the First Amendment exactly right, he's your guy. Lawrence Lessig is the Roy L. Furman Professor of Law & Leadership at Harvard Law School & the founder of Equal Citizens. A former Scalia & Posner clerk who turned from copyright law to the fight against money in politics, he wrote Republic, Lost: How Money Corrupts Congress & ran a 2016 presidential campaign built entirely around the issue. He has testified before the Senate against Citizens United & the rise of super PACs, & is currently litigating to push the Court to revisit it. If you want the case that Citizens United corrupted American democracy, he's the person to ask. UNMUTED is a discussion forum for the politically curious. Humor. Tension. Social. Open-minded is the name of the game. Join your people.

events.name: Latinos x AI Hackathon
events.description: Latinos x AI Hackathon - NYCSaturday, October 10  10:00 AM - 6:00 PM  New York City Nuestra gente. Nuestros problemas. Nuestro cdigo. For Hispanic Heritage Month, 150 builders are spending one Saturday in New York building AI for the problems our communities actually live with. Not a demo day. Not a panel. Eight hours, three tracks, working software by 5pm. Applications are reviewed. Attendance is free. The Three TracksPick one when you apply. Build for it all day. 01  Immigration - Papers & Process Status, documents, deadlines, & the systems that decide who belongs. Think intake triage for legal aid clinics, plain-language explainers for immigration forms, interpreter tooling, case-status tracking, know-your-rights assistants. 02  Healthcare - Care Without Barriers Language, coverage, & access for patients the system was not built for. Think interpretation at the point of care, insurance navigation, discharge instructions people can actually read, community health worker tooling, prescription & benefits literacy. 03  Finance - Banking the Unbanked Credit, remittances, & building wealth without a financial history. Think remittance transparency, credit-building for thin-file borrowers, small business bookkeeping for cash operations, benefits & tax navigation, fraud protection for first-generation account holders. Prizes$4,500 total - $1,500 per track. Every track winner also gets [sponsor perks once confirmed]. ScheduleSchedule 10:00 AM - Doors, breakfast, team formation10:45 AM - Opening remarks & track briefings11:15 AM - Building starts1:00 PM - Lunch3:00 PM - Mentor office hours & mid-day checkpoint4:45 PM - Submissions close5:00 PM - Demos on stage5:45 PM - Judging & awards6:00 PM - Close Who Should ApplyEngineers, data scientists, & designers who want to ship something real in a day Product people & founders who can shape a problem & pitch it Clinicians, immigration attorneys, paralegals, social workers, & financial counselors - the people who know the problem from the inside. You do not need to code to be valuable here. Teams with a domain expert consistently win. Students & career switchers You can apply solo or with a team of up to four. Solo applicants will be matched at 10:00 AM. What to BringLaptop & charger A problem you have seen up close ID for building security We provide breakfast, lunch, coffee, wifi, power, mentors, & the room. RulesBuild during the event. Prior research & planning are fine; prior code is not. Teams of one to four. Every submission needs a public repo, a two-minute demo video, & a short written description. You keep everything you build. No IP claims from organizers or sponsors. Be decent to each other. Harassment of any kind means you leave. Mentors & Judges[ADD once confirmed: names, titles, organizations.] Partners & Sponsors[ADD once confirmed: logos & names.] Interested in sponsoring or partnering? Write to chris@ziora-copilot.com or book 30 minutes. Sponsorship closes October 1. FAQIs it free? Yes. Applications are reviewed because space is limited to 150. Where is it? New York City. The exact address is shared with approved attendees. Do I have to be Latino to attend? No. The event is built by & for the Latino community in New York, & everyone who wants to build for these problems is welcome. Do I need a team? No. Come solo & we will match you at the start. What language is the event in? English, with Spanish spoken throughout. Apply & demo in whichever you prefer. Can I keep working on my project afterward? Please do. That is the point. A note on selection: This edition is built for & centered on the Latino community in New York. Applications from Latino & Hispanic builders will be prioritized. Allies are welcome to apply & will be considered as space allows. Questions: chris@ziora-copilot.com Hosted by Christopher Martinez

events.name: AI Engineer Kids Day
events.description: Welcome to our very first AI Engineer Kids Day in New York City. We're thrilled to have you here! This special event brings together curious young minds & their families for a fun, hands-on introduction to artificial intelligence, coding, & technology. We're especially excited to welcome Cassandra Chin, an outstanding computer science graduate & author, who has led engaging workshops at conferences around the world. Cassandra will guide participants through interactive sessions designed to spark creativity, build confidence, & make complex ideas accessible & fun. These workshops are recommended for kids aged 9 to 15, & parents are encouraged to join. Whether you're completely new to AI or already curious about how things work behind the scenes, this is a chance to learn, explore, & create - together! Agenda 12:30 PM - Doors open & registration - Arrive, check in, & get settled. 1:00 PM -  AI Workshop 3:00 PM - Workshop concludes, parents arrive for pickup 3:30 PM - Event ends Workshops Learn AI by Making Games with Phippy!Taught by Cassandra Chin What if you could dream up a game & bring it to life with AI? In this hands-on workshop, kids will team up with an AI coding assistant to create their own playable 2D games using the open source Godot game engine & colorful Phippy & Friends characters. From treasure hunts to tricky mazes, they'll choose the adventure & help shape the rules. As they build, play, & improve their games, kids will practice giving AI clear instructions, checking its work, & solving problems when things don't go as planned. Along the way, they'll discover that AI can help write the code, but they're the game designers in charge! No previous coding or game-making experience is needed, just curiosity & a willingness to experiment, explore, & play! Bio: Cassandra Chin is a keynote speaker, author, podcast host, & computer science student. She has led technology workshops for kids at international conferences since age 13 & is passionate about expanding access to tech education for women, minorities, & underserved communities. What to know before you come:Please bring your own laptop so you can fully participate in the hands-on activities. Space is limited, so if you're unable to attend, please cancel your registration to allow another child to join. We will be taking photos & videos during the event, which will be shared online & featured at the keynote of the AI Engineer World Fair conference that week. Please let us know if you agree to be included in the registration process. Parents or guardians will need to be present to sign their child in at the beginning & sign them out at the end of the event & they welcome to stay & assist your child. No lunch provided, please bring your snack & water Call for Volunteers We're looking for volunteers to support kids during the hands-on workshops. Parents & those with some technical background are invited to help guide & inspire kids as they build & explore. Please register at Open Google Form We can't wait to build with you!

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Let's Talk About Jev
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries - Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quick research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data.  45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Let's Talk About Jev! A tiny AI startup called Jev just went viral for doing the opposite of what every other AI company is doing - it doesn't chat at all. Built by an ex-OpenAI researcher, Jev only returns fast, structured decisions (yes/no, multiple choice, confidence scores) instead of generating text, & it's reportedly fielding funding offers north of $10 billion just over a week after launch. We're decoding: Is Jev a genuinely new category of AI - a faster, cheaper layer sitting underneath the chatbots - or is this hype-cycle enthusiasm for something that's really just a narrow classifier with good marketing? Supporting questions: Does the "specialized model" approach threaten the big general-purpose LLMs, or complement them? What would it take for Jev's $10B valuation talk to actually make sense a year from now? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like. **Refunds available up to 48 hours before the session. After that, we are sorry but the fee is non-refundable.

events.name: Speaking For The Invisible City
events.description: Welcome Kevin Slavin to the Civic Hall stage to present Speaking for the Invisible City! Kevin Slavin makes invisible systems playable, legible, & lately, accountable. This is a thin but discernible through-line in a career across art, design, science, game development, & biotech. Trained in sculpture at Cooper Union under Hans Haacke, Kevin co-founded Area/Code Entertainment, whose pioneering work in location-based games led to acquisition by Zynga. He was recruited to the MIT Media Lab as faculty, where his work on urban metagenomics was exhibited in the context of the Venice Architecture Biennale & at the Storefront for Art & Architecture. His 2011 TED talk on how algorithms shape the world became a frequent reference in understanding the ways that systems change our world, & our experience of the world. Kevin was the founding Chief Science & Technology Officer of The Shed at Hudson Yards, & a co-founding editor of the MIT Press Journal of Design & Science. He spent years in biosecurity between commercial real estate, public health & the intelligence community, & is now co-founder of Fairfield Bio, building a global marketplace for non-human genomic data. He served eight years on the board of Cooper Union, including four years as Vice-Chair. Kevin lives in the Bronx with his wife, daughter, & 14 trees.

events.name: Future Forum - Science For Society
events.description: The 2026 FUTURE FORUM will convene leaders from diverse backgrounds including academia, museums, journalism, media, public engagement, government, industry, & scientific organizations from the United States & Germany to explore how science can more effectively serve society through communication, collaboration, & public engagement. Centered on the theme Science for Society, the meeting will examine how trust in science is built & sustained, how scientific discoveries & long-term research can be communicated more effectively to diverse audiences, & how institutions can demonstrate the societal value of science. A panel discussion will address the roles of museums, journalists, policymakers, & other non-traditional science communicators; strategies for strengthening public confidence in science & evidence-based decision-making; the importance of open & international scientific collaboration amid increasing geopolitical pressures; & approaches to fostering public engagement, scientific literacy, & global collaboration. Through interdisciplinary dialogue & transatlantic relationship-building, the 2026 FUTURE FORUM aims to develop new partnerships, identify best practices, & strengthen the role of science communication in advancing an informed, engaged, & resilient society. About the FUTURE FORUM The FUTURE FORUM brings together experts from Germany, the United States, & beyond to exchange perspectives on emerging issues in science, innovation, & society. Through focused expert dialogue & public engagement, the format creates space to examine shared challenges, identify new perspectives, & strengthen transatlantic exchange. Previous editions have explored themes including Science Diplomacy in an Era of Technological Disruption at the Science Diplomacy Hub at Johns Hopkins University, Washington, D.C. in 2025. Or Health. Tech. Diplomacy., which focused on global health at the Broad Institute of MIT & Harvard in 2025. In 2026, the FUTURE FORUM returns with Science for Society, bringing together transatlantic experts to explore questions around science communication, public trust, scientific literacy, public engagement, & collaboration across disciplines & borders.

All three are current or former members of the Numerai Council of Elders, with the panel moderated by another member of the Council. Tim (aka jefferythewind) (see episode 2) ShatteredX (see episode 3) Jason (see episode 4) More speakers & session details coming soon. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/ Important Note  This is an in-person-only event; there will be no livestream. For security reasons, we must provide a guest list to the security team at least 24 hours before the event. You must provide your  FULL NAME  when registering for this event. If you prefer not to display your full name publicly, please provide it in the final registration question instead. Your full name will be shared only with the security team. About Decentralized AI Days  Decentralized AI Days are community-driven events exploring how open, decentralized AI & Web3 can work together in practice. We bring together engineers, researchers, & builders for a day of technical talks, hands-on workshops, & honest conversation - no hype, no sales pitches, & no pay-to-play. The ecosystem we care about includes projects such as Numerai & CrowdCent. The door is open to anyone building with or curious about decentralized AI. Come for the substance, stay for the community. Call for Presentations  Interested in sharing your experience with our community? Please contact me (Joe) directly via X, or on LinkedIn. I'll get back to you as soon as possible. Everyone is welcome to apply, as long as your talk or workshop topic is relevant. Agenda  More details will be announced soon! Expect a program of tech talks & workshops, followed by a relaxed evening mixer. What to Expect   Connect with a friendly community of AI & Web3 builders, researchers, & curious minds.  Enjoy zero-hype technical talks focused on real problems & practical insights.  Take part in hands-on workshops where you can learn by building.  Watch live demos of decentralized AI & related projects.  Meet the organizers & share your questions & feedback directly.  Explore community resources & connect over food. Who Should Attend)  Decentralized AI Days are for everyone curious about where AI & decentralized systems meet: AI/ML engineers, Web3 developers, researchers, students, & builders at any experience level. If you are new to the space, you are welcome; if you have been building for years, you will find your people here. Come ready to learn, share, & connect. The Venue  Register to see the address. Here are some photos of the venue: Main Room Sponsors  DeAI Day is a community event series sponsored by Numerai & the Numerai Council of Elders. Complimentary refreshments will be provided throughout the day. Come early & grab some cool swags! Code of Conduct  All attendees, speakers, sponsors, & volunteers must agree to the following Code of Conduct. Event organizers will enforce these guidelines throughout the event. We expect full cooperation from everyone to help ensure a welcoming & safe environment for all participants. Our event is committed to providing an inclusive & harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of gender, gender identity or expression, age, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance, body size, race, ethnicity, religion (or lack thereof), or technology preferences. Harassment in any form will not be tolerated. Sexually explicit language or imagery is inappropriate for any part of the event, including talks, workshops, social activities, or online platforms. Participants who violate these rules may be warned or expelled from the event at the discretion of the organizers. Past Events  Materials from past Decentralized AI Days live in the community meetups repository. We have also hosted similar events under a different name (Numerai Community Meetup) from 2022 to 2024: London (July 2022) New York (September 2022) Tokyo (April 2023) Prague (July 2023) Toronto (October 2023) San Francisco (January 2024) Frankfurt (April 2024) Tokyo (July 2024) Bangkok (November 2024) Finally, here's one meme to sum up the vibe.

events.name: Building Internal Community Programs - Ambassadors, Advocates & Beyond
events.description: Building an ambassador program from scratch? Scaling one that's outgrown its original playbook? Join CMX NYC for a moderated panel featuring community professionals who've built & run ambassador & community programs inside some of the industry's leading companies. Learn about what makes these programs thrive, how to measure impact in a way leadership actually cares about, & the challenges of scaling & sustaining momentum over time. Whether you're launching your first ambassador program or leveling up an existing one, you'll leave with practical takeaways from people who've done this work firsthand. Grab a bite, connect with fellow community builders, & stay for open networking after the panel wraps. What to Expect 6:00-6:30 PM: Arrive, connect, & meet fellow community builders & attendees. Light bites & refreshments will be served 6:30-7:30 PM: Panel (45 minutes of facilitated discussion, 15 minutes of open Q&A) 7:30-8:00 PM: Closing reflections + open networking Meet the speakers: Dory Jackson (Moderator): Dory is an NYC-based entertainment journalist with experience at major publications such as Newseek & PEOPLE. Dory is currently building a community of film & television lovers on TikTok & a YouTube interview series with notable celebrities. Darragh Collins: Darragh leads Community & External Communications at Rillet, an AI-native ERP for high-growth tech companies. He's built three B2B communities from the ground up, including Off the Ledger at Airbase, which grew to more than 7,000 finance professionals, the Zip community for procurement leaders, & Close Club at Rillet, a curated, application-only community of 1,200+ finance leaders. Mary Findley: Mary is a community builder based in Brooklyn, NY. She has 15+ years of experience across education, edtech, SaaS, & marketplaces - including Webflow, Miro, Depop, & Skillshare - launching advocacy programs, community challenges, & creator initiatives from the ground up. Currently, she's growing the community at Lovable, where she leads ambassador programming for people across industries, cities, & skill levels. She thrives at the intersection of community, product, & marketing. Paula Rosenberg: Paula Rosenberg has worked in Community for over a decade. She's worked at Quirky, VHX, & Vimeo. She spent the last five years at Stack Overflow, where she was Director of Communities. She's also a writer & a consultant. Outside of work, she's an active member & volunteer of multiple communities including The Old Girls Club, Eat Your Books, & Animal Care Centers in NYC. She is a Yelp Elite member & a Brand Ambassador for Sur La Table. Erica Hanson: Erica has spent 12+ years building communities at Google, FlutterFlow, & outside work. At Google, she led the Google Developer Student Clubs program, scaling it to 2,000 communities across university campuses in 110 countries & reaching 1.8M students annually. She recently joined 645 Ventures as a Fractional Developer Relations & Community Lead, & is the founder of Coffee & Career Transitions NYC, a community for people navigating layoffs & job searches. She spends a lot of time at the playground with her baby & toddler & is training for the NYC marathon. About CMX CMX is a global network of community professionals dedicated to advancing the community industry & empowering communities to thrive. With chapters around the world, CMX fosters local connection & shared learning. Meet the Chapter Leads: Lauren Indovino is a Community & Client Engagement Manager at an education technology startup, with a career dedicated to expanding access to education. Lauren enjoys hosting, running, dogs, live music, travel, & spontaneously exploring NYC! Erica Hanson is a Fractional Developer Relations & Community Lead at 645 Ventures. She has loved building communities for Google & FlutterFlow & outside of work for 12+ years. Erica lived in LA, San Francisco, London, & Singapore before moving to NYC. She enjoys traveling, running, & dancing with her toddler. Kayla Green is a Senior Community Manager at a research technology company with 5 years of building & growing customer communities. Her bread & butter is ambassador programs & helping companies scale their community from 0 to 1. Kayla loves dancing, all things woo woo, & reality TV. About Fabrik: Welcome to Fabrik! We are on a mission to uplift communities & foster serendipitous connections in real life. Fabrik is a home for communities where everyone has a place to belong. With spaces designed to feel more like your living room than your office, Fabrik's social spaces are vibrant hubs where people can come together in real life, explore interests, forge meaningful connections, & build a sense of community.

events.name: Mobility Flow For Techies
events.description: Science meets dance meets yoga! Mobility Flow combines mindful movement patterns with dynamic stretching to help you move better, feel better, & perform better in daily life. This class focuses on improving joint range of motion, muscle flexibility, & movement control through flowing sequences that target common problem areas like hips, shoulders, & spine.  Perfect for desk workers wanting to counteract sitting, or anyone seeking to move more freely & reduce stiffness. Each session incorporates mobility drills & functional movement patterns that will help you build body awareness & develop lasting mobility improvements. You'll leave feeling loose, energized, & more connected to your body.  All levels welcome! Our experienced teachers will provide modifications to match your current mobility level while helping you safely progress. Registration on MindBody (required): https://clients.mindbodyonline.com/classic/mainclass?studioid=5741940&date=10/08/26&fl=true&tabID=7&view=day This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/

events.name: Advertising Week
events.description: Four Days. One Industry. Be Here.For four days, New York becomes the meeting place for the ideas, companies, creators & leaders moving our industry forward. WHAT IS ADVERTISING WEEK?FOUR DAYS THAT MOVE THE INDUSTRY FORWARD.Advertising Week New York isn't just a conference. It's where the entire ecosystem of marketing, media, technology & culture comes together - from global leaders & breakthrough brands to creators, innovators & the people building what comes next. THE PEOPLE SHAPING WHAT'S NEXTTHE INDUSTRY, ALL IN ONE PLACE. CMOs. Creatives. Founders. Media leaders. Technologists. Creators. Agency executives. Cultural voices. Rising talent. Advertising Week brings together the people making the decisions, challenging the status quo & defining where the industry goes next. The conversations you want to be part of - & the people you want to have them with - are here. IDEAS WORTH SHOWING UP FORSEE AROUND THE CORNER. Across hundreds of sessions, Advertising Week explores the forces transforming our industry right now - from AI, creativity & commerce to media, technology, culture & the creator economy. Come for the big ideas. Leave with a clearer picture of what's coming next - & what you're going to do about it. WHERE CONNECTIONS BECOME BUSINESSCOME FOR THE CONTENT, STAY FOR THE PEOPLE. Some of the most important moments at Advertising Week never happen on a stage. They happen over coffee, between sessions, inside a lounge or during a conversation you didn't plan to have. Thousands of industry leaders, partners, clients & collaborators come together in one neighborhood - creating four days where your next meeting, idea, partnership or deal could be five minutes away.

events.name: NY Tech Meetup: International Edition
events.description: ATLAS Innovation Exchange @ NY Tech Meetup   NY Tech Alliance is excited to welcome back our friends from ATLAS in Rome, Italy for another special international edition of the NY Tech Meetup. We're bringing together the NYC tech community & a new group of standout Italian founders building ambitious companies & technologies for the future. It's an opportunity to connect two dynamic tech ecosystems, meet founders you may not otherwise encounter in New York, & build new relationships across the Atlantic. Whether you're a founder, investor, technologist, operator, or simply curious about what's emerging next, come meet the people building it. Come for the demos. Stay for the connections. Agenda 6:00 PM - Doors Open & Networking6:30 PM - Welcome & Demos8:00 PM - Community Ask/Offer8:15 PM - After Party & Networking Demo lineup will be announced soon. Seats are limited - register now to secure your spot! About the NY Tech Meetup The NY Tech Meetup (NYTM) is a signature event of theNY Tech Alliance that has been a monthly staple for the NYC tech ecosystem since 2004. It is the world's largest meetup group of its kind with over 50,000 members who have a common interest in learning from & helping one another. At each event, entrepreneurs, founders, CEOs, & their teams demo cutting edge & transformative tech, answer questions from attendees & network with all in a welcoming & fun-filled space. Since its creation, over 1,200 companies have participated & have been a driving force of innovation & job creation in NYC & the greater NY area. About ATLAS ATLAS is a leading Italian ecosystem supporting the internationalization of startups. Based in Rome & part of Confindustria's innovation network, ATLAS helps founders expand into the U.S. & global markets through education, tools, & strategic support.  Learn more: www.assoatlas.org

events.name: Bridging Adherence Gap - How Can Tech Help People Stay On Their Treatment
events.description: At its core, adherence is a deeply human problem. We know following through with a treatment plan improves our health, but in the moment, taking that immediate next step isn't always easy. The root causes are complex-ranging from forgetfulness & fear of side effects to a lack of visible benefits & high costs. Yet, despite billions of dollars invested in digital health tools, smart devices, & patient support programs, the core statistic remains stubbornly unchanged: roughly 50% of patients still fail to take chronic medications as prescribed over the long term. With rapid shifts in consumer behavior & technology, healthcare companies have unprecedented opportunities to engage with patients.  Join Smart Design as we bring together experts from across the industry to explore how we can apply new technology to the messiness of everyday life & the healthcare system to drive real, lasting health outcomes.

events.name: The AI Founder Playbook, Rewritten
events.description: Invitation only  15 seats  Approval required For leaders of Series A+ startups building proprietary AI models, with a select number of seats reserved for investors. This is a roundtable, not a panel: everyone at the table is welcome to bring opinions. Some of the investors in the room: Merck Global Health Innovation Fund (GHI Fund) Presidio Ventures (Sumitomo Corporation) Morgan Stanley Inclusive Ventures Momentum Partners (Private Equity) United Korean Founders (UKF) Description: When AI compresses engineering cycles from months to days, the scarcest thing in a startup is no longer the ability to build. It's knowing what to build, for whom, & how to win when everyone can ship. That shift rewrites the founder's job. Moats move from code to data, distribution, & judgment. Team shapes change. Capital efficiency changes what "venture scale" even means. The playbooks most of us learned are quietly going out of date, & the new ones are being written right now, by the people in rooms like this one. The evening: Dinner & conversation with a curated table of ~15 founders, operators, & investors. Exceptional wines, thoughtfully curated cuisine, & original artwork. Guests will experience a thoughtfully curated progression of refined dishes, premium selections, & seasonal ingredients, accompanied by Cava Brut & Ros, Petit Chablis, & Malbec. The evening concludes with an exclusive dessert pairing & the Signature Cocktail, a bespoke finale to the experience. What we'll get into: What's newly easy, what's suddenly hard, & what that does to the first 18 months of a company Where defensibility actually lives when software is cheap How team composition & hiring change when one builder does the work of five What the next generation of founder playbooks will look like House rules:Off the record. No slides, no pitches, no recording. Come with a point of view. Trinovation Partners: The "Scale AI" of Venture Backed Startups We are an AI data operations partner for venture-backed teams building computer vision & AI products. We build & run dedicated annotation pods: named, trained teams assigned to your product, not an anonymous crowd. Covering image & video annotation, gold-set calibration, human-in-the-loop QA, & edge-case review. Pods launch in 1-2 weeks, scale with your deployments, & deliver quality you can audit: 500+ annotators deployed, 95%+ QA accuracy, & a 30% model accuracy lift for our clients. Independent & New York-based. Elpis LabsWe work with the government sector & international trade agencies to help their startups find corporate partners in the U.S. The VerticalAn online publication, community platform, & event series focusing on international venture ecosystem.

events.name: UGLY TALK: FAILURE IS KEY TO SUCCESS
events.description: Failure gets talked about like it is part of the journey. That is the lie.The real thing is messier. Missed bets. Wrong hires. Near-breakdowns. The week you stop sleeping and start doing math at 3:00 AM.Founders are expected to eat it quietly and keep moving. No language for what happened. No playbook for what to do next.Ugly Talk is a founder room for the part nobody posts. No fluff. No consultants. Just builders with scars, talking about the call that cost them. Why you should be in this room.Hear what failure cost them. Then hear what they did next.Learn how experienced founders separate self-worth from outcomes when things go sideways.Spot the patterns behind repeat mistakes. And the early signals you should not ignore.Leave with a few concrete moves for the next hard week. Not inspiration.Meet other founders in the thick of it. The ones who are still building. What's on the table.Dare to suck: how permission to fail unlocks real progressThe moment things broke: missed opportunities, wrong turns, near-breakdowns, and what changed afterwardFailure vs identity: separating self-worth from outcomesTreating setbacks as data: what to measure, what to ignore, and how to decide fastRejection as redirection: how founders find the signal in the noHabits for staying focused and resilient when everything feels uncertain Run of show6:00  6:30 PM: Reception (check-in & light drinks)6:30  6:40 PM: Welcome remarks6:40  6:50 PM: Keynote Speech by Ben McKean6:50  7:30 PM: Panel Discussion7:30  7:45 PM: Audience Q&A7:45  8:00 PM: Mixer + snacks and drinks Featured speakers.Ben McKean - Founder & Chief Executive Officer, HungryrootBen McKean is the Founder and CEO of Hungryroot, a personalized healthy eating assistant that uses AI to make meal planning, food shopping, and nutrition effortless and enjoyable. Prior to Hungryroot, Ben was a Vice President and General Manager at Groupon, overseeing their food and beverage business. Ben came to Groupon through the acquisition of Savored, which he founded in 2009. Savored was the nations leading provider of yield management technology to the restaurant industry, used by over two thousand restaurants nationwide and nearly one million diners. Prior to Savored, Ben worked in Merrill Lynchs technology investment banking group. Ben is a graduate of Georgetown University and currently lives in North Carolina with his wife and kids.Stephen McKinney - Founder & CEO, BizbeStephen McKinney is a serial entrepreneur with over a decade of experience across tech, marketing, and logistics. He's the founder and CEO of Bizbe.com, an AI-native business brokerage and lower middle market M&A firm based in New York and Miami. A former contestant on ABC's Shark Tank, Steve previously founded and led Retty Logistics, a seven-figure last-mile delivery company acquired by DXP Logistics and Webster Logistics.Dmitry Koltunov - Founder and CEO, ArborDmitry Koltunov is a serial entrepreneur, technologist, educator, and storyteller. He is the founder and CEO of Arbor, an AI-powered content engine that helps enterprises scale their communications with video and beyond. Previously, he co-founded and served as CTO of ALICE, a hospitality technology company that grew into a global industry leader before being acquired by Expedia Group.Dmitry also leads the New York City chapter of the Startup Leadership Program, New Yorks oldest startup fellowship, whose 500+ alumni have collectively raised more than $1 billion in funding across every industry imaginable. He is passionate about helping founders navigate the challenges of building and scaling companies.Outside of technology, Dmitry is an award-winning songwriter and theater producer currently developing a new musical for Broadway. He holds degrees in Computer Science and Economics from the University of Pennsylvania and is a CFA charterholder.Gwendolyn von Rahn - Co-Founder and CEO, Sweetling HealthGwendolyn von Rahn is the Co-Founder and CEO of Sweetling Health, an postpartum intelligence platform built for at-risk and hard-to-reach populations. Shes a second-time exited founder, an award-winning marketer with over a decade of experience building consumer brands for women, Gwen led creative and brand teams at Vogue, InStyle, and POPSUGAR before founding and scaling a mission-driven consumer brand into Nordstrom distribution that raised over $1M for melanoma research through the Melanoma Research Foundation. She holds a Cornell Johnson MBA and founded Sweetling from her own lived experience with the postpartum care gap. Who's hosting it.Victoria Yampolsky - President, The Startup StationVictoria Yampolsky is the Founder and President of The Startup Station, a strategic CFO advisory firm and financial education platform for startups. She partners with founders on financial strategy, modeling, and fundraising, having supported over 150 companies across 15 industries in raising more than $50M in venture capital. Victoria is also an advocate for female founders and access to capital, and has taught finance to more than 20,000 entrepreneurs through programs including the Bank of America Institute for Womens Entrepreneurship at Cornell. She began her career at Deutsche Bank and Capgemini, and holds a BS in Computer Science from Cornell University and an MBA from Columbia Business School. Who's getting in.Early-stage tech founders and operators navigating uncertainty, setbacks, or the emotional weight of building a company. Expected roles may include:Founders and co-founders (pre-seed to Series A)Operators (COO, Head of Ops, Chief of Staff)Product and Engineering leads building through ambiguityGrowth and GTM leads working through missed targets and pivotsFinance and strategy leaders supporting founder decision-making Who's backing this.The Startup StationThe Startup Station - is a CFO advisory and financial education platform for early-stage startups. We help early-stage founders build investor-ready financials and tell their funding story with confidence. In the past decade, weve helped 150+ founders raise over $50M and educated 20,000+ entrepreneurs worldwide. The Startup Station also runs Speed Pitch, an exclusive investor-founder matchmaking event series for early-stage startups where founders are matched with 3 investors by sector, stage, and check size.Mind Your BusinessEvery attendee will receive a free copy of keynote speaker Ben McKeans Mind Your Business.  Mind Your Business is a practical parable for people rethinking work as AI advances. Set over a four-day retreat, it follows six participants competing for funding to bring one vision to life. As they evaluate six competing proposals, they begin to confront deeper questions about what gives them energy, who they serve, and what they uniquely contribute. Those patterns form what the book calls their Soulcodethe way purpose, belonging, imagination, and courage shape how they work. Told with humor and warmth, the story turns familiar workplace tensions into practical lessons for contributing more deeply, seeing new possibilities, and acting with greater conviction. At its core, the book argues that the opportunity of the AI era isnt doing more workits knowing what work is worth doing.GREY JournalGREY Journal - Media partner spotlighting modern entrepreneurs (featured on Apple News + Google News). events.description: Kick off ElasticON week with the Elastic NYC User Group & Pulumi at our special pre-ElasticON NYC meetup on Tuesday, October 6! Engin Diri from Pulumi & Ines Potier from Elastic will share technical talks, followed by pizza, refreshments, & networking with the New York City tech community.  Continue the experience at ElasticON NYC ElasticON NYC takes place on Thursday, October 8, & registration is free! Connect with Elastic experts & the community, gain hands-on experience, & discover how the Elasticsearch Platform powers real-world AI, search, observability, & security solutions. Register for ElasticON NYC here  Date: Tuesday, October 6th from 6:00-8:00 PM  Location: Elastic NYC Office1250 Broadway, Floor 16, Training RoomNew York, NY 10001  Want to present at our next meetup?Are you interested in presenting your Elastic use case? We welcome 5-10 minute lightning talks, 45-minute deep dives, & everything in between. If you're interested, please send us an email at meetups@elastic.co. Agenda: 6:00 pm: Doors open; say hi & eat some food 6:30 pm: Give Your Coding Agent an (Elastic) Memory - Engin Diri (Pulumi) 7:10 pm: Stateless vs stateful: Learn how the stateful architecture was transformed into stateless for Serverless & why Ines Potier (Sr. Software Engineer at Elastic) 7:30 - 8:00 pm: Networking & event wrap-up  Talk Details:Give Your Coding Agent an (Elastic) Memory - Engin Diri (Pulumi)If you work with a coding agent every day, you know the routine. Each new session starts blank: the agent re-reads files it read yesterday, asks about decisions you settled last week, & redoes debugging you already finished. Its only memory is the context window, & that empties every time you close your laptop. Claude Code ships a built-in fix: markdown notes the agent writes for itself & reads back at the next session start. It helps, but the notes live on one machine, there is no real search, & anything past the first page of the index gets dropped. agent-memory, an open source project based on Elastic, takes the same idea further: memory lives in Elasticsearch, where decisions, tasks, & session history are searchable & shared across machines. I'll run both side by side, kill an agent mid-task, & show how much more a fresh one remembers when its memory is a search engine instead of a text file. And here comes Pulumi: one command creates everything in Elastic Cloud, it lives in a repo you can review, & every teammate gets an identical memory backend instead of their own snowflake. No promises about becoming a 1000x AI engineer, but your agent will stop asking you the same question twice. Stateless vs stateful: Learn how the stateful architecture was transformed into stateless for Serverless & why Ines Potier (Sr. Software Engineer at Elastic) Details coming soon!

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Personal AI Agents, Muse, Instinct & Fight For Your Inbox
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quick research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data.  45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Personal AI agents - Muse, Instinct, & the fight for your inbox Meta's new agent Muse hit #1 on the App Store within 10 days of launch, passing ChatGPT - while a much smaller startup, Instinct, is quietly building a following by working entirely through text message, no app required. Both agents now book things, send emails, & make purchases on your behalf, & both have already run into real trust & privacy controversies. We're decoding: Are personal AI agents actually ready to be trusted with your accounts & money? Supporting questions: What's the real difference between "an agent that acts for you" & "a chatbot that answers you" - & does that difference justify the privacy trade-off? Does Meta's distribution advantage make Muse the inevitable winner, or does Instinct's leaner, invite-only approach have a real shot? What if Google, Apple & others launch personal AI Agents like Muse? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like. **Refunds available up to 48 hours before the session. After that, we are sorry but the fee is non-refundable.

My thesis for 2026-2027 events is to distill the highest-impact parts of those programs away from the noise & pageantry into short, intensive workshops open to any founder willing to commit the time in participating. -V] By signing up you agree to subscribe to both Healing Healthtech, a monthly Substack of in-person NYC digital health events as well as interviews & deep dives with builders, investors, clinicians, & operators seeking to better the human condition as well as periodic outreach from our sponsors. About Qapita Qapita provides cap table management, valuations & ESOP administration for startups building & working anywhere in the world. events.name: AI Fraud & Death Of Resume - Restoring Algorithmic Trust
events.description: Conquer the AI job market battleground with elite CISO Dr. Rachel Levitch. Learn to restore algorithmic trust & secure your pipeline!  The 2026 job market is facing an unprecedented security & operational crisis. The recruitment landscape has evolved from a standard talent search into a high-stakes battleground of synthetic data. Candidates are deploying advanced, hyper-automated AI agents to mass-apply to hundreds of open roles instantly, reverse-engineer corporate Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS), auto-generate perfect skill matches, & deploy deepfake technology to bypass initial technical screenings. HR departments & engineering teams are drowning in a sea of algorithmic noise. As talent pipelines become flooded with AI-polished fraud, a staggering percentage of enterprise managers report that total trust in the inbound pipeline has completely eroded. In this high-stakes security & talent briefing, Dr. Rachel Levitch-seasoned Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) & founder of the Cognitive Institute-shifts the conversation from simple recruitment metrics to hard-line Systems Security & Information Integrity. We will move beyond the traditional interview structure to explore the mechanics of modern algorithmic fraud, the vulnerabilities of automated screening systems, & the implementation of secure identity & skill verification frameworks. This session provides human resource executives, tech founders, & venture capitalists with the exact tactical roadmap required to bypass synthetic candidate noise, protect personal data privacy, & restore institutional trust in a market-led crisis. Key Takeaways for Attendees: The AI Vulnerability Audit: A live technical breakdown of how 2026 AI-auto-apply bots actively breach, manipulate, & exploit corporate ATS filters.Detecting the Synthetic Candidate: Concrete, practical strategies for talent acquisition teams to identify AI-forged certifications, deepfake video setups, & automated resume stuffing.Rebuilding the Trust Chain: Transitioning your organization toward zero-trust recruitment frameworks, secure identity verification, & authentic human-sustainability metrics. Purchase Tickets At URL Below or See All Events here: https://www.eventbrite.com/o/121452823948

events.name: Sampura Research Talk & Lunch
events.description: Sampura Research: Hill-climbing Alignment using Humans Sampura Research is a London-based nonprofit, founded by Google DeepMind alumni, building Human-AI Complementarity for AI alignment. As AI systems grow more capable, the judges we use to train, evaluate & monitor them increasingly fall short. Most of the field responds by replacing humans with LLM judges; we think humans & AIs have complementary strengths, & that human oversight is an uncorrelated layer of defence that AI-only judges can't provide. events.description: Invitation only  15 seats  Approval required For leaders of Series A+ startups building proprietary AI models, with a select number of seats reserved for investors. This is a roundtable, not a panel: everyone at the table is welcome to bring opinions. Some of the investors in the room: Merck Global Health Innovation Fund (GHI Fund) Presidio Ventures (Sumitomo Corporation) Morgan Stanley Ventures Lab Description: When AI compresses engineering cycles from months to days, the scarcest thing in a startup is no longer the ability to build. It's knowing what to build, for whom, & how to win when everyone can ship. That shift rewrites the founder's job. Moats move from code to data, distribution, & judgment. Team shapes change. No slides, no pitches, no recording. Come with a point of view.

events.name: Jev Demo Day
events.description: Jev Demo Day: show us what you've been tinkering with. Before LinkedIn finds Jev, join us for a demo day focused on anything built with Typesafe AI's new shiny Jev model, the System One model that made classifier models cool again.Jev launched two weeks ago, so nobody has a finished product yet, & that is the point. Work-in-progress is not just allowed, it is encouraged. Half-working prototypes, weird experiments, dead ends, benchmarks, & here is what I learned talks are all welcome.Part demo day, part unconference. Five-minute demos, hot takes, half broken projects, burning opinions on the main stage. No demo? Grab a slot anyway & talk about what you tried with Jev, what surprised you, or where it broke. Sponsors & venue to be announced. Space is strictly limited & we will be screening attendance.  Apply now for an evening of hands-on demos & talks & connect with a community of active builders! Participate by presenting your own work, or just share ideas with like-minded people. RSVP in the form above  What is AI Tinkerers?AI Tinkerers is a meetup exclusively for practitioners with technical, machine learning, & entrepreneurial backgrounds who are actively building & working with foundation models, such as large language models (LLMs) & generative AI. If you're deeply passionate about creating LLM-enabled applications, have hands-on experience in building such systems, & want to connect with like-minded people who share your level of commitment, then this group is the perfect fit for you. With AI Tinkerers meetings happening in many cities, we support a dedicated global community. Who is this for?We are AI Tinkerers. The core essence of AI Tinkerers is active collaboration around early-stage discovery & innovation, which requires a high degree of experimentation, vulnerability, openness to sharing challenges & learnings, & collaboration among individuals with a shared level of expertise. This unique environment allows us to embrace experimentation, foster an atmosphere of trust & innovation, & create world-changing solutions.  Read more in the FAQ Some slots still available, submit your demo!   Demo SubmissionsBuilt something with Jev, or tried to? This is your moment to share it with people who will actually get it. The format is part demo day, part unconference. A demo or talk is about five minutes in length & demonstrates a work in progress or shares lessons learned, followed by Q&A & discussion with the community (this is the best part!) Ideas for what to bring: A routing layer that decides code vs LLM vs humanTool-call gating for an agentJev as a judge or jurorA System One vs System Two bake-off against Claude or GPT on the same decisionLatency experimentsAnything through OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, Cloudflare, LangChain, or Langfuse FILL OUT THE DEMO SUBMISSION FORM HERE  Pitch decks are not allowed - we want to see your work in progress, no matter how messy! Read What Makes a Great Demo at AI Tinkerers Please note that capacity is limited, so we'll prioritize those who are able to present a demo or talk. Event Schedule6:00 Doors open, networking & pizza.7:00 Opening remarks from AI Tinkerers7:15 Demos~8:15 Open floor / unconference9:00 Doors Close

events.name: The Age Of AI  - Live Recording Of The Builders
events.description: Bestselling biographer Walter Isaacson joins us for a live recording of the first episode of his brand-new podcast, The Builders, with Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of Microsoft AI & one of the most influential thinkers & leaders working in artificial intelligence today. AI is reshaping our world at breathtaking speed. But behind the technology, real human beings are making choices about what our future will look like, how we'll work & live, & whose vision will shape what comes next. And as AI grows more powerful, so does the unease surrounding it. Will it usher in an era of extraordinary human possibility - or are we building something we may ultimately struggle to control? On The Builders, Walter Isaacson talks to the entrepreneurs, scientists & technologists building AI & other technologies that are rapidly reshaping our world to get inside the thinking of some of the most consequential figures of our time. Throughout his career, Isaacson has been fascinated by the people who change the world - from Leonardo da Vinci & Albert Einstein to Steve Jobs, Jennifer Doudna & Elon Musk. With The Builders, he turns his attention to the entrepreneurs, scientists & technologists building AI & the other technologies transforming our lives. For this special live recording, Isaacson sits down with Suleyman to go inside the ideas, ambitions & decisions driving the AI revolution. From fears about jobs & misinformation to the existential question of whether superintelligent machines could one day threaten humanity itself, the stakes can feel almost impossibly high. What does it mean to build technology with the power to reshape society? Who gets to decide where it takes us? Hear two singular thinkers explore the promise, power & profound questions of the AI age & the question at the heart of The Builders: whose imagination do we want to live in?

events.name: Teaching America - Screening & Discussion
events.description: Join Anew & Anthem of us for a very special screening & discussion of the student-led movement to accurately teach our country's history.Teaching America honors the high school students & teachers who join forces to stand up for African-American studies, after the state of Arkansas threatens to shut their classes down. The in-classroom testimony of a movement sparked by the unflinching desire to learn that crosses boundaries & generations  in a time of intentional efforts to segregate & divide & to forcibly erase Americas history, culture, & humanity.The film provides a lens & a point of intervention into the larger attacks on education & learning as a core chapter in the authoritarian playbook. There is a clear throughline between the efforts to limit & erase the teaching of history; the banning of books, curriculum & classes; the intentional push to segregate & divide; & the limitations being placed on free & open inquiry, expression, & teaching in K-12 & higher education.The screening will start at 5:30pm, followed by a conversation.Anurima Bhargava (Director/Producer, Teaching America): CEO of Anthem of Us, a strategic advisory & consulting firm that centers dignity, justice, & belonging in schools, workplaces & communities.  Anurima previously led federal civil rights enforcement in schools, colleges & universities at the U.S. Department of Justice & directed the education practice at the NAACP Legal Defense Fund.  She also served as Chair & Commissioner of the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom.  Anurima has advised & produced numerous documentary films & projects; including the Oscar-nominated & Peabody Winner Writing With Fire; Peabody Winner While We Watched; Emmy-nominated Our Body Politic, Patang, A Shot At History, The Inquisitor, & the docuseries The Vow.  Anurima chairs the U.S. Board of Doc Society & serves on the capacity council for Brown Girls Doc Mafia.Vanessa Liu (Host/Discussant): Co-Founder & CEO, Sugarwork; Board of Overseers, HarvardUniversityEleonora Sharef Moreno (Host/Discussant):  Head of Philanthropy, Mercer PartnersAnew is a gathering space & discovery center for social transformation located in NYC. Get Hired Hack is a one-day, in-person hackathon at Columbia Startup Lab where NYC's fastest-growing startups bring real problems from their roadmaps, & you show them what working with you looks like. Founders who are hiring will be in the room, watching you build. events.description: Sales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). events.name: Zenity AI Agent Security Summit
events.description: Shape the Future of AI Security AI agents are no longer novelties for future consideration - they're scaling across industries & borders at breakneck pace today, bringing with them a security landscape that grows continuously ambiguous. Don't just witness the conversation around agentic security - contribute to it. The AI Agent Security Summit returns to four international cities in 2026. Save your spot now. What You'll LearnWith AI agents becoming integral to many workflows, they introduce unprecedented challenges. This summit navigates the uncharted territories of AI agents with discussions around:  Real RisksLearn how attackers exploit AI Agents & what you need to change in your security strategy to stay ahead.  Deconstructing AI AgentsDive deep into adversarial tactics, prompt manipulation, & unintended behaviors that can turn trusted systems into threats.  Defense Beyond the PerimeterDiscover new defense methods that monitor behavior, detect deviations in intent, & break malicious automation. After launching the AI Agent Security Summit in New York City & San Francisco in 2025, we're taking the Summit global - expanding to NYC, San Francisco, London, & Asia. Each Summit will feature local speakers, fresh content, & original research highlighting emerging vulnerabilities & attack pathways in AI agents. We invite researchers & practitioners to share new findings, tools, & firsthand experiences exploring the security challenges & risks that emerge as AI agents are developed & adopted in enterprise environments.

events.name: Faith at Work: A Conversation with Christians Working In Big Tech
events.description: Our daily work can be a calling only if it is re-conceived as God's assignment to serve others.  Tim Keller, Every Good Endeavor: Connecting Your Work to God's Work So many of us fool ourselves, believing our work is all about us: What can I accomplish? What do I get from it? Will it give me the money & life that I crave? We're convinced there's a better, different path Christians are meant to consider in how you can show up at work with a sacrificial posture in the tech space. On October 12th, FaithTech NYC is putting a panel together of Christians working in Big Tech companies who've had to work it out on the job, under deadline, with serious consequences. During out time together, we'll unpack: How they make tough decisions based on what the gospel compels us to consider. How they lead & navigate layoffs when they're the one delivering the news. How they talk about Jesus with their co-workers & how you can too. How they think about serving their team in the midst of a work culture obsessed with performance & output. Why their faith has made them better at their job. We'll make some room for your questions at the end. Our hope is that you come away encouraged & inspired to show up different at work the next day. Light food will be provided (donations are appreciated). See you there!

events.name: Hack For Impact - AI Workflow Hackathon
events.description: Pioneering Minds AI: Hack for ImpactAn AI Workflow HackathonDont just use AI. Redesign how work gets done.AI is changing how we research, learn, build products, analyze contracts, manage money, & make decisions. But adding a chatbot to an existing process is not the same as building an AI-native workflow.The real opportunity is to rethink the workflow itself:What should humans still do?What should AI handle?What can be automated entirely?And where does human judgment become even more important?This is a one-day hackathon where participants redesign real-world workflows using AI.Teams will choose a problem from one of four tracks, identify a broken or inefficient workflow, & build an AI-native product, agent, or system that makes it dramatically better.You do not need to arrive with a startup idea.Come with curiosity. Find a problem. Build something.The winning teams can also secure their spot at our upcoming Pitching Masterclass, where they can sharpen their story, product positioning, & pitch.The ChallengeTeams will identify an existing workflow & redesign it for the age of AI.Your project should answer three questions:What is broken, slow, repetitive, or unnecessarily difficult today?What should AI do differently?What does the new workflow look like when AI is built into it from the beginning?Projects can take the form of an AI agent, internal tool, workflow automation, consumer product, enterprise application, or prototype.Hackathon TracksParticipants may choose one of four tracks.Critical Thinking & LearningAI can produce answers in seconds. But getting an answer is not the same as understanding something. As AI becomes capable of performing more cognitive tasks, skills such as critical thinking, judgment, curiosity, problem decomposition, & learning how to learn may become even more important. Build a product or workflow that uses AI to help people think better rather than simply think less.AI for Product Management WorkflowsProduct managers spend enormous amounts of time gathering information, coordinating teams, analyzing feedback, writing documents, prioritizing ideas, & turning ambiguity into decisions.Many of these workflows were designed before AI existed. Redesign them.Legal Tech WorkflowsLegal work is full of complex, document-heavy processes where accuracy, judgment, & context matter.AI creates an opportunity to fundamentally rethink how legal professionals research, review, draft, analyze, & manage information.They must also consider accuracy, explainability, accountability, & human review.Fintech & Insurtech WorkflowsFinancial services & insurance involve some of the most complex workflows in business: underwriting, compliance, risk assessment, fraud detection, claims, financial analysis, & customer onboarding.Many still involve fragmented systems, repetitive manual review, & enormous amounts of unstructured data.What You'll BuildTeams will have one day to identify a problem, design a solution, build a prototype, & present it to our judges.Your prototype does not need to be production-ready.We care about:The quality of the problemHow thoughtfully you redesign the workflowHow meaningfully AI improves the processThe usability of your prototypeWhether someone would actually use itAll backgrounds are welcome.You do not need to be an engineer to participate.Product managers, designers, lawyers, finance events.description: Topic: Emerging, Non-obvious Needs for Industry in the Midst of Accelerating Climate Change.    Speaker: Naveen Krishnamurthy, SVP Executive Programs Lux Research Date: Monday October 5, 2026. Time: 5 pm. Online. KINDLY REGISTER TO ATTEND The recent fires in Southern Europe & France were a major reminder that climate change is not merely a weather risk, buried in sustainability reports. The fires hurt tourism, wine making & other agro-industries, electricity, transportation & supply chains. In France, more than 120,000 workers were temporarily unable to work. More than 14 were killed & roughly 350,000 were displaced from their homes. What are the as yet, widely unknown business risks from rising climate damage? What are the business opportunities? Which climate-related job skills will continue to be in demand by businesses, irrespective of favorable or unfavorable government policies?   These & related issues will be discussed by Naveen Krishnamurthy, SVP Lux Research. It provides research & tools to enhance performance across agrifoods, health, chemicals, utilities & other industries. Naveen advises companies on navigating multi-decade, growth strategies. Earlier, he served as business development manager at Harvest Power, a waste-to-energy business, funded by Kleiner Perkins, & was an environmental engineer at AECOM. events.name: Agentic AI In The Wild: Open Source Agents In Production
events.description: AI & Open Source Builders Meetup, New York City AI agents are moving into production, & more & more of them are built on open source. The question is no longer whether to use them, but what it takes to make them reliable once the demo is over. This meetup brings together builders, maintainers, & practitioners integrating AI agents into real codebases, CI/CD pipelines, internal developer platforms, cloud native infrastructure, & observability stacks. The evening focuses on the conversations that rarely fit into conference talks: what breaks at scale, how open source tools & standards shape agentic systems, where failure modes hide, & how teams build systems they can trust. Under the theme Open Source in Production, we will explore agentic code review, agent loops in CI/CD, developer platforms, eBPF-powered observability & security, & the role open source communities play in how production AI gets built. No vendor pitches. Just practical lessons from systems running in production. Agenda 5:00 PM Doors Open, Drinks & Networking5:30 PM Welcome & Opening Remarks5:40 PM [Speaker TBD], Qodo Dev Community6:05 PM Break, Food & Networking6:25 PM Panel: Agentic AI in the Wild7:15 PM Ryan Hamilton, Senior Developer & Community Lead, CircleCI AI Lab7:40 PM Closing Remarks7:45 PM Networking until 8:00 PM Speakers & Sessions [Speaker TBD], Qodo[Talk title TBD][Talk abstract TBD] Ryan Hamilton, Senior Developer & Community Lead, CircleCI AI LabOne Take: Engineering Agent Loops That Ship 100% Green PRs on the First PushMost teams optimizing AI-assisted development are focused on the wrong variable: prompting harder, adding rework, dumping larger failure logs into context. The real question isn't how to fix red PRs faster. It's how to stop producing them.Ryan shares findings from three connected Loop Lab experiments, each using the same controlled Snake game benchmark to isolate one variable at a time. Each one reveals something unexpected about where the real leverage lives in an agent loop, & what it means for cutting the cost of agentic development.Together, these experiments map a clear path from "rework is inevitable" to "rework is reserved for the unknowable." The result is a practical harness design that bakes a low Merge Efficiency Ratio (MER, the number of validation cycles it takes to get a change onto main) in from the start, & a new way to think about where validation belongs in the agent loop. Panel: Agentic AI in the WildWhat does it take to move AI agents from proof of concept into systems that operate reliably, & what role does open source play?Practitioners from across the stack will discuss context management, governance, open standards, observability, security, & what changes when agentic systems scale.Expect concrete lessons, not talking points. ModeratorDana Fine, Open Source & Developer Relations Manager, QodoDana leads open source programs & community initiatives at Qodo. She runs the GitHub User Group, CNCF local & GenAI communities, & the Bond AI meetup series. PanelistsBaruch Sadogursky, PortBaruch is a longtime developer advocate & a well-known speaker at developer conferences around the world. He co-authored Liquid Software & DevOps Tools for Java Developers, & focuses on developer productivity, DevOps, & how AI is changing the way software gets built & shipped. [Speaker TBD], Claude Community[Bio TBD] [Speaker TBD], NVIDIA[Bio TBD] Community PartnersAWS User Group NYC, CNCF NYC, Frontend NYC, WeMakeDevs, Bond AI, Qodo Dev Community Join the CommunityQodo Dev Community on Discord: [Discord invite link]Follow us on Meetup: [Meetup group link]

events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: The AI-ndustrial Revolution?
events.description: Companies are spending billions on AI. But is it actually making the economy better? Right now, the evidence is weird. Only 1 in 8 CEOs says AI is both increasing revenue & cutting costs. At the same time, 77% of CEOs say AI has been overhyped so far-but may actually be underhyped over the next decade. So what happens next? A productivity boom that creates new industries & better jobs? Or enormous investment, displaced workers, & technology that never delivers enough value to justify the hype? Daniel Di Martino, an economist & Fellow at the Manhattan Institute, studies economic growth, labor markets, & the policies that drive American competitiveness. Dr. Cecilia Dones is a Columbia lecturer & longtime data & AI executive who works with organizations trying to turn massive AI investments into actual business value. Will AI be a net benefit to the American economy? Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die.

events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: AI & China
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In July, a Chinese lab you'd probably never heard of published Kimi K3: 2.8 trillion parameters, billed as the largest open model on earth, weights posted free on Hugging Face for anyone to download. It's one of four Chinese labs that spent the last year closing the gap with the American frontier, then giving the result away. Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi. Four of the five most-used open models in the world now come out of Beijing, & American developers are running them inside hospitals, law firms, & startups because they're the cheapest, fastest tools available. No API someone in Washington controls. No off switch. Just download & go. One camp says a model is just math. Open weights run on a consumer's machine, the code is right there to inspect, & cutting Americans off from the best tools on the planet is how you lose a technology race. The other camp says the giveaway is the strategy. China seeds the world's infrastructure with their standards, their defaults, their assumptions, & the dependency follows once switching costs become unbeatable. So: should Americans be allowed to build on Chinese open-weight models or is this the new Cold War's Monkey's Paw? Arguing for, Rob Li is Managing Partner of Amont Partners, a New York global equity firm that invests across the US & Asia. events.description: Meet Your AI Teammates: Remy, Casey, & IvyThree AI teammates, one perpetual memory.Any firm can deploy a generic AI assistant. But these tools weren't built to remember your clients or understand your relationships. Your firm already has the intelligence. What's missing is memory. What your firm knows about a client sits in inboxes, CRM notes, & people's heads. It gets rebuilt from scratch every time, & it walks out the door when someone leaves. Remy, Casey, & Ivy fix that - each one built for a different function, each backed by perpetual memory. Remy handles financial advisory, working the client lifecycle end to end - onboarding, meeting preparation, account review - backed by a continuously updated client memory. For compliance, Casey runs perpetual KYC & Source of Wealth work, flagging risk before it reaches a client. Her second brain holds the full relationship & case history. Ivy sits with investor relations, turning a living investor memory into faster, more consistent RFP & DDQ responses.   Join Dana Ritter, Chief Product Officer & the Unique AI Executive Leadership Team for a live look at the Teammates & what agentic AI can do for wealth & asset management.    Agenda 6:00 to 7:00 pm: Networking, drinks, hors d'oeuvres 7:00 to 7:45 pm: 7:00 to 7:20 pm: Launch & live demo 7:20 to 7:45 pm: Client testimonial 7:45 pm onward: Networking, drinks, hors d'oeuvres   What you'll see live We'll showcase how Remy helps advisors onboard clients, prep for meetings, & run account reviews - all while building a client memory that syncs back to your CRM. We'll also preview how Casey supports compliance teams & how Ivy helps investor relations teams manage RFP & DDQ workflows. Discover what agentic AI can do across all functions at your firm & connect with peers across wealth & asset management tackling the same questions.  Who should attend COOs, CTOs, & Heads of AI exploring agentic solutions to improve operational efficiency & scale technology investments within wealth & asset management platforms Financial Advisors, Wealth Advisors, & Relationship Managers who want to improve client prep, reduce administrative drag, & scale personalized service Heads of Compliance, KYC, & Financial Crime looking to modernize review & oversight workflows Heads of Investor Relations handling investor updates, DDQs, & RFPs at volume Learn more about Unique AI at unique.ai.
