events.name: Urban Future Summit - 10 Years Of Impact
events.description: The 2026 Urban Future Summit is supported by New York Community Trust, New York State Energy Research & Development Authority, MUFG Bank, & NYU Tandon School of Engineering - this year is extra special as we're celebrating 10 years of supporting climate innovation & the entrepreneurs who have shaped it. 2 PRIZE TRACKS. 8 FINALISTS. HEAR THEM PITCH ON 10/22.Read the full press release  Climate Adaptation Prize: focused on solutions that help communities & ecosystems adapt to & build resilience against the impacts of climate change. Airbuild: Autonomous biological nutrient recovery systems that convert wastewater nutrients into carbon-sequestering biochar fertilizer, helping municipalities meet EPA compliance & cut costs while creating new revenue for farmers. Class 3 Technologies: Engineering-grade, building-level climate risk assessments powered by Iris, a proprietary simulation engine, helping large property owners quantify physical vulnerability & evaluate resilience strategies across their portfolios, while extending that same risk intelligence to underserved communities. Rarefied: A sunlight-driven propulsion mechanism enabling persistent flight in near-space, building a new atmospheric data layer to improve weather forecasting, disaster resilience, & climate risk modeling - data especially valuable in equatorial & developing regions, where sparse observations weaken storm & drought forecasts. Supercool Earth: An end-to-end precipitation enhancement platform that uses biology to increase rain & snowfall on demand for ski resorts, water utilities, hydropower operators, & agriculture, giving water-scarce communities a tool to stabilize supply before rationing or crop failure set in. Climate Mitigation Prize: focused on solutions that reduce greenhouse gas emissions & mitigate the impacts of climate change. Arcticar: An intelligent, clean energy platform for the cold chain, replacing diesel-powered trailer refrigeration with lower-cost electric units & integrated battery storage, eliminating the emissions & noise pollution reefers create. Emulate Cities: AI infrastructure that helps local governments automate permit review, cutting permitting timelines from weeks to minutes to accelerate deployment of housing, clean energy, & climate-resilient infrastructure. Every Electric: Operator of New York City's largest plug-in powerbank network, giving households access to affordable backup power while strengthening grid reliability for all New Yorkers. Ultropia: An ultrasonic mechanical water extraction platform that removes moisture from materials, targeting the energy-intensive gas dryers used across the industrial laundry industry. For more than a decade, the Urban Future Prize Competition has identified & accelerated the founders building the technologies, infrastructure, & systems that cities need to thrive in a changing world. What begins as an early-stage idea has repeatedly become a market-shaping company: 23 startups supported, more than $1 million awarded in non-dilutive funding, & over $515 million in follow-on capital raised - a remarkable 515x return on prize dollars deployed. At this year's Urban Future Summit, attendees will actively participate in the next chapter of that story. The Summit will culminate with presentations from the 2026 Urban Future Prize Competition finalists - founders tackling some of the most urgent challenges we're facing today, from climate resilience & emissions reduction to mobility, energy, & the circular economy. These entrepreneurs are not only competing for funding; they are competing for the opportunity to join ACRE, New York's longest-running climatetech incubator, where breakthrough ideas are transformed into scalable businesses. This year marks an important milestone for the Urban Future Prize Competition. For the first time, four awardees will be selected across the Climate Adaptation & Climate Mitigation prize tracks. Two winners get access to $50k & two runner-up teams in each track will also receive $10k in non-dilutive funding & admission into the ACRE Incubator. By expanding support to a broader cohort of entrepreneurs, we're investing in a larger pipeline of innovators at a moment when climate resilience & decarbonization must advance together.

events.description: Do books still matter?Have you ever wanted to publish a book?A book launch & panel discussion on publishing in the AI age - Times Square, Thursday, October 8th, 2026 Agentic AI is automating every layer of the tech stack. If AI writes the code, drafts the docs, & answers the question before you finish typing it - do books still matter? That's the question we're putting to 50 to 60 founders, AI sellers & specialists on October 8th. Justin Leto is a Global Principal Solutions Architect for Private Equity at AWS. Ben Schreiner, Head of AI & Modern Data Strategy at AWS, moderates. Bonus Presentation: "Owning the Machine - IP & Data Rights for Agentic AI Startups" A partner from Pearl Cohen will walk through what founders can patent, what they should lock down as trade secrets, how open-source model licenses constrain commercial use, & where agentic systems create fresh liability when software acts on its own. events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: Peptides vs The People
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In partnership with Pepper NYC & the Peptide Club of NYC A peptide to heal your tendon. An injection to rebuild your knee. Exosomes to make your body younger. Regenerative medicine is moving fast, & consumers increasingly don't want to wait ten years for the clinical trials to catch up (the AIDS crisis..). Some of these treatments have real science behind them. Others have promising early evidence. And some are being sold for thousands of dollars long before anyone can say with confidence that they actually work. But maybe that's the point. We let adults make risky decisions everywhere else. If a patient understands the evidence is uncertain, why shouldn't they be allowed to spend their own money trying something experimental? The alternative is the basic bargain medicine has relied on for decades: prove it works before you sell it. Because when the person explaining the risks is also making money from the treatment, "informed consent" can start looking a lot like a sales pitch. So: should experimental regenerative therapies be sold to consumers, or should medicine have to prove they work first? Arguing for, Julius Ritter is the founder of the California Peptide Club & CEO of Transcendence, a longevity company working with peptide, exosome, & regenerative therapies. He's part of a growing movement that thinks patients & physicians should have much more freedom to experiment at the frontier of medicine. Arguing against, Dr. Tiana Woolridge is a primary sports medicine physician at Hospital for Special Surgery, double board certified in pediatrics & sports medicine. She's trained in regenerative treatments like PRP herself, which is exactly why she thinks there's a difference between promising medicine & selling something before the evidence is there. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Reality Of Data Centers In Space
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a small, curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for.Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data. No talking, just thinking. 45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: The Reality of Data Centers in SpaceStarcloud just raised $250M to build satellites that run AI workloads in orbit, joining Google's "Project Suncatcher" & a SpaceX effort in a race to solve AI's power problem by moving compute off the planet entirely. The pitch is compelling - unlimited solar power, no water usage - but basic questions about heat dissipation, launch costs, & maintenance remain mostly unanswered. We're decoding: Is space-based computing a real solution to AI's real estate & energy issues? Supporting questions: What would actually have to be true for orbital data centers to beat a terrestrial one on cost? Who's positioned to win this race - the well-funded startups (Starcloud), or the hyperscalers who already have the capital & infrastructure (Google, SpaceX)? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like. **Refunds available up to 48 hours before the session. After that, we are sorry but the fee is non-refundable.

events.name: Product Leader Collective - The Software Factory Debate
events.description: The software factory is under construction. Come debate what it should look like.A lot of teams are trying to build a software factory: AI agents that can help plan, build, test, & ship software. The idea is compelling, but the reality is still messy. The tools are changing quickly, the playbook is far from settled, & the biggest bottlenecks may be showing up in places teams are not expecting. Join Ben Levine, CPO @ Candidly & product & engineering leaders for an open conversation about what's actually working & what still gets in the way. Then, get a close look at a few teams putting these ideas to work today. Who should be in the room  Product & engineering leaders figuring out where AI agents belong in the product development process, & what changes when they move from demos into daily work. Come ready to Pressure-test software factory claims with people doing the work. Think beyond coding agents: how should planning, specs, feedback, & handoffs change? Debate real tradeoffs instead of sitting through another polished product demo. Ben Levine is Chief Product Officer at Candidly, where he leads product, data science, & design. events.name: Plug&Play x PMAI Hackathon - Rapid Response
events.description: Plug & Play x PMAI Hackathon: Rapid Response #AIWeekNYThree challenges. Three rounds. 45 minutes each. Most hackathons give you hours - sometimes days - to solve one problem. Rapid Fire is different. In this fast-paced, emergency-response-themed hackathon, participants will compete in teams of 2-4 across a series of short challenges designed to test how quickly you can understand a problem, make decisions, build a solution, & communicate your thinking under pressure. Each round will introduce a new emergency-response scenario. Your team will have roughly 45 minutes to develop & submit a solution before moving immediately into the next challenge. No long build cycle. No endless polishing. You'll have to prioritize what matters, divide responsibilities quickly, & make tradeoffs in real time. How It Works Participants will form teams of 2-4 people. Over the course of the event, teams will face 3-4 short emergency-response challenges, revealed one at a time. For each round: A new problem is announced Teams have approximately 45 minutes to respond Teams submit their solution before the deadline Judges score the submissions The next challenge begins Scores accumulate across the rounds, & the team with the strongest overall performance wins. The challenges may involve areas such as emergency coordination, communication, resource allocation, information management, public safety, or rapid decision-making. What Are We Looking For? You do not need to build a fully finished product. Depending on the challenge, your submission could be a prototype, workflow, AI agent, product concept, operational system, or another practical solution. What matters is your ability to: Identify the real problem.Prioritize under pressure.Build quickly.Make smart tradeoffs.Explain why your solution works. Who Should Join? This event is designed for a mix of: Engineers, designers, product managers, founders, operators, students, & anyone interested in building with AI. You do not need to be highly technical to participate. Strong teams will likely combine different skill sets - technical, product, design, operations, & strategy. Come with teammates or meet people at the event. Why Rapid Fire? Real emergencies rarely give you perfect information, unlimited resources, or weeks to plan. They demand fast thinking, clear priorities, & decisive execution. Rapid Fire is an experiment in building the same way: under constraints, against the clock, & as a team. Think fast. Build fast. Respond faster. Schedule5:00 - 5:30  Check-in, Team Formation & Food5:30 - 5:45  Keynote: Sharing by PMAI Team5:45 - 6:30  First Problem6:30 - 7:15  Second Problem7:15 - 8:00  Third Problem8:00 - 8:30  Judging Session8:30 - 9:00  Winners Announcement & Group Photos Sponsorship Enquiry: https://community.pioneeringminds.ai/forms/c50df13a About Plug & PlayPlug & Play is the leading innovation platform, connecting startups, corporations, venture capital firms, universities, & government agencies. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, we're present in 60+ locations across 25+ industries. We offer corporate innovation programs, helping our partners in every stage of their innovation journey, from education to execution. We also run startup acceleration programs & have built an in-house VC where we've invested in hundreds of successful companies including Dropbox, Guardant Health, Honey, Lending Club, N26, PayPal, & Rappi. For more information, visit Plug & Play. About Vibranium LabsAt Vibranium Labs, we build Tony SRE, a 24/7 OnCall AI Incident Commander that proactively hunts down production issues before engineers ever get paged. We help hyperscaling startups & enterprises stay ahead of incidents, cut the 3am wake-ups, & ship with confidence.We're backed by Plug & Play, a16z, Franklin Templeton, Gaingels, & others. Our mission: Get ahead of incidents, not just respond: Tony SRE proactively investigates your systems around the clock, surfacing issues & root causes before anyone gets paged. Kill on-call burnout: Give teams their nights & weekends back by catching problems early, so humans step in only when it truly matters. Build lasting reliability: Every incident makes Tony SRE smarter. It learns your systems, improves your workflows, & becomes the living runbook your team actually uses. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. Learn more at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/

events.name: [AI Briefing] Private Equity - What Owners & Buyers Pay For
events.description: The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise.  This month's source: The PE AI Adoption Benchmark: From scaling to systematizing (Accordion with Wakefield Research - May 2026) Somebody's going to ask what your AI spend returned. If your company has a board or an eventual buyer, that question is already scheduled. Private equity gets asked first, so that's where this month's data comes from. Accordion surveyed 150 technology & AI operating partners at PE sponsors about the finance functions inside their portfolios. 41% are scaling AI across multiple companies with no operational playbook, & only 29% describe their firm as systematizing or leading. 75% of those companies arrived at acquisition unprepared or only partially ready for any of it. 86% of these operating partners expect buyers to pay a premium for AI-enabled finance capability within two years, & 44% say buyers are already asking in diligence without paying for it yet. Conviction is running ahead of price. The deployment that worked & left no evidence behind it is the one that costs you at exit. 67% of firms measure hours recovered. 29% put AI impact in front of a board.  The Mission: Building the evidence a board or a buyer will accept We'll work the measurement problem directly: which AI metrics connect to EBITDA, & how a company gets there without starting over. We'll examine why only 14% of portfolio finance functions have crossed from back-office automation into real decision intelligence, & what the rest are paying for instead.  The Format: The benchmark, fast: Five findings & the numbers under them, including the ones that don't hold up. Translating it out of PE: Sponsors run this test on a clock, so the pressure shows up there first. We'll take what it exposes & apply it to companies with other kinds of owners. Cross-pollinated debate: Operators compare what agentic finance already does in production (58% report automated covenant monitoring, 44% report AI-drafted board packages) against what their own governance can defend today.  Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: Leave with the measures a buyer or board will scrutinize, & an honest read on which ones you could produce this quarter. Founders & Builders: See what sponsors & portfolio CFOs are buying, & where the 47% assembling AI tools case-by-case stall out before anything compounds. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Compare notes on the constraint everything else runs into. Poor data infrastructure ranked first among all barriers by a wide margin, ahead of talent, legacy systems, change management, & budget. Most of it arrives at close & gets fixed while the books are closing.  The Prep: This is a working session, not a lecture. Read the report here. Bring your perspective.

events.name: SOSV Deep Tech Summit
events.description: SOSV DEEP TECH SUMMIT Join thousands of founders, VCs, technologists & scientists in Deep Tech The SOSV Deep Tech Summit (Nov. 4-6) is free to all participants, completely online, & encompasses three broad areas, climate tech, human health, & AI in the physical world. Top founders, VCs, & scientists are appearing on panels & in fireside chats expertly moderated by journalists & others. Based on attendance at our past summits, SOSV expects more than 5,000 attendees this year. Alongside the summit, SOSV is also hosting a Deep Tech VC-Founder Matchup & Co-Founder Search event. The producers of the Summit are SOSV's Ned Desmond, Ben Joffe, & Norm Amandi. More DetailsSOSV's mission is to invest in deep tech companies that advance human & planetary health, & embedded in building an 800+ company portfolio with a remarkable array of companies applying AI in the physical world. The SOSV Deep Tech 100 is a selection of our best. The SOSV Deep Tech Summit brings those themes together over three days of programming featuring climate tech, human health, & AI in physical world. SOSV's goal is to deepen venture, academic, corporate, & media understanding of the accomplishments & world-changing potential of startups in deep tech, whether that's new pathways to cure cancer, more climate friendly technologies to generate & store energy, robotic systems to take on physical work, or applying AI to develop more heat-resistant crop strains. Speaker selection for the Summit starts with SOSV's extensive networks & expertise in many areas of deep tech-thanks to our three deeply resourced programs in New York (SOSV NY), San Fransisco (SOSV SF), & Newark ( SOSV HAX)-and the 1000+ investors in our portfolio companies. The majority of speakers, however, draw from the broader deep tech ecosystem, not SOSV's portfolio.

events.name: Bridging Adherence Gap - How Can Tech Help People Stay On Their Treatment
events.description: At its core, adherence is a deeply human problem. We know following through with a treatment plan improves our health, but in the moment, taking that immediate next step isn't always easy. The root causes are complex-ranging from forgetfulness & fear of side effects to a lack of visible benefits & high costs. Yet, despite billions of dollars invested in digital health tools, smart devices, & patient support programs, the core statistic remains stubbornly unchanged: roughly 50% of patients still fail to take chronic medications as prescribed over the long term. With rapid shifts in consumer behavior & technology, healthcare companies have unprecedented opportunities to engage with patients.  Join Smart Design as we bring together experts from across the industry to explore how we can apply new technology to the messiness of everyday life & the healthcare system to drive real, lasting health outcomes.

events.description: We're bringing together engineers, founders, builders, & investors for an evening of agentic commerce, live demos, & building with the Ophelia API. Ophelia gives consumer software the infrastructure to search, book, buy, & transact end-to-end directly inside the products, agents, & devices people already use. Let a wearable turn find me a workout into a booked class Create a new interface for commerce that doesn't look like a checkout page Or build something we haven't imagined yet THE HACK CHALLENGEUse the Ophelia API to build a product, feature, agent, or experience that turns intent into a real transaction. We're especially interested in what happens when commerce moves inside the products, agents, devices, & interfaces people already use. Available commerce categories include:  Restaurants & reservations Flights & travel Hotels Events & tickets Fitness & classesand thousands of other services with Ophelia V3 PLEASE COME WITH PRODUCT OR DEMO ALREADY BUILT. We strongly encourage you to build beyond a chatbot or general-purpose AI assistant. THE NIGHT6:00 PM: Check-in + drinks Meet other NYC builders, grab a drink, get set up, & meet the Ophelia team. 6:30 PM: Ophelia API kickoff We'll give you a quick walkthrough of the API, what you can build, & how to get started. 6:45 PM: DEMOS Teams will have a short window to demo what they built. Show us the actual customer experience not just a pitch. 8:00 PM: JUDGING + WINNER Both the audience & our team will select one winning builder or team based on the quality of the build, creativity of the experience, & how compellingly it demonstrates the future of agentic commerce. 8:30 PM: WINNER + AFTERPARTY Announce the winner, celebrate, & keep the conversations going.  THE PRIZEThe winning team gets the opportunity to: Pitch their startup or idea directly to Betaworks. Plus:  AI credits across Betaworks teams $100 in Ophelia credits + merch Meta smart glasses Whether you're building a startup, experimenting with an idea, or just want to see what you can make with the infrastructure, come build. Come if you:  Build AI agents Build consumer apps Work on iOS or mobile Build with LLMs Work on commerce or payments Build for wearables or new interfaces Want to experiment with agentic commerce Have an idea you've been waiting to build Solo builders & teams are both welcome. ABOUT OPHELIAOphelia enables consumer software to build commerce directly into their products. Our API infrastructure powers end-to-end booking & buying for AI agents, iOS platforms, & devices from intent to purchase. Today, every merchant has its own website, booking flow, authentication, payment system, & operational requirements. Ophelia connects these fragmented systems through one integration, allowing software to parse availability, initiate checkout, process payments, & complete transactions directly within the products people already use. 3.8M+ users are already routed through Ophelia-powered products. Built for platforms. Made for people.  EVENT DETAILSEvent: Ophelia Demo NightDate: October 6, 2026Time: 6:00-9:00 PMLocation: Betaworks, New York CityAddress: 29 Little West StreetHosted by: OpheliaFormat: Build + live demos + food + prizesWho: NYC developers, founders, designers & buildersCost: Free Space is limited. RSVP required. Come build something that can actually execute.

events.name: The Quantified Self - What AI Can Actually Tell US About Our Data
events.description: This year, ChatGPT started connecting to people's medical records & Apple Health data, & a glucose sensor no longer needs a prescription. Gary Wolf (Co-founder, Quantified Self; longtime WIRED writer & editor) has studied how people make sense of their own data for 20 years. Hear what AI now makes possible for users, & how founders can build answers people trust. This year, OpenAI started letting people connect their medical records & Apple Health data to ChatGPT.  Since 2024, Americans can buy a continuous glucose monitor without a prescription. For most of the Quantified Self movement's history, answering a question with your own data meant manual logs & spreadsheets. Today a sensor collects the data & an AI model analyzes it on demand. That leaves every founder building in this space with one hard question: when an AI's answer changes what someone eats or takes, how do they know it's right? Gary Wolf has spent nearly 20 years watching people try to answer questions with their own data.  He co-founded Quantified Self with Kevin Kelly, joined the WIRED editorial team in 1994, became the first executive producer of Wired Digital, & launched Wired News. His New York Times Magazine cover story on self-tracking brought the practice to a mainstream audience, & his TED talk on the subject has been watched more than a million times. His current work is about AI & personal data. He's researching a cryptographic protocol to prove where sensor data came from at the moment it's recorded, & writing essays on how people talk to AI chatbots.  His new book, The Quantified Self: Learning to Observe, lays out a method anyone can use to test a question against their own data. On Thursday, October 15, Gary joins Startup Grind to talk about what AI changes for people using their own data, & what that means for the founders building those products. WHAT YOU'LL LEARN What AI changed for self-trackers: The analysis Quantified Self members once did by hand, & what a user can now do in one conversation with a model.When to trust a model's answer: How to tell when an AI reading of your sleep or blood sugar holds up, & what a user needs before acting on it.Proving where data came from: Gary's research on verifying sensor data at the moment it's recorded, & what it means for products that make health claims.Building around the user's question: The question, observe, reason, discover method from his new book, & how to design a product around what a user is actually asking. WHO SHOULD ATTEND AI health & wellness founders: Your model tells people what their data means, & they're going to act on it.Wearable & sensor founders: You collect the data, & your users can now hand it to an AI to interpret.AI product builders in any category: You're shipping personalized advice & want to hear from someone who has studied how people make sense of their own numbers for nearly 2 decades.Founders who track themselves: You've already asked a chatbot about your sleep data & want to know how far to trust the answer.Tickets for this event include food & drinks, as well as time with Gary after the chat to ask about your own product.  BONUS: you'll have an opportunity to purchase Gary's new book & get your copy signed by the author, himself! You'll also meet dozens of other high-performing entrepreneurs who are creating their next big thing. Seriously, it's some of the best founder networking in the city. Getting a ticket guarantees admission. No waitlisting. AGENDA 6:00 PM: Networking, Food & Drinks7:00 PM: Fireside Chat with Gary Wolf8:00 PM: Meet the Speaker + Book SigningAnd don't miss our other monthly tech events. They are great opportunities for builders, founders, & operators to network with each other to share best practices & find new resources to grow your startup the right way. events.name: 'Teaching America' Screening & Discussion
events.description: Join Anew and Anthem of us for a very special screening and discussion of the student-led movement to accurately teach our country's history.Teaching America honors the high school students and teachers who join forces to stand up for African-American studies, after the state of Arkansas threatens to shut their classes down. The in-classroom testimony of a movement sparked by the unflinching desire to learn that crosses boundaries and generations  in a time of intentional efforts to segregate and divide and to forcibly erase Americas history, culture, and humanity.The film provides a lens and a point of intervention into the larger attacks on education and learning as a core chapter in the authoritarian playbook. There is a clear throughline between the efforts to limit and erase the teaching of history; the banning of books, curriculum and classes; the intentional push to segregate and divide; and the limitations being placed on free and open inquiry, expression, and teaching in K-12 and higher education.The screening will start at 5:30pm, followed by a conversation.Anurima Bhargava (Director/Producer, Teaching America): CEO of Anthem of Us, a strategic advisory and consulting firm that centers dignity, justice, and belonging in schools, workplaces and communities.  Anurima previously led federal civil rights enforcement in schools, colleges and universities at the U.S. Department of Justice and directed the education practice at the NAACP Legal Defense Fund.  She also served as Chair and Commissioner of the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom.  Anurima has advised and produced numerous documentary films and projects; including the Oscar-nominated and Peabody Winner Writing With Fire; Peabody Winner While We Watched; Emmy-nominated Our Body Politic, Patang, A Shot At History, The Inquisitor, and the docuseries The Vow.  Anurima chairs the U.S. Board of Doc Society and serves on the capacity council for Brown Girls Doc Mafia.Vanessa Liu (Host/Discussant): Co-Founder and CEO, Sugarwork; Board of Overseers, HarvardUniversityEleonora Sharef Moreno (Host/Discussant):  Head of Philanthropy, Mercer PartnersAnew is a gathering space and discovery center for social transformation located in NYC. We host interactive events and workshops, an accelerator program for nonprofits, and a retail lab featuring ethically-sourced coffee and gifts.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Personal AI Agents, Muse, Instinct & Fight For Your Inbox
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quick research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data.  45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Personal AI agents - Muse, Instinct, & the fight for your inbox Meta's new agent Muse hit #1 on the App Store within 10 days of launch, passing ChatGPT - while a much smaller startup, Instinct, is quietly building a following by working entirely through text message, no app required. Both agents now book things, send emails, & make purchases on your behalf, & both have already run into real trust & privacy controversies. We're decoding: Are personal AI agents actually ready to be trusted with your accounts & money? Supporting questions: What's the real difference between "an agent that acts for you" & "a chatbot that answers you" - & does that difference justify the privacy trade-off? Does Meta's distribution advantage make Muse the inevitable winner, or does Instinct's leaner, invite-only approach have a real shot? What if Google, Apple & others launch personal AI Agents like Muse? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like. **Refunds available up to 48 hours before the session. After that, we are sorry but the fee is non-refundable.

events.name: Forbes Future Of Work Summit
events.description: Bringing together Chief Human Resources Officers, other top talent leaders, as well as founders & CEOs who are helping shape the workforce agenda & the workplace of the future.  Two seemingly disparate themes absolutely dominate the discussion right now around the future of work: the rise of generative artificial intelligence, & the shift to a skills-based economy. Yet these topics-one about pushing the frontiers of digital innovation, the other often tied to advancing workers who may not have college degrees-are more connected than it may seem. Today, these two critical issues intersect in more & more ways, as AI tools help organizations unearth the hidden skills of their workforce, AI advancements require employers to upskill their workforce & AI creates the white space for people to learn & develop in new & expansive ways.   The in-person portion of this Summit is by invitation only. All applications/registrations are subject to review by Forbes.

events.name: An UNMUTED Book Club: The Road To Serfdom
events.description: An UNMUTED Book Club: Islamic Exceptionalism READING NOT REQUIRED - just be curious! Next up: Friedrich Hayek's The Road to Serfdom, the 1944 book that argued central planning doesn't just fail on its own terms but sets a country sliding toward tyranny, no matter how decent the intentions behind it. Hayek wrote it as a warning to his adopted Britain, watching wartime economic controls & the postwar appetite for planning & fearing they'd curdle into something far worse. The core claim is uncomfortable: that the road to authoritarianism is often paved by well-meaning reformers who want the state to steer the economy toward fairness, & that once you hand government that kind of control, individual freedom rarely survives the trip. It's a foundational text of modern libertarian & conservative thought, & it's the book people keep reaching for when they want to argue that good intentions & coercion aren't opposites. Show up even if you only got through a chunk. We'll talk about planning versus markets, where Hayek looks prophetic, where he looks paranoid, & what an argument written against 1940s socialism has to say to a very different 2026. And we'll do a fun hypothetical case study. UNMUTED is a discussion forum for the politically curious. Accessible. Engaging. Social. Open-minded is the name of the game. Join your people.

events.name: Unique AI Presents - New AI Teammates
events.description: Meet Your AI Teammates: Remy, Casey, & IvyThree AI teammates, one perpetual memory.Any firm can deploy a generic AI assistant. But these tools weren't built to remember your clients or understand your relationships. Your firm already has the intelligence. What's missing is memory. What your firm knows about a client sits in inboxes, CRM notes, & people's heads. It gets rebuilt from scratch every time, & it walks out the door when someone leaves. Remy, Casey, & Ivy fix that - each one built for a different function, each backed by perpetual memory. Remy handles financial advisory, working the client lifecycle end to end - onboarding, meeting preparation, account review - backed by a continuously updated client memory. For compliance, Casey runs perpetual KYC & Source of Wealth work, flagging risk before it reaches a client. Her second brain holds the full relationship & case history. Ivy sits with investor relations, turning a living investor memory into faster, more consistent RFP & DDQ responses.   Join Dana Ritter, Chief Product Officer & the Unique AI Executive Leadership Team for a live look at the Teammates & what agentic AI can do for wealth & asset management.    Agenda 6:00 to 7:00 pm: Networking, drinks, hors d'oeuvres 7:00 to 7:45 pm: 7:00 to 7:20 pm: Launch & live demo 7:20 to 7:45 pm: Client testimonial 7:45 pm onward: Networking, drinks, hors d'oeuvres   What you'll see live We'll showcase how Remy helps advisors onboard clients, prep for meetings, & run account reviews - all while building a client memory that syncs back to your CRM. We'll also preview how Casey supports compliance teams & how Ivy helps investor relations teams manage RFP & DDQ workflows. Discover what agentic AI can do across all functions at your firm & connect with peers across wealth & asset management tackling the same questions.  Who should attend COOs, CTOs, & Heads of AI exploring agentic solutions to improve operational efficiency & scale technology investments within wealth & asset management platforms Financial Advisors, Wealth Advisors, & Relationship Managers who want to improve client prep, reduce administrative drag, & scale personalized service Heads of Compliance, KYC, & Financial Crime looking to modernize review & oversight workflows Heads of Investor Relations handling investor updates, DDQs, & RFPs at volume Learn more about Unique AI at unique.ai.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Let's Talk About Jev
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries - Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quick research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data.  45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Let's Talk About Jev! A tiny AI startup called Jev just went viral for doing the opposite of what every other AI company is doing - it doesn't chat at all. Built by an ex-OpenAI researcher, Jev only returns fast, structured decisions (yes/no, multiple choice, confidence scores) instead of generating text, & it's reportedly fielding funding offers north of $10 billion just over a week after launch. We're decoding: Is Jev a genuinely new category of AI - a faster, cheaper layer sitting underneath the chatbots - or is this hype-cycle enthusiasm for something that's really just a narrow classifier with good marketing? Supporting questions: Does the "specialized model" approach threaten the big general-purpose LLMs, or complement them? What would it take for Jev's $10B valuation talk to actually make sense a year from now? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like. **Refunds available up to 48 hours before the session. After that, we are sorry but the fee is non-refundable.

events.name: The Age Of AI  - Live Recording Of The Builders
events.description: Bestselling biographer Walter Isaacson joins us for a live recording of the first episode of his brand-new podcast, The Builders, with Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of Microsoft AI & one of the most influential thinkers & leaders working in artificial intelligence today. AI is reshaping our world at breathtaking speed. But behind the technology, real human beings are making choices about what our future will look like, how we'll work & live, & whose vision will shape what comes next. And as AI grows more powerful, so does the unease surrounding it. Will it usher in an era of extraordinary human possibility - or are we building something we may ultimately struggle to control? On The Builders, Walter Isaacson talks to the entrepreneurs, scientists & technologists building AI & other technologies that are rapidly reshaping our world to get inside the thinking of some of the most consequential figures of our time. Throughout his career, Isaacson has been fascinated by the people who change the world - from Leonardo da Vinci & Albert Einstein to Steve Jobs, Jennifer Doudna & Elon Musk. With The Builders, he turns his attention to the entrepreneurs, scientists & technologists building AI & the other technologies transforming our lives. For this special live recording, Isaacson sits down with Suleyman to go inside the ideas, ambitions & decisions driving the AI revolution. From fears about jobs & misinformation to the existential question of whether superintelligent machines could one day threaten humanity itself, the stakes can feel almost impossibly high. What does it mean to build technology with the power to reshape society? Who gets to decide where it takes us? Hear two singular thinkers explore the promise, power & profound questions of the AI age & the question at the heart of The Builders: whose imagination do we want to live in?

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Reality Of Data Centers In Space
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a small, curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for.Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data. No talking, just thinking. 45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: The Reality of Data Centers in SpaceStarcloud just raised $250M to build satellites that run AI workloads in orbit, joining Google's "Project Suncatcher" & a SpaceX effort in a race to solve AI's power problem by moving compute off the planet entirely. The pitch is compelling - unlimited solar power, no water usage - but basic questions about heat dissipation, launch costs, & maintenance remain mostly unanswered. We're decoding: Is space-based computing a real solution to AI's real estate & energy issues? Supporting questions: What would actually have to be true for orbital data centers to beat a terrestrial one on cost? Who's positioned to win this race - the well-funded startups (Starcloud), or the hyperscalers who already have the capital & infrastructure (Google, SpaceX)? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like. **Refunds available up to 48 hours before the session. After that, we are sorry but the fee is non-refundable.

events.name: Building Internal Community Programs: Ambassadors, Advocates & Beyond
events.description: Building an ambassador program from scratch? Scaling one that's outgrown its original playbook? Join CMX NYC for a moderated panel featuring community professionals who've built & run ambassador & community programs inside some of the industry's leading companies. Learn about what makes these programs thrive, how to measure impact in a way leadership actually cares about, & the challenges of scaling & sustaining momentum over time. Whether you're launching your first ambassador program or leveling up an existing one, you'll leave with practical takeaways from people who've done this work firsthand. Grab a bite, connect with fellow community builders, & stay for open networking after the panel wraps. What to Expect 6:00-6:30 PM: Arrive, connect, & meet fellow community builders & attendees. Light bites & refreshments will be served 6:30-7:30 PM: Panel (45 minutes of facilitated discussion, 15 minutes of open Q&A) 7:30-8:00 PM: Closing reflections + open networking Meet the speakers: Dory Jackson (Moderator): Dory is an NYC-based entertainment journalist with experience at major publications such as Newseek & PEOPLE. Dory is currently building a community of film & television lovers on TikTok & a YouTube interview series with notable celebrities. Darragh Collins: Darragh leads Community & External Communications at Rillet, an AI-native ERP for high-growth tech companies. He's built three B2B communities from the ground up, including Off the Ledger at Airbase, which grew to more than 7,000 finance professionals, the Zip community for procurement leaders, & Close Club at Rillet, a curated, application-only community of 1,200+ finance leaders. Mary Findley: Mary is a community builder based in Brooklyn, NY. She has 15+ years of experience across education, edtech, SaaS, & marketplaces - including Webflow, Miro, Depop, & Skillshare - launching advocacy programs, community challenges, & creator initiatives from the ground up. Currently, she's growing the community at Lovable, where she leads ambassador programming for people across industries, cities, & skill levels. She thrives at the intersection of community, product, & marketing. Paula Rosenberg: Paula Rosenberg has worked in Community for over a decade. She's worked at Quirky, VHX, & Vimeo. She spent the last five years at Stack Overflow, where she was Director of Communities. She's also a writer & a consultant. Outside of work, she's an active member & volunteer of multiple communities including The Old Girls Club, Eat Your Books, & Animal Care Centers in NYC. She is a Yelp Elite member & a Brand Ambassador for Sur La Table. Erica Hanson: Erica has spent 12+ years building communities at Google, FlutterFlow, & outside work. At Google, she led the Google Developer Student Clubs program, scaling it to 2,000 communities across university campuses in 110 countries & reaching 1.8M students annually. She recently joined 645 Ventures as a Fractional Developer Relations & Community Lead, & is the founder of Coffee & Career Transitions NYC, a community for people navigating layoffs & job searches. She spends a lot of time at the playground with her baby & toddler & is training for the NYC marathon. About CMX CMX is a global network of community professionals dedicated to advancing the community industry & empowering communities to thrive. With chapters around the world, CMX fosters local connection & shared learning. Meet the Chapter Leads: Lauren Indovino is a Community & Client Engagement Manager at an education technology startup, with a career dedicated to expanding access to education. Lauren enjoys hosting, running, dogs, live music, travel, & spontaneously exploring NYC! Erica Hanson is a Fractional Developer Relations & Community Lead at 645 Ventures. She has loved building communities for Google & FlutterFlow & outside of work for 12+ years. Erica lived in LA, San Francisco, London, & Singapore before moving to NYC. She enjoys traveling, running, & dancing with her toddler. Kayla Green is a Senior Community Manager at a research technology company with 5 years of building & growing customer communities. Her bread & butter is ambassador programs & helping companies scale their community from 0 to 1. Kayla loves dancing, all things woo woo, & reality TV. About Fabrik: Welcome to Fabrik! We are on a mission to uplift communities & foster serendipitous connections in real life. Fabrik is a home for communities where everyone has a place to belong. With spaces designed to feel more like your living room than your office, Fabrik's social spaces are vibrant hubs where people can come together in real life, explore interests, forge meaningful connections, & build a sense of community.

events.name: UGLY TALK: FAILURE IS KEY TO SUCCESS
events.description: Failure gets talked about like it is part of the journey. That is the lie.The real thing is messier. Missed bets. Wrong hires. Near-breakdowns. The week you stop sleeping and start doing math at 3:00 AM.Founders are expected to eat it quietly and keep moving. No language for what happened. No playbook for what to do next.Ugly Talk is a founder room for the part nobody posts. No fluff. No consultants. Just builders with scars, talking about the call that cost them. Why you should be in this room.Hear what failure cost them. Then hear what they did next.Learn how experienced founders separate self-worth from outcomes when things go sideways.Spot the patterns behind repeat mistakes. And the early signals you should not ignore.Leave with a few concrete moves for the next hard week. Not inspiration.Meet other founders in the thick of it. The ones who are still building. What's on the table.Dare to suck: how permission to fail unlocks real progressThe moment things broke: missed opportunities, wrong turns, near-breakdowns, and what changed afterwardFailure vs identity: separating self-worth from outcomesTreating setbacks as data: what to measure, what to ignore, and how to decide fastRejection as redirection: how founders find the signal in the noHabits for staying focused and resilient when everything feels uncertain Run of show6:00  6:30 PM: Reception (check-in & light drinks)6:30  6:40 PM: Welcome remarks6:40  6:50 PM: Keynote Speech by Ben McKean6:50  7:30 PM: Panel Discussion7:30  7:45 PM: Audience Q&A7:45  8:00 PM: Mixer + snacks and drinks Featured speakers.Ben McKean - Founder & Chief Executive Officer, HungryrootBen McKean is the Founder and CEO of Hungryroot, a personalized healthy eating assistant that uses AI to make meal planning, food shopping, and nutrition effortless and enjoyable. Prior to Hungryroot, Ben was a Vice President and General Manager at Groupon, overseeing their food and beverage business. Ben came to Groupon through the acquisition of Savored, which he founded in 2009. Savored was the nations leading provider of yield management technology to the restaurant industry, used by over two thousand restaurants nationwide and nearly one million diners. Prior to Savored, Ben worked in Merrill Lynchs technology investment banking group. Ben is a graduate of Georgetown University and currently lives in North Carolina with his wife and kids.Stephen McKinney - Founder & CEO, BizbeStephen McKinney is a serial entrepreneur with over a decade of experience across tech, marketing, and logistics. He's the founder and CEO of Bizbe.com, an AI-native business brokerage and lower middle market M&A firm based in New York and Miami. A former contestant on ABC's Shark Tank, Steve previously founded and led Retty Logistics, a seven-figure last-mile delivery company acquired by DXP Logistics and Webster Logistics.Dmitry Koltunov - Founder and CEO, ArborDmitry Koltunov is a serial entrepreneur, technologist, educator, and storyteller. He is the founder and CEO of Arbor, an AI-powered content engine that helps enterprises scale their communications with video and beyond. Previously, he co-founded and served as CTO of ALICE, a hospitality technology company that grew into a global industry leader before being acquired by Expedia Group.Dmitry also leads the New York City chapter of the Startup Leadership Program, New Yorks oldest startup fellowship, whose 500+ alumni have collectively raised more than $1 billion in funding across every industry imaginable. He is passionate about helping founders navigate the challenges of building and scaling companies.Outside of technology, Dmitry is an award-winning songwriter and theater producer currently developing a new musical for Broadway. He holds degrees in Computer Science and Economics from the University of Pennsylvania and is a CFA charterholder.Gwendolyn von Rahn - Co-Founder and CEO, Sweetling HealthGwendolyn von Rahn is the Co-Founder and CEO of Sweetling Health, an postpartum intelligence platform built for at-risk and hard-to-reach populations. Shes a second-time exited founder, an award-winning marketer with over a decade of experience building consumer brands for women, Gwen led creative and brand teams at Vogue, InStyle, and POPSUGAR before founding and scaling a mission-driven consumer brand into Nordstrom distribution that raised over $1M for melanoma research through the Melanoma Research Foundation. She holds a Cornell Johnson MBA and founded Sweetling from her own lived experience with the postpartum care gap. Who's hosting it.Victoria Yampolsky - President, The Startup StationVictoria Yampolsky is the Founder and President of The Startup Station, a strategic CFO advisory firm and financial education platform for startups. She partners with founders on financial strategy, modeling, and fundraising, having supported over 150 companies across 15 industries in raising more than $50M in venture capital. Victoria is also an advocate for female founders and access to capital, and has taught finance to more than 20,000 entrepreneurs through programs including the Bank of America Institute for Womens Entrepreneurship at Cornell. She began her career at Deutsche Bank and Capgemini, and holds a BS in Computer Science from Cornell University and an MBA from Columbia Business School. Who's getting in.Early-stage tech founders and operators navigating uncertainty, setbacks, or the emotional weight of building a company. Expected roles may include:Founders and co-founders (pre-seed to Series A)Operators (COO, Head of Ops, Chief of Staff)Product and Engineering leads building through ambiguityGrowth and GTM leads working through missed targets and pivotsFinance and strategy leaders supporting founder decision-making Who's backing this.The Startup StationThe Startup Station - is a CFO advisory and financial education platform for early-stage startups. We help early-stage founders build investor-ready financials and tell their funding story with confidence. In the past decade, weve helped 150+ founders raise over $50M and educated 20,000+ entrepreneurs worldwide. The Startup Station also runs Speed Pitch, an exclusive investor-founder matchmaking event series for early-stage startups where founders are matched with 3 investors by sector, stage, and check size.Mind Your BusinessEvery attendee will receive a free copy of keynote speaker Ben McKeans Mind Your Business.  Mind Your Business is a practical parable for people rethinking work as AI advances. Set over a four-day retreat, it follows six participants competing for funding to bring one vision to life. As they evaluate six competing proposals, they begin to confront deeper questions about what gives them energy, who they serve, and what they uniquely contribute. Those patterns form what the book calls their Soulcodethe way purpose, belonging, imagination, and courage shape how they work. Told with humor and warmth, the story turns familiar workplace tensions into practical lessons for contributing more deeply, seeing new possibilities, and acting with greater conviction. At its core, the book argues that the opportunity of the AI era isnt doing more workits knowing what work is worth doing.GREY JournalGREY Journal - Media partner spotlighting modern entrepreneurs (featured on Apple News + Google News). About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough \

events.name: Red Carpet Room Launch Party
events.description: If you show up with a backpack or your laptop you will be banned from the event. Please leave backpacks at home. RED CARPET ROOM Formerly Fun HouseHosted by Anwar EnterprisesSaturday, October 31, 2026 Exact address released to confirmed guests 24 hours before doors. About the Event Red Carpet Room is the next chapter of Fun House, rebuilt around a single idea: the people building brands should be building them together. This is a mixer for founders, creators, & investors from the Anwar Events community, gathered in one room with a shared reason to be there. Everyone in attendance is constructing something with their name attached to it. The night is designed so the person who can unblock you is standing a few feet away. We are doing it on Halloween on purpose. The city will be full of parties where nothing happens beyond the party itself. This one gives you a panel worth sitting through, a room worth working, & footage of yourself that you will actually use. Run of Show [7pm] - Doors, check-in, & open networking to start the night[8pm] - Panel: operators who built audiences, companies, & reputations from nothing   SPECIAL GUESTS BEING REVEALED NEXT WEEK [9pm] - Open mixer, with Red Carpet Show interviews running in the back room Who's Coming The typical guest is a founder raising or building, a creator monetizing an audience, or an investor looking for both. Expect crossover from fashion, music, media, tech, art & consumer brands, since that is who the Anwar Events community actually contains. Whether you are hiring, raising, pitching a collaboration, or looking for people who take their work as seriously as you do, you will be in the right room. The Red Carpet Show Throughout the night, Ilias will pull guests aside for on-camera interviews for The Red Carpet Show. There is one question at the center of every interview: how can he help you. Those conversations get cut into content that reaches an audience of 70,000 plus founders, investors, & creators. Sitting down costs you four minutes & can put your company in front of people you would never cold email. Dress Code Halloween night calls for more than a costume assembled at the last minute. Come dressed as the version of yourself the press would photograph, whether that means black tie, full character, or your own blend of both. Cameras run from the door onward, so arrive accordingly. Capacity & Entry Space is limited & the guest list is curated. A confirmed RSVP secures your place only until capacity fills, so arriving early is strongly recommended. Bring a valid ID for check-in at the door. About the Host Ilias Anwar is an entrepreneur, marketer, & community builder based in New York City. He has produced more than 600 events across NYC, LA, & San Francisco, cultivating a network of over 70,000 founders, investors, & creators. His work includes brand partnerships with Google, Red Bull, Andreessen Horowitz, & Universal Music Group, along with activations at NFL Super Bowl Weekend & New York Fashion Week. Today he runs Anwar Enterprises, a venture studio that launches & scales consumer & tech companies through distribution first. If you need to meet someone in this city, they have probably attended one of his events. Partners & Sponsors Creatorsarethenewstudios.comCanvas helps creators, founders, & brands turn ideas into media IP they own. AI agents handle the story, production plan, budget, & distribution, & your first IP is free. Happyboards.comHappyBoards makes chef-built charcuterie boards & grazing tables from locally sourced ingredients. It delivers same-day across 27+ Northeast cities, & HappyBoards is feeding the room tonight.Stay Connected Future Anwar Events drop to the community first. Get on the list at luma.com/iliasanwar & follow along on Instagram, X, & LinkedIn for everything we run next. Community Standards Red Carpet Room is inclusive of gender, sexuality, race, religion, & ability. Discrimination or harassment of any kind will not be tolerated on site. For urgent security concerns during the event, please contact venue staff directly. Disclaimers By attending this event, you agree to the following terms. Photography, Video, & Recording: This event will be photographed, filmed, live-streamed, & audio recorded. By entering the venue, you consent to being captured on camera & to the use of your name, image, voice, statements, & likeness by Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, The Red Carpet Show, & their affiliated partners & sponsors. Marketing & Promotional Use: Any material captured at this event may appear in promotional content, social media, websites, newsletters, press coverage, paid advertising, sponsor recap materials, & future marketing assets, worldwide & in perpetuity, without compensation. Guests waive any right to inspect or approve the finished material before publication. On-Camera Interviews: Participation in The Red Carpet Show is entirely voluntary. Sitting for an interview grants Anwar Enterprises the full right to edit, distribute, & monetize that footage across any platform, in any format, without further approval. Opting Out: If you do not wish to be photographed or filmed, please notify event staff upon arrival & avoid the designated filming areas. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to accommodate your request, though appearance in wide or crowd shots cannot be fully prevented. Guest Policy: This is a private, invitation-only event. RSVPs are non-transferable & entry is subject to ID verification. Organizers reserve the right to refuse entry at their discretion. Capacity & Access: This event has a strict capacity limit. A confirmed RSVP does not guarantee entry once capacity has been reached, so early arrival is strongly encouraged. Code of Conduct: All attendees are expected to conduct themselves professionally & respectfully. Organizers reserve the right to remove any guest whose behavior is disruptive or inappropriate, without refund or recourse. Liability: Anwar Enterprises, Anwar Events, & the venue are not responsible for loss, theft, or damage to personal property. Attendance is at your own risk. Data & Registration: Information submitted at registration may be shared with event sponsors & partners in accordance with their respective privacy policies. Guests may opt out of sponsor communications at any time. Changes & Cancellations: Event details including time, venue, panelists, & programming are subject to change. Organizers will make reasonable efforts to notify registered guests of any material changes.

events.name: Sampura Research - Lunch+Talk+Social
events.description: Sampura Research: Hill-climbing Alignment using Humans Sampura Research is a London-based nonprofit, founded by Google DeepMind alumni, building Human-AI Complementarity for AI alignment. As AI systems grow more capable, the judges we use to train, evaluate & monitor them increasingly fall short. Most of the field responds by replacing humans with LLM judges; we think humans & AIs have complementary strengths, & that human oversight is an uncorrelated layer of defence that AI-only judges can't provide. In this talk we'll share how we're building better judges: a leaderboard of 50+ alignment-relevant datasets, & methods that route, decompose & assist across humans & AIs to hill-climb it. Schedule (you can join for any part)12:30 - Talk (20 min)12:50 - Q&A (20 min)13:10 - Informal chat with the team (20 min) Backed by an $11M grant from Coefficient Giving, we're a small in-person team hiring founding technical staff, looking to solve alignment instead of pausing AI. Come along & say hello! Apply: Founding Member of Technical Staff applicationWebsite: https://sampura.org/ Lunch will be provided! Update: We're almost at capacity, & will admit folks based on their profile

events.name: An UNMUTED Debate: AI & China
events.description: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 In July, a Chinese lab you'd probably never heard of published Kimi K3: 2.8 trillion parameters, billed as the largest open model on earth, weights posted free on Hugging Face for anyone to download. It's one of four Chinese labs that spent the last year closing the gap with the American frontier, then giving the result away. Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi. Four of the five most-used open models in the world now come out of Beijing, & American developers are running them inside hospitals, law firms, & startups because they're the cheapest, fastest tools available. No API someone in Washington controls. No off switch. Just download & go. One camp says a model is just math. Open weights run on a consumer's machine, the code is right there to inspect, & cutting Americans off from the best tools on the planet is how you lose a technology race. The other camp says the giveaway is the strategy. China seeds the world's infrastructure with their standards, their defaults, their assumptions, & the dependency follows once switching costs become unbeatable. So: should Americans be allowed to build on Chinese open-weight models or is this the new Cold War's Monkey's Paw? Arguing for, Rob Li is Managing Partner of Amont Partners, a New York global equity firm that invests across the US & Asia. He has spent his career putting capital on both sides of the Pacific, from Yum China to Alibaba deals, & he thinks the country that walls itself off from the best tools available loses. Arguing against, Will McKelvey is a Principal at Lerer Hippeau, one of New York's oldest venture firms, where he backs early-stage founders & spends his days watching for the future of AI, especially in consumer. He got his start by way of a congressional office, & he thinks the cheapest model on the market is the one you pay for slowly. Let's get into it. UNMUTED is the place where talking points go to die. Talk politics. Keep your friends. Make new ones. In collaboration with COMMITTEE OF 100Committee of 100 (C100) is a nonprofit U.S. leadership organization of distinguished Chinese Americans dedicated to advancing the full participation of Chinese Americans in American society & fostering constructive U.S.-China relations. For more than 35 years, C100 has brought together leaders across business, government, academia, technology, media, the arts, & other fields to advance its dual mission. Learn more at committee100.org.

events.description: Step into the Future of Ocean Renewables:  An Electrifying Evening with the 2026 Offshore Wind Innovation Hub Innovator Cohort!The 4th annual Wind-Win Startup Showdown offers a pitch experience like no other, spotlighting cutting-edge technology breakthroughs to transform the future of ocean renewables. Thermoelectric cooling vest for workers in extreme heat.Fleet Robotics (Massachusetts, US) - Data insights powered by submersible, autonomous cleaning and inspection robots.Hefring Marine (Iceland) - events.name: Latinos x AI Hackathon
events.description: Latinos x AI Hackathon - NYCSaturday, October 10  10:00 AM - 6:00 PM  New York City Nuestra gente. Nuestros problemas. Nuestro cdigo. For Hispanic Heritage Month, 150 builders are spending one Saturday in New York building AI for the problems our communities actually live with. Not a demo day. Not a panel. Eight hours, three tracks, working software by 5pm. Applications are reviewed. Attendance is free. The Three TracksPick one when you apply. Build for it all day. 01  Immigration - Papers & Process Status, documents, deadlines, & the systems that decide who belongs. Think intake triage for legal aid clinics, plain-language explainers for immigration forms, interpreter tooling, case-status tracking, know-your-rights assistants. 02  Healthcare - Care Without Barriers Language, coverage, & access for patients the system was not built for. Think interpretation at the point of care, insurance navigation, discharge instructions people can actually read, community health worker tooling, prescription & benefits literacy. 03  Finance - Banking the Unbanked Credit, remittances, & building wealth without a financial history. Think remittance transparency, credit-building for thin-file borrowers, small business bookkeeping for cash operations, benefits & tax navigation, fraud protection for first-generation account holders. Prizes$4,500 total - $1,500 per track. Every track winner also gets [sponsor perks once confirmed]. ScheduleSchedule 10:00 AM - Doors, breakfast, team formation10:45 AM - Opening remarks & track briefings11:15 AM - Building starts1:00 PM - Lunch3:00 PM - Mentor office hours & mid-day checkpoint4:45 PM - Submissions close5:00 PM - Demos on stage5:45 PM - Judging & awards6:00 PM - Close Who Should ApplyEngineers, data scientists, & designers who want to ship something real in a day Product people & founders who can shape a problem & pitch it Clinicians, immigration attorneys, paralegals, social workers, & financial counselors - the people who know the problem from the inside. You do not need to code to be valuable here. Teams with a domain expert consistently win. Students & career switchers You can apply solo or with a team of up to four. Solo applicants will be matched at 10:00 AM. What to BringLaptop & charger A problem you have seen up close ID for building security We provide breakfast, lunch, coffee, wifi, power, mentors, & the room. RulesBuild during the event. Prior research & planning are fine; prior code is not. Teams of one to four. Every submission needs a public repo, a two-minute demo video, & a short written description. You keep everything you build. No IP claims from organizers or sponsors. Be decent to each other. Harassment of any kind means you leave. Mentors & Judges[ADD once confirmed: names, titles, organizations.] Partners & Sponsors[ADD once confirmed: logos & names.] Interested in sponsoring or partnering? Write to chris@ziora-copilot.com or book 30 minutes. Sponsorship closes October 1. FAQIs it free? Yes. Applications are reviewed because space is limited to 150. Where is it? New York City. The exact address is shared with approved attendees. Do I have to be Latino to attend? No. The event is built by & for the Latino community in New York, & everyone who wants to build for these problems is welcome. Do I need a team? No. Come solo & we will match you at the start. What language is the event in? English, with Spanish spoken throughout. Apply & demo in whichever you prefer. Can I keep working on my project afterward? Please do. That is the point. A note on selection: This edition is built for & centered on the Latino community in New York. Applications from Latino & Hispanic builders will be prioritized. Allies are welcome to apply & will be considered as space allows. Questions: chris@ziora-copilot.com Hosted by Christopher Martinez

events.name: NY Tech Meetup: International Edition
events.description: ATLAS Innovation Exchange @ NY Tech Meetup   NY Tech Alliance is excited to welcome back our friends from ATLAS in Rome, Italy for another special international edition of the NY Tech Meetup. We're bringing together the NYC tech community & a new group of standout Italian founders building ambitious companies & technologies for the future. It's an opportunity to connect two dynamic tech ecosystems, meet founders you may not otherwise encounter in New York, & build new relationships across the Atlantic. Whether you're a founder, investor, technologist, operator, or simply curious about what's emerging next, come meet the people building it. Come for the demos. At each event, entrepreneurs, founders, CEOs, & their teams demo cutting edge & transformative tech, answer questions from attendees & network with all in a welcoming & fun-filled space. Since its creation, over 1,200 companies have participated & have been a driving force of innovation & job creation in NYC & the greater NY area. About ATLAS ATLAS is a leading Italian ecosystem supporting the internationalization of startups. Based in Rome & part of Confindustria's innovation network, ATLAS helps founders expand into the U.S. & global markets through education, tools, & strategic support.  Learn more: www.assoatlas.org

events.description: We're bringing together builders & long-time contributors from the Numerai & decentralized AI ecosystems for a mix of talks, a workshop, & a special community panel. Featured speakers: Jason - Co-Founder & CEO, CrowdCent Nick - Co-Founder & CEO, Allora Labs Matteo - Co-Founder & CEO, Orion Finance The Numerai "Out of Sample" Special Panel  A discussion & AMA-style panel with guests featured on the Out of Sample interview series. All three are current or former members of the Numerai Council of Elders, with the panel moderated by another member of the Council. Tim (aka jefferythewind) (see episode 2) ShatteredX (see episode 3) Jason (see episode 4) More speakers & session details coming soon. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/ Important Note  This is an in-person-only event; there will be no livestream. For security reasons, we must provide a guest list to the security team at least 24 hours before the event. You must provide your  FULL NAME  when registering for this event. If you prefer not to display your full name publicly, please provide it in the final registration question instead. Your full name will be shared only with the security team. About Decentralized AI Days  Decentralized AI Days are community-driven events exploring how open, decentralized AI & Web3 can work together in practice. We bring together engineers, researchers, & builders for a day of technical talks, hands-on workshops, & honest conversation - no hype, no sales pitches, & no pay-to-play. The ecosystem we care about includes projects such as Numerai & CrowdCent. The door is open to anyone building with or curious about decentralized AI. Come for the substance, stay for the community. Call for Presentations  Interested in sharing your experience with our community? Please contact me (Joe) directly via X, or on LinkedIn. I'll get back to you as soon as possible. Everyone is welcome to apply, as long as your talk or workshop topic is relevant. Agenda  More details will be announced soon! Expect a program of tech talks & workshops, followed by a relaxed evening mixer. What to Expect   Connect with a friendly community of AI & Web3 builders, researchers, & curious minds.  Enjoy zero-hype technical talks focused on real problems & practical insights.  Take part in hands-on workshops where you can learn by building.  Watch live demos of decentralized AI & related projects.  Meet the organizers & share your questions & feedback directly.  Explore community resources & connect over food. Who Should Attend)  Decentralized AI Days are for everyone curious about where AI & decentralized systems meet: AI/ML engineers, Web3 developers, researchers, students, & builders at any experience level. If you are new to the space, you are welcome; if you have been building for years, you will find your people here. Come ready to learn, share, & connect. The Venue  Register to see the address. Complimentary refreshments will be provided throughout the day.
