events.name: Climate Cafe w/ CUNY
events.description: Join CUNY at the Climate Imaginarium!Open to the public! Members of the CUNY community will be joining us for a gallery tour, followed by a meditation & climate cafe. Climate cafes are listening circles for your climate-linked emotions. Get help facing your climate anxiety & connect with impactful local organizers. Vegan snacks provided!  About the Climate ImaginariumThe Climate Imaginarium is a center for climate, community, & culture in New York City. Located on Governors Island, the Climate Imaginarium is activating a cultural destination at the heart of New York City's burgeoning green economy, where artists, scientists, advocates, & storytellers come together to reimagine & build toward a more resilient future.  Getting to the Climate ImaginariumFor the weekend ferry schedule to Governors Island, please check here. Ferries run every 15 minutes. Take the ferry that's most convenient for you from either Lower Manhattan (10 South Street), Brooklyn Bridge Park (Pier 6), or Red Hook/Atlantic Basin. Please arrive 15 minutes prior to your ferry departure time with your ticket ready to display. Ferry tickets must be purchased at the ferry terminal or online. Fares are $5 for a round trip ticket & free for adults over 65, children 12 & under, Climate Imaginarium summer volunteers, & others. All passengers ride free before 11am on weekends. Cars are not permitted. Governors Island is also accessible from any route via NYC Ferry by transferring at Wall Street/Pier 11. You can find the NYC Ferry schedule here. Tickets on NYC Ferry are $4.50 each way. Once you get to Governors Island, you will either get out at Soissons Landing (from Manhattan) or Yankee Pier (from Brooklyn). You can use this map of Governors Island to locate Colonels Row. The Climate Imaginarium is in Building 406A, in the middle of Colonels Row, & will have a visible sign outside the doorway. Our address is 406A Comfort Road.

events.name: [AI Briefing] Private Equity - What Owners & Buyers Pay For
events.description: The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise.  This month's source: The PE AI Adoption Benchmark: From scaling to systematizing (Accordion with Wakefield Research - May 2026) Somebody's going to ask what your AI spend returned. If your company has a board or an eventual buyer, that question is already scheduled. Private equity gets asked first, so that's where this month's data comes from. Accordion surveyed 150 technology & AI operating partners at PE sponsors about the finance functions inside their portfolios. 41% are scaling AI across multiple companies with no operational playbook, & only 29% describe their firm as systematizing or leading. 75% of those companies arrived at acquisition unprepared or only partially ready for any of it. 86% of these operating partners expect buyers to pay a premium for AI-enabled finance capability within two years, & 44% say buyers are already asking in diligence without paying for it yet. events.name: AI & Future Of Education
events.description: AI & the Future of Education Artificial intelligence has caused seismic disruption in the field of education in just a few years. Students, educators, & parents are confused about how to navigate this game-changing technology. How should schools from K-12 to colleges & universities approach learning in this new era, & how can they prepare students for success in a transformed workplace? events.name: The Age Of AI  - Live Recording Of The Builders
events.description: Bestselling biographer Walter Isaacson joins us for a live recording of the first episode of his brand-new podcast, The Builders, with Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of Microsoft AI & one of the most influential thinkers & leaders working in artificial intelligence today. AI is reshaping our world at breathtaking speed. But behind the technology, real human beings are making choices about what our future will look like, how we'll work & live, & whose vision will shape what comes next. And as AI grows more powerful, so does the unease surrounding it. Will it usher in an era of extraordinary human possibility - or are we building something we may ultimately struggle to control? On The Builders, Walter Isaacson talks to the entrepreneurs, scientists & technologists building AI & other technologies that are rapidly reshaping our world to get inside the thinking of some of the most consequential figures of our time. Throughout his career, Isaacson has been fascinated by the people who change the world - from Leonardo da Vinci & Albert Einstein to Steve Jobs, Jennifer Doudna & Elon Musk. With The Builders, he turns his attention to the entrepreneurs, scientists & technologists building AI & the other technologies transforming our lives. For this special live recording, Isaacson sits down with Suleyman to go inside the ideas, ambitions & decisions driving the AI revolution. From fears about jobs & misinformation to the existential question of whether superintelligent machines could one day threaten humanity itself, the stakes can feel almost impossibly high. What does it mean to build technology with the power to reshape society? Who gets to decide where it takes us? Hear two singular thinkers explore the promise, power & profound questions of the AI age & the question at the heart of The Builders: whose imagination do we want to live in?

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Let's Talk About Jev
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a small, curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries - Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data. No talking, just thinking. 45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Let's Talk About Jev! A tiny AI startup called Jev just went viral for doing the opposite of what every other AI company is doing - it doesn't chat at all. Built by an ex-OpenAI researcher, Jev only returns fast, structured decisions (yes/no, multiple choice, confidence scores) instead of generating text, & it's reportedly fielding funding offers north of $10 billion just over a week after launch. We're decoding: Is Jev a genuinely new category of AI - a faster, cheaper layer sitting underneath the chatbots - or is this hype-cycle enthusiasm for something that's really just a narrow classifier with good marketing? Supporting questions: Does the "specialized model" approach threaten the big general-purpose LLMs, or complement them? What would it take for Jev's $10B valuation talk to actually make sense a year from now? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like. **Refunds available up to 48 hours before the session. After that, we are sorry but the fee is non-refundable.

events.name: Future Forum - Science For Society
events.description: The 2026 FUTURE FORUM will convene leaders from diverse backgrounds including academia, museums, journalism, media, public engagement, government, industry, & scientific organizations from the United States & Germany to explore how science can more effectively serve society through communication, collaboration, & public engagement. Centered on the theme Science for Society, the meeting will examine how trust in science is built & sustained, how scientific discoveries & long-term research can be communicated more effectively to diverse audiences, & how institutions can demonstrate the societal value of science. A panel discussion will address the roles of museums, journalists, policymakers, & other non-traditional science communicators; strategies for strengthening public confidence in science & evidence-based decision-making; the importance of open & international scientific collaboration amid increasing geopolitical pressures; & approaches to fostering public engagement, scientific literacy, & global collaboration. Through interdisciplinary dialogue & transatlantic relationship-building, the 2026 FUTURE FORUM aims to develop new partnerships, identify best practices, & strengthen the role of science communication in advancing an informed, engaged, & resilient society. About the FUTURE FORUM The FUTURE FORUM brings together experts from Germany, the United States, & beyond to exchange perspectives on emerging issues in science, innovation, & society. Through focused expert dialogue & public engagement, the format creates space to examine shared challenges, identify new perspectives, & strengthen transatlantic exchange. Previous editions have explored themes including Science Diplomacy in an Era of Technological Disruption at the Science Diplomacy Hub at Johns Hopkins University, Washington, D.C. in 2025. Or Health. Tech. Diplomacy., which focused on global health at the Broad Institute of MIT & Harvard in 2025. In 2026, the FUTURE FORUM returns with Science for Society, bringing together transatlantic experts to explore questions around science communication, public trust, scientific literacy, public engagement, & collaboration across disciplines & borders.

events.name: Sobremesa - Private Dinner For Latin American Founders
events.description: Twenty Latin American founders. One table. No stage, no badges, no programme. Sobremesa is the part of the meal nobody schedules - when the plates are cleared & the real conversation starts. That's the whole event. We skipped straight to it. This is not a mixer & it is not a pitch night. There is no panel & no deck. Just founders who are building between Latin America & the United States, at one table, talking about the parts they don't put on LinkedIn. The guest list is the product, so it is built by hand. Every application is reviewed. Who's at the tableFounders who have raised Seed or beyond, based in New York or operating here. Cross-sector by design - fintech next to healthtech next to logistics, because the useful conversations happen between people solving different problems with the same constraints. Our host sponsorDinner is covered by a sponsor who works with founders like the ones at this table. They'll say a few words at the start & then eat with everyone else. We pick partners whose work actually applies to this room - immigration, payroll, hiring across borders - so the conversation stays useful in both directions. Why October 16It closes a week. The night before, Ugly Talk NYC brings Latino founders on stage to tell the version they leave out of the pitch. This dinner is the smaller, quieter room the night after - same community, twenty seats instead of a hundred. Co-hosted by Christopher Martnez (Ziora Copilot) & Sharon Rao, MD. Nuestra gente, nuestra mesa.

events.name: The AI Founder Playbook, Rewritten
events.description: Invitation only  15 seats  Approval required For leaders of Series A+ startups building proprietary AI models, with a select number of seats reserved for investors. This is a roundtable, not a panel: everyone at the table is welcome to bring opinions. Some of the investors in the room: Merck Global Health Innovation Fund (GHI Fund) Presidio Ventures (Sumitomo Corporation) Morgan Stanley Ventures Lab Description: When AI compresses engineering cycles from months to days, the scarcest thing in a startup is no longer the ability to build. It's knowing what to build, for whom, & how to win when everyone can ship. That shift rewrites the founder's job. Moats move from code to data, distribution, & judgment. Team shapes change. Capital efficiency changes what "venture scale" even means. The playbooks most of us learned are quietly going out of date, & the new ones are being written right now, by the people in rooms like this one. The evening: Dinner & conversation with a curated table of ~15 founders, operators, & investors. Exceptional wines, thoughtfully curated cuisine, & original artwork. Guests will experience a thoughtfully curated progression of refined dishes, premium selections, & seasonal ingredients, accompanied by Cava Brut & Ros, Petit Chablis, & Malbec. The evening concludes with an exclusive dessert pairing & the Signature Cocktail, a bespoke finale to the experience. What we'll get into: What's newly easy, what's suddenly hard, & what that does to the first 18 months of a company Where defensibility actually lives when software is cheap How team composition & hiring change when one builder does the work of five What the next generation of founder playbooks will look like House rules:Off the record. No slides, no pitches, no recording. Come with a point of view.

events.name: Papers We Love
events.description: Papers We Love, Espresso AI, & Antithesis are pleased to present the September edition of PwL. Papers We Love is a community of programmers who love reading & discussing computer science papers. What was the last paper within the realm of computing you read & loved? What did it inspire you to build or tinker with? Come share the ideas in an awesome academic or research paper with fellow engineers, programmers, & paper-readers. Lead a session & show off code you wrote that implements these ideas, or just give us the lowdown on the paper. Otherwise, just come, listen, learn, & discuss. Speaker: Samuel Laferriere More about Sam: I'm a Staff Software Engineer at Seismic, where I work on the execution layer of an EVM-compatible privacy L1 - a reth fork running BFT consensus inside TDX enclaves. Before that I spent three years at EigenLabs, where I led the integrations team for EigenDA, a high-throughput BFT blobstore, building & maintaining its rollup integrations (Optimism, zkSync, & others). For the details, have a look at my resume. I work mostly in Rust & Go on distributed systems: BFT consensus + blobstore, EVM, & confidential compute. Before blockchain, I did academic research in robotics, developing Koopman-based control algorithms for self-driving cars & quadrotors. I completed my Master's degree at the Montreal Institute for Learning Algorithms (MILA), where I developed Bayesian optimization algorithms for neurostimulation, & before that earned my bachelor's in mathematics & computer science at McGill University. Paper: https://www.cs.virginia.edu/~evans/cs551/saltzer/ Title: What Saltzer & Schroeder knew in 1975 about the agents we're building in 2026 Supporting Papers: Hardy, The Confused Deputy (1988)  Miller, Yee & Shapiro, Capability Myths Demolished (2003) Outline: Every discussion of sandboxing AI agents starts with the wrong noun. Container or microVM? gVisor or WASI? Those choices answer where computation happens. They say nothing about what authority that computation can exercise - & an agent inside a perfectly isolated VM can still exfiltrate your source through an allowed API, spend your cloud credentials, or push to main. Saltzer & Schroeder framed the real problem fifty years ago, with three of their eight design principles directly relevant to agent sandboxing problem: 1. Complete mediation turns out to be the whole reason an LLM proxy counts as security rather than decoration: the sandbox is enforcement only if the workload cannot route around it. 2. Least privilege is where agents genuinely break the classical model, because an agent's useful authority changes with its plan - authority becomes a runtime protocol, not a static profile. 3. Saltzer & Schroeder warned that a protection mechanism people find annoying will be circumvented by the people it protects. Fifty years later, the most popular sandbox configuration in the industry is --dangerously-skip-permissions. To close, a detour through Hardy's two-page note from 1988. Prompt injection is not a new vulnerability class - it's the confused deputy with a natural-language calling convention, & an LLM is the perfect confused deputy: maximally helpful, broadly authorized, & structurally unable to tell a request from data. The fix Hardy proposed is the fix Google's CaMeL rediscovered in 2025. 6:30pm - Doors 7:00pm - Speaker begins PwL curate a repository of papers & places to find them. Contributions welcome via PR. Join the PWL Discord & hop into the #nyc channel: Join Discord Server Papers We Love has a Code of Conduct. Be good to each other & to the PWL community.

events.description: Learn How to SellSales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. Well cover how to identify and reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach and customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, and build the foundation for your first 100, and eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, and only scale the sales function when the business is ready.Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: NetworkingWho should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether youre preparing to launch, looking for your first 10100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, youll learn how to take ownership of sales and get closer to what customers actually want. Its especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, and generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets.- Bring a computer. You're writing three things tonight.- Most founders can get meetings. The deals die after meeting one.- You'll leave with your buyer in one sentence, a cold email written to a real person, and five questions for your next call.About Farzad, the speakerFarzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, and an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth and sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs and Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, and Blackstone. He has helped build and scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, and customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, and consumer brands.He has served as a fractional COO and CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) and Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding and generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the companys $140 million Series C.About Pioneering Minds AI:Atpioneeringminds.ai,we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, and govern AI responsibly and put humans at the front seat. events.name: Unique AI Presents - New AI Teammates
events.description: Meet Your AI Teammates: Remy, Casey, & IvyThree AI teammates, one perpetual memory.Any firm can deploy a generic AI assistant. But these tools weren't built to remember your clients or understand your relationships. Your firm already has the intelligence. What's missing is memory. What your firm knows about a client sits in inboxes, CRM notes, & people's heads. It gets rebuilt from scratch every time, & it walks out the door when someone leaves. Remy, Casey, & Ivy fix that - each one built for a different function, each backed by perpetual memory. Remy handles financial advisory, working the client lifecycle end to end - onboarding, meeting preparation, account review - backed by a continuously updated client memory. For compliance, Casey runs perpetual KYC & Source of Wealth work, flagging risk before it reaches a client. Her second brain holds the full relationship & case history. Ivy sits with investor relations, turning a living investor memory into faster, more consistent RFP & DDQ responses.   Join Dana Ritter, Chief Product Officer & the Unique AI Executive Leadership Team for a live look at the Teammates & what agentic AI can do for wealth & asset management.    Agenda 6:00 to 7:00 pm: Networking, drinks, hors d'oeuvres 7:00 to 7:45 pm: 7:00 to 7:20 pm: Launch & live demo 7:20 to 7:45 pm: Client testimonial 7:45 pm onward: Networking, drinks, hors d'oeuvres   What you'll see live We'll showcase how Remy helps advisors onboard clients, prep for meetings, & run account reviews - all while building a client memory that syncs back to your CRM. We'll also preview how Casey supports compliance teams & how Ivy helps investor relations teams manage RFP & DDQ workflows. Discover what agentic AI can do across all functions at your firm & connect with peers across wealth & asset management tackling the same questions.  Who should attend COOs, CTOs, & Heads of AI exploring agentic solutions to improve operational efficiency & scale technology investments within wealth & asset management platforms Financial Advisors, Wealth Advisors, & Relationship Managers who want to improve client prep, reduce administrative drag, & scale personalized service Heads of Compliance, KYC, & Financial Crime looking to modernize review & oversight workflows Heads of Investor Relations handling investor updates, DDQs, & RFPs at volume Learn more about Unique AI at unique.ai.

events.name: Decentralized AI Day
events.description: We're bringing together builders & long-time contributors from the Numerai & decentralized AI ecosystems for a mix of talks, a workshop, & a special community panel. Featured speakers: Jason - Co-Founder & CEO, CrowdCent Nick - Co-Founder & CEO, Allora Labs Matteo - Co-Founder & CEO, Orion Finance The Numerai "Out of Sample" Special Panel  A discussion & AMA-style panel with guests featured on the Out of Sample interview series. All three are current or former members of the Numerai Council of Elders, with the panel moderated by another member of the Council. Tim (aka jefferythewind) (see episode 2) ShatteredX (see episode 3) Jason (see episode 4) More speakers & session details coming soon. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/ Important Note  This is an in-person-only event; there will be no livestream. For security reasons, we must provide a guest list to the security team at least 24 hours before the event. You must provide your  FULL NAME  when registering for this event. If you prefer not to display your full name publicly, please provide it in the final registration question instead. Your full name will be shared only with the security team. About Decentralized AI Days  Decentralized AI Days are community-driven events exploring how open, decentralized AI & Web3 can work together in practice. We bring together engineers, researchers, & builders for a day of technical talks, hands-on workshops, & honest conversation - no hype, no sales pitches, & no pay-to-play. The ecosystem we care about includes projects such as Numerai & CrowdCent. The door is open to anyone building with or curious about decentralized AI. Come for the substance, stay for the community. Call for Presentations  Interested in sharing your experience with our community? Please contact me (Joe) directly via X, or on LinkedIn. I'll get back to you as soon as possible. Everyone is welcome to apply, as long as your talk or workshop topic is relevant. Agenda  More details will be announced soon! Expect a program of tech talks & workshops, followed by a relaxed evening mixer. What to Expect   Connect with a friendly community of AI & Web3 builders, researchers, & curious minds.  Enjoy zero-hype technical talks focused on real problems & practical insights.  Take part in hands-on workshops where you can learn by building.  Watch live demos of decentralized AI & related projects.  Meet the organizers & share your questions & feedback directly.  Explore community resources & connect over food. Who Should Attend)  Decentralized AI Days are for everyone curious about where AI & decentralized systems meet: AI/ML engineers, Web3 developers, researchers, students, & builders at any experience level. If you are new to the space, you are welcome; if you have been building for years, you will find your people here. Come ready to learn, share, & connect. The Venue  Register to see the address. Complimentary refreshments will be provided throughout the day. Event organizers will enforce these guidelines throughout the event. Sexually explicit language or imagery is inappropriate for any part of the event, including talks, workshops, social activities, or online platforms. Participants who violate these rules may be warned or expelled from the event at the discretion of the organizers. Past Events  Materials from past Decentralized AI Days live in the community meetups repository. We have also hosted similar events under a different name (Numerai Community Meetup) from 2022 to 2024: London (July 2022) New York (September 2022) Tokyo (April 2023) Prague (July 2023) Toronto (October 2023) San Francisco (January 2024) Frankfurt (April 2024) Tokyo (July 2024) Bangkok (November 2024) Finally, here's one meme to sum up the vibe.

events.description: Topic: Emerging, Non-obvious Needs for Industry in the Midst of Accelerating Climate Change.    Speaker: Naveen Krishnamurthy, SVP Executive Programs Lux Research Date: Monday October 5, 2026. Time: 5 pm. Online. KINDLY REGISTER TO ATTEND The recent fires in Southern Europe & France were a major reminder that climate change is not merely a weather risk, buried in sustainability reports. The fires hurt tourism, wine making & other agro-industries, electricity, transportation & supply chains. In France, more than 120,000 workers were temporarily unable to work. More than 14 were killed & roughly 350,000 were displaced from their homes. What are the as yet, widely unknown business risks from rising climate damage? What are the business opportunities? Which climate-related job skills will continue to be in demand by businesses, irrespective of favorable or unfavorable government policies?   These & related issues will be discussed by Naveen Krishnamurthy, SVP Lux Research. It provides research & tools to enhance performance across agrifoods, health, chemicals, utilities & other industries. Naveen advises companies on navigating multi-decade, growth strategies. events.name: Coding Agents w/ Elastic Memory + Evolution To Stateless Serverless
events.description: Kick off ElasticON week with the Elastic NYC User Group & Pulumi at our special pre-ElasticON NYC meetup on Tuesday, October 6! Engin Diri from Pulumi & Ines Potier from Elastic will share technical talks, followed by pizza, refreshments, & networking with the New York City tech community.  Continue the experience at ElasticON NYC ElasticON NYC takes place on Thursday, October 8, & registration is free! Connect with Elastic experts & the community, gain hands-on experience, & discover how the Elasticsearch Platform powers real-world AI, search, observability, & security solutions. Register for ElasticON NYC here  Date: Tuesday, October 6th from 6:00-8:00 PM  Location: Elastic NYC Office1250 Broadway, Floor 16, Training RoomNew York, NY 10001  Want to present at our next meetup?Are you interested in presenting your Elastic use case? We welcome 5-10 minute lightning talks, 45-minute deep dives, & everything in between. If you're interested, please send us an email at meetups@elastic.co. Agenda: 6:00 pm: Doors open; say hi & eat some food 6:30 pm: Give Your Coding Agent an (Elastic) Memory - Engin Diri (Pulumi) 7:10 pm: Stateless vs stateful: Learn how the stateful architecture was transformed into stateless for Serverless & why Ines Potier (Sr. Software Engineer at Elastic) 7:30 - 8:00 pm: Networking & event wrap-up  Talk Details:Give Your Coding Agent an (Elastic) Memory - Engin Diri (Pulumi)If you work with a coding agent every day, you know the routine. Each new session starts blank: the agent re-reads files it read yesterday, asks about decisions you settled last week, & redoes debugging you already finished. Its only memory is the context window, & that empties every time you close your laptop. Claude Code ships a built-in fix: markdown notes the agent writes for itself & reads back at the next session start. It helps, but the notes live on one machine, there is no real search, & anything past the first page of the index gets dropped. agent-memory, an open source project based on Elastic, takes the same idea further: memory lives in Elasticsearch, where decisions, tasks, & session history are searchable & shared across machines. I'll run both side by side, kill an agent mid-task, & show how much more a fresh one remembers when its memory is a search engine instead of a text file. And here comes Pulumi: one command creates everything in Elastic Cloud, it lives in a repo you can review, & every teammate gets an identical memory backend instead of their own snowflake. No promises about becoming a 1000x AI engineer, but your agent will stop asking you the same question twice. Stateless vs stateful: Learn how the stateful architecture was transformed into stateless for Serverless & why Ines Potier (Sr. Software Engineer at Elastic) Details coming soon!

events.name: PMAI - Creativity & Business Problems In Age Of AI
events.description: Creativity & Business Problems in the Age of AI - a workshop for entrepreneursWe are entering a strange moment for creativity. For decades, we have been taught that innovation comes from thinking outside the box, brainstorming more ideas, & waiting for that breakthrough moment. But in the age of AI, & ideas are suddenly abundant, the real challenge is no longer simply coming up with more ideas. It is knowing how to find the right pieces, make unexpected connections, & turn them into something genuinely new & useful. This hands-on workshop, led by our head of program Jeffrey, introduces a practical methodology for doing exactly that. What we'll cover We'll start by looking at some of the traditional assumptions behind creativity & innovation: brainstorming, originality, intuition, & the idea of the lone creative genius, & why some of those assumptions are becoming less useful in an AI-native world. We'll then introduce a different way to approach creative problem-solving: instead of trying to invent the answer from scratch, you'll learn how to break a problem apart, deliberately search for useful precedents & ideas, & recombine existing elements in new ways. Through real-world case studies, we'll examine how successful products, businesses, & innovations often emerge not from a completely original idea, but from making the right connection between things that already exist. Most importantly, this will not be a lecture. You'll work through the methodology yourself, apply it to actual business problems, & leave with a framework you can reuse when thinking about products, positioning, growth, operations, or your next startup idea. Who should attend This workshop is designed primarily for: Early-stage founders, aspiring entrepreneurs, small business owners, product builders, & operators who regularly need to solve ambiguous problems with limited resources. No technical background is required. If you have ever stared at a blank page thinking, I need a better idea, this workshop is for you. Come with a problem. Leave with a different way of thinking about it.

events.description: Distribution is Your Moat: A series on Distribution & Marketing for Startups August 6 9:30 am: Innovation Is Your Moat ft. Alex Chung Presented by Surface AI "As the cost of code goes to zero, distribution is your only moat." While marketing, distribution, & go-to-market are established fields with many tried & true methods, each startup's playbook will be as unique as its company. To help companies understand, define, & grow their distribution, Ari Spool of Surface AI brings together a selection of startup marketing leaders for a breakfast panel to strategize. Refreshments by Donut Pub. Alex Chung is Head of Growth at System, a telehealth company built around clinician-prescribed peptide therapies. Alex has worked on both sides of the growth equation. Before System, she led growth at a consumer AI startup. Before that, she invested as a venture capitalist. That mix shapes how she evaluates markets, builds trust in unfamiliar categories, & turns early attention into real revenue. She holds a bachelor's degree from the University of Chicago & an MBA from Chicago Booth. This conversation gets into the core challenge of her work: how to take a product that customers don't fully understand, build credibility around it, find the right audience, & convert interest into lasting growth. The principles apply well beyond telehealth. Outside of work, Alex is training for her third marathon, in Tokyo. Surface AI is an autonomous landing-page optimization engine. We connect to your existing site with one line of code - a quick setup through your CMS. From there Surface automatically generates & tests new headlines, CTAs, layouts, & images in brand voice, shifting traffic toward what's winning & continuously optimizing over time. All attendees will receive a free 14-day trial of Surface!

events.name: The Quantified Self - What AI Can Actually Tell US About Our Data
events.description: This year, ChatGPT started connecting to people's medical records & Apple Health data, & a glucose sensor no longer needs a prescription. Gary Wolf (Co-founder, Quantified Self; longtime WIRED writer & editor) has studied how people make sense of their own data for 20 years. Hear what AI now makes possible for users, & how founders can build answers people trust. This year, OpenAI started letting people connect their medical records & Apple Health data to ChatGPT.  Since 2024, Americans can buy a continuous glucose monitor without a prescription. For most of the Quantified Self movement's history, answering a question with your own data meant manual logs & spreadsheets. Today a sensor collects the data & an AI model analyzes it on demand. That leaves every founder building in this space with one hard question: when an AI's answer changes what someone eats or takes, how do they know it's right? Gary Wolf has spent nearly 20 years watching people try to answer questions with their own data.  He co-founded Quantified Self with Kevin Kelly, joined the WIRED editorial team in 1994, became the first executive producer of Wired Digital, & launched Wired News. His New York Times Magazine cover story on self-tracking brought the practice to a mainstream audience, & his TED talk on the subject has been watched more than a million times. His current work is about AI & personal data. He's researching a cryptographic protocol to prove where sensor data came from at the moment it's recorded, & writing essays on how people talk to AI chatbots.  His new book, The Quantified Self: Learning to Observe, lays out a method anyone can use to test a question against their own data. On Thursday, October 15, Gary joins Startup Grind to talk about what AI changes for people using their own data, & what that means for the founders building those products. WHAT YOU'LL LEARN What AI changed for self-trackers: The analysis Quantified Self members once did by hand, & what a user can now do in one conversation with a model.When to trust a model's answer: How to tell when an AI reading of your sleep or blood sugar holds up, & what a user needs before acting on it.Proving where data came from: Gary's research on verifying sensor data at the moment it's recorded, & what it means for products that make health claims.Building around the user's question: The question, observe, reason, discover method from his new book, & how to design a product around what a user is actually asking. WHO SHOULD ATTEND AI health & wellness founders: Your model tells people what their data means, & they're going to act on it.Wearable & sensor founders: You collect the data, & your users can now hand it to an AI to interpret.AI product builders in any category: You're shipping personalized advice & want to hear from someone who has studied how people make sense of their own numbers for nearly 2 decades.Founders who track themselves: You've already asked a chatbot about your sleep data & want to know how far to trust the answer.Tickets for this event include food & drinks, as well as time with Gary after the chat to ask about your own product.  BONUS: you'll have an opportunity to purchase Gary's new book & get your copy signed by the author, himself! You'll also meet dozens of other high-performing entrepreneurs who are creating their next big thing. Seriously, it's some of the best founder networking in the city. Getting a ticket guarantees admission. No waitlisting. AGENDA 6:00 PM: Networking, Food & Drinks7:00 PM: Fireside Chat with Gary Wolf8:00 PM: Meet the Speaker + Book SigningAnd don't miss our other monthly tech events. They are great opportunities for builders, founders, & operators to network with each other to share best practices & find new resources to grow your startup the right way. See our full event lineup here.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Reality Of Data Centers In Space
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a small, curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for.Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data. No talking, just thinking. 45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: The Reality of Data Centers in SpaceStarcloud just raised $250M to build satellites that run AI workloads in orbit, joining Google's "Project Suncatcher" & a SpaceX effort in a race to solve AI's power problem by moving compute off the planet entirely. The pitch is compelling - unlimited solar power, no water usage - but basic questions about heat dissipation, launch costs, & maintenance remain mostly unanswered. We're decoding: Is space-based computing a real solution to AI's real estate & energy issues? Supporting questions: What would actually have to be true for orbital data centers to beat a terrestrial one on cost? Who's positioned to win this race - the well-funded startups (Starcloud), or the hyperscalers who already have the capital & infrastructure (Google, SpaceX)? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like. **Refunds available up to 48 hours before the session. After that, we are sorry but the fee is non-refundable.

events.name: Bridging Adherence Gap - How Can Tech Help People Stay On Their Treatment
events.description: At its core, adherence is a deeply human problem. We know following through with a treatment plan improves our health, but in the moment, taking that immediate next step isn't always easy. The root causes are complex-ranging from forgetfulness & fear of side effects to a lack of visible benefits & high costs. Yet, despite billions of dollars invested in digital health tools, smart devices, & patient support programs, the core statistic remains stubbornly unchanged: roughly 50% of patients still fail to take chronic medications as prescribed over the long term. With rapid shifts in consumer behavior & technology, healthcare companies have unprecedented opportunities to engage with patients.  Join Smart Design as we bring together experts from across the industry to explore how we can apply new technology to the messiness of everyday life & the healthcare system to drive real, lasting health outcomes.

Think remittance transparency, credit-building for thin-file borrowers, small business bookkeeping for cash operations, benefits & tax navigation, fraud protection for first-generation account holders. Prizes$4,500 total - $1,500 per track. Every track winner also gets [sponsor perks once confirmed]. ScheduleSchedule 10:00 AM - Doors, breakfast, team formation10:45 AM - Opening remarks & track briefings11:15 AM - Building starts1:00 PM - Lunch3:00 PM - Mentor office hours & mid-day checkpoint4:45 PM - Submissions close5:00 PM - Demos on stage5:45 PM - Judging & awards6:00 PM - Close Who Should ApplyEngineers, data scientists, & designers who want to ship something real in a day Product people & founders who can shape a problem & pitch it Clinicians, immigration attorneys, paralegals, social workers, & financial counselors - the people who know the problem from the inside. events.description: Plug & Play x PMAI Hackathon: Rapid Response #AIWeekNYThree challenges. Three rounds. 45 minutes each. Most hackathons give you hours - sometimes days - to solve one problem. Rapid Fire is different. In this fast-paced, emergency-response-themed hackathon, participants will compete in teams of 2-4 across a series of short challenges designed to test how quickly you can understand a problem, make decisions, build a solution, & communicate your thinking under pressure. Each round will introduce a new emergency-response scenario. Your team will have roughly 45 minutes to develop & submit a solution before moving immediately into the next challenge. No long build cycle. No endless polishing. You'll have to prioritize what matters, divide responsibilities quickly, & make tradeoffs in real time. How It Works Participants will form teams of 2-4 people. Over the course of the event, teams will face 3-4 short emergency-response challenges, revealed one at a time. For each round: A new problem is announced Teams have approximately 45 minutes to respond Teams submit their solution before the deadline Judges score the submissions The next challenge begins Scores accumulate across the rounds, & the team with the strongest overall performance wins. The challenges may involve areas such as emergency coordination, communication, resource allocation, information management, public safety, or rapid decision-making. What Are We Looking For? You do not need to build a fully finished product. Depending on the challenge, your submission could be a prototype, workflow, AI agent, product concept, operational system, or another practical solution. What matters is your ability to: Identify the real problem.Prioritize under pressure.Build quickly.Make smart tradeoffs.Explain why your solution works. Who Should Join? This event is designed for a mix of: Engineers, designers, product managers, founders, operators, students, & anyone interested in building with AI. You do not need to be highly technical to participate. Strong teams will likely combine different skill sets - technical, product, design, operations, & strategy. Come with teammates or meet people at the event. Why Rapid Fire? Real emergencies rarely give you perfect information, unlimited resources, or weeks to plan. They demand fast thinking, clear priorities, & decisive execution. Rapid Fire is an experiment in building the same way: under constraints, against the clock, & as a team. Think fast. Build fast. Respond faster. Schedule5:00 - 5:30  Check-in, Team Formation & Food5:30 - 5:45  Keynote: Sharing by PMAI Team5:45 - 6:30  First Problem6:30 - 7:15  Second Problem7:15 - 8:00  Third Problem8:00 - 8:30  Judging Session8:30 - 9:00  Winners Announcement & Group Photos Sponsorship Enquiry: https://community.pioneeringminds.ai/forms/c50df13a About Plug & PlayPlug & Play is the leading innovation platform, connecting startups, corporations, venture capital firms, universities, & government agencies. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, we're present in 60+ locations across 25+ industries. We offer corporate innovation programs, helping our partners in every stage of their innovation journey, from education to execution. We also run startup acceleration programs & have built an in-house VC where we've invested in hundreds of successful companies including Dropbox, Guardant Health, Honey, Lending Club, N26, PayPal, & Rappi. For more information, visit Plug & Play. About Vibranium LabsAt Vibranium Labs, we build Tony SRE, a 24/7 OnCall AI Incident Commander that proactively hunts down production issues before engineers ever get paged. We help hyperscaling startups & enterprises stay ahead of incidents, cut the 3am wake-ups, & ship with confidence.We're backed by Plug & Play, a16z, Franklin Templeton, Gaingels, & others. Our mission: Get ahead of incidents, not just respond: Tony SRE proactively investigates your systems around the clock, surfacing issues & root causes before anyone gets paged. Kill on-call burnout: Give teams their nights & weekends back by catching problems early, so humans step in only when it truly matters. Build lasting reliability: Every incident makes Tony SRE smarter. It learns your systems, improves your workflows, & becomes the living runbook your team actually uses. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. events.name: [AI Briefing] Private Equity - What Owners & Buyers Pay For
events.description: The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise.  This month's source: The PE AI Adoption Benchmark: From scaling to systematizing (Accordion with Wakefield Research - May 2026) Somebody's going to ask what your AI spend returned. If your company has a board or an eventual buyer, that question is already scheduled. Private equity gets asked first, so that's where this month's data comes from. Accordion surveyed 150 technology & AI operating partners at PE sponsors about the finance functions inside their portfolios. 41% are scaling AI across multiple companies with no operational playbook, & only 29% describe their firm as systematizing or leading. 75% of those companies arrived at acquisition unprepared or only partially ready for any of it. 86% of these operating partners expect buyers to pay a premium for AI-enabled finance capability within two years, & 44% say buyers are already asking in diligence without paying for it yet. Conviction is running ahead of price. The deployment that worked & left no evidence behind it is the one that costs you at exit. 67% of firms measure hours recovered. 29% put AI impact in front of a board.  The Mission: Building the evidence a board or a buyer will accept We'll work the measurement problem directly: which AI metrics connect to EBITDA, & how a company gets there without starting over. We'll examine why only 14% of portfolio finance functions have crossed from back-office automation into real decision intelligence, & what the rest are paying for instead.  The Format: The benchmark, fast: Five findings & the numbers under them, including the ones that don't hold up. Translating it out of PE: Sponsors run this test on a clock, so the pressure shows up there first. We'll take what it exposes & apply it to companies with other kinds of owners. Cross-pollinated debate: Operators compare what agentic finance already does in production (58% report automated covenant monitoring, 44% report AI-drafted board packages) against what their own governance can defend today.  Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: Leave with the measures a buyer or board will scrutinize, & an honest read on which ones you could produce this quarter. Founders & Builders: See what sponsors & portfolio CFOs are buying, & where the 47% assembling AI tools case-by-case stall out before anything compounds. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Compare notes on the constraint everything else runs into. Poor data infrastructure ranked first among all barriers by a wide margin, ahead of talent, legacy systems, change management, & budget. Most of it arrives at close & gets fixed while the books are closing.  The Prep: This is a working session, not a lecture. Read the report here. Bring your perspective.

events.name: Papers We Love
events.description: Papers We Love, Espresso AI, & Antithesis are pleased to present the September edition of PwL. Papers We Love is a community of programmers who love reading & discussing computer science papers. What was the last paper within the realm of computing you read & loved? What did it inspire you to build or tinker with? Come share the ideas in an awesome academic or research paper with fellow engineers, programmers, & paper-readers. Lead a session & show off code you wrote that implements these ideas, or just give us the lowdown on the paper. Otherwise, just come, listen, learn, & discuss. Speaker: Samuel Laferriere More about Sam: I'm a Staff Software Engineer at Seismic, where I work on the execution layer of an EVM-compatible privacy L1 - a reth fork running BFT consensus inside TDX enclaves. Before that I spent three years at EigenLabs, where I led the integrations team for EigenDA, a high-throughput BFT blobstore, building & maintaining its rollup integrations (Optimism, zkSync, & others). For the details, have a look at my resume. I work mostly in Rust & Go on distributed systems: BFT consensus + blobstore, EVM, & confidential compute. Before blockchain, I did academic research in robotics, developing Koopman-based control algorithms for self-driving cars & quadrotors. I completed my Master's degree at the Montreal Institute for Learning Algorithms (MILA), where I developed Bayesian optimization algorithms for neurostimulation, & before that earned my bachelor's in mathematics & computer science at McGill University. Paper: https://www.cs.virginia.edu/~evans/cs551/saltzer/ Title: What Saltzer & Schroeder knew in 1975 about the agents we're building in 2026 Supporting Papers: Hardy, The Confused Deputy (1988)  Miller, Yee & Shapiro, Capability Myths Demolished (2003) Outline: Every discussion of sandboxing AI agents starts with the wrong noun. Container or microVM? gVisor or WASI? Those choices answer where computation happens. They say nothing about what authority that computation can exercise - & an agent inside a perfectly isolated VM can still exfiltrate your source through an allowed API, spend your cloud credentials, or push to main. Saltzer & Schroeder framed the real problem fifty years ago, with three of their eight design principles directly relevant to agent sandboxing problem: 1. Complete mediation turns out to be the whole reason an LLM proxy counts as security rather than decoration: the sandbox is enforcement only if the workload cannot route around it. 2. Least privilege is where agents genuinely break the classical model, because an agent's useful authority changes with its plan - authority becomes a runtime protocol, not a static profile. 3. Saltzer & Schroeder warned that a protection mechanism people find annoying will be circumvented by the people it protects. Fifty years later, the most popular sandbox configuration in the industry is --dangerously-skip-permissions. To close, a detour through Hardy's two-page note from 1988. Prompt injection is not a new vulnerability class - it's the confused deputy with a natural-language calling convention, & an LLM is the perfect confused deputy: maximally helpful, broadly authorized, & structurally unable to tell a request from data. The fix Hardy proposed is the fix Google's CaMeL rediscovered in 2025. 6:30pm - Doors 7:00pm - Speaker begins PwL curate a repository of papers & places to find them. Contributions welcome via PR. Join the PWL Discord & hop into the #nyc channel: Join Discord Server Papers We Love has a Code of Conduct. Be good to each other & to the PWL community.

events.name: The Quantified Self - What AI Can Actually Tell US About Our Data
events.description: This year, ChatGPT started connecting to people's medical records & Apple Health data, & a glucose sensor no longer needs a prescription. Gary Wolf (Co-founder, Quantified Self; longtime WIRED writer & editor) has studied how people make sense of their own data for 20 years. Hear what AI now makes possible for users, & how founders can build answers people trust. This year, OpenAI started letting people connect their medical records & Apple Health data to ChatGPT.  Since 2024, Americans can buy a continuous glucose monitor without a prescription. For most of the Quantified Self movement's history, answering a question with your own data meant manual logs & spreadsheets. Today a sensor collects the data & an AI model analyzes it on demand. That leaves every founder building in this space with one hard question: when an AI's answer changes what someone eats or takes, how do they know it's right? Gary Wolf has spent nearly 20 years watching people try to answer questions with their own data.  He co-founded Quantified Self with Kevin Kelly, joined the WIRED editorial team in 1994, became the first executive producer of Wired Digital, & launched Wired News. His New York Times Magazine cover story on self-tracking brought the practice to a mainstream audience, & his TED talk on the subject has been watched more than a million times. His current work is about AI & personal data. He's researching a cryptographic protocol to prove where sensor data came from at the moment it's recorded, & writing essays on how people talk to AI chatbots.  His new book, The Quantified Self: Learning to Observe, lays out a method anyone can use to test a question against their own data. On Thursday, October 15, Gary joins Startup Grind to talk about what AI changes for people using their own data, & what that means for the founders building those products. WHAT YOU'LL LEARN What AI changed for self-trackers: The analysis Quantified Self members once did by hand, & what a user can now do in one conversation with a model.When to trust a model's answer: How to tell when an AI reading of your sleep or blood sugar holds up, & what a user needs before acting on it.Proving where data came from: Gary's research on verifying sensor data at the moment it's recorded, & what it means for products that make health claims.Building around the user's question: The question, observe, reason, discover method from his new book, & how to design a product around what a user is actually asking. WHO SHOULD ATTEND AI health & wellness founders: Your model tells people what their data means, & they're going to act on it.Wearable & sensor founders: You collect the data, & your users can now hand it to an AI to interpret.AI product builders in any category: You're shipping personalized advice & want to hear from someone who has studied how people make sense of their own numbers for nearly 2 decades.Founders who track themselves: You've already asked a chatbot about your sleep data & want to know how far to trust the answer.Tickets for this event include food & drinks, as well as time with Gary after the chat to ask about your own product.  BONUS: you'll have an opportunity to purchase Gary's new book & get your copy signed by the author, himself! You'll also meet dozens of other high-performing entrepreneurs who are creating their next big thing. Seriously, it's some of the best founder networking in the city. Getting a ticket guarantees admission. No waitlisting. AGENDA 6:00 PM: Networking, Food & Drinks7:00 PM: Fireside Chat with Gary Wolf8:00 PM: Meet the Speaker + Book SigningAnd don't miss our other monthly tech events. They are great opportunities for builders, founders, & operators to network with each other to share best practices & find new resources to grow your startup the right way. See our full event lineup here.

events.name: Latinos x AI Hackathon
events.description: Latinos x AI Hackathon - NYCSaturday, October 10  10:00 AM - 6:00 PM  New York City Nuestra gente. Nuestros problemas. Nuestro cdigo. For Hispanic Heritage Month, 150 builders are spending one Saturday in New York building AI for the problems our communities actually live with. Not a demo day. Not a panel. Eight hours, three tracks, working software by 5pm. Applications are reviewed. Attendance is free. The Three TracksPick one when you apply. Build for it all day. 01  Immigration - Papers & Process Status, documents, deadlines, & the systems that decide who belongs. Think intake triage for legal aid clinics, plain-language explainers for immigration forms, interpreter tooling, case-status tracking, know-your-rights assistants. 02  Healthcare - Care Without Barriers Language, coverage, & access for patients the system was not built for. Think interpretation at the point of care, insurance navigation, discharge instructions people can actually read, community health worker tooling, prescription & benefits literacy. 03  Finance - Banking the Unbanked Credit, remittances, & building wealth without a financial history. Think remittance transparency, credit-building for thin-file borrowers, small business bookkeeping for cash operations, benefits & tax navigation, fraud protection for first-generation account holders. Prizes$4,500 total - $1,500 per track. Every track winner also gets [sponsor perks once confirmed]. ScheduleSchedule 10:00 AM - Doors, breakfast, team formation10:45 AM - Opening remarks & track briefings11:15 AM - Building starts1:00 PM - Lunch3:00 PM - Mentor office hours & mid-day checkpoint4:45 PM - Submissions close5:00 PM - Demos on stage5:45 PM - Judging & awards6:00 PM - Close Who Should ApplyEngineers, data scientists, & designers who want to ship something real in a day Product people & founders who can shape a problem & pitch it Clinicians, immigration attorneys, paralegals, social workers, & financial counselors - the people who know the problem from the inside. You do not need to code to be valuable here. Teams with a domain expert consistently win. Students & career switchers You can apply solo or with a team of up to four. Solo applicants will be matched at 10:00 AM. What to BringLaptop & charger A problem you have seen up close ID for building security We provide breakfast, lunch, coffee, wifi, power, mentors, & the room. RulesBuild during the event. Prior research & planning are fine; prior code is not. Teams of one to four. Every submission needs a public repo, a two-minute demo video, & a short written description. You keep everything you build. No IP claims from organizers or sponsors. Be decent to each other. Harassment of any kind means you leave. Mentors & Judges[ADD once confirmed: names, titles, organizations.] Partners & Sponsors[ADD once confirmed: logos & names.] Interested in sponsoring or partnering? Write to chris@ziora-copilot.com or book 30 minutes. Sponsorship closes October 1. FAQIs it free? Yes. Applications are reviewed because space is limited to 150. Where is it? New York City. The exact address is shared with approved attendees. Do I have to be Latino to attend? No. The event is built by & for the Latino community in New York, & everyone who wants to build for these problems is welcome. Do I need a team? No. Come solo & we will match you at the start. What language is the event in? English, with Spanish spoken throughout. Apply & demo in whichever you prefer. Can I keep working on my project afterward? Please do. That is the point. A note on selection: This edition is built for & centered on the Latino community in New York. Applications from Latino & Hispanic builders will be prioritized. Allies are welcome to apply & will be considered as space allows. Questions: chris@ziora-copilot.com Hosted by Christopher Martinez

events.name: Token Economics - Why Cost Kills More AI Projects Than Hallucinations
events.description: Token costs have overtaken hallucinations as the top reason enterprise AI projects die before reaching production; it's cited by 29% of technical leaders as the primary production killer, ahead of every reliability failure combined. The teams seeing success don't treat inference cost as an after-the-fact line item. They architect for token costs from the beginning. This event examines what that shift actually looks like in practice: GPU memory & data architecture decisions that determine cost per token served & the orchestration choices that separate a project that survives its second budget review from one that doesn't. We'll open with new VentureBeat Pulse Research on how enterprises are - & aren't - measuring the economics of the AI they're already running. This isn't a panel. It's a small group of peers, over drinks, working through the hardest question in enterprise AI right now. Featured Speakers: An evening conversation & drinks with a small number of enterprise AI leaders, kept intentionally close to keep the conversation substantive.

events.name: PMAI: Sell Me This AI - A No BS Sales Workshop
events.description: Learn How to SellSales goes without saying is one of, if not the most critical problem that most AI startup faces (and VCs care an awful lot). This hands-on workshop will give early-stage founders a practical playbook for founder-led sales, before hiring an expensive sales team or committing significant budget to customer acquisition. Well cover how to identify and reach your first customers when nobody knows your name, run effective outreach and customer conversations, turn early wins into a repeatable sales motion, and build the foundation for your first 100, and eventually 1,000 customers. The goal is simple: learn to sell your product yourself, validate what works, and only scale the sales function when the business is ready.Agenda6:00 p.m.: Doors open6:30 p.m.: Workshop begins7:15 p.m.: Q&A7:30 p.m.: NetworkingWho should attend?This workshop is built for early-stage founders who need customers before they need a sales team. Whether youre preparing to launch, looking for your first 10100 customers, or still figuring out a repeatable sales motion, youll learn how to take ownership of sales and get closer to what customers actually want. Its especially useful for founders who want to validate demand, sharpen their pitch, build an early pipeline, and generate revenue without prematurely committing to expensive sales hires, agencies, or large acquisition budgets.- Bring a computer. You're writing three things tonight.- Most founders can get meetings. The deals die after meeting one.- You'll leave with your buyer in one sentence, a cold email written to a real person, and five questions for your next call.About Farzad, the speakerFarzad Khosravi is a three-time founder, fractional COO, owner of the snack brand Hot Date Kitchen, and an ICF-trained executive coach who has built a dozen growth and sales teams. He has coached over 100 sales ICs and Managers at Fortune 500 companies like Salesforce, HP, PayPal, ServiceNow, and Blackstone. He has helped build and scale teams across product, engineering, go-to-market, and customer success, with operating roles spanning venture-backed startups, enterprise software, and consumer brands.He has served as a fractional COO and CPO for multiple high-growth startups. Most recently, he served as a Fractional COO/CPO for Humoniq (YC S25, $8.5M raised) and Chief Rebel ($2M raised). At a dozen other companies, his leadership has helped secure $10 million in funding and generate millions in revenue. Earlier in his career, he built the Customer Success department at Nylas from scratch, scaling it into a full customer-facing organization through the companys $140 million Series C.About Pioneering Minds AI:Atpioneeringminds.ai,we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, and govern AI responsibly and put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI and create real value out of AI.Our mission is straightforward:Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes.Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teamsstudents, engineers, and civic leadersto tackle urban challenges head-on.Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship and post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend.

events.name: Ugly Talk - Hispanic Heritage Month
events.description: Building between Latin America & the U.S. gets ugly fast. Markets move differently. Customers expect different things. Teams cross borders & cultures. The pitch deck leaves that part out. This Ugly Talk puts it back in. 3 Latino founders will share the false starts, hard calls, & mistakes behind the growth.  Why you should be in this room.Hear what building across Latin America & the U.S. actually takes. Learn from failed ideas, wrong turns, & hard calls. Get specific lessons from founders still in the thick of it. See how other builders handle different markets, customers, teams, & cultures. Meet founders who understand the friction because they live it too.  What's on the table.The version that missed the pitch deck. The false starts, setbacks, & calls they wish they could take back. Decisions made without a clean answer. The bets they placed before the outcome was clear. Building across borders. The real friction behind different markets, teams, customers, & cultures. Lessons earned the hard way. What helped after the original plan stopped working. The next hard call. What they would do differently if they started again.  Featured speakers.Christopher Saravia - Founder & CEO, Carebox HealthTech entrepreneur with 20+ years building, scaling, buying & selling companies.  Who's hosting it.Christopher Martinez - Founder & CEO, Ziora Copilot Christopher Martinez is the Founder & CEO of Ziora Copilot & Chapter Leader for AI Tinkerers, Health2Tech & Ugly Talk in Mexico City. He splits his time between Mexico City & New York & has produced founder & healthtech events at Google, One World Trade Center, BBVA & Tecnolgico de Monterrey, IBERO, each bringing together 50-150 founders, operators & investors from across the local ecosystem.  Who's getting in.LatAm founders building between Latin America & the U.S. Builders managing cross-border customers, markets, & teams. Founders at different stages who are still doing the work. An application-only room built for honest conversation.  About Ugly TalkStarted in 2019, Ugly Talk has been transforming business setbacks into breakthrough "aha!" moments by hosting unfiltered, no-nonsense events where battle-tested entrepreneurs share their raw lessons & insights. With a growing presence in cities like New York, Chicago, San Francisco, & Miami, we've built a vibrant community of thousands of founders & industry leaders making a profound impact on the entrepreneurial landscape. Official Website: UglyTalk.com  Important Notice for Ugly Talk AttendeesAdmission & Confirmation Attendance is by approval only. Approved guests will receive a confirmation email along with a calendar invite. Invitations are non-transferable. Additional event details will be shared as the event approaches. Code of Conduct By attending, you agree to: Maintain respect & professionalism, adhering to all venue rules, policies, & applicable laws. Refrain from harassment, discrimination, unwelcome sexual advances (verbal or physical), intimidation, or inappropriate photography/recording. Report any violations to the event hosts immediately. Violations may result in immediate removal from the event & exclusion from future invitations. Liability & Risk Participation is voluntary & at your own risk. events.name: Scene By Scene - Brand Relevance, Video AI & Next Era Of CTV
events.description: As billions of advertising dollars shift to Connected TV, the industry is entering a new era. The challenge is no longer simply reaching the right audience - it's ensuring every advertising dollar reaches viewers at exactly the right moment. New advances in AI - including scene-level understanding that can interpret video content with unprecedented context - are transforming how premium video inventory is valued, bought, & sold. Join an invitation-only gathering of the voices defining the future of brands & CTV. From the leaders responsible for the world's largest advertising budgets to the innovators building the next generation of AI & video technology, this evening will feature an intimate fireside conversation, followed by networking among the industry's top decision-makers.   About NVIDIA NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) is the world leader in AI & accelerated computing. Its platforms power work across data centers, graphics, robotics, & autonomous systems, & underpin much of the AI infrastructure the technology industry runs on today.   About PYLER PYLER is an AI-driven company specializing in video understanding & brand safety for digital advertising. Its core product, AiD, interprets video, audio, & metadata in real time to ensure ads appear in safe, relevant, trusted contexts. PYLER is a winner of the 2025 NVIDIA Inception Startup Grand Challenge.   About Supermomos Supermomos is a community platform connecting more than 35,000 founders, investors, & operators across New York, Boston, San Francisco, London, & Singapore. We host curated gatherings that bring together the people building & funding what comes next.  Speakers:Matt Groshong, Business Development Director, AdTech & MarTech, NVIDIA: Matt Groshong is a Business Development Director at NVIDIA, covering AdTech & MarTech. He has been in technology, advertising & media long enough to remember when "digital" was a separate budget line, & now spends most of his time helping the ecosystem work out what AI & accelerated computing actually do for them, rather than what the keynote said they would. Lately he is preoccupied with agentic systems, & what happens to marketing when the software starts making its own decisions. Before NVIDIA he was an Account CTO at Microsoft, aligned to WPP, & EMEA CTO at McCann Worldgroup. Earlier stops include the BBC, ServiceNow & the Newspaper Licensing Agency. He started his career at Microsoft, so the loop is closed. He lives in North London with his wife, three children, a cat, a dog, & more bikes than he will admit to anyone who isn't a cyclist. Jaeho Oh, Co-Founder & CEO, PYLER ($40M raised): Jaeho Oh is the founder & CEO of PYLER. Under his leadership, the company has scaled to 2 million videos analyzed a day, the equivalent of 60 years of content every 24 hours, for advertisers including Samsung & Kenvue. He sold his first company, a port decentralization protocol startup, at 18. He spoke on multi-modal video intelligence at NVIDIA GTC 2026 & has been named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 list.

events.name: Tech x Market Decoders - Personal AI Agents, Muse, Instinct & Fight For Your Inbox
events.description: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a small, curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data. No talking, just thinking. 45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Personal AI agents - Muse, Instinct, & the fight for your inbox Meta's new agent Muse hit #1 on the App Store within 10 days of launch, passing ChatGPT - while a much smaller startup, Instinct, is quietly building a following by working entirely through text message, no app required. Both agents now book things, send emails, & make purchases on your behalf, & both have already run into real trust & privacy controversies. We're decoding: Are personal AI agents actually ready to be trusted with your accounts & money? Supporting questions: What's the real difference between "an agent that acts for you" & "a chatbot that answers you" - & does that difference justify the privacy trade-off? Does Meta's distribution advantage make Muse the inevitable winner, or does Instinct's leaner, invite-only approach have a real shot? What if Google, Apple & others launch personal AI Agents like Muse? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like. **Refunds available up to 48 hours before the session. After that, we are sorry but the fee is non-refundable.
