events.name: Plug&Play x PMAI Hackathon - Rapid Response
events.description: Plug & Play x PMAI Hackathon: Rapid Response #AIWeekNYThree challenges. Three rounds. 45 minutes each. Most hackathons give you hours - sometimes days - to solve one problem. Rapid Fire is different. In this fast-paced, emergency-response-themed hackathon, participants will compete in teams of 2-4 across a series of short challenges designed to test how quickly you can understand a problem, make decisions, build a solution, & communicate your thinking under pressure. Each round will introduce a new emergency-response scenario. Your team will have roughly 45 minutes to develop & submit a solution before moving immediately into the next challenge. No long build cycle. No endless polishing. You'll have to prioritize what matters, divide responsibilities quickly, & make tradeoffs in real time. How It Works Participants will form teams of 2-4 people. Over the course of the event, teams will face 3-4 short emergency-response challenges, revealed one at a time. For each round: A new problem is announced Teams have approximately 45 minutes to respond Teams submit their solution before the deadline Judges score the submissions The next challenge begins Scores accumulate across the rounds, & the team with the strongest overall performance wins. The challenges may involve areas such as emergency coordination, communication, resource allocation, information management, public safety, or rapid decision-making. What Are We Looking For? You do not need to build a fully finished product. Depending on the challenge, your submission could be a prototype, workflow, AI agent, product concept, operational system, or another practical solution. What matters is your ability to: Identify the real problem.Prioritize under pressure.Build quickly.Make smart tradeoffs.Explain why your solution works. Who Should Join? This event is designed for a mix of: Engineers, designers, product managers, founders, operators, students, & anyone interested in building with AI. You do not need to be highly technical to participate. Strong teams will likely combine different skill sets - technical, product, design, operations, & strategy. Come with teammates or meet people at the event. Why Rapid Fire? Real emergencies rarely give you perfect information, unlimited resources, or weeks to plan. They demand fast thinking, clear priorities, & decisive execution. Rapid Fire is an experiment in building the same way: under constraints, against the clock, & as a team. Think fast. Build fast. Respond faster. Schedule5:00 - 5:30  Check-in, Team Formation & Food5:30 - 5:45  Keynote: Sharing by PMAI Team5:45 - 6:30  First Problem6:30 - 7:15  Second Problem7:15 - 8:00  Third Problem8:00 - 8:30  Judging Session8:30 - 9:00  Winners Announcement & Group Photos Sponsorship Enquiry: https://community.pioneeringminds.ai/forms/c50df13a About Plug & PlayPlug & Play is the leading innovation platform, connecting startups, corporations, venture capital firms, universities, & government agencies. Headquartered in Silicon Valley, we're present in 60+ locations across 25+ industries. We offer corporate innovation programs, helping our partners in every stage of their innovation journey, from education to execution. We also run startup acceleration programs & have built an in-house VC where we've invested in hundreds of successful companies including Dropbox, Guardant Health, Honey, Lending Club, N26, PayPal, & Rappi. For more information, visit Plug & Play. About Vibranium LabsAt Vibranium Labs, we build Tony SRE, a 24/7 OnCall AI Incident Commander that proactively hunts down production issues before engineers ever get paged. We help hyperscaling startups & enterprises stay ahead of incidents, cut the 3am wake-ups, & ship with confidence.We're backed by Plug & Play, a16z, Franklin Templeton, Gaingels, & others. Our mission: Get ahead of incidents, not just respond: Tony SRE proactively investigates your systems around the clock, surfacing issues & root causes before anyone gets paged. Kill on-call burnout: Give teams their nights & weekends back by catching problems early, so humans step in only when it truly matters. Build lasting reliability: Every incident makes Tony SRE smarter. It learns your systems, improves your workflows, & becomes the living runbook your team actually uses. About Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans at the front seat. We help YOU - our AI pioneers - to truly understand AI & create real value out of AI. Our mission is straightforward: Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to deliver rapid prototypes. Foster Collaboration: Unite diverse teams-students, engineers, & civic leaders-to tackle urban challenges head-on. Create Lasting Impact: Offer continued mentorship & post-event partnerships so promising concepts can scale beyond the weekend. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. Learn more at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/

events.name: Agentic Security - BSides NYC Week
events.description: Agentic Security NYC is a practitioner-only gathering for security engineers & leaders actually running AI agents in production not a conference, not a panel, & not a place to pitch a product. We ran the first one in August. This one lands during BSidesNYC week. The format: a small room, real conversation, no slides. We pose a handful of hard questions & let practitioners argue them out: what actually broke, who in your org has the authority to say no to an agent going to production, whether you could actually prove what an agent did last week if you had to, where your own line on autonomy really sits. Rules of the room: Chatham House - share the ideas afterward, not who said what No vendor pitches, from us or anyone else Practitioners only If you're building or defending AI agents in production: security engineering, AppSec, ProdSec, InfraSec, AI governance & this is genuinely on your mind, request an invite. Space is limited.

events.name: Papers We Love
events.description: Papers We Love, Espresso AI, & Antithesis are pleased to present the September edition of PwL. Papers We Love is a community of programmers who love reading & discussing computer science papers. What was the last paper within the realm of computing you read & loved? What did it inspire you to build or tinker with? Come share the ideas in an awesome academic or research paper with fellow engineers, programmers, & paper-readers. Lead a session & show off code you wrote that implements these ideas, or just give us the lowdown on the paper. Otherwise, just come, listen, learn, & discuss. Speaker: Samuel Laferriere More about Sam: I'm a Staff Software Engineer at Seismic, where I work on the execution layer of an EVM-compatible privacy L1 - a reth fork running BFT consensus inside TDX enclaves. Before that I spent three years at EigenLabs, where I led the integrations team for EigenDA, a high-throughput BFT blobstore, building & maintaining its rollup integrations (Optimism, zkSync, & others). For the details, have a look at my resume. I work mostly in Rust & Go on distributed systems: BFT consensus + blobstore, EVM, & confidential compute. Before blockchain, I did academic research in robotics, developing Koopman-based control algorithms for self-driving cars & quadrotors. I completed my Master's degree at the Montreal Institute for Learning Algorithms (MILA), where I developed Bayesian optimization algorithms for neurostimulation, & before that earned my bachelor's in mathematics & computer science at McGill University. Paper: https://www.cs.virginia.edu/~evans/cs551/saltzer/ Title: What Saltzer & Schroeder knew in 1975 about the agents we're building in 2026 Supporting Papers: Hardy, The Confused Deputy (1988)  Miller, Yee & Shapiro, Capability Myths Demolished (2003) Outline: Every discussion of sandboxing AI agents starts with the wrong noun. Container or microVM? gVisor or WASI? Those choices answer where computation happens. They say nothing about what authority that computation can exercise - & an agent inside a perfectly isolated VM can still exfiltrate your source through an allowed API, spend your cloud credentials, or push to main. Saltzer & Schroeder framed the real problem fifty years ago, with three of their eight design principles directly relevant to agent sandboxing problem: 1. Complete mediation turns out to be the whole reason an LLM proxy counts as security rather than decoration: the sandbox is enforcement only if the workload cannot route around it. 2. Least privilege is where agents genuinely break the classical model, because an agent's useful authority changes with its plan - authority becomes a runtime protocol, not a static profile. 3. Saltzer & Schroeder warned that a protection mechanism people find annoying will be circumvented by the people it protects. Fifty years later, the most popular sandbox configuration in the industry is --dangerously-skip-permissions. To close, a detour through Hardy's two-page note from 1988. Prompt injection is not a new vulnerability class - it's the confused deputy with a natural-language calling convention, & an LLM is the perfect confused deputy: maximally helpful, broadly authorized, & structurally unable to tell a request from data. The fix Hardy proposed is the fix Google's CaMeL rediscovered in 2025. 6:30pm - Doors 7:00pm - Speaker begins PwL curate a repository of papers & places to find them. Contributions welcome via PR. Join the PWL Discord & hop into the #nyc channel: Join Discord Server Papers We Love has a Code of Conduct. Be good to each other & to the PWL community.

events.name: Decentralized AI Day
events.description: We're bringing together builders & long-time contributors from the Numerai & decentralized AI ecosystems for a mix of talks, a workshop, & a special community panel. Featured speakers: Jason - Co-Founder & CEO, CrowdCent Nick - Co-Founder & CEO, Allora Labs Matteo - Co-Founder & CEO, Orion Finance The Numerai "Out of Sample" Special Panel  A discussion & AMA-style panel with guests featured on the Out of Sample interview series. All three are current or former members of the Numerai Council of Elders, with the panel moderated by another member of the Council. Tim (aka jefferythewind) (see episode 2) ShatteredX (see episode 3) Jason (see episode 4) More speakers & session details coming soon. This event is part of #AIWeekNY by Pulse NYC - a community-led festival celebrating innovation across the AI ecosystem. More at https://pulse.nyc/ai-week/ Important Note  This is an in-person-only event; there will be no livestream. For security reasons, we must provide a guest list to the security team at least 24 hours before the event. You must provide your  FULL NAME  when registering for this event. If you prefer not to display your full name publicly, please provide it in the final registration question instead. Your full name will be shared only with the security team. About Decentralized AI Days  Decentralized AI Days are community-driven events exploring how open, decentralized AI & Web3 can work together in practice. We bring together engineers, researchers, & builders for a day of technical talks, hands-on workshops, & honest conversation - no hype, no sales pitches, & no pay-to-play. The ecosystem we care about includes projects such as Numerai & CrowdCent. The door is open to anyone building with or curious about decentralized AI. Come for the substance, stay for the community. Call for Presentations  Interested in sharing your experience with our community? Please contact me (Joe) directly via X, or on LinkedIn. I'll get back to you as soon as possible. Everyone is welcome to apply, as long as your talk or workshop topic is relevant. Agenda  More details will be announced soon! Expect a program of tech talks & workshops, followed by a relaxed evening mixer. What to Expect   Connect with a friendly community of AI & Web3 builders, researchers, & curious minds.  Enjoy zero-hype technical talks focused on real problems & practical insights.  Take part in hands-on workshops where you can learn by building.  Watch live demos of decentralized AI & related projects.  Meet the organizers & share your questions & feedback directly.  Explore community resources & connect over food. Who Should Attend)  Decentralized AI Days are for everyone curious about where AI & decentralized systems meet: AI/ML engineers, Web3 developers, researchers, students, & builders at any experience level. If you are new to the space, you are welcome; if you have been building for years, you will find your people here. Come ready to learn, share, & connect. The Venue  Register to see the address. Here are some photos of the venue: Main Room Sponsors  DeAI Day is a community event series sponsored by Numerai & the Numerai Council of Elders. Complimentary refreshments will be provided throughout the day. Come early & grab some cool swags! Code of Conduct  All attendees, speakers, sponsors, & volunteers must agree to the following Code of Conduct. Event organizers will enforce these guidelines throughout the event. We expect full cooperation from everyone to help ensure a welcoming & safe environment for all participants. Our event is committed to providing an inclusive & harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of gender, gender identity or expression, age, sexual orientation, disability, physical appearance, body size, race, ethnicity, religion (or lack thereof), or technology preferences. Harassment in any form will not be tolerated. Sexually explicit language or imagery is inappropriate for any part of the event, including talks, workshops, social activities, or online platforms. Participants who violate these rules may be warned or expelled from the event at the discretion of the organizers. Past Events  Materials from past Decentralized AI Days live in the community meetups repository. We have also hosted similar events under a different name (Numerai Community Meetup) from 2022 to 2024: London (July 2022) New York (September 2022) Tokyo (April 2023) Prague (July 2023) Toronto (October 2023) San Francisco (January 2024) Frankfurt (April 2024) Tokyo (July 2024) Bangkok (November 2024) Finally, here's one meme to sum up the vibe.

events.name: AI & Future Of Education
events.description: AI & the Future of Education Artificial intelligence has caused seismic disruption in the field of education in just a few years. Students, educators, & parents are confused about how to navigate this game-changing technology. How should schools from K-12 to colleges & universities approach learning in this new era, & how can they prepare students for success in a transformed workplace? A panel of experts weighs in on the salient issues, the points of tension, & possible paths forward.   Featuring Steven Jackson, professor of information science & science & technology studies & vice provost for academic innovation at Cornell University; Aankit Patel, university dean for technology & computer & information sciences, The City University of New York; & Natasha Singer, a technology reporter for the business section of The New York Times, whose new book is Coding Kids: Big Tech's Battle to Remake Public Schools. Luke Waltzer, director of the Teaching & Learning Center at the CUNY Graduate Center, moderates.   Presented with the Teaching & Learning Center, CUNY AI Lab, GC Digital Initiatives, the American Social History Project/Center for Media & Learning, & the Mina Rees Library.

events.name: Hack For Impact - AI Workflow Hackathon
events.description: Pioneering Minds AI: Hack for ImpactAn AI Workflow HackathonDont just use AI. Redesign how work gets done.AI is changing how we research, learn, build products, analyze contracts, manage money, & make decisions. But adding a chatbot to an existing process is not the same as building an AI-native workflow.The real opportunity is to rethink the workflow itself:What should humans still do?What should AI handle?What can be automated entirely?And where does human judgment become even more important?This is a one-day hackathon where participants redesign real-world workflows using AI.Teams will choose a problem from one of four tracks, identify a broken or inefficient workflow, & build an AI-native product, agent, or system that makes it dramatically better.You do not need to arrive with a startup idea.Come with curiosity. Find a problem. Build something.The winning teams can also secure their spot at our upcoming Pitching Masterclass, where they can sharpen their story, product positioning, & pitch.The ChallengeTeams will identify an existing workflow & redesign it for the age of AI.Your project should answer three questions:What is broken, slow, repetitive, or unnecessarily difficult today?What should AI do differently?What does the new workflow look like when AI is built into it from the beginning?Projects can take the form of an AI agent, internal tool, workflow automation, consumer product, enterprise application, or prototype.Hackathon TracksParticipants may choose one of four tracks.Critical Thinking & LearningAI can produce answers in seconds. But getting an answer is not the same as understanding something. As AI becomes capable of performing more cognitive tasks, skills such as critical thinking, judgment, curiosity, problem decomposition, & learning how to learn may become even more important. Build a product or workflow that uses AI to help people think better rather than simply think less.AI for Product Management WorkflowsProduct managers spend enormous amounts of time gathering information, coordinating teams, analyzing feedback, writing documents, prioritizing ideas, & turning ambiguity into decisions.Many of these workflows were designed before AI existed. Redesign them.Legal Tech WorkflowsLegal work is full of complex, document-heavy processes where accuracy, judgment, & context matter.AI creates an opportunity to fundamentally rethink how legal professionals research, review, draft, analyze, & manage information.They must also consider accuracy, explainability, accountability, & human review.Fintech & Insurtech WorkflowsFinancial services & insurance involve some of the most complex workflows in business: underwriting, compliance, risk assessment, fraud detection, claims, financial analysis, & customer onboarding.Many still involve fragmented systems, repetitive manual review, & enormous amounts of unstructured data.What You'll BuildTeams will have one day to identify a problem, design a solution, build a prototype, & present it to our judges.Your prototype does not need to be production-ready.We care about:The quality of the problemHow thoughtfully you redesign the workflowHow meaningfully AI improves the processThe usability of your prototypeWhether someone would actually use itAll backgrounds are welcome.You do not need to be an engineer to participate.Product managers, designers, lawyers, finance professionals, founders, students, operators, & domain experts are strongly encouraged to join.Coaching & mentorship will be available onsite.What We'll ExploreAI agents & workflow automationHuman + AI collaborationProduct design in the age of AICritical thinking & human judgmentLegal AIFintech & insurtechRapid prototypingStartup product strategyVenture-style pitchingSchedule09:00  09:30 Check-in & Breakfast09:30  10:00 Opening Keynote & Track Introduction10:00  10:30 Hackathon Rules & Team Formation10:30  12:00 Hackathon Begins  Problem Discovery & Building12:00  13:00 Lunch (provided on-site)13:00  16:00 Continued Development & Mentor Sessions16:00  17:30 Live Project Pitches & Judging17:30  18:00 Winners Announcement & Group PhotosSponsorship Enquiry: https://community.pioneeringminds.ai/forms/c50df13aPioneering Minds AI GroupAbout Pioneering Minds AI:At pioneeringminds.ai, we grow AI-native pioneers who build, deploy, & govern AI responsibly & put humans in the front seat.We help our AI pioneers understand AI deeply & turn it into real-world value.Our mission is straightforward:Accelerate Innovation: Equip participants with cutting-edge AI tools to rapidly turn ideas into working prototypes.Foster Collaboration: Bring together students, engineers, operators, domain experts, & founders to solve meaningful problems.Create Lasting Impact: Help promising ideas continue beyond the hackathon through mentorship, community, & future opportunities.

events.name: NYFW Debrief - Fashion Mixer
events.description: NYFW Debrief New York Fashion Week is about to take over the city, the shows, the street style, the 6am fittings, the group chats blowing up with front row photos. It's a lot. And by the time it's over, everyone needs a minute to actually talk about what happened. That's what this is. Once the tents come down & the last show wraps, we're getting the industry back in one room, no seating charts, no dress codes to stress over, no rushing between venues. events.name: [AI Briefing] Private Equity - What Owners & Buyers Pay For
events.description: The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise.  This month's source: The PE AI Adoption Benchmark: From scaling to systematizing (Accordion with Wakefield Research - May 2026) Somebody's going to ask what your AI spend returned. If your company has a board or an eventual buyer, that question is already scheduled. Private equity gets asked first, so that's where this month's data comes from. Accordion surveyed 150 technology & AI operating partners at PE sponsors about the finance functions inside their portfolios. 41% are scaling AI across multiple companies with no operational playbook, & only 29% describe their firm as systematizing or leading. 75% of those companies arrived at acquisition unprepared or only partially ready for any of it. 86% of these operating partners expect buyers to pay a premium for AI-enabled finance capability within two years, & 44% say buyers are already asking in diligence without paying for it yet. Conviction is running ahead of price. The deployment that worked & left no evidence behind it is the one that costs you at exit. 67% of firms measure hours recovered. 29% put AI impact in front of a board.  The Mission: Building the evidence a board or a buyer will accept We'll work the measurement problem directly: which AI metrics connect to EBITDA, & how a company gets there without starting over. We'll examine why only 14% of portfolio finance functions have crossed from back-office automation into real decision intelligence, & what the rest are paying for instead.  The Format: The benchmark, fast: Five findings & the numbers under them, including the ones that don't hold up. Translating it out of PE: Sponsors run this test on a clock, so the pressure shows up there first. We'll take what it exposes & apply it to companies with other kinds of owners. Cross-pollinated debate: Operators compare what agentic finance already does in production (58% report automated covenant monitoring, 44% report AI-drafted board packages) against what their own governance can defend today.  Who Should Attend: Enterprise Executives: Leave with the measures a buyer or board will scrutinize, & an honest read on which ones you could produce this quarter. Founders & Builders: See what sponsors & portfolio CFOs are buying, & where the 47% assembling AI tools case-by-case stall out before anything compounds. Product, Data, & Operations Leads: Compare notes on the constraint everything else runs into. Poor data infrastructure ranked first among all barriers by a wide margin, ahead of talent, legacy systems, change management, & budget. Most of it arrives at close & gets fixed while the books are closing.  The Prep: This is a working session, not a lecture. Read the report here. Bring your perspective.

events.name: Bridging Adherence Gap - How Can Tech Help People Stay On Their Treatment
events.description: At its core, adherence is a deeply human problem. We know following through with a treatment plan improves our health, but in the moment, taking that immediate next step isn't always easy. The root causes are complex-ranging from forgetfulness & fear of side effects to a lack of visible benefits & high costs. Yet, despite billions of dollars invested in digital health tools, smart devices, & patient support programs, the core statistic remains stubbornly unchanged: roughly 50% of patients still fail to take chronic medications as prescribed over the long term. With rapid shifts in consumer behavior & technology, healthcare companies have unprecedented opportunities to engage with patients.  Join Smart Design as we bring together experts from across the industry to explore how we can apply new technology to the messiness of everyday life & the healthcare system to drive real, lasting health outcomes.

events.name: Scene By Scene - Brand Relevance, Video AI & Next Era Of CTV
events.description: As billions of advertising dollars shift to Connected TV, the industry is entering a new era. The challenge is no longer simply reaching the right audience - it's ensuring every advertising dollar reaches viewers at exactly the right moment. New advances in AI - including scene-level understanding that can interpret video content with unprecedented context - are transforming how premium video inventory is valued, bought, & sold. Join an invitation-only gathering of the voices defining the future of brands & CTV. From the leaders responsible for the world's largest advertising budgets to the innovators building the next generation of AI & video technology, this evening will feature an intimate fireside conversation, followed by networking among the industry's top decision-makers.   About NVIDIA NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) is the world leader in AI & accelerated computing. Its platforms power work across data centers, graphics, robotics, & autonomous systems, & underpin much of the AI infrastructure the technology industry runs on today.   About PYLER PYLER is an AI-driven company specializing in video understanding & brand safety for digital advertising. Its core product, AiD, interprets video, audio, & metadata in real time to ensure ads appear in safe, relevant, trusted contexts. PYLER is a winner of the 2025 NVIDIA Inception Startup Grand Challenge.   About Supermomos Supermomos is a community platform connecting more than 35,000 founders, investors, & operators across New York, Boston, San Francisco, London, & Singapore. We host curated gatherings that bring together the people building & funding what comes next.  Speakers:Matt Groshong, Business Development Director, AdTech & MarTech, NVIDIA: Matt Groshong is a Business Development Director at NVIDIA, covering AdTech & MarTech. He has been in technology, advertising & media long enough to remember when "digital" was a separate budget line, & now spends most of his time helping the ecosystem work out what AI & accelerated computing actually do for them, rather than what the keynote said they would. Lately he is preoccupied with agentic systems, & what happens to marketing when the software starts making its own decisions. Before NVIDIA he was an Account CTO at Microsoft, aligned to WPP, & EMEA CTO at McCann Worldgroup. Earlier stops include the BBC, ServiceNow & the Newspaper Licensing Agency. events.description: Token costs have overtaken hallucinations as the top reason enterprise AI projects die before reaching production; it's cited by 29% of technical leaders as the primary production killer, ahead of every reliability failure combined. The teams seeing success don't treat inference cost as an after-the-fact line item. They architect for token costs from the beginning. This event examines what that shift actually looks like in practice: GPU memory & data architecture decisions that determine cost per token served & the orchestration choices that separate a project that survives its second budget review from one that doesn't. We'll open with new VentureBeat Pulse Research on how enterprises are - & aren't - measuring the economics of the AI they're already running. This isn't a panel. It's a small group of peers, over drinks, working through the hardest question in enterprise AI right now. Featured Speakers: An evening conversation & drinks with a small number of enterprise AI leaders, kept intentionally close to keep the conversation substantive.

events.name: Future Forum - Science For Society
events.description: The 2026 FUTURE FORUM will convene leaders from diverse backgrounds including academia, museums, journalism, media, public engagement, government, industry, & scientific organizations from the United States & Germany to explore how science can more effectively serve society through communication, collaboration, & public engagement. Centered on the theme Science for Society, the meeting will examine how trust in science is built & sustained, how scientific discoveries & long-term research can be communicated more effectively to diverse audiences, & how institutions can demonstrate the societal value of science. A panel discussion will address the roles of museums, journalists, policymakers, & other non-traditional science communicators; strategies for strengthening public confidence in science & evidence-based decision-making; the importance of open & international scientific collaboration amid increasing geopolitical pressures; & approaches to fostering public engagement, scientific literacy, & global collaboration. Through interdisciplinary dialogue & transatlantic relationship-building, the 2026 FUTURE FORUM aims to develop new partnerships, identify best practices, & strengthen the role of science communication in advancing an informed, engaged, & resilient society. About the FUTURE FORUM The FUTURE FORUM brings together experts from Germany, the United States, & beyond to exchange perspectives on emerging issues in science, innovation, & society. Through focused expert dialogue & public engagement, the format creates space to examine shared challenges, identify new perspectives, & strengthen transatlantic exchange. Previous editions have explored themes including Science Diplomacy in an Era of Technological Disruption at the Science Diplomacy Hub at Johns Hopkins University, Washington, D.C. in 2025. Or Health. Tech. Diplomacy., which focused on global health at the Broad Institute of MIT & Harvard in 2025. In 2026, the FUTURE FORUM returns with Science for Society, bringing together transatlantic experts to explore questions around science communication, public trust, scientific literacy, public engagement, & collaboration across disciplines & borders.

events.name: Why You Think the Way You Do About Money
events.description:
Why You Think the Way You Do About Money: A live panel on the psychology behind every financial decision you've ever made

​Here's a question nobody asks at a normal finance event:

​Why does your best friend save obsessively while you can't walk past a sale, even though you make the same salary?

​Why do you know exactly what you "should" do with your money and still not do it?

​Why did you inherit your dad's spending anxiety instead of his frugality?

​That's the whole point of this panel. Rebecca Pino (financial advisor) and Suzanne Kirkendall (behavioral scientist) are turning the mic on each other — and on you.

​No slide decks, no "5 tips to save more" energy. Just two people who study money and behavior for a living, asking each other the questions they actually want answered, then opening the floor so the audience can grill them both together.

events.name: Derek Parfit's Birthday!
events.description:
Derek Parfit was perhaps the greatest moral philosopher of the 20th century, in how he shaped the discipline and raised important new questions. 

He gave us the Repugnant Conclusion and the Hitchhiker's Dilemma, and put a plug for giving 10% into On What Matters, his masterpiece. Had he lived long enough to finish another volume, he had plans to discuss existential risk and dive deeper into questions of how we ought to act.

How to celebrate Parfit's life and work? You could discuss population ethics, philosophize about something else, or consider, as a group, ways to make your lives slightly more rational. (Or just eat cake and sing Happy Birthday and engage in idle, friendly conversation; Parfit surely wouldn't object.)

RSVP https://www.eventbrite.com/e/nycresistor-ham-radio-club-tickets-1633091413379

Monthly Amateur Radio club meeting of NYCResistorRadio curious? Join the NYC Resistor Ham Radio Club (call sign N2YCR) for our open and regular meetings, the 4th Wednesday of each month from 8:00 – 9:30 pm at NYC Resistor (87 3rd Avenue, 4th Floor).
The amateur radio hobby has something for everyone, from Morse code to modern digital modes. Bring projects you're working on, gear to fix, problems that puzzle you, outings you'd like to organize, or just yourself to meet & greet your friendly local hams. Drop by the #n2ycr channel in Discord any time to say hi.
You do not need to be a member of Resistor to be a member of the club, nor do you need to be a licensed amateur radio operator (though of course we hope you'll become licensed with our help).
We aim to create an inclusive, encouraging, and diverse environment to bring together Brooklyn's radio hackers, antenna experimenters, shortwave listeners, toroid winders, satellite chasers, and balloon launchers.
Come make some noise in the weird and wonderful medium of radio!This is a masks optional event.
As with all NYC Resistor events, this class is 18+ and governed by our Code of Conduct. The Code of Conduct, as well as accessibility information, can be found at www.nycresistor.com/participate/.
Please note that refunds must be requested 24 hours in advance. If you have any questions, please email classes@nycresistor.com.

events.name: NYCResistor Ham Radio Club
events.description:
RSVP https://www.eventbrite.com/e/nycresistor-ham-radio-club-tickets-1633091463529

Monthly Amateur Radio club meeting of NYCResistorRadio curious? Join the NYC Resistor Ham Radio Club (call sign N2YCR) for our open and regular meetings, the 4th Wednesday of each month from 8:00 – 9:30 pm at NYC Resistor (87 3rd Avenue, 4th Floor).
The amateur radio hobby has something for everyone, from Morse code to modern digital modes. Bring projects you're working on, gear to fix, problems that puzzle you, outings you'd like to organize, or just yourself to meet & greet your friendly local hams. Drop by the #n2ycr channel in Discord any time to say hi.
You do not need to be a member of Resistor to be a member of the club, nor do you need to be a licensed amateur radio operator (though of course we hope you'll become licensed with our help).
We aim to create an inclusive, encouraging, and diverse environment to bring together Brooklyn's radio hackers, antenna experimenters, shortwave listeners, toroid winders, satellite chasers, and balloon launchers.
Come make some noise in the weird and wonderful medium of radio!This is a masks optional event.
As with all NYC Resistor events, this class is 18+ and governed by our Code of Conduct. The Code of Conduct, as well as accessibility information, can be found at www.nycresistor.com/participate/.
Please note that refunds must be requested 24 hours in advance. If you have any questions, please email classes@nycresistor.com.

Join us in New York on November 13th for the NYC Physical AI, ML, and Computer Vision Meetup, co-presented by Nebius and Voxel51.

Talks will include:
Closing the human to robot gap for dexterous hands — Irmak Guzey at New York University
Building Real-World Computer Vision Systems with Voxel51 — Dan Gural at Voxel51

Learning the Geometry of Compression: OrBIT — Yunied Puig de Dios at Independent

events.name: Cozy Sundays — Fall '26 Session III - HALLOWEEN 🎃👻
events.description:
Fall has arrived, and every fortnight we gather again for Cozy Sundays. You know the drill.
house rules
To enter the space, buzz Ambrook and take the stairs. If you have accessibility needs, message a host for elevator access (key fob required)
The buzzer will be muted after 2:30, as it is quite loud. Please come on time to avoid disrupting the quiet work periods, and to ensure you can get in.
Bring snacks or tea to share, or a suggested donation to the snack fund to continue to support cozy sundays <3
The office has rooms, but they are not soundproof. So please refrain from taking calls during this session as there is limited phone booth availability.
Ambrook is a shoes-off office! Wear your best socks :)
Please only RSVP if you can make it and stay the whole time.
schedule
2-2:30p: arrive, quick primer on the session, intros circle
2:30-3:30p: deep work session #1
3:30-3:45: break
3:45-4:45p: deep work session #2
4:45-5:30: demos - sharing ideas, works in progress, and celebrating wins
5:30-6:00: mingle & wrap up
~ optional ~ some of us grab dinner after!
About Cozy Sundays
We exist to support people as they work on the things that they love but struggle to make time for — this place is not for job hunting, catching up on work, sending emails, making sales pitches or networking.
We fiercely protect what makes each session special because the magic only exists when we all buy in together.
Thank you Ambrook for lending us their space. Ambrook is building the financial layer powering American industry. They are hiring across roles in engineering, growth and sales.
If you can't make it this time but are interested in attending a future session 👉 subscribe to the events calendar lu.ma/cozy-sundays

events.name: Is Everything Predictable?: AI, Prediction Markets, and the Philosophy of Foresight
events.description:
In this six-week course, explore works from philosophy, cultural studies, and journalism to understand how technologies that predict the future also shape the present.
The age of AI, prediction markets, and real-time data analysis brings predictive reasoning into all corners of human life. Once considered a niche academic interest area, the philosophy and politics of prediction is now relevant to everybody. “Is Everything Predictable?: AI, Prediction Markets, and the Philosophy of Foresight” presents scholarly material on forecasting technologies in a rigorous but highly accessible format.
Drawing from a range of sources, we center scholarly texts and deeply-researched journalism that uncover the links between digital calculation, philosophical notions of time and free will, and the reality of living in an age where everything seems reducible to calculation.
Guest speakers from academia and tech journalism will round out our seminar sessions, and for our final meeting, students have the option of presenting original research or creative work in an event open to the general public.
Syllabus
In the early weeks of the course, we read texts from contemporary media studies and political theory that construe prediction and speculation as  forms of governance. We also address probabilistic reasoning as a key feature of artificial intelligence and prediction market mechanisms, using frameworks suitable for participants without any background in STEM. As we will see, the similarities and differences between how probability works in AI versus prediction markets have much to tell us about these tools’ effects on everything from global warfare and the environment to creativity and personal relationships.
After establishing a strong practical and theoretical foundation in AI and prediction markets, we turn to philosophical writing on the nature of freedom, self-expression, and power. These texts urge us to ask whether predictive technologies empower us with highly advanced forms of knowledge; if they inhibit  us by constraining our imagination of what’s possible; or if both of these outcomes might be true at once. We also read articles and listen to podcast interviews with our guest speakers in anticipation of their visits.
Throughout our sessions, we examine case studies related to tech companies, specific applications, and major actors in the AI and prediction market space. The course’s culminating event – a salon open to the general public – reflects our interest in connecting questions and concerns that seem highly academic to current events and everyday life. Students who choose to give presentations will participate in an additional workshop or one-on-one advising session to help them prepare. By the course’s end, we will be able to navigate a world driven by predictive technologies with greater clarity, confidence, and wisdom, and to share our perspectives on them in a way that empowers those around us.
Learning Outcomes
Connect AI and prediction market functionalities to political and cultural affairs
Develop critical reading skills applicable to philosophy and journalism
Apply frameworks from the theoretical humanities to real-world developments in politics and technology
Make scholarly ideas accessible to a wide range of audiences
Course Dates
October 29
November 5
November 12
November 19
December 3
December 10
There will be a break during the holiday week on November 26th.
Scholarships
Index scholarships are designed to benefit underrepresented groups, BIPOC members of our community, and those for whom the class price is not accessible. These need-based scholarships will go to the candidates who best demonstrate why they should be chosen for the free spot to our class. You can apply for a scholarship here.
Instructor Bio

Emma Stamm is a writer and professor with a background in philosophy and the social study of science and technology (STS). She holds a PhD in Interdisciplinary Studies from Virginia Tech and has taught courses on the philosophy and social implications of technology at Villanova University, Virginia Tech, the Acid Horizon Research Commons, New York University, where she currently teaches for the Department of Media, Culture, and Communication. As a public-facing scholar, she has written for Vice Motherboard, Real Life Mag, and Communications of the Association for Computing Machinery, in addition to co-hosting the LEPHT HAND podcast. She is the co-founder and Executive Director of the Lenox Institute for Advanced Study, which makes critical science and tech education accessible beyond academia.

Refunds
We get that things come up, but we rely on headcounts to make our programs viable. If you request a refund...
More than 4 weeks before the program begins → 100% refund
More than 2 weeks before the program begins → 50% refund
Fewer than 2 weeks before the program begins → No refund
Thanks for understanding and for supporting our ability to provide cool offerings through your purchase.
Media Release Clause
By attending this event, you consent to being photographed, filmed, or recorded, and grant Index Space permission to use this content for promotional or informational purposes.

A primer on magnetic tape, no-input mixing techniques, tape loops, and analog tape echo. How it works, how to set it up, how to play with it



A primer on magnetic tape, no-input mixing techniques, tape loops, and analog tape echo. How it works, how to set it up, how to play with it. events.name: Reading for Writers: James Baldwin
events.description:
Most writers read a lot. But reading isn’t enough; you need to study great writing.
This workshop is a chance to analyze and understand how he does it.
What’s the structure of the workshop?
The specific essay we'll be reading will be shared close to the date!
Together, we'll break down the storytelling structure, the literary techniques, and the format. We’ll reverse-engineering what turns a good idea into a piece of writing people can't stop reading and sharing.
You'll leave with:
A clearer sense of what makes a great personal essay
A method for using personal stories to carry a broader message
An understanding of how to shape a personal essay for Substack and online readers
Who is this for?
Anyone who writes personal essays
Writers on Substack or anywhere online
Anyone who wants to get better at nonfiction writing
Details
This is an in-person workshop in NYC. We're keeping it intimate at 15 people.
Spots are limited.
If you're serious about your writing, you won’t want to miss this!
About the Facilitator
James Q is a former computer engineer turned writer and community organizer. He left his job in tech to pursue writing and community full-time. He’s been writing online since 2020 and now writes personal essays about becoming, relationships, and creativity on his Substack. Through Olive Tree Writing Club, the community he founded, he's hosted over 100+ writing events in New York City.
Personal Website | Substack
What's OTWC?
Olive Tree Writing Club is a New York City-based writing community founded on the belief that writing is thinking. Since 2022, they've hosted 100+ events for 1,000+ writers, spanning weekly writing sessions, workshops, retreats, and community gatherings.
Website | Substack | Instagram

events.name: Satori Book Club Vol. 3: Stop Bowling Alone
events.description:
A chill book club for ambitious people who want to read interesting books, have better conversations, and make life a little more interesting.
Welcome to Satori Book Club: Vol. 3.
We’ll spend the afternoon hanging out in the park or a home or somewhere cool, geeking out on interesting ideas, sharing spicy takes, debating the things we disagree on, and inevitably going down a few completely unnecessary rabbit holes along the way.
📚 What we're reading
Main Book
Yesteryear by Caro Claire Burke
A modern-day "tradwife" influencer romanticizes the old-school pioneer lifestyle... and then wakes up in 1855 and has to actually live it. Turns out the good old days may not have been all that good.
⚔️ Biz / Professional Development Side Quest
The Science of Storytelling by Will Storr
Because storytelling is one of the oldest and most important skills, and we decided we're tired of people blowing good stories with bad storytelling skills. This one digs into the psychology of why stories grip us and how to tell better ones.
🧠 Personal / Philosophy Side Quest
Bowling Alone by Robert D. Putnam
Because seriously, we've got to stop bowling alone. Or reading alone. Or doing anything alone. Haven't you heard the memo? Community building is cool again. The classic on why Americans stopped joining things and what it's cost us.
Quick reminder: You really don’t have to read the books — read one, read them all, read half, or come in completely blind. The books are really just fuel for interesting ideas, deep conversations, spicy takes, and random rabbit holes. No pressure, no homework vibes.
We started this thing so we could geek out on deep ideas, philosophy, and life’s big questions together instead of having all those conversations in our own heads. 🧠
TBD on where we meet for this next one
A rough idea of the afternoon:
👋 Hang out and catch up
📚 Break into groups around the different books and discussion prompts
🌶️ Share insights, hot takes, disagreements, and whatever rabbit holes we find ourselves in
🗳️ Nominate + vote on what we read next
Every ~6 weeks we’ll pick some new books, get together to talk about them, and sprinkle in casual reading hangs and other shenanigans in between.
If you like interesting people, interesting ideas, and conversations that go a little deeper than “so, what do you do?” — come hang. 📚🤙

events.name: Simple Data Networks for Multidisciplinary Artists
events.description:
RSVP https://www.eventbrite.com/e/simple-data-networks-for-multidisciplinary-artists-tickets-2002982579815

Learn to create projects involving multiple separate components that communicate together to provide unique interactive experiences!If you're a multidisciplinary artist who likes to explore combinations of multiple different backgrounds, mediums or genres, or if you're a curious experimentalist who loves to mix and match various skillsets or software tools, you may not always find one single solution or application that accomplishes everything your project needs. You often just have to create the solution yourself!Consider these examples:- Using a physical sensor (distance, light, pressure, etc.) as an input to a computer program- Using a machine learning model (hand pose, body pose, face detection, etc.) to interface with an interactive kinetic or LED-based sculpture- Creating a handheld or wearable wireless controller for your generative synthesized musical instrument, allowing you to move around freely instead of being stuck to your computer on stage, or better yet, repurposing an existing smartphone to function as one- Enabling audience participation during a performance through the smartphones they already own- Solving any creative problem where no out-of-the-box solution already exists!For these tasks above and many many more, you may just have to break down your idea into separate components, handle each component separately using whichever tool that's best for the job, and then allow those components to work together to solve the larger task. No compromise needed!To accomplish this, we will go over OSC, the most widely supported real-time communication protocol that exists. OSC is the common language that your favorite hardware/software tool most likely speaks, and which allows multiple otherwise-incompatible programs to easily communicate with each other. We will introduce some basic networking concepts and dive right into how to send/receive OSC messages between devices. We'll work in pairs to mix-and-match different software tools together and see what kinds of interactions we can create. Time permitting, we'll have some time for creative brainstorming and ideation at the end. 

What kinds of projects and experiences would you want to create with this technology? Who is the class for? This 95% code-free workshop is intended to complement your existing interests and skills.Creative multimedia tools that support OSC include:- TouchDesigner- Max/MSP- Ableton (with M4L)- Processing / OpenFrameworks / p5.js- Arduino, ESP32, Raspberry Pi- Unity/Unreal- Any iOS/Android mobile device- Just raw code baby (Python, Node.js, C++, etc.)- Many othersIf you already use or are interested in any of the items listed above, or are just curious to explore the potential of networking together multiple programs/devices, this beginner-friendly, 95% code-free (code starter examples provided) workshop is a great starting point.Bring a laptop and your smartphone!
Instructor bio:
Yonatan Rozin is a multidisciplinary interactive technologist, prototyper, educator and classically-trained percussionist based in New York City. His freelance and personal practice frequently explores novel combinations of multimedia software and hardware platforms in the creation of unfamiliar installations, performances and experiences. As a freelance interactive art consultant, software engineer at the Harvestworks Digital Media Arts Center and avid collaborator, he has created bespoke interactive solutions for numerous independent artists across a variety of mediums and backgrounds.
This is a masks optional workshop.
As with all NYC Resistor events, this class is 18+ and governed by our Code of Conduct. The Code of Conduct, as well as accessibility information, can be found at on the NYC Resistor website.

events.name: Responsible Tech Summit 2026. From Principles to Power: Embedding Accountability in the AI Era
events.description:
At a time when artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping society, the conversation is shifting from broad principles to real-world accountability. The 2026 summit will explore the theme of Principles to Power: Embedding Accountability in the AI Era. For years, the Responsible Tech field has been guided by ethical frameworks, voluntary commitments, and emerging standards. Today, the challenge is clear: how do we translate those ideas into systems of governance, oversight, and design that ensure innovation does not come at the expense of safety, rights, or trust?
The Responsible Tech Summit is designed as a curated convening for 375 leaders that helps align and shape the direction of the movement. Participants will include global governance leaders, AI researchers, industry practitioners, policy experts, civil society advocates, and philanthropic leaders who are building the infrastructure of accountability for the digital age. Through keynotes, panels, and conversations, attendees will explore topics such as accountability by design, platform oversight, youth online safety, the Responsible Tech economy, and the evolving global regulatory landscape.

events.name: Breaking Walled Gardens
events.description:
An iOS jailbreaking workshop where we discuss permacomputing and the advantages of breaking out of a walled ecosystem.
Try hacking existing devices to extend their longevity and limit our own production of e-waste. Non iOS devices also possible to explore.
A workshop to jailbreak old Apple devices for reusability in modern livelihoods. Each participant will be requested to bring an old i-device to go through the process of “jailbreaking”. If participants do not have old Apple devices, they are welcome to bring other specific hardwares to experiment with modifications and tooling to get them up and running again (think old phones, media players, game consoles). We will be looking for ways to play around with the existing hardware and re-incorporating them back into serviceable devices. Potential avenues could include: extra screens for an art installation, modded gaming consoles to play lost media, or simply using your old iPod as a music player again.
This workshop will also have a discussion on the philosophy of permacomputing, or ways we can hack existing devices to extend their longevity and limit our own production of e-waste. Devices are planned to become obsolete, and it is our job as soft(ware) custodians to maintain, cultivate, and care for these old and forgotten tools.
Some sample materials may be provided to practice using these modding tools, but participants are encouraged to bring their own devices.
Learning Outcomes
Permacomputing philosophies and practical applications of them
Repurpose old (but powerful) devices into our own artistic practices
How we can leverage open source tools to build resilience against e-waste
Program/Resources
Sam's GitHub
Sam's Zine
Scholarships
Index scholarships are designed to benefit members of our community who do not have expendable cash to pay for the course, and those for whom the class price is not accessible. These need-based scholarships will go to the candidates who best demonstrate why they should be chosen for the free spot to our class based on the following criteria:
Belong to groups that are traditionally underrepresented in the graphic design and creative industries
Do not have jobs that would pay for these courses as professional development
Cannot independently afford the class at list price
Share our value of intentional community
The number of selected applicants chosen is subject to the discretion of Index and the instructor, but every course will select at least one. Apply for a scholarship here. Applications close October 14th.
Instructor

Sam Heckle is a bi-coastal educator and artist specializing in ethical software, generative systems, and decentralized network design. They are currently exploring permacomputing through repurposing electronic waste, queer representations in media, and the rituals that bring us back into the algorithmic fold. Sam currently teaches creative computation and critical media theory at The New School, New York University, Hunter College, and the School of Visual Arts. They are also an active organizer of Destruction Junket, a Brooklyn-based art collective that creates community from chaos.

events.name: Data Salon: Context and Data
events.description:
An event series for fostering thought leadership across data disciplines and those who work closely with data practitioners, hosted by Newtown Analytics at Fractal Tech. This event will go beyond the hype and inspect the potential impact of AI on labor from well-informed business perspectives both on the ground and systemic.
MC'd by Akpanoluo Etteh, Sr. Director of Data Engineering at Arcspan (fmr: Anthropic, Bandcamp) and founder of The Soundshop music salon series, and co-hosted by Michael Bartoli, Founder of Newtown Analytics (fmr: obé Fitness)
Our featured collaborator: Omni
Omni is an AI analytics platform that gives every person and every AI agent the same governed definitions of the business's metrics. That puts Omni close to this month's question: what context does AI need before the business can trust its answers? Omni joins us through JD Costantini of their go-to-market team.
Bio: Began my career as a data engineering consultant at IBM working across industries and getting exposed to tons of different technologies across the data stack. After recognizing the innovation happening in the space, I moved into the AI Analytics startup space in 2021, and joined Omni 2 years ago. I love being able to work with clients of all shapes and sizes, finally delivering a trustworthy self-service analytics experience for the masses.
Presentation Teaser: We'll discuss how the marriage of context and data is the key to unlock the AI-era version of analytics. How data teams are evolving to be the stewards of semantics. Why you need to keep the business SMEs squarely in your feedback loop. And why collecting context is good, but optimizing how you use it is great.

You'll end with a set of tools, the knowledge of where to go next, and the confidence to continue your programming journey.This tutorial is presented by Al Sweigart, author of Automate the Boring Stuff with Python and several other Python books. All of his books are freely available under a Creative Commons license at https://inventwithpython.com.This tutorial is for complete beginners with no programming experience. You will need a laptop with Python installed (it is free from Python.org). You will need to install a code editor: I recommend Mu for free from https://codewith.mu/. Course materials are at https://inventwithpython.com/pyconus2026/.Attendees will get a printed workbook that we'll work through during the class. You'll be able to take it home for self-completion and review.
There are 2 spots reserved for people who cannot access the class at the full price, so please make use of one of these pay-what-you-can tickets if that is your situation. Checkout Code: 4-ACCESSTIX
This is a masks optional class.
As with all NYC Resistor events, this class is 18+ and governed by our Code of Conduct. The Code of Conduct, as well as accessibility information, can be found at www.nycresistor.com/participate/. Please note that refunds must be requested 24 hours in advance. If you have any questions, please email classes@nycresistor.com.

events.name: Building a New Market: Compute as an Asset Class
events.description:
We're hosting a panel on the emerging market for AI compute.

Compute is becoming something you can price, hedge, and trade. As demand for GPUs outruns supply and prices swing, the people who buy and sell compute are building the same market infrastructure that exists for energy and other commodities: indices, benchmarks, spot markets, and derivatives.

Join us at SPC NYC for a conversation with people building that market from different sides:
Alejandro Soumah leads compute trading at Jump Trading, overseeing trading and transaction structuring across compute markets. He previously co-founded Itô Markets, an agentic compute trading desk, and worked as a quantitative analyst at Goldman Sachs.

Carmen Li is the founder and CEO of Silicon Data, which provides GPU pricing, benchmarks, and market data for AI compute. She is also CEO of Compute Exchange, a marketplace for trading compute. Before founding Silicon Data in 2024, she spent more than 15 years in financial services, including roles at Bloomberg (global head of strategic alliances for enterprise data), Citi, and DRW.
Brexton Pham is Global Co-Head, AI & Compute Infrastructure at the Cantor Group where he leads cross-group compute efforts across Cantor, BGC, and Newmark.

events.name: Reading for Writers: James Baldwin
events.description:
Most writers read a lot. But reading isn’t enough; you need to study great writing.
This workshop is a chance to analyze and understand how he does it.
What’s the structure of the workshop?
The specific essay we'll be reading will be shared close to the date!
Together, we'll break down the storytelling structure, the literary techniques, and the format. We’ll reverse-engineering what turns a good idea into a piece of writing people can't stop reading and sharing.
You'll leave with:
A clearer sense of what makes a great personal essay
A method for using personal stories to carry a broader message
An understanding of how to shape a personal essay for Substack and online readers
Who is this for?
Anyone who writes personal essays
Writers on Substack or anywhere online
Anyone who wants to get better at nonfiction writing
Details
This is an in-person workshop in NYC. We're keeping it intimate at 15 people.
Spots are limited.
If you're serious about your writing, you won’t want to miss this!

James Q is a former computer engineer turned writer and community organizer. He left his job in tech to pursue writing and community full-time. events.name: Frontier Paper Club
events.description: Frontier Paper Club — NYC​Papers. People. Possibilities.​How do we know an AI agent is actually getting better? What makes a research result hold up beyond its benchmark? And which ideas are ready to become systems people can depend on?​Frontier Paper Club is a monthly gathering in New York for researchers, engineers, and founders exploring the next generation of AI.Sponsored by Betaworks andBlobfish.ai, we bring together people developing new methods, building agent systems, and testing what works in practice.​Each session centers on2–3 papers, benchmarks, or technical implementationsselected around a shared research question. Topics span AI agents, reinforcement learning, post-training, reasoning, memory, evaluation, and simulation environments.​Presentations are brief and technically grounded, leaving plenty of time to examine the work together: the assumptions behind a method, the strength of its evidence, the details needed to reproduce it, and the failures that suggest where research should go next.​📝 Want to present your work?​Have research or an implementation you’d like to discuss with New York’s AI community?​We’re accepting submissions covering:​AI agents, reasoning, planning, and memory​Reinforcement learning and post-training​Benchmarks, evaluation methods, and agent reliability​Simulation environments and synthetic training data​Reproductions, negative results, and practical lessons from deployment​Share a link to yourpaper, benchmark, project, or slides, along with what you’d like to present. Submissions will be considered for upcoming sessions.​Submit your work here →​Questions? Contactsam@blobfish.ai.
